title: OPEN for Business
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I hope you are well and managing to navigate the problems that seem to beset us all one way or another these days.

Last week I was telling you there is always light.. and that resilience can overcome almost anything.

We had just had an Indian shipment arrive that had taken more than a year from order to market.. you can read about Mahul and the Orgonite here.

Meanwhile talking about resilience and overcoming barriers.. we finally overcame the Brexit barrier, more info below.


A customer who reads this newsletter emailed me with the news that small tables that can be used as plant pot stands are selling well as people focus on bringing more greenery into their homes. He was even kind enough to tell me the best selling dimensions and designs. Some companies just copy what's good, but at AW we always like to take a good idea and develop it further. I forwarded pictures and dimensions to Ringo, our man in Indonesia and then called him up on Whatsapp. I had an idea who could make the product for us. The lady who makes display stands, in Ubud, opposite her factory are two guys that do metal fabrications (they could work together). The guy we call the letterman way up in the mountain, him and his village made small furniture before. And then there is a guy in Mas not far from our warehouse who buys scrapped fishing boats and his team of artisans upcycle them into furniture and display stands. (see here).

Ringo was off to see them all and yesterday we had virtual meetings, this is the new way to do business. It was amazing to chat to my old friends in Bali, and they were of course delighted to get the chance to develop some extra business. But it struck me this kind of product development is only possible because of those personal relationships and that a good level of trust has already been established. At AW we have a lot of relationship capital in the bank, but how long that lasts.. who knows.

It's a strange world we live in, I think the consequences of how Brexit and covid issues unwind in the coming months could be lots of things we don't expect. 

 

We ordered racking for the new warehouse in Sheffield.. it's a hell of an investment. 8000 pallet spaces, of course we got quotes from several companies. The best quote was from a Czech company, which before brexit would have been no issue. But now the delivery came (five truck loads) and of course there was a whole host of covid issues, and then Brexit issues. Why has life got so complicated..?



Open for business.. finally. Finally the AW hero's.. this includes Katka and Bryant in the UK, Tomas and his team in Slovakia, Raul (IT wizard) in KL, James (warehouse manager), Adam and the Slolvak accountants and a host of customs clearance experts. They made it happen.. our EU customers orders finally got delivered without our customers having to pay duty or vat. How? Good question.. this plan is down to Tomas.

 

We picked and packed that first batch of orders after Christmas.. using specially written software linking DPD Slovakia to the label printer in the UK.. then all the orders were put on ten pallets and one special consolidated invoice for all those orders made.. selling them to our AW Slovaka company.. then after a huge effort managed to find an agent to customs clear that invoice.. which had 99 different tariff codes, each with different duty and regulations.   Then a company to ship it, and because it needed to go through other EU countries we needed a T1 (transit form), the UK system to produce these was temporarily broken.. delays.. then we needed a Slovaka customs agent to clear the goods.. 99 tariff codes, pay duty and vat and deliver to the AW Slovak warehouse.. 

They dragged up 25 questions, checking CE documents, cosmetic licences, labeling, country of origin etc etc. Tomas spent two days supplying everything asked for..(fortunately we know how to import to the EU, so all this work had been done before) and finally they cleared the shipment.  They wanted actual pictures of the products in his hands, so really hard work. Anyway in the end.. we did it and 225 boxes were handed over to DPD and are now on the way to different points within the 27 EU nations. 

 

Now we made it happen, we have to streamline it, learn how to scale it, and make it more efficient. And we have to do this whole job once or twice every week. 

But at the end of the we made it happen, so we can say.. we are open for EU business once more.

 

Of course this friction trade is not ideal.. even though we are happy to help our customer order in the UK.. many have already started ordering in our Spain and Slovak websites. Tomas in Slovakia was today looking for a bigger warehouse.

The pictures he showed me look surprisingly like Affinity Park in Sheffield.



Meanwhile it's almost Valentine's Day..

We have lots of offers and ideas, see below. Plus I'm sure you don't need reminding but this is the "Season of Love" - V-Day followed by Mothering Sunday, by Easter, by Father's Day.. by the Wedding season.. so many reasons why your customers need to buy a gift.

Don't forget you can also trade via the AW dropshipping websites: AW-Dropship.com (in UK) and there is nothing to stop you leaping over the Brexit barrier and simply trading in the EU with our Spain Dropshipping site: AW-Dropship.es or Slovakia: AW-Dropship.eu.

Now you can make it happen also.

 

Take care, stay safe, be resilient. 

 

Happy trading.. 


David

title: David’s AW News: A Buddha on the Mountain
content_html:
Greetings once again from Spain... Hope you are well and enjoying the Summer..

Well, this is not something you see every day...

One of our customers has installed one of our Giant Garden Buddhas on a mountain top in Slovakia. We are told all planning and permissions were correctly obtained, which is always nice to hear. More on that later, but I thought it made a pretty wonderful picture to start this week’s newsletter.

...but not for much longer. Next week I will be packing my bags and heading off again. It is back on the road, back to visiting suppliers, back to hunting down new ideas and hopefully bringing you the next wave of interesting products.

One thing I have learned over the years is that new products do not find themselves. You have to go looking.

Last week I was telling you about flirting with danger in Mijas, the almost-lost Spanish ID card, and my close encounter with the famous mustard scam. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

This week has been less dramatic, but actually very important.

I have been working closely with Raul and his team in Bali. And Tomas and Toni on some of the boring background stuff that keeps AW moving forward. For the last couple of years we have been slowly moving our websites away from our old, dated platform onto our new system. It has been a massive job. Thousands of products. Thousands of images. Descriptions, prices, stock feeds, customer accounts, checkout testing, translations and all the little details that nobody notices unless something goes wrong.

This week was historic because the last of our five Spanish websites finally moved across to the new platform.

That might not sound exciting, but it is a big step. It means we are now in a much stronger position to keep improving the websites, adding better tools, making ordering easier and giving you more useful ways to find and sell products.

Sometimes the important work is invisible.

Talking of history...

Today also marks six years since the AW Inferno, when our main warehouse in Sheffield burned down on a hot, muggy summer night following an extraordinary, mystical chain of events captured on CCTV.

It was one of those moments that could have finished the business.

But it did not. Staff came together. Customers supported us. Suppliers stood by us. We rebuilt, restocked and somehow came back stronger.

If you have never read the story, you can find it here:
https://www.ancientwisdom.biz/21anniversary

Anyway, back to the here and now.

Rodrigo tells me his “Hydration Break” Instagram reel has now had almost half a million views.

Half a million! https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZ-Lm6rI9YG/?hl=en

Apparently watching people stop work for a drink of water or tea in the heat is exactly what the internet needed this week. Still, with the weather we have all been having, hydration breaks are no joke.

And speaking of heat, parts of the UK have again been hotter than Spain. So perhaps I should stop pretending I am suffering down here.

The sunshine is also good news for camping, garden centres, festivals, outdoor living and all those shops that do well when people finally remember they have a garden, a tent or a campervan.

This week Holly’s new Can You Sell This? video is all about Mandala Leaves Tea.

Here it is: https://youtu.be/Gzo1TnN8zks

Tea might sound simple, but it is one of those lovely gift-shop products that ticks a lot of boxes. It is easy to display, easy to understand, repeatable, comforting, and ideal for customers looking for a little everyday ritual.

A peaceful cup of hydration tea feels rather appropriate this week. 

Because BIG NEWS: Happy Holi-Daze has started - July is the Month for Holidays.

We are calling it Happy Holi-Daze! With new offers every day and FREE SHIPPING in July.

Free shipping begins, and from Monday there will be fresh offers coming daily. So keep checking the site because Rodrigo and the team have been busy lining up some very tempting summer deals.

We also have some very welcome back-in-stock arrivals: Mixed Gemstone lines, Gemstone Magic Pendulums, Mini Gemstone Trees.. 

These are always strong sellers. Gemstones have that lovely mix of beauty, meaning and impulse appeal. They work in gift shops, crystal shops, garden centres, wellness stores and tourist shops. Small products, good stories, strong margins. Also newly arrived are the Agnes + Cat Bath Fizzer Gift Sets. 

These look great, smell lovely and make very easy gifts. Bath and body is one of those categories that just keeps working. People may cut back on some big purchases, but a small treat, a relaxing bath, a pretty boxed gift... these SELL!

Now back to that Buddha. I love this.

A product that began life with artisans in Indonesia, travelled through the AW system, and now sits quietly looking out across a Slovakian landscape. That is the magic of this business.

Most days we think we are moving boxes. A pallet here, a container there, another order out the door before the courier arrives.

But actually, these products go into real homes, shops, gardens, studios, spas, retreats, hotels and sometimes, amazingly, mountaintops.

They become part of someone’s space. Part of someone’s story.

That is why we keep travelling. That is why we keep rebuilding websites. That is why the warehouse teams work so hard at month end. That is why we keep searching for new products, better suppliers and more interesting ideas. Six years ago, after the fire, it would have been easy to think the story had ended.

But here we are.

New websites. New products. New teams. New videos. New offers. A viral hydration break. A Buddha on a mountain. And next week, me back on the road again.

Finally, for our UK customers, Monday morning may be a little slower than usual. England play Mexico in the World Cup at 1am, and pubs in England and Wales are being allowed to stay open until 5am.

Good news for football fans. Possibly less good news for Monday productivity.

Good luck, England; enjoy the sunshine, drink plenty of water (or Mandela leaves tea), and thank you as always for being part of the Ancient Wisdom journey.

Have a great weekend.

David

title: Bad Lands of Java
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about the new residents of Yellow Coconut Village in Ubud, Bali. You canread it here.
This week I have been on a road trip to East Java. It happened like this; I have been looking for something to replace the root baskets we have been buying from China. These are made from sustainable fur-tree roots, they are beautiful but fur tree roots if not properly treated and dried can crack. On the last few shipments this has been a growing issue. So I have been tasked with solving this knotty problem :).
In Udud, where I am now, there are lots of traders selling teak root products. As you know teak is very hard, and the oil in it allows a little movement which means cracking is not a big issue. The big problem is whenever I ask about sustainability of the teak supplies, I get blank looks. So Ringo (our Balinese agent) and I started to do some rooting around to find out how the teak-wood business works here. The first thing we learnt is there are no commercial teak forests on Bali, or teak artisans. The teak is trucked in from Java roughly carved but not finished, the artisans stain and varnish the pieces to suit the customers. So it seems the teak trader middlemen don't verify the source of the wood, it's all a cash business.
A lady in one of the wood carving markets gave us the name of a town where she thought the teak came from. A quick bit of googling revealed the place. It didn't seem so far away, just a ferry to East Java and and a hop over the mountains. We decided to branch out and make the trip. All I can say is don't trust google maps estimation of driving time in Indonesia! It was a long way, mostly spent going up and down steep windy hills though thick jungle stuck behind trucks crawling along at snails pace.
The ferry to East Java drops you at the foot of a jungle clad volcano right out of National Geographic, the road after a couple of hours enters the vast teak forest. Now Ringo tells that this road is home to bandits who roll rocks out of the forest at night, when a car or truck hits one in the night they come to "assist" you and take money or goods for their help. These same forest folk probably illegally take teak wood which finds it's way to the dodgy traders. It's known as the bad lands of Java.
In the day time it's better, but we were still stopped three times at unofficial tolls, a "broken" truck blocking the road and dodgy guys with buckets claiming to be collecting for Ramadan.
The good news is that this forest is controlled by the government, and in the last year have made big steps to enforce the control. The road has been upgraded to a good tarmac road, every twenty kilometres or so there is a ranch style police station with round the clock security.
Eventually we made it to a small coastal sugar cane town. The industry was devolved by the Dutch who built cute narrow-gauge railways running through the plantations bringing the sugar cane to the port. Some parts of it still working. There has been a half-hearted attempt to make a tourist industry here. It's certainly beautiful, stunning mountains, mangrove swamps and white sand beaches. But no tourists, Ringo and I hired the two best (teak lined) rooms in a big run down beach road hotel for about £12, there was just one other guest. Ringo said the Muslim call to prayer from the many mosques at four am and lack of alcohol, put many tourists off coming. Sad because the people were lovely and the place stunning.
But there is a thriving handy-craft industry. We found marble carving, shell jewellery, mother of pearl boxes and the like, and teak wood of course. We were taken to workshops practically on the beach where families worked together making lovely stuff. Eventually we found a village with teak wood work-shops, we visited them all.
One guy in a small factory told us he was "just the local chief of police" (pointing to a police station along the road), his wife was the boss, could we come back later.
What we learnt was the the government have cracked down hard on the teak wood trade to ensure the sustainability of supplies. Local artisans can (or should) only buy from the official run logging company, and the police enforce the rules, hence the police presence in the forest.
Teak wood of course is mainly used for furniture and flooring, the roots are a by-product and of less interest to the bad guys because it's more work to dig up. But the most beautiful bowls and plates are made from the random root shapes all slightly different. Yes a little expensive, but will last forever and help support families like this.
The lady on the right is the boss. Her son and his wife are part of the business, and the little guy with long hair in a Man-united shirt is their son who just wanted to be in the picture.
More news next week.
Expect to read more about the Ubud outpost in future reports..
Until then.
Take care..
David

title: David's AW News: About Tomas, Erika and Buddha
content_html:
Greetings from Trnava, Slovakia.


Yes, I'm in our Eastern Europe distribution warehouse.. Our big beautiful (Buddha) warehouse.

On Wednesday afternoon, Tomas, Raul (the IT wizard), and me took an Uber to Leeds Bradford airport and boarded a packed and rowdy Ryanair flight to Bratislava. When we landed, all the Slovaks clapped and cheered, have you experienced that? I think only Slovak and Czech people do that. 
Last week, I was telling you about sinkholes in Bali and our soft launch of the new Dropshipping website. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Regular readers will know about our Trnava adventures. This is Tomas's home town, and after Brexit happened and we realised that selling into Europe to independent gift shops was just not going to work well, so opened a warehouse quickly here.. it has been wildly successful, and a few years ago we moved to a big, beautiful new warehouse - 6000 pallet spaces. 
We wanted to make an amazing space that our team could enjoy working in.. Tomas and Erika (and team) worked hard to make it happen..
Tomas in the staff room.. with its lovely views over the countryside. Unfortunately, the heatwave here ended just as we arrived, it's a bit wet and drizzly, the guys here are complaining that I brought regular UK weather with me.

The sinkhole that appeared in the road on Bali and brought the whole island to a grinding halt.. has been fixed - probably because of the social media storm showing log-jammed roads..  the local government pulled out all the stops, and the road will reopen this weekend. title: Bloom & Grow
content_html:
Greetings

It's been so hot, blisteringly hot.. that's a good thing right?
By the time you read this, I will be back in the BBUK... Brexit Bound United Kingdom - or should that be.. BBBUK.. you can probably work out what the extra B stands for :)

So this week I have been looking for a new warehouse in Spain, surprisingly empty warehouses still exist and at reasonable prices - the only issue is finding one big enough for all our plans and ambitions.. I was worried that lots of companies from the UK would be soaking up the spaces as companies from the BBUK make Brexit escape routes. After all South Spain has to be one of the best places to work.. 

In Slovakia - where we also have a distribution warehouse, they are building new warehouses like crazy, and everyone and their aunt is after a warehouse, Amazon have one so big it's like a small country. Why not here also?

Last week I was telling you about the Olive Tree.. you can read about it here.

As the Boris Brexit  shapes up, the need to make plans becomes more urgent. As importer and exporter, and almost half our sales going to our European customers it is a real concern. Who knows how things will pan out? That known unknown is the tricky thing to plan for.. there are 60 staff in the UK who's jobs rely to high degree on the trade, I feel incredibly responsible. 60 families for goodness sake.

Of course in India, Indonesia and China many more people rely on trade with AW to support jobs and families. We mostly deal with small family businesses, over the years we have seen many bloom and grow. At a rough estimate, maybe 500 families rely on AW around Asia. Plus of course we try to help where we can, Mr Chatterjee in India has done a fantastic job with the orphanage we support over twenty children are getting a good education, decent living standard and even weekly art lessons.. 
I'll maybe be reporting from there later this year. Here is a picture of the kids with me, the art and computer teachers. 

  
I'm not going to let a little thing like Brexit endanger all this.. hell no!

The fox.

I was telling you about the Olive Tree, symbol of Ancient Wisdom and Peace. We planted one in a big pot in the garden here in Spain. It was also symbolic of our new AW company in Spain.. with love and water it will bloom and grow.. but it seems to be under attack from the local wild life, an urban fox (we think) comes in the night, jumps in the pot and for some reason digs up the soil. Why does it do this, every day we fix the soil, every night it comes back, why.. is it mad? Obviously you can't kill a fox, but I will have to find away to make it go away.  

Meanwhile back at AW HQ.. so many new things are blooming and growing it's untrue.
Smudge sticks.. yes it's true, that most requested of item, it is finally here..
From Mr Chatterjee's jute factory in India.. Natural (no plastic) Shopping Baskets.
The creation of AW Team.. Natural Beard Oils.. absolutely stuffed full of good stuff.. 
The mystical Palo Santo incense wood.. full AW range now on line.
and more.. see below.

The natural shopping baskets were my project. Working with Mr Chatterjee in India earlier this year we created a range of natural shopping baskets.
All those plastic shopping baskets, there has to be a better way. No-one online seemed to be offering an alternative. So I spent a couple of days with Mr Chatterjee and his super talented team. 
I want a basket I told them, it has to be 100% organic, must stack inside each other (like plastic ones do) and be strong enough to last for years. And it should work out cheaper than the plastic version.. not much to ask right? 
And then we made a mini version of the same..


Mr Chatterjee shows an early prototype of the mini version.
You start with a sketch, pick the materials, the model man goes at it, cranking away on his sewing machine. Model made, you make mods and he goes (patiently) and does it again, and again and again.

Eventually, you end up with a product you hope people will love.

And we really love gifts at AW.. remember giving a gift is an act of love..  
I learn from google that today is Grandparents Day.
So to Grandparents everywhere - have a wonderful day. Spread the love.. 

More news next week.

Take Care

David

title: Interesting Times
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Spain

I'm here with Tomas and Katka (who just left) working on our new venture AW Artisan in Malaga.
It's part of our Brexit ready strategy  - to enable our customers to access genuine AW products after Brexit.
It's fun, frustrating, exciting and exhausting is equal measures. But Interesting Times - we are learning a lot.
Last week I was telling you about the SOL - and how it is bigger than Christmas - How to get ready for the SOL - you can read about it here.  
Tomas has been working on the new showroom in Spain, and this later we will recreate in the UK.. (which badly needs a revamp).


Meanwhile the customer service team from Spain have been dispatched back with Katka to the UK for the full "thrown in the deep-end" learn on the job type training.
They get "partnered" for a day with different people at AW - make friends (for life!) and soak up as much knowledge, experience and skills as possible. I just hope they don't catch Yorkshire flu :)
So if you need to call or chat to AW over the next few days and find a Spanish person.. please by kind and say Hola!  Here they are freshly arrived - wrapped up for British weather :-)


And.. here they are learning fast.


And to be honest - we need all the help we can get.. It's so busy in the UK it's unnatural. Last week I was (sort of) joking that the SOL - Season of Love is bigger than Christmas.. and it is - just spread out over the next few months. Incredibly important to be focused on love and relationship gifts at this time of year.. and we have lots and lots of new stock arriving and arrived (over Christmas).. It's crazy - it really is like Christmas. 

Normally we cut down agency staff after Christmas - this year we are taking them on the books and getting more in. I just checked we are this week (so far) 76% up on last year.. The Brexit effect maybe, sales to Europe are booming but UK sales are also up an incredible 43%. 

We have some tremendous products - your customers will love them.. only problem as usual we are back up and running behind again (sorry sorry sorry) -  weekend shifts are back on, we are doing our best.
Are we ready for Brexit? Does anybody know.. ? We have warehouses already trading in Spain and Slovakia.. but what will happen come 1st February. After Big Ben Bongs (or not) what changes?
We received a memo from UK largest couriers - and the bottom line is - with just days to go - they don't know either.

We live in interesting times.. 

Take care.. be kind - smile.

Monday is the most depressing day of the year - Blue Monday.. I'll write you then..

David

title: In search of dream stones
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Happy Easter, hope it will be peaceful and calm.
Last week I was telling you about my trip with Toni to Morocco hoping to find more products. I was telling you about our stay in Fez and how it was not what I expected. IF you missed it you can catch up here.
After Fez we hired a car to drive to the town where our selenite and gemstones guy operates from. 

In the shadow of the snow covered Atlas Mountains this is a special geological place, whatever momentous events that threw up those mountains created a wealth of interesting gemstones and minerals.
What surprised me is that finding gemstone minerals is not big business, it's really just individual prospectors hacking away at rocks in caves and holes hoping to find something valuable. Small traders in the towns buy the finds and assemble them into what are called "flats". Basically a small tray with a collection of 20 - 30 stones arranged to show off the best aspects. These "Flats" are bought by gemstone traders that turn up often in campervans, and ship them back home the long way. Apart from the flats are the more spectacular finds,  Vanadinite is one of the most famous. Our man Ismail took us out into the desert to meet a friend of his who mines vanamight, living in a simple shack close to his staked location, he spends the nights (because it is cooler) in search of his dream stone. Ismail told us a couple of years ago he found a piece that he sold for $4000. I bought this small piece from the guy directly for €20 he seemed very happy.


Here is one of the many small traders that buy up the finds and some pictures of the more special stones he had to offer.


Apart from the minerals they also of course find fossils which are fascinating in themselves, but the main thing in this area is Selenite.
The Selenite deposits are plentiful and easy to find, and many miners collect the almost luminous moon stone and bring it to our man Ismail. All over town small workshops each with a few artisans turn the raw selenite into beautiful objects, lamps, heart shapes, bowls and jewellery. Ismail runs around commissioning jobs supplying the raw stones and then packing in his warehouse. We could see it was a whole minor industry employing several hundred people.
Since we have worked with Ismail we have brought five container loads to Europe and I'm pretty sure that has kept a lot of artisans busy in this area.
So in the end we ordered about 50 new product lines with Ismail, he also agreed to be our mineral agent and supply us with "flats" of local stones. 


Here's Ismail.
Ismail has a plan to bring his artisans under one roof, a modern warehouse with ventilation and all the health and safety to EU standard. We promised to support his dream with regular orders and increased range.
"Next time you come to my village it will be very different" he told us. 

So this is the story of Ismail, in the Easter spirit of renewal it seems appropriate.
Hope you have a wonderful Easter, with chocolate, love and good wishes.

Take care

David

title: More China Secrets
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu City in China

Yes I'm still in China and still very busy. Last week I was telling just how busy Coco (my wife and your China agent) actually is, if you missed it you can catch up here. 
This morning and yesterday morning Coco was out of bed at 5.30am because these two days are container loading days, yesterday's container is on its way to Spain (AW-Artisan.eu), today's container is being loaded as I write and will go to our Slovakia warehouse (Awgifts.eu). A team of guys on motorbikes turn up, they are the professional Container Loading Gang.. they know how to use every single square inch of space, because in a container space is actually money.
Depending on the type of products and size of the team they can load a container in three to five hours. Jolly chaps, no drama they get the job done chop chop, Coco gives them soft drinks and a tip, and they are off to some other part of town to load another container. Today was very quick because most of the order was big boxes, done by 10.30am and the container is already on the way to Ningbo Port.


Other wholesales get upset with me telling you all the trade secrets. But I don't care, if we can't deliver great value without  keeping secrets then we are not doing our job right. Anyway nothing really secret any more (just ask Ask AI), Yiwu itself was a trade secret years ago and I told you all about it here.. 

Most days we have been heading to the huge Yiwu market, and working our way down a wish list of products. The market is like a trade fair exbo, but permanent and vast. There are about 88,000 showrooms literally under one roof.  On four floors with highly specialised areas for all sorts of products.. It's split into 5 areas with new ones being built. For example there is a ribbon area with what must be every ribbon manufacturer in China having a showroom there. We need to find some bespoke printed ribbons for a particular product, and were swamped with too much choice. But as you can imagine having so many competing companies cheek to jowl means highly competitive prices. But even so when Coco explains she is an agent that doesn't require a secret commission, the prices come down another 5%.. This is one of the reasons you will find our China product prices highly competitive. 
All over the market, and maybe on your social media you can find adverts for Yiwu Agents, if you want to do business here you will need one, and most claim to charge you 1 or 2% commission. We know from experience that hidden commissions can be a whole different ball game. And very dodgy agents will without your knowledge "sell" your order to the supplier that gives them highest commission. Basically holding small businesses hostage with threats of moving trade as a means to extract more.. you can imagine what happens to quality, trust and ethics.. and those hidden costs find the way back. 
I'm very happy that we do straight business in Yiwu - most of our suppliers are small family businesses and I can tell you they are super happy to trade with AW, and we are able to work closely on new products and always have a good feel for the ethics and trading standards of our suppliers. 

Another secret I will tell you is about my favourite area, it is not even in the market, but quite near by and it's the crystal and gemstone area. A grid of about 4 by 6 leafy back streets with rows of stores all dealing in different crystals. Cheap hotels cater for foreign folk from Africa to South America because gemstones and gemstones traders arrive here from all over the world. Here you can buy every type of gemstones, gemstone jewellery, fittings and components.. At AW we already buy a lot directly from India and Africa but gemstones (like essential oils) come from all over the world. Some products we can buy better but many items from here are good value. We spent two happy days seeking out new suppliers, disappearing into huge cellars full of amazing crystal products, and making friends with passionate gemstone folk. Here are few random pictures from our time in the gemstone streets.


We were totally blown away by the stuff available.. and Coco who has many talents has an eye for jewellery design and we bought lots of samples to play with.. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. it's getting busy. Lot of fast selling items back in stock and with Father's Day fast approaching not before time. Check out the Father's Day page here for inspiration. It's no secret we have some brilliant gifts lined up for Fathers everywhere.

This weekend Coco and I are heading to Xiamen, which is the city across the water from Taiwan - so it should be interesting. I'll spill the secrets next week.
Have a great weekend. More updates next Friday, where we will be somewhere else altogether. 

Take care

David

title: Brexit! - No Big Deal.
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ in Sheffield.

I just arrived having been in Spain at the new AW distribution depot in Malaga.
So it is happening, it's finally here - Great Britain is leaving the EU.
Whatever way you voted (I'll make no secret - I think leaving is a mad mistake) it's kind of the like the end of an era - and the beginning of something new.
A new beginning, a new dawn - we have to make the best of the situation. And we are. We have depots in Slovakia and Spain already in full swing. You can read last week newsletter here.


Check out our Spain banner :)   
And other good news.. our AWArtisan.pt   Portuguese website launched yesterday and seems very busy from the off.

But there is a bigger problem that is occupying my mind these days. Some of you will know Coco (my wife) and our China agent. She is the reason why we have such a great range of quality artisan products from family businesses in China and at the right prices. Coco and Tomas are the dream team, they really make things happen. Coco was with me in Spain until the 15th of January, when she flew to China to be with her family in her home town in Jiangxi province. She got home to Yiwu (where our office and warehouse is) and then drove to the home town. Because of the Chinese New Year an epic drive 16 hours - half a billion people go home at this time.. Once home, the celebrations for New Year began.. and then abruptly ended as the Corona virus problem engulfed the area. 
Jaingxi province is next to Wuhan and at first people there thought the issue was far away, but as each day passes it gets more immediate. The last 5 days Coco and her immediate family have not left the house. Police cars drive up and down the one street village telling residents to remain in doors, last week four cases were reported in the nearby city of Dongxiang and yesterday a case in the next village just along the road. I speak to Coco every day, and she is upbeat and cheerful, but today I can see the strain on her face, she no longer believes the government news feed, it's worse much worse than they say.
The thing is - I should be there. It's the first time in 7 years I have not been in China for CNY. Thanks to Brexit and our new Spain company, I decided to stay in Europe. 
If you want to send a message of encouragement - I can pass it on, it would mean a lot.

Hopefully these things will also pass. But it kind of make's the Brexit problem look like no big deal.
Practical problem is that, no factories are going to open anytime soon in China, CNY has already been extended. All the roads and trains between cities are closed or suspended. So it's unlikely that any China products will arrive in Europe until at least June. So I think there will be a significant hit to China stock. Fortunately, we have - Indian, Indonesian, Nepal stock all on the way, and you should be able to rely on all the stuff made in our Sheffield factory. So.. don't panic :)

50p coin has been released to "commemorate" the day, I think it should have been a 52p coin.. with 48p coin we can still spend in Europe .. 
Anyway "Always look on the Bright Side of life" der dum der dum der dum.. 


Also happening this weekend is the Birmingham Spring Fair.
AW won't be there of course, but our Very British Brand - Agnes & Cat.. will be there making an appearance. Do call and say hi.. Tomas, Tiphanie, Lenka & Rodrigo will be there. On Monday I may be around.


Anyway - have a wonderful weekend.

Take care

David

title: Hello from China
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Gosh I seem to be running from place to place these days, it's like a mad catch up. I realised that I haven't spent more than 6 or 7 days in one place in months.. Last week I was in Bali (on a flying visit), telling you how everything was absolutely buzzing.. it's all happening at once.. If you missed it you can catch up here.
On Tuesday night I left Bali on a China Southern flight to Guangzhou arriving at 6am. There I cleared immigration after a long wait.. the foreigner queue seemed to have very few westerners in it (apart from me). I was a little confused and thought maybe I was in the wrong line. But then I realised by spying on the passports folk were clutching that these were mostly Chinese Americans or Chinese Australians etc going to China for family reunions ahead of the Mid-autumn festival. Which happens shortly and means I'm going to have to eat copious quantities of Mooncakes.. especially since most of our old suppliers will give them as gifts. 
I had a few hours in Guangzhou and then a short flight upto Yiwu, as we landed the crew instructed us to (strangely) close the window blinds. Two Danish ladies close to me got into a small argument, insisting that the shades should be up, and being told quite firmly that they should be down. Turns out (Coco told me later) that some top secret military aircraft are stationed at Yiwu and paranoid officials are worried that foreign buyers arriving in Yiwu might actually be spies.

Yiwu is only a small airport, not so many flights these days, and my luggage arrived on the belt quickly, I headed out and Coco was there hopping from foot to foot, happy to see me.   We headed home to the apartment chatting and catching up.. the next morning after catching up with the family and distributing the many gifts I had accumulated along the way.. we headed to Yiwu market to see some suppliers.


I discovered that Yiwu market is 30 years old this year and celebrating the milestone. But not a glorious celebration by any means.
Bali might be Buzzing as I told you last week, but Yiwu is distinctly placid. Coco tells me that many traders have closed, the pandemic was actually busy with re-orders but no visitors. Now there are only a few western buyers arriving and business generally is bad. The expected rebound never came. The only other buyers I saw were Russians, and a few Africans. One of our suppliers told me they don't buy the volumes the Europeans or Americans buy and want everything at rock bottom prices.  We have a warehouse and candle factory in Yiwu, and Coco this week was able to renegotiate the rent at a substantial discount, it's the first time ever that rents have reduced.



The main entrance is virtually empty, and traders wait for days to meet an international buyer.. It's a little sad.
There are 88,000 showrooms in Yiwu market, it's a massive place and used to be a hive of activity.. and actually in some places it still is.. not strictly in the market but a neighborhood nearby is the gemstone trading area.. this area is my favourite place - full of interesting traders, lovely passionate creative people and exotic, esoteric products. perfect for AW..  Coco and I can spend happy days there discovering all manner of exotic jewellery, artifacts and the like. 
Last time I was here, raw crystals were taking off.. we developed and bought the Gemstone Crystal Lights.. (which are selling very well), and now lots of products including candles and jewellery are been made with "Raw Crystals" it's the next big craft trend.. and we have bulk raw crystals on the way to your shop.. soon.. 

Back in the UK and Europe.. so many new and (in my humble opinion) brilliant exciting  products are arriving.. and in these days when trade might not as vibrant as it should be - the importance of NEW and EXCITING products in your store has never been so important.. and I believe we are on the button with trends that are selling.. New incense trends, Indian and Indonesian products.. Gemstone, exoteric items and essential oils are always great sellers in difficult times.  

I was just chatting with our webmaster wizard Rodrigo in the UK.. he tells me he has a massive 10 new product families to add today.. see below.. if he (and team) manages all of them that will have been a magnificent marathon of an achievement. And Rodrigo, always up for a marathon, is running one on Sunday..  for charity.. Details here if you want to support him.

We have Halloween aplenty for you.. approaching fast.. and less than 100 days to Christmas.. 
Time to get organised and secure the best stock for a successful season.

Take care and have a wonderful weekend.
More news next week from China. Coco says Hi! 

David

title: Welcome Welcome Welcome
content_html:
11th January 2013

Hi ,
Well it's a new year, next stop Valentines Day (yes just weeks away) and things are getting off to a flying start at Ancient Wisdom.
We have three big welcomes for you..
Welcome Buddha at AW.
I'm in the UK right now and it's all happening. a new Indonesian container came with amongst other things huge Buddha's. We put one outside our warehouse to welcome visitors and it looks amazing. I have ordered a big sign to go with it which should go up next week that says "Welcome to Ancient Wisdom".
They are made with resin, gypsum and cement, like stone they will weather nicely but they are not so heavy you cannot manoeuvre them. Best of all they are rather calming and zen-like, as well as surprisingly good value, check them out and feel the calmness.
Even better.. they are on our Drop-shipping website at the same price (plus shipping) so no need to stock them - just ship them direct to your to your customers.
Welcome Gold Reward Amnesty. Finishes Monday at Midnight.
So this is to welcome our customers (this is you!) to the new year. A Gold Reward Amnesty.. maximises discounts and stuff (read more here - or see below)..
What's more to welcome you to our website, we finally introduced one of those new-fangled "online chat" widgets. It's wonderful, now we can chat and answer questions in real time with all our customers. You can see it at the bottom right of the page. Looks like this..
Out of hours you can use it to leave a message, which we will deal with first thing. I think we are the first UK gift wholesaler to offer this service..
So don't be shy, need to know something, Just Ask..
Finally we have a brand new range of candle holders, made by a Indonesian family. What's better than romantic candle holders for Valentines Day?
Marry these these up with our Church Candles and you have beautiful gifts for Valentines Day.
This couple are passionate about candle holders. Wayan, the chap shown here, is the designer and head man of his village. Also a local hero because his candle holder designs have won some quite big orders with a large French department store (and AW), and he has subcontracted lots of work to practically every family in his village. This picture was taken in the paddy field right outside the small workshop they have built in an old cattle shed. See the candle holders here.
So from Wayan and his wife and all at AW wishing you successful trading for Valentines Day and beyond.
All the very best
David

title: David's AW News: In hard core India.
content_html:
Greetings from Goa, India


We just arrived in (or I should say escaped to) Goa. Catching up with old friends and checking on the renovation of the apartment we have here.. it's almost completed!
Last week I was telling you about our last days in Kathmandu and how we got invited to a wedding..and found ourselves in the year 2082 (tes really!) if you missed it, you can catch up here.
After arriving in Delhi - we spent a few days at the Spring Fair - the huge trade show where Indian exporters exhibit. Usually packed, but this time horribly empty..
and very, very hot!
Here's Toni from Spain and our man in India - Mr Chatterjee, behind.
It was not just the heat that was hard core in Delhi.. let me explain..

In the Trade Show
There is a hotel adjacent to the halls, mostly booked in advance by the traders, and Mr Chatterjee managed to get us rooms in there, which is super convenient, other people have to take shuttle buses sometimes to distant hotels.. Not that there were many buses running, the show clashed both with Easter holidays, the Canton fair in China and Trump tariffs - resulting in many long faces. So as we ventured round the stands, we saw the same faces, and began to realise there were simply not many foreign buyers. Very sad, you could feel the desperation in the air.. one guy told us their business was 80% American bound, and all orders had been cancelled or put on hold. 
Needless to say, we were very popular - Toni, mine and Mr Chatterjee phone non-stop messages, requesting a visit.. please come, sir.. and people following us around, or waiting in our path, hoping to capture us.. as much as we'd like to see every supplier and make an order.. it's not possible.. sadly had politely declined people to focus on the main people we need to see.
Sorry guys.. I know you read this newsletter.. Please be patient. 

In Old Delhi
We spent two days in Central Delhi.. Mr Rashid, one of our wooden box suppliers, came to our hotel, he came with his daughter, three staff and 19 cartons of samples, which they laid out all over Mr Chatterjee's hotel room. That was Hard Core! Crazy.. but in the end we found some awesome products because Rashid is an old supplier and knows exactly what AW customers (like you are looking for) with our designers input, I'm sure we can make magic happen.
It was hard core.. 

Deep in to Old Dehi (hard core)
Next day we went deep into old in to the ancient maze of streets that house some of India artisans for generations.. Hot day.. so hot. Our supplier meets at the point the taxi cannot go further, and we follow him through the maze of streets, stepping over people sleeping on the sidewalk, into a maze of alleyways.. then deep deep inside, then finally up tiny stairs through almost hidden doors and out to a showroom. We have been here many times.. a fan chops the hot air, and across one wall, a long table filled to the brim with carefully made stuff, especially for AW.  Our supplier Mr Karim is a humble chap, keep cricket player and devoted to finding the perfect AW lines.. I know he has spent the last six months working hard with his swathe of Delhi artisans (and far beyond) to produce the samples he has for us.


If you think this is hard core..

Next Level Hard Core
Well, the next morning, before going to the airport to come down to Goa, we squeezed in a visit to the oldest and most notorious trading area in India.. that place is truly hard core. I'll tell you all about Pahar Ganj next week. 

Going great guns!
Meanwhile, in the UK - things are hotting up! So many new and fast selling products we are actually struggling to catch up.. the Big Buddha Statues are flying out..(one lady told us she puts one outside her store and it sells in a day). Dinner Candles back in stock but selling like crazy.. new products see below..

Now we are in Goa. The place we are staying at is so peaceful and quiet. And I just realised it must be a bird watchers paradise. I woke up this morning to find a big, fluffy bird tapping on my bedroom window. We have seen storks and peacocks, and this morning, as we were meeting with our gemstone guy, a cute, friendly parrot came to visit us. Just wanted feeding..haha.
We made a new friend in Goa!

Hope you have a lovely weekend. 
More updates next Friday. 

Take care
David

title: Enthusiastic Ideas
content_html:
Greetings from India

Last week I was telling you about the Denmark Pub, an unlikely heritage hotel on the banks of the Ganges. We was in Serampur and the home town of our India agent; Mr Chatterjee. You can read about it here.
Since then we took a flight to Delhi, noticeably more people wearing face masks, both on the flight and in the streets of Delhi. It's all anyone talks about.
Anyone with a dry cough is avoided, people are noticeably scared.. our supplies casually ask where we came from.. when I tell them not China, I came from Europe - but not Italy they relax. These are scary times, apart from the virus it's affecting lots of businesses and people. I had planned to go to China after India, but that option seems to be off the table.. A few people asked for an update.. details below.

One morning before starting work in Serampore Mr Chatterjee suggested we take the local ferry across the Ganges and back just for the experience. Return ticket on a rickety ancient boat about 9p  so it seemed like good value.
They actually do have health and safety in India and we were issued big yellow life jackets and crammed on board the ferry with lots of locals heading to school or work on the other-side. There is definitely something mystical and magical.. even majestic about the mother river. From a small boat early in the morning, it was serene, powerful and strangely spiritually moving experience.. plus we made lots of friends.



Working hard with Mr Chatterjee and his team, creating a new range of wheatbag designs, eye pillows and some new bags. It's cool having all the materials on hand and skilled machine guys who quickly make up your ideas, and patiently adjust them. It's the best way to make things happen, my ideas, Tomas creativity and Mr Chatterjee and his team making it come together. 

On Saturday we took a break and went to the Children's home. These days Mr Kundo and his wife look happy and relaxed, all the Children love them and it's like they have a great big family. Supporting the home and bringing it up to a reasonable standard has been one of the most rewarding things ever. The good news is that Coco and all her family are fully healthy, no problems at all. Grand-children have school lessons from home over the computer, no-one goes out without a mask. In Yiwu (the government reports) only 17 cases of which 16 have totally recovered. If it's true.. then it sounds promising. 
Here in India; the government have stopped all China imports, which seems a bit extreme.. can the virus travel on objects and survive long periods? If they do the same in EU/UK that will be a problem.

I'm speaking to Coco (she is also my wife) all the time.. I was supposed to go to China next, but now who knows.. "When will I see you again?" she asked me.. and I don't know :(
But we do have plenty of stock from Indonesia on the way, a big shipment is leaving Nepal and always lots on the way from India. So don't worry we do have other stock than just Chinese.

Drop-shipping 
Thank you to everybody who has made feedback and suggestions.. It's wonderful to get such enthusiastic ideas.
If you didn't register yet you can do it here: AW-Dropship.com 

Next week - I have no idea where I will be!

Anything could happen, take care and stay safe.

David

title: My favourite team
content_html:
Greetings from Malaga airport

I'm here with Tomas and Raul.. we are on the way to the UK. 
Last week I was telling you a business traveller secret, that might surprise you.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
I was also telling you about our new upcoming Yoga Department.. which seems to have generated an enthusiastic response, thanks for your ideas and suggestions. 
In the UK we will be focusing on AW-Aromatics - which is just in the process of moving into a long awaited new factory complex. Again any ideas and suggestions are welcome.

This week we crammed into the bulging offices of AW-Artisan in Spain.. Toni (our manager is doing his best) but as we continue to expand and more people are needed it's starting to get a bit squashed.. but the ever cheerful team seem to cope quite well.. our lease has another two years to run.. and we are already thinking about exactly where we can expand to. It was Spain's national day and a bank holiday on Wednesday so Tuesday after work we took  the team out after work for a meal on the beach.. they love to party in Spain. Work hard and play hard.. it's the Spanish way.. It's a tradition that I have to make a little speech and thank everyone for their hard work. We have a long running joke where I call them "My favourite team" - of course it's only in jest, all our teams in various parts of AW amazing, but it gives them bragging rights and the ability to poke fun at the other teams. All of AW is integrated on a thing called Slack it's a corporate version of WhatsApp so people can trade ideas and connect across the company. And sometimes it is used for social interactions..
So we went to trendy beach chiringuito not far from our warehouse and after to the roof top bar of a nearby hotel.. it was really special and nice time to get know the new people.


I made my little speech.. "I'm really happy to be having dinner in my favourite type of restaurant, eating my favourite food, favourite wine, and especially doing this right here with my favourite team.. " Everyone cheers..  even the new guys they understand the joke.. 

Our flight was delayed of course, but we finally made it back to British soil..
This morning (Friday morning) the first job was to visit the new factory for AW-Aromatics.. We have already moved into the warehouse part and I was impressed how organised it was.. all stock neat and tidy and everything booked into locations.. The production area is almost ready to move into and the finishing touches are being made to the offices and showrooms. Erik our operations manager has everything ready to make the leap from our old factory to the new one with the minimum of disruption to production.. he tells me he has a five day plan. Wow the team here is really on the job.. They are also my Favourite Team.


Erik.. ready to move.


This is our new Aromatics factory.. not quite finished but almost..


We have 1200 pallet spaces.. already in use.
We are hoping to be able to move soon.. when we do we can expand production massively.. So if you are looking to develop your own brand.. or maybe you just want "own label" products. I have just been catching up with the marketing team and they tell me are already working with some interesting people with amazing ideas and brilliant designs.. 
We were just discussing how when it comes to bigger projects we need to carefully select who we work with, because at the end of the day even with added capacity there is a limit. So we should work with people we can get on with.. just like My Favourite Team (all of them).
If you want to join us.. register at AW-Aromatics - and start a new adventure today.

More news next week.

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: Nepal to India
content_html:
Greetings from Varanasi, India 


Happy October - can you believe it is October??!!
It's also Dashain (Nepal's main holiday - like Christmas) and in India Durga Puja - actually the world's biggest (under the radar) celebration.

Buddha air services has only one international flight.  And we took it, it goes to Varanasi.  From one holy city to another.
Last week I was telling you about Dashain - the Nepali Christmas - and flying kites. And our trip to Bhaktapur, a nearby city which is surprisingly nice, but hides a secret the Gen Z are angry about.
I made a YouTube video about it, see below.. or check last week's news here.
The Tika blessing
Our last day in Nepal was a major holiday and a special day in the Dashain festival.. We were lucky and honoured to be invited to the family home of one of our suppliers - the Lokta paper guy. Like Christmas, they have lots of traditions.. including flying kites on the roof, and the Tika blessing ceremony. This is traditionally performed by the elder in the household. This father in the family actually runs the small factory they have in a village up in the hills outside Kathmandu. Last year we visited there, so we had met the father before. 
One by one, all the family first.. then Toni and I.. sit crossed legged in front of the father..He puts a red ribbon around your neck, then takes a big splodge of red tikka paste and plants it on your forehead.. then an apple, a banana and two small denomination notes are pressed into your palms whilst you bow your head for a blessing. Finally, you're given a sprig of grass to put in your hair.
I asked what the symbolism of all these elements ment.. you know the ancient wisdom behind the ceremony?.. nobody knew! Well, why do you do this? Because we always do.. everybody does it.. 
Then we sat on the floor with heaps of cushions and low tables, played UNO and drank wine, beer whisky.. Even the ladies enjoyed a drink, and everyone relaxed, and it was great fun..
In many ways it was just like a British Christmas.. too much food and drink and lots of bonamie - and such lovely people. Kind and sweet people, it was an honor to be guests in such a household.
The wives of Bicky and his brother, his mother and two girls from the factory are in the picture with me. This kind of socialising is special because it builds trust and makes doing business much improved, and in ways that could never be achieved in just cold negotiations.  We are happy to work with this artisan family, and they are proud to make us high quality beautiful products. 

Anyway the next morning (this morning) we needed to be up at 4am.. to get to the airport in time for a 7.15am short flight from Kathmandu to Varanasi... 

It was a small aircraft with propellers. Buddha air.. very nice friendly staff, and as we lifted out of Kathmandu, we caught a glimpse of a majestic Mount Everest catching the rising sun. 
In Varanasi, we were the only international flight at that time, so quickly through immigration, and luggage already on the belt.. outside in an overcast but humid morning Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) was waiting for us. He has a car and driver, and we went to the Radisson Hotel.. too early in the morning to check in, so I'm writing this newsletter in the lobby.. shortly we have an appointment with a silk manufacturer.. 

Meanwhile in the UK..
Halloween is creeping up fast.. always lots of great deals for you..
Lots of new products also... including a rather interesting massage tool..

Namaste.. peace and love

More updates from India next week.

David

title: Explaining China
content_html:
Greetings from AW new HQ at Europa Way Sheffield.

Last week I was telling you about our first days at the new warehouse, and how it looks from the eagle's view office I'm using. If you missed it you can check it out here.


Since then the pace has been full on relentless, the task at hand is biblical - it's massive - it's virtually Christmas, on top of a major move on top of a huge backlog of deliveries coming in.
The warehouse guys have been working mad-crazy-hours for days on end. We started the week 1500 orders behind, and despite best efforts we are ending it still 1300 behind. Quite simply as many orders come as we can ship out.
Some of the guys have worked every day including Saturday and Sunday for the last 14 days.. and 12 hour days. They are looking ragged and blurry eyed.. poor old Jacob who books orders and sticks despatch labels on your parcels looks at me through shrunken eyes, how are you doing mate? - I ask.. he shrugs and says we have to just do it. You are not working this weekend Jacob, I tell him, get some rest.
I realise if you are waiting for your order, letting poor old Jacob recover is not much comfort to you. You just want your delivery and quite right, so this weekend we still have an emergency shift..
Next week we will have more packing benches, more order pickers and more of the products will be booked into locations.. meaning capacity will increase.. please bear with us as we get through this..  
Thank you for your support .


Meanwhile this strange life goes on. News of Donald Trump and his wife getting the "China virus" as he likes to call it seems in retrospect an obvious outcome.  This stoking of China hatred is terrible and as bad as Hitler stoking hatred of Jews and Polish people.  

How the most practical down-to-earth decent people on earth (yes I'm talking about you Germans) could fall for this brain manipulation and be pulled into an evil war now seems unbelievable. But the more we learn about behavioural science the more we learn that human brains can be pretty easy to control. 
All this anti-China retric right now is worrying, regular readers will know that my wife is Chinese and works for AW as our China agent. I haven't seen her since the 15th January - when she left Europe to go home for Chinese New Year.. and we know what happened since then. One lady wrote to me asking why we still buy from China? Given all the human rights abuses going on in that country, how could we support such a country. I have a long and a short answer to that.. if you want to read the long version, I have put up a page here: Trading with China.  But the short simple answer is that the CCP - The Chinese Communist Party, run China, they are a subset of the Chinese people and are the ones who should be held accountable for human rights violations. Not.. I would argue the lady who makes our reed diffuser flowers, or the bright young guy who designs and makes our atomisers, or the family that produce soap flowers.  At AW we have always been pleased to deal with the small family business, and these people we can trust to be good to their staff to set high standards.. it's not their fault, heavens there is no democracy there so they can't even vote the CCP out of business. So that's why we still want to support our Chinese artisans.



Regular readers will remember when Tomas and I was in Nepal.. it seems like years ago. We ordered lots of things from three new suppliers.. stock from Nepal generally has to come by air since it is a land-locked country. But with coronavirus, hitting just as our orders were ready to ship - the airport closed. Stock was stranded there for months. In one way it was a blessing, because if it had come on time it could have been lost in the fire. In the end we sent it by truck, down the mountains, across India and it sailed from Kolkata port, finally arriving recently. Hemp bags, amazing.. beautiful brass and copper bracelets.. see below, I'm so excited to see it. If it sells well we will be happy to re-order to support the artisan families of Nepal.
See below.


Take care - stay safe.
More news next week.


David

title: In China.. Long Time No See!
content_html:
Greetings from Dongxiang City, China

Happy May Day Weekend.. hope you have Spring in the air and a Spring in your step.
I'm in Dongxiang City, which certainly does, it's a small up and coming city close to the hometown village of my wife. It's a friendly and well kept place, everyone seems to know each other.. I'll explain why below.
Last week I was telling you about my arrival in China at Shanghai, where I met up with Coco (my wife and your China agent) and we hung out in the coolest (we think) neighbourhood in Shanghai - I was telling you about the profound changes there.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

From Shanghai we took the fast train to Yiwu, travelling in business class it was super pleasant. Airline style reclining seats, loads of space, free snacks, fruit and soft drinks and almost flying across the country on overhead rails at 300+ km/h. Yiwu station used to be a hassle where you shuffled sheeplike through tunnels and turnstiles to get out and then had to hustle for a taxi. Now there is a large underground taxi stand directly beneath the station, and a super efficient queuing system, within two minutes you are on the way to town. 

Most people in China (including Coco) will tell you that despite covid and everything else things are getting better and better in China. In many many ways things are getting better since I was last here.. but some things are not.
It was amazing to be reunited with my wife and her son, wife and kids.. who live in a new super modern, hi-tech apartment on the outskirts of Yiwu. They relocated during the pandemic and this of course is (apart from video tours) my first sight of them and the apartment. There are forty low rise blocks - seven floors each in the development. Underground parking and beautiful gardens between the blocks. It's maybe (by my estimate) about 10% occupied - although if you ask the sales office they tell you everything sold out. The super posh development next door is also sold out but I can see almost no lights on at all... strange.


The big problem I have is internet connection.. it was always a bit of a problem in China but the solution was to use a VPN to get round the fire walls.. now I'm fighting a running battle all the time to get connected to the internet.. I have five devises, two sim cards, two VPN's hotlinks to Coco's mobile, and of course the house Wifi.. Now even with the VPN connected I can lose connection to google after a few minutes, (BBC in seconds) and the connection will drop totally.. often I'm offline (outside China) totally for hours at a time. Someone told me that it's reginal - the fire wall policy is dictated nationally but different places interpret it harshly or softly. And this is true. 

So one of the first jobs is to connect with our old suppliers, and many of them have showrooms in or around the massive Yiwu market. 88,000 showrooms under one roof.. it's mind boggling huge.. but organised into Area's specialising in various (what they call) small commodities. Area 1 and the main entrance to the whole grand place - It houses on the ground floor the cheap and tacky plastic flower department, one floor up is hairbands, scrunchies and small flashing objects department. On the third floor is the home of general giftware, and all things bad taste. The top floor is more posh with big flashy show rooms for the big flashy companies. 


Haha - I'm kind of exaggerating - in amongst the plastic and bad taste are some very arty and ethical family businesses many of which we have done good business with for over ten years. Regular readers will know we avoid the faceless factories accessed only via agents, and try to deal with real people.. like our lovely Soap Flower lady.. Xiao Pao who works exclusively with just a couple of Japanese companies and Ancient Wisdom.


We also went to visit Tina and her arty husband (Tina is the boss) who make quite a lot of the gemstone jewellery we sell. They closed the showroom in the market in the pandemic, and now just work from the factory come studio, where they work hard at making new designs and mostly market to the Chinese market online. Their biggest customer outside China is AW.. and we spent a day with them and in the evening had a local Yiwu food meal. It was really nice to catch up.


The first words every one exclaims is "Haojiu bujian"  or Long Time No See! And they certainly seem very pleased to see me.
Many suppliers are telling us that the Europe and USA trade has dropped by 80% but Middle Eastern, African and Russian trade is replacing it. The type of products on display in the showrooms reflect this.. to western eyes bad taste and golden flashy stuff is back front and centre. Massive wheels are moving, who knows how a new world order will pan out. 

Now we just arrived in Dongxiang city, five hours drive down the G60 - it's a major holiday (May 1st) and we wanted to get here before the massive traffic. When I first came here it was a poor backwater city with muddy streets and poor lighting, that very rarely saw westerners, I was spectacularly strange, and quickly became famous in town - haha drawing crowds of people who wanted to try out their English with me. Now the city has a beautiful lake with a park, wide clean streets and smart shops.. lots of good restaurants. In the evening families, kids and old people hang out on the brightly lit streets chatting and playing.. Coco knows many people - the ones that like her sisters and parents have moved from the villages to the city and bought smart apartments. Many have small businesses and trade seems good. I was the first western customer to come in the shop.. I was granted "Friends discount" and treated like a royal visitor. 

There is clearly a lot of new money in Dongxiang - Porches and Mercs are common.. nice restaurants and expensive shops - all despite the pandemic. But I quickly realise why.. this city main factories are medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.. I let you figure out what happened.

Anyway more news next week.

Hope you have a wonderful May Day and may spring sunshine bless you and your business.

David (and Coco) from China.

title: Dream come true..
content_html:
Greetings from Spain
Here in Spain it is almost Christmas.. Three Kings day is on the 6th January. And the traditional Christmas day for gift giving. It makes more sense when you think about it - the Three Kings or wise men brought gifts and kicked off the whole giving gifts at Christmas thing, and they didn't arrive until a bit later.. They brought gold, frankincense and myrrh, but in Spain they just bring sweets to toss to the crowds of excited children.


Last year (in the last newsletter) I was writing to you from AW HQ in Sheffield, wishing you a (British) Merry Christmas - you can read about it here

So here we are in 2020. All nice round numbers, and kind of clear thinking ring to it..
Of course I wish all our customers, subscribers, suppliers, staff, competitors - anyone who reads this newsletter - all the very best for the coming year, heck the coming decade.
The beginning of the year is always the time I sit with the managers in the various parts of the AW business.. and make bold ambitious plans for the year ahead. But it is 2020 - the start of a decade so this calls for an even bigger and more grand vision. So, my friends how will the next ten years pan out? 

Are you making plans? 
How do you make plans? How do you make grand plans.. that can plot out a ten year future. I'm talking here about business..
Well I think you start by looking back, back.. to see how things were 10 years ago. Gordon Brown was PM in the UK. Bad Romance - Lady Gaga was blaring out everywhere, Netflix was still two years away, Instagram had not yet been born.
At AW we had just moved to a new modern warehouse, about 30 staff and had launched our own warehouse in China. Today there are about 100 staff, warehouses in Slovakia, Spain, Indonesia and customer database of over 200,000 - supplying independent (in the main) gift-shops across Europe. 
How did that happen? 
As you have heard me say - and I think this applies to every business.. It's about the PRODUCT.. You can have the best marketing, the best customer service, flashy everything, but if your product is fake or not good then the foundation of the business is flawed.
Sure you can survive with teams of high pressure salespeople, you can even grow with hype and dubious marketing, but long term it's the right product at the right price that makes a business scale upwards. At AW we don't have salespeople, (strange I know) so the products have to work for themselves.
So how does this impact the BIG PLAN?
More focus on the product, more design, more working with artisans and producers to develop the gift products that your customers like. We believe the trends now are for less plastic, more artisan, more natural. Watch out for AW-Earth range.
So we are making big plans to increase capacity and products at our aromatherapy and soap factory in Sheffield, source the best products from more places (Nepal & Morocco are new) and we of course need your valuable feedback to guide the directions we move in.
Plus more ways to help you our customers do better.. thinking of improved drop-shipping, ways for you to sell on Facebook & Instagram with ease.  More White Label products.. what's that? It's products that are unlabelled so you can make them your own brand, or localise them, more gift packaging for the same reasons. 
For your plan.. just dream big.. how many people / shops / sales will you have in 10 years. Close your eyes and imagine what everyone is doing in that business. If you don't have a dream - how can you have a dream come true?

If you are planning to grow your business this next year and beyond, then look no further than Ancient Wisdom. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. there is a backlog of orders, but we are working hard to get them turned round. Over Christmas two containers arrived, these with Spring stock and there is some great new stuff. 
Check out the deals below and order early to be sure of stock ahead of Valentines season.

Wishing you the biggest of big plans and great success for 2020 and beyond.

Take Care

David

title: Fast Feng Shui
content_html:
Last week I was telling you Children's Day here in China... Read below
So here I am back in Yiwu, China. We have an office and warehouse (and now a small factory) here so I'm often in this town. For those new to this newsletter, or have not come across this Chinese city before: Yiwu is a trader's paradise. 80,000 factories have showrooms in this city - they have a market for every small commodity you can imagine. From scarves to socks, to silly pens.
The other day I visited the main gift-ware market, it is maybe 3 months since I was last there, so it's interesting to see just how many new items have appeared, and which ones have disappeared. Only by been a regular can you see such things. A lot has happened in three months, the Chinese currency has shifted 10% and the shipping costs have doubled, wages have increased 20% meaning cheap and cheerful things are much less viable. So like little whippets they are reinventing themselves with higher value designer type items.
One thing is for sure the world is changing fast, exciting times. I read about a very small chain of Chinese Feng Shui shops that made over a million pounds in Singapore last year, they are floating on the London stock exchange (at a lucky 8p of course) and coming to Europe and opening up across China.
I think that's very interesting, there's money in Feng Shui, retailing is not dead. But more precisely specialist retail is not dead because it marries well with a web-shop. People love specialists, and an enthusiastic is naturally endearing. In the future I see retailers specialising more and more.
Feng Shui Shop - Retro Jewellery Shop - Ethnic Soft Furnishing Shop - Everything Lavender Shop - Funky Collectables Shop -
Like the Chinese we need to reinvent ourselves quickly..
More thoughts and news next week.. from China.
Regards
David

title: David's AW News: StrangeThings
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China


Hope you are doing well!
Last week I was telling you about the Muggy weather and Mooncakes here in China. If you missed it you can catch up here. We are still eating the mooncakes. And still in Yiwu city.
The weather has strangely cooled dramatically.. 15c drop in a day. 
We have been working crazy here, running around working down our wish list but also happening on some new products that you are absolutely going to swoon over.
Tomas and Coco are an ace team.. making lots happen. I'm just the spreadsheet guy :/
Yesterday Coco loaded two containers in one day.. working late into the night. So Tomas and I were able to focus on our orders and get organised. 
On the same day in India.. Mr Chatterjee loaded a container and Ringo in Bali also.. his team always sends me a picture when they finish.. 
Looking cool and our head of security.. Pupim the dog.

China drama - the end of the world as we know it.
Coco told me that the dramatic change in temperature is messing with nature in China. This time of year the highly fragrant Osmanthus Fragrans or Tea Olive tree blossoms across China giving off a jasmine like fragrance.  Except this year this late blossoming tree just didn't blossom. And apparently that is a sign that the world will end soon.
The tree that did not blossom. Strange no?

Indian drama - money in a black hole
Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) is in a flap, the flow of money to India to fund the artisans that supply us came to an unexpected and unexplained halt. Mr Chatterjee and his son are our agents in India and deal with the small artisan businesses that we like to trade with. An Indian major holiday is coming up, and most small companies pay holiday money at this time, so there is a big rush to finish orders and get paid. But a lump of €29,000 in that supply line had gone missing. Chatterjee started to ring alarm bells more than a week ago, and then it seemed no money was arriving. Adam, our financial controller, was chasing, but he put it: total radio silence. 
I don't want to tell you the bank's name, but one of the biggest, you can guess. Almost two weeks waiting for the money and nothing, nada, zilch in the way of communication. I called our bank manager directly and left answer phone messages. Finally he called me back.. well it's not his personal fault so no point in getting angry, but it turns out that the reference number used on this payment was similar to a sanctioned Russian business. Apparently lots of international payments have been thrown into limbo, and the staff checking them are in no rush. As I write this the money is still blocked.. we are currently being asked to prove that nice Mr Chatterjee is not a Russian gangster.. it's a strange world..

Talking about strange things.. Yiwu wholesale market has everything you can imagine (80,000 showrooms).. but I was amused to see Trump playing cards and fake money on sale..
Check that out! 

Back in the UK.. lots of Indian stock has arrived. Rodrigo and his team are working very hard to get everything online.
With less than 90 days until Christmas.. now is the time to stock up.

And if you are passing by why not call in to our Showroom Open Week.. lots of things happening.
Anyway, there's a lot to do..
Wishing you a wonderful weekend, and (if the world doesn't end) more news next week.

Take care
David
