title: Monkey Business
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

I hope you are doing well and trade is good as we head to Christmas.
There has been some much delayed stock finally arriving in our warehouse., Stock from India, China and Morocco has all recently arrived. Check out the details below. 
Meanwhile this week we shipped two containers from our warehouse in Bali now on the way to the UK. Including new stock recently ordered, which must be the fastest turnaround ever in Bali. although when they will arrive in Blighty is anyone's guess.

It was just the 11th of the 11th and this means different things in different places. 11's day or singles day in China is a kind of valentines day for people with erm no valentine. It's also metamorphosed into the equivalent of Black Friday and the best day to go shopping. 
In the UK, Commonwealth countries and parts of Europe it's Remembrance day. Here in Bali it's falling on the day after Galungan  there (Christmas Day). So in theory I had a two days holiday.. 

Even here it's making the news. The monkey business that UK politicians are getting up to. Everyone is asking me what I think of Boris and crew. I can't help thinking that when our leaders are dodgy, it gives a degree of license to the type of person who is prone to be dodgy to act more so. So a kind of rot sinks in. It's almost embarrassing to be British. We do a lot of business on trust, and being British is a brand that people trust. A good advantage over some other nationalities. But that is being eroded.

Last week I was telling you about Week 3 in Bali and almost getting washed away.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Well now it's week 4, and I'm happy to report things are progressing quickly. We have formally taken on Bondan - and he joins the team as an assistant to Ringo.
I took Bondan and his wife Debbie out for a meal to celebrate.. They were recently married so getting a proper job is jolly useful at this time.


Bondan is a super bright talented guy and I feel sure he will be a big help to Ringo and an asset to AW.
He has already got to grips with redesigning packaging, and had meetings with the box company. And lot's more besides.


Bali is full of these Penjars - they help the spirits come to earth.. even our warehouse has one.

On Wednesday it was the first Galungan day in Bali, it will last 10 days. They did tell me I needed to get up at 4am if I wanted to see some ceremonies in the streets..And of course I overslept and missed all that.  
At 8am - I thought let's go for a walk through the streets of Ubud.. things must still be happening. I got that wrong.. it was a ghost town, nobody nowhere, nothing open, nothing happening. So I just carried on walking.. There are two main streets in Ubud that both drop down off the through road by the Palace and Market. One is called Jalan Monkey Forest, and the other Jalan Hanoman. Jalan means "Street" and also "to walk" in Indonesian.. Both loop round and end up at the legendary Monkey forest park area.  You will know that Hanuman is the Hindu Monkey god.. so both streets are very monkey themed.  I decided to jalan-jalan (walk) down Hanoman and back up Monkey Forest. 
Half way down Hanoman the only person I met was this guy..



He is helping himself to the offerings that have been made all along the street on those 4am ceremonies that I had missed. Now if you have been to Ubud you will know that around the Monkey Forest entrance are lots of monkeys, but beyond 50 meters or so you never see monkeys. This little fellow was a long way from home.
Just then I became aware of a frantic comotion, some guy tumbled out an avenue with a gun, some other folks waving long bamboo sticks about and up above a swarm of monkeys big and little all moving the same way.. bouncing off roofs, running along telephone cables some along the ground. What's going on? It was like a monkey invasion. 
The guy with the gun said to me, Don't worry I'm not killing them, it's blanks, I just want to scare them away because they cause lots of damage when they are like this.
Later I learned that there are about 350 monkeys living in the forest and they are usually well fed by the tourists that buy bananas and fruits to give them. Since the park has been closed for about 20 months, they haven't been fed so well. 
They certainly did look a lot skinnier than I remember.. and that day taking advantage of the lack of traffic and people they had gone on a daring raid en-mass uptown to feast on the fresh offerings. 
Here is the little video I shot at the moment..


After I walked all the way down to the Monkey Forest main entrance.. normally swarming with monkeys. This morning not one to be seen. 
That area in normal times is abuzz with activity, the gift shops and cafes opposite are alive with customers. Now sadly all closed down, and actually falling down as the jungle and the monkeys do damage. It's very sad.


Monkey Forest entrance.. no monkeys.

So that was my little adventure on my day off. A little sad, but hopefully things will improve. The manager at my hotel told me that funds have been found to properly feed the monkeys, because without them Ubuds main attraction will not recover.

Since then we have been working hard and so many projects are coming together.. It's really exciting, and very rewarding bringing much needed business to both our long term suppliers and quite a few new family businesses.
More updates next week.

Take care, stay safe and remember to be kind to someone today.

David

I can't help thinking that when our leaders are dodgy, it gives a degree of license to the type of person who is prone to be dodgy to act more so. So a kind of rot sinks in. It's almost embarrassing to be British. We do a lot of business on trust, and being British is a brand that people trust. A good advantage over some other nationalities. But that is being eroded. Last week I was telling you about Week 3 in Bali and almost getting washed away.. if you missed it you can catch up here . Well now it's week 4, and I'm happy to report things are progressing quickly. We have formally taken on Bondan - and he joins the team as an assistant to Ringo. I took Bondan and his wife Debbie out for a meal to celebrate.. They were recently married so getting a proper job is jolly useful at this time. Bondan is a super bright talented guy and I feel sure he will be a big help to Ringo and an asset to AW. He has already got to grips with redesigning packaging, and had meetings with the box company. And lot's more besides. Bali is full of these Penjars - they help the spirits come to earth.. even our warehouse has one. On Wednesday it was the first Galungan day in Bali, it will last 10 days. They did tell me I needed to get up at 4am if I wanted to see some ceremonies in the streets..And of course I overslept and missed all that. At 8am - I thought let's go for a walk through the streets of Ubud.. things must still be happening. I got that wrong.. it was a ghost town, nobody nowhere, nothing open, nothing happening. So I just carried on walking.. There are two main streets in Ubud that both drop down off the through road by the Palace and Market. One is called Jalan Monkey Forest, and the other Jalan Hanoman. Jalan means "Street" and also "to walk" in Indonesian.. Both loop round and end up at the legendary Monkey forest park area. You will know that Hanuman is the Hindu Monkey god.. so both streets are very monkey themed. I decided to jalan-jalan (walk) down Hanoman and back up Monkey Forest. Half way down Hanoman the only person I met was this guy.. He is helping himself to the offerings that have been made all along the street on those 4am ceremonies that I had missed. Now if you have been to Ubud you will know that around the Monkey Forest entrance are lots of monkeys, but beyond 50 meters or so you never see monkeys. This little fellow was a long way from home. Just then I became aware of a frantic comotion, some guy tumbled out an avenue with a gun, some other folks waving long bamboo sticks about and up above a swarm of monkeys big and little all moving the same way.. bouncing off roofs, running along telephone cables some along the ground. What's going on? It was like a monkey invasion. The guy with the gun said to me, Don't worry I'm not killing them, it's blanks, I just want to scare them away because they cause lots of damage when they are like this. Later I learned that there are about 350 monkeys living in the forest and they are usually well fed by the tourists that buy bananas and fruits to give them. Since the park has been closed for about 20 months, they haven't been fed so well. They certainly did look a lot skinnier than I remember.. and that day taking advantage of the lack of traffic and people they had gone on a daring raid en-mass uptown to feast on the fresh offerings. Here is the little video I shot at the moment.. After I walked all the way down to the Monkey Forest main entrance.. normally swarming with monkeys. This morning not one to be seen. That area in normal times is abuzz with activity, the gift shops and cafes opposite are alive with customers. Now sadly all closed down, and actually falling down as the jungle and the monkeys do damage. It's very sad. Monkey Forest entrance.. no monkeys. So that was my little adventure on my day off. A little sad, but hopefully things will improve. The manager at my hotel told me that funds have been found to properly feed the monkeys, because without them Ubuds main attraction will not recover. Since then we have been working hard and so many projects are coming together.. It's really exciting, and very rewarding bringing much needed business to both our long term suppliers and quite a few new family businesses. More updates next week. Take care, stay safe and remember to be kind to someone today. David

title: David's AW News: Back to work. Back to dreaming. Let’s make 2026 a good one.
content_html:
Hello,

Yes.. here we are.. Back to work… and back to some new possibilities in 2026.

I'm in Spain at the moment, in the midst of Storm Francis (it's blowing a gale outside). My phone just made the most alarming noise.. a Civil Protection Alert and warning not to go outdoors. I see that snow is falling across much of the UK.. But despite the extreme weather (and even more extreme news) there’s something quietly powerful about these first few days in the year.

The whole year lies ahead, and for a brief window we’re allowed to dream & plan — not just about what we sell, but why we do it, and where we want this year to take us. All I can say is don't be afraid to think big. 

At Ancient Wisdom, we’re starting 2026 (despite the weather drama) with a sense of calm optimism. And BIG plans. 

It seems to me that Retail is changing (again), but that isn’t bad news. Independent retailers, agile businesses, and people like you willing to try new models are finding real opportunities — especially where story, ethics, kindness, and flexibility matter more than brute scale. 

This year we are focusing on our key brands, this protects you from the bottom end of the market (and the loophole traders) - you have my word that we will never sell these brands directly to your customers. AW is all about B2B - retailing is your part. Not all wholesalers hold to this ethic. 

Agnes & Cat - Hop Hare - Ancient Witch - Mandala Leaves - Nomed Sari.  find these brands and more exclusively at AW.

Last Year's TOP new products in reverse order HERE.


And the year ahead?

We already have a strong pipeline in motion:
We have ALL NEW product groups on the way, deeper artisan stories, improved stock flow across UK and EU warehouses, and a growing focus on dropshipping as a low-risk, high-flexibility way to trade — whether you’re adding it alongside a physical shop, or building something entirely online.

Dropshipping in 2026 isn’t about shortcuts. It’s about choice:
• choosing what to list
• choosing how much risk to carry
• choosing how fast you want to move

We’re investing heavily behind the scenes to make that easier — better systems, better content, clearer data, and products that actually convert once they’re live.

Above all, we’re staying true to what’s always mattered to us:
good design, fair pricing, reliable stock, and long-term relationships.

Thank you for trading with us — whether you’ve placed one order or hundreds. We genuinely appreciate it.

So here’s to a fresh start, a bit of dreaming, and some good planning.

Let’s make this year a good one — together.

Warm regards,

David
& the Ancient Wisdom team

PS. If you’re thinking about trying something new this year — a new product range, a dropshipping experiment, or a different way of trading — now is the perfect time. We’re here to help.

title: Our Eclectic Home and Back To School Offer
content_html:
Greeting from Malaga, Spain where I have just landed after a brief visit to AW Sheffield. Last week I was telling you about our Ancient Wisdom wedding couple.
You can read it here.
Weddings don't get more eccentric and eclectic (I love that word) than theirs. But then any given day at AW can be pretty eclectic. Probably because our product range is stuffed with a load of esoteric and mystical stuff, our customers are also a pretty strange and eclectic bunch. When I say "strange" I mean that in a good way.
The other day I'm just stood in our order processing department. It was buzzing, every phone ringing, warehouse staff running in an out like bumble bees, and stuff been sorted out at a rapid pace. We have been rather busy this week, a short week because of the bank holiday, sort staffed because of the holiday season and a record number of orders received. I know we are a bit behind - so please bare with us. Honestly we are working hard to catch up.
Back to eclectic.. I was stood there just watching and listening to what was going on. If those government spy's are eaves dropping on our offices they may be a bit confused.
Kerry; (across the office) "I have The Arc Angel on the phone, can we add a pack or "Let Angels Pass" simmering granules. Ursula: "There's someone from Another Realm in reception"
Bruno: "I think the postcode for Cloud Nine is wrong.. Jessica: The courier can't find the entrance for "Heavens Gate".. Zoe: "Have you got that message from "Whispering Angels"?
No, it's really like that. And those really are the names of our customers. :)
Crrrrumbs! Have you noticed it's practically September.. which means it's almost Christmas. Action stations.
Actually this year I think we are more prepared than ever before. Thanks to a ton of hard work from Craige (warehouse manager) and his motley crew. The steady stream of containers (arriving for the busy season) have been offloaded and sorted and put away ready for the rush. Warehouse systems are go! We have more new and eclectic stock than ever before. The best ever deals, and faster selling lines, scummy soaps and bath-bombs etc etc.. You can't get better. (even if I say so myself :) )
Until next week take care.
David
PS
ec·lec·tic (iˈklektik) Adjective: Deriving ideas, style, or taste from a broad and diverse range of sources.

title: The Adventure Continues
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

Where it's all happening at pace. Last week I was telling you about why we bought a beach bar, and if you missed that you can catch up here.

We also announced that this month we will repatriate all profits from products sourced from Turkey back to Turkey to help the earthquake relief . One family that produces the Kilm rugs we sell is homeless and living in his car. Our lovely agent contacted him with an offer of help, and he told us that he was relatively OK but local people actually need food, so he would spend our donation feeding people. That's just one heartbreaking story.. she has been working tirelessly identifying personal contacts in need that in small ways we can help.- even visiting a refugee centre personally and offering to help.
She has sent money to six different families in six different cities. Each time sending me awful details of the situation and a copy of the bank transfer.

Thank you to everyone stocking Turkish products. A special thanks to our Agent Hatice, for actually making a difference.  

Meanwhile here in Bali, we are cracking on making things happen. 

The beach bar project, which is being converted into a cool office space to attract young talented people - is at that stage where everything has been ripped apart, apparently a big mess but actually organised chaos as we put it all back together. Tomas has been buying just the right shades of paint ordering big rattan lamps, the plans are set and a team of young industrious guys are on it.  Very soon it will be cool.


In the meantime we have been brainstorming and working on the basics of the product that will leap like a magic from this space and revolutionise your business.
But of course - as I say often - the most important thing is the giftware products and we spend the mornings still doing that job.. the Lombok Vases arrived in the UK and early feedback is that people love them, they are selling well, so we are quickly adding to the range. The boss, who is a lovely gentle guy with kind intelligent eyes, came to our office in Sukawati with samples straight off the boat from Lombok.


Sitting on the floor, that's our guy from Lombok, Ringo and in the back Bondan and Raul. Tomas taking a selfie as the deal is done.

Soon the adventure continues - we have to work hard another week and then soon we head to Nepal.. our first visit since before the pandemic.
After putting the wheels in motion here, we will be 100% focused on Nepal and India products for a full month, after which the plan is to return here by which time everything should be in place to rock and roll.
Stay tuned..

Once again thank you for all your support.
Take care - wishing you a wonderful weekend.

David 

PS
Please consider our Turkish products, Thank you.

title: Fighting the Bullies..😉
content_html:
How are you doing?

 

Another week has flown by, it seems at another level of stress, but maybe there is light at the end of the tunnel..

Last week I was telling you about how very often the "Devil is in the Detail" and how quite clearly our leaders are not quite getting those details..

With monumental consequences we all have to deal with later.. anyway if you missed it you can read about it here.


With international trade between GB and the rest of Europe (including NI) in a state of turmoil, details as I mentioned in the last newsletter are getting more and more complicated.

It's looking like the only solution for businesses like AW to become almost two.. one in the EU and one out.. I know one of the other UK wholesalers has just signed up for a warehouse in Poland and others are in the process. 

In this turmoil there are bad actors who seek to take advantage. 

There is a big story that has to break at sometime about trademarks and copyright.    Before Brexit you could easily register a trademark across Europe, now of course you need to do it in the UK and the EU, double the cost and effort. And expiring trademarks are vulnerable to be exploited.. be warned. 

A few weeks back I was telling you about "Whales" - this was before the news about the GameStop share squeeze.. but it amounts to the same type of bad behavior. Customers often complain that products go out of stock too quickly, and sometimes this is because some annoying Whale is buying up all the stock of a particular product type. Think about it with the niche like products that the giftware trade sells, some products might only be imported by a handful of companies into Europe, and supply lines are really slow right now.. so if you are an online retailer with good exposure.. If you can buy up all the available stock you can squeeze out the competition and ease up prices.. evil no? I can't name names but one very big online company (you can hazardian a guess) has been accused of such dodgy behavior. 

Another annoying Whale like company took it to a whole new level recently.. I'm probably going to get sued but I will tell you the story anyway because it makes me very angry (like we don't have enough things to deal with right now).

This company managed to take out an EU trademark for the term "Backflow" (it's a generic word so probably challengeable at some cost and time) while at the same time buying up all the stock of backflow incense and burners they could find. They then started via a high power (but lowlife) lawyer to send nasty cease and desist letters to everyone they could find selling "Backflow" products with a demand for €5000 or more as settlement. The letter even warns about changing the name not being an option to avoid paying them. Of course if you are just a small business owner already struggling to survive with just online trade this is scary. 




Tomas talked to the boss there long and intense conversations, explaining that we didn't think it was a nice thing to do. Pointed out we and others have been selling backflow incense burners for years before them. But no joy.. the guy just said he would stop it only if we gave him exclusivity in his country. He pointed out how much business he was doing with us and how much more he could do.. 

Tomas sent him a nice whats app asking him to cease and desist sending cease and desist notices out to poor defenceless retailers. He asked for an email confirming this so we could put the minds of retailers at ease.

 

Now I'm always happy and proud to be a giftware trader..  giving a gift (you have heard me say) is nothing less than an act of love.. so we folk in the gift business should and are humbled and honoured to be part of this process. We sell  beautiful things to lovely people who help their customers to bring more love into this world. 

 

This guy finally responded by telling us to get lost. And then changed his profile picture of (I assume him) pointing a massive gun, wearing shades,looking like a mafia boss. 

So I told Tomas that means.. we cannot supply his company anymore. It's very rare we sack customers.. but this is one of those times. 

Of course he was pretty mad.. and arrogant.. he can buy elsewhere, he will import from China and India himself.. etc. well I say..good luck to him.. 

Please tell me if you think we did the right thing or not?  If you have received such a letter please forward it to us.. as far as I know they are not targeting GB customers.  

I know most of the other gift wholesalers in Europe will not like this and I have had offers already to share the legal costs of challenging the trademark.. but this is another problem we don't need right now.

 

 But meanwhile things are looking up.. those 29 pallets I told you about last week trapped in Madrid because of some bottles of aromatherapy grade olive oil - base oil. Finally Spanish customs saw the irony of trying to block an import of their own nations product.. That shipment arrived in our warehouse in Malaga today.. Hopefully the next shipment will be easier, we are applying for a food distributor licence and a cosmetic license to ease the way further. 

Another 32 pallets destined for our Slovakia warehouse left on Tuesday and with minimal fuss arrived on Thursday, still with considerable extra expenses but we are finding ways to gradually smooth those Brexit bumps a bit.

 

And I was telling you last week that heaps of stock was arriving.. including some new products see below.

It's all go! - very soon it will be Mother's Day.. then Easter.. shops opening hopefully on 12th April, and holidays will be the Great British holiday.. which means not so many people travelling abroad. So maybe good for UK trade.

 

Next week I will be explaining to you our crafty plan to help you (the independent retailer) fight back against the big retailers like Amazon and those nasty whales.. 

Until then, stay safe and be happy.

 

Peace & Love.

 

David

title: On the Wild Side
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal.


Yes, we returned to Kathmandu, our first visit after the pandemic. This city went through a nightmarish time and is now still getting itself together. 
Last week we were in Bali and I was telling you what things cost in Indonesia.. If you missed it you can catch up here. 

Since then we took a Batik Air flight to Kuala Lumpur and a connecting flight to Kathmandu arriving late evening. Our contact in Nepal; Mr Padam, his son and our guy Bryant from the UK who had arrived ahead of us were waiting to greet us outside the airport in the cool mountain air. It was October 2019 the last time I was here.. in those innocent pre-covid days and a totally different age.. 
Tomas has been here with me before, but this is the first buying trip for Bryant and I know he is nervous and excited. Actually, over the last few years, Bryant has been the point of contact at AW for reorders, so Bryant has built up good relations with our suppliers and Mr. Padam our shipping agent here.. now he can meet them in the flesh. We got off to a flying start the first morning when Mr.

Dom, one of our oldest suppliers came to our hotel with a big bag full of all the items he had been working on for AW ahead of our visit.  And boy has he done a good job.. amazingly creative, with some exciting beautiful products exclusively for AW and thus for you.

We have a few suppliers here and the first job was to catch up with them all and see what fresh ideas and products we can find. 
We have suppliers of Tibetan incense, singing bowls, hemp bags, felt products and brass bangles.. And the plan is to increase the products we buy enough to regularly fill a 40ft container that can be shipped by sea via Kolkata port. 
Actually, most exports from Nepal traditionally go by air, because Nepal is of course land-locked and that is a significant extra cost. During the pandemic, the airport closed completely and the only way to ship was by land to India and by sea from Kolkata port.  We (and all exporters) were forced to ship by container even though shipping costs were extremely expensive. New roads opened up and India made it easier to trans-ship to help keep Nepal's economy alive. Now costs are normalising so an opportunity to trade more effectively has opened up. 

But is it possible to find enough good products to achieve that aim? I was a little worried about this.. The area where exporters set up showrooms is also the backpacking area known as Thamel. It had a reputation as a wild place after dark with dodgy dive bars, unsavoury characters trying to con foreigners and drugs freely available. Now the organised begging gangs are gone, a subtle police presence keeps the bad actors away and many trendy bars and boutique hotels and nice restaurants have opened. A portion of the muddy streets have been paved, the pedestrian only area greatly extended since my last visit..  and most importantly many new creative young people are displaying their products in clean modern showrooms.  That said the maze of narrow streets is just as confusing and you can find yourself in pretty rough areas still.  Just wandering around we realise there is huge creativity and endless products - but the only problem is that only eight days to make it all happen is a tall order.. 

A few random images of Thamel life. 
The wild side still exists, the other evening I went alone to a local shop to buy shampoo, and a very polite elderly gentleman in suit and tie, with a leather briefcase approached me . "Excuse me sir", he said with a slight bow, "might you be interested in buying something to smoke", and then listed a variety of herbal products. Cannabis has been illegal here since 1973, but so much part of the culture it seems to be mostly tolerated. I'm told though that tourists can be technically jailed of up to a month for using drugs.




Meanwhile back home in the UK.. great excitement.. we have a new bath bomb product - Gemstone bath bombs are here!! Your customers can take a bath, and find a gemstone, each stone has a different meaning. Add some fizz and find your gemstone wisdom in the bath.. a leaflet explains the meaning of your gemstone.

I just found out a container arrived from Indonesia this morning.. so many more wonders are coming your way.. including a wonderful range of recycled beer bottle products.. from the same supplier as the hugely popular Molton glass on wood.. a new green glass range.. I loved them and hope your customers do also.. beautiful and also great value. 
After Kathmandu we go to India.. the adventure continues. 
More news next week.
Take care

David

title: David's AW News: Kites in Kathmandu
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu


It's been a really interesting week.. here living in the aftermath of the Gen Z revolution. 
Last Friday, I had just arrived and made this YouTube - Meeting the Gen Z ..  and the newsletter for last week here.
Since last week's newsletter, Toni from Spain has arrived. He was a little apprehensive about coming, given all the news. But like me, he is happy to be here.
The manager of the hotel where we are staying told me they had many cancellations. He was so happy that we turned up - we got an upgrade to the best rooms! 
At this time of year, the beginning of the climbing and trekking season, normally they are full.. but at breakfast, we see maybe only two or three other guests. 
The other day, Bicky, our Lokta paper supplier, took us on a trip to a nearby city to visit a ceramics factory.. Bhaktapur - the first time I have been there, they have a place called Pottery Square where local artisans sit and make pottery. But there is so much more in this epic town.  Bichy has friends and relatives in that city, and they all came to meet us. We had a special tour of this beautiful, very historic place, one of Bicky's friends' wife is actually a heritage architect working to restore and maintain the city's heritage. From  a rooftop terrace restaurant, I was admiring a dramatic tiered temple. Which I later learned was a restoration project run by this lady.
Beautiful Bhaktapur

Burned out buildings.
On the way out of Kathmandu, we passed several burned out buildings, others with all the windows smashed in. Bicky showed us we passed the Supreme Court, completely destroyed. He said most people think that was wrong and shouldn't have happened. But there had been a major jailbreak, and he thought it was criminals attempting to destroy records. A small tent has been erected in the grounds, and Bichy told us the most important cases were being held there.  Life is getting back to normal. 
before..
Our taxi driver told us one good thing is that there is no traffic police to annoy him.. and the traffic manages fine (just as bad) but without bad tempered traffic police blowing whistles and directing traffic. The police, who were getting increasingly brutal until the government collectively stepped down and went into hiding, are very thin on the ground now. Instead, army checkpoints and security (but not much on view) keep the peace. Big news here is the Gen Z that started all this are now mobilised to tidy up and fix the damage where they can. Social media is full of posts of police stations being repainted and repaired, street damage being fixed. 

Bhaktapur 
I was surprised - Bhaktapur is not like Kathmandu, it's so calm and peaceful - maybe because of the lack of tourists - but also spotlessly clean and tidy. The people are known to be kind and gentle, and it reflects in the nature of the place. After our VIP tour, we had a nice terrace lunch.. then went to talk to some ceramic factory owners that a Vichy friend knew. 
I have to say they make beautiful ceramics here, but logistically I'm not sure how to bring to Europe and even if they would be competitive in the market. Let me know what you think..
The pottery square is really interesting.. Late afternoon, when it's not too hot, a truck arrives with fresh clay from a local clay pit. All around the sides of the square are tiny artisan studios which take delivery of they clay and, like a public performance, make their particular speciality. Then in the centre of the square is a very rustic public kilm to fire the finished pots. A very ancient tradition that grew out of the towns speciality, which is basically fresh yogurts, or curd as they call it here. Stall and shops all over town sell curds served in chilled clay pots.. very tasty, almost like ice cream but more healthy, I guess. Anyway, the pots are discarded after use.. I watched a guy just making those pots.. out of this ancient art.. 
I'm so happy to discover this place.. artisans heaven.. I think I have enough content to make a YouTube video.. I'll try to upload something later.

Meanwhile in the UK...
Holly and Rodrigo have been busy, and we have a new "Can You Sell This? video.
And the T-shirts that come from Nepal - slow fashion style. Stonewashed Nomad Sari T-Shirts.. 100% Nepali cotton made in Kathmandu, double stone-washed by a lovely local guy, screen printed in a back street studio, labels, final stitching, QC and packing done by the nice Mr Suman. This is not fast fashion, artisan t-shirts bearing our Nomad-Sari (spirit of travel brand)  - on DOUBLE DISCOUNT.. 30% off.  

Also, happening quite a few new products coming online - perfect NEW things for Christmas..
I'm particularly excited by the Animals upside down Shot Glasses Sets.. super decorative and I feel easy to sell as a gift this Christmas.

Here in Nepal, it's actually the festival of Dashain starting now.
It's their biggest festival and has a big kite flying theme.. I can already see the sky filling with playful kites. A tradition of kite flying during the Dashain festival. Kites are flown to mark the end of the monsoon season, signal the gods to stop the rain, and symbolise joy and freedom. Everyone, not just kids, do it, flying kites from their rooftops, and often compete in friendly kite-flying contests. 
Toni and I have already been invited to a rooftop kite party, apparently, there will be beer as well as kites..

Anyway, wishing you all a peaceful and enjoyable weekend.
Namaste from Kathmandu 

David

title: Time to say goodbye
content_html:
Greetings from Central Jakarta

Last week I was telling you about Moonshine and Mystics and our visit to the peaceful town of Sideman. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Coco (my wife and your China agent) has been with me in Indonesia for almost two months.. but the time has come for her to go home. 
We booked flights from Bali to Jakarta and then on to Guangzhou for the 29th August, where Coco will need to do a 7 days quarantine before flying back home to Yiwu..and then probably another 7 days. On Monday we thought we had a full last week to enjoy together in Ubud, but then the long arm of Chinese authoritarianism reached out and buggered up the plan.  News came that in order to board the flight Coco would need a PCR test at a specific location in Jakarta four days before, then if negative need to check into a hotel for three days quarantine and four separate PCR tests. After which she will be taken by bus directly to the flight. 

The zero covid regime in China is serious control freakery, and Coco has been so happy to be free of all that crap.. the 72 hour regular testing.. free to walk around without a mask, free to escape all the mindless rules and regulations now abruptly came to an end.. so on Wednesday she needed to be in Jakarta.. so naturally I came along also.. to say goodbye. 


Coco (in the blue dress) waiting to be tested. 

The testing site was in the carpark of a hospital. It took almost three hours to get tested, because it seemed to me like a mindless confused admin.  Queue to get a ticket, queue to register, queue to get a photo taken, finally queue for the test - both nostrils and throat - deep ouch. Later Coco got a call with instructions to go to a particular hotel.. no choice. I googled it - the reviews don't look good. 

But interestingly most of the people on the flight and in the queue were contract workers working on Chinese projects around Indonesia. Coco has a hobby.. she uploads whimsical videos to Chinese TicTok (Douyin) - it's the same company and logo, but totally unconnected eco-system. Days after arriving in Indonesia in a hotel bar in Surabaya she made a short video about Bintang Beer, pretending to drink from a bottle (she doesn't drink) and the upload went viral..(16k views) since then she has picked thousands of fans mostly Chinese folk in Indonesia, chatting to some of them, they are mostly contractors, and often only had a vague idea of where they were in Indonesia. I think she is pretty unique because there are virtually no tourists from China now.. and the algorithm seems to pull people in the locality.  

Whilst waiting Coco made a little video and later in the day uploaded it.. within minutes 8 people from the queue had messaged, that's me in the video.. I knew I knew you.. and I was two people behind you.. 


I fall asleep, whilst Coco is chatting to her fan club of joiners and electricians. 

11pm 
Coco wakes me up.. 
BIG PROBLEM!!
Despite being told verbally the result was OK, an emailed Positive test has arrived and a message not to go to the quarantine hotel in the morning. 
The situation has gone from difficult to horrible and Coco finds social media stories of people trapped in limbo for months unable to pass the Chinese rigorous test. I phone the clinic hosting the PCR tests and finally get through to someone who tells me that yes the result is borderline, with a CT score of 39, 40 apparently is classified as negative. I ask if we can retest.. yes is possible. So we grab a taxi from the hotel this morning straight to the clinic, not far from our South Jakarta hotel.  The staff there are lovely and kind, and quickly organise everything.  Whilst we are waiting to be tested the airline calls to say it's too late anyway, and she will not be able to join the quarantine program. 
The particular test the Chinese insist on is of course the most expensive, but we pay up, have the test and are outside within a few minutes. The results of this test are slow, maybe we will get a result in the evening or next morning. 

So it looks like 7 days in Jakarta, we can't really go anywhere.. I found an apartment hotel, where we can stay for a week. It's on the 31st floor and there is a view of central Jakarta downtown. Whilst Coco is a little distressed and worried, the good news is she is fine healthwise and we can at least spend another 7 days together. 


Downtown Jakarta is not like Bali..

Back in the UK we have lots of stuff back in stock and a few things running out. It's actually all systems go.

In Slovakia - it's a party weekend, our new warehouse is now totally finished and a delegation from the UK has gone to visit. They are having an official launch party. The idea is our teams can swap ideas and encourage each other as well as bouncing big ideas around and doing some serious bonding. It kicks off this afternoon (friday) and will last all weekend. 
Here are a few pictures added by our on the ground photographer Rodrigo.



I'll report what happens to Coco and me next week.

Hope you are doing well and things are buzzing along..
All the best from Jakarta.

David

title: Bombshell in Spain
content_html:
Greetings from Spain
Where we are busy putting together a new distribution warehouse and team in Málaga. Raul (the IT wizard) is here flown in from KL, Malaysia. Rodrigo had to go back to the UK, Tomas (Marketing wizard)  s here, and Coco - my wife (and our China agent) just arrived. Last week I was telling you about the Emotional Decisions involved in selecting a team, all the interviews and one very sad story.. You can read about it here. We had 947 applications of which we interviewed 47 people, these were whittled down to 12 contenders, of which we needed to select 4 for the launch team.

So my idea was to write the names of the 12 on 12 pieces of A5 paper with a marker pen, together with the key skills, languages spoken, what job they applied for and a hook so we could recall them. The Chatty Guy.. the Architect, the Instagram Girl and so on..  then we put all the pieces of paper on the table and juggled them around to see how they fitted together. All last weekend we debated - Rodrigo, Tomas, Raul and I all having different opinions. Sunday the sun came out, we went to the beach and ate sardines and debated some more.. we kind of decided who the manager should be.. but I woke up on Monday morning feeling it was a bad call, and we had missed a trick.

 Thinking about how the candidates had grasped the AW concept and values, one or two had gotten visibly excited when they understood the concept of what we do. (Which is finding beautiful things to supply to lovely people in the gift trade, who help people buy gifts for loved ones, and we try to do it with integrity and values). Enthusiasm is important - so who was the most grasping of the concept, and excited to work for us..
This rejigged the deck.. and The Chatty Guy came into play.. the team dynamic changed.. by Monday afternoon we had finally got consensus. Rodrigo (now back in the UK) started to call them with the good news, everyone very happy and two available to start right away.
So on Tuesday, The Chatty guy started and The Architect started Wednesday. So Toni and Luis joined the AW family this week, with two more to follow (they had to give notice) over the next two weeks. 

Luis, qualified as an architect, but is happy to join us as the warehouse manager (and some marketing), seems so happy and grateful. He is a big gentle guy, a little shy but clearly quite intelligent. Several times in halting English he has thanked me for the opportunity.
Yesterday he asked me if he could have a private word. I said sure and we stepped out of the office, I noticed he was shaking. "There is something I should have told you at the interview".. he looked pale.. Go on - I said apprehensively, all sorts of things sliding around my brain. "I'm so sorry, I hope it is OK.. Next Saturday the 30th November".. long pause.. gulp.. "I should have told you.. I'm getting Married!"... 
OMG... Is that it?  I blinked a couple of times, smiled and shuck him vigorously by the hand. "Congratulations.. and I guess you need some time off for a honeymoon". "Well two or three days if possible" - he said. Of course, I told him no problem.. lets go see what Tomas thinks..  Tomas laughed immediately and agreed, he can have what time he needs. New wife and a new job.. important to start his new life well.
It's a Bombshell..  but I think this is a good omen for our new company..
I'd like to say AW Artisan is born... but not quite..
We are still working on it.. but a new concept is developing.. where we focus on the Artisan products of Ancient Wisdom. AWArtisan.es will of course be the official and only distributor for all things AW in Spain.. and the authorised supplier of Agnes & Cat in Europe as well as delving into such things as Drop-shipping,  Portugal website and in the near future a French website. title: David's AW News: So Efficient so Slovakian!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.. yes I'm back home for a while.

Last week I was telling you about our beautiful Slovakia warehouse and all those Buddha we have there creating a calm and serene working environment. If you missed it you can catch up here. 

It was amazing working with the Slovakian team.. so organised and efficient. Something about eastern European folk so good at finding the best way to have a smooth workflow. Well done team!



Here me with the Buddha in the outdoor relax zone we have.

On Wednesday I left Tomas and Raul working on the new dropshipping website (update below) and took an early morning taxi from Trnava, Slovakia to Vienna Airport. 

More efficient stuff..

I'm so impressed with the stress free check in experience. No people, just scan your boarding card to get a luggage label, take luggage to the belt, here is the weight shown, scan the luggage tag and boarding card again .. And my luggage is gone. So quick, sweet and easy. All the airlines share the system. Austrian/Eastern Europe efficiency! Amazing. 

Notes about YouTube

I'm very excited about using YouTube to showcase our products as a marketing tool. As you know at AW (from day one) we have never used salespeople that travel the country, never done trade shows - we rely on online marketing, newsletters like this, referrals and Adwords. But with the advent of AI - adwords is fast losing power, now good SEO and Social Media is the way AI finds its sources.  And lets face it, a video is more engaging and informative than a static web page alone. 

So I have been working hard getting young people like Holly and Rodrigo excited and organised to make useful content. 

When you need to research new products to boost sales.. we have a YouTube playlist called:  Can You Sell This? when you have time, get yourself a coffee (or glass of wine) and watch us tell you about our favorite products, get to know the AW team and discover some great (money making) products - that maybe you could sell. 

While in Slovakia with the help of Katrina our very able social media girl there we made some content.. which I'll upload when I get time to YouTube..

But for now we have a new "Can you sell this?" video from Holly in the UK.. showcasing one of my favourite products.. Copper bracelets.. this product just arrived and seems to be trending.. so much so we are already sold out (but more on the way). 



There are so many reasons to sell these fast moving Copper Bracelets - Find out here.

Dropshipping Update

OK full disclosure.. this project has been a massive challenge.. a big investment and I'm sorry if you have been using it and finding bugs.. Thank you for all the constructive feedback guys.. all of it is incredibly helpful...  Please stay tuned and have faith because I believe it will be amazing when it all comes good.

The Shopify API had to be taken offline for new users this week due to reported bugs. Thank you for your patience. I’ve been told our IT team is working around the clock to resolve the issue — please bear with us.

I can see that we have a few super users that have been using it very successfully and orders are flowing through the system. 

You can register here: AW-Dropship.com  and take a gander.. you start by selecting products you think you can sell.. 

Soon we are going to make some exclusive NO BRAINER products that you will not want to miss! 

I'm working on something.. 

Today I'm visiting (my favourite team*) in the AWArtisan office in Malaga.

I'm showing everyone our new YouTube plan.. they are enthusiastic and so creative, already rushing around making content.. just not quite as efficiently as those Slovakians.. haha.

Maybe next week I'll share some of the Spain content.. 

Busy re-organising the showroom.. ready for action!!




So Spanish - so much fun!

Take care - have a lovely weekend!!

David

PS

* That's my favourite team - in Spain..

title: Why Some at Ancient Wisdom Want Brexit Now
content_html:
Greetings from Slovakia

Yes, I'm here at the Eastern Europe HQ in Trnava a pretty town near Bratislava. 
Raul the IT wizard from Kuala Lumpa arrived the same day as me, and Tomas chief marketing Wizard was already here.
So it's a bit of a reunion, working here with Erica and the EU team. 

Last week in the UK HQ and telling you about getting over the Brexit Bump. You can read about it here.
Here in Slovakia, there was great excitement at the approaching Brexit Day, after all the Slovakia distribution centre was born out of Brexit.

It was our own backstop for keeping frictionless trade with our Euro customers. So as the 29th of March approached the team here braced themselves for an influx of migrating customers but the day that never was came and went.
It's as though you have been training for the Olympics, building those muscles, getting ready mentally and physically.. you got the kit all ready to go...  and then at the last moment they cancel it.

But Erica and the team have been developing their own markets for AW range of products. And sales to Slovakia, Czech Republic and Austria are booming.. plus we have an English language site AWGifts.eu that is bringing interesting customers from all sorts of diverse places right across Europe and the world. From Iceland to Spain, from Caribbean islands to Greek Islands. Matej our international manager has the most diverse range of customers.
So AWGifts is growing fast even without Brexit.. up 500% this week. So it's a very dynamic time growing fast is so much fun..

Back in the UK, lots of things are going on.. this week has been a Salt Lamp container, an Indonesian container, an emergency air shipment of the fast-moving Aroma Jewellery amongst other things. It's all happening.
Check out the deals below.. 

Thoughts..
Greta Thunberg.. OMG only 16 and changing the world, quietly determinedly.. Have you seen the Greta Thunberg Ted Talk..? wow I'm so impressed that young lady is beyond remarkable. Mrs May.. are you really so busy with brexit and botched meetings you can't meet and be inspired by this girl.. it's the future. Now more and more people are thinking about a sustainable future thanks to people like this.. Well done Greta.

Talking about saving the planet.. Check out our Cotton bags and Jute bag ranges.. we put them all together in two web pages for you..
They come from our Kolkata supplier.. who right now is being roughed up by the edge of Cyclone Fani, a million people displaced along the Bay of Bengal already.. we send them our best wishes. 
I just spoke to Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) to see if he was OK.. so far so good he says not the worst affected. We are praying.  
We are told using cotton and jute rather than plastic will help our planet.. and right now the very people who make it need saving..

Soooooo many bank holidays... I have already experienced one - it was May Day on 1st of May here, next week we have a bank holiday to commemorate the end of World war 2... on Wednesday. 
In the UK another bank holiday weekend! Hope you are not just mad busy but find time to be still and simply enjoy being with friends and family. 

All the best.. more new next week.

title: I'm just doing my job in Goa
content_html:
Greetings from South Goa, India.
Last week I was telling you about going round and round at the Indian Spring fair in Greater Noida near Delhi. 
I had some problems trying to negotiate a workable price with some of the guys there.. You can read about it here.


Lots people sent me positive feedback but one guy.. I don't really know who.. but somebody with an Indian name came on our online chat system with a massive rant about how I was living in the 9th century and abusing Indians by screwing down the prices to the minimum. He practically accused me of being colonial and abusing India. So sir.. whoever you are.. Calm down dear.. I'm just doing my job. It's very simple, when we find a product we like - we check the market - back in the UK/EU these days there is a market price, if you try and sell higher you won't sell anything. Especially with the Ancient Wisdom online system, we don't employ salespeople who can sell on the back of relationships, and a bit of sales chat.. the sales agents can always get higher prices. But the savvy buyer, and if you are reading this - that's probably you - knows that sales agents cost money and that has to come from somewhere. So to cut a long story short.. we have to get the right price, or there is no business, certainly no repeat business. 

But I understand these guys in the trade-show, they spend a huge amount on getting there and putting on the show - that money has to come from somewhere - and it goes in the prices. It's the same issue as the sales agents. 
Soooo... after the trade show Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) head to Delhi to see our suppliers on the ground. Near the old train station is an old established giftware wholesale trading area, it's a bit wild, first time visitors find it scary. Rickshaws, and cows, and holymen and god knows what is going on here. It attracts some colourful characters from around the world who I suspect are sourcing products other than gift-ware.. erm herbal products.. if you get my drift..
But not far away, within walking distance - if you know how to find it is a different world. The more respectable (and successful) traders have moved to some quieter cleaner streets nearby where larger professional warehouses exist.

Checking the price of products, checking the provenance and doing a deal is fall less stressful and prices are basically right. India is changing and in spite of what you might read lots of things are better. This is one of them.

The five star hotels attract the begging gangs and other bad elements, and the average tourist experience is not good. The tourist trap restaurants are best avoided by simply taking a cab to the South Delhi middle class residential areas. They have great names like.. East of Kailash or New Friends Colony. In the mist of these places you can find leafy squares with funky gift shops, coffee bars and european style restaurants. We went to Block M Greater Kailash which also has a night market. Had dinner in the hippest Italian restaurant with female staff (unheard of a few years ago), a young girl with a guitar singing like an angel and we ate perfect food. After Mr Chatterjee likes a whiskey or two so we asked if there was a bar.. now I can remember when a bars in Delhi were dirty dark guilt ridden places, hidden away and strictly men only. We found ourselves in trendy friendly place, live music again, Indian folk singers and lots of youngster having a chilled time - even shock horror - a middle class lady enjoying a glass of wine on her own - whilst waiting for friends. We had our whiskey soaked up the vibe and headed back to the hotel.. Whilst waiting for the taxi, I realised I didn't have my phone. Moment of panic.. I turn to go back and almost bu

mp into to a guy running round the corner. Sir, thank goodness I found you.. please come back, we have your phone. 
Mr Chatterjee 50% couldn't believe it, only a couple of years ago he lost his new phone to a pickpocket gang not far from here, and 50% proud of his honest India.

South Goa. Twenty minutes from the airport, we have a company apartment practically on Majorda beach, acquired about twelve years ago, It's almost heaven, totally peaceful and an escape from hectic India. South Goa is opposite to the North Goa party scene - it's very peaceful - imagine only the noise of nature, distant crashing waves, bird song, frogs croaking of an evening.. I like to come here when I'm in India - it's a time to quietly complete the orders and sort the details, I can have pre-production samples couriered to here, even some suppliers are happy to fly in and and spend an afternoon working on an order by the pool. 

And there are friends here that have become like family, so it's a bit like coming home. It's a full year since I was last here - and sadly time constraints mean that even now this is only a few days. But its quality time, rising before dawn I like to walk on the beach as the sun rises behind the palm trees, allsorts of birds can be seen, storks, peacocks, sea-eagles - I think it's a bird spotters paradise :). Walking/jogging on the pristine freshly washed sand is good exercise and time to clear the head and make plans.
Tomorrow I leave for Kolkata. A different world. 
More news next week.
Take care..

David

title: David's AW News: The End is Near.
content_html:
Greetings from calm and peaceful South Goa, after a super hectic week.


Last week I was telling you about my flying visit to Kathmandu to finalise some new products. I was telling you about the mafia there and my little battle with them. If you missed it you can catch up here.
On Monday I took an Air India flight from Kathmandu to Delhi, changed and flew down to Kolkata arriving at midnight. After two days, I caught an Indigo flight direct to Goa. 
It's an absolutely crazy schedule, but this last mad dash is needed to sort things before I head back to Europe for Christmas. I leave soon.. the end of this Asia trip is near.

In Kathmandu it was cooler than Bali but still 24c in the city. So just t-shirts and shorts still. I needed to visit the artisan felt factory. Mr Padam our shipping agent wanted to see the factory so offered to drive me there.. Kathmandu is a city in a valley with the outskirts lapping up against the mountains. The felt factory we visited is at the very edge of the city, and as we drove onwards and upwards the temperature dropped dramatically. Blue sky and sunny but just a little chilly.  I spent a fascinating afternoon in the felt factory, finalising samples. Watching the artisans doing the magical felting process and then the super skilful needling that produces the vivid felt picture work.  It was super interesting and I was total absorbed in tweaking the designs and seeing the ladies grasp immediately what we wanted.
From just a bundle of wool using water and a kneading process a bag magically appears, then using a needle and painstakingly needling tiny threads of wool into the base these ladies can make beautiful art. Just amazing.
While I'm Nepal as it happens a shipment of felt products arrived in the UK. And as they keep telling me in Nepal felt products are back trending. Mr Padam tells me that Nepal felted items are selling well and a wave of new design ideas are driving good exports. 
I'm happy to see the felt zipper pouches back in stock after so long. And i can see we have already sold a third of the stock in a few days.. so definitely trending. Grab stock quickly if love it. 

From Kathmandu there was no direct flights to Kolkata, so I had to fly via Delhi arriving late at night. Mr Chatterjee was waiting for me at the airport and we drove to his hometown on the banks of the Ganges about an hour away. They have a system where big trucks over a certain size cannot use the highway until after 9pm, so we hit the highway from hell, I really don't know how we made it.. all these massive pimped up trucks honking and switching lanes roaring through the night. Our little car driven by a guy with no fear and a magical ability to thread us between massive hulking trucks. My god, I was a nervous wreck by the time we made it to the hotel.
Highway from hell. 
Then I spent a day checking production in Mr Chatterjee factory. We are working on a new range of Iconic Tote bags. They will be awesome.. (I think) cheap enough that your customers won't think twice, witty, fun and practical. 100% Indian cotton and strong enough to last a long time. Designed for gift shops specifically. And coming soon..
Access all areas.. you will understand why later.

Then after approving all the samples, Mr Chatterjee and I flew down to Goa. Here in peace and quiet, to sort out all the details. Hangtags, barcodes, PO's and compliance details.

My good friends Alex and Maria are as proud as proud can be.. their daughter Anthea has just been elected the Sarpanch of the panchayat of the area. Sort of like council leader in the UK. At just 26 she is the youngest female to take such a roll in India. And thus making history. The family has a history in politics especially fighting for environmental issues along time before it was fashionable. Anthea's grandmother (now passed away) was actually the first female Sarpanch in the state of Goa in 1968. A formidable lady whom I got to know quite well over the years, now Anthea is following in her historic footsteps. 
Alex and Maria with their newly elected daughter.
So I'm here with Mr Chatterjee just at the right time to celebrate this event. Alex and his team have also been working hard on renovating our apartment here in Goa. In the pandemic it was sad and neglected, termites and the monsoon took it's toll. But over the last couple of months, everything has been renewed. New windows and doors, new electrics a whole new kitchen. 
My plan is to use it as a base for a buying team from AW, a Spanish, Slovakian and UK members of the team. I will train them how to do business in India and we will invite suppliers to come to Goa and show us the best of their wares. So that's also why I'm here.. I'm selecting lamp shades and home furnishing.

Anyway the end is near and soon I will be winging my way back to Europe..
In the UK it's so busy - the warehouse team are in full flow.. Christmas is upon us.. Almost December and we have the weather to prove it.
Rodrigo has been getting voucher happy again, so there are Black Friday vouchers to help you grab the stock you need at lower prices.

Wishing you a lovely weekend.

David

title: There is Always Light ❤
content_html:
Greetings from inside the EU


Hope you are well and surviving all the trials and tribulations that seem to beset us all around.

Last week I was telling you about how I seem to be telling all the AW managers in various parts of the world to Keep Calm.. and carry on, you can read here.

It was snowing last week in Slovakia, UK and even Spain.. this week the storms continue. Much of the UK under flood alert, like we didn't have enough issues.

Katka is doing her best to navigate the shipping to EU issues which at point seemed insurmountable. With hundreds of customer orders stuck in limbo and hundreds of customers complaining, it's been stressful. 

Dear EU customers, if you are reading this please give us a chance, we are really doing our best to resolve your shipments. Hopefully today a big chunk of orders will clear customs.. and be on the way to you.

You, dear reader wherever you are also must be feeling the stress, more lock-downs and more complications. Take heart.

 

When day comes we step out of the shade,
aflame and unafraid,
the new dawn blooms as we free it.
For there is always light,
if only we're brave enough to see it.
If only we're brave enough to be it.  

 

Amanda Gorman. OMG.. what a talent, I was half watching the Joe Biden inauguration on Sky news whilst finishing some jobs..  

Like the sun came out. I'm not a big poetry fan, but watching that young lady, bright eyes, hands forming shapes in the air as she performed the poem, and expressed exactly in inspired words the feelings of the world and then transformed those feelings to hope.  If you didn't see it.. You Tube Here...   words to the poem here   The hill we climb, by Amanda Gorman.

 

October 2019, place Goa, India. 

Disappointingly it was raining I remember, torrential downpour. Tomas and I had been in Delhi, exhausting Delhi for two weeks and had flown down to Goa for a bit of R&R. AW bought a beach apartment there ten years ago, and it's our bolt hole in India.  



But Mehul had flown down as our guest from Khambhat in Gujarat, brandishing carton loads of samples. Khambhat is the gemstone crafting capital of India (you learn all the secrets here), and Mehul is one of four suppliers we have in that area.

He is a gentle creative guy. A strict vegan and a spiritual humble Hindu. He is also quite jolly and one of the main pioneers of the orgonite business. This is where gemstones, base metals and artifacts are suspended in resin to create beautiful esoteric art. 

We commandeered one of my friend's hotel bedrooms and laid out all the samples on one bed while (as the rain bucketed down outside) we designed some meaningful product ranges.  Many prototypes, design changes, a hundred emails and several WhatsApp meetings later two new ranges came into being and a major extension to another. Orgonite Chakra Pendulums, beautiful Oronite Keyrings, and some stunning additions to the popular Pyramid range.





Later that evening in the Pentagon restaurant along with Mr Chatterjee we tried to corrupt Mehul with fresh fish and Kingfisher beer, but he was having none of it. Eight months later (these things take time) our delivery finally arrived. It was July 2nd 2020. Regular readers and customers will know that the next day a midnight fire destroyed our main warehouse. It was our deepest blackest moment at AW, from which we fought tooth and nail to come back from. That shipment was destroyed, but within days we had raised the Purchase Order and asked Mehul to get to work on a replacement shipment. And my friends.. It just arrived!.. see details below..

And this proves that resilience can overcome almost anything.  

 

And I'm looking forward to the day we can meet up again with Mehul and our other Indian friends to do business once more. And hopefully next time it won't rain :) 

 

For there is always light.

 

Have a good weekend.

 

David

title: David's AW News: It came crashing down!
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield, UK.

I’m back at the heart of Ancient Wisdom.

Coco flew back to China on Tuesday. She had a bit of a nightmare.. delayed in Istanbul 12 hours. But she wasn't stressed in the least; she just took it in her stride.. and worked from a lounge.. And yesterday I caught an easyJet flight from Málaga — from sapphire blue skies and sunshine to foggy Manchester. Also, not stressed, it is what it is.. My Uber driver struggled over the Pennines to Sheffield in thick fog. Quite the contrast. Still, it’s good to be home. There’s something grounding about being back home in Sheffield, back where it all started.

From this...


to this.

Last week I was telling you about Civic pride in Spain.. And about our warehouse move that's going on right now. If you missed it you can catch up here.

So much is happening across AW right now. 

Before I left Spain, I spent time with Toni, who is still right in the middle of our Spanish warehouse move. And when I say middle, I mean the kind of middle where everything feels like it’s going wrong at once. 

Feels like one drama after another.. I was there the other day in the new office when we heard the most almighty crash from the warehouse.. The racking company we contracted to move existing racking to our configuration had been moving sections of racking via a two-forklift manoeuvre (to avoid dismantling and reassembling). This went badly wrong, causing a section of the racking to come crashing down and wrecking it. Thankfully, no one was hurt, but it could have been serious. So, the racking company was sacked.. have to find more professional people. 

I'm not stressed!

On top of the a racking company fiasco! - Key staff off ill at the worst possible moment. - Boxes in the wrong places. Plans are changing daily. Deadlines that don’t move, even when everything else does.

If you’ve ever moved premises — or tried to grow a business while keeping customers happy — you’ll know that feeling. That moment where it’s totally messy, … and you just have to keep going. The thing is, Toni (and his team) is on a deadline.. he has basically two weeks to fix everything. Because... Well, I'll explain next week.. There is a lot more DRAMA to come.. 

I’ll leave that story right there for now… because it’s not finished yet. (and yes, hopefully there will be a happy ending.)

So TODAY!!   Here in Sheffield, I’m catching up with teams, customers, plans, and the year ahead. Containers are coming like crazy, we have one container every day for the next 7 working days..  new products are landing, and behind the scenes we’re laying foundations that won’t be obvious today — but will make a big difference in the year ahead. 

And on top of that, we are in the Season of Love (SOL), kicking off with the big V-Day—Valentine's Day—almost upon us.. Holly has been getting all inspired by AW classic and new products selected for Valentine's Day and beyond. Check out the video.. if you are looking for ideas right now.. 

As always, thank you for trading with us, growing with us, and sticking with us — even when things are a little chaotic. Especially then.

More news soon.

Warm (despite the cold) regards,
David
Founder – Ancient Wisdom

title: Visiting the Unfinished Village
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Yes, I'm back.. and if you read last week's news, that was a big surprise. I was also telling you about my strange and redirected flight with Korean Airways, if you missed it you can catch up here.
I can hardly believe I have been here one whole week.. lots of things have been happening. Lot's of things have been getting sorted. We are thinking positively everyday.
Today is one of those magic number days.. 11-11-22  like 11+11=22  some mystics believe that numbers carry meanings.. 22 is associated with ancient wisdom.. so it's double ancient wisdom day. It is a day for letting go of the old and moving forward with the new. It's remembrance day also in the UK. 
Today Ringo, our main man in Indonesia, took delivery of a new car. A good day to start new.


Here's Ringo with his new car. The old car he had for 15 years, and cared for it and kept it in top condition.. so this is a big step forward.
In fact, Ringo has been driving me around Bali for more than 10 of those years in this car. Speaking of special anniversaries - AW is 27 years old on Wednesday..  We'll update you with something special then.
This evening Ringo tells me he will have a special ceremony - a holy man will come to make a blessing for the car.
Next week we'll take it on a road trip to the far north of the island.. we have a special mission.

Today we went in Ringo's new car to the "Unfinished Village" - it's away up the mountain, in the middle of nowhere. We had a supplier there a few years ago supplying us with big candle sticks, but the guy stopped making them so we haven't been for a long time. Last time I was here I saw some nice wooden carved vases and bowls. We couldn't get a price that would seem reasonable by the time it was in Europe, now we found the same kind of thing in lots of showrooms.. it's become a buzzing trend in Ubud, and the price has dropped by half. So this morning just as we had finished one supplier visit we spotted this large truck being unloaded with just this type of wooden vase.


Ringo jumped out of the car and asked the driver where he had come from.. He said the "Unfinished Village" - that's not it's actual name it's our nick-name. Because in that village they just make rough unfinished pieces usually out of albasia wood. It's a village of workshops, and piled up in each place is a stack of what they specialise in there. One guy just makes elephants and another Greenman carvings.. and yes we found the place pumping out these wooden vases.. Traders and artisans come to the village and fill up their cars picking and mixixing from the village workshops, they will finish the items in their own style.
Ringo's idea is we buy unfinished in bulk to get a good price and employ our own finishing artisans to ensure good quality..


Whilst we were there a tropical storm came out of nowhere. A few dig drops then a huge downpour and the road turned into a raging torrent of a river.. with Ringo's new car getting a good swishing.. 
It was too loud to even talk with the rain banging on the tin roof of the workshop.. We decided to come back later.. because there are actually quite a few interesting things in the "Unfinished Village"


Here the G20 is about to start and 17 of the world's leaders will attend. Mr Putin has naturally bottled out, much to the annoyance of his host but there will be some of the world's biggest egos in just one the corner of the island, a place called Nusa Dua. We found out today that there is an expo showcasing the artisans and materials of Indonesia that the delegates can visit if they want. We are trying to get access.. one of Bondan's friends is on the organization committee. 

As luck would have it a container with new products from Indonesia just landed.. see below.

News next week.

Hope you have an amazing weekend..

David

title: Resident of Yellow Coconut Village
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about my recent visit to Serampore on the banks of the Ganges and it's links with Wimbledon. You can read it here.
Since then I have been back to Delhi, to Bangalore and then flown via Kuala Lumpur to Bali. More precisely Ubud in Bali.
It may cheer you up to know the weather in the UK is much better than Bali. Here it's been raining all week, with electric storms at night :).
Ubud is one of the worlds great giftware hubs. Highly creative people and hugely industrious locals produce artisan giftware that is shipped all over the world. I doubt there is a giftshop (at least one with taste and style) that doesn't stock some Indonesian handicrafts. There are other places (and growing fast) in Indonesia that produce handicrafts but Ubud sits regally up in the mountains, like a mythical giftware kingdom.
So it makes sense to have a warehouse here. Mainly so suppliers orders can be consolidated, and we can ship whenever we have a full container load. Right now we have to try and coordinate suppliers to finish their production at the same time, at the point we want to ship. This means that inevitably, some suppliers are waiting to deliver long after stock is made, and others rushing to complete in order to get stock in the next container. It all ends up a bit of a botch job, and quality control can suffer.
Last time I was here, on my last day. We spotted a part built warehouse, this been Ubud, as picturesque a warehouse as you can imagine, with stone statues outside and it's own roof top temple. Inside enough floor space for two container loads, although two walls were missing and the office at the back had been taken over by the jungle it looked almost perfect. The landlord, a young local architect (a pretty cool guy with a funky handshake), appeared and offered to do the place up to our specifications. He assured us it would be to a high standard. Ringo (our agent) was worried that a 40ft container wouldn't negotiate the narrow lanes to the site. So before we could finalise we had to make sure the access was OK. But subject to that we shook hands on the deal, and as good as his word the warehouse was ready for occupation on time.

This is the system here, every area, each village has elders who ensure that everything is equatable and peaceful and beautiful. The rules can change, I'm not even sure what the current rules are. It's going to be interesting I think.
Our village is called: "Br. Nyuh Kuning" or the Yellow Coconut Village.. which seems as good a name for the location of an Ancient Wisdom outpost.
Expect to read more about the Ubud outpost in future reports..
Until then.
Take care..
David

title: Bali update week 3
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Happy Bonfire Night.. is that still a thing?
Anyway I hope if you are celebrating Guy Fawkes and his failed attempt at blowing up parliament.. you and your family keep safe,
Last week was Halloween.. Thank you to everyone who voted in our costume competition.. I guess you know who won.. once again :)
I would like to extend happy and peaceful Diwali greetings to all our friends in India (and elsewhere) celebrating the festival of lights.

Here in Bali a different kind of festival is in the offing.. Galungan day is coming soon.. and every day leading up to it is some kind of special event. It starts officially next Wednesday and lasts ten days.. during this time the spirits are allowed to visit earth as the gap between the earthly realm and the spiritual realm is very close.  Lots of preparations and from what I can gather great excitement.. this is the Bali Christmas I feel.
Last week I was telling you about Bondan the music Guru.. you can read it here.

It's the rainy season in Bali.. which means when it's not raining it is stinking hot.. and when it's raining it's a torrential downpour. 
If you are thinking of coming to Bali and feel you should avoid the rainy season.. I say don't worry about it.. it rains and then stops and the sun comes out, it's not like you suffer days and weeks of no sunshine. Even when it rains it can be super localised.
Yesterday I was on Jalan Tegallalang, the road that leads from Ubud to that famous rice terrace view. Ensconced with a supplier checking out a fantastic range of new recycled glass wind chimes when we became aware of that drumming noise of heavy rain.. 
I went to look outside to find that the road had turned to a rushing river.. the rain stopped but the water kept on coming.. I thought it would be fun to go stand in the middle of the flow for a picture..



That's was a dumb idea.. because it's not just water rushing down the hill.. sticks and stones, coconuts and I even spotted a rather large snake. I escaped with just a minor scrape. You live and learn.
Some of the showrooms were getting flooded and it occured to me that our warehouse about 40 minutes drive away might be suffering damage.. I called Bondan who keeps making himself useful and was photographing a new range of Molten Glass Bowls at the office.. no Boss he said.. here is blue sky and sunshine.

I have been here in Bali for three weeks and it's never been so productive. Partly because I have the almost undivided attention of suppliers, and partly because Ringo is mega organised and plans every minute of every day to the max. Also Bondan the music Guru, decided that he wanted to work for AW even if it was for free.. he took time off from his job at the music store in Denpasar just to offer his help to Ringo and me. He is a quick learner, has very good English and like many Indonesians a very talented artist.
Of course we are paying for his time.. but let's see how things pan out. I was kind of worried that after ten years Ringo might feel as if some young upstart would steal his job.. But Ringo, at first reserved, is now very keen to take on an assistant.

So we made a plan to increase the amount shipped from Indonesia fourfold.. it can be done. We just need to up our game, beef up management and bring our warehouse into the modern age with a forklift truck, racking and an organised packing and QC area.
In Bali none of the artisans actually pack the products in boxes.. barcodes and cartons are all beyond them. So (I have explained before) most exporters use what they call cargo companies.. who do that job for you and then stuff the containers, sort the paperwork and send it to the port.. we do all that ourselves in our AW Frangipani warehouse near Sukawatti. Maybe with Bondan on board I can see it happening.

In recent days I have spotted a few more foriegn faces around Ubud.. Maybe I'm not the only Englishman in town anymore.. the ones I have spoken to are all American but I have overheard French speaking.  In the coffee shop we eye each other like Squid Games contestants because this is the competition for sure. The only visas available are business visas.. and most of the people I have seen are solo carrying a laptop. So a few buyers like me are here.. but not many.. the other occupant of Ubud is the blogger, or instagrammer. The social media influencers can get business visas and Bali is a lucrative territory. Yesterday outside the pretty much abandoned Monkey Forest I noticed a pink spiky haired young lady being filmed by her boyfriend with all the tech to hand, including a fluffy mike and a drone. Japanese was my guess. 

Enjoy the weekend, stay safe and I'll update you next week.

David
