title: David's AW News: I was hooked.
content_html:
Greetings from La Cala, Mijas

Today I'm working from home. Our house is on the hills, above the town of La Cala not far from Marbella. I'm writing this newsletter, while Coco is busy connecting with suppliers in China and organising the next container shipment. 
Last week I was telling you how busy we were unloading containers, if you missed it you can read about it here.
The clocks go back this weekend - you probably know that, but here in Spain for the last time. They tell me the clocks will go back and then stay that way in Spain. The time for switching times has passed, they say.
It's almost Halloween weekend..the good old Bonfire night (in the UK) and a then the time when everyone suddenly realises - OMG it's almost Christmas - I need to get those presents!
But you probably know that too.. 

I'm so happy to see the Indian shipment of Gemstone trees finally arriving... regular readers will remember our epic Nepal and India trip early this year. Tomas, Bryant and myself spent more than a month visiting suppliers and sourcing our greatest and best selection of Indian and Nepal products ever. Some are yet to be delivered.. because artisan production is always slower than promised but better late than never.. 
We have a long standing supplier - actually one of the first Indian gemstone suppliers we had.. I originally worked with Hadil the father, who now has moved to America to be with his family, but makes regular trips back to India. 
I remember maybe 15 years ago going to visit Hadil and his family in Khambhat on the Arabian sea. The nearest airport was Ahmedabad, and Hadil picked us up in his rugged bone rattling Bolero jeep. And we drove down Khambhat to visit their factory and workshops. It was pretty basic in those days, Hadil had a big stick behind his seat, which he explained was to beat off any bandits that might try to rob us. 
The town was a maze of narrow streets, with artisans working in little workshops each producing a particular speciality. It was one of my first visits to an off the track part of India, and I was hooked. Been travelling as often as possible ever since..
One of Khambhat's most celebrated ancient exports is its agate beads.. It is believed that the art of crafting agate beads in Khambhat dates back to at least the 4th century. Even Marco Polo came here to trade.  Khambhat's artisans have perfected the skill of cutting and polishing agate these days especially for esoteric products.  Perfect for Ancient Wisdom.


Ancient Cambay now known as Khambhat.


The town centre these days.


Selecting Gemstone trees.


This picture was after an epic six hour meeting with Hadil on the right.. and the son in the middle. 
  
The son in-law now runs the business with renewed passion and lots of ideas. He took the short flight with his suitcase of samples to meet us at our mini base in South Goa. 
Tomas and Bryant and I spent a happy couple of days checking out a huge selection of Khambhat wonders, and placing an order big enough to keep a decent number of artisans busy all year.
So check out the new gemstone items below.. especially the mini gemstone tree's.. your customers will be Hooked.. I'm sure they are a winner. 
But there are many more esoteric and gemstone items from India - we aim to be your best supplier of this kind of thing. 

Tomas is still in Bali - working with the AW-Advantage team and by all accounts making huge progress.. Check it out here if you need marketing superpowers.. 

Meanwhile.. It's all happening.
Containers of stock arriving, goods being shipped as quickly as we can.. 
We are working on a big surprise.. because it's AW's birthday coming soon.. stand by for important news.

Have a wonderful Halloween weekend.. more news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Leaving on a Jet Plane
content_html:
Greetings from Bali,


Little sad because this is my last day of this asia trip. But also looking forward to getting back to Europe - later this evening I will catch a Turkish airways flight to Istanbul, then change there for Malaga, Spain.
It's been an epic journey - starting 6 months ago.. and travelling to Bali, Java, Nepal, India, China and back to Bali.. Many new products, sourced, designed, ordered and on the way (hopefully) to your shops and stores. Toni from Spain came for part of the trip, Tomas from Slovakia and Sandra (our talented designer) came for the China and Bali parts of the trip. Thank you to them all for their epic contributions.  You can catch up last week newslleter here.
Also a special thank you to Bondhan our Indonesia main man, who has been a big part in the developing travel videos - you can follow on YouTube.
Last week I was telling you about Blitar City and drum making artisans.. if you missed it you can catch up here..  Or see the YouTube video that Bodhan crafted here. And as a bonus you can see Bondhan playing the drums..


AI changes everything.
On this trip I have been trying to develop skills as a YouTuber.. I am quite a shy person, and really didn't want to go down that route, but so many friends, customers and my team kept banging on about it that I had to try.. it's a lot harder than I realised.. before we used to just use YouTube as a convenient place to store clips, and the occasional "Can you Sell this Video"  which I want to develop more..

The marketing world is changing so fast.. before we just did SEO and a bit of Google adwords and your customers came.. and we kept a relationship via newsletters like this. But gradually google decreased the amount of space for natural listings and pushed paid content.. until users got fed up.. and now they have an alternative, AI.. I for one rarely use google now ( I use perplexity and ChatGBT4o) .
This last three weeks Tomas and the digital marketing team here in Bali.  AW-Advantage.com have been working hard to understand and pivit.. Basically if you are not prepared to spend a high proportion of your sales on google ad's then you need to do SEO or OFE  Optimize for Everything.. including or especially AI. and social media.. and I would argue information media.. because YouTube is not really social media, you can't socialise much there.. but you can soak up News, Information and Entertainment. 


Check out our Java Village of Stone YouTube also.. 


New Dropshipping Site in the works..
We had five or six developers working on an updated Dropshipping Website.. for a longtime.. One thing Tomas and I have been doing (with Raul our IT wizard) is getting this project over the line. 
There is definitely a resurgence in dropshipping, we are getting more and more customers on AW-Dropshipping.com  doing really well on the site, even though the user experience could be better.. and we are working on it.. we think by the end of the month, we can release a major upgrade.

Meanwhile back in the UK..
Lots of Indian stock has been rolling into our warehouse.. Rodrigo and the team are working hard to get everything online.. And some of these lines are beautiful and on trend.
I'm particularly excited to see the Iconic Jute Bags.. A lot of work went into this range.. we tried to bring you ethically sourced Indian cotton at Chinese polycotton prices..put a good range by the till nicely displayed and I believe a good proportion of customers will buy.. Everyone needs a bag and these are stylish, funny and cool at no brainer retail prices.
 
See details below.

Fathers day is almost here.. and we have the deals and the trending stuff you need to wow your customers.. 

Anyway have a lovely weekend.. I'm just off to the airport..

David

title: David's AW News: A 2023 Round up @ AW
content_html:
Seasons Greetings from Spain..

I hope you are enjoying the festive period and you have time to enjoy the company of your family and friends. 

Last week I was telling you about our Pizza Party traditions on the last day of work at AW in the UK.. if you missed it you can catch up here.  


I had the pleasure of spending Christmas day with my Brother's wife's family who are from Zimbabwe and extended family from all over Africa. Well, the food was awesome: traditional goat stew for Christmas lunch, but the meeting with the extended family was delightful.. Nurses, a lawyer, university administrators and even a maths teacher. I learned a lot about emerging Africa, the good and the bad.. We already do a bit of business (gemstones) from Mozambique (next to Zimbabwe) but I'm thinking of drawing on family connections to explore more opportunities. 

I took the early morning Ryanair flight from Manchester to Malaga and arrived here on Wednesday. Tomas and his family are here, so it's New Year in Spain.

It's the last Friday before 2024, so I thought I'd make a brief round-up of the year at AW.. 


Well it's been another epic year for AW with lots of fun and lots of stuff happening.. The most important thing for our customers is the wealth of new fast selling products. 

Notable events and new products at AW included the following:

 

January - Completing the move to the new AW-Aromatics.com factory in Sheffield, housed in the rebuilt burnt down AW warehouse. New products have been coming every month since.

 

February - This is when we bought the Beach Bar in Bali (almost by accident) read about it here.

 

March - The Epic India/Nepal trip with Tomas, Bryant and Myself.. the first for Bryant and our first since before covid.  A big success.. resulting in 463 new products including beautiful Singing Bowls. Now we have the best range in the UK. Also simply the best range of Indian Incense. 

 

April - The launch of our new baby.. AW-Advantage.com. A digital marketing agency that can give your website super powers. Established in that abandoned beach bar in Bali.

 

May - Working with Coco in China to produce many new products including new Chakra Gemstone Candles.. a massive success.

 

June - In Bali, the development of our Popup Shop range of Shopfitting. This is going to be awesome - but only just arriving in

Europe - it's not all here yet. But it's just what you need to open a popup shop with ease. Stay tuned.

 

July - New managers appointed at AW-Aromatic.com.. James and Bryant take the helm and make rapid changes and improvements. Launched the Whipped Cream Soap range.. instantly sold out.. and one of the best selling products this year from the AW Aromatic team.

 

August  - I return to India to tie up some loose ends. And finally get to see Mr Chatterjee's new factory. Details here. Lots of new products developed - which are now on the way to Europe. From AW-Gifts.eu in Slovakia we launched the Croatia website. AW is now reaching every corner of the EU and GB.

 

September - Back in China -  Coco, the team (and me).. work on the amazingly detailed and enchanting: Hop Hare Gemstone Flowers Candles. Honestly, I think it is our greatest design achievement. Ok maybe I'm a bit biased :) - but so far seems to be our fastest selling candle in the history of AW..

title: Andy Murray and Ancient Wisdom
content_html:
Greetings from Indonesia, where I have just arrived from India.
Since last weeks newsletter from Saharenpur in Northern India (read it here), I have been to Kolkatta.
The big floods, you will have seen on the news, close to Saharenpur are a long way from Kolkatta but the same water flows down in to the Ganges which, by the time it reaches Bengal is a truly mighty majestic river.
Mr Chatterjee picked me up in his new Nano car from my hotel on Sunday morning. We drove out of Kolkatta across the Howrah Bridge (built by the British in 1943 and still possibly the busiest bridge in the world) just one of the 300,000 who cross here every day. Rudyard Kipling said; " This is Imperial. This is worth coming across India to see!"

Actually the water flowing under it was worth seeing, high up the banks, scraping the temples. This normally placid river, dark brown rushing and angry. So much water moving so fast.
We drove, along the river bank through little towns busy and shambolic, catching glimpses of the river between buildings until we reached the town of Serampore. So from Saharenpur in the far north to Serampore in the far east, connected by the water. In the hot wet monsoon, this is real India.
Mr Chatterjee has a small company making gift products from Jute. Seampore was once rich, in the days when the jute industry here supplied the world with jute backing for carpets. There are magnificent wonderfully ornate streets of villas, now magnificent only in their decay. You can imagine a British Raj living in some style here. The British have long left and this town always feels to me like it was frozen in time since then.
Mr Chatterjee's oldest friend was a professional tennis player of some fame, now a tennis coach of renown in Hong Kong where he helps the rich and famous win a few aces.
He also helps his home town, not least investing in Mr Chatterjee's jute business, and he also supports the local tennis club. He was in town for the annual general meeting of the club and invited me to see. In this tumbledown river town of temples, holy cows and creeping vines it seemed incongruous to find such a thing as a tennis club. They told me with some pride that four members of the club were at Wimbledon this year. Alas not playing, all four are umpires. The Bengal Indians are famous for fair minded debating, so I'm not surprised they make world class umpires.
So there you have it, my tenuous link to Andy Murry all the way from banks of the Ganges in India to centre court Wimbledon in two handshakes.
I'm here working on the next batch of jute and cotton related products, one of which is door stops, here are some preproduction ideas. The coming new trend of 2014 (I hope).
Later Mr Chatterjee and his partner showed me the new factory they are building on the outskirts of the town. Four floors with better working conditions and nice views of open countryside.
Some stock just arrived from there you can see below. This is Mr Chatterjee with his staff proudly showing their work.
You can support the town of Serampore, Mr Chatterjee and his team, the new factory, the tennis club and AW by stocking jute products.
Did I mention that Jute is ultra green, JUTE Bags are very eco-friendly.
Jute is 100% bio-degradable.
Jute is a fast growing crop with a much higher carbon dioxide assimilation rate than even rainforest.
Jute production creates much needed jobs in areas that need it.
... actually I probably did. Sorry to go on so.
Anyway until next week.
Further distractions. Howrah Bridge, JuteNotPlastic.com, Seampore Tennis Club Facebook page - please hit like button.
Regards
David

title: The Ultimate Gift ❤
content_html:
Greetings from a wet and windy Sheffield.

 

Hope you are well, let's hope the weather improves and we can enjoy sitting outside a pub or cafe in the sunshine.

Last week we were forced to sit outside under an umbrella wrapped up against the elements just to be able to commune with our fellow human over a drink or meal.

On Sunday I was with Tomas trying to find a table for lunch, even though it was wet and miserable every available pavement table in Sheffield town centre was occupied or pre booked.

This is crazy I thought, tomorrow the bars and restaurants will actually be allowed to let us go indoors, and yet the simple desire to socialise with friends overcomes drizzle, discomfort and inconveniences.

Finally we found a rain splattered table - It's our last chance to sit in the rain and drink beer - I joked as the waiter wiped down the seats and table.

 

There are some other basic human desires often overlooked..  one of which is the need to give gifts. 

It's always nice to receive a gift, but it is often overlooked the pleasure that the giver feels. Hence the saying; "It's better to give than receive"

On behalf of Mr Chatterjee, I want to give a big THANK YOU to all the people who contributed this week to an appeal to supply oxygen to people of his town in India who can not afford it and otherwise could die.

Last week I was telling you about Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) and his plan.. you can read about it here.

And here is the link  to the Go Fund Me page.. and more information here: India Appeal 

Within a few hours you had raised enough to buy 5 tanks of refillable oxygen, I didn't wait for Go-fund-me to send me the funds - I bought Indian rupees in my Revolut account and sent them directly to Mr Chatterjee.  It's five lives we can help.

There are no free beds in the hospitals in  Serampore , the seriously ill are put on a waiting list, and many (especially those without oxygen) don't make it.    To those who gave, in these terrible times. Thank you, you gave the ultimate gift.

Please help. Even if you cannot afford actual money, you can go to the link Go-Fund-Me click on the share button and send to all your friends on all your social networks.. You can also send them a link to our Info Page..  Think of the good karma points you will be accruing - and feeling you get from giving the ultimate gift.. 




Mr Chatterjee - ready for action.

 

Today an Indian container arrived from our wooden craft supplier in northern India.  So lot's of stuff is back in stock. Including some starters that require wooden stands.  - See below..

Importing wood is very difficult, governments around the world have quite rightly signed up to protecting deforestation. So all wood imports need to be provable from sustainable sources. You need a license to export and in Europe a license to import, you also now need a certificate for each shipment. At AW we are up for all this, of course this needs to be done.. Our man in Indonesia (Ringo) is particularly good at checking all documentation and working with the Indonesian authorities to make sure everything is legal. We always have our Fledge certificates in proper order.

 

Even so when a container of wooden products arrived in our Slovakian warehouse the submitted documents had still not been approved for release by the Slovakian authorities..   and then a separate office demanded to know if our papers were in order. One day after the delivery the papers were released and approved but we were technically in default.

Tomas, who is the MD of Slovakia company, gets a call saying we are importing and marketing illegal wood, and they are issuing a €200,000 fine. So unjust, so stressful, so totally not our fault. 

Yesterday he had to appear in (a virtual zoom style) court to answer charges.. in the end they agreed it was a rather disproportionate punishment.   

 

Tomas - here telling them.. but we are importing hand carved Hati Hati Angels and wooden elephants.. things that make people happy, (in these stressful times) and been treated as if we were importing evil contraband.




It all ends well, but in this day and age do we need such unnecessary stress?

 

So now you know the kind of hoops we jump through to bring you and your customers beautiful things.

Don't worry we love it really :)

 

Have a wonderful weekend. Take care, stay safe.. and spare a thought for Mr Chatterjee and the Ultimate gift.

 

David

title: Weird and Wonderful
content_html:
Greetings from Weird Ubud

Last week I was telling you about our trip to the far north of Bali, to the second city of Bali: Singaraja - The lion kingdom. We tracked down a clove oil distiller deep in the forest. If you missed it you can read about it here.
It's been an extremely busy week since then - trying to squeeze in far too many deals before I have to return to Europe - which is generally a mistake. It's much better to focus and make one or two really good product ranges than ten average ones. So many of the projects I'm thinking of hanging over until when I return.. Although our man Ringo and his able assistant Bondhan can keep a lot of things gradually progressing in the right directions..

Whilst dashing from supplier to supplier.. I noticed something about Ubud, it's changing.. not in a bad way..

It's changing in many ways, its getting bigger, it's getting busier, it's buzzing.. but most of all it's gone weird.. very weird in some places. So many shops like Merlin's Magic shop and restaurant, so many crystal shops, healing chakra massage places, vegan trance studios, mystic tattoo studios everywhere, Yoga barn has a menu of meditation zones for every outcome. Ubud has always been Indonesia's if not all of Asia's most creative zones, helped and enabled by an army of skilled artisans. It's always been a bit alternative - but now every other business has just gone weird. Wonderfully weird. And the weird and wonderful people are being mystically drawn to Ubud.. 

Last week I was telling you about the rustic clove oil production plant we found in the forest.. well on the return journey after a tip off we took a detour to another area and found a village with very organised and modern production. Family run businesses who were delighted to show us everything and sell us samples for testing. They also promised to help with how to source other oils in Indonesia directly.. this is a major breakthrough - I'm really pleased about this because this is a secretive and almost impossible world to break into. 

This week we have been discovering the wonderful world of the Payung - or Balanese umbrella. They come in every size - used in temple decorations and sun shades alike.. The information we have is that they are selling really well in Europe as exotic decor.. I have a collection in my house in Spain.. and it's true you can find them in many gift shops in Spain..
We found the village where they make export quality, the ones used in homes and temples here are low quality and wouldn't meet export requirements. But the same processes are used in manufacturing so out of interest we also went to the village where payungs are made for local use, this village is along the coast from our warehouse and inland a little. A huge industry of family businesses working together.. 
A complicated moving bamboo frame is made first, a pole made from treated dorian wood, a base made from albacia wood and a cover from cotton or canvas.. When it is finished different artisans attach decorations, tassels and shapes to make the finished article.  It's a lot of work. But I think they are wonderful.


Well it's that Friday again.. Black Friday.. and last chance to grab a deal - check out some of the deals below..
It's also just one month until Christmas Day.. and so I must be back for Christmas..

Hope you have a lovely weekend

David

title: So We Decided To Get High
content_html:
Greetings from India














Only been here two days but it feels like a week :-) 
I'm travelling with Tomas on a grand sourcing trip - finding the products that are going to be your big sellers next year.. well that's the plan :)
Last week I was telling you about arriving in Kathmandu, Nepal, and how earlier we had been brainstorming in a storm high in the sky in KL. You can read about it here.

Of course Kathmandu is already high in the sky, and it's a place where it's possible to get extremely high. After checking in our hotel late at night we ventured out to get a nightcap drink. in the centre of Kathmandu, there are lots of hip and happening bars catering to the trekkers and climbers who come to do epic things in the mountains. Before and after - they come to relax and recover in Thamel the backpacking area (and also the wholesale exporting area). I can tell you after midnight it is a wild and bizarre place, and would seem to be full of groups of young people totally stoned, and totally happy having the time of their life.


So we decided to get high, but being responsible adults we stuck to a quick shot of Black Durban.. the local whiskey and headed to bed. After doing our job we planned to set Sunday aside to get high.
Friday first thing we met with the delightful Mr Padam our shipping agent, he had lined up several meetings with potential suppliers, and took us along to meet them. Such interesting people, Nepal is full of the most diverse and inventive entrepreneurs. We met one guy that makes ultra pure essential oils by taking steam distillation equipment to high altitude villages, sometimes by helicopter so that the locals can turn otherwise unused crops in to valuable oils and bring income to super remote locations. Another guy a genuine Mr Sherpa who has a passion for working with artisans including Tibetans exiled from near by China who make exquisite singing bowls and other beautiful things. Ceremonial gongs that could also be wall art, who wouldn't want such a lovely thing hanging on their dining room wall?


The "ABC" experience.
Sunday morning we woke early before dawn, a taxi waiting outside the hotel took us to the domestic airport. An interesting airport where tickets are a bit fluid, and flight numbers change. Flights are cancelled because of weather conditions and you are on another flight before you know it. The small plane took us below mountain height - spectacular endless snow capped mountains - to tiny Pokhara airport.. a young lady in a red t-shirt was waiting for us on the tarmac right from the plane.  We followed her very excited, it was time to get high...

A four-seat helicopter waiting for us, quickly we were weighed, asked to sign a disclaimer document.. then seconds later strapped in - given head phones - all the flight control chatter in our heads - . OMG!.. OH-MY-GIDDY-AUNT!!!.. we are off.. Up up up.. Pokhara lake getting smaller below us rising up and up.. cresting spectacular ridges, following a tumbling river, up and up we go. Then surrounded by the most awesome mountain peaks I have ever seen eventually we spiral down to land on a tiny patch of green at ABC.. otherwise known as... Annapurna  Base Camp and it's as high as I have ever been. The altitude sends you a quite lightheaded.. like smoking dope (Tomas told me), so now I know what it feels like to be high. And I can report.. The most exhilarating experience ever - it was amazing!



Back to Pokhara where we had time for lunch by the tranquil lake in a laid-back hippy restaurant.. it's a very cool place Pokhara.. we plan to return.
Back in Kathmandu time to work.. so much to do and so little time. Monday and Tuesday long days sorting out details, approving samples jumping from meeting to meeting. Tomas in one meeting me in another.. finally we catch the evening flight down to Delhi. 
Mr Chatterjee, our man in India had sent his guy to meet us with a car.. then a long drive to the hotel... 
Bad air day..






From the ultra clean air of ABC to the thickest dirtiest air on the planet.. my app: AirVisual on arrival showed an incredible 203 US AQI - described as dangerous. Today as I write this it's 180 US AQI - Unhealthy.

You can read about it here. Of course Kathmandu is already high in the sky, and it's a place where it's possible to get extremely high. After checking in our hotel late at night we ventured out to get a nightcap drink. in the centre of Kathmandu, there are lots of hip and happening bars catering to the trekkers and climbers who come to do epic things in the mountains. Before and after - they come to relax and recover in Thamel the backpacking area (and also the wholesale exporting area). I can tell you after midnight it is a wild and bizarre place, and would seem to be full of groups of young people totally stoned, and totally happy having the time of their life. title: David's AW News: Toni Touched in India
content_html:
Greetings from peaceful South Goa


Our mad dash around India is winding up as we arrive at our (kind of) India base for rest, recuperation and paperwork. Nice to catch up with old friends and soak up the sun, natural beauty and Goan hospitality. Last week I was telling you that poor old Toni was taken to a new culture shock location everyday and why they drink English Wine in India. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Just when he thought he had seen everything, Chatterjee took us to a place off the culture clash scale.. more info below.


Har Ki Pauri Ghat - Feet of Lord Vishnu

Last week I was writing this just as we arrived in the wooden craft city of Saharanpur. I came here last eight years ago, and thought I'd landed in Afghanistan. Mud streets, burka clad ladies, camel carts, army presence with machine guns and broken basic infrastructure.  


I can report a big improvement, big brand Indian retailers are here, the main road in is good, it feels safe and they even have a "!  Saharanpur" sign for selfies. While the old town is still unpaved and very congested, and there are still camels pulling carts loaded with huge mango wood logs you can feel that there is more money here now. 
We have an old supplier here, a very nice family but old school crafts and we feel that they have reached capacity with us because it takes six months plus to produce our orders and that means we are out of stock of many items for long periods of time. So after careful research we made a short list of other factories to visit and was surprised to find a pretty high standard of work place and modern processes. One place we visited very close to the old town was in a big compound with several large buildings, each building devoted to a different process. With artisans employed in proper paid jobs working in teams. We was impressed.


They said they had the capacity to produce container load quantities within weeks.

But our old friend and supplier we will of course still support especially since Rashid family are so kind and his wife makes the best biryani in India. We went to visit and Rashid had prepared a room full of AW style samples just for us which I have to say was impressive and clearly they had put a lot of thought and time into producing.. After doing business Rashid's wife appeared with food. And very tasty it was too.


Rashid and his Brother


In that town we had trouble finding a decent hotel, almost every hotel had bad reviews. Take my advice when travelling in India - never stay at a hotel with "Royal" in the name. We stayed at the Hotel Royal Classic. 


Never again. Pokey rooms no windows, dubious sheets and lumpy hard beds.. we escaped and cancelled our second night preferring to get out of town. Our supplier told us there was no good standard hotel in town the nearest good hotels were in Dehradun where the airport was - 2 hours away. 
Dehradun was a complete chalk and cheese to Saharanpur, a long drive uphill into the foothills of the Himalayas it's a resort town and has developed into a beautiful thriving clean organised town. Smart high-rise hotels a plenty, bars and restaurants, I could hardly believe this was India. There we stayed for only a little more money in an old colonial home (the Mango Tree Courtyard) restored to boutique hotel standard. Big spacious rooms, luxury beds, friendly staff and home cooked food. India is like that - a land of extremes, as I have said many times: Rich and poor, good and bad, awful and beautiful. Side by side.


Then onwards to Jaipur by Indigo airways via unbelievably efficient airports.. where we spent four nights many adventures (maybe tell you more next week).. then to GOX Goa's brand new airport, again so organised and trouble free. Amazingly again the luggage is on the belt by the time we get there. 
So now our last few days in India, before heading to Nepal, where Coco will join us after her Chinese New Year festivities. I think Toni has been truly touched by India, seeing things and meeting people your average holiday tour wouldn't accommodate..  
In the place where the Holy Ganges spills forth from the mountains onto to the Indian plains pure, cold and rushing, at the feet of Lord Vishnu. There is certainly something magical about the water there, and the people who come there are erm.. well the more eccentric type Indians.. Toni met some.


Toni is touched and blessed..

Meanwhile..
Back in the UK.. lots of new products arriving.
Tomas has been working hard, revamping the website trying to make it more intuitive. Your feedback ahs been amazing, thank you so much. I believe sometimes really good products almost get lost. Rashid asked me about his star sign incense holders, his American customers best selling line - I check our sales and realised we are not communicating this.They are a perfect star sign birthday gift and can be teamed with incense to boost your sales. So Rodrigo and team improved the pictures now I think you can see the potential.
Also launching this week in the same theme a new product from the AW- Aromatics team.. a lot of work has gone into this.. Zodiac Fragrance Oils. A beautiful job guys - well done! The fragrance has bio-glitter to give a star like feel to the fragrance, the packaging is awesome. Carefully selected and developed fragrances, I also checked these fragrances personally (with my nose) at the development stage.. I know they are good.

I'm also excited to see our new Seven Chakra Cedarwood Bangles have arrived. This is a Coco production item.. well my basic idea (he says modestly haha), packaging design by Bondhan our designer in Bali and Coco's jewellery design and making it happen, we used high quality gemstone beads fatter than usual with the natural aromatic cedarwood beads. Stack them mixed in a big basket £6 - £8 retail I think they will fly out..

Mother's day is coming soon.. so stock up now whilst we have Feb-free shipping still available.

Take care have a lovely weekend.
Namaste from India.

David

title: David's AW News: Meet our new Friends
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China


Happy Easter Weekend. Wishing you lots of brisk friendly business, chocolates and hopefully some quality time with your friends and family. 
Here in China Easter hardly registers as an event, and we are working every day, weekends included, to find the next best big thing for your store.
Last week I was telling you about the "A" team in action.. and the issue we have with moving warehouse.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

This week has just flown by, each morning Coco and I collect Tomas from his hotel and head off to see suppliers in one area or another of the vast Yiwu market. We do a bit of walking around to see what we might happen upon, but to walk all the Yiwu permanent market would take weeks, there are 90,000 showrooms! But we head to see old friends and along the way find some new ideas. 

Coco with our agent and the new landlord, doing the deal.

I was telling you we needed to find a new warehouse and home for our candle factory as our old landlord had gone bust. That's normally a time consuming job right? But not here in China, Coco decided on a new warehouse on the fifth floor of a warehouse block not far from our old warehouse on Monday. On Tuesday the agent took us back for a second look, and with some access issues ironed out we decided to go ahead.  No messing, straight to the boss man's office, he had a standard contract already stamped with red marks and just filled in the blanks. The agent oversaw the deal, and Coco and the Boss signed the paper, money sent via WeChat, agent fees paid on the spot. We have official access from 1st April, but can send in the workmen the next day to build an office, move the factory and fit toilets. Breathtakingly quickly, not a lawyer or notary in sight. Over 1000 square meters, access to two big lifts down to a loading bay big enough for 40ft containers. It's enough room for the factory, and space for three containers worth of stock at any one time plus a nice corner office with a view for Coco. We have a three year lease with options to extend. 

Things just get done in China so much quicker and with no fuss.  And because of this we have so many projects in development my brain is getting overloaded and we seem to be working ridiculas hours. Tomas, Coco and myself.often until the early hours, and breakfast then into meetings. But don't feel sorry for us, working with the mainly small family business is a delight and great fun. And seeing unique and interesting product ranges form so quickly is exciting and fun. And because we don't deal with mega factory corporations we develop real relationships with artisans, young folk, lady bosses and small family businesses much more than your average China importer..
Here are a few from this week..

So that's the update from China for this week.
Hope your long weekend is restful enough.. and more updates next week.

Happy Holi, to all our Indian Friends. India is bursting with colours and goodwill, as they celebrate the festival these few days.
I have been there a few times at this time, it's wild, good natured, totally colourful and crazy. Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) sends Holi best wishes (and few pics from his hometown) to all AW customers and the AW team.


Take care, enjoy the chocolates!

David

title: Moonshine & Mystics
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

We are back in ultra busy Ubud. Last week I was telling you about the peaceful town of Amed and the Gates of Heaven. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
From Amed on the way back to Ubud we spent one night in a small town high in the mountains called Sideman. I'd read about this place, described as Ubud 30 years ago, a town nestled in the rice terrace with a mountain river rushing by and spectacular views of Mount Agung nearby.  It's pretty undiscovered, only a few hotels and restaurants.. but the locals couldn't be more friendly.. walking round the village down little gangways along the edge of rice terrace you were practically inside the homes of the villagers. Local crafts include textile weaving and brewing the best moonshine in Bali. Not quite the level of handicrafts found in and around Ubud, but first grade Coconut Arak seemed like a good idea.


Sideman 

Sideman was evacuated in 2017 when Mount Agung started erupting, because it lies in the danger zone and thus not many hotel chains have risked investment there.. so the place is peacefully underdeveloped with most people stay in homestays or guest houses. We booked a taxi to take us back to Ubud, and I asked our young driver a local guy where we could by Arak. "My aunty makes the best in the village" he said proudly and he took us a detour to visit. Follow me he said and we followed him up some steps into a Balinese family compound, on an open balcony an old lady was busy working on a loom making Sideman textile for temple wear. When she learned we wanted to buy her moonshine she smiled and got up.. we averted our eyes because she was topless, (old ladies in Bali often don't bother to dress and don't see why they should change their ways). She pulled on a tee-shirt and went to get her wares. She poured some of the crystal clear liquid into a shot glass for us to try.. Some call it Balinese whiskey and it has quite a kick. The nephew explained to us how to tell the best stuff.. shake the bottle and see if small bubble appear on the surface if they do that's the good stuff.  I bought three bottles one each for Ringo and Bondan and one for spare. About £3 a bottle seems good value. 

The 17th August is Indonesia Independence day, and usually the streets are filled with a sea of massive red and white flags. I remember before the pandemic the enthusiasm. This time not many huge flags, and on closer inspection some crumpled flags (not new) and many businesses and homes not even bothering. There was a free concert in the evening in Ubud to celebrate, we could hear it from our hotel.. and they kicked off with patriotic Indonesian songs.. but soon reverted to Eric Clapton and all the rock classics that Indonesians all love. I don't know why, but maybe because there is a popular president here and a robust democracy they don't feel the need to stoke nationalistic pride by flag hugging all the time. 

Big news here.. but under reported in Europe is that Xi Jinping and Putin will after all be attending the G20 meeting in Bali in November. People here think Volodymyr Zelensky might be persuaded to come.
In other news, the first of our products from Turkey arrived.. Kilim Cushions & Rugs.. (I can see selling fast) readers will remember our trips there.. and my friends there is quite a bit afoot in the pipeline. 

Here in Ubud area I have been busy since we came back.. yesterday went to visit a father and son team - both mystics who have produced a range of plant based incense made with over 30 herbal ingredients that they claim detox your aurora and connect you to the spiritual world. Before our meeting they made offerings and and conducted a small ceremony. They don't speak English - just a few words, and even Indonesian is poor. Ringo spoke to them in Balinese, they have a unique incense product I have never seen before.. not a cone, or stick or coil.. now is sold almost exclusively for the temple market. Whist we were there a steady stream of jolly holy men popped in, helped themselves to a carton of stock and left money on the side.


I'm quite excited, I told them if we can make this work they will need a bigger factory and more workers.. but a lot of obstacles to overcome, we are going to need export papers and product analysis and of course packaging suitable for the EU market.. right now only in Balinese and very bad English. 
Whist I'm working Coco (between calls to China suppliers) is learning Yoga. 


Because we need to understand this market.. and Ubud is the number one place to do this.

Lots of other products on the way also.. 
And in the UK - stock arriving.. it's all go!
Hope you are finding trade improving.. 
Have a great weekend

More news next week.

David

title: Jackfruit Village
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about a secret city on Java and the giant turtle. You can read about it here.
Since then we caught a short flight to Bali and spent a mad few days working on some new products and also negotiating a deal for a new warehouse.
Sadly we will be leaving Yellow Coconut Village near Ubud. Regular readers will know about our sojourn in Nyuh Kuning, we have been there six years and in that time it has gone from being a quiet area near Ubud to being a busy urban part of the town. Getting containers in and out has become almost impossible, so it's time to pack up and go. Ringo (our man in Indonesia) has been searching for for a while for something more suitable. Just two weeks ago I received excited WhatsApp messages about a potential place not far from his family home.
The very first job after arriving from Java to Bali was to drive to the warehouse he had found. It's closer to Denpasar and not far from the main road, so containers can easily access. I was happy to learn that the address translates as in Jackfruit Village, so from Yellow Coconut to Jackfruit sounds kind of poetic. It is owned by a local family, and as is the custom in Bali, you not only have to do a deal with the owner but seek the blessing of the head of the village and the local holy man.
The place is quite run down after being empty for about a year, the last tenant was the Coca Cola distributor for Bali so it has a good roof a big yard and about 1000 square meters plus two offices, one of which could be a studio/showroom.

It's going to need quite a bit of work doing to bring it up to a decent standard, and the owners are expecting the new tenant to do that. So we met with one of the sons who showed us round and tentatively made an offer. Over a few days, Ringo was taking phone calls from all the family and village elders until we reached a deal good for everyone.
I'll spare you all the commercial details, but the social details of the lease you will find interesting.. there will have to be a ceremonial blessing and a donation to the local temple, the amount not specified only that it comes from the heart. Then there will be an annual rice tax of 100kg to be given to the village holy man once per year, we will have to plant a garden and as is the custom make the place pretty. And all this was actually written into the short unfussy lease agreement which we signed in a local Notary Office, whereas it happened the landlord's daughter happened to work. Doing business in Indonesia is refreshingly uncomplicated, do we need government approvals..? nope.. can a foreign company sign a lease..? yep, are there any taxes to be paid..? only tiny ones.

Bali is a high trust place making business easy to do. I asked Ringo what about the land registry and if the family really own the building and land, he said don't worry 100% safe - the fact that the holyman is involved means that everything is legit.

Meanwhile back in the UK.. Brexit is making things complicated. Who knows what is going to happen?
We have a huge wave of orders from our European customers as they stock up ahead of the unknown situation coming up.. this has set our order turnaround back as we try to cope. So I'm sorry about the delays currently.. we really can blame it on Brexit ..
Whatever you might think or feel about Brexit, I can tell you for our business it will be pretty disruptive on several levels. And nothing much to be done, because no one knows what the hell will happen.

Whatever will be will be.
Hope you have a peaceful and happy weekend.
Next week I'll update you on what's happening in Yiwu..
Take care
David

title: A Washout in India
content_html:
Greetings from Goa, India

Last week I was telling you about Nepal and getting high.. it was awesome.. you can read about it here.
Tomas and I took the short flight from Kathmandu down to Delhi and then on to the trade show in Greater Noida.
It's the biggest and most glam trade show in India for the gift world, Tomas's first time and I knew he would be impressed...


While I live the creativity on display and the enthusiasm of the traders at the trade show, I'm not really a huge fan. I written here about thoughts and feelings, and managed to upset Indian fans who feel I'm being too hard on them.
The fact is we like to deal with small family businesses and get closer to the actual artisans that hands on make the products. But there are some lovely things and we got quite excited by some new style incense which we think you will love.
Mr Chatterjee our man in India, has a cotton and jute factory in Kolkata area and takes a stand to show his products. We use it as our unofficial office and meeting point for some of the artisan traders who come to the show to meet us.
After the show we went up to Delhi central - where it is suddenly Real India all honking horns, rickshaws and cows and crammed go-downs in colourful and lively back streets. A world away from the polished glamour of the show but where the real Indian artisans can be found.

We do more deals here than in the show and find wonderful organised people to work with. 

It's hot and sunny in Delhi, which belies the fact the air is the most polluted in the world. A few days is enough, and I find if the air is bad it upsets my digestion and have a constant acid stomach. So it's escape to Goa time.
Delhi to Goa takes two hours something, and it's nice to be home. A friendly face picks from the airport and we make it late at night to the small village in South Goa I feel is like a home. We have lots of friends here and a small apartment that we bought about 12 years ago.
The plan is to fly in some suppliers with a carton or two of samples. Everyone loves to go to Goa, and it's great to do business by the sea. It's also a lot cheaper and more time efficient than jumping to different cites around India.
So every year at this time I visit Goa - it's the beginning of the season, pristine empty beaches, fresh air, clear sky and smiling faces. 
Except something strange has happened to the usually predictable Indian weather.. the Monsoon normally hits hard here July & August, September is a little rainy on and off.. October is the best month.. But this year got all mixed up. And this week is HUGE rain.. lashing a constant full on monsoon.. today Friday we have been given a Red Weather warning, a near-bye typhoon could hit. The seas are high and windy and it's raining like hell.. everyone says they didn't see weather in October like this in living memory. But at least the air is fresh and clean.

Mr Mehul our exotic gemstone and orgonite guy flew down from Ahmadabad.. his flight delayed by weather conditions of course.. he made it late last night, we laid his samples out in his room - amazing and beautiful things.. 
Then went for dinner in a local restaurant - lashed down windows and constant power cuts - but cold beer and amazing seafood.. Mr Mehul seems very happy to be here despite everything..  Hope we can do a good deal..

Soon it's back to the UK.. looks like Brexit is delayed.. but who knows?
Meanwhile, it is almost Halloween - and a crazy rush of orders - Christmas season orders, Halloween stocking up.. and (not least) panic buying from Europe has put our team under huge pressure. Katka tells me it's getting extreme. So I have to report we have fallen behind on the speed front. A weekend shift will hopefully help. 

More news next week.
Take care.

David

title: Lock-down? So What You Gonna To Do?
content_html:
Namaste  from day 8 of lock-down Bali. 

Last week I was telling you about Tomas leaving me here and me finding out I couldn't go to China. Also a quick round up of AW people situations. You can read about it here.
Since then, I had to move hotel, where I was, was nice but too expensive for long term even when they offered me a discount. Anyway sooner or later like all the hotels in Bali they will close. 
So I checked on Hotels.com and Booking.com to find something cheap, because like everyone else at AW I have to cut costs. Strangely no amazing deals showing up.. so I decided to just walk and ask in the other hotels nearby.. then I learned why..
"Sorry sir, new lock-down rules for hotels" .. oh what rules I asked?  "No new check-ins allowed". OMG.. I suddenly had visions of me sleeping on an abandoned sun-lounger under a frangipani tree in a hidden corner of the beach. 
So face mask on, observing social distancing (pretty easy because almost no people) I walked and walked asking in any hotel lobby that seemed open.. same story.. 

So what could I do.. I sat in an empty cafe (the only one open) and ordered a fresh coconut, and googled villa rental.. up comes a website, a villa letting agency.. A reach me by WhatsApp button.. oh joy.. minutes later I'm chatting with a nice Bali lady who is asking what my budget is.. so I start low.. "OK" she says.. "I can do that" and sends me pictures of potential places, but warns me all private villas are filling fast as hotels close.. She asks for my location and says she will pick me up in ten minutes and take me to view.. OK thanks.
Five minutes later she arrives on a funky Vespa and says jump on the back.. No!! I cry  - I can walk.. that's not social distancing, and anyway I'll get a bad back doing that.. so I walk half an hour back the way I came. She is waiting for me on the side of the road with an elderly posh lady from Switzerland, who owns a plot with eight small villa's. I'm hot and sweating, from walking in the sun and quite conscious I must look like I have a fever..


But we go and view.. just one left, it seems nice and I say yes I'll take it. I'm relieved not to homeless.
Bali is closing.. hotels are shuttering up.. many restaurants write fond love letters to their customers.. others just say "We are Closed".. 

Streets, closed up restaurants, closed up beaches.. Bali is closed.
So now I'm working from my new home, just like you and so many other people. And modern technology, it strikes me that before we were not so sure would work.. and guess what? It's working pretty damn fine.. Haha who'd have known?  After this is all over - many things will change, for sure people will travel less, shaking hands will be replaced by Namaste, we will all chat and connect more online. It strikes me that lawyers, accountants and stockbrokers won't need expensive downtown offices.. retailers won't need expensive high street sites (as sales move online) and the world will need less airline companies and airports (and extra runways) - so commercial property prices will crash and burn.. with all the grim financial consequences that will bring. I'm sitting here trying to think how this might all play out longer term. One things for sure you have to be planning what to do about it now rather than later..

So what are you doing all day?
When you are totally binged and up to-date with Netflix, BBC iPlayer, and done all you Wim Hoff (awesome no?) breathing exercises.. then what? hey, what you gonna do them hu?


Here's what.. you can invest your time in: Your Future.. build more and better online stores.. (yes more than one) and channel your creative energy into creating something special. 
And (I hear you ask) How the hell am I going dispatch orders when I can't even leave my bed?  We have the answer: AW-dropship.com now in full swing.  If you are thinking big you can even register with our Slovakia and Spain distribution centres and sell across Europe as well. 
In Sheffield, Tomas and Katka are leading our minimum team in safely working to still pick and pack your orders. Rest assured every measure is been taken.. safety first.  Just like the NHS Hero's we have our AW Hero's who are masked up wearing latex gloves and are keeping your orders flowing.
Of course signing up for our drop-shipping site is not the whole answer. I keep getting emails from people asking me what to do next? Well dear retailers.. you need to make retail sites.. you can sell on Amazon (if you want to give the evil empire all your stats) or ebay or many other similar emerging platforms. And yes you should, but ultimately you need your own online webshop. Sometime in the future there will be an AW (almost) free shop for our customers.. you can make and add AW products and your own to.. it is in the IT pipeline.. but for now.. here are my top website creating recommendations. 
My advise: Forget Presta shop and magento.. those guys are old school and bogged down with their own self importance, there are more cool systems these days..

1. Shopify  - probably the most popular these days and we are working on a plugin for this first to streamline AW dropshipping and Shopify. At $29/ month you pretty much get what you pay for but what many people don't realise with Shopify lite, (just $9/month) you can add order buttons to any site  even facebook, and sell stuff everywhere.
2. Squarespace - I have had a little experience with this, and was delighted how easy it is to make a cool website quickly. An eCommerce site starts at £20 / month. 
3. Bluepark - this I like because you can add your own payment method in the cart.. meaning your giving a cut of your sales to the platform. Gets good reviews. From £25 / month
4. Wix - this is cool but budget.. you can pretty much make it do what you want. I have played with it in it's early days and it was good then. From about £10 / month (or even free - but don't do that it's not a cool look)

NB: These are just my recommendations - full disclosure - AW nor me is getting money for your clicks so these are completely unbiased suggestions.
If you know any others that are good, let me know.. and we can share.

I don't want to upset you, but I'm reliably informed that here in Bali you can order a same day home service covid-19 test, a nurse will visit, take the test and message you two days later the result.. cost about £40.
I was thinking to get tested, for peace of mind. I have no worrying symptoms, so perhaps not. But if this service can be organised here by a private lab - why not in the UK? 

Take care and stay safe. 
More news from my kitchen table in Bali next week.

David

title: How to Make a Coconut Lamp
content_html:
Greetings from Bali.. trapped in Bali day 55 

Another week on this island, time passes quickly. Most mornings Ringo picks me up around 9am, sometimes he brings nasi goreng - Egg and fried rice Bali style and super strong local coffee.
Then we head to the warehouse (you can see a short guided tour in last weeks newsletter - here) meet suppliers, organise packing and packaging. Occasionally risk a trip to see suppliers in their workshops.
On the way, we pass police road blocks and army patrols checking where people are going and enforcing the "masks to warn outside homes at all times" rule. So far they have never stopped us, we seem to have a magic pass and get waved through.

I noticed recently the road block guys also performing another function, handing out plastic bags with food parcels into anyone who needs it. The other day we went to Ubud to catch up with three different suppliers like old times. Ubud is all but closed practically a ghost town but in the home compounds and surrounding villages handicraft production continues.


   We have a new product in the pipeline - a beautiful natural Coconut lamp, a bedside light perhaps.


The shade is made from a cotton string ball, the holder from a coconut tree leaf. Simple and beautiful.
I wanted to go and see the production in action so we invited ourselves along. This boss - a jolly guy - was delighted to show us his workshop, He met us at his showroom on the Tegallalang road just outside of Ubud, and then a short walk away down a small alley we see cotton ball shades drying in the sun then a big stack of coconut leafs, a special type imported from Java because of the leafs size and ability to be moulded. 


This really is a family business the does the finishing, his wife makes the cotton ball shades and his son is the master of shaping the leafs. 
Using a blow torch and a wine bottle the son expertly shapes the leafs.


I asked how the shades are made and he sat down to show me. Basically taking three strands of cotton and wrapping it around a small football. After the ball is deflated to get it out and pumped up again for re-use. 


They are such a jolly family, all laughing and joking as they work. Clearly happy to be busy. He told us normally he has regular orders from a French business but since the virus no re-order coming. Our order is about a container load and it will keep them occupied for about two months. They were really grateful for the business and viewed it as a gift from God. 

Meanwhile back at the AW Bali warehouse we are receiving finished stock from previous orders and have six people working on quality control and packing. The system in Bali is that the artisans don't expect to do packaging, cargo companies do this part of the process. We basically have our own cargo company - our warehouse, where I am writing this newsletter from right now. I was telling you how we made a photo-studio and made a nice office space. Next job is to make a nice staff room for our team to have lunch in. We already provide lunch from a local warung (small cafe/takeaway) and now they go off to a corner of the warehouse to eat.. social distancing. But soon things must relax here.. no new cases only 4 deaths, so I see no reason not to make the staff room as nice as possible. We started work on it today. 

Back in UK.. things are critical.. we are actually pretty busy, but finding it really hard to quickly full-fill orders because of social distancing and supply problems. We have brought almost everyone back to work, but organising everyone is a huge headache. Please bear with us as we gradually increase production in the factory and find ways to pick and pack orders more efficiently under these conditions. It's amazing that you our customers seem to be doing such a good business, but frustrating we cannot meet the orders quickly enough.  Everyone is working as hard as possible.. we are getting there.. 

Take care - stay safe.

More news next week.

David

Using a blow torch and a wine bottle the son expertly shapes the leafs. I asked how the shades are made and he sat down to show me. Basically taking three strands of cotton and wrapping it around a small football. After the ball is deflated to get it out and pumped up again for re-use. They are such a jolly family, all laughing and joking as they work. Clearly happy to be busy. He told us normally he has regular orders from a French business but since the virus no re-order coming. Our order is about a container load and it will keep them occupied for about two months. They were really grateful for the business and viewed it as a gift from God. Meanwhile back at the AW Bali warehouse we are receiving finished stock from previous orders and have six people working on quality control and packing. The system in Bali is that the artisans don't expect to do packaging, cargo companies do this part of the process. We basically have our own cargo company - our warehouse, where I am writing this newsletter from right now. I was telling you how we made a photo-studio and made a nice office space. Next job is to make a nice staff room for our team to have lunch in. We already provide lunch from a local warung (small cafe/takeaway) and now they go off to a corner of the warehouse to eat.. social distancing. But soon things must relax here.. no new cases only 4 deaths, so I see no reason not to make the staff room as nice as possible. We started work on it today. Back in UK.. things are critical.. we are actually pretty busy, but finding it really hard to quickly full-fill orders because of social distancing and supply problems. We have brought almost everyone back to work, but organising everyone is a huge headache. Please bear with us as we gradually increase production in the factory and find ways to pick and pack orders more efficiently under these conditions. It's amazing that you our customers seem to be doing such a good business, but frustrating we cannot meet the orders quickly enough. Everyone is working as hard as possible.. we are getting there.. Take care - stay safe. More news next week. David

title: The Final Custodian
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield, I'm at Ancient Wisdom HQ, this week and next.

Last week I was telling you about Village Bothering in the beautiful Ubud area of Bali. You canread about it here.

Since then I have flown from Denpasar, Bali to Kuala Lumpur, one meeting in the airport with our IT wizard who lives there and then a Turkish Airways flight to Istanbul. First time with Turkish airways and I would highly recommend - the best food and service in the air I can remember. A nice touch was an actual candle light dinner - ok led candles, and full silver service with food served by someone in a chefs outfit. And they even had wifi. It's a long time since I have been to Istanbul, but I could see from the air it's a huge city. Just recovering from an attempted coup. You do wonder.. but the airport was the busiest hub ever with huge hectic shops and everywhere a giant mad rush - thousands of folks from all over the world changing planes and heading off again. Then, I find my flight, a peaceful run down to Manchester. To England, to earth.

It's always good to come home. In fact within an hour or so it's like I never left. The team at AW are amazing, all sorts of ideas and plans. It's life at a hundred miles an hour as I try to wrestle with all the things that need thinking about and need my decisions or input on. And it's Christmas already and it real is. The amount of orders we are trying to get despatched is it seems beyond our capacity, so this week I have mostly been involved to figuring out how to speed up our picking, packing and despatch without compromising the care and quality of packing.

I need to talk to everyone and connect, to find out if the passion for gifts is truly running in everyone's veins. Because I really believe it is important to love what you do. If that is: hand crafting lavender soap loaves, or bubble wrapping bath bombs or taking pictures of Minimalist Christmas Trees from Bali... We are all artizans in a way, just like the people in India, or Java or Yiwu who make stuff, here in Sheffield (I'm sure you know) we make aromatherapy and bathroom gifts also. AW is a hub, just like Istanbul airport, carrying a million expressions of love (that's what a gift is) this way and that.. and finally we despatch to their final custodians..

That's you. The final artisans, the final custodians, delivering (retailing) the gifts of love to the, lover, the wife, the mother the son. "I bought you something" - It means.. "I love you" it means "I care" it means "I'm sorry". What does it mean to you?

Here are a few pictures of the AW hub in action.. you can find more on my instagram feed right here. Instagram

So here's the thing.. Send us your in shop pictures on instagram of facebook or directly by email of that final act of retailing gifts to your customers.
To the top fifty pictures sent this weekend we will send a free shipping voucher. And the winning picture as judged by the good folk in the marketing department, will get a bonus prize of £100 voucher to spend on the next order.
So get your smart phone snapping and save money have fun, and yes.. spread a little love. And don't forget to add your email address with your pictures so we can get back to you :)
Hope you are busy and having a great day..
Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: Big Plans on Black Friday
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

Happy Black Friday!.
Hope you are well and business is booming. Here in Spain the weather has suddenly turned cool but the sky is blue and the sun is still shining.
All around AW it's the very busiest time.. it's crazy, its manic, but it's what we like best. Absolutely not complaining.
Last week I was telling you about something magic that happened on Coco's last day here. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Now Coco is back in China and happy to be reunited with the grandchildren. She also returned to an office full of samples, (sent in by existing suppliers). She called me very excited about new designs of backflow incense burners.
And I have to send regular updates on the reformation of our terrace at home. It's coming along slowly.


A new home for our Bali statues.

Big Plans. Epic 24 Trip.
Following the huge success of our Epic India/Nepal trip early this year..which brought hundreds of new products and totally revamped our ranges. It's time to plan.. So I spent most of yesterday chatting with our India agent: Mr Chatterjee. I'm planning a trip to India and Nepal running from late January to early March.. then to China. That's if there is not another pandemic, Coco tells me all the hospitals are full and this time it is young people most affected. It's blocked in the news.. you read it here first. Hopefully all will be OK.. because the plan keeps getting more exciting. 
This time Toni (our main man in Spain) is coming, and Tomas will join later.  We plan to get to unseen parts of India and Nepal.. and go deeper and further to bring you the very best in esoteric and artisan products. 
I'm so excited already - I can barely sleep - so much research, planning and meetings to set up.. 


Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) always ready for an adventure.

Four years.
I can't believe it has been four years since the pandemic started.. We had just launched AWArtisan.eu a new warehouse in Malaga. The owner of the warehouse is a Chinese lady. It had previously been rented to Netfilx who had used it as a stage set for shooting "The Crown". Mario, our man in Spain for all things legal or administrative (our gestor) had been dealing with Chinese handymen tidying up the place.. He came down with a terrible flu, and instinctively isolated himself. he was the first person I know to catch covid - although at the time we didn't know. Coco was in Europe for Christmas and returned in January, I went to India with Tomas and all hell broke out. Almost got trapped in India. Didn't see Coco for almost two years..
Four years.. somehow seems like an age ago.


Talking to Mario in the new warehouse four years ago.

Meanwhile!
Black Friday is happening, soon it will be Cyber Monday (here's the link) and yes it's just 30 days away from Christmas!! Yes, another year has come and gone almost.
Yesterday in the UK an Indonesian container arrived.. so plenty of juicy items back in stock (see below) and some goodies as well, watch out for updates soon.
Tell you what I have noticed.. candles generally are selling like mad.. check you have all the latest in stock.. if not you are missing out big time.


 Heads up.. Chakra Gemstone Candles will sell out soon..

Anyway.. I know you are super busy.. 
Wishing you all the best for the weekend.
More news next week. 

David

title: From Crete to Istanbul
content_html:
Greetings from Istanbul, Turkey

We just arrived after what should have been two short hops, an hour from Crete to Athens and an hour and ten minutes from Athens to Istanbul. But unfortunately the first flight was delayed, we missed the connection in Athens by 5 minutes and then was rescheduled on a later flight 8 hours later (which was then delayed 2 hours). We didn't make it to our hotels in central Istanbul until 3am. But this is peak season and the airports are full stretch. 
This is life, no point in getting stressed... 
We found ourselves at the departure gate - outside the Schengen area - with no flight.. and need to go back to Greece to rebook a flight.. a very nice guy took us personally through the back lanes of Athens airport, found a policeman to un-stamp our passports, located our displaced luggage and  then delivered us to the ticket counter. There are kind people everywhere. 

Last week I was telling you about the amazing hippy town of Matala, if you missed it you can catch up here: Today is life - tomorrow never comes.
After a delightful few days it was time to move on, and hopefully do some business in a different part of Crete.. We have been chatting to Nikos (the King of Sponges) on and off since before the pandemic. Now seemed a good time to meet and see if we can plug a rather large gap in our Bathroom Heaven product range.

Yes still kind of on holiday, but actually working much of the time. WFH in our case is - Work from Holiday and a whole lot more fun.
I was comparing the island of Crete with the island of Bali..  both are heavily dependent on tourism for the economy and both islands cater for around 4 million visitors a year.
Which is the biggest by area? Crete is a bit bigger.  Which has the biggest population? Crete's population is only about 700,000 whilst Bali has about 4.5 million..  Very different places, and yet some things in common - a thriving handicraft industry built up to serve the tourists but also exported. In Bali some estimate that up to 1 million people work in the creative craft industry, certainly almost every (decent) gift shop in the western world stocks something from Bali or Indonesia. In Crete not so much.. there is however a thriving cosmetics and skin care industry, of course olive oil is famous.. and many shops sell gifts made from olive wood. I'll tell you a secret.. quite a lot of what passes for olive wood is actually Indonesian teakwood.. although I'm sure if you ask they would tell you the true source. 

One thing that is indisputably associated with Greece is the Aegean Sea Sponges. Expensive but the best quality sponges are found in the Aegean Sea.  
They make a perfect gift, and are absolutely ancient wisdom.. used by ancient Greeks and Romans for over 3000 years. There is something slightly decadent about soaping yourself down with a real sea sponge, nothing quite feels the same. The last time we was in Crete (4 years ago) Coco bought sea sponges as gifts for her family back in China and they are used daily and still in use.. 

We made friends with the, Nikos, the king of sea sponges and his lovely Yorkshire wife.. from a warehouse and factory high on a hill looking down on that blue Aegean sea, they showed us the secrets of sponges. Bought from sea sponge fishermen, they have to be cleaned, sorted, trimmed and graded. Then packaged labelled, often vacuum (to save space and shipping cost) packed before being shipped all over the world. The far east is a big market.




Obviously we need to be sure we are buying sustainable and good quality sponges. Interestingly the sponges when harvested correctly grow back better and stronger.. bit like cutting a privet hedge. An interesting thing is a sponge, not only all that ancient wisdom, but a fascinating creature. Not plant, but not exactly an animal, they have no heart or brain, but grow mushroom like. Heck there is a lot to learn about sponges.  Anyway, I think we have a deal and we should be able to bring you best in luxury quality sponges fairly soon. 

It's Coco's first time in Istanbul, and I'm keen to show her around, she will meet our agent here.. lets see what happens.
A full report next week.

Have a lovely weekend.
Take care.


David

title: Go Wild and Let's Get Cracking!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain 

Hope you are well and there is a spring in your step. There is light at the end of the tunnel, and together we are going to emerge blinking in the covid free sunlight of a new world.

Well hopefully.. 

Last week I was telling you about our big plans.. and how your creativity, positive thinking and AW can together change the world. How we can fight the whales & bully boy retailers and win. If you missed it the link is here.

For sure the first day of Spring this year is the 20th March.. Saturday.

Here in Spain, the flowers are just starting to bloom, bursting forth in a blaze of colours. In the evening the smell of night queen and jasmin in the garden is amazing. Wild garlic is growing with abandon in all the boarders - and on top of that the lockdown is being lifted. 

The wild garlic is just that.. wild.. we never planted it, or bought any.. a few years ago it just arrived, and now like a welcome weed it blooms to welcome the spring. It's everywhere.. it might be a weed but it's welcome, a pretty and useful weed.. you can cook with it.

From tonight for the first time the restaurants can open in the evenings. So there is an air of optimism.. but I'm leaving shortly..  My time here for now is almost done.. time to take a very rare flight back to the UK. 



Spring is here.. next stop is Easter. Next week even.. it's our western spring festival. Eggs, symbolic of new birth, the resurrection of Jesus, a symbol of hope. But all around the world Spring festivals express those feelings of hope and rebirth.

In India, at the first full moon of spring is the Holi festival.. but the festivals in very spiritual India have started already. Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) sent me pictures..



The Basanti Durga Puja is very famous in the Kolkata region. It is the Spring Durga Puja, the area is wild with the sound of conch shells and brightly lit pandals with extensively decorated idols of the Goddess and people wearing colourful attires and dancing to the beat of 'dhakis' lots of orange robes and flowers.. I have been there a few times at this time.. 

Mr Chatterjee tells very few cases of Covid in his area, people are still wearing masks but much more relaxed. 

 

So it's Spring, time to think big, think positive, get a shift on, get cracking (as we say in Yorkshire).

Last week I was telling you our Spring plans, and we had a huge feedback - thank you so much for all the thoughts and ideas. Lots of folk have registered at AW-Aromatic.com - even though it is still work in progress. We will be approving registrations as soon as there is something to see. But thank you all for your support and interest.  

 

Meanwhile.. drop shipping is a buzz.. if you need us to add any product you want to market and sell not already listed, just email Lucy at support@aw-dropship.com she is happy to add lines. And if you have ideas for prepackaged deals, you know.. an oil burner and wax melts set.. Do let us know.

AW Wheat bags are back.. these are a cracking Easter / spring product..easy to sell.. links and details below..

 

Lot's of things are rolling in.. Oil Burners are a great spring product line.. and we took in a lot of stock this week.. 

Plus check out the other spring deals below..

 

Anyway - I know you are busy..

Stay safe,

 

David
