title: David's AW News: NEXT UP... China
content_html:
Greetings from Dongxiang City, China

Ok… quite a week. Last week I was telling you about two dramatically different lease negotiations..one in Bali one in UK.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

I finished up in Bali in that familiar last-minute whirlwind… squeezing in meetings - samples finalised with minutes to spare.. a bit of a creative last few days rush. 

Bondhan (our man in Bali) insisted on picking me up at 6am to take me to the airport. Not negotiable - and we got to see a beautiful sunrise as we drove over the spectacular road bridge to the airport.. We said our goodbyes there… hugs, and yes, maybe a tear.


Bali airport was almost empty.. actually calm and peaceful, I think the Dubai issues are having a dampening effect.. (many flights to Bali connected via the middle east). But my flight from there with China Southern to Guangzhou landed in a massive electric storm with lots of turbulence! … and then a small surprise. 

I couldn't find my connecting flight to Yiwu on the departure screen at all, so I went to ask which gate to go to.. My connection to Yiwu? Cancelled until the next morning. No drama, just “tomorrow.” 

But then something quite unexpected… they put me up in what I can only describe as the China Southern staff hotel. Shuttle bus, straight there. I think I may have landed a captain’s room—very nice, tucked away in a smarter wing—but you could see the other side too, more basic, more functional.

Dinner was in a big cafeteria—long tables, buffet style. But really quite nicely decorated, and good food. Sitting there with pilots, crew, engineers… the whole hidden world behind a massive airline. Not something you normally see as a passenger. I asked for a beer and was met with horrified looks.. obviously off the menu in this world.

Early start the next morning, a short flight to Yiwu… and then straight into a more hectic China life. Coco picked me up at the airport and we headed off to her hometown—Dongxiang. About a four-hour drive down the G60. And just like that… a different world.


We stopped on the way at a motorway service station for KFC—China style. Familiar… but not. Different menu, different pace, families gathered, kids choosing meals… the same global brand but somehow very local at the same time. Later we pulled into what can only be described as a luxury fruit shop… honestly more like a gift shop than a greengrocer. Beautifully displayed, carefully lit, almost ceremonial. We bought durian for the family visit—serious purchase, not a casual one. In China, fruit at that level is a gift, a gesture.


Smelly but posh Durian fruit.

I haven’t been here since before Covid, and it feels more settled now and less dynamic. Feels like village life in the city.

We spent time with her family, eating proper home-cooked food—big shared dishes, everyone talking at once, that warm chaos you only get around a family table. Simple moments, but they stay with you.

And right now, it’s a special time here. This weekend is a national holiday—Qingming, or “grave sweeping day.” Families visit ancestors, clean the graves, bring food, remember those who came before. It’s quiet, respectful… but also deeply about family coming together.

It struck me how close that feels to our Easter weekend coming up back home. Different traditions, different beliefs… but the same thread underneath. Remembering, reconnecting, family, renewal.

Wherever you are in the world… we’re all doing versions of the same thing.

In a couple of days, Bryant and Sandra arrive from the UK—so the AW team will be fully assembled here. Then it’s on to Yiwu, visiting suppliers, walking the markets, chasing ideas… seeing what magic we can make happen this time.

Because that’s really what these trips are about. Not just products… but people, stories, little sparks.

From Bali artisans… to a China Southern staff canteen… to a motorway KFC… to a family table in Dongxiang… it all connects.

And in our own way, we help carry those stories forward into your shops… little pieces of the world, passed hand to hand.

And with some products from the opposite side of the world.. This week we have a super informative video from Holly explaining how to sell Smudge Sticks and Palo Santo. 

Meanwhile in the UK.. lots of new stock arrived from Nepal.

More news from China next week…

Take care, and if you’re celebrating—have a wonderful Easter weekend with your family.

David

title: David's AW News: Secrets
content_html:
Greetings from AW Warehouse, Bali

Hope you are doing well, and business is good!

Last week I was telling you about how Donald Trump delayed me and I could have missed my flight to Bali. If you missed it you can catch up here.
This week Tomas arrived and we have been working in (what we call) the beach office.. with our team of young programmers and digital marketing folk.
We have been working on a big upgrade to our system. You see AW is all bespoke, we don't use Shopify or Squarespace everything, all the backend: warehouse, stock control, websites, marketing tools it's all in-house. Masterminded and constantly reinvented by Raul, our IT wizard. It's a lot of work actually.
And today as I write we are loading a container from the warehouse here.. this one going to Slovakia. It's too hot to work later in the day, so they start loading in the early hours.. we came to check..
Tomas might just see this container in Slovakia around Christmas or New Year.. so for fun (yes I know a little bit naughty) we secretly signed our names.. to prove we could be at either end of the process.

Temu loophole closure hope.
Well I read that maybe, just maybe the dodgy de minimis loophole, that allows Temu and the like to import dangerous, untaxed and unfairly traded products directly to the UK.. that loophole is going to be closed in the upcoming budget.. LET'S HOPE SO!
As you know - it's NO SECRET - we have been lobbying hard on this issue at AW.. letters to MP's, petitions, YouTube protests and even an AI music video (just for fun) and to make a point!


So much great stock arriving!

So happy to see all the new products going online.. I think Rodrigo and team must be working like crazy.


new leather books arrived
The new leather books arrived.. I particularly like the "STOP DOOMSCROLLING"  leather printed book. 
And the new sets of Witch Spell Books in a display pack (designed by Sandra) with Ancient Witch branding.. are going to be a bestseller.. I feel.
The leather book range generally is wonderful for Christmas gifts.. Stock up now.. Your customers all need somewhere to write down their SECRETS..








  




















New "Can You Sell This? " from Holly.. she takes a deep dive into Massage Oils..


Which to me is like a blast from the past..
You see massage oils were one of the first products at Ancient Wisdom. If you have time you can read the story of Ancient Wisdom Here. 

Ancient History of AW - let me tell you a secret..
If you are a regular reader, you probably know I'm the founder and I started AW almost 30 years ago.. (the anniversary is approaching soon). From a street market in Sheffield. I sold essential oils, and soon people were asking for massage oils.. After lots of research and testing I launched a range.. I called it Massage and Bath Oil, because I thought maybe people could be embarrassed (I felt) buying massage oil. Anyway there is basically no difference it seemed to me between massage and bath oil.. why couldn't it be the same thing? 
Well I had one product I developed for my mother, who suffered from arthritis joint pains.. I called it Arthritis Ease. And it was a big success on the market, with regular customers. Much later, years later I was told we couldn't sell it because of course you can't make medical claims. I remember getting emails from old folks, regular customers complaining (I think this was about 2007) so we quietly put it back on sale, with the same formulation.. (Rosemary, Lavender, Myrrh, Ginger).. but just called it "Special A2 Mix"  - if you know you know..  and to this day we sell it! 

Ancient Wisdom has come a long way in 30 years.. I'll tell you some more secrets next week.
Meanwhile check out the other new products below..

All the best.. have a great week..
More news next Friday

David

title: David's AW News: Toni in India.
content_html:
Greetings from the banks of the Ganges River in India.

I travelled here with Toni (our man in Spain) from Bali on Wednesday. After an emotional farewell from Ringo and Bondhan we took an afternoon flight to Kuala Lumpur, changed for the late night flight to Kolkata. Arriving  just after midnight India time. It was strangely cold, I have never felt chilly in India, but Chatterjee (our man in India) was waiting with a warm welcome.
Last week I was telling you about the interesting election unfolding in Indonesia with "Trust Me" posters.. if you want to catch up here is the link.
Chatterjee had an ancient jeep-like car which bounced over the dreadful roads (busy even at 2am), honking and swerving the mighty over decorated trucks. Welcome to India, I said to the slightly shell shocked Toni.  We arrived exhausted at our small hotel in Chatteree's home town of Serampore.  And in the morning awoke to this view of the languid Ganges, clumps of greenery floating downstream and big crows in the trees crowing welcome to India... the adventure begins.



Chatterjee welcomes us at Kolkata airport. The moment Toni finally meets Chatterjee.

First job yesterday was to go and visit the factory, and review production and see if we can create some new products. We'd already sent Chatterjee and his team a selection of bags purchased in Spain for inspiration and development. So we should be off to a good start.. 
Arriving at the factory, where we treated to the usual welcome party of all the staff.. almost 40 people doing the Namaste, nice but I always think - slightly embarrassing. 
I was last here in August 2023, and the products we developed and ordered then are still in process. Some have been shipped and some are yet to be shipped, we were able to do random QC checks and I'm pleased to report the quality is excellent. I'm really excited by the products that are on the way to the UK now.. 
Drishanta, Mr Chatterjee's son has had a big impact on the business and fresh ideas and a younger outlook are really making a difference. He gave Toni a tour of the factory.


Maybe coincidence, but today almost everyone in the factory is working on AW products. Bags, Pouches and Jute Sacks.. You can see most of the existing products in our Bags & Accessories Department. We have been working with Mr Chatterjee as our India agent and with his factory a very long time. In fact.... 20 Years!
It's a twenty year anniversary.. I just realised that the first time I came to this town was 20 years ago. I remember asking Mr Chatterjee if we could visit a Jute farmer, and see how jute was produced, after we went to an ancient British era Jute mill, and we were one of the first UK companies to import all natural Jute bags to the UK. Mr Chatterjee keeps a picture of that visit in his office.
 

2004. Really, my goodness - the years pass so fast. 

So Toni is getting quite over enthusiastic in Chatterjee factory - working with the pattern guys here.. developing samples at a furious pace - busting with ideas and creativity.


Toni, Suvendu (the pattern guy) and Drishanta (Chatterjee's son). It's really good to have fresh eyes on the job. He is connecting with his team in Spain and getting our designers there involved. But we have started way too many projects, and time is limited.. 

Thank you everyone who answered our survey questions! It's really useful when you give feedback and direction. I already learned a lot from your responses, and already today acting on your suggestions and ideas.  It's not too late to add your voice.. "Help us choose products" link.. it only takes 5 minutes and helps us serve you (and your customers) better and better. 
I was really interested to see how many of you are interested in us sourcing more Indian products.. 52% which is encouraging. So here we are working on it.

Birmingham Trade Show
If you are going.. enjoy, but you won't see AW there. Regular readers and customers know why. If you don't know - it's because AW is something different to all the other wholesalers - find the answer here..

It's almost Valentine's Day - here in India they call it V-Day.. back in the UK, it's all go.. as Valentine's Day gift season kicks off the Season of Love. It's all gone seriously PINK.. check out V-Day Department at AW for best fast selling products anywhere!
And as luck would have it an India container just arrived, so lots of products back in stock and a new range of bags.. 
More details below..

Take care - hope trade is booming.
More news next week as we travel around India. 

Namaste
David

title: Grand Tour
content_html:
Greetings from Affinity Park Sheffield.

Hope you had a wonderful Easter!

 

Last week I was in quarantine , a peaceful cocoon like, quarantine in a hotel room at the Kenwood Hall Hotel in the leafy suburb of Nether Edge Sheffield. I reminded you about Rodrigo & Jess's back story (if you didn't know) and also their new baby; Freda. Rodrigo & Jess would like to thank all many people who sent them lovely messages. You can read that newsletter here.

 

I had paid extra for a test-to-release kit, which was supposed to enable me to emerge from the cocoon after five days rather than ten. But Easter got in the way, the result was slow coming. And.. so in the end it was day 9 anyway before the email arrived and I was liberated.  A little bit frustrating, I was a little tempted to go AWOL especially since I have my own lateral flow kits and tested myself.. in any case a friendly police lady came knocking on the bedroom door to remind me about the £10,000 fine and a possible ten years in prison.. erm yes that was a good deterrent.

On Tuesday morning leaping from the hotel like a spring lamb I was FREE..  Tomas picked me up from the hotel and we went on the grand update tour of AW..

 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 73,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka, Rodrigo and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken.   

 

It's almost six months since I was last here.. that's hard to believe.  When I see long standing members of the AW family, it's like no time has passed. But when I look at what has been achieved, how things have changed - I can't help but feel proud of the team.

First stop to Parkwood where Dusan (brother of Tomas and now boss of AW Aromatics) has been working incredibly hard installing new production lines, training new artisan producers and making the place buzz like a bee hive. Still struggling to meet demand but in the last six months production has more than doubled, so that's quite an achievement. I was happy to see lots of new faces and be introduced, this is a bigger achievement as we grow our AW team/family.

The three warehouse units there are now fully utilised and it's becoming clear we will need more space soon. Regular readers will know about the fire last year that burned down our main warehouse block, they are due to start the main construction soon. To coin a phrase, our landlord, Keith is building back bigger and better. When it is finished, we can either reoccupy or sublet or a bit of both. I have one plan in mind (thinking big) where we take it all back.. but this would need Keith to build to our specification - so I called him up to see if he was happy to invest in our dreams. Sure he said, but can we meet at your affinity Park site? I'd like to see it.

 

After the morning at Parkwood, Tomas and I went across town to Affinity Park. Now the entrance is via electronic gates which recognise your car reg. As the gate opens the first thing you see is the famous AW Buddha - backdrop to many group pictures at AW and sole survivor of the fire. 

Inside I see much has changed, the 6000 bay pallet racking is complete, and more importantly again many new faces. We are still working from a kind of home made office area, so the next stage is to make a beautiful work area. I have a mission to make all the work places from Indonesia, to China, to Spain, to Sheffield as pleasant as possible. A good working environment means a better place for us to care for our customers. It's the same mentality as taking care of yourself so you can care better for others.

As they (used to) say in the inflight announcements: Secure your own mask first, before assisting others. 

As humans sometimes I think we confuse self sacrifice and unselfishness above everything. Obviously good things, but you need to care for yourself first in order to do the other.. in business it's the same (if and when you can afford it). So this is the dream office.. I don't know if it will work like this but we are sure going to try..

Then Keith and his wife (and co director) Gill came to visit. We gave them the grand tour of Affinity.. and then sat down to discuss the future rebuild at Parkwood.

 

Keith & Gill have been amazing landlords, they gave us huge emotional and practical support after the fire, even turning out at 2am to help Tomas cope on that dreadful night.

People often say to me.. why don't you own your own warehouses? Well my thinking is slightly different to MST (mainstream thinking). At AW we are in the business of making and importing beautiful things and supplying them to lovely retailers (like you). That's our business to focus on - NOT the property business. Best to focus on what we do best and let the experts like Keith & Gill do what they do best. 

 

Too many (non-MST) thoughts for one newsletter!!

 

Take care, stay safe, have a great weekend.

David

 

PS: The shops are re-opening soon in the UK.. we have deals just for you.. see below..

To coin a phrase, our landlord, Keith is building back bigger and better. When it is finished, we can either reoccupy or sublet or a bit of both. I have one plan in mind (thinking big) where we take it all back.. but this would need Keith to build to our specification - so I called him up to see if he was happy to invest in our dreams. Sure he said, but can we meet at your affinity Park site? I'd like to see it. After the morning at Parkwood, Tomas and I went across town to Affinity Park. Now the entrance is via electronic gates which recognise your car reg. As the gate opens the first thing you see is the famous AW Buddha - backdrop to many group pictures at AW and sole survivor of the fire. Inside I see much has changed, the 6000 bay pallet racking is complete, and more importantly again many new faces. We are still working from a kind of home made office area, so the next stage is to make a beautiful work area. I have a mission to make all the work places from Indonesia, to China, to Spain, to Sheffield as pleasant as possible. A good working environment means a better place for us to care for our customers. It's the same mentality as taking care of yourself so you can care better for others. As they (used to) say in the inflight announcements: Secure your own mask first, before assisting others. As humans sometimes I think we confuse self sacrifice and unselfishness above everything. Obviously good things, but you need to care for yourself first in order to do the other.. in business it's the same (if and when you can afford it). So this is the dream office.. I don't know if it will work like this but we are sure going to try.. Then Keith and his wife (and co director) Gill came to visit. We gave them the grand tour of Affinity.. and then sat down to discuss the future rebuild at Parkwood. Keith & Gill have been amazing landlords, they gave us huge emotional and practical support after the fire, even turning out at 2am to help Tomas cope on that dreadful night. People often say to me.. why don't you own your own warehouses? Well my thinking is slightly different to MST (mainstream thinking). At AW we are in the business of making and importing beautiful things and supplying them to lovely retailers (like you). That's our business to focus on - NOT the property business. Best to focus on what we do best and let the experts like Keith & Gill do what they do best. Too many (non-MST) thoughts for one newsletter!! Take care, stay safe, have a great weekend. David PS: The shops are re-opening soon in the UK.. we have deals just for you.. see below..

title: David's AW News: Wish us Luck
content_html:
Greetings from (wait for it...)  Spain!


Yes, we are in Malaga. Just arrived from Bali.
Mission accomplished in Bali, we left Tomas and the team to finish the job in hand (see AW-Advantage.com).. and Coco and I have to make it to Spain for a very important event.. details below. 
Last week I was telling you about how we had to "Run like the wind" to catch the connection to Bali.. and all the running like the wind that AW teams are doing right now.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Sadly we had to say goodbye to Ringo and the team.. Hugs and tears at the airport. We took a good old Airasia flight from Bali to Jakarta, because of the time difference you arrive almost before you leave. From the lowrise provincial but lovely domestic terminal we took the Skytrain to T3. It's a quaint monorail, a little bit dinky with the driver actually just sitting in front of the carriage..  l like it.


T3 is modern and flashy just like any other capital city International airport.. We checked in without any delay at the Turkish Airways counter. Flight to Istanbul, business class, very nice food served by a real chef on board. Then we have an 8-hour connection before the flight down to Malaga, no delays, and amazingly no lost luggage. It is sunny, blue sky and still 25c in the late afternoon. It's nice to finally get home after all these months of traveling.

With a little luck by the time you read this Coco will have acquired a Spanish residence card (called a TIE) which will make travelling to Spain in the future much less hassle. We have an appointment at the local town hall in the morning and another official appointment in the police station in the afternoon. After that we just need to wait for the ID card to be made. I did it a while ago and it's the best thing ever..   
Hopefully this weekend we can celebrate with our friends in Spain. Wish us luck.

So that's the important reason to be here in Spain.. but I'm also very much looking forward to catching up with Toni and the team at AW-Artisan.eu  like the rest of AW right now they are buzzing and running and might not have time to celebrate.. but this is Spain.. 

Lots of deals.. and lots of new stock still arriving.
India Incense from Bangalore came.. check it out.. it's all next-level Incense. All sorts of new concepts, all sorts of new exotic fragrances.. Incense is having a resurgence. Regular readers of this newsletter will remember our Epic Nepal and India trip early this year.. we came across the new designs, actually from an old friend of mine who left to start his own Incense company and worked incredibly hard on these new designs. When we saw them, I called the guy and said we are coming to Bangalore to see you because we absolutely love your incense and really would love to distribute it in UK and Europe for you. He said he was more than happy to work with AW and would wait for us to come.. we secured the deal and placed a huge order.. and now it's here.. Check it out below..

Also arriving after a lot of work by our man Bryant.. are the new Himalayan Salt Cooking Plates..actually from the Salt Lamp company we have worked with for years.. they are already available in Spain and selling very well.
And just in time for the cooler weather.. cool Indian scarves.. Boho scarves that make you look like a world traveller.. we sold these years back and they are a solid staple product.. 

I'm always so excited to see new stock arrive..
And there is so much right now..

Our new Christmas fragrance products are selling really well.. we sold out of the initial production runs.. but today we have new stock  being booked into the system.. grab it while you can. And just landed catch them while you can.. the all new Festive Fragrance Sets... 

Take care and have a lovely weekend.

David

PS: Expect exciting and interesting news from Spain next week.

title: When Coco met Hatice
content_html:
Hola and Greetings from Spain.. 

It's nice to be home, and wonderful to see my favorite team (in Spain).. I just arrived so not much to report yet..
But it's crazy hot here, the air is unmoving and humid, like being in a sauna without complimentary cucumber slices..  the sweat is running down the back of my neck as I type this with my sweaty sticky fingers.. 
Last week I was in Istanbul with my wife (and your China agent) Coco having an absolutely amazing time.. (more below) and I was telling you about our last days on Crete and the journey to Istanbul, if you missed it you can catch up here. The weather in Istanbul was hot, but not uncomfortable and with pleasant breezes and beautiful sunsets.


Now Coco is back in China and I'm in Spain. We spent our last few days together in Istanbul. Regular readers will know that I have made a few trips to Turkey in the last year sourcing a new range of products and developing relationships with the locals. I really wanted Coco to see Istanbul and instead of business do the touristy things. We did however spend one day with our lovely agent Hatice.. you will remember after the terrible earthquake, the money we raised we gave to Hatice to distribute to the most needy people she knew. We stay in the same hotel that me and Tomas stay in, The Story Hotel, a small boutique hotel in the utter heart of Istanbul.  In a side street, just off the main walking street, behind the huge Russian embassy and opposite the best back-packers cafe (Varuna Gezgin Cafe) there is. I would highly recommend it if you go there. 
We met Hatice in the cafe for breakfast.. and then she took us to the grand Bazaar and around the wholesale area. So Coco met Hatice.. Our star China agent meets our newish Turkish agent.. She taught us how to use local public transport, and l we had a really good day exploring the shops and identifying plenty of potential Turkish products that might just sell like crazy in your shop. That's the plan!  


When Coco met Hatice.

Turkey is kind of crazy right now.. last time I was there there was 20 TL to £1.. this time it is 33TL to £1.... in theory that should open up all sorts of importing opportunities. But inflation is also out of control. And Hatice told us, for ordinary Turkish people this is no joke. Bitcoin and Crypto I can tell you are alive and well and booming in Turkey, slick adverts for platforms everywhere, booths on every street corner selling crypto as a potential hedge against the collapsing currency.  Istanbul city is absolutely booming, the streets are crammed with tourists and the restaurants fully booked..  but there is danger in the air, as though something terrible could happen any time.

We were doing some shopping in the main street, when out of nowhere a pro-democracy protest formed right in front of Zara.. all these gentle looking folk holding up red flowers above their heads.. The next minute a battalion of riot police, some with machine guns, are piling out of an armoured bus. Coco is so excited.. I'm saying let's get out of here.. they have guns.. she is weaving through the crowd trying to live stream what's happening on her Chinese social media (not surprisingly immediately blocked). There were scuffles with some media people and things started to get a bit hairy.. It wasn't easy but I managed to drag Coco away.. 




That was our little, slightly stressful adventure in Istanbul.. and I still didn't find out exactly what was happening.. Later, walking through a park near Taksim square, we found an encampment of riot police hidden in the trees already prepared for the next public descent.  Scary place really. 

I flew Turkish airways back to Malaga, and Coco flew Egypt air to Cairo and on to Guangzhou. Parting in Istanbul airport after 3 months of epic traveling.. we shared a glass of champagne in the business lounge, hugged and said goodbye..  so hard. But hopefully not for long.. On landing in China Coco was put in a queue to be questioned, on what she was doing while out of China, had to fill forms and upload them.. before getting to passport control.  The world is all a little crazy..

Dear reader, here's a huge heads up.. Well we have a CRAZY Summer sale right now.. The stuff that sells good in the Summer such as: Fragranced Hand & Body Lotion, Shower Steamers, Tropical Paradise Coco Bath Bombs.
I hope your world is calm and peaceful, hope you are not hot and bothered.. wishing you a great and wonderful weekend.
By next week I should have the next travel plan.. details then.

Take care

David

title: Gathering Storms from the East
content_html:
Hello everyone, last wee I was telling you about about an un-mistakable smell high in the mountains of northern Bali and those coffee cats. Since then I have been visiting suppliers in Java, spent one day in the city they call the Big Dorian - That's Jakarta - and like the Big Apple it is a modern high rise city, and like a Dorian it can smell disgusting, (but taste great).
The stock from Indonesia is beginning to arrive, and I'm delighted to see is selling very well. See below, for a new world of gifts. More containers coming soon!
Now I have landed back in China, and at the AW base in Yiwu city. I'm happy to be amongst the Chinese already missing the clean air and blue sky of Indonesia.
Yiwu is hot and muggy with a wane sun trying to break through the grey haze that hangs high over the city... Like a meteorological allegory: Exchange rates - the most dire for trade in recent history are starting to bite. I can almost feel it in the air. When the big bosses say that growth has slipped (to an obviously spun) 7% you know this country must be in under a cloud. Who knows what the real truth is. They tell me that trade is down badly , massively and in some industries drying up.
A further cloud is gathering - all the other Asian countries are ganging up. A major trade grouping is emerging, from Singapore to Burma. Including massive Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam and Philippines. They are busy forming a huge trading block, like Europe but without the mistake of the single currency - and bigger. It will rival China, because that combined area contains resources that China is having to import. You might think that these countries don't have the advantage of the hard working industrious Chinese. You'd be wrong, because as much as 20% of the population of these areas is actually ethnic Chinese and usually the business people. Furthermore where China has choked off a young population with it's one child policy, these countries in ten years will be positively youthful.
As always the world turns, the cards fall and things change. China is a mighty place, but the cards are been reshuffled.
I reported the early signs here earlier. Luxury property at heavenly prices.. all but unsold, but still with monthly rising prices. All a bit Alice in Wonderland.
But under it all are the irrepressible ordinary Chinese people. Honest, hard working and accepting of any hardship. These good people underpin the Chinese economy, whatever happens as the tectonic plates shift you have to wish that they come out of it OK. At Ancient Wisdom we will do our best as elsewhere to support the small family businesses. With your help of course.
Enough.. gathering storms..
Back home as the Olympics kick off.. we have the deals.. Gold, Silver and Bronze.
Take care.
Regards
David (In Yiwu)

title: David's AW News: Inside the Infamous Pahar Ganj!
content_html:
Greetings from Goa, India

Yesterday we escaped Delhi's honking and traffic..
India is a country of contrasts, and now we are in calm and peaceful North Goa. Where the only sound - as I write this - is of bird song.
Peacfeul Goa

Years ago we bought an apartment here to escape to. It's being renovated at the moment so we are staying in the hotel next door. 
Last week we were in Greater Noida at the big trade show. I was telling you many of the suppliers we met were not actually exhibiting except from hotel rooms nearby. So we spent a lot of time in small hotels crammed in bedrooms full of samples. If you missed it you can catch up here.
After the trade show we headed to Central Delhi. We need to check on some shipments that are about to be dispatched and seek out possible new suppliers.. 
There are many trading areas in Delhi.. but none so crazy as the infamous.. Pahar Ganj!
We love Pahar Ganj

All the travel YouTubers are rocking up here these days. It's a reliable chaotic place, with beggars and hawkers, and drugs and oxen carts. A never ending maze of alleyways dissected by the Main Bizarr the main street of the Parar Ganj that leads from the central train station into the heart of this trading area. You can see the old British Imperial Cinema in ruins at the heart of it all. 
You love it or hate it.. but end up doing both. Newby tourists come to see clutching their bags close to the chest, scared of being robbed. But in the years I have been here despite the crazinessm, the beggars and the hawkers, I have never witnessed anyone being robbed and personally feel relaxed and safe. These guys might cheat and scam you but would never outright mug you. 
I have never been here at night, after dark.. I can imagine it could be full on. There are lots of dodgy bars and clubs in the shadows and we were handed fliers offering drinking deals. Not the type of deals we are looking for.. The youtubers I have watched here are pretty naive, they have little understanding about what actually goes on.  
Hotel room.. £8 a night.

Lot's of backpackers and casual traders do small business deals along the Main Bizar - those guys are actually organised, they can link you up with shipping companies and you can get cheap shirts and hippy clothes, jewellery and exotic items back to your store in your country. But be warned. They don't care (or don't know) about proper labeling, nickel free metals, certificates etc etc. Your goods can easily get stuck in customs. Most of the traders are one time dealers, moving on to the next new-comer.. we learned our lesson years ago. Don't even think about shipping container quantities with those guys.. we spoke to one guy who lost €50,000 like that.

But turn a corner, pass through a security railing, and find clean relatively quiet streets, see the nice cars parked and organised spacious showrooms. The professionals who understand the modern export trade and have their own factories and good contacts across India. Here is where good business is done. See I tell you all the trade secrets.. These are usually small family businesses where the second and third generations - younger switched on people have become specialists in their particular products. Big business, one guy ships container loads of paros to Ibiza Spain every month. Another claims to have a contract with Zara. Yes, Delhi people are prone to exaggeration but I wanted to spend some time here and develop some new trading relations.

But after a few days of this and the noise and hassle just getting there and back from our South Delhi hotel. Enough is enough. Tomas, Mr Chatterjee and I took an Air India flight from Delhi to Goa. We arrived last night.. This morning catching up with friends here.. when disaster struck.

Well two actually.. 

Massive Storm in Kolkata: Cyclone Dana
Operations at Kolkata's Chandra Bose International Airport (I was there two weeks ago) were suspended from 6 PM on Thursday to very high winds and heavy rain. Mr Chatterjee is on the phone like all the time, organising things.. The factory is closed and everything locked down. Let's hope this thing passes without casualty.  

Website attack.. 
Our Portuguese website at AW Artisan.. had a few hundred thousand registrations starting early this morning. Raul says a very sophisticated possibly AI driven attack that got past all our (expensive) defences. Once registered, robots are trying to access and disrupt our system.. Raul has been manfully fighting it the last few hours. At one point it took down the main server - it's back up now. But as I write the attack continues.  No other websites have been attacked (yet) but Raul and his team are on it.

Meanwhile back in the UK.. a huge wave of NEW Indian products have been arriving.
Rodrigo and team have so much they have been actually struggling to get them all online. But wonderful new Incense ranges including exclusively for AW a beautiful artfully packaged range of Buddha incense I'm particularly excited about.

I can't believe it's already the last Friday in October, and this weekend the clocks go back.. Halloween is practically here!
It's all go go go.. check out the very special deals we have for you including FREE Halloween bath bombs if you move quickly.

OK I have to go.. There is a Gemstone Guy down from Gujarat with his samples waiting for me in his hotel room almost next door.

Have a lovely spooky and fun weekend.

Namaste from India

David

title: David's AW News: 29 Years - A Crazy Thank you!!!
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


Last week I was explaining why we bought a Buddha oven. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Malaga survives!
It's raining, it's pouring .. massive storms in Spain. Our warehouse in the epicentre.. lots of damage in Malaga as an unbelievable amount of rain falls.
Toni and the team were ordered to take the day off on Wednesday. On Thursday they came to work to discover part of the roof blown off, water flooding the floor and so we have suffered some water damage.  But they guys got to work cleaning up and sorting out damages, they were picking orders by 10am and like the rest of Malaga picking themselves up and getting on with it. 
Despite the sighting of a massive tornado off the coast of Marbela and huge winds, my house on the coast survived unscathed, and on Thursday morning 4am I'm calling all my friends there to make sure they are ok.. it seems ok but with some lucky escapes. Thank God.
Then yesterday - after work back to my villa in the evening. It seemed like a nice evening for a walk to find dinner. Then distant rumbling thunder, a flurry of hailstones then suddenly big fat raindrops are falling. Within minutes the sky is black and then it rains in an absolute deluge. There is sheet lightning,  and then the loudest thunder clap I can ever remember, walls shake and my eardrums hurt.  
This morning I noticed that pot plants with palms have been blown flat and my eardrums still feel tender.  A volcano on a neighbouring island is erupting, displacing thousands of people and many flights have been cancelled. So the world is like this. These days.
But life goes on and even though my time here is short, I have been catching up with the marketing teams. Reinventing SEO and pay per click because AI is a massive upheaval in this field. 
I also want to finish a couple of products (that I know are trending) and we really should have. It's important to stay ahead, no?

Future plans.
Our man here, Bondhan, has been telling me about a small city in Java. Apparently there are many family businesses making textile products for export. He visited last month and already made some interesting contacts, I'm keen to develop this area of business within AW. We are already doing quite well with yoga pants, and watch this space for very cool t-shirts. Coming soon.
We are already planning a trip next year.

It was 29 years ago!
Important News - Thank You!
Well tomorrow actually.. when I started Ancient Wisdom and sold my first bottle of lavender oil on a street market in Sheffield town center.
There is quite a back story, and so much has happened over the years. But the first day (16th November 1995) was a disaster and I almost gave up..

It was a wet cold Thursday morning a long time before Google and Facebook, and as I laid out my market stall on a Sheffield street I was more than apprehensive about what people would think. But I was ready by eight, my humble offering laid out on that simple stall.. and stomping from foot to foot I awaited my first customer.

A few months earlier, I'd been reading a book called "Ancient Wisdom" - now out of print. The book highlighted many things that seem out of place in history - the pyramids, Stonehenge etc. At the same time I'd been researching aromatherapy. It struck me that essential oils had been used for thousands of years and ancient people must have known more about them - (healing and enchanting) than perhaps we did. So I put the two together and devised the brand of "Ancient Wisdom" slowly (very slowly, no Internet remember) I found supplies of oils. I found a potter down in Stoke who made me my own design of oil burner, and invested in a pallet load of candles.

The truth was I was stone broke, every penny and more I put into my unusual retail business. In those days no-one had any idea what aromatherapy was, oil burners were a new fangled thing and this was Yorkshire! The first person to approach was a well built lady of colour with a broad Yorkshire accent. Picking up a bottle of Lavender oil she asked me bruskly "what's it good for lad?" Oh I said recalling my Julia Lawless quotes.. "it's good for relaxing, will help you sleep and if you burn yourself it's an amazing healing oil".

Well I can remember it clear as day.. she looked at me, took me in with big brown eyes, and in a low voice said; "You are completely bloody bonkers". And wandered off to the fruit and veg.
You can imagine how I felt. That first day I sold one lavender oil and gave some tea tree away to a spotty teenage girl. I went home and almost packed it in...

If you have time you can find out what happened next and catch up on the rest of the colourful journey that AW has taken here. 

Rodrigo and the team in the UK around this time of year get quite excited; they want to do something remarkable to celebrate.. I said let's wait until 30 years.. but after much discussion we basically decided to go a bit crazy.. I guess it's my way of saying thank you for the last 29 years, without your support AW wouldn't have come this far. So thank you!

So here we go.. GOING A BIT CRAZY / BIG THANKYOU
We already have BLACK FRIDAY (prep) DEALS with upto 50% off
Add to that..
STOREWIDE Minimum 15% OFF everything. EVERYTHING! (for goodness sake)
 And then.. just for good measure for our 29th Anniversary weekend.. thank you so much..
29% OFF 29 Best selling Product Families.. on our 29th birthday.
====================================================================================

So Tomas is in the UK now and has been working hard.. he pulled off a deal to help you..
SO.. we have a new deal with our BNPL partners especially for you our customers.. It's called Purchase Hub. from Pastpay.
It's to help our customers THINK BIG.. and take advantage of opportunities when they come along.. (like above). Upto £16,000 credit could be available to you.
Now you can login and see just how much credit you have and the system helps you to plan carefully your expansion plans.
Literally you can stock up now and pay in 2026. How good is that?  


Little update from Bali.
Yesterday Ringo and his team celebrated dispatching another Container. With at least two more to dispatch this month.. so lots of stock early next year.
Coco despatch two containers this week.. with another 3 or 4 to go.. 
We have lots of lovely products in the pipeline..lots of retail opportunities.. these days with AI changing the retail landscape I believe there are more opportunities opening up all the time.. 

So meanwhile in the UK..  new stock arrives every day... and I know they are working hard to get stuff online. 
I'm expecting a big shipment of exciting new Nepal products any day now.

Hope life and business are going well for you..
Not long until Christmas.. 

Take care

David

title: Dancing in the dark
content_html:
Greetings everyone. I'm still in China, and desperately trying to get anyone interested in the Olympics. When it was in Beijing there was near universal frenzy. Now it's in some far off little island off the coast of Europe it hardly seems worth getting active about. The opening ceremony can't possibly compete with Beijing, and when I point out that we might not have cash to flash, but we are damn-sight more original, entertaining and artistic.. I might as well have insulted the national pride. But they declare emphatically as if playing a trump card we Chinese are just more energetic. And on this point I cannot argue.
I read in the Times that 63% of British people are classified as inactive. They are hoping the Olympics will inspire us to get off our lazy backsides and do the hurdles or long jump of an evening rather than slumped in front of the box watching Corrie. I don't know what the inactive percentage of Chinese people is but I'd like to bet its close to zero.
As far as I can see the average Chinese person is up early doors, breakfast in cheap cafe en-route to work, ten hours then a meal.. latest about 6.30pm in some hectic cafe on the way home. Whereas in Europe we like to linger after food, chatting, order another coffee, perhaps a brandy. The second they have finished eating its.. OK then we are off. Bill please. And what do they do after dinner, of an evening.. let me tell you 99% do dancing in the dark.
Really. Back in the UK parks are hardly occupied after dark, if they are we don't really want to know what goes on. In China, all over China after dark a billion folk have got themselves dressed nicely and hit the parks to dance. Flamenco, tango, classical, disco and some strange Chinese line dancing that they seem to love right now. In the park next to my apartment, I counted twenty dance classes, some with as many as 200 members. Young folk and very old, children and teenage girls. Its all very friendly and jolly. The foreign guy (me) is waved at and invited to dance, old ladies want pull me in. So much energy been expended it made me feel faint.
Each dance group has a sufu.. or master who will charge you about 1000rmb (about £100) for a years membership, but a night or two for free is fine. They bring the music, a blurry amp box and the cool moves. With some of the groups I really couldn't work out who was the sufu and what music they were dancing too, maybe if you just copy the person next to you it kind of evolves like a huge Chinese dancing whisper. I have a video from my phone to give you little idea of the nightly madness
All that surplus energy. Maybe it explains why China has done so well and the balance of wealth in the world is slipping east. Everyone is so worried about GDP and balance of payments, I think we should make everyone eat with chopsticks. It's worth a try.
Talking about energy, on a more serious note I was really moved by a TED talk I recently watched.Jane McGonigal is a game designer with an amazing tale to tell. By the way if you need a little extra positiveness (and who doesn't) I can recommend an hour or two on the TED website. :)
We are celebrating the Olympic opening with as much positive energy as we can muster.. in the form of a whole raft synchronised all dancing all singing special deals.
More good news: we had three containers delivered this week, from Indonesia, China and Thailand. See below.
Take care.. wishing you an happy and energetic Olympics.
David

title: It's a Strange World
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

It's day 83.. and still no sign of relaxing the travel restrictions.
I could fly to Spain, there are flights to Jakarta and from there via Istanbul to Malaga. Coco, my wife is in China and it seems like I'm heading the wrong direction. So not over keen.. anyway the flights only start in July so will have to wait a bit. You can read last week newsletter here.
To be honest the thought of taking a rapid test, before flying - navigating several airports and travelling all that way in a mask, doesn't fill me with excitement. My visa in Indonesia expired a long time ago, but the government simply declared that all visa's were automatically extended until further notice... but the website that states this has not been updated since April, so I worry. I have never over stayed a visa in my life, and I don't want to get in trouble. The prisons here are famously bad.
Ringo just called the immigration office.. and..

In the day I'm working with Ringo, we are making amazing products. In the evenings in touch with the UK office, so the days seem to fly past.
In the pharmacy here they sell all sorts of aromatherapy blends - everyone uses them, apply to mosquito bites, achy bones, forehead when you have a headache, can be used for massage oil even. Ringo always has a bottle in his car and I started to take an interest, because this is basically aromatherapy, but local Bali style. The one he uses is called Kutus Kutus, which means 88 in Balinese language, it's made locally - very local to our warehouse and they already have it turns out an EU distributor. Another popular oil is Varash Classic, also produced not so far away... this oil is more expensive but less greasy on the skin. I love it, the aroma, the texture the whole marketing concept that goes with it. 


My desk and the oils.

There is actually an ancient Balinese culture of blending local essential oils to make "healing" oils. I tried the Varash oil on my mosquito bites, and was amazed that they healed in a day and stopped itching in seconds. 
So this week we made an appointment to see the boss at the office they have in Denpasar.. 
In the affluent suburb of Renon - all leafy villa's and embassy buildings. There is a park with an impressive statue in the centre, the area around the park is very posh.
The offices of Varash are built to impress, we were left to wait in a reception area with walls painted with mythical scenes, a large flat screen TV showed a sales conference in full swing with a thousand people, a rock band, a professional compare.  The reception area reminded me of the incense companies we visit in Bangalore, India. Just a bit too flash.

The staff all in company uniform, young and smiling arrived.. we were taken to a board room for the meeting. The boss was away but a team of executives could help us.. 
Of course, I realised the set up by then.. Varash is distributed across Indonesia.. by the MLM system.. just like Amway and Herbalife. My heart sank, this was going to be hard work. I explained that we wanted to buy factory direct and have a distribution agreement for Europe. Ringo translated, their English was not that good, they looked blank. So it seems they have never exported the product beyond Indonesia, they didn't need to because Indonesia is a huge market... 260 million people.

I explained the concept of sole distribution, we would give them a decent initial order, say $20,000 and contract to buy a minimum amount over a year. In return we could have the exclusive rights to distribute in Europe, if we failed to meet the minimum they could pass the rights to some other company..  so what do you think guys?  Bemused and slightly blank looks..   I think you might need to talk to the boss?  Yes, please.. can you organise a meeting?
So now we are waiting for a meeting, but I fear the MLM system is too lucrative and they won't want to do old fashioned trading. But we will see what happens. Meanwhile I'm investigating a few other companies and products.

Meanwhile in the UK, we remain super busy.. Tomas, Katka and the crew have been working like crazy to make a system to cope with the business and with some success, we have been gradually catching up this week, not yet back to next day delivery (it's almost a dream) but now things a buzzing along sweetly.

Oh and yes.. the call to the immigration office.. No problem at the moment all and every visa is automatically extended until further notice... so I can stop worrying. Until when I ask? Even we don't know said the lady at the office.. it's a strange world.

I hope you are keeping safe and well.  
More news next week .. probably from Bali. 

David

title: Dreams Audit
content_html:
Greetings from Surenpur on the banks of the Ganges. I'm in jute territory working with our main jute products supplier Mr Chatterjee. This is what I call real India, and probably one of the poorest area's we do business. It is a long way from the nearest five star hotel, so you don't get many NGO's here, or at least I have never seen any. But if ever a place needed help it's here.


The people are gentle and thoughtful, not in any sense pushy. I once was taken to meet the local chief of police, a muscular guy and a keen Manchester united fan, he told me that as areas go there was virtually no crime, and his biggest problem was crashes in the narrow streets. Other than that they often had problems with homeless children. A combination of high mortality amongst the poorer people and domestic fall outs often leave young children on the streets. He told me there were gangster types who tour rural areas offering money to "take care" of homeless children.
These unfortunates can end up in the big cities tapping on your taxi window begging for coin. He told me they take them to Mr and Mrs Kundo who look after about twenty five children in a small shack that had been donated by a local businessman. The police guy told me that the Kundo's were really good hearted people, and as honest and decent as they come. They give the children a sense of family and ensure they attend school.


That afternoon Mr Chatterjee and me went to see.. Mr Kundo was truly a kind hearted guy and the kids seemed clean and cared for. On first glance all seemed good, a nice location on the edge of town overlooking a tranquil lake. But on closer inspection the shack was barely standing, the only running water through the leaky roof, food cooked on an open fire and no toilet facilities. Washing and ablutions performed in the lake. All they asked for was the roof fixed up because in the monsoon, nowhere was dry.
Two years on and we have fixed the place up a bit. A complete new roof, a proper kitchen, shower and toilets. Running water was a challenge they said it couldn't be done, but Mr Chatterjee found a way.
There is lots more to do, next step is to employ an English teacher, the local school don't offer more than very rudimentary English. And spoken English is one of the best routes to a decent job in India..
The kids are always excited and delighted to see me, and now it is mandatory that the first job on arriving in town is to visit the children's home, shake hands, see how they are doing, inspect the latest works and take pictures.
This time I was interested in taking stock of the kids. There is a hardcore of about twenty children and always someone being repatriated with family and new ones, eyes still untrusting, learning to fit in.
I wanted to know just five things, their names, how old they were, how long they had been there, if they had a parent where they were and what they did and finally and most importantly I wanted to know what they wanted to be when they grew up. I'll tell you why later.
Great excitement, there is a bit of jostling for position. Mr Kundo finds an exercise book and sitting on a stool by the lake we start taking stock.
If parents existed, they were in far off towns, all were from broken homes, parents jobs were the like of rickshaw puller or street vendors.

Ages from five to fourteen, they have been living in the shack between one week and seven years.
We have ten budding policemen, probably because of the kindly cops who rescued them and brought them here. Six prospective teachers (like Mr and Mrs Kundo), three army types, two engineers, two cricketers, an electrician and one doctor.
Not bad, not one kid wanted to be a rickshaw puller, and some excellent choice of careers. But now we have a stock figure of expectations and dreams. I wanted to know if anyone wanted to be a businessman like Mr Chatterjee, no-one had thought of that.. I'm feeling a bit put out :(
Next year, we will see if we can raise dreams and expectations, because as I always say; "If you don't have a dream how can you have a dream come true?".
If you want to help.. it's easy just stock some Freedom product lines.. see below.
Until next week.
Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: Lost Moon Bowls came home.
content_html:
Greetings from Ancient Wisdom HQ.. Sheffield


It's all happening this week, and a bit of drama as we almost lost our Full Moon Bowls.
Last week I was telling you about the Lokta paper that just arrived, and how the new Dropshipping website is launching.. If you missed it, you can catch up here:
It's July already.. I can't believe how fast this year is flying by.. and on the 1st of July (that was Tuesday), we welcomed a new team member.. Holly.. who is our new social media manager. 

These days a very important job. Holly is a keen yoga enthusiast and instructor, so already halfway an Ancient Wisdom team member.
An Indian shipment of Gemstone Tree Gardens - some with Yoga figures just arrived.. so it seemed a good fit for Holly to make her first social media about this collection.

 https://youtu.be/FkwipLyGKDc
So a BIG welcome to Holly, if you have time please check out the above YouTube and send Holly some encouragement, feedback or just say Hi.. in the comments..
Thank you  and you might even like the new collection.

Well, we had a bit of drama this week.. 
A shipment arrived from Nepal.. 155 cartons, pretty much a full truck load. It came by air (everything from Nepal comes that way). I don't know if you know this, but generally shipping rates from Nepal are cheap, I think probably subsidised or controlled by the government there. Nepal is landlocked, of course, and sending by sea is possible via India, but is very slow, bureaucratic, and you need to wait for a full container load to be ready.. We have done it, but it's very hard work. This shipment by air came in at £1.50 per kg, that compares with current China rates at about £5. Of course, you need decent volume and a good shipping agent to make this happen. 

Anyway, Mr Padam, our lovely Nepalese shipping agent, consolidated our orders, packed and arranged shipment from Kathmandu, to Istanbul to Manchester airport with Turkish Airways. All the export documents sorted, packing lists, etc sorted. The stock arrived on Monday morning, I was quite excited - a full truck load.. I went to see it unload..
Big mess!
Alarm bells started ringing when we saw a jumbled mess, cartons had been slung on the truck, badly stacked and not secured at all. Our guys unloaded the truck, and the second the last carton was off, the driver was hassling to get a scrap of paper signed, offered no copy and was away like the wind. We made a big mistake not getting a copy, and he was away.
Sure enough.. There were ten cartons missing.. and those cartons were the most expensive.. our Full Moon Tibetan Singing Bowls..
Lost.
James was on it.. but the shipping company said we had all the stock. Gave us the full fob off.. Lots of calls, no joy.  I was so depressed.. We checked the CCTV.. We got pictures of the guy running away. 
Mr Padam found us proof of shipping in Kathmandu, in Istanbul and Manchester airport.. and even customs clearance confirmed the amount. 
Anyway, to cut a long story short.. James went to the airport, to personally check.. and guess what - in the back of the warehouse he found 10 cartons.. about £5k stock actually.
So your singing bowls finally came home.

Also on the shipment was the long-awaited Lokta paper notebooks.. We made a video about that company in Nepal.. so very happy to see that stock here.
I made a video about it.. https://youtu.be/oKUTDDLJNwQ

More details below..

Anyway, got to rush.. It's Tomas' birthday today, so we are having a little celebration..

Wishing you an amazing weekend, I hope the British sunshine comes through again.

Take care of more news next week. 

David

title: Crazy Crazy times
content_html:
Greetings from the pretty town of Trnava, Slovakia.

Last week we were in Istanbul on the edge of Europe, checking out the giftware buying opportunities there. Which I have to say was way beyond my expectation (details below).
I was telling you about all the flags in town and how Istanbul was nothing at all like we expected, if you missed it you can catch up here.
We soon bailed out of the trade show when we discovered that you could find things cheaper in the retail shops than the tradeshow and started making contact with local family businesses. Originally we planned to stay 3 days but extended another 3 to try and make some deals...
But we had to go... Slovakia calling, they had just finished making an epic move from our modest warehouse to a brand new custom built massive crazy big shed. This will be our home for the next 15 years. So we took Turkish airlines from Istanbul to Vienna and from there by car across the border into Slovakia and to Trnava.


I love Trnava - it's nice to be back.

Although Turkey is not that far from Slovakia, culturally it is a different world. For example in the tradeshow the booths were a cross between showroom and a cafe, some even had apron clad baristas on hand serving Turkish tea or coffee. In Europe we get down to business quickly, but here doing business and establishing a level of trust is an elaborate courtship. The way it works is they are not going to wheel out the best deals to strangers (who might be spies) first you have to drink tea and sound each other out, eventually when you have been forced to consume platefuls of baklava - massive overload of delicious honey pastry and sugar snacks -  eventually when you have bonded, only then will the best prices emerge slowly. 

So we were a little shocked to find that in the Grand Bazaar - a tourist trap if there ever was - the price before negotiations was cheaper than in the tradeshow. Wow.. this is a topsy turvy crazy world. It can partly be explained by the massive financial crisis that Turkey is going through right now. The value of the currency has collapsed in the last year, so this in theory should make exports cheap. Turkey is running out of reserves and ever more extreme extreme measures are been taken by the government. I'm not sure what I expected but what we found was a boom town, traffic jams, cafes and restaurants full, hotels expensive and fully booked, streets crammed with shoppers. The only cracks on view where rumours of protests downtown, taxi drivers telling us it was impossible to go to such and such an area right now. Lots of foreign exchange booths had been converted to cryptocurrency shops and seemed to be busy. The ATM offered USD and EURO as well as local currency. A city on the edge..

But we made a few friends and discovered nice people willing to help us find the genuine family businesses we like..  Turkey has a hammams, Turkish baths.. and so a cotton textile industry.. so spa towels, robes, bath towels etc. Lots of craft soap and cosmetic preparations.. Also wonderful tea mixes and other exotic herbs. Actually lots that fit in with existing AW ranges and I feel could bring a breath of fresh air to your stores and online shops. We will be back to finalise some deals soon.

Here in Slovakia we found a team slightly bewildered by what they had just done.. led by Tomas - often at a distance - they have achieved miracles, and managed to move from our warehouse of five years into this big mega shed - it's a bit crazy. The old warehouse cleaned repainted and handed back to our lovely landlord with no drama, a French company are already moving in.. the new place is almost finished - workmen are still working around us fixing windows and the finishing touches. No drama.

I have to say I'm so proud of the team here.. they are a little serious in that Eastern Europe kind of way, but super professional and hard working. Definitely my favourite team in the way they cope with any challenge without drama and just make it happen.  We left our original home and moved to the next stage of growth, it's like AW Gifts has grown up. From a warehouse that became way too small for our level of trade to one.. we are rattling about in..  and at this moment in time when sales are a bit subdued, (although we are still up on last year), it's easy to think "have we done the right thing?" 
Even I look at it and think OMG.. this is crazy, I have to go and check the sums again.



Yes! I tell them of course we have! We got a fantastic deal on this super shed.. it will enable us to be Europe's top giftware wholesaler and open up a world of opportunities - I make a speech that would have had the Spanish or UK guys bouncing off the walls and whooping with joy.. here they just nod seriously and scratch their chins. There are things to be worried about these days.

And I guess many of you will be feeling it also. Maybe it is the looming cost of living crisis but I think it is something else, more like a shift in focus. Tourist shops are doing good.. 

What is hot right now?
So somethings are selling well, notably bags, backpacks, wearables like bangles etc (because people are out and about). And for some reason anything gemstone related is selling very well indeed. Here is Slovaka by far the best seller is the Craft Soap Flowers..  as I guess shops get creative and make their own products in response to the cost of living crisis.

Meanwhile..
In the UK great excitement at the Jubilee celebrations, which should be a right royal knees-up and lighten the mood. Also not far away is Father's Day.. 
In Turkey where inflation is off the scale and everything is going pear-shaped, they are in the next stage.. where folk suddenly realise that it's better to spend money now whilst you still can because later it will buy you even less than today. Crazy no?

So cheer up.. Crazy times but at least we have some great deals and opportunities for you - see below..

More news next week.

David

title: Smudge Sticks & Yorkshire Tea
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield - AW HQ..

I'm actually here at the beating heart of AW, where it all happens! A veritable bee hive of creativity and giftology.. 
At the weekend I flew down from Malaga to Manchester - all week I had been hearing about how the UK was enjoying/suffering the hottest weather on record, so I didn't dress warm.
Arriving in Manchester it was a shock to find it cold and raining.. such is live.
Last week I was telling you about a new warehouse in Spain, you can read about it here.

In the UK we also have warehouse problem.. we really don't have enough space. As we have expanded and grown and gradually taken on other units in the business park, we have reached a point where no more units are available.. It's very frustrating and very hard work for the warehouse team. Many of the isles between the racks are blocked and that means it's difficult to get the forklift trucks in to every area. So when we pick your order, and something is out of stock, because the replenishment stock is high in the racks we can't get it quickly - so orders have to wait an extra day or so until that particularly area is cleared. So to cut a long story short.. to speed up your orders we need more space. 

Guess what? Everyone it seems is looking for more space, blaming Brexit stock-piling as the reason. We went to look at nearby warehouses, even went knocking on doors of near by "big" warehouses asking if they have spare space to rent. But to no avail.
In the end we are fast-tracking a plan to pull out some small racking put in big racking, add a mezzanine floor and possible erect a permanent tent style warehouse in the car-park. 

Meanwhile.. it's like Smudge stick central here.. sometimes you get a new product that almost everyone orders of the bat, you look at the orders being packed and everyone contains a pile of Smudge Sticks..
So what the heck are Smudge Sticks? And why are people just so enthusiastic?

I have done some research.. and condensed here all what you need to know to tell your customers..

1. Although smudging is fairly new in Europe, the practice of burning sage is in fact an ancient tradition.-  I was in Greece recently and seen big bundles of sage where it has been used in rituals since the ancient Minoans.. 
2. First practised by Native Americans, like Dream Catchers and taken up by spiritually connected people world-wide. Many combine Singing Bowls with Smudging Rituals.  
3. Smoke and incense is regarded as spiritually powerful in many cultures for thousands of years -so it really is an Ancient Wisdom practice. 
4. Witches, shamans, holy-men and mystics commonly burned sacred plants and used their smoke to ascend to the heavens; a way to connect the material and spiritual worlds. Now you can connect your customers to this most ancient of things..
5. People do smudging typically before or after a significant events, such as moving into a new house, weddings, birthdays etc. To protect, to balance, to clear.. So a perfect gift for a special occasion. 
6. In many traditions, smudging involves a four directions ceremony or prayer, i.e. the sending of smoke or prayers in the four points of the compass. Soooo.. you can also sell compasses 
7. Our Smudge sticks are the real deal, hand made in Mexico and California.
8. The Romans considered Sage a sacred herb and associated it with Wisdom.. so there you are Ancient Wisdom in action once again :)


Some people also use Gemstones within the rituals.. 

Also check out AW  Palo Santo ‘sacred wood’ burning ceremonies are still practised in the present day. We have good stocks of this Holy Wood.
And.. from mystic India a new range of Orgonite Desk Power Packs.. truly esoteric, really beautiful and a perfect gift.

Meanwhile this Thursday was Yorkshire Day, so to all Yorkshire folk (ee bye gum) we know everyday is actually a Yorkshire day! but cheers - here's to a nice pot of Yorkshire tea.
Not far from here in Derbyshire a major flood drama is unfolding in Whaley Bridge - a place I know very well, a Victorian dam wall is under danger of collapse and the whole town could be washed away. Chinook helicopter is desperately dumping rubble to block water running into the dam. We wish them well and hope all is going to be OK. I can remember even as a child walking near the dam and being told that it was unsafe and one day would break.. hope now something will be finally done to invest in this area. 
Flooding is affecting many area right now.. we send love and blessings. To all those climate change deniers - Greta is coming for you!

I'm writing this after a Big Breakfast with all the team at AW.. as a special thank you to all the hardworking guys at AW we ordered in from a local deli a slap up breakfast, Yorkshire tea and had a jolly good chat before work.
It's also a big goodbye as I leave tonight for Asia, but first stop is Africa, it's back to Marrakesh.   Regular readers will know I was there with Coco a few weeks ago and searching out potential suppliers.. time to go back and meet suppliers.

Full report next week.

Take care, hope you have a good week.

David

Meanwhile.. it's like Smudge stick central here.. sometimes you get a new product that almost everyone orders of the bat, you look at the orders being packed and everyone contains a pile of Smudge Sticks.. So what the heck are Smudge Sticks? And why are people just so enthusiastic? I have done some research.. and condensed here all what you need to know to tell your customers.. 1. Although smudging is fairly new in Europe, the practice of burning sage is in fact an ancient tradition.- I was in Greece recently and seen big bundles of sage where it has been used in rituals since the ancient Minoans.. 2. First practised by Native Americans, like Dream Catchers and taken up by spiritually connected people world-wide. Many combine Singing Bowls with Smudging Rituals. 3. Smoke and incense is regarded as spiritually powerful in many cultures for thousands of years -so it really is an Ancient Wisdom practice. 4. Witches, shamans, holy-men and mystics commonly burned sacred plants and used their smoke to ascend to the heavens; a way to connect the material and spiritual worlds. Now you can connect your customers to this most ancient of things.. 5. People do s mudging typically before or after a significant events, such as moving into a new house, weddings, birthdays etc. To protect, to balance, to clear.. So a perfect gift for a special occasion. 6. In many traditions, smudging involves a four directions ceremony or prayer, i.e. the sending of smoke or prayers in the four points of the compass. Soooo.. you can also sell compasses 7. Our Smudge sticks are the real deal, hand made in Mexico and California. 8. The Romans considered Sage a sacred herb and associated it with Wisdom.. so there you are Ancient Wisdom in action once again :) Some people also use Gemstones within the rituals.. Also check out AW Palo Santo ‘sacred wood’ burning ceremonies are still practised in the present day. We have good stocks of this Holy Wood. And.. from mystic India a new range of Orgonite Desk Power Packs . . truly esoteric, really beautiful and a perfect gift. Meanwhile this Thursday was Yorkshire Day, so to all Yorkshire folk (ee bye gum) we know everyday is actually a Yorkshire day! but cheers - here's to a nice pot of Yorkshire tea. Not far from here in Derbyshire a major flood drama is unfolding in Whaley Bridge - a place I know very well, a Victorian dam wall is under danger of collapse and the whole town could be washed away. Chinook helicopter is desperately dumping rubble to block water running into the dam. We wish them well and hope all is going to be OK. I can remember even as a child walking near the dam and being told that it was unsafe and one day would break.. hope now something will be finally done to invest in this area. Flooding is affecting many area right now.. we send love and blessings. To all those climate change deniers - Greta is coming for you! I'm writing this after a Big Breakfast with all the team at AW.. as a special thank you to all the hardworking guys at AW we ordered in from a local deli a slap up breakfast, Yorkshire tea and had a jolly good chat before work. It's also a big goodbye as I leave tonight for Asia, but first stop is Africa, it's back to Marrakesh. Regular readers will know I was there with Coco a few weeks ago and searching out potential suppliers.. time to go back and meet suppliers. Full report next week. Take care, hope you have a good week. David

title: Chatty News
content_html:
25th January 2013

Hi ,
I have spent this week in Spain, at our sister company here.
The one thing you can say about southern Spain is that it's the best place to get a decent English breakfast. :)
Apart from that, at least it's not knee deep in snow, although the mountains are frosted. In Blighty it's all we talk about, the weather I mean. But here in AW Spain they will talk about anything.. all the time. They love to chat.
So I shouldn't have been surprised when we booted up the new chat feature we have on the UK site in Spain (bottom right-hand corner of the page), within seconds customers were communicating with us, like ducks to water.
In the UK about one in twenty visitors will use it. In Spain it's about one in eight.
I also read that despite the dire economic weather the Spanish are the most prolific users of smart phones in the world. Yep they all seem to have very fast thumbs. This brings out the amateur anthropologist in me. I love to compare cultures as I'm travelling. Must check all our euro sites we have to see which race is most chatty on-line.
Meanwhile back at base things are warming up..(at least in-doors) lots of new stock arriving for the spring. Three containers over the next few day.. Forgive me I get exited about such things. It's just that all that work months ago finally comes together when the stock is delivered and goes on-line.
Nothing makes me more happy than when you (our customers) like the new lines. That's my job satisfaction. Do let me know what you think.. feel free to chat!
Next week, I'll be in (completely snow free) India. News from there.
Take care, keep warm, happy trading.
David
