title: David's AW News: Spain an Emotional Update
content_html:
Greetings from La Cala de Mijas, Spain


Wow I feel like I have been running around like crazy, I just landed in Spain three days ago exhausted. And last night we had the AW-Artisan Christmas party..

Last week I was telling you about my last days in India after a quick trip to Kathmandu and a chilly visit to the artisan felt factory in the foothills. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Since then I went to Kolkata via Delhi, then after a couple of days to Goa, to see my friends and check on the renovation of our apartment there. Getting from Goa to Spain was a little difficult, Air India to Mumbai (delayed 3 hours) then five hours in Mumbai before a 2.30am flight to Amsterdam, five hours before a flight down to Malaga.   
As we came into land .. I couldn't believe how green everything was.. that rain in Spain..
so green..
Malaga was like a dream. I got off the plane first, walked to the luggage belt, and my luggage was waiting for me. Strolled to the minibus meeting point for MalagaCar.com which was waiting there. a short hop to the carhire place and I'm away within minutes. MalagaCar.com have taken over the carhire business by simply not being dodgy, I can't recommend them enough. Fast, friendly and fair.. just like another company I could mention...

So anyway, last night we had the AW-Artisan Christmas party in a very nice restaurant, very posh (one of many) owned by Antonio Bandares. This year twenty one people, and of course as usual I had to give a speech, translated to Spanish by our English girl Molly, I traditionally have to mention that they are my favorite team (it's just a joke guys) but they always love it. Afterwards I was surprised, our warehouse manager:  Juani, asked if she too could make a speech. It was very emotional.. basically this year as been for her and her team very challenging as we have dramatically increased the number of products we offer. The warehouse is not actually big enough (we are looking for a larger place) but Juani is a perfectionist, a wonderful manager and keeps everything in its place and organised. This year has been hard, some disasters like part of the roof collapsing from the storm, but together with incredible team spirit we came through it. One by one she gave credit to her team members, praising them, and joking about them. So much love, kindness and compassion. At the end we are all in tears. Then after Graciela, who is Toni's right hand also gave a heartfelt speech, she is pregnant and will leave us shortly, and she said very shortly she will be back. Because she too loves AW-Artisan. Then more speeches just kept coming.. It was almost too much emotion..
After all those emotional speeches - it was already 1am - well past my bedtime, lots of hugs and I got a taxi home - while the rest of the team would enjoy each other's company and party until dawn. Friday is a bank holiday in Spain so no problem.

Meanwhile.. in the UK.. no time to party (yet) they are riddiculacly busy.. I'm told containers of Spring stock are arriving at least one everyday, Tomas is there making plans for next year (BIG PLANS) and customer service is buzzing. Rodrigo tells the AW team is on full steam right now and ready for the Big Boss (apparently that's me) to arrive next week. 
I'm excited to be there - coming home for Christmas.. I'm also excited because one of our most worked on products of the year has finally arrived. 
But before I tell you about it - big apologies to you Libra people..

Tomas and I visited the factory in China.. (actually AW factory) just as these candles were going into production. Designed by Sandra of (Hop Hare fame) made into life by Coco in China and with a little input from me and Tomas.. we are proud to present.. big roll of drums..

Zodiac Crystal Candles with a Gemstone Bracelet.

Beauty beyond words.. special midnight blue candle jars with silver embossed star sign constellations, out of this world fragrances (tested by my nose), Soywax, wooden crackle wicks and decorated with actual Peruvian Pyrite. Each candle is designed and devoted to a different Zodiac - and to top it all is a gemstone bracelet each one carefully designed to reflect that zodiac sign.  Presented in beautiful boxes with silver embossed. What more can I say!! If you can't sell these you then just go home.

But apologies to Libra folk that particular candle is coming early next year.. 

Christmas is here.. we have a countdown on the website.. Christmas songs and all AW is in the Xmas spirit.
There is a NEW Christmas deal every day... and with that..

Wishing you a lovely weekend.

David

title: From Bali to Bengal: More Trade Secrets
content_html:
Greetings from Serampore, India

I'm in the hometown of our man in India, Mr Chatterjee. 
It's a town about an hour from Kolkata on the banks of the Ganges river. Chatterjee and his son; Drishtranta run a small factory producing cotton and jute products.
I just arrived, and the whole factory, thirty five workers, stopped work to greet my arrival, handshakes and flowers. It was a little bit embarrassing.
Last week I was in Bali, and I was telling you about Indonesian Independence day, our marketing office celebrations and letting all those cute baby turtles free to swim in the wild. If you missed it you can catch up here.


On the banks of the Ganges.

On Wednesday morning Ringo and Bondan drive me to the airport, with a heavy heart I'm leaving because so much to do is not completed. But needs-must and it's time to go to India. I hug them both goodbye. 

The airport is mega busy, it's peak travel time, but surprisingly unstressed and gracefully organised despite the crowds. I caught a cheerful  2 hour Airasia flight to Kuala Lumpur, where I needed to clear immigration, collect my luggage, go upstairs and check back in for my India flight. Then clear immigration again...  and I have five hours before my flight so I head to the business lounge. The best in KL is the Sama-Sama lounge, with an excellent buffet and pleasant work space - where I can catch up on office jobs. My flight is scheduled to leave at 10.35pm  - it's almost on time.. The flight to Kolkata is full of Indian workers returning home, a few very tired holiday makers who have also been to Bali. It's an old plane, the seats are very tight, there are lots of crying babies and it's a fractus 4 hour flight. I think I'm the only European on the flight.  I arrive at 1am India time (but actually 4.30am Bali time) quite exhausted. 
Clearing immigration for the 3rd time into India is surprisingly easy and fast. The immigration officer sees I have a business visa and asks what business I'm doing, I tell him textiles and giftware for export to Europe and he smiles, shakes my hand and says "Welcome to India".. 

Mr Chatterjee is waiting outside for me, it's always a pleasure to see him. We chat and catch up as he takes me to the hotel nearby.  It's the early hours but Kolkata is full of people, what are they doing? The traffic is heavy and the place is just the same as before the pandemic, the last time I was here - a total mess. The culture clash from beautiful cared for Bali, to the garbage and mud and cows and zero maintained pot-holed roads is like a slap in the face. I always remember when my wife Coco (from China) first came here she said "But there are so many people here just hanging around, why can't they just tidy up?" It's such a good question. 
But the hotel I always stay in is spotless, efficient, luxury like you never see in Europe. For the price of a Travelodge in Trafford, I get VIP check in (at 2am),a suite room - deep (much appreciated) fluffy bed. In the morning Chatterjee and I have a breakfast buffet including the best full english breakfast you can imagine. India is basking in the glory of the successful moon landing, and it is a massive achievement, Modi is in South Africa for the Brics summit and lapping up the full credit as usual for anything good that happens in India. Hmmm.. I think as our small car crunches over another pothole on the way to  Serampore.


My initial impressions of Serampore. The three cricketers in the bank advert.. were staying in our hotel in Bangalore on the last trip to India. We were rubbing shoulders at the breakfast buffet for a week.

Then I spent the rest of the day in the factory, checking stock and meeting Mr Chatterjee revamped team. Some of the old faces are there - but since Mr Chatterjee took full control (with our help he bought out his business partners) earlier this year - the team is expanding fast and the place is buzzing with activity. 
Here's a trade secret... From Spain a month ago we sent a carton full of bags purchased in and around Malaga. This is not to copy but to inspire and establish the export quality we need. In this back-water environment without European reference it is hard to understand the quality and type of finish we need. It's been the best thing ever! The team here has been studying those bags down to the last stitch and taken it as a personal challenge to make that standard to the price points we set.  Yesterday they were proudly showing off their work to me.

This is a fundamental change to Indian thinking.. instead of how cheap can we make this bag and negotiating down and down.. squeezing everyone in the chain. Now the thinking should be I try and explain: This is the price we want to pay, so how good and beautiful and detailed can you make the bag upto that price. Compete with quality not price. 


Mr Chatterjee and his head of security and the product manager showed me the quality they can achieve. 
In the evening I'm installed in the only good hotel in town, it opened just before the pandemic. The Denmark Tavern.. it's a historic building that has been recently restored and turned back to it's original glory and function.
The website looks amazing.. but the reality is somewhat different. It's not bad, but 
Mr Chatterjee, his son and the manager Mr Supenu chatted and drank whiskey and consumed a selection of snack food brought by over enthusiastic staff. It seems I am the only guest.

This morning on the way to the factory we stopped off to visit the tye-dye guys. 
These enterprising guys run a small workshop with a water tank, a heater, a selection of clamps, a spin dryer mounted on a rubber tyre and a drying area. They make the designs that make our funky tye-dye bag range. (see below).


I made a video of the whole process.. You can see it here.


Meanwhile back in the UK it's getting super busy.. lots of containers arrived this week meaning lots back in stock.. so very busy.
We might be slipping behind with same day despatch but they tell me they are working hard to catch up. 
New items from Indonesia arrived.. see below.. 

It's a Bank Holiday weekend, so I wish you a very successful and/or relaxing weekend.
More news from India next week.

Namaste

David

title: Bali Is Cut Adrift
content_html:
Greetings from lock-down Bali day 27

To be honest I don't know what day it is. Everyday is more of the same and it's all taking on a dreamlike quality. Or nightmare.. seriously when is this going to end? maybe I will wake up and find it was all a bad dream.. Do you feel like that?

Last week I was telling you about Mount Agung, which I can see from here, across the bay, smouldering like an exotic painting - like a view to heaven. The locals believe it is the key to the centre of the universe.. weird things happen there. You can read about it here.  
The shock news - a rumour passed to me by my land-lady yesterday is that Bali will self isolate totally. News today is that all flights will stop, all boat crossing - nobody leaves or comes to Bali.. Officially until 1st of June.  But Ringo tells me that maybe until a vaccine is available. So a long time.. - the island of Bali will be like Noah's Ark, floating in the tropical sea.

Am I the only one to think about this.. but surely all the worlds airlines can't just go bankrupt.. there has to be a solution. And here it is: All international travellers be tested at the point of travel? You'd have to turn up 3 hours early, be tested - and if clear be allowed to check-in. They just need 10 minute tests..  This way the virus couldn't migrate between countries, you wouldn't need to social distance once air-side or onboard, and the world could start to functioning again.. I could see my wife and family. You read it here first!!

Meanwhile, life goes on. I took a trip into Denpasar with Ringo, we went to buy a photo studio set up and a colour laser printer. The idea is to photograph all the new products here so that we can save time later. Also, we want to print picture barcodes on all the packaging, and cartons. Denpasar.. it's an exotic city. lots of gardens, tropical plants, low-rise - no towers at all. Normally it is gridlocked a huge slowly moving traffic jam. But now clean air, the streets seem wider and almost empty, a few people all wearing masks (it's the law now) walking, shops open but empty.  I said to Ringo, it's like a sleepy provincial town, a pleasant place to be. 
So Ringo has a brother, who has a daughter.. Natalie.. I said that's not a Bali name.. she said.. "cause my dream is to go to America, so I have an American name"..  

One office has lots of natural light. She is studious, seems shy but I think smart. Normally works for an internet company setting up hotel wifi systems. But all the hotels are closed, so she is laid off. Her hobby is photography and she even owns a decent camera..  So today we spent setting up a studio space and me (and what do I know?) explaining about product photography.. Ringo says we can send her on a training course, but actually she was doing good and had an understanding in no time what we wanted.
So we will see how it goes.. 

Meanwhile in Europe.. we are making Hand Sanitiser as fast as possible, but orders are outstripping production, which is delaying orders a bit.
I understand we are working Saturday (full safety measures - masks and gloves and social distancing) to full-fill the orders, so please bear with us we are getting there.  As usual the team at AW  - hero's everyone, are doing their level best under difficult circumstances to look after the wonderful AW customers.

Drop-shipping department is also crazy busy and growing, and I'm amazed at what is selling.. anything for the home..  what's with the Indian wall-hangings, and the Round jute & cotton rugs..  see below..

So until next week.. stay safe.. stay home.. 

Take care

David

Officially until 1st of June. But Ringo tells me that maybe until a vaccine is available. So a long time.. - the island of Bali will be like Noah's Ark, floating in the tropical sea. Am I the only one to think about this.. but surely all the worlds airlines can't just go bankrupt.. there has to be a solution. And here it is: All international travellers be tested at the point of travel? You'd have to turn up 3 hours early, be tested - and if clear be allowed to check-in. They just need 10 minute tests.. This way the virus couldn't migrate between countries, you wouldn't need to social distance once air-side or onboard, and the world could start to functioning again.. I could see my wife and family. You read it here first!! Meanwhile, life goes on. I took a trip into Denpasar with Ringo, we went to buy a photo studio set up and a colour laser printer. The idea is to photograph all the new products here so that we can save time later. Also, we want to print picture barcodes on all the packaging, and cartons. Denpasar.. it's an exotic city. lots of gardens, tropical plants, low-rise - no towers at all. Normally it is gridlocked a huge slowly moving traffic jam. But now clean air, the streets seem wider and almost empty, a few people all wearing masks (it's the law now) walking, shops open but empty. I said to Ringo, it's like a sleepy provincial town, a pleasant place to be. So Ringo has a brother, who has a daughter.. Natalie.. I said that's not a Bali name.. she said.. "cause my dream is to go to America, so I have an American name".. One office has lots of natural light. She is studious, seems shy but I think smart. Normally works for an internet company setting up hotel wifi systems. But all the hotels are closed, so she is laid off. Her hobby is photography and she even owns a decent camera.. So today we spent setting up a studio space and me (and what do I know?) explaining about product photography.. Ringo says we can send her on a training course, but actually she was doing good and had an understanding in no time what we wanted. So we will see how it goes.. Meanwhile in Europe.. we are making Hand Sanitiser as fast as possible, but orders are outstripping production, which is delaying orders a bit. I understand we are working Saturday (full safety measures - masks and gloves and social distancing) to full-fill the orders, so please bear with us we are getting there. As usual the team at AW - hero's everyone, are doing their level best under difficult circumstances to look after the wonderful AW customers. Drop-shipping department is also crazy busy and growing, and I'm amazed at what is selling.. anything for the home.. what's with the Indian wall-hangings , and the Round jute & cotton rug s .. see below.. So until next week.. stay safe.. stay home.. Take care David

title: Mystical Mythical Mix
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about just how jolly hard those Spanish chaps can work...
Well I'm still in Spain as I write this, but by the time you read it I should have bounced through a Jubilee / Eurovision jumping UK and onward to the Moniachy light Peoples Republic of China. I'm considering a detour to Indonesia where our agent is bubbling with excitement at the discovery of some new suppliers he wants me to see. Meanwhile in India, my goodness it will be too hot and humid, but the projects there have slowed to a halt..
You know me, (if you read this newsletter regularly), I love to be busy and am always travelling. Our lovely AW customers are always hungry for the new, exotic and interesting - it drives their businesses and ours not to mention keeping thousands of artisans in gainful employment. It's my job to go where no importer has been before to keep finding new nice companies and great stuff to feed the nice AW monster. OK it's a little unfair to call it a monster, maybe more of a mystical mythical mix of interesting and funky retailers. Real people who understand the magic inherent in simple gifts. Is that you?
But recently I have been feeling the need to find place to lay my hat (for more than a week at a time), and Spain seems to be it. Similar time zone as the UK, only a hop away. We have a business here and it's warm. Then there are the property bargains of a life time.. or is it a currency gamble of a lifetime?
So in between I have been looking for a house. My criteria is simple, must be within 20 mins of the AW warehouse in Malaga and have stunning views. I want to be writing this newsletter on a Friday from a desk with an inspiring view.
There is big news in the UK (apart from Beth's big do) our production of much awaited Guest Soaps are finally on stream. Really, is that so exciting? Well for us we have spent a year installing some pretty heavy duty soap making machinery, developing a new set of skills, finding the right ingredients and having all the tests done etc. etc.. Finally we have AW Guest soaps. So we are excited.
For our clued up customers, they are excited because they know this is a hard to buy product with hundreds of uses (and sells very well). 
More news next week.. from somewhere else.
Regards
David

title: Success Stories
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

I just arrived, today went to the main giftware area in the huge wholesale permanent market they have here.
Regular readers will know that it is epic, an endless exhibition of manufacturers showrooms.. now over 100,000. Apart from Chinese New Year it is open for business 7 days a week.

We have an office and warehouse here, it's not as pretty as the warehouse in Bali  - you can read about that in last weeks news here - but essentially does the same job.
Ringo dropped me at the spectacularly beautiful Denpasar airport, he is always a bit emotional when I leave.. then I took the evening Airasia to KL, 7 hours in the air-side Sama-Sama hotel, then the morning flight to Hangzhou where my driver was waiting to take me the 90 minute drive to Yiwu. 
From Bali to Yiwu.. it takes two flights. Sometimes three. My carbon footprint is terrible, I have been thinking about this..and a few people have written to me encouraging me to do something about it.

Driving to the airport Ringo was telling me about Kalimantan, you might have read the government of Indonesia is moving from the vastly over the crowded capital city of Jakarta to sparsely populated East Kalimantan, or you probably know it called Borneo, to a brand new city.
Kalimantan is huge and the land is very cheap, it is been bought up in vast swathes and used for intensive palm oil farming. 
So, as you probably know you can pay to off-set your carbon foot-print by sending money to companies that plant trees. But my idea is that with Ringo's help we cut out the middleman, make sure it really happens and AW actually buys a chunk of Kalimantan and reforest it enough to offset all our companies executive travel for years to come.. will be a grand adventure also. Ringo says they even have government schemes to help you do this kind of thing. So he is looking into it.. I'll keep you updated.

Meanwhile, it really has all been happening this month. What with the new warehouse in Bali coming online, when I left the artists we found were working in the night making it the most beautiful warehouse you have ever seen :)


In Spain at the same time, our lawyer was signing a deal on a new Big & Beautiful warehouse in Malaga, it's got a huge car park that we also plan to make beautiful with landscaping and planters. After all, we are in the business of selling beautiful things to amazing people, so why shouldn't everyone who works for AW not have the best possible environment. I'm really into this, inspired by the WeWork concept, where people have the best working environment possible,  perform the best. We have big plans to redesign the main offices at AW HQ.
And I really want to find somewhere to put a table tennis table :)

In Bali, on the last day I managed to meet up with two of our most successful suppliers.. both companies run by ladies. The lady that makes the Bath Bomb display stands amongst other things: Widya Dewi.. when we first started working with her she had rented a small showroom on the main wholesale road outside of Ubud and was living with her family in a single room at the back - working part-time at the bank opposite to make ends meet.

She was making candlesticks for us in Albasia wood, and later we started making display stands.. she took on workers, bought some land a strip that goes way back to the rain forest behind. She is a lovely lady, very organised always thinking of ways to get more efficient. She proudly showed me the house she was building for her family - three stories.. all thanks to you she said. It has to be said her husband is there always working, but she is the brains and boss.. 


On the right, this Dewi always hands on. Here working on Dinner Candle display stands coming soon. This is the house she is building for her family.. 

We also went to see Wayan who has a thriving business and a similar story in the heart of Sukawati. Wayan is mega organised, always immaculately dressed in trendy skinny jeans, she has two young kids and truly handsome husband. Who, Ringo says is just in charge of security.. rather unkindly.. but for sure Wayan is the boss. We discovered she had bought a house behind her showroom and built a decent sized warehouse to finish and pack orders. Her staff all pretty girls look up to her and dress fashionably. "Mr David" she always calls me.. "We just wanted to say thank you, since we worked with you we have done better and better" she explained it's not just the good orders - but the products we develop she also sells to USA and Australia.. unlike other buyers we don't demand exclusivity for this reason.

Wayan on the right.. she makes the Mahogany Soap Dishes amongst other things. So this is the most satisfying part of my job when I see how real families and their workers benefit. Would this happen if i didn't go there?

 MEANWHILE!!
Back in the UK it's the Birmingham Autumn Fair.. as you know AW doesn't do trade shows, never has, because we don't have any sales people :)
But we have to make an exception for our very British brand: Agnes & Cat.. we are displaying our wares... FIND US IN HALL 6 STAND H13
Sorry, still no sales people but you will meet Tomas and the team behind Agnes & Cat.

NB.. all the beautiful recycled wood (made from old fishing boats) furniture is made in Bali.. and another success story I will tell you about another time..

Next week news from China..

Have a great weekend.


David

title: Reincarnation & Other Special Offers
content_html:
Greetings from Affinity Park, Sheffield - HQ of AW.

Hope all is well with you, and you are keeping busy and safe.

It's almost the Bank Holiday weekend and according to Borris everything is looking up in Blighty.

Last week I was telling you about George and the Crack Buying team at AW.. I introduced you to them and asked if you'd like to lend a hand.. you can read about it here.


First of all I like to thank everyone who put forward suggestions to the buying team - normally I would reply, but there was a lot! So please forgive me not thanking you individually, but a BIG THANK YOU to everyone and some really fresh original ideas. Lots and lots of food for thought and stuff to really get cracking with.

 

Looming stock shortages.

I don't wish to sound alarmist, but we live in troubled times and in the best of days developing products and shipping them is challenging.. now with covid, shipping crisis, Brexit, travel bans and raw materials shortages - it's getting to be hard work.

I messaged Mr Chatterjee in India with some of your suggestions for new products and asked if it was possible to make samples. He said he would try but it was difficult right now. I called him on Whatsapp for a chat. He is OK and putting a brave face on things, but of his factory staff all but one person was self isolating or down with covid. The children's home we support, all the kids are OK but all the teachers are infected. Mr Chattergee's own sister has it. Fortunately no-one is severely ill, but to say the situation is bad, is an understatement. He tells me the official figures are massively understated by the government in denial.. it is probably ten times worse. Your best wishes and prayers would be appreciated, if you want to send a message, I'm happy to pass it on.

 

Then our main German candle supplier informed us that they had trouble buying paraffin wax, prices if you can even get supplies at 60% up. We have several purchase orders open with them, but no dates for delivery.  

Coco in China who also runs the AW Soywax candle factory there, has a similar problem with Soywax supplies. The trade war with America has frozen imports of soybeans. Coco also tells me that shipping to the UK is such a pain that many factories proratise orders to Japan or Korea because there are no problems, so we find ourselves at the back of the list. 

Ringo in Indonesia is still struggling to find container shipping prices at anything like workable. It was just easing when that ship got lodged in the Suez Canal and now it's back to square one, all the empty containers are in the wrong places.  

India was just getting back to a decree of normality, and we managed to ship a few containers over the last few weeks. One arrived from Delhi today..



All this is going online right now.. details below.

 

But Mr Modi was convinced that India had beaten coronavirus. With massive Nationalist hubris encouraged the big Hindu festivals, the cricket matches and (of course) his election rallies to go ahead. Within weeks  the terrible consequences. 

You can blame coronavirus of course, but I blame evil Nationalism - leaders standing in front of flags, telling us our particular country is best..(better than all the rest) really just to control our minds.. sorry for the rant.. must take deep breaths..

 

Anyway last week I introduced you to our beefed up buying team.. We have two new recruits to our Customer Service Team.. We are also beefing up the AW CS team.. (OMG can you say "beefed up"? maybe it is sexist or veganist or something).

I'd like you to meet: Daniella & Michael.. we took the whole team outside to get a group picture next to the AW Buddha..  


I asked if they could offer some odd insights - so we could get to know them a little. Michael (on the left of the tree): "I enjoy flying my drone while walking my dog"

 

Daniella (on the right of the tree): "I make my own crystal healing soywax candles, I love animals and all things metaphyscial." and our Kerry (to the left of the Buddha added: "I'm a member of the UK wide Rock choir and like to volunteer for charity events when I can". And our other Kerry (behind Michael) "Well l just love our caravan and camping in Whitby"




Not to be left out, Urszula (on the right of the Buddha) let it be known she is a member of the imfamous Boomshanka belly dancing group..

So next time you chat to our team.. you can say Hi - I have seen you in the newsletter.

 

I hope you have a lovely weekend. 

Please just take a moment of it, a minute of it...  To pray/meditate/send good karma to all of India, but especially to any of your friends there and also to our Mr Chatterjee and his family and team.  

Your best wishes and prayers would be appreciated, if you want to send a message, I'm happy to pass it on.  

 

Take care

 

David

 

PS:

I know many of you will want to help financially, you have done this generously before in the first wave. But I have asked Mr Chatterjee if they need any support, he says; no not at this time.

( AW has already sent additional funds for the children's home). But maybe you (and us) can support India more sustainably by simply stocking and marketing more Indian products (not just from AW - there are many good importers) this would be a small but important win for everyone.

title: David's AW News: I'm so Jealous.
content_html:
Greetings from La Cala, Mijas

Yes I'm still here in (mostly) sunny Spain, expecting to get battered by the after effects of storm Ciaran shortly. Actually that is one of the reasons we are here, it was extreme weather last winter that caused a glass balustrade to collapse and damaged the decking around our Bali inspired pool. So we finally have the builders in,to build a new nice solid wall, and replace the decking with indestructible tiles. Apparently October was the warmest on record in the world, and the fourth consecutive to beat that record. Climate change deniers can go take a running jump. Seriously humans stop fighting stupid wars and face up to this. 


Looks a big mess, but will be beautiful soon.

Last week I was telling you about one of my first trips to India, and how I got hooked on visiting remote out of the way places to do business with the locals. If you missed it you can read about it here.

News from Tomas (our no.1 marketing and all round wizard), he is still in Bali with Peter (from Slovakia) finalising work with the amazing AW-Advantage team. Our beach-side marketing office is making huge strides and already helping a number of clients find their marketing superpowers.. But Tomas couldn't leave without sourcing and developing a few more artisan products from Indonesia. On his days off from the office he has been out with Ringo visiting our artisan suppliers and finding new ones. While that is a good thing - I'm actually a little jealous because that's my favorite job in all AW.  
Tomas was in a small factory where skilled workers finish hand-carved Buddha statues with special process to produce an antique look. It involves a particular skill set, and only a few artisans can do it. Sadly they can only make a maximum of 100 statues per month. This is a common problem these days. 


Even more frustratingly Bondhan (Ringo's assistant in Indonesia) was despatched to Java (to a remote village) to find the source of a range of beautiful natural place mats and runners that we had seen. This is Bondhans home turf, and he speaks the local language so was able to locate the artisan village that specialises in these. The other day, we had a three ways WA meeting, Bondhan in Java, Tomas in Bali and me in Spain. To finalise a selection of place mats. Water Hyacinth, Seagrass and scented Vertver. The village is basically just a street of small workshops with ladies and gents working on ancient looms weaving away.  Just the sort of place I love to visit.


Sadly Bondhan told me that in all the workshops he didn't see a single young person doing this job. And he was told that young people don't want to do it, naturally they want good jobs in the city. Maybe in a digital marketing job in an office by a surfing beach... it's a story we hear all the time. I have told you this story before, it's a big problem with a shrinking pool of artisans.. but maybe a solution is forming in my mind. 

So today in Bali is the last day for Tomas and Peter, they are leaving to return to Europe. Our young team will be (kind of) on their own, although I'm sure they will thrive. Debbie our office manager is a good mother to them all. Anyway they threw a surprise leaving party them both.. as I write this it's closing time on Friday afternoon in Bali, and Tomas and Peter are making their emotional farewells. 


Flowers and personalised "Thank You" sashes.. 

Now I'm even more jealous because all I get is a hug.. seriously though they are delightful people and a joy be around. 
Hopefully I will see them soon and be visiting remote villages and doing deals again.. actually I'm making plans for India and beyond now.

But Christmas is coming and a lot of work this end, including making plans for next year.
It's all go in the distribution centres.. Crazy in Slovakia, Manic in Spain and Bedlam in Sheffield.. 
And lots of new exotic and beautiful products coming online almost everyday. Check out the deals below.

Hope the storms and flooding has past you by.. have a lovely weekend.
Thank you so much for your support.

David

Actually that is one of the reasons we are here, it was extreme weather last winter that caused a glass balustrade to collapse and damaged the decking around our Bali inspired pool. So we finally have the builders in,to build a new nice solid wall, and replace the decking with indestructible tiles. Apparently October was the warmest on record in the world, and the fourth consecutive to beat that record. Climate change deniers can go take a running jump. Seriously humans stop fighting stupid wars and face up to this. Looks a big mess, but will be beautiful soon. Last week I was telling you about one of my first trips to India, and how I got hooked on visiting remote out of the way places to do business with the locals. If you missed it you can read about it here . News from Tomas (our no.1 marketing and all round wizard), he is still in Bali with Peter (from Slovakia) finalising work with the amazing AW-Advantage team. Our beach-side marketing office is making huge strides and already helping a number of clients find their marketing superpowers.. But Tomas couldn't leave without sourcing and developing a few more artisan products from Indonesia. On his days off from the office he has been out with Ringo visiting our artisan suppliers and finding new ones. While that is a good thing - I'm actually a little jealous because that's my favorite job in all AW. Tomas was in a small factory where skilled workers finish hand-carved Buddha statues with special process to produce an antique look. It involves a particular skill set, and only a few artisans can do it. Sadly they can only make a maximum of 100 statues per month. This is a common problem these days. Even more frustratingly Bondhan (Ringo's assistant in Indonesia) was despatched to Java (to a remote village) to find the source of a range of beautiful natural place mats and runners that we had seen. This is Bondhans home turf, and he speaks the local language so was able to locate the artisan village that specialises in these. The other day, we had a three ways WA meeting, Bondhan in Java, Tomas in Bali and me in Spain. To finalise a selection of place mats. Water Hyacinth, Seagrass and scented Vertver. The village is basically just a street of small workshops with ladies and gents working on ancient looms weaving away. Just the sort of place I love to visit. Sadly Bondhan told me that in all the workshops he didn't see a single young person doing this job. And he was told that young people don't want to do it, naturally they want good jobs in the city. Maybe in a digital marketing job in an office by a surfing beach... it's a story we hear all the time. I have told you this story before, it's a big problem with a shrinking pool of artisans.. but maybe a solution is forming in my mind. So today in Bali is the last day for Tomas and Peter, they are leaving to return to Europe. Our young team will be (kind of) on their own, although I'm sure they will thrive. Debbie our office manager is a good mother to them all. Flowers and personalised "Thank You" sashes.. Now I'm even more jealous because all I get is a hug.. seriously though they are delightful people and a joy be around. Hopefully I will see them soon and be visiting remote villages and doing deals again.. actually I'm making plans for India and beyond now. Thank you so much for your support. David

title: Just ONE thing...
content_html:
Greetings from a cool and windy Spain.

Tomas was here until Wednesday (now back in the UK) and we were making plans and setting targets.. at AW we always think big. It's easy to get bogged down in management speak and technical fixes. Of course every element of the business is important,each and everyone's jobs are important - from customer service to despatch to goods-in to marketing.. But the one thing that is most important, without which any business plan will fail.. is easy to forget..do you know what it is?

Last week I was musing about the 5 most important retail trends as I see it.. if you missed it you can catch up here?

It's nice in Spain, I enjoy working with our team at AW Artisan.. they are hard working but know how to have fun. We have more parties than 10 Downing Street. It was my birthday and my favourite team surprised me with a birthday cake and a rousing rendition of "Happy Birthday" . We had a 15 minute jolly party, where everyone kindly pretended not to believe how old I am..  then went back to work.  

At Christmas in the UK, I happened to visit M&S in central Sheffield and was shocked and saddened to see a virtually empty store, not much seasonal fizz at all. Spaced out shelves, stock shortages, glum staff, no queues at all. Very sad.  So this morning I was surprised to read in the Times "Marks & Spencer" hails sparkling sales across the board" 
On closer reading I discovered that on-line sales had been well up, and that.. "a light-up tin of shortbread and a bottle of gin that incorporated a snowglobe, each sold more than a million units" - thus saving M&S from the knackers yard.
So the one thing that saved them was great products.. and in the gift trade this matters as much (if not more) than any other business.

It's the middle of January 2022..and next up in the gift trader calendar is Valentine's Day,  Which marks the start of what we call "The Season of Love" - Mothers Day, Easter, Father's Day.. the Wedding Season. Spring should put a spring in your step.. time to get busy.. and let's not forget the lesson M&S teaches us.. always focus on the product. PRODUCT is king.. 

That's the ONE thing to never lose focus on, your products make your business. New products, repeat selling products, on trend products.. If you don't delight your customers then it's time to refresh those products.

Well I don't want to bang our own gong too much.. but AW is the best place to find great "Season of Love" products, it's what we do best. Check out the new products and deals below.
And if you did want to bang your own gong.. Now you can because we just received stock of Gongs from Indonesia. See below, these gongs are traditionally used in Bali and Java in temple ceremonies, but these days used in Yoga studio's and many believe the gong sound to have healing properties.. sound the gong to bring peace and love into your place..

Talking about the season of love.. 2 years ago to the day I took Coco (my wife and our China agent) to Malaga airport, and waved her goodbye as she flew back to China.. I expected to see her again in just a few weeks after a trip to India. Of course covid happened and that blasted that plan apart. So today marks two years since I have last seen Coco. Hopefully soon things will change.

Lots of stuff back in stock this week.. which is making us pretty busy and a little behind with orders. 
We are doing our best to catch up and I understand we have a saturday shift to catch up with the orders.

Also the famous Sheffield street artist: Peachzz has been finishing off her beautification of AW HQ.. turning an otherwise boring passageway to the main office into a jungle run..



Hope you have a lovely weekend.
Take care - more news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: What they pray for is amazing..
content_html:
Greetings from the AW Advantage marketing office, Bali..


HAPPY MOTHER'S DAY weekend to all the mothers and everyone who celebrates this important day!

Yes I'm at our beach office, and it very much has an end of year feel. Tomorrow is Nyepi Bali's New Year day, and this year it almost coincides with Eid al-Fitr celebrating the end of Ramadan. 
So many of our staff are already heading to their hometown, and the rest will break today for a national holiday until Wednesday next week.

Last week I was telling you about our visit to the Bali Baby Home we support close to here, helping runaway single mothers and their children put their lives back together. If you missed it you can catch up right here, or see the Youtube we made about it here. Update, they already spent the donation we made and made a classroom area double quick, they sent pictures today.

The Melasti Ceremony.
It's all happening near our office. Since this time last year the local village has made a beautiful ceremonial area, and built a car park for one special occasion it's the Melasti Ceremony.
This is where the local village communities go to the nearest body of water (sea or lake) and ceremonial objects are dipped in the sea for cleansing, then everyone prays.. what they pray for is amazing..
Outside our office..
The ceremony aims to cleanse the world of all sins and bring good karma. These guys are praying for the whole world and the universe. For you and I.
Now this is not for tourists, the Pecalang (security) will turn you back, but because we are practically local I went with Bondhan to mingle with the Balinese people just a little. Video short here.

The Melasti ceremony is a purification ritual for Balinese Hindus held over the three days before the Nyepi Day. Later the massive Ogoh-Ogoh monsters made by imaginative and creative youngsters will parade through the streets, they represent
the evil in the world and will conduct mock battles, eventually some will be burned symbolising the end of evil all a bit wild.
Crazy night..
 ..then..
Silence will fall over Bali, complete silence. Roads close, the airport is closed, the internet is off (except tourist hotels),  Pecalang (local security) will politely tell you to return to your hotel if you try to venture out. I'm really looking forward to it.. a time to be alone no distractions just to reflect and think. And after dark, the sky is amazing because there are no lights at all on the island. 

My taxi driver yesterday  was from Padang bay, just up the coast, he told me he was a holy man and must return to his village to preside over a Melasti ceremony. 
He asked me what my business did in Bali, I told him we buy handicrafts from artisans and send them to Europe. Eyes shining, he thanked me and told me this was vitally important for Balanese culture, because those with "proper jobs" in hotels or construction companies don't have the flexible time to attend ceremonies and support the communities. That's the reason I'm a taxi driver - I can work when I want. It's the same with artisans, they can work in times that fit around their cultural life. 
So it strikes me by buying artisan products, you actually help support the beautiful and unique culture of the island.

Some News..
A young journalist from Sheffield called Lauren J Reay-Williams  produced a small article about our efforts to Tax Temu.. You can read it here.

Next week I will be in Kathmandu, with a totally different vibe..

There is still time to order and support our Bali Baby Home fund.. 
Absolutely amazing NEW stock next week..from the team at AW-Aromatics: Zodiac Fizzers!!
Also watch out for Witchy Candles.. Quite Amazing.
So much work has gone into both these products you wouldn't imagine.. 

Take care and have a lovely weekend and perfect Mother's Day..

title: David's AW News: Heatwaves, Holly & India
content_html:
It's hot here in summer but this summer is a little too much. Hard to sleep at night, I'm waking up in a pool of sweat. Sorry, too much info.

Last week I was telling you about Slovakia, and how damned efficient they are there. But also friendly and fun. And I was telling you with the help of Katarina, we make some content for YouTube.. It was lots of fun!!



Travel Update

Regular readers will know that the circle of life goes on at AW and that involves constantly bringing you new products, and that involves travelling..

I have spent much of this week coordinating with our man in India, Mr Chatterjee about an Indian tour in October.. and it's looking pretty epic we are going gemstone hunting in regions unknown, hoping to open up new hippy textile connections in one of India iconic cities and meanwhile catching up with old suppliers. Before that will be Indonesia, China and Nepal.. so a lot to organise.. stand by for adventure.

Trump Tariffs & Indian trade deals

Big wheels turning, who knows if this ends well or not.. we live in interesting times. So many moving parts I don't think anyone can predict how it goes.

One customer was asking if the India trade deal means cheaper incense.. Let's hope so! As far as India goes, duty on most things is single digit, so I'm not sure if we can save money, rest assured we will do our best to be the first to bring you better deals.

Well done Holly (and the whole team) 

Holly has been working in our Social media team for just one month and has kicked one hell of a storm.. congratulations on some really informative and useful content. I can see you like it by the views and watch hours.. it's hard work but I now feel good that YouTube content with some detail and substance is useful to you and your customers, helping you sell more!

This week Holly was doing a deep dive with Sandra, our talented designer discussing her beloved Zodiac range of products. 

There is Zodiac Fragrance Oils with stars in the oil.

Zodiac Candles with pyrite and beautiful jars and a matching bracelet.

and the Zodiac Bath Fizzes with horoscopes inside.. 

Sandra explains to Holly why you should stock the full range here..



Meanwhile in the UK

Some new stock from India came.. will be online next week.

Next up is Halloween and the Aromatics are on the ball with new products already..

 

I'm working on some new content from our Spain showroom..



Maybe I will upload it this weekend.

Subscribe to keep up..

 

Wishing you a wonderful weekend.

Thank you for reading 

Take care

title: On to India
content_html:
Greetings from Panipat, India

Yes we are finally back in India, after three years. Arriving in the midst of Holi celebrations. 
Last week I was telling you about the wild side of Kathmandu and shared some images of our time with supplies from Nepal. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Since then we took Indigo air from Kathmandu to Delhi (downhill as it feels), a short flight from Nepal to India. 
I'm travelling with Tomas and Bryant. Tomas (our product and marketing wizard) is an old hand and has travelled in Nepal and India before, but Bryant is totally new. He has been working in the UK office placing re-orders with Indian and Nepali suppliers for a few years so already has good relations.. so finally now covid is over, Bryant goes to meet the suppliers.

It's been a very busy week in Kathmandu. And I'm happy to report that it was very successful and productive. We have greatly expanded our range of hemp products, found an amazing new singing bowl  supplier and landed some new Tibetan Incense ranges. I'm very excited about Nepal products in general, I'm hoping in the future to further extend our range of stock from Nepal..

Even though we have been so busy, we managed a couple of excursions - after a visit to the hemp guys factory on the outskirts of Kathmandu and a long meeting finalising our order.. he suggested taking us on a tour of the nearby Monkey Temple. I had never been there before and was quite surprised.. Most of the visitors seemed to be local tourists, and the temple is perched on a hill with spectacular views of the city, Of course there are Monkeys hence the name Monkey Temple and beautiful old buildings and an ancient Stupa. It was also Holi here one day earlier than in India.. and here more restrained than the crazy Indian riots that take place.. Bryant was given the Holi treatment in our hotel by the staff. The street crowds are good natured, calling out "Happy Holi" and only splashing colours or water bombs if the recipients are up for it. 



Sadly our time was up in Kathmandu and we had to say a sad farewell to friends there.. On Wednesday we had to leave for India. 

We arrived in Delhi, the airport is huge, but international arrivals seemed very quiet, almost no queuing and within the hour we were through immigration. Mr Chatterjee and his son were waiting for us outside. so a long overdue reunion. Mr Chatterjee had organised two cars to take us all to Panipat. As we exited the airport area, it seemed awfully quiet for India. This is because we had arrived on a national holiday, the festival of Holi. When we did see anyone in a taxi or other cars or the odd stragglers curbside, they were all covered in the multi colours of Holi and looking very happy. 
We have nice clear blue skies and temperatures of 30c. Actually very nice weather for India this time of year, I was expecting it to be much hotter and muggy and grey. The journey to Panipat was smooth and fast on a brand new four  lane highway. We had been promising Bryant an India of hectic traffic, masses of bikes, tuk tuks and holy cows. The city of Panipat is a textile city with not many creature comforts, our hotel barely has internet and the rooms are basic - but we needed to visit our supplier here (Rag rugs) and add more products.. The very popular rag rugs always sell out within weeks of arriving (more coming soon) so we came to arrange a bigger and better supply. 

As I write this the weather and conditions in the UK are completely opposite. I hope you are managing to cope safely. It looks like trade all round will be disrupted by the extreme cold and snow.
Here is the situation in Sheffield..


However we are open and have enough staff to pick orders.. the AW hero's have made it to work and are keeping things going. Thanks guys!!
Hopefully we will get a courier collection today, but if not then by monday all should be OK..

This week we have lots back in stock including beautiful candlesticks from Indonesia.


Also some amazing new products from the team at Aromatics..
Its all happening.. 

Hope you are managing the weather ok..
More news from India next week.

Take extra care..

David

title: David's AW News: A Busy Week in Bali… and Happy Mother’s Day!
content_html:
Greetings from Bali,

First of all, a very Happy Mother’s Day weekend to all the mums in the UK. 


Rodrigo sends greetings from our Sheffield showroom. Do come and visit soon!

 
Mother’s Day is one of those lovely moments in the gift trade when people remember someone important. Flowers, candles, little treasures — it’s not about the size of the gift, but the thought behind it. 

So if you are a mum reading this… or if you’re rushing out today to buy something for yours… we hope it’s a special weekend.

Meanwhile, here in Bali, Raul is visiting and we’ve been working together most days from the AW Advantage office. The pace has been intense.  Last week I was telling you about Stones, Storms & Safe Landings, you can read it here.

We’re running around like crazy updating websites and systems. The latest to go under the hood is AWArtisan.eu. From the outside it might look like a simple refresh — but behind the scenes the backend work is huge. Cleaning data, restructuring systems and preparing things for the next stage. All the websites including the UK main site will change over the next few weeks. We hope you appreciate the changes.. it should be a better (we hope it is) user experience.. and that you can find ever more Gifting Opportunities at AW.

It’s a bit like renovating a house while still living in it.

At the same time there’s a real “end of term” feeling around the office.

Across Indonesia the big celebration is Idul Fitri, marking the end of Ramadan. Many of our team are heading home this weekend to visit their families — travelling to different islands across the archipelago.

For our Balinese colleagues there’s another special event approaching: Nyepi, the Balinese New Year.

Nyepi is famous as the Day of Silence, and it really is extraordinary. For 24 hours the whole island shuts down. No traffic, no flights, no work, no lights at night. Even the airport closes. Streets empty, the island rests, and everyone reflects quietly before the new year begins.

Imagine an entire island pressing pause for a day.

But the night before is Ogoh-Ogoh a time.. wild celebration of the battle of good over evil.. Mongsters paraded through the streets mock fighting each other. 



I'm planning to watch it on Mertasari beach.. where if I'm lucky there will be fires and monsters in the sea.

So all go!!

And just to add to the atmosphere… today also happens to be Friday the 13th. So yes — quite a lot happening at once!

Fortunately our warehouse team here are mostly from Floris or Sumba, and many are Christian, so while others travel home the packing and dispatch continues. Orders are still moving.

And some beautiful new musical stock has just arrived:

• Pangi Seed Shell Shakers – wonderful natural percussion instruments made from jungle seeds.
• Kenari Seed Rattles – bracelets and hand rattles with a rich earthy sound.
• Manglid Wood Rainsticks – when you turn them slowly they produce a gentle rainfall sound that can last for several minutes.


They’ve just landed in the Bali warehouse and will be making their way onto the websites — keep an eye out. Music instruments are trending and one of our planned growth areas for 2026. Check here. 

News from Kathmandu

While all this is happening here in Bali, we’ve also been following some exciting news from Nepal.

My Nepali friends are delighted that the Gen Z candidate won the election this week.

What impressed me most was his first message — asking people to celebrate calmly and respectfully, and to first remember the young people who died during the uprising.

That says a lot about a leader.

The man is Balen Shah — once a rapper, later the mayor of Kathmandu, and widely respected because he actually got things done. Real improvements, not just speeches.



To celebrate the moment (and send a little support from Bali) I wore my Gen Z T-shirt this week and sent congratulations to many of our suppliers and friends in Nepal. From what I can see they are overwhelmingly optimistic about this new chapter. And my YouTube I made just after the uprising (I was there) - you can check here: Kasthmandu Aftermath




Getting Things Done

Watching that energy in Nepal is quite inspiring.

And it reminds me of something important at Ancient Wisdom.

Ideas are great. Plans are great. Meetings are great.

But in the end…

What really matters is getting things done.

Whether it's improving websites, sourcing new products, packing orders or supporting artisans around the world — progress happens one small step at a time.

And thankfully, our team is very good at that.

Looking Ahead

So from Bali — between website updates, rainsticks, holiday travel plans and the occasional Friday-the-13th chaos — we keep moving forward.

To all our Indonesian friends: Selamat Idul Fitri.
To our Balinese team: Selamat Nyepi.
And to our friends in Nepal: Congratulations on an exciting new chapter.

And once again to all the mums celebrating this weekend in the UK — Happy Mother’s Day.

Because in the gift world, one celebration always leads to the next…

And the next one on the horizon is Easter, just a few weeks away.

So enjoy the weekend, thank your mum, and then — as always in our trade —

It’s time to start thinking about the next opportunity. 

Take care, have a great weekend!

David

Watch it now — and don’t forget to subscribe for more videos like this. Our goal is simple: to help you sell more.

title: David's AW News: Stones, Storms & Safe Landings
content_html:
From Gujarat to Goa… and back to Bali

Before leaving Khambhat, our gemstone friends insisted we visit a nearby Hindu temple — a place filled with enormous Shiva Lingam stones.

Inside the temple stands a monumental lingam, the sacred symbol of Lord Shiva. In Hindu tradition the lingam represents the creative force of the universe — the endless cycle of creation, destruction and renewal. Locals were so happy to welcome us, excited even, wanted selfies and thanked us for visiting. 

Devotees perform a ritual known as abhishek, gently pouring water, milk or oil over the stone while offering prayers. Watching Mr Chatterjee perform this ancient ritual up close is surprisingly moving. The smooth stone slowly darkens as the liquid flows over it, collecting in channels below — a simple act repeated for centuries.

Our friend, the mining guy above right in the picture and his brother took us on a VIP tour.. The temple is full of local agate, many gemstone decor and huge lingam stones. For people who work with stones and minerals every day, it felt strangely appropriate. Our trip to Khambhat began with gemstones and ended in a temple celebrating one of the most sacred stones of all.

After saying our goodbyes, we left Gujarat — though not before hearing about one of its little quirks.

The Dry State… with One Curious Exception

Gujarat is famously a dry state, where alcohol is frowned upon and totally prohibited.

But our mine-owner friend told us about a fascinating loophole. When he goes on holiday with his family and friends they head here...


Just off the coast of Gujarat lies Diu, a small island that was once a Portuguese colony. Because of its unique history, Diu today belongs to the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, where the liquor laws are far more relaxed. Yes it's news to me.. it's the first I heard of this place.. one for the bucket list!

So while Gujarat itself stays dry… a short drive over the Diu Ghoghia Bridge and you can legally enjoy a drink on a tropical island with Portuguese forts and palm trees.

India never fails to surprise.

From Dry Gujarat to Wet Goa

From there we drove back to the city of Vadodara, got one of the four flights that day south to Goa — another former Portuguese outpost, but far better known.

The contrast could not have been greater.. but..

In Gujarat the alcohol free dry state.. 
In Goa the party state duty free drinks abound...

Both places are full of kind and warm people. 

Goa is always a good place to pause, catch up with friends and — importantly — catch up with POs and paperwork after a busy sourcing trip.

A few well-earned People’s Lager helped the process along nicely. 

The Great Escape

After a few days it was time to split up.

Toni flew Goa → Kochi → Doha and then onward to Europe.

Incredibly, the Doha flight turned out to be the last flight heading to Europe that day. A bit of luck was clearly on his side. He is now safely back in Málaga, Spain, breathing a well-earned sigh of relief.

Meanwhile Bondhan and I headed north. Mr Chatteree came to the airport with us.. he was heading back to Kolkata.  Us to Delhi then Bali.. on this trip Bondhan (our man in Indonesia) and Chatterjee (our man in India) have become firm friends.. So now in the departure hall it was time to say goodbye until next time.. 


yes... There were tears shed..

Goa → Delhi → Bali.

Which brings me to where I’m writing this now.

Back in Bali

Bali has welcomed us back with big winds and heavy rain.

At the same time, tourist numbers are currently down because several Emirates flights have been cancelled, leaving hotels and beaches quieter than usual.

For those of us working here it’s a strange contrast — dramatic tropical weather, but also a rare moment of calm before the island fills again.

For now it’s back to work with our Bali team and artisans, preparing the next wave of products for you.

Today we went to Ubud.. which is like artisan heaven.. 

After all, the journey from gemstones in Gujarat → temples → Goa → Bali is just one small part of the story behind the things we bring to your shops.

And as always…

More adventures are coming soon.

Take care.. Hati Hati (as they say here)

title: Poetic Train Trip
content_html:
Greetings from Mumbai airport. Where today is Independence Day in India.
Last week I was telling you about the Chapatti Redeye flight from Shanghai to Delhi.
Since then I have bumping around India trying to complete a few missions. In Delhi with the help of our agent, Amit the Poet (yes he's really a poet - more later) we found a supplier of pretty cool block prints. Little hand carved wooden blocks, originally made for the sari industry, but now sold as beautiful craft items, you can decorate cards and letters with little owl, or yin-yang stamps.. Coming soon.
People kept telling me about the Delhi metro, how modern, clean and smart it was. Just like Shanghai metro. So off we went, Amit showing me the ropes. From Nehru Place to Grand Bazar. We bought a pass card it's mine for life. Pretty slick system, you just top up your card from time to time. Wave them at convenient machines and it tells you your balance. As you enter or leave stations it reduces your balance. It's scary cheap, just penny's per station.
Well it might have been state of the art two years ago, but like anything else run by the state here it has degenerated in to a state of glorious squalidness. Really the ticket booth is a den of badly written signs cracked glass and disinterested staff. Paint work is a splash job, and I can't say anything looked particularly clean. When I tried to take a picture, two security guys were on me in seconds. No pictures sir.. Why? Terrorists apparently.
The privately run airlines, five star hotels and top restaurants are the finest you can find. The contrast between the excellence of young private businesses and the rotten corruption of old establishment government is one those Indian culture shocks.
The train journey was predictably jolly. In the crush we quickly made friends, everyone asking me lots of questions, where are you from, how many children do you have, how much do you earn, do you know David Beckham? those sorts of things.. Then someone recognized Amit the Poet, and a large circle opened up in front of us in a kind of awe. For here amongst them is a very large man, with an impressive mustache and a big booming voice. Very soon we have a poetry rendition underway.
We get off the train at our stop and now have a following. This is India.. I love it.
More tales next week.
Take care.
David

title: End of Year AW international updates
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield, UK

Yes I'm here in AW HQ.. and even though it is almost Christmas and normally peaceful at the wholesale end of things at this time.. it still seems to be all happening at full pace.
Containers arrive one after the other, the warehouse is buzzing and the office is full of chatter. In the lobby we have a famous local artist transforming the entrance so your first impression should you ever visit AW HQ.. is wow this place is pretty cool.. or something like that..
Last week I was telling you about the inner mystical meanings behind our new logo.. if you missed it you can read about it here.
Here are some pictures of the famous Peachzz at work. you can check out her website here..


Last Friday evening we had our Christmas party.. last year it was of course cancelled so it was kind of special to renew the tradition. It was 1920's themed and everyone got glammed to the eyeballs up for it, we had heaps of fun - it was like an old fashioned family knees up.  And then after the emotional speeches everyone danced until the small hours.  Yes, there is omicron.. it's scary, but we asked everyone to self test before and damn it all.. there is a feeling that enough is enough after what we have been through this year and it is OK to enjoy life a little. 

Of course I'm here for Christmas, but also it is the time of year we brainstorm and make BIG plans for the next year. And things are changing fast - it's a very different year we live in so we have to change and adapt to keep AW growing and healthy. Before Brexit half our sales were to the EU, now our customers there are dwingerling faster Conservative byelection votes. They find it too much trouble and delay to import from the UK and fast & easy to buy from our Spain or Slovak distribution centres. While UK sales are up and exports to the rest of the world are up a bit, it's not enough to cover the gaps. So we are planning and thinking big and thinking  outside of the box. 

One thing we will never do at AW is sell directly to the public. We focus on product sourcing and development, the job of retailing is your job. As customers/partners we will never undermine that relationship. 
So if you have any suggestions and ideas of area's we could expand into do let us know. 

India Update
Mr Chatterjee our man in India called me just now for a chat. He tells me that covid is pretty much over there, and all restrictions are lifted. He was urging me to visit in March next year, there is a trade show in Delhi and a lot of suppliers with new ideas.  Yesterday he loaded a container and today he went to visit the children's home we support in Saharanpur on the banks of the Ganges not far from Kolkata.Chatterjee tells me that four of the older kids have found jobs and moved out making way for four new homeless kids. 
Here is a picture of an art lesson..


They have a Christmas art competition.. 
If I can go in March - I'm looking forward to visiting and seeing how we can improve things more.

Indonesia Update
Ringo and his assistant Bondhan are working well, many of the products that I was working on while I was there a few weeks ago are now arriving in the warehouse. Yesterday they loaded two containers working until 3am and employing everyone they could find to pack and load the stock. In Bali covid is practically over, almost everyone is double jabbed and yet they still wear masks and social distance.. so cases are down to a handful. 10 day quarantine is back in force to counter the omicron variant so sadly no hope for tourism businesses just yet. At least we can do our bit giving the artisans work.


3am container number two leaves our warehouse in Bali.

China Update
I just spoke to Coco, she just finished loading a container for Spain. We had applied for a UK visa a few weeks ago with the idea that maybe she could fly to the UK for Christmas. But there are severe travel restrictions and, rather depressingly, her passport has not been returned yet from the British consulate in Shanghai, and no update whatsoever. Covid cases are appearing again and there is talk of a blanket travel ban ahead of Chinese New Year, so she might not even be able to get to her hometown.

Slovakia Update
It has been a massive year, everyone has worked very hard - under difficult conditions. Next year we will move to a brand new warehouse and lots of preparations are in hand.
I was telling you that there was a big problem with covid cases there.. I'm happy to report that everyone has recovered, and only one team member is still in isolation. This week they have unloaded a China container, an Indonesian and a full trailer from AW Aromatics UK.. to say they are knackered and ready for a Christmas break is an understatement.
Here they are..an amazing team in Slovakia..


Spain update
Toni our man in Spain came to the UK for the Christmas party and also to learn what he can. He made it back to Spain on Monday..
Christmas is very much in full flow there.. Three Kings Day on the 6th January is the main day for giving gifts, so the trading pattern is very different.
My favourite team (in Spain) is working hard even as we begin to relax.
My plan is to travel back to Spain on the 27th, so I can celebrate the New Year with them and make a plan for 2022. 

So as you can see - everyone at AW from all over the world is working hard to bring you the best in giftware. Thank you as always for your suggestions, feedback and valuable support.

Meanwhile in the UK.. it's not too late to order.. we can get your orders to you next week, and there is plenty of stuff back in stock see below.
You might want to stock up now ahead of the New Year sales.

This is the penultimate newsletter of the year.. 
I hope you are enjoying the festive season and staying safe.

Take care
David

title: David's AW News: The Conspiracy Guy.
content_html:
Greetings and Namaste from the Red Fox hotel Delhi.

I hope you are having a fun-filled Halloween!

I didn't plan to be here (in Delhi today) but things happen that you don't expect. (see below).

Little North/South correction.
Last week I was telling you about our very peaceful time in North Goa.. If you missed it you can catch up here... as my good friend in Goa quickly spotted, I had made a big mistake! My humble apologies.. I should have written South Goa. South Goa is peaceful and still underdeveloped, North Goa is like an Indian version and more hectic version of Benidorm. Party zone and noisy. They still have beautiful beaches (so I'm told) but not as tranquil and unspoiled as you can find in the South. 
We have this system where we invite our suppliers to visit us in Goa, they stay at the hotel we use and can bring only a limited range of samples. In peace and quiet we can carefully access the goods, make our modifications, organise our design team and then.. after making our PO, we head to the beach to watch the sunset and eat fresh fish with our friends. This week we have seen three different suppliers. Much less stressful than working in Delhi.. except..
Peace in SOUTH Goa.

Well all good things must end and Tomas had to leave on Wednesday, he got a flight to Dubia and after a short break will head to the UK. Yesterday Mr Chatterjee and I went to the airport together, me flying to Delhi to catch an onward connection and Mr Chatterjee back to his hometown, flying to Kolkata. As always an emotional goodbye. It's Diwali in India, the festival of lights. It's all peace and love, and everyone dresses in new beautiful clothes and greets each other with "Happy Diwali" on every interaction.  So nice, the airport staff and crew all have the Diwali spirit.. 
Here in India it's all Love, Lights and Laughter. 
In Europe it's all Ghouls, Ghosts and.. Laughter.

All Ghoulish AW folk..  
And as usual the AW teams are having fancy dress competitions..
 The Spanish team is celebrating their best month ever.. in Ghoulish fashion.
UK team.. the warehouse team too stressed and busy to take part, but accounts dept and marketing got in the spirit.
Hope your Halloween is as dramatic and fun. If you have time you can still vote (and get a shipping voucher).

Mine turned out to be a bit goulish.. 
So In Goa airport after wishing lots of perfect strangers "Happy Diwali" and saying goodbye to Mr Chatterjee I boarded a Vistara flight to Delhi. So very nice, I had the best food I have tasted on a plane, complete with Diwali chocolate fireworks.. and nice friendly staff.
Slightly strange chocolate fireworks.. 

Brutal News..
Then we landed in Delhi, only short lines at the immigration.. security took forever because the staff were in a jolly relaxed mood, but it was ok.. then to the business lounge, one of the best. I have four hours before my flight, so I open my laptop, grab a glass of wine and catch up with some work. I wish several random fellow travellers "Happy Diwali" which seems to bring so much pleasure to folk that it's addictive. Then I'm just thinking about going to the gate, when my phone pings.. "Your flight has been cancelled".. just that. No explanation or apology.. not even: "Happy Diwali, your flight has been cancelled". Just those brutal words.
I go and check the screens, everything seems normal. Maybe a mistake so I go and ask the chap at the reception.. who agrees it must be a mistake, but he phones Vistara office for me, and confirms it's true. But what to do..? 
To cut a long story very short.. it turns out that the flight was very light, maybe 50 people, some of whom were at a party of very rich Delhi people who were expected at a wedding the next day. An American lady had a similar story.  We settled down and kind of bonded in adversity.. 

The Conspiracy Guy
One guy (IT programmer) reckoned that because the flight was so light they had cancelled it to save money and the next day's flight would accommodate. A conspiracy theory that got everyone angry and upset and fights almost breaking out on the concourse.. A manager finally appeared and assured us it was a machine failure and nothing to be done..  We had been in the dark for three hours not knowing if we had an alternative route or not. Conspiracy theory man suggested they had kept us in the dark until the last flight to Singapore (where there are many connections) had departed.. This got everyone upset and angry again. Lots of pushing and shouting.
After a while I noticed the same manager at the next gate.. I wandered over to chat, wished him "Happy Diwali" - I said boy you have the toughest job in the world. He said but what can we do? Machine failure can happen anytime - I just do my best. 
Later they took us out of the airport, cancelling visa exit stamps, then to collect our luggage from a belt. Some luggage didn't come.. Conspiracy theory man, said this was on purpose to delay us further..more shouting..

Then we all trooped with our luggage (most of us) to a small ticket office with that manager and two staff to issue new flight tickets and hotel accommodation.   I'm standing on one side patiently.. just observing.. After a while someone quietly passed me a hotel voucher.. can I go now? I asked. Thinking I can get a taxi myself.. which I did and ended up getting a bit scammed by, but I made it bed..

So now I'm writing this update from the breakfast room.. this hotel is budget style but not bad at all.. nice friendly staff and all my new friends. We are all resigned to our fate, enjoying the experience for what it is..  I can't see the conspiracy guy, but I'm just reflecting how much a conspiracy can cause stress, upset and trouble. Words in the wrong mouth can be so dangerous. 

November is here.
Yes it's really November.. be careful with those fireworks.. but wishing you a lovely weekend.
Check out all the new Indian stock.. so much coming it's quite exciting. And much more on the way.

Namaste, Happy Halloween Weekend / Happy Diwali .. Christmas is coming..
Relax and roll with it.. 

Take care.
David
