title: A proposition for you..
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Now the mad tourist season has calmed down as the school holidays draw to a close, calm has descended on my part of the world.
But just as it gets cool and calm here, our distribution centers are really hotting up as folks' thoughts turn to the winter and xmas season. 
Our Spain and Slovakia warehouses are pushed to capacity already, so I hope we can manage to keep a decent turnaround of orders.. plans in progress..
Last week I was telling you about the time we imported tribal lapis jewellery from Afghanistan .. and what went badly wrong.. you can read about it here..
I have an important warning about potential fraud.. and a proposition for you..

But first some AW updates.. 
Ringo - our man in Indonesia - has been super busy. There has finally been availability of shipping containers, so in the last week or so he has loaded and shipped one for Slovakia, one for Spain and last night working through the night (day time is too hot) shipped two containers to the UK.
He always sends me pictures on Whatsapp of the packing progress... as it happens..

Calm down ladies that's not Ringo - these are professional container packers.. not wasting an inch of expensive space.

Coco - our girl in China - tells me that the two containers trapped in Ningbo port because of the lock-down have finally been released and on the way. Local media say just one case of the Delta variant was found in the port triggering a massive lockdown for over a week.
One of the drivers was confined to his cab for the duration.. poor chap that can't have been nice.

Mr Chatterjee - our man in India - was trying to convince me to go to India, apparently India is now on the Amber List.. and you can fly to Goa - quarantine in a hotel and then meet suppliers. Interesting, I'm checking out the possibilities. I do know that cases are dropping quickly there and the vaccination drive has finally kicked in at an impressive rate.  According to the BBC a hundred million doses in the last 19 days. 

I also learned that Indonesia may relax entry rules next week.. so finally a bit of good news, and light at the end of the tunnel.

Fraud alert!
This week in Spain we received a nice order - over €6000 and the customer requested to pay by bank transfer, so as always we sent a proforma invoice with the bank details to make the transaction.
Somehow.. we don't know how.. the customers email address was hacked. That email was deleted, and another sent from an email address that could be mistaken for an AW Artisan email address, with the same proforma invoice but the bank details altered to a Turkish bank account - and a very unlike us "URGENT" demand for payment. .  Fortunately google flagged the email as possible spam and the customer thought to check..
It was a close call and flung us all into a bit of a flap.. I'm not sure how to prevent this from happening. Much safer to always pay by credit card, gives you more protection and control.

Anyway.. lots of things happening that are good at AW.. it's getting busy now. It's almost September.. and before you know it the Christmas season is here. We have curated an Autumn Selection for you.... 

Lot's of articles in the news about stock shortages - and we have had lots of shipping delays one way or another - we are doing our best to contain prices and get sufficient supplies. Our man Bryant and his team in the UK are really on it, chasing everybody up and working on supply solutions and sourcing new products from new places.. even (get a grip) the good old UK.. We really think we'd be in a good position with our EU warehouses and streamlined (Brexit beating) export plan to distribute UK made products in Europe as well as the UK.. Do you make anything? Would you like to supply us? Drop us a line.. obviously you must be able to supply fully compliant products in volume and at a commercial price for the open market - bearing in mind we sell to retailers..
Reply to this email or email purchasing@ancientwisdom.biz directly.

Take care, have a great weekend, be kind to someone...

David

title: Keep Calm and Carry on
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 

A lot of new people registering at AW this week, I think possibly looking for new suppliers as supplies from the EU shrink.

Anyway whatever the reason.. Welcome! welcome to AW newsletter that tells you what's going on and keeps you updated on all things AW. 

 

Last week I was telling you about Storm Philomena which was lashing my home at the time. Also I was warning about other types of approaching storms. If you missed it you can read it here. And it's been getting that way all week, everyday bringing a new set of frustrating problems. Whose idea was it to do Brexit in the middle of a pandemic in the middle of a snow storm in the middle supply problems?

Oh yes.. I think we know who that might be..

Anyway UK supplies are running smoothly, and apart for snow reled delays we are shipping ok.





For our customers in Europe I strongly recommend using our EU warehouses for future orders, at least until this storm settles down. AWGifts.eu  (Slovakia) or  AWArtisan.eu (Spain)  
Current shipping update: DPD (the biggest) has extended their freeze on shipments until an update expected today (15th Jan) and other large companies are doing the same kind of things.  

Courier Logistics - UK all OK, but Northern Ireland technical problems. 
UPS - the online system for uploading customs documents is still not correctly working.
DHL & TNT - still seems to be working.

 

Katka, Bryant and the team in UK are desperately trying to solve a range of what the shipping company refers to as "supply events" and what I would call something a bit more caustic.. how do you explain to a French person that they can't cancel an order that's sat in a lorry in heaven knows where, but on the way.. for the last ten day.. I told Katka.. keep calm and carry on..

 

This was supposed to be a free trade deal, it's not. If anything it's worse. At least we prepared for this in opening warehouses in Spain and Slovakia. They at least are mega busy as trade shifts. We are taking on more staff in both places, we are looking to recruit a French speaking person to be the webmaster of AWArtisan.fr - if you know anyone in the Malaga region please forward this email to them. 

Toni, our man in Spain is getting a little stressed, we don't have enough staff and fast running out of stock.. I told him to calm down and carry on.. 

 

The situation with the cost of shipping containers from Asia still remains a problem, prices to EU destinations are easing a bit, but to the UK still remains sky high. 

We are still shipping from China, hoping to absorb most of the costs, but big bulky items will need to increase in price. Soap flowers for this reason we put on hold. Coco told me she is having trouble even booking a container at any price. Plus it's almost time for Chinese New Year and many places are closing early because of rumours the government will lockdown all the country to stop people travelling home for New Year - workers want to get away early to escape the ban. I told Coco to stay calm and carry on..

 

From Indonesia we took the decision to halt shipments until the prices reduced, because the shipping cost would have been as much as the product cost, potentially doubling prices.

Ringo, our man in Indonesia called me begging us to find a way to ship.. our warehouse is about 2000 square meters.. that's big, but now is crammed to the rafters. Even the offices and staff room are being used to store stock.

I told him to stay calm and carry on.. what can we do but wait until this storm passes.

 

Mr Catterjee called me from India, shipping prices are still a problem but more than this the domestic market has collapsed and suppliers have taken to asking for humanitarian price rises just to survive. I told him to keep calm and carry on.

 

So welcome to 2021, how's it going for you?

Keep calm.. and carry on.

 

Some good news.. some Atomisers came back in stock including some beautiful new models. 

 

More good news next week.

 

David

title: An Historic Day
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ Sheffield

Things are happening, we are moving..
Last week I was telling you how we needed someone to trust us with something big.
I was telling you how important trust is in a successful business. You can read about it here.
Today things are happening.. really happening.. great excitement, the great leap forward is happening :-)


Today is a historic day, well almost. We have the key to the new home of AW. It's not quite the end of the story, but it's looking like we have a new home. 
It is 77 days since our main warehouse burned down, if you have been following this story - you will know the drama, tears and triumphs over the last few weeks.
But now is time for a major, massive logistical operation.. something like 6000 product locations needs moving from one warehouse to another 15 minutes away from here.


So here it is..




It is in it's own compound, self contained.. almost 100,000 square feet. Offices, big carpark, 10 loading bays including container docking bays. This is a serious step forward, and after we move we expect to improve our service levels, increase the product ranges and offer a ramp of profitable opportunities for you, our customers. 
But we need your help. The building apparently doesn't have a name. Worse than this the address without a name could be several places in that postcode. search the postcode and you find a number of buildings with the same (almost) address.
Our new landlord suggested we rename it "AW House" - Adam our accountant suggested "AWThe  Giftorium"  but now it's your turn to suggest a new name.. 
Like everything at AW we are shaped by our customers.. so let us know your suggestions, the winner will get massive kudos, fame, an invitation to the official launch party as the guest of honor and or a decent bottle of champagne. 


That's the good news, the downside (at least in the short term) is the disruption to orders. Please be kind to us, try and understand that orders will be delayed probably from next weekend, but after we hope to catch up.
The other good news is that several containers have been stacking up at the port, and now we can release them - so lots of new stock can be diverted directly to the new warehouse.. 
Particularly exciting are several ranges of incense from India.. It was last October that Tomas and I first tried to source this Incense at a trade show in Delhi, at that time they told us the brands were not available to us (signed to another distributor), but perceived. Eventually, we managed to get a meeting with the big boss of the incense factory, a delightful charming guy who's French wife was the product designer. title: David's AW News: Happy New Year! X2
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China


Happy New Year! - Yes, it is - I received messages from my Nepali contacts, it's 2083 in Kathmandu - and on the same day, messages from Mr Chatterjee in Kolkata - it's Bengali New Year 1433. I was actually in Kathmandu last year with Toni, the city is a full-on party town for the New Year..  So strange, no?

But here.. It’s been one of those full-on weeks… proper China pace.
Sandra, Bryant and Coco… what a team. Long days, late nights, running between factories, samples appearing almost overnight… You get into that rhythm where you just keep going because you know you’re building something. Last week, I mentioned the plan — 12 Days in China to get it all done. If you missed it, here’s the link: 12 Days in China

Well… the twelve days are up. Sandra and Bryant have just headed off — an early morning taxi to Hangzhou, then onto Hong Kong. Bit of a strange moment really… that quiet pause after the intensity.

But I’m still here. Just tying up the last loose ends… final checks, making sure what we started actually lands properly.
We went to Old Yiwu.. (see below) but now… I need to tell you about something I’m really excited about....

A new arrival has just landed in the UK…
Melt Eaze Crystal Wax Melts.
And honestly — these are not your typical wax melts. They were created right here in Yiwu, the last time Sandra was here. A lot of work went into them — Sandra on the design, Coco making it happen on the production side. Proper collaboration. They’ve come out beautifully… something quite different, a bit more Ancient Wisdom… more gift, more story, more presence. Gold foil, fragrant wax and gemstones.. A premium product that, per my brief, would sell all day at the 3 for £10 price point. Melt Eaze Here

Feels quite fitting that they’ve just launched as Sandra and Coco are back already meeting again to start the next chapter…

And yes… we did have a bit of a secret mission. 
A proper “not sure if this is even possible” kind of idea.

Let’s call it a pet project for now…
This is Twan-Twan Coco's pet dog.

I won’t say too much (yet)… but I can tell you this —
I think we pulled it off. More on that later,,,

Before Sandra and Bryant left, we managed to squeeze in something a bit special… A visit to Fotang Ancient Town.
This place goes back to the Ming and Qing dynasties… and you can still feel it. It used to be a proper trading hub — boats coming up the river, goods moving through… in a way, not that different from what Yiwu still is today. We walked along the old wharf… crossed these beautifully lit bridges… streets full of little shops, all with that mix of old China and modern energy.

One minute you’re looking at traditional buildings, next minute there’s a glowing dragon running through the trees, families out walking, kids playing… real life happening around you.

We even ended up at a cabaret-style dinner — traditional Yiwu dancing, full costume, proper performance. One of those moments where you just sit back and think… this is why we come here.

And it did make me think… Ancient Wisdom isn’t that different, really.

Built on old ideas… trade, craft, story…
but always evolving, always finding new ways to bring it to life.

From a Ming dynasty trading town… to a modern global marketplace…
And somewhere in between, we’re creating products that carry a bit of that journey with them.

Anyway… a few more days here for me.

Then onwards.

Next week, NEWS from somewhere else.. see you there..

David

title: Nothing is Normal
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 

Hope you are well, welcome to February. It's almost Valentine's day, but not like a normal one.

Nothing is normal. Last week I was telling you about the new way we source and develop products in Indonesia, also how we managed to ship from the UK to Europe. 

None of it normal.. but you can read about it here.

It's almost Valentine's day, as I just mentioned and there is still time to land some V-deals.. see below.

The vaccine rollout in the UK is going amazingly well, at last, something to feel good about.

Snow is forecast, big snow.. so I hope you can bunker down and like grizzly bears hibernate until it passes. 

Meanwhile here is a roundup of what's happening around AW..


Coco in China. - CNY is cancelled.

It's the holiday season in China, as Coco and team breaks for Chinese New Year. We are taking the opportunity to move to a new better and bigger warehouse.

There is the AW candle factory also moving so it's quite a big job. Everything from the internet to toilets to be organised. She was trying to get everything done before heading back to the hometown for the CNY festivities. But there has been a big media campaign to try to persuade people not to make the annual trip this year.  Even though the Chinese government are claiming almost no cases and that China is safe, they are making it hard with expensive tolls on the motorway, limited rail tickets and.. a 500rmb (about £56) shopping voucher per person if you stay home. So for the first time ever Coco and the family are staying in Yiwu for the holiday.

 

Mr Chatterjee in India. Things are improving.

It's Mr Chatterjee's birthday so I called him up. He was in the children's home that AW supports. It's just a few minutes drive from the factory so he is often there checking on the teachers and wellbeing of the kids. They were just having a weekly computer lesson.

"How's it going there with the virus?" I asked him. It's good, he said - he told me no cases now in the area, people are relaxing, shops are open, things are getting back to normal. It seems they have developed a good natural immunity. Although most people still keep a distance and wear masks in public, it feels a lot safer. The factory is in full swing, we are giving them plenty of orders so life is looking up a bit.

 

Ringo in Indonesia. Can begin to breathe again.

He was really struggling for space. We had to put on hold shipments because the cost of shipping containers had exploded to where it would double the price of products just to ship them. So the warehouse was backed up to the point they were working in the carpark and the offices and staff room were full of stock. But we are loading containers again, a slight price drop means we can ship some more expensive items without a massive price impact. This week Ringo is sending me by courier a parcel of product samples for checking and development. So hoping to get some new products on the way.

 

James in the UK - our warehouse manager. 

He is manfully juggling thousands of pallet loads of stock as a team errects racking in the warehouse. It's a massive project, £200k of racking over 6000 pallet locations. We are blindly investing in Brexit Britain without really knowing if we will really need so much capacity. But somehow I feel if we have the capacity we will find a way to use it. Tomas is still in Slovakia, but next week (if all goes well) he is moving back to the UK. After quarantine he will start work on making our office space beautiful.

We are still managing to ship truck loads of orders to the EU via Slovakia, it's really hard work and expensive but we can do it. I'm hoping longer term to keep about half the EU business from the UK.

 

Meanwhile I'm in Spain, sales here are up massively as EU customers switch from the UK warehouse to Spain or Slovakia. We just took on an extra warehouse guy.. we will need more soon.. and Quentin a delightful French webmaster to look after marketing and customer service of all the new French customers. So it feels like everything is in flux, but we will find our way somehow or other.

 

So everything is happening, just not in a normal way.

 

Stay safe, stay warm.

More less normal news next week.

 

David

title: All Around AW - Please Help Us..
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

The weather is better in the UK I think.. but things are brightening up, and anyway no time to lay in the sun.. too much to do.
Coco (my wife and your China agent) is here and working round the clock. Last night she was remotely supervising another container being loaded from our China warehouse at 3am our time.. she is endlessly chasing orders and connecting via WeChat voice messages with suppliers, shipping companies and our China warehouse.
I have been spending time with Toni our man in Spain, discussing whether our warehouse is big enough, and how long (as we expand) before we have to move. 
But even though there is so much to do here.. I'm making plans to travel.. actually also need to squeeze a holiday (kind of) in to the schedule.. so stay tuned for details.
Last week I was telling you about the big Summer-Shake-Up in the UK..  if you missed it you can catch up here..

Graciela our talented designer (and webmaster) here in Spain kindly redesigned the header to this newsletter.. do you like it?
I wanted to change the tagline from "David's Travel Blog" - to News from around AW .. but as usual these days they just ignored me. 
My point is that there are things are happening all the time everywhere all around AW - all around the world.. it's like a dynamic creative force all purposed to deliver the best in giftware to your store.. 
For example...

1. I'm making plans to go to India and visit Mr Chatterjee, earlier this year we made an investment into their factory and I want to see how it is going. And see if we can't produce some super cool eco-friendly bags and things.. ideas please. Mr Chatterjee tells me that it's well over 40c there and unbearably humid. But they continue to work..  and are keen to make AW the best place for jute and cotton bags.. I really love the oversized Tie-dye cotton bags.. but we need more ideas to make the factory busy. Mr Chatterjee asks me everyday if I have made my plan to visit. 



2. The marketing / software development office on the beach in Bali. If you are a regular reader you will know that we bought a beach bar not long ago turned it into  digital marketing company cool office.  Our main IT wizard Raul who lives in KL not far away has been working with Peter from Slovakia to develop an ACE team.. and  Bondan and his wife Debbie have been nurturing and caring for it including organising bonding camping trips at weekends.
I really need to go and meet the new members of the team and anyway Bondan and Ringo message me every week.. when I'm I coming?



3. I didn't go to Turkey this year.. and our lovely agent Hatice who so diligently distributed the funds we raised after the awful earthquake - is ultra keen to work on more products with us.. the exchange rate now is incredible.. so in theory at least there should be good value to be found. The Bamboo Socks have been a great hit .. (father's day default gift) and the carpets particularly good in the UK market (all sold out - stock coming).
Strangely as I type this Hatice messaged me.. (she must have physic powers) "When are you coming to Turkey David?"


4. In AW-Aromatics.com Tomas has been continuing the Summer Shake Up and things are happening at pace.. Actually that factory is a gold mine of opportunities.. and my feeling is that we have for so long been sat on our backsides not really opening up the possibilities to you our customers as much as we could. The website has been revamped, and everyday lots of new products listed.. the mega trend in wellness and skincare is perfect for the independent business to capture a share.. check it out.. we need your feed back and ideas.. One major trend is Rosemary Essential Oil as a hair growth agent.. Yes I know we have known that for years it's practically ancient history.. but it is trending now.. so Tomas (who strangely worries about his hair) is into this.. See The World of Rosemary here  If you have time help us by filling our.. QUESTIONARE LINK HERE . we'd appreciate it.

5. Likewise Rodrigo at our main office.. AncientWisdom.biz has been reaching out to find what our customers are looking for.. we need your help to shape AW in the future..
QUESTIONARE LINK HERE .

6. Nepal (more tea and giftware)... 7. Morocco (more gemstones).. 8. China..  9. Slovakia..
Making a travel plan is not easy... haha but I will update you soon.. 

It's almost Father's Day.. and the wedding season is in full swing.. 
Check out our products and deals below..

Enjoy the warm weather.. wherever you are..
Any ideas for what we should be bringing you next.. please let us know. Thank you!!
Greetings from everyone at AW everywhere.. stay cool!

David

title: Meet Mr. Triangle
content_html:
Greetings from Bali .. now 62 days and still counting..


I tell myself there are worse places to be trapped in, and count my blessings.. but some days I feel just a bit depressed and frustrated. On the other hand, working with Ringo (our man in Indonesia) is great, and we have made our office space really nice. Working on the products, making them better than ever with enthusiastic suppliers who are delighted to have business is all good.

Following the newsletter about Mr Chatterjee and his good work in India (you can read it here) lots of people ask how they can help.
So I have made this gofundme campaign. I know lots folks have issues closer to home, but life is seriously buggered there.. if you can help a little you will save lives and gain massive karma.



Last week I was telling you about one of our suppliers, the guy who is making coconut lamps for us. You can read about it here. This week we took the first delivery of them into our warehouse in Bali. And it wasn't good.. 50% failed our QC tests...


he cotton ball shades came in various sizes.. including too big, and too small, the hole for the electric light fitting was too big. Even though we had tested a pre-production sample, and given him our fitting.. he had produced a thousand lamps that just didn't work.
Ringo called him to a meeting to discuss the problem.. he sat crossed legged on the floor with Ringo in the midst of the rejects. This big jolly guy almost crying, his English is not great but he used the word "responsible" a lot. It was his problem, he was sorry, he would find a way to sort it - he was a responsible man. The thing is that - and you can imagine the back story - he is an older guy - maybe 50, with a younger wife and small child, his grown up son with them. they live in a tiny set of rooms at the back of their workshop. They came from Bandung a big city in Java a year ago. His skill is making Coconut Lamps.. and with some success, but (covid-19 disruption to trade) barely surviving financially. Normally we pay 30% deposit and the balance as soon as stock is delivered to the warehouse. But this guy had requested extra money every week from Ringo, until eventually the balance on delivery was not that much. I could see this problem was going to kill him.


An idea.. I suggested that we fit rubber tabs to the feet of the lamps to upgrade the product a bit.. and since he was checking and reworking the product he could do this the same time, and we would pay extra for this upgrade. Good job I'm here stuck in Bali, because if not I don't know how it would have been resolved.

Most of our suppliers do well from AW, it's one of the rewarding things to see people get on, buy a car, build a house improve life dramatically, and I really hope this guy and his family can make it.
Another of our suppliers is in a different league. A big business really. Another "immigrant" this time from the island of Flores, Marsel a gentle, softly spoken Christian guy and his wife have a business turning redundant fishing boats into beautiful furniture. His cool crew of guys all from Flores are hands on artisans that can see the beauty in junk boats. We have been working with them a few years making teak displays for our Agnes & Cat brand (customers absolutely adore). When Tomas was here a couple of months ago, we came up with the idea of making a range of what you might call occasional furniture. Bedside tables, coffee tables and Mr Triangle.. designing and reinventing products to fit a range that we feel our drop-shipping partners will love to sell.

 

Up-cycled products are great no? Indonesia is home to over 6000 inhabited islands and for hundreds of years, traditional teak boats have been used to ply trade between islands and also for fishing. Traditionally when old and repairs become too expensive, they were burned for cooking fuel. People like Marcel buy up old boats so the owners can get a better return and save the precious timber for a second life. It's a circle of rebirth that appeals to me.


                                                       Old Boat

Is Junked...

Then crafted..
Into this....

Meet Mr. Triangle crew in action

The boats are at least 40 years old probably older when junked, the teak wood is truly aged - it's older than you when it is made new again, hopefully, to live with a family for generations.
Mr Triangle came from India, I bought him when I was young, a triangular set of draws, and home to bits of junk you only just needed to keep, Draws full of old phones, faded photos, receipts, and nick-nacks. Mr Triangle was a family friend and moved from house to house.. somewhere along the way I lost him.. but here in Bali, he was recreated.. reborn in more ways than one.



Next week we will be shipping to UK..

 

Last night I was woken from a bad dream, by the news that AW was on fire.. turned out to be a business across the road from us, gone up in flames so high half of Sheffield could see it.
Scary.. we might be insured if this happened to us, but I would never get over the heartbreak.



Hope you are doing OK.. don't worry AW is still very much alive and kicking. We are still fighting to catch up with orders - but making progress..

Here in Bali we maybe getting news that flights are opening up, that lock-down rules maybe relaxed - an announcement is expected 1st June..
As lock down eases - let's see what happens. Please stay alert.. stay safe, and smile at someone - even if they cant see you behind the mask :)

 

David

title: Warp Speed Ahead
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

My goodness it's full on all go, multiple things all happening at once. It's like the whole of AW from Indonesia, to India, to China,to Slovakia, to Spain, to the UK has slipped into some kind of warp drive.
Multiple containers being loaded - whole swathes of new products arriving - new equipment being installed, new people being started, new websites being (almost) launched, the new warehouse being organised.
Talk about full on activity and all in the face of covid second or third waves, Christmas trade and frantic preparations for whatever flavour of Brexit is going to be fausted upon us.
Last week I was telling you a huge potential problem we are facing with our new warehouse, that even though we are in residence we might have to move out... you can read about it here.

I'm in Spain at the moment trying to give some TLC to our talented and dedicated team here. Because of covid they have been left somewhat to their own devices, but that's not to say Toni and his team have not made great leaps forward. They have - with the most beautiful showroom at AW, the most delightful websites, the neatest and most organised warehouse. I'm proud of them. But now I'm here, I can help them move to the next level.. we got a truck full of racking from the UK, that we took out of Parkwood warehouse (in Sheffield to make room for the Beast) - the extra racking will give them spaces for quite a bit more stock, and enable a rapid expansion of the product ranges. And it's all happening fast. Very soon there will be a French and Europe wide website - all ready to cope with that Brexit moment. 

 

Meanwhile in Sheffield at our Aromatic Factory, the Beast from France arrived. Oh boy.. it's bigger than we quite appreciated even from the pictures and the written dimensions. It's a soap plodder to replace our old faithful one that was destroyed in the fire.. this was the only one we could find at short notice.. and it will produce like 10x what the old setup could. What it does is take sacks of eco-friendly soap noodles in at one end - mixed with all the good stuff.. aromatics (essential oils, botanicals etc) and mince them up into a plasticine type state and squeeze it out with huge force from various shaped dyes.. That's the first part.. the second part still is essentially by hand, cutting, stamping, molding, finishing and packing. Quite a labour intensive, but with this bit of kit we really can ramp up supplies - so we expect to build up good stocks and a good range of products.. fast selling beautiful high end soaps your customers will love.. and you (hopefully) will love that we can keep you supplied like never before.
We have the electricians wiring everything up today, all the packaging and raw materials have been delivered, staff will be trained on Monday next week.. we hope to be in production by Tuesday or Wednesday.. I'll update you.



So last week I was telling you about the mine shaft problem under our new warehouse.. It seems like there are eight mine shafts beneath our feet that could at any moment collapse plunging all your stock into a big black sinkhole.. obviously our new landlord (an investment fund) wouldn't want to buy the warehouse and we would be out on our ear.  No-one can find the papers that prove the mine shafts have been made safe.. Just now as I type this newsletter, Mike, our potential landlord, called me.. He told me.. "Don't worry David, it's going to be OK, we can't find the papers but the original developer has confirmed they did exist, and they are a highly respected public company.. so we are happy to take a view on it". 
Phew! I can tell you it's another load of stress lifted.. similar to when the insurance company finally (after way too long) told us they were accepting the claim. Like a huge weight lifting from your shoulders. 
2020 - who needs Netflix..  just too much drama already..


I'm sure you know this.. but in the UK this is the weekend that the clocks go back.. or is it forward? I'm easily confused.. Anyway, the thing is that the nights will suddenly be DARKER.. and that triggers that Christmas-is-coming part of the brain. The  Xmas songs will start a-jingling, talk of turkey and cranberry stuffing, and my friends the "Hunt for Gifts for Gran & Co" is officially underway. Usually when the clocks go back and Halloween and bonfire night are upon us - the gift trade leaps into a frantic higher gear.  How it will work this year (in the age of coronavirus) is unknown.. but one thing is for sure.. those with an online sales channel are going to be the biggest winners.. we can already see which type of customers are ordering big these days. Check out our AW-Dropship.com if you want to get in on the act without carrying (or investing in stock).


Anyway hope you have a good weekend, stay safe, wear a mask, be kind to someone, check out the deals below :)


More news next week.

 

David

title: David's AW News: I'm leaving.. (and my SOL picks)
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield - snowy Sheffield


This week has been mad, amazing, inspirational and a little stressful.  Valentine's Day is almost upon us. The SOL is in full swing. 

Last week I was telling you about my arrival here, the crashing, racking crisis in Spain and all the new stuff coming.. if you missed it, you can catch up here.

I'm staying in the Kenwood Hotel in Sheffield, there is a beautiful lake there, and I went for a walk and made a little video about how we humans have used love and romance to get us through the cold of the winter months.. Then I introduce my top 10 picks for the SOL (Season of Love).. I'll put a link to it below... and here.
Normally, I take a car from our car pool, or hire one while I'm here.. but for some reason, I just thought I'd manage with a combo of Uber and Friends just for the human connection.. and yes, learn so much. .every taxi driver has a life story to tell..  and I got to spend more time with my good friend Katk, who is a director at AW.. who kindly picked me up every morning. Thank you!!

This morning..
A fresh, beautiful Sheffield morning.. 

There’s a real sense of building right now at Ancient Wisdom. Katka and I have been sitting and talking to everyone (as much as possible) and finding out how we can grow together. 

We’re recruiting. We’re investing. We’re planning ahead — we have to grow this year. YOU have to grow this year.. 

One role I’m especially excited about is finding the right person to love, nurture and grow the Agnes & Cat brand. It’s a brand with a heart, a story, and huge potential — and it deserves someone who really gets it. Working at AW-Aromatics 
We’re also looking to strengthen our marketing team, because the next chapter needs more voices, more creativity, and more energy.

 If that sounds like you (or someone you know), please take a look here:
INDEED AW JOB

Join us. We genuinely have big plans.

So Holly made a deep dive into Agnes + Cat brand.. (we have some new candles just launched).

Check it out to discover or rediscover Agnes + Cat

Trade Show..?

Many people ask about the Birmingham Spring Faire.. we never exhibit.. So you won't find us there. But if you are passing Sheffield on the way there or back.. Why not call and see our showroom at AW HQ.. In my humble opinion far better than any stand in Birmingham. Showroom Sheffield.

You will be made very welcome (possibly by Rodrigo).. Serving the.. Best tea in town!

Spain Update
Toni, poor guy.. under so much stress.. working 24/7.. but I just spoke to him, and things are finally coming good.  All the stock is now in one warehouse.. a new racking company is starting, and everything should be in place this coming week. They are already back to picking orders as normal.. WELL DONE TEAM.. Huge relief, lots of teamwork, and a proper sense that it’s coming right. Well, you know what they say about Spanish people.. (it's not true!). 
The thing is, Toni has to finish this.. because when he has.. he is needed urgently in..

Kathmandu
Yes, it's travel time again.. Tomorrow I'm off to Nepal.. full report from there next week.. Hope you are coming along for the ride!  After India.. going to be a wild ride I can promise you.. If Toni makes it there (I hope he does), we have a lot of work to do.  New ideas, new inspirations, new partnerships… the adventure is about to begin again, and I’ll bring you along for the ride.

Finally, I have to tell you about the NEW STOCK..

Stock, stock, stock.
We’ve got lots of beautiful new arrivals landing right now for the Season of Love (SOL) — Valentine’s, Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, Easter, and beyond. Fresh lines, strong margins, and plenty of inspiration for the months ahead. And this is new for AW..  EXCLUSIVE to AW-Dropship.com - new Mini Speakers

Do you pack and dispatch yourself? AW Drop-shipping department is booming so much that we sourced (in China) all the envelopes, and mailers we use.. as green as possible.. And we found that we that our prices on them are better than market prices in the UK.. so we are happy to share.. 

Mailers etc from 4p


Scroll down, have a look, and stay tuned — there’s so more to come. New Money/Lucky Cats, new Floppy Hats.. New New New!!  

Speaking about the SOL.. here's my very personal take on it. Walking round the Lake at Kenwood Hall.  looking a bit ridiculous.. I'm just learning how to use my new Insta360 5X camera.. I bought it for making YouTubes in Nepal and beyond..  Top 10 SOL products..


Actually, if it had arrived earlier (NEW this week), the stackable rings - the latest Sandra-designed product would have been in the list.. 

As always, thanks for being part of the journey.

Warm wishes,
David
Ancient Wisdom

title: Looking for Letters
content_html:
Greeting from somewhere in China, the middle of nowhere.. where I can safely say I am the only Englishman. And it's great :)
Actually when I'm the only western face in town, that's when I'm happy - that's when I have made it well off the tourist/hippie/backpacker trail. And if I can locate beautiful products from family businesses then I'm ecstatic!

So it's still happening - Chinese New Year.. it's not over until the dragon dances. and that's a few more days. And enough CNY.. you can read about it in last weeks news: Right Here (if you missed it).

I had my haircut yesterday, it was fun. Everyone in the hairdressers wanted a selfie with me. They were so happy to have a tall englishman in their salon. I thought.. yes now I know what it's like to be Brad Pitt. Lots of questions like, can I have your QQ address (like a facebook address), are you married?, do you have a brother?, is he married?, can we have his QQ address? how big are your feet?... and so on :)

Now, do you remember Alastair Cooke, and Letter's from America?  You do? Then your getting on a bit old, old bean.. those honey tones coming down the radio, colouring in pictures of far away places and peoples. Well I want to tell you about my "Letter's from Indonesia" .. not what you think. I mean LETTERS - as in ABC.


I have been looking for letters, for ages. Not just any letters, but letters the right size, typeface, colour and most importantly at an acceptable price. I figured letters are a no brainer for gift shops, so many rich and varied gift applications. Everything from spelling your loved ones name, making "I LOVE YOU", MR&MRS (wedding gifts), naming your house, making a rude word, house numbers, heck there are endless uses for letters. 

I had been looking in China, India and Indonesia for a long time. Actually tried to get one or two companies geared up to make them but in the end quality or price was always an issue. Then one day talking to the magic box guys in Bali, I asked if they would be interested, they told me no.. but in a village near by they knew a guy who used to make letters.

So we went to see. We met a lovely guy, who turned out to be the head of his village. It was the usual Bali set up, a compound of houses with a shared work area, temple and farm yard. The village was high up the mountain, so from the bosses house terrace was the most amazing views. He told me they used to have a contract to supply vintage letters to an American company, but the orders had stopped coming. (I googled it and found letters at much too high price point - I reckon there's a limit to how much you will pay for your wifes name in wood).

Must be, letters about 15cm high (check), rustic hand carved (check), must stand up on their own  (never done that but, check), vintage typeface (check), our target price (without a blink..check) and from our research/experience by far the best selling items are whitewashed, shabby chic style. What's white wash? they asked, what's it mean? - Goodness me, no clue about whitewash? where are these guys living? Ah.. yes, up a mountain in the middle of nowhere. 

So we started to train them in white washing, it took some time and several samples. The guy came to see us in our Ubud office, and I was impressed by his attention to detail, every letter style he tweaked to look good and stand up, they worked hard to perfect the white washing technique. You have to paint it white, let it dry just long enough, and then wash it it off. Then sand and polish to get the right feel. 
Several times the guy said to me, please sir we want this business it will be so good for my village. He promised me they would do a careful and good job. 

Finally we worked out an order, OK, there's 24 letters, 10 numerals, and we got to have an "&" and a "@" - we are gonna need a few ready made sets "I LOVE YOU" and so forth.. and I think we need enough stock to supply half the gift shops in Europe, so I did the maths, and then did the order.. Our agent Ringo opened his haversack of cash and we counted out a deposit, it was a massive stack of cash. Indonesian money is bulky, even so it was bank robbery big. They looked happy.

On my next trip to Bali (last December) - Ringo and I went to visit. That sleepy compound was no longer sleepy, now a hive of activity. Some guys were cutting shapes, ladies were carving, some were painting and washing. In the house every room was full of letters, even the steps of the temple were full of shabby chic letters in big wicker baskets.  Even now as you read this in that far off village, folk are beavering away making letters for your customers. The daughter is a bit fed up, because her bedroom is a barcode labeling area but our man of letters in Bali is a very happy chap.

And it's been eight months since that initial meeting (pun intended), but those letters have finally started arriving. There are one or two letters missing from the first shipment, but they are on the way, and we hope to keep up a regular supply of letters from Indonesia, now the village is geared up they can make quite a lot.  

So... do I have to spell it out for you?   ORDER SOME LETTERS TODAY!  (see below) and keep a whole village happy.

Any suggestions... let me know - I'll be back there in about three weeks.

Take care
David

title: Turtle Tales and Team Triumphs in Bali. Be inspired.
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia.

Yesterday was Indonesian Independence Day. 78 years ago Indonesia was a diverse Dutch collection of places, cobbled together bloody conquest by bloody conquest.. Very different places stretching a very long way in a string of islands. Islands of different cultures, religions, languages. Some called it the Impossible country. More below.
Last week I was telling you about some of the modern day problems we face here and the story about the last artisan. If you missed it you can catch up here.
We have a Digital Marketing Team in Bali, regular readers will know how Tomas, Raul and I accidentally (almost) bought a beach bar.. and started a team.. now 15 strong.


Here they are.
So Debbie (top right in that picture) thought it would be a good team bonding idea to have a regional costume competition, the day before Independence day. One hour in the morning we would show off a costume, stand up and explain the costume and then entertain us in some way. Our team is very diverse and comes from all parts of Indonesia and it turns out they have many talents.  One by one with Ringo, Raul, Made (our export manager) and myself as X factor type judges they performed. Monologues, Dances, Storytelling and comedy.. all with great humour and enthusiasm.

Then back to work.. the serious business of marketing.. at the end of the day after work.. Debbie organised games in the garden. Then to support a local charity that protects turtles in the sea. Let me explain.. the Turtle population in the sea around Bali has been declining - lots of problems, mostly tourist related. The adult turtles in the night crawl up the beaches and lay eggs in the sand. Beach dogs eat them, tourists inadvertently stand on them.. Well lots of things happen and at one point only 1% of the hatching turtles made it back to the sea. So this Charity seeks out the freshly laid eggs, carefully transfers them to a secure hatching area, and then at a quiet time when the conditions are good the baby turtles are released back into the sea. They raise funds by allowing supporters to do the release. So we wanted to release 78 turtles, one for each year of independence but they only had 50 so it was symbolic 78.... 



Then back to the office to announce the judges' decisions, best costume, best entertainment ect.. everyone one got a prize in the end. After we had food delivered from a local  restaurant, cheap but very good, the party continued. By the end I felt that I had got to know the whole team so much better and also come to understand Indonesia better.
The Impossible country made up of very different cultures thrown together, has actually made it work. The founding father of Indonesia had the difficult job of binding this strange set of peoples together. They came up with five principles, the most important: Unity in Diversity. And has become a slogan of the country.   It's been a bloody and difficult journey with riots and deaths in living memory. Despite this (or some argue because of this and the lessons learned) the country has matured into one of the most friendly, respectful and peaceful places in the world. Personified, I'm proud to claim, in our diverse team here in Bali. And celebrated in our own way on the eve of Independence Day. 


Meanwhile despite all this excitement I have been super busy. This morning I was at the Chinese consulate in Denpasar to collect my passport now sporting a Chinese visa. So now I can make my travel plans.
Shortly I have a presentation from the Development Team. A new version of our website and backend is in the works, this should take us to the next level. 
This afternoon I have three sets of samples from three suppliers to approve.. this evening (Europe time) I have online meetings. So all go.
And... Next week I will be on the next leg of this trip to India.. 

So from diverse marketing teams.. turtle rescue missions and the artisans of Indonesia..  it's all happening here.
But I hear you ask... What can a gift trader like me learn from this?
I asked that jolly smart AI thing... and..

Team Bonding and Diversity: Just as the Digital Marketing Team in Bali found strength in their diversity, a UK gift shop owner can foster a diverse and unified team.
 Different perspectives and talents can lead to innovative product curation and creative marketing strategies.
Engaging Events: The costume competition and charity event underscore the importance of engaging events for customer interaction. Hosting themed events or collaborations can draw foot traffic, create buzz, and enhance the overall shopping experience.
Charitable Endeavors: Supporting a cause, like the turtle protection charity, not only contributes positively to the community but also aligns the business with social responsibility. Partnering with local charities can foster goodwill and attract socially conscious customers.
Online and Offline Integration: The mention of online meetings, website development, and backend improvements reminds gift shop owners to maintain a strong online presence. A user-friendly website and effective online marketing strategies complement the physical store's efforts.
Customer Engagement: Storytelling aspect highlights the value of engaging content. Sharing behind-the-scenes stories, customer testimonials, and product narratives can deepen your customer connections and make the shopping experience more personal.
Unity in Diversity: The concept of "Unity in Diversity" from Indonesia's founding principles can remind UK gift shop owners to cater to a broad customer base. Offering a diverse range of products that cater to different tastes, preferences, and occasions can boost sales.
Balancing Work and Enjoyment: The blend of work and enjoyment shows the importance of finding joy in the business journey. Incorporating elements of fun and passion into the business approach can contribute to a positive work environment and customer experience.

Wow.. did you feel inspired?

Great news - we have an Indian container just landed, Indonesia coming today and a China container on Monday - plus new products coming from AW-Aromatics... it's all happening!!

Wishing you an amazing weekend.. 

More news updates next week from India!

David

title: Catching the Zeitgeist & Free Sweets in 2023
content_html:
Greetings and Happy New Year from Spain.

The first Friday newsletter of 2023. Today in Spain is Christmas.. it's a holiday. Last night the Three Kings came.. throwing sweets and treats as the carnival went past. Sweets, you didn't know you wanted.. but here they come - lots of them an abundance.. 

 

It's a great fun way to start the new year, a fresh start and bright sweet abundant outlook. It's time to re-focus, get energised, let's get this party started!

I spent this week making big bold plans for the coming year..

And I had a really smart helper - you must have heard already but if not... prepare to be amazed.





And this helper is really going to change the world.

You remember the first time you opened google?. (if you're old like me) you will. Gosh it was twenty years ago.

In those days google was so clean, simple and useful. It's still useful, but these days you have to wade past far too many adverts, maps, shopping boxes, before you can find a list of websites that you can click to find what you want.. 

Do you hanker after those early clutter free results?

 

Well click here >>> Chat GPT  - you can thank me later.

It's artificial intelligence on tap..   

The key to using this jolly smart AI friend is to ask very specific questions .

After you have logged in.. type this.. I have a gift shop in Sheffield (put your town), and I want to increase my sales of Gemstone Power Bracelets (you chose a product), list me 20 ideas to do this.

 

Check that list.. if you want more - click "regenerate response".. I just did and the second list gave me more creative ideas than the first.. 

WOW!!  - it's amazing.. I was having dinner with friends who dream of opening a restaurant.. I typed.. Please create me a menu for a new Cuban / Japanese restaurant.  5 starters, 5 main courses and 5 deserts.

Imagine you gave a chef that job, how many weeks would it take to research and design..  in seconds it pumps out a pretty damn perfect menu. Jaw dropping stuff!!

 

I have made sure everyone at AW knows about this.. we are using it already.

This is going to be a massive productivity boost for the world.. What a great start to 2023! 

 

Our mission at AW this year is to bring you Quality, Value and the Zeitgeist.. The Three Kings of the Gift world.

You can sell cheap tatty discounted gifts if you want. You can engage in that race to the bottom. Price is important, but if that is all you focus on - you actually cheapen the concept of gift giving.



This picture is made by DALL-E - AI art.. I asked it to produce ..The Three Kings of the Gift World.. in digital art.

 

Quality also means integrity - fair trade and being good to our planet. Good Karma.

Value means balance.. Quality and Price. 

and the Zeitgeist.. What does that mean?  It's the thing you want and need but didn't know it until you found it.. It's the thing that's perfect for the time and place.. Like Chat GPT.. 

 

I will be travelling again soon.. hope you follow me by catching this newsletter every Friday.

Tomas (product guru) and Bryant (purchasing wizard) from AW are coming parts of the journey.. 

Here is a quick round up of news around AW.. at the beginning of 2023.

 

In Spain.. well as usual it's party time. But the team (MFT) has been working hard. The warehouse is already too small and the offices too full.. but with creative energy and ingenuity, Toni and the team are finding ways to manage.

In two years our lease ends and we will move to a bigger warehouse.. onwards and upwards.

AWArtisan.eu  - Delivering to Spain, France and Portugal - and Ireland - dear Irish customers this is your best place for AW goods.

 

In Slovakia.. Erika and the team are storming into the new year. New website is being launched for Sweden - so that's exciting. 

AWGifts.eu - 

 

In Aromatics - Sheffield, the production of the aromatic is back in full swing.. and one very important new product is coming to fruition.. maybe a Zeitgeist Product.. but let's wait and see.. Register to be the first to know.

AW-Aromatics.com  - Buying bulk or unlabeled or branded.. Buy direct from the factory for the best prices.

 

In China.. Coco is struggling - half the people have covid, and that means everything has ground to a halt. It's Chinese New Year soon.. so Coco is working hard to despatch the last couple of containers before closing.. and they keep getting cancelled, stock deliveries delayed.. so a bit of a headache. Good news is all the family have had Covid (except Coco) and recovered now. It seems the storm is passing.

 

In Bali - It was Galungan day - when the gods come down to earth. They are also having terrible storms.. part of our warehouse roof was blown off. But Ringo has it sorted.

 

In India - Mr Chatterjee and his son have a major new project underway.. we will be visiting soon.. so stand by for more details.

 

In AW HQ at Affinity Park. Rodrigo and his team are busy uploading new products, and it's surprisingly busy. Opening sales 50% up on this time last year.. I hope this is a good sign for 2023.

Dear customers - if you are looking for the Zeitgeist in 2023 just maybe you can catch it at Ancient Wisdom...

 

So, if you're looking for Quality, Value, and the Zeitgeist in your gift store, then Ancient Wisdom is here for you in 2023 and beyond.


And as always thank you for your support, feedback and ideas.

All the best for the year ahead.

title: The Devil is in the Detail 😉
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 

How are you doing? 

Last week I was telling you about two AW projects, one big one in the UK and one small one in Spain. How they are both important. The UK one comes with an amazing time lapse video..

You can read about it here..  I also gave you some fake news by mistake...

 

So I have an apology to make..  

Last week unilaterally changed Mother's Day from the 14th of March to the 22nd of March.. several eagle eyed readers pointed out. It was just a mistake. I googled it and somehow in my rush typed the wrong date.  

So just to make absolutely crystal clear mothers day is..(according to google) linked to Easter, which is different each year as it is determined by the lunar calendar. The UK's Mother's Day always falls on the fourth Sunday during the period of Lent, when people typically give up things like certain foods or bad habits for the days leading up to Easter*.


So it's so important to get the details right.. or you get in a right royal mess.

It's only two months ago that Boris was proudly bragging about his Free Trade Agreement. Remember under the Christmas tree on 24th December.  His oven ready deal was just for starters and in fact the Brexit FTA was a lovely Christmas feast with lots of fish included. 

You couldn't make it up.. But don't take it from me.. here is the link. 




The point is all that work put into the deal and all that fighting for the Scotish fisherfolk.. they missed a small detail. Sure the fisherfolk might be able to catch a bit more fish.. but they were not able to actually sell those fish, at least not efficiently because of the same trade deal details. And day by day more details that were not really appreciated come tumbling out of the woodwork. 

There was an article in the Times that seeks to blame economic modelling, how difficult it is to predict such things. It actually mentions that.. who would know that goods containing parts wholly or partly made outside the EU and re-exported to the EU would not be duty or tariff free?.. which turns out to be... erm most things. All the other stuff, like cheese, fish, lamb.. has a whole load of other regulations to climb over - the same as any other 3rd country. 

Fortunately Covid dominates the news agenda, so not so much bad news is making the MSM.. 

 

The unforeseen details are casting long shadows.. many consequences have yet to unfold.

What I'm saying is.. Brace yourselves.. expect stock shortages and increased prices.

Even here in Spain.. in the supermarket, food from the UK is either missing or double the price. There are no lamb chops and salmon is crazy expensive. Can this be good for anyone?

 

Back in June 2016, I was in the UK with Coco, my wife. She woke me at 3am to tell me via her Chinese news app that the UK had voted in favour of Brexit.. they knew before the BBC! 

Maybe because we had years of experience importing from Asia.. we had already figured out the fatal detail.. that whatever trade deal they could make it was impossible to avoid charging customers vat. So we moved quickly to open the Slovakia and Spain warehouses.. a huge and basically unnecessary investment but thank goodness we did it. 

 

Not that it has solved all our problems - far from it. 

Three weeks ago we shipped 29 pallets of stock from Sheffield to AW Spain.. we took all the advice we could, even checked things with Spain customs beforehand, we used the biggest shipping company.. with access to their top clearance experts..

Lots of paperwork, duty to pay, papers to produce.. we did it all, satisfied everything.. only one product couldn't make the grade, and held up all the shipment. Ironically it is a base oil.. aromatherapy grade olive oil...Originally from which country? You guessed it.. Spain!  they said but it could be used as a food product and we need a licence to import foods. Finally they agreed to release 22 of the pallets that we knew for sure didn't have the dreadful Olive oil on them. Then on Wednesday a team of customs officials turned up and wanted to open random boxes and started photographing everything, another load of questions and papers to supply followed. Including and I suppose this is a compliment.. Why are our prices so cheap? 

Maybe we will have to send the olive oil back to the UK in order to release the rest.. it's very complicated and hard work these days.. thank you Boris.

Dropshipping orders are up hugely on the same period last year, this is the covid effect I suppose, and we are adding staff to help keep dispatch times to the minimum. 

Gift shops (they are non-essential apparently) are due to reopen on April 12th and we are already seeing customers getting organised for this date.. Easter is coming and the wedding season could be great for business.

 

So it's not all bad.. the gift trade might be more complicated but it's still a great business. 

Hope you can think positive, and have a lovely weekend.

Take care, stay safe and remember those details matter..

 

David

title: David's AW News: Awesome
content_html:
Greetings from my hometown of Sheffield.

Happy BLACK FRIDAY!! 
Hope business is booming for you.
Here is the last trading day of the month.. so everyone is running like crazy..

Yes I'm home and at the HQ of AW. It's always good to be home, even if it's cold outside. Back home with friends and family and the teams at AW. 

Well it's just awesome. Last week I was writing the newsletter from the airport in Bali on the way here. From there I flew to Istanbul, and changed flights to Manchester. At the gate I had to pass two profiling checks and somehow avoided a final security search.. slightly scary when your flight has this extra layer of security. It's like they are expecting something.  You can read last week's newsletter here. 
But anyway from the beautiful art filled airport in Denpasar, Bali to the glamour stuffed stores of Istanbul international terminal.  





 Back down to earth :) 

Well it's just awesome. Like I said lovely to be home. Our man James met me outside and drove me back over the spectacularly beautiful Pennines to Sheffield. It was 10am on Saturday.. and we made it to the warehouse at Affinity park, Sheffield in time to thank the volunteer team that was picking and packing the huge backlog of orders.  In the aftermath of the 30th Anniversary offers. 

Yes we celebrated the 30th Anniversary, and by all accounts it was a big success.. parties across the AW world.. from Bali to India to Spain, Slovakia and of course the Mother company in the UK. 


My little speech on YouTube got over 170k views - and the promo brought in an all time record orders for one day.. but at the same time we received so many awesome new products..

Including the new Wellness & Gratitude Journals.. New fluffy Dream Journals.. so the combo of the offer and beautiful new products really made things buzz.


I have been trying the Dream Journals this week.. It's like an Intentional thing.. put the fluffy book by your bed with a pen.. read the bookmark details before sleeping.. You will dream for sure and remember the dream by immediately writing it down when you wake up.. 


Holly got inspired and made a cool video about the Journals.



I left Tomas in Bali.. 
Where he is working with the IT team.. and making excellent progress. We have some new team members and some new projects underway.
They are still working hard on the dropshipping websites which are booming right now..  and set to explode shortly (see below).
I was just chatting to him... he was complaining about the Indonesian staff.. 



5.30pm They never want to go home..

Death of Temu (maybe)


Well I had the budget on the big screen at AW.. waiting for Rachel Reeves to tell us that the De minimis Loophole was closing that a there would be a level playing field, and that all that dodgy stuff coming my air everyday - upto a million parcels a day.. all under a loophole avoiding duty, tax and regulations - including safety regulations.  Blink and you could have missed it.. just one line.. and in the small print we find the loophole will not be fully closed until March 2029.. A lot of people are up in arms.. SOMETHING HAS TO BE DONE..  
I am investigating a Class Action against Temu trading unfairly.. It's happening in other European countries.  A million parcels a day could have been stealing 20% of your business through unfair and unregulated business. Imagine you could claim that back. 


So Register Now.. in your down time this Christmas you could be creating a new income stream.
Anyway thank goodness we have Temu proof products to fall back on.. and if Temu is regulated soon then at least - YOU can grab a share of that online market via AW-Dropshipping.. API working well for Shopify, WooCommerce and I'm told Ebay is getting better by the day.

And see the new stock still arriving ready for next season.. the Season of Love - starts in January - we are preparing for it now.


Take care - have a lovely weekend.

David

title: French India & New-Age wonders
content_html:
This is a timely repost of a newsletter, a while back..
It's almost Mother's Day... so I thought you'd like to meet... The Mother..
Since the last newsletter from Delhi we have been to Goa and Chennai. Then we drove down the right-hand side of India along the Coromandel coast though beautiful peaceful country almost biblical, with palms and stretches of lakes replete with net casting fisher folk. Most un-Indian.
Finally we reached Pondicherry … forget everything you know about India. This is a town is place like no other. We arrived late in the afternoon, though the usual Indian city honks and hustle and bustle. Managed to find our little hotel on the edge of the French quarter of town. Basically a grand old Tamil house, central courtyard, rooms with high ceilings and monastic stained glass windows. It has been converted gracefully into a colonial haven of peace.
As dusk fell I took myself off for a walk around the tiny closed in streets. Almost immediately I came upon a fire ritual been performed by two priests on a slowly moving stage brightly lit and thronged by a fire-carrying crowd. I turned another corner and came upon an almost naked sadu blessing a mans new motorbike. Another corner and outside a street temple a huge pained elephant blocked the way, he was been fed by a queue of supplicants and seemed to be hugely enjoying the attention stamping his feet and waving his trunk.
I got a little lost in the grid of streets, but made my way back to the hotel to get my wife and Carlos.. they were both glued to the laptops catching up with work. Forget that guys.. you gotta get out here and see what’s kicking off.
By the time we set off (about 9pm) the place had reverted to an attractive, former French colonial town exuding a calm Mediterranean aura. What we saw were chic streets, elegant houses and ornamental gardens. All the street names are in French, policemen dress like gendarmes, and elegant French ladies cycle past on the way to evening rendezvous.  Honestly I told them.. really there was an Elephant and… but I could see they didn’t believe. 
Apart from the charming atmosphere what attracts many people to Pondicherry is the Sri Aurobindo Ashram and its strange new-age offshoot: Auroville about 15 km outside town. Auroville is a township founded by a French lady called Mirra Alfassa in the 1960’s with high ideals about no religion and no ownership.
It’s about all nationalities working toward a new world in peace and prosperity.  About 2000 people from 40 nationalities live here. Mirra Alfassa died in 1973 but her work and plans have continued, for the last 40 years they have been building a huge golden golf ball like building in the centre of town, it had finally been completed.

 In Auroville.>
So the next day we took a taxi to see this legendary place, you had be impressed. They have a trendy little shopping complex full of giftware and clothing produced in Auroville, a slick brain-washing, sorry information centre complete with a moving video show explaining the ideals and history of the place. After the show you take a peaceful gardened walk to view a symbolic Banyan tree and to the view point to see the what they call the: Matrimandir – what we called the golf ball. You can only look from a distance, your not allowed in to view the crystal ball that the building contains at it’s centre.. that is unless you want to go further..
The place is calm and reflective. It’s well ordered and not the least bit pushy neither were we charged anything to be there.  But high ideals about no religion had obviously failed as the French lady had now become “The Mother” and seemed to be revered and her attributes and images adorned the place.  While we wished them well, there was just a slightly creepy feeling to the place. 


This is Mirra Alfassa... also known as "The Mother"
Since it's almost Mother's Day.. it seems apropriate to give her a mention..

title: In Bali (the other one)
content_html:
Greetings from the beautiful island of Crete

I'm on holiday with Coco. On the island of Mythology, where the ancient Gods and Goddesses held court.  Over the years we have been to Crete a few times, and we love the little villages, fresh food, clean air, the smell of olives and pine trees and lots of ancient wisdom. We like to go a little off track, just hire a car and travel randomly around the island, finding rooms in small villages on spec. But for safety I'd booked the first two nights in the small resort town of Bali about 40 minutes from the airport. 


Bali (the other one)

I had managed to find a (slightly strange) flight leaving from Malaga at 1.55am to Athens, transit to Thessaloniki and onward to Heraklion Crete.  And as we drove to Malaga airport, I had a strong feeling in my gut, apprehension maybe, do you know what I mean? - when you just feel something bad will happen but can't explain it...

Last week I was asking you to "Join the Revolution" and a little bit about my business life before AW.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

We dropped the car off in the car hire returns area, dumped the keys in the out of hours drop-bin and headed up to the check-in desks. I opened my logged in tickets in google wallet.. to find a message "Flight Cancelled" - What!! That's a great start to our holiday. At the check-in desk we found the usual queue waiting for check-in to open. I showed my phone message to the lady behind the desk.. Oh really she said looking a little shocked.. picking up her phone and speaking rapidly for a long time to someone.. when she hung up, she said no problem, it's just a mistake..  but there was an hour delay. I wondered how many fellow travellers had seen that message and just gone back home..

Here is some strong travel advice: Always take pictures of your luggage including hand luggage.. you never know when you might need them.
When we checked in - I pointed out that we had missed the connecting flights, but the lady still issued the flight tickets. As we boarded the plane the same check-in lady was there and she told us that there was no room for large hand luggage and Coco cabin bag was whisked away and I was given another luggage tag stuck to the back of my flight ticket. 

We arrived in Athens, and an email very efficiently informed us we had been booked on a different flight to Crete leaving in a couple of hours, and sure enough a ground staff member handed us fresh tickets as we left the plane.  
Whilst waiting, I checked the hand-luggage tag, in the box marked "final destination" was the letters SKG - that's a big mistake - I thought  (not Crete) and went to find the Aegean desk to report it. They fixed it with a few taps on the keypad - and told me all OK now. Anyway when we finally landed in Crete, and collected our luggage when the belt finally stopped, of course Coco's bag was missing. 

Coco was very stressed, because in that bag was all the essential things, meds, jewellery, important papers. A nice lady called Olga took our details at the lost luggage desk, and assured us it would be found and forwarded to our hotel. But a day later she called me to say the tag had probably come off, and they needed a picture of the bag to locate it.. we found one by luck.. 

Anyway the town of Bali is beautiful, and maybe because of it's name - it has built up connections with the Island of Bali (regular readers will know we have a warehouse and offices there). Our hotel is furnished almost completely with stuff from Bali. Many restaurants and bars have Balinese light shades and even the shops have plenty of Balinese giftware. It's a total coincidence that this old fishing village is called Bali. The origin for the name of the village was the Turkish word balik, meaning fish.. But it's funny how name coincidences can shape a place.. They even have Yoga studios and Bali style spa's here and Coco felt relaxed practicing Yoga on the cliff top.


Bali vibes in Bali


Yoga is good for easing the stress of losing your luggage..

Olga called me and said the luggage had been on a solo european tour and had been found in Stuttgart, Germany.. and would arrive in Crete at midnight, because the tag was missing we must go to the airport to collect. That was good news and bad news..  But turns out Olga was slightly confused or misinformed.. because as we went to breakfast, someone had delivered the lost bag already - there it was sat

Hope your weekend is trouble free and you are suitably relaxed..
It was the International Day of Yoga this week.. and we have lots of chilled deals for you..

Take care - more news next week.

David

title: Let's Get Cozy
content_html:
Greetings again from Sheffield. It's 55 days since the fire. 

...and we are doing OK, well surprisingly well considering.. I'm sure it is because of all the positive vibes fizzing our way from our amazing friends and customers.

Last week I was telling you it was 4444 days from when we occupied the building to where they finally pulled it down. That number is the angel number, (and it has a surprising meaning) you can read about it here.
The building was utterly destroyed, nothing survived the inferno, nothing at all.. everything, but everything reduced to ash. Oh except for one thing.. one building panel only remained untouched.. the one that held the sign "Ancient Wisdom", the name survived.

So finally the insurance company started to be nice, hopely we have reached an agreement, the bank if we need it will support us, we found an insurance company to insure us (at a reasonable fee) moving forward.. Everyone at AW has a list of things to sort, and I feel we are gradually as a team making them happen, ticking off the items on our lists one by one. My list is written on a blackboard on the wall by my desk for all to see.. one thing remains un-ticked.. A New Warehouse. And this my friends is the dilemma. 

So it's like this.. Keith our amazing landlord - I can't begin to tell you how supportive he has been - will of course rebuild Block B. It was big, over 30,000 sq ft. but nowhere near big enough. We estimate we really need 50,000 minimum. So it seems now is the time to move to a new location. Especially since it will take maybe 18 months to rebuild it, and we will have to muddle through with temporary warehouses, outside storage and a car park full of rented containers.. not ideal. 
It turns out there are not that many big empty warehouses in the area, you can count them on one hand, so we have maybe two that could work for us. One is mega 96,000 and a huge leap of faith.. 

Yesterday Keith came to see us with his architect who is called Tall Ted, on account of being a lanky 6' 4" - Ted had drawn up beautiful plans.. a bigger, longer, higher warehouse.. now 40,000 sq ft, with offices high on the back of the building that will have spectacular views down Don Valley to the Sheffield wednesday football ground.  Nice. "We want you to stay - we don't want to lose you,'' Kieth said. And he outlined a plan to build temporary buildings, use part of the car park.. all sorts of things to mitigate the pain.  But he also understands we actually need bigger for AW to continue to grow. I also feel a moral obligation to stay.. not least because we have a lease commitment. Sure the building could be re-let in the 18 months, but the question is do we stay or do we go?
In any event a move is not cut and dried, acquiring the mega warehouse is in itself a mountain to climb. We also need it immediately, scrub that we need it - really really need it like yesterday.  

Big Charley the manager of the demolition team came to say goodbye, this gentle giant and his three guys (and some monster machines) have dismantled the building and dumped it in skips in 18 days. A big nasty mess to a big clean empty space. Seems like a monumental task. But that burned out mess, gone for good, hells-bells, feels better. I gave him a Hymalayan salt lamp and some Rose & Ylang Bath Salts as a parting gift. 

It's a bank holiday weekend, the last holiday for a while. It's September almost, and peoples thoughts begin to turn to Christmas. It's going to be a strange Christmas in this covid world, all we want for christmas is a vaccine.. but I feel this year candles will be popular. I noticed posh candles are in high demand already - which is odd in the summer... so as the nights close in - in difficult times - folks seek out cozy and that means candles, attomisers, fragrances and incense and hot baths. Let's get cozy..

We have prepared some great deals for the weekend. Oh and great news Attomisers are back in stock.. Check below.
