title: David's AW News: Got Zapped!
content_html:
Greetings from the AW Frangipani Warehouse, Bali


Yes I'm back in Bali (on the way back to the UK).  Last week I was telling you about our time in China and some of the new family businesses we are forging relationships there. 
If you missed it you can catch up with our new friends here. 

Tomas took himself off to Beijing to visit the Great Wall of China for a couple of days, and agreed to meet me in Bali later. But huge storms across China, delayed and cancelled swathes of flights, it turned into a bit of a drama just getting from China to Denpasar, Bali.  I missed a connection and had to spend an extra day in a Guangzhou airport hotel. Tomas came down from Beijing on a seriously delayed flight and somehow we ended up on the same flight - even sat together. After a very bumpy flight we arrived in Bali at midnight yesterday.  The storms followed us in and I didn't get any sleep (it seemed) because of biblical crashing thunder and epic electric lightning which seemed to be zapping my particular hotel room..

The next morning bleary eyed we headed to the AW-Advantage beach office to discover our electric supply had been zapped by the storm...  

Our Frangipani warehouse is not far away and has a small office for Ringo and his admin team and a sample room / meeting room. Not much space.. but somehow tables and chairs were found and all 16 people from the beach office packed up laptops and computers and (no drama) relocated to the warehouse office.. crammed cheek to jowl.. we found them cheerfully getting on with it. Ringo's team graciously relocated to the warehouse sitting on boxes.

Raul (the IT wizard) and Peter (the SEO wizard) from Slovakia are already here ahead of us. So because it is already one year since we launched AW-Advantage.. It is time for staff reviews and renewal of contracts. 

Our second day in Bali improved, a good night's sleep,  the stormy weather passed, the sun came out, electricity was restored and we were able to get back to the beach office. 

So today we have been doing staff reviews, the system is very different in Indonesia. How it works is staff are given an annual contract, at the end of which some robust negotiations take place. Someone who feels they have contributed well over the year might ask for a hefty increase, or if someone has performed badly they might not be renewed at all. In our case we are very happy to keep everyone and we are looking to expand at least another three people - we don't want to lose anyone.  So far as I'm writing negotiations are continuing and nobody seems to want to move on... looking good! 

Today is the one year anniversary of launching AW-Advantage, regular readers might remember we had a Balanese ceremony and blessing from the local holy man - actually something strange happened then. 
You can read the report here.
To celebrate, we are planning our first (of many hopefully) annual staff meals.  Apparently we are going to Turtle Island.. should be interesting..
I'll tell you about it next week.

Meanwhile in the UK.. we have lots and lots of things back in Stock. A big India shipment arrived and lots of wonderful lines ideal for your spring displays.
I was just chatting with Rodrigo, our UK webmaster, and he was excitedly telling me about Crystal Elemental Soaps. Soaps with an elemental theme (water, fire etc) they are beautifully packaged and the best thing is they have a mystery crystal inside. The AW-Aromatics team has been working on this for about six months.. I love the concept.. wash your hands and eventually a crystal will emerge.. I feel this will be so easy to sell to your customers.

Take care. Have a lovely weekend. Don't get zapped :)
More news next week.

David

title: So what happened?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

Last week I was telling you about the blooming flowers and busy busy resort of Whitby.. You can read it here.
It's almost the end of May, and it's almost the end of May :) - so hard for Mrs May, she was given the impossible mission, drank the poison chalice, never gave up when everyone else did. Finally, the rock and the hard place meet. 
Whatever you think of Brexit you have to give her credit for her grit and determination.

Regular readers will know we have a sister company in Spain, AW-Regalos, you will have read over the years tales of Carlos our business partner here and his talented team.

Dear friends, customers and readers. Take my earnest advice: If you want to put your trust in someone in business, for goodness sake ALSO get a contract drawn up.
Actually, I do a lot of business with a lot of people, mostly on a handshake and an exchange of emails. It mostly works because mostly my judgement of character is pretty good, but we all can make mistakes, or people can of course change.

I met Carlos at the wedding of good friends, a Chinese couple, they had invited us to China for their wedding, my first time in China. I was introduced to this charismatic good looking young Spanish guy, Carlos - and we immediately hit it off. He was in partnership with the Chinese couple, in a giftware wholesale business in Spain, in Malaga. To cut a long story short, the company wasn't doing so well, it was practically bankrupt, and I ended up helping out. We took a 66.6% stake, bailed it out - put in AW products and marketing systems and quickly turned it around. I would love going to Malaga (often with UK team members), our team working with the lovely Spain team, developing new ideas making things happen. I loved experiencing the different business cultures, getting involved in the products that work better here, eating sardines and enjoying relaxed Spanish live style. It made for many an interesting newsletter :)

So what happened? 
It started to go wrong (I think) at the point I gave Carlos shares to make him 50% owner and also sole administrator (like MD) in 2006 on trust with no contract...  By this time the company was pretty healthy, looking like it would soon pay back the capital invested by AW UK, and start to make a contribution to the greater good at AW. Of course, it didn't work out like that.. after 13 years of patiently waiting, asking nicely, requesting openness and honesty..  right now it is looking like the end of the road.. despite trying everything I can think of to build bridges, even extending extra credit.. and this being abused. Carlos took the credit and then stopped buying from AW and stopped paying AW 6 months ago. So it was bound to end in tears.
I really understand how Mrs May feels.. she is having a hell of a job making something happen and it's just not happening.

Maybe I will tell you more of the sad story next week..  I still hold out for a happy ending.
All you need to know for now is that the AW in AW-Regalos no longer stands for Ancient Wisdom.. at best a bloody.. Awful Waste..  

We have this week launched AWGifts.es (direct from UK) so that our Spanish customers can still have access to AW products, and even though it's still work in progress a veritable flood of customers are registering, and orders coming already. 
More information here.. looking for 

MOVING ON...
It's another Bank Holiday.. hopefully, it is going to be successful and sunny.. 
Spring Bank Holiday in the UK.. the official start of Summer I always feel.. 

Lots of stock in this week, including Soap Flowers back in stock.

More news next week.

take care

David

title: David's AW News: Blue Screens.
content_html:
This morning seems like that Netflix movie where strange unrelated things keep happening. Strange things..

Anyway it's still all happening all at once.. big announcement soon (probably) for AW-Aromatics.. stand by for BIG NEWS!

Last week I was telling you about why we had to visit the Police Station in Spain - if you missed it you can catch up here.
Meanwhile some good news..


Containers for storage in Spain finally came.

Three second-hand containers now sit in our carpark at AW-Artisan Spain.. our warehouse is at capacity and we have many containers on the way from India etc.. with nowhere to put the new stock items.
We had a bit of a panic, because the company took our money then went quiet on us.. but ended well in the end. This is our temporary fix.. 


They need to be cleaned and painted in bright cheerful colours. I think we will need more.. but let's see.

Meanwhile in UK.. following feedback from our lovely customers.. Rodrigo and team have been taking better pictures of our bag ranges.. this involves field work - notably to Meadowhall the big shopping centre just outside Sheffield not far from our warehouse. 
Since we started sending free samples of our bags and improved presentation.. orders are coming for bags - thank you for your support


Here in Spain everyday a big yellow fire plane flies low over my house and skims the sea in the bay below picking up water to go and dump on a wild fire somewhere inland.


By all accounts this year they (so far) are keeping things under control.
I watched the historic Spain / England match at home, you could hear cheering and celebrations (maybe some crying) from far away in the hot night air.
So afterwards you can understand my alarm to hear some folks setting off celebratory fireworks around my neighbourhood. Stupid and Scary.

In further news.. lots of new stock arriving in the warehouse - I'm so excited to see new esoteric gemstone items.. 
Also by popular demand we secured a stock of Macrame style gemstone holding necklaces..
Personally I like the Guohua picture stones - we found them in China. Quite a specialist thing (not for everyone) - but the idea of natural million year old art - I find calming. Part of a range of products from a small family business, a mother and two sons. The Father (we didn't meet yet) is often on road trips around China and outside to secure raw stock whilst the Mother and sons work hard in the showroom and warehouse.


A super hard working family, and Coco has been getting on well with them to get some of the most exciting gemstone lines to us.

Wishing you a beautiful weekend and hope the "Blue Screen of Death" doesn't catch you..
Strange days.

David

title: Connecting the Dots
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Sheffield.

Yes we are in the hometown of AW. Sunshine and blue skies, friendly Yorkshire folk and lashings of the worlds best pale ale.
I'm so happy to be back in my hometown and catching up with family, friends and all the team at the heart of AW. And my wife (and our China agent) Coco is here also.
It was December 2019 the last time she was here, just as rumours about a strange illness were starting to circulate from China. I remember getting in a crowded hotel lift in a city centre hotel and seeing two people wearing masks for the first time, we were all holding our breath until we could get off.  Then KERBANG.. the whole world changed. 
Last week I was telling you about the trip from Xiamen (China) to Sheffield (UK) and realising ten years had past.. if you missed it you can read about it here.

There is (I can see) brilliant blue skies over the UK and a long bank holiday weekend ahead. So I'm wishing you all a very busy trading week ahead. But I hope you can find time to dream a little, let some creative ideas bubble up as you chat to customers or friends.. join a few dots and see what happens.
Last weekend I took Coco to Chatsworth House.. she absolutely loved it. Although she kept asking me how one family could amass so much money to create such a place. I didn't know, it was (I asked ChatGPT) Coal mines, iron works, farming and finance. The Cavendish family was pretty industrious 400 years ago. Even today with farm shops, beautiful gift shops, the brand is awesome.. they connected a lot of dots..


Coco being a typical tourist.

We have been mostly spending time at the AW Aromatics factory where new ideas are bouncing around like excitable spring bunnies, trying to focus all that energy into actual new products is a task in itself. Coco has been connecting the dots, many products just don't make it because of missing components (at the right price) or simply missing altogether.. and China can fix many things.. and PDQ. Whatever you think about China, the fact is we need them to make our UK factory actually work. The world needs to work together, to even (for heaven's sake) actually work. 

Do you have an idea for a product? Are you an Influencer? Do you need us to make your product a reality? We already produce for a number of personalities.. and I can tell you this is where the big money is.
In China, almost everything is sold this way.. their version of Tik Tok is full of specialists, enthusiastic people, passionate people selling directly to their fan bases.. It's the future. And at AW-Aromatics we can help you be part of that future.
We even can connect the dots for you.. AW -Fulfillment  (ask for James) can store your product and then ship it to your customers as and when you need.

Imagine if you will for a minute.. Your journey connecting the dots...
1. A customer asks for a product she has heard about (for example that Grapeseed oil is good for under eye bags), you ask Chat GPT for more info, find out that this is trending on Instagram.
2. You have a brainwave about branding, and added ingredients.. 
3. You log-on to AW-Aromatics buy the raw materials you think you need.. in your kitchen start experimenting..
4. You test and re-test your product in your store.. and in your social media channels.. and...people love it!
5. Back to AW-Aromatics.. can you help me make my product on a big scale?. For sure.. That's what we do. 
6. Onward and upward.. now you just need to get it on the supermarket shelves... 

I believe most ideas, most solutions, most success stories are not difficult, probably in plain view.. you just need to do it. Connect the dots.. damn it!!

Meanwhile at AncientWisdom.biz  we have containers unloading everyday - it's buzzing here.. I just came over to chat with Rodrigo and the team.. we have containers just arrived from Indonesia. Now shipping costs are getting back to normal, Rodrigo is keen to revise prices where we can. So you might have noticed a few chunky (and timely) price drops on some of our best selling lines. Natural Coconut Lamps, last week, this week on Molten Glass on Wood. See below for lots of great deals. And some awesome new products.. I'm so happy to see the Healing Incense Powder. The ritual of making a pyramid of powder on the healing plate is just so zen.. your customers are going to love it, and collecting the full kit to do it. 

Yesterday was National Bath Bomb Day.. can you believe? Haha, whatever we all need a special day.. anyway I do feel that Bath Bombs are trending again - we have some new funky ideas on the bath bomb front and some mega deals on the Fragranced Just Desserts Bath Bombs.

In other news.. the AW Buddha at AW HQ, got a bit of a revamp today. Ula decided to brighten up our icon a little. 


Anyway whatever you are doing... ENJOY the weekend, hope you can connect your dots.. and have fun and a fantastic time.
Take care.. and as always thank you for your support.. 

David

Last week I was telling you about the trip from Xiamen (China) to Sheffield (UK) and realising ten years had past.. if you missed it you can read about it here . There is (I can see) brilliant blue skies over the UK and a long bank holiday weekend ahead. So I'm wishing you all a very busy trading week ahead. But I hope you can find time to dream a little, let some creative ideas bubble up as you chat to customers or friends.. join a few dots and see what happens. Last weekend I took Coco to Chatsworth House.. she absolutely loved it. Although she kept asking me how one family could amass so much money to create such a place. I didn't know, it was (I asked ChatGPT) Coal mines, iron works, farming and finance. The Cavendish family was pretty industrious 400 years ago. Even today with farm shops, beautiful gift shops, the brand is awesome.. they connected a lot of dots.. Coco being a typical tourist. We have been mostly spending time at the AW Aromatics factory where new ideas are bouncing around like excitable spring bunnies, trying to focus all that energy into actual new products is a task in itself. Coco has been connecting the dots, many products just don't make it because of missing components (at the right price) or simply missing altogether.. and China can fix many things.. and PDQ. Whatever you think about China, the fact is we need them to make our UK factory actually work. The world needs to work together, to even (for heaven's sake) actually work. Do you have an idea for a product? Are you an Influencer? Do you need us to make your product a reality? We already produce for a number of personalities.. and I can tell you this is where the big money is. In China, almost everything is sold this way.. their version of Tik Tok is full of specialists, enthusiastic people, passionate people selling directly to their fan bases.. It's the future. And at AW-Aromatics we can help you be part of that future. We even can connect the dots for you.. AW -Fulfillment (ask for James) can store your product and then ship it to your customers as and when you need. Imagine if you will for a minute.. Your journey connecting the dots... 1. A customer asks for a product she has heard about (for example that Grapeseed oil is good for under eye bags), you ask Chat GPT for more info, find out that this is trending on Instagram. 2. You have a brainwave about branding, and added ingredients.. 3. You log-on to AW-Aromatics buy the raw materials you think you need.. in your kitchen start experimenting.. 4. You test and re-test your product in your store.. and in your social media channels.. and...people love it! 5. Back to AW-Aromatics .. can you help me make my product on a big scale?. For sure.. That's what we do. 6. Onward and upward.. now you just need to get it on the supermarket shelves... I believe most ideas, most solutions, most success stories are not difficult, probably in plain view.. you just need to do it. Connect the dots.. damn it!! Meanwhile at AncientWisdom.biz we have containers unloading everyday - it's buzzing here.. I just came over to chat with Rodrigo and the team.. we have containers just arrived from Indonesia. Now shipping costs are getting back to normal, Rodrigo is keen to revise prices where we can. So you might have noticed a few chunky (and timely) price drops on some of our best selling lines. Natural Coconut Lamps , last week, this week on Molten Glass on Wood . See below for lots of great deals. And some awesome new products.. I'm so happy to see the Healing Incense Powder . The ritual of making a pyramid of powder on the healing plate is just so zen.. your customers are going to love it, and collecting the full kit to do it. Yesterday was National Bath Bomb Day.. can you believe? Haha, whatever we all need a special day.. anyway I do feel that Bath Bombs are trending again - we have some new funky ideas on the bath bomb front and some mega deals on the Fragranced Just Desserts Bath Bombs . In other news.. the AW Buddha at AW HQ, got a bit of a revamp today. Ula decided to brighten up our icon a little. Anyway whatever you are doing... ENJOY the weekend, hope you can connect your dots.. and have fun and a fantastic time. Take care.. and as always thank you for your support.. David

title: David's AW News: Team China in Action.
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China.

Hope things are going well for you and you are all ready and prepared for Easter weekend - coming soon!
I'm finally in Yiwu now with Coco and a few days ago Tomas arrived. 
Last week I was telling you about our journey from Pokhara to Kathmandu to Guangzhou to Yiwu.. including a leg on the world's most dangerous airline. If you missed it you can catch up here. 
Since then Tomas arrived on a flight into Hangzhou and Coco arranged a car to pick him up and bring him. We met him just as he checked into his downtown hotel. Which was lucky because credit cards often don't work, nobody accepts cash and anyway most ATM don't like visa or mastercards. So lucky Coco was on hand to make his room deposit. So the "A" team is reunited. Tomas, Coco and Myself.. This is Tomas's first visit to China since before the pandemic.. so a lot of catching up to do.

Downtown Yiwu is looking more and more like Shanghai these days.

Well it's been a frantic busy week so far..Tomas arrived with a huge wishlist (collected from you our customers) and a selection of mood-board type creative ideas from our talented designers. Our time here is a little limited so off to a hectic schedule.. on top of this we have a back-logg of compliance paperwork to bring up to scratch.. much of this needs to be dealt with face to face to make sure we are actually fully compliant and all the relevant tests and certificates can be properly done. On Top of this our warehouse landlord has gone bankrupt, and we need a new place to store and load containers.. so between factory visits we are viewing potential warehouses.


It's pretty hard work, most of the warehouses are dank, dark and totally unsuitable. I suspect our property agent, a natty dressed young chap driving a Tesla, is playing the usual game all agents do.. showing us a few bad and expensive places first in order for something half good to look great. 

Coco and Tomas posing outside the main entrance to the wholesale market.

Last time I was here 6 months ago, it was dead quiet in the market with traders complaining of practically no business. But now something has changed. The place is buzzing again, although with South Americans, Russians and Africans the main buyers. Not so many Americans or Europeans. Some but not so many - so our suppliers are super happy to see us. But when business has been slow it leads to much more innovation, new products and ideas aplenty as traders work hard to attract trade. 

We spent one day doing factory visits, another exploring the main giftware parts of the market saying hello to old suppliers. But then we just had to go visit the gemstone market - it's not in the Yiwu official market.. in the back streets old school traders.. and wow it's full of fresh ideas! Whole days eaten up checking out the new amazing stuff here this time. Yesterday and today we spent many hours totally immersed in gemstones. Beautiful things that I'm sure your customers will just fall in love with. In China the internet is restricted (as you probably know - even VPN's don't work too good now) but fortunately I found a way to hack the phone and internet so that we have a pretty good connection and can research on the spot online and check market prices.. this is speeding up things no end. Thus we have access to Google lense and this is also a major boon to check if prices given are good enough for you to compete.. 

Tomas making selections..

Meanwhile back in the UK..
New stock arriving.. today we have a Salt Lamp container landing and a China container in. So lots of fast selling things back in stock..

Take care and more updates next week.

All the best
David

title: David's AW News: For the Cosmic Record
content_html:
Greetings From Spain.

Friday again… and the football has started.


Last week I was telling you about life here in Spain, the warehouse, Peter and Tamara’s wedding, Slovakia’s 9th birthday, Kane moving on to his dream job, and all the usual Ancient Wisdom comings and goings. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

This week, things are looking up.

I finally have a date to collect my NIE card here in Spain. Once that little card is safely in my hand, I can travel outside Spain again without the usual paperwork drama, border complications, or me trying to explain myself in my best emergency Spanish.

Coco is coming to Spain soon too, so travel plans are being made, bags are being half-packed, and life suddenly feels like it is moving forward again.


Meanwhile, we are deep in the middle of Midsummer Madness. And honestly… it is living up to the name. Today is Day 3 - — Midsummer Bath Rituals! 


Rasos — the Festival of Dew.

Fun Fact for today: In Lithuania, Midsummer is also known as Rasos — the Festival of Dew. People once believed that the dew gathered on Midsummer morning had special power, and that herbs picked at this time were at their strongest. A wash in the morning dew, a dip in the water, a gathering of flowers and herbs — it was summer self-care long before anyone invented the phrase. 

Today we bring that idea indoors with bath salts, floral soaks, Sunflower Serenity and Greenman Rituals. 

Every day we are learning some crazy midsummer fact, some strange tradition, some bonfire ritual, some odd little historical thing about summer, luck, light, flowers, water, fire, wishes and general seasonal madness.

It is slightly affecting everyone. Our Alex came to work and immediately fell over - so keen to get to the deals. Captured on the CCTV.. Don't worry he is fine.  


The deals have also got a little bit out of hand. Perhaps too enthusiastic. Perhaps someone should have been supervising the discount button more carefully.

But it is what it is.

Midsummer Madness!

For a few more days we have sweeping voucher discounts, special 48-hour family deals, extra surprises, and the odd little gift thrown in because, well… we seem to have gone a bit mad.

This is a good moment to stock up, try something new, fill a gap in your shop, or grab one of those product families you have been meaning to test for ages.

And then next Sunday is Father’s Day.

This year it falls on the same day as the summer solstice — the longest day of the year — and, just to complete the strange cosmic triangle, the World Cup is underway too.

Father’s Day, the summer solstice, and World Cup football all circling around the same weekend.

Not quite once-in-a-lifetime, but it does not happen often. A bit like the planets aligning — only with dads, daylight, discounts, and football.

So dads, grandads, stepdads, father figures, and all the quietly useful people who know where the spare screws are kept get the longest day possible.

That feels fair.

A long bright day for family, football, gardens, BBQs, slightly overdone sausages, and maybe a gift that says: “I remembered.”

So yes, football has started, midsummer is nearly here, Father’s Day is almost upon us, my paperwork cloud is lifting, and the AW teams are pushing on through the seasonal madness with good energy.

Thank you as always for being with us.

Enjoy the deals, enjoy the light, enjoy the football if that is your thing — and if it is not, enjoy the brief moments when everyone else is distracted.

Peace & Love,

David
Ancient Wisdom

title: David's AW News: Delayed by Donald
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


And happy Halloween.
Happy last day of October.. November is here!!
It's scary how fast the time flies, it doesn't seem like ten minutes since last year's Halloween.
Traditionally at AW we get in the spirit and come to work in ghoul and ghost mode.. 
I'm writing this before all the costume drama has taken place..(time zone issues) but see below for the results.


Last week I was telling you about saying goodbye to Toni and Chatterjee (my travel companions for the last few weeks in India) and flying from our base in Goa to Bangalore and then to Kula Lumpa.
If you missed it you can catch up Here.


Goodbye Mr Chatterjee - see you next time.

Full Body check
I was in KL for my regular body check at the Gleneagles Hospital. One of the nicest hospitals in the world, I want to call it the Gleneagles Hotel, because it has a lobby, bell boys, a grand piano and welcome drinks. There is something about hospitals in the UK that is stressful and desperate.. here I don't feel that. Anyway I spent a day in their health screening dept kept busy moving from room to room getting every organ and body part checked by delightfully kind and friendly people. Normally I get a full bound report with print outs and a consultation with my assigned Doctor by the end of the day. But I was on a Saturday shift, so they emailed me on Monday.  I highly recommend it. And it's great value. 

Delayed by Donald
Sunday I travelled to Bali.. Which was bad timing because Donald Trump was just arriving. All the city was in lockdown for the ASEAN conference, and the motorway between the city and the airport had been closed in both directions, for the exclusive use of Trump. So my taxi driver seemed more stressed than me.. taking the back routes to the airport, I saw parts of the city I have never seen before, instead of 40 minutes it took us two hours to get to the airport. Anyway because of all the VIP movements my flight had been delayed. Thank you Donald.
In the airport, I was asked twice to stand still and stand back whilst some minor VIP came past on an airport buggy. At arrival points small teams of dancers in traditional costumes were waiting to greet delegates with Malaysian gift packs. History in the making.


Gemstones Horror Story 
Now I have never really thought about this before.. We have checked carefully the people we buy gemstones from, the artisans in India, China, and even in Morocco. Making sure conditions are good and trade is fair. But think about it.. it's kind of blindingly obvious that those rocks come out of the ground. That part of the process that's not really visible.. 
Well, a little AI research and I was horrified to discover that in poor areas children have been used to getting into small shafts to dig out gemstone deposits. I mean WTF? 
Well in India it turns out not all bad news.. but we had to go and investigate.. I made a YouTube video about it.


But questions still remain, gemstones trading routes are complex. The world's gemstones come from Africa, Madagascar, India, China and Brazil.. (in the main).
One of our suppliers here in Bali, who originates from West Java, told me about an area there rich in Gemstone production. I'm thinking of going and visiting.

Meanwhile in the UK..
So much stock has arrived.. a lot as it happens from India.
And also some wonderful creations from the AW Aromatics team. 



These amazing Bath Spell Potions (Bath salts) have a gemstone amulet attached (actually from India).
I feel they will be a top selling product this Christmas..

Holly has been busy reviewing the new Ancient Witch Ritual Candles..


A beautiful detailed product. Another design master piece (in my opinion) from Sandra.

Since I'm in Bali now - I'm happy to see that the popular Molton Glass Bowls are back in stock..
Plus we have three new designs just arrived including a pretty fancy Duck Decanter - perfect for Christmas.


Artisan, beautiful and a perfect gift.

Anyway wishing you a wonderful fun and festive weekend.

More updates from Indonesia next week. 


Take care
David

title: I'm in 1944
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali - it was Bali New Year this week.. 


Hope you are well during these troubling times, I'm having trouble sleeping because just doom scrolling all hours over the horrible Ukraine situation.
Here in Bali there have been large demonstrations outside the Russian consulate in Denpasar with most Russian people here supporting Ukraine. 
Last week I was telling you about a spooky village where storks are gods.. you can read about it here..

Nyepi is the Bali New Year, a year is 210 days long, so it's a bit complicated and apparently this year is 1944.. Regular readers of this newsletter will know about it - I seem to have been here at Nyepi several times. If you don't know about it.. new years eve is a festival of the Ogoh-Ogoh - basically, huge evil monsters that are paraded around the streets and hold mock battles until late at night they are ceremonially burned. From 6am until 6am the next day is a Day of Silence. The entire island comes to a standstill, with no scheduled incoming or outgoing flights from the airport and absolutely everything closed. "Nyepi" in Balinese means “to keep silent” and falls on the day after the dark moon. .
I remember the first time I stayed in Ubud it was Nyepi.. it was a wild festival of Ogoh-Ogoh all over Ubud, dozens of the things each with their own gang of creators humping them around banging drums, and total festival atmosphere..It was so crammed with people and parties that we had to abandon Ringo's car and walk back to our hotel on the outskirts of Ubud. The next day, total peace and quiet..



Ogoh-Ogoh monsters.
How things have changed. The last two Ogoh-Ogoh parades across Bali were completely cancelled due to Covid regulations.. this year there was much discussion about getting back to something normal.. we were told there would be an actual parade through Ubud..
So yesterday evening I bagged myself a front line table at the fabled Kafe Ubud which faces Hanuman Street and is the perfect spot to see a passing parade. The waitress told me it would pass by about 7pm, Bondan and his wife came up from Denpasar for the evening and I arranged to meet them there.  The manager at my hotel told me the parade was on and off all day because of an argument between Ubud and Denpasar who wanted to cancel it due to rising covid cases in Ubud.

7pm came no parade.. 8pm nothing.. So we decided to leave and try and find out what was happening. No parties in Ubud this Nyepi, quite the opposite.  Walking back towards the hotel, we found it was pitch dark.. every light everywhere was already off. The day of silence had it seemed, already started. A hot, humid and an electric storm flashed occasional sheet lightning casting ghostly shadows..  In the gloom we came across a lady in Balinese ceremonial dress carrying an offering on her head.. Bondhan asked what happened to the ceremonies.. she told us it was all happening deep inside the Monkey Forest. We decided to go and investigate..
If you don't know about the Monkey Forest, it's a famous park in the heart of Ubud. Full of moss covered statues, jungle paths, deep pools, hanging vines and thousands of sacred monkeys. At the heart is a temple. We got to the entrance and sure enough there were hundreds of motor bikes parked.  Something must be happening - temple security guys known as Pecalang stood at the entrance. We asked if it was Ok to go inside, and was told politely that it was not open for outsiders.

So disappointing.. then I had an idea, a slightly naughty idea.. "Come on guys" I said follow me. I remembered from the time we had our warehouse in Udud that there is a secret pathway that runs along the back edge of the Monkey Forest and is a shortcut to Yellow Coconut Village.. there is a back entrance to Monkey Forest, and I remember not so far from the temple. I found the cutting and we stumbled in.. now pitch black, even the mobile phone torch light barely pierced the darkness.. It was hot and I was sweating, animals moving nearby, fallen trees to get past, a little tunnel, a footbridge over a stream.. I had forgotten how far it was.. "Come on guys, we can make it.."
Finally we tumbled out into the top of Yellow Coconut Village.. and the back entrance. Nobody there.. no Pecalang to be seen and the gate slightly ajar.. We could hear the gongs and rhythmic chanting of a mystic ceremony.. lets go..
Keeping to the edge of the path in the dark we snook down the path towards the noise.. as we came around the back of a large building we saw the temple bathed in flood lights.  We got as close as we could.. Heart beating, I made a short video.. then we spotted two Pecalang just on the other side of the wall and decided to hotfoot it back to safety.


We stumbled back down the jungle path, out on top of Monkey Forest Road, and back to the hotel.
So hot and humid, we all needed a shower and change of clothes.. but wow.. at least we had had an adventure.

Today - as I write this it is the Day of Silence and the streets are empty, Balinese people (including Ringo) do not work at all. It is a day to contemplate life, to think about how to improve relationships and balance.
Something the whole world could do with doing right now.. 

Tomorrow we are going to a Balinese wedding as guests of Ringo. It's in his home town of Bangli far from the tourist trail.. His niece is getting married and Bondhan and I are very fortunate to be invited, we are to wear a traditional dress so it will be super interesting - I hope it's not cancelled like the parade at the last moment.

Lots of new stuff online including products such as Macrame Hanging Shelves from Indonesia...
Plus some stunning deals.

Take care. 
More news next week.

David

Nyepi is the Bali New Year, a year is 210 days long, so it's a bit complicated and apparently this year is 1944.. Regular readers of this newsletter will know about it - I seem to have been here at Nyepi several times. If you don't know about it.. new years eve is a festival of the Ogoh-Ogoh - basically, huge evil monsters that are paraded around the streets and hold mock battles until late at night they are ceremonially burned. From 6am until 6am the next day is a Day of Silence. The entire island comes to a standstill, with no scheduled incoming or outgoing flights from the airport and absolutely everything closed. "Nyepi" in Balinese means “to keep silent” and falls on the day after the dark moon. . I remember the first time I stayed in Ubud it was Nyepi.. it was a wild festival of Ogoh-Ogoh all over Ubud, dozens of the things each with their own gang of creators humping them around banging drums, and total festival atmosphere..It was so crammed with people and parties that we had to abandon Ringo's car and walk back to our hotel on the outskirts of Ubud. The next day, total peace and quiet.. Ogoh-Ogoh monsters. How things have changed. The last two Ogoh-Ogoh parades across Bali were completely cancelled due to Covid regulations.. this year there was much discussion about getting back to something normal.. we were told there would be an actual parade through Ubud.. So yesterday evening I bagged myself a front line table at the fabled Kafe Ubud which faces Hanuman Street and is the perfect spot to see a passing parade. The waitress told me it would pass by about 7pm, Bondan and his wife came up from Denpasar for the evening and I arranged to meet them there. The manager at my hotel told me the parade was on and off all day because of an argument between Ubud and Denpasar who wanted to cancel it due to rising covid cases in Ubud. 7pm came no parade.. 8pm nothing.. So we decided to leave and try and find out what was happening. No parties in Ubud this Nyepi, quite the opposite. Walking back towards the hotel, we found it was pitch dark.. every light everywhere was already off. The day of silence had it seemed, already started. A hot, humid and an electric storm flashed occasional sheet lightning casting ghostly shadows.. In the gloom we came across a lady in Balinese ceremonial dress carrying an offering on her head.. Bondhan asked what happened to the ceremonies.. she told us it was all happening deep inside the Monkey Forest. We decided to go and investigate.. If you don't know about the Monkey Forest, it's a famous park in the heart of Ubud. Full of moss covered statues, jungle paths, deep pools, hanging vines and thousands of sacred monkeys. At the heart is a temple. We got to the entrance and sure enough there were hundreds of motor bikes parked. Something must be happening - temple security guys known as Pecalang stood at the entrance. We asked if it was Ok to go inside, and was told politely that it was not open for outsiders. So disappointing.. then I had an idea, a slightly naughty idea.. "Come on guys" I said follow me. I remembered from the time we had our warehouse in Udud that there is a secret pathway that runs along the back edge of the Monkey Forest and is a shortcut to Yellow Coconut Village.. there is a back entrance to Monkey Forest, and I remember not so far from the temple. I found the cutting and we stumbled in.. now pitch black, even the mobile phone torch light barely pierced the darkness.. It was hot and I was sweating, animals moving nearby, fallen trees to get past, a little tunnel, a footbridge over a stream.. I had forgotten how far it was.. "Come on guys, we can make it.." Finally we tumbled out into the top of Yellow Coconut Village.. and the back entrance. Nobody there.. no Pecalang to be seen and the gate slightly ajar.. We could hear the gongs and rhythmic chanting of a mystic ceremony.. lets go.. Keeping to the edge of the path in the dark we snook down the path towards the noise.. as we came around the back of a large building we saw the temple bathed in flood lights. We got as close as we could.. Heart beating, I made a short video.. then we spotted two Pecalang just on the other side of the wall and decided to hotfoot it back to safety. We stumbled back down the jungle path, out on top of Monkey Forest Road, and back to the hotel. So hot and humid, we all needed a shower and change of clothes.. but wow.. at least we had had an adventure. Today - as I write this it is the Day of Silence and the streets are empty, Balinese people (including Ringo) do not work at all. It is a day to contemplate life, to think about how to improve relationships and balance. Something the whole world could do with doing right now.. Tomorrow we are going to a Balinese wedding as guests of Ringo. It's in his home town of Bangli far from the tourist trail.. His niece is getting married and Bondhan and I are very fortunate to be invited, we are to wear a traditional dress so it will be super interesting - I hope it's not cancelled like the parade at the last moment. Lots of new stuff online including products such as Macrame Hanging Shelves from Indonesia... Plus some stunning deals. Take care. More news next week. David

title: Of Drugs & Dragons
content_html:
Hello and Happy Holi.

I'm in China now right after Chinese New Year, (in Yiwu) but in another part of Asia it is a full blown colourful crazy holiday.. known as Holi.

Last week I was telling you about my Letters from Indonesia.. read them here..
Yes it's India's biggest festival and the most fun. A time when normally conservative Indians go a little bit wild, throwing buckets of colour at each other and painting the town red... and yellow and blue..

It is the festival of colours, the festival of love and heaven knows.. anything goes. I remember the first time I experienced the crazy full blown Holi festival. I was in in Kolkata, staying in the ITC hotel in Salt Lake, it is a peaceful hotel famous for minimalism and peace and calm.

But outside we could hear a tremendous roar of activity, a street market come party come mad-house. We ventured out, against the advice of the door-man and went to see what was happening. Before long Carlos (our man in Spain) and I were swamped by street kids and covered in paint. We were offered, and I remember drinking something from rather grubby looking clay pots from a dreadlocked holy man. Only later realised I had been drinking a cannabis smoothy. It's called Blang.. you can read about it here. About Blang.
Soon I'm off to Java for a short trip then to Kolkata and Bangalore.

So have things Indian on my mind..
Have you seen our new Yin Dragon Incense Gift packs? I think they actually make a nice Mother's Day gift, for any old Hippie Mums.
Someone asked me for the back-story to these and if they were from a reputable source. So I want to introduce you to Mr Holk.
Most incense in India comes from village people who hand roll the incense.. which is OK, working at home. Then it it is fragranced and packed at a furious pace in hell-hole factories - much worse than clothing factory sweatshops, because the dust and fumes. I can tell you I have cancelled orders more than once when when I have seen working conditions..
Mr Holkor who makes our bulk incense and now the Yin dragon.. is good guy. A smallish family business, very humble people, we are his first export customer.
I remember the first time we met, he picked me up from my hotel in my hotel in Delhi. I don't think he'd been inside a big hotel before, because I found him sitting in reception on the edge of a chair looking terrified. I don't think he'd been inside a big hotel before, because I found sitting in reception on the edge of a chair looking terrified at the all the comings and goings of a city hotel. Back then he had a ancient tiny car waiting in line behind the taxis and limos. I was sat in the back with my legs left to right bouncing along banging my head on the roof for what seemed like hours wending our way on little rural roads to the north of Delhi. On the way Mr Holkor explained to me that that they had only worked as a contractor for other bigger incense companies, producing cones and sticks that then got packaged and turned into various brands. He wanted to escape the contract production and export directly, but he frankly told me he had no idea how.
We finally arrived in his village, where his company operated from a series of farm buildings. Inside semi automatic machines stamped out incense cones and on the roofs the fragranced sticks were laid out to dry in the sun. It was a beehive of activity and people seemed surprisingly well dressed and jolly. His office was a bare table in basically a cow shed, mud floor, bench table and plastic chairs. But he'd arranged for a wholesale perfume guy from Delhi to be there, to sample fragrances that might be suitable for the European market. So I thought they are thinking about this... they also seem to understand that certain materials can't be used in exported incense and that quality was a big issue. At the end of the day they were so humble and open, that I agreed to help them get started exporting.
At a later meeting I introduced him to Mr Chatterjee our agent in India, who helped them obtain an export license and talked them through all the (massively) complex bureaucracy that is Indian exporting.
For the next six months, parcels of fragrant samples followed me around asia, waiting for my approval or rejection. Finally we whittled down a range of acceptable fragrances, tested burning times and ended up with a super range of incense that make up the bulk incense sticks and coneswe now stock.
Then last year, Mr Holkor brought me a range of boxed incense, using our fragrances and a bit of nifty packaging. We redesigned the labels and put together a range of gift boxed sets. Mr Chatterjee later told me that during negotiations, Mr Holkor had asked him how much to charge and given him all his product costing, saying I trust you to advise us fairly. See the Yin Dragon Incense here.
Mr Chatterjee has helped them a lot, last month (February 2015) at the grand Delhi trade show, next door but one to Chatterjee and his Jute company stand was Mr Holkor and his incense company stand on his very first trade show outing, proudly displaying his wares to the world. It's great to see people get on, don't you think?
So you know it makes scents... stock up withYin Dragon Incense and Bulk Incense today :)
More news next week.
Take care
David

title: David's AW News: Homeward bound
content_html:
Greetings from Bali on my last hours here. I'm in the airport in Bali.. Quickly writing this before my flight. 


It's time to head back to the UK. 

Last week I was telling you about our 30th Anniversary of the founding of Ancient Wisdom. I recalled the very first day of trade on a Sheffield street market - 30 years ago. (If you missed it you can catch up here).
The events of that day have kind of fallen into folk law status at AW. How it was a total disaster and almost gave up. But fortunately I didn't and here we are today.
We ran a 30 hour 30% discount starting at 9.30am on Sunday.. across all our websites. And it was astounding it felt like we almost broke the internet.
Thank you everyone for kind words and congratulations. And thank you for your continued trust and trade. 


Then of course the next day all our websites collapsed for real when the worldwide Cloudflare downage hit. We are thanking the gods of the internet that it didn't happen during the 30 hour promo.  That would have been catastrophic. 
Well the wheels keep turning and things move on. Tomas and Raul are in Bali with me and they are working to expand our IT team here. 


I have been helping but mostly working with our man in Indonesia Bondhan, who manages the warehouse and container despatches.. there is an ongoing problem in Bali, the pool of Artisans who make our products -not just ours but for the local market and to countries all over the world - every classy gift shop from Scarborough to Sanfansisco has hand crafted artisan products from Bali.


They call it the "creative industry" . There is a government minister devoted to it and it's a significant export market for Indonesia. When I first came to Bali 12 years ago, they recond of the 4 million population of Bali a million - 25% - were involved in the Creative Industries.  Now of the data I can find they calculate that now it is less than 400,000 less than half. We can feel the effects, our suppliers complain of not enough workers and it takes longer to fulfil orders, prices rising and stock shortage of the most artisanal products.
Anyway I have been doing some investigating, learning the reasons why.. and I'm working on a new YouTube video to explain this. Stand by.


Meanwhile in the UK it's been CRAZY busy.. With no let up.. NEW brilliant stock arriving that I'm so excited to see.. including a whole range of Indian artisan made Incense.. You have to see, smell and experience to understand. A few weeks ago I was at the Delhi trade show and our supplier there had fresh samples from the factory production samples..  They were not on display, because of our bespoke design, but as I'm checking the product range one by one, people are coming on the stand saying wow! That's awesome and we were getting serious interest. 


Lots more new stock including beautiful lamps on driftwood.. 
Hope you are keeping warm in the big chill and trade is good! 
Take care and an update ftom the UK next week.

title: Here be Dragons
content_html:
My friend told me on arrival at our China office that we were off chasing dragons this very night.. "what do you mean?" I said. "First they feed the Dragon with fireworks - so we look for big fireworks and then go."
So on Tuesday night we are chasing around the countryside village to village looking for dragons..
The tradition is like this: a village will put on a firework display to feed the dragon (and attract attention).. the dragon is the whole village carrying interlinking planks each with a lantern propped on top. They troop off along a route lined with well wishers shouting "xinnian hao!" which is like Happy New Year. We found two separate Dragons, one of which was at least a kilometre long. Maybe longer it went on and on.. why so long I asked. Apparently the dragon can control the weather and bring good crops for the year ahead. If you are part of the dragon then you are helping your village to succeed, so everyone wants to be involved. Practical and fun Feng Shui in action!


 
  

At the end of the route a truck load of special bead rolls awaits and an alfresco party takes place as the Dragon unwinds. Above, this being the year of the rabbit young girls sport rabbit ears.
I thought this must be a whole of China experience but I was told no this is special to this area. Just for a few nights around the CNY holiday dragons can really be found.. as they say on those old maps.. Here be Dragons.

Anyway with dragons in mind, soon it will be Mother's Day. Whoops that came out wrong. Actually next week's topic will be Angels - more in keeping with Mother's Day.

title: David's AW News: Secret Factory in Java
content_html:
Greetings from Bali


Hope you are doing well!

Last week, I was telling you about our Java road trip, we went to beautiful Blitar City, and I sprinkled petals in a special place.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
I was also telling you what product comes from Blitar City and why you should be selling this.
From Blitar, we drove three hours to the nearest commercial airport in Surabaya. The route took us through small rural villages on almost dust track roads in real backwater Indonesia, occasionally catching views of Mount Lima. Eventually getting to the new toll road, then arriving in Indonesia's second megacity with modern fly-overs across the city to the beautiful and efficient airport. 
The contrast between rural and big city was dramatic...
Also, please register (if not already) on our YouTube channel to see past adventures and catch the new ones here.

Last week I was also telling you about the marble city we visited on the way to Blitar - we made some content for YouTube there that's really interesting.. Watch your feed!
We have another YouTube just uploaded here about the Big Buddha Statues, where I explain just how we get them to the UK cost effectively. 

I really liked Blitar City, it's a small, neat city with well cared for tree lined streets and nice parks and the most lovely, calm people. And for a small city in the middle of nowhere, I was amazed how everyone could speak relaxed, confident English. There is a well kept secret that not many people know about Blitar. It's not coming up on Google or even AI yet.. but this newsletter, blog and coming YouTube, everyone will know.. You will know first. 

That is.. In Blitar, there are Drum factories supplying the world's Djembe Drums, the kind used by musicians from Africa to India to Europe. 
We visited to factories and discovered absolutely amazing artisan skills to make these drums.
This boss lady showed us around her factory. She told us she has a 1200 a month standing order for this drum to a Chinese company. But also customers in Bali, India and even Africa. 

But then we found a guy two streets away with a huge warehouse, and he told us he made two 40ft container loads a month for China also. And one 40ft to a German company. 
Amazingly made from raw logs of jackfruit wood, sustainable, they told us (with certificates) that they are carved skillfully on a lathe. That wood has to be treated and dried, then later it's painted and carved, a goatskin drum covering is fixed and tuned with a wire and a shoe lace type string, finally, a rubber base is attached. Seems like a lot of work to make a drum and all artisan work.
Here you can see the lathe process, the carving and the tuning and stringing process.
It was actually amazing to watch; the skills were just awesome. We have a YouTube in process.. coming soon.

Bondhan is a musician, and he tested the products and told me they were of good professional quality. So with the lady above, we have an order placed for our own design, a professional standard range of drums. We are buying more gift style and designer ones from the other guy.. meanwhile we have stock online from our current supplier. Djembe Drums here..  

Meanwhile, back in the UK..
Several Indian shipments have arrived, including a spectacular range of Gemstone items - ordered last year. Long time coming, but I think worth it.

Father's Day
Yes, the Big Daddy Day is almost upon us.. at AW, we have more products than most for the big day - Father's Day Gifts Here.

Something New is Coming
Meanwhile - I'm still in Bali at our digital marketing office working hard to bring you a major update to our Drop-shipping Website.
So stand by for an EXCITING UPDATE - coming very soon.  And if you need Fulfilment Services.. We have an updated site already in operation..AW-Fulfilment.co.uk
I can't believe it's June already (almost)..

Wishing you a lovely weekend!!

David

Greetings from Istanbul

Yes, I'm back in Istanbul after only a few weeks. I'll tell you why below.
Last week I was reporting from Spain, where I introduced you to our slightly crazy but brilliant designer Graciela, and we said goodbye to our customer service girl (of almost 15 years) Kerry.
If you missed it you can read about it here.

By the time you read this I will be coming in to land at Kuala Lumpur airport, I'm there for a few days meeting our India agent; Mr Chatterjee & son. Meanwhile Tomas and I have been running around Istanbul uncovering lots of potential suppliers and many more ideas. 

This time we stayed in central Istanbul in a small hotel just off the main shopping street. Opposite the hotel we found a legendary back-packer bar & restaurant with a roof terrace overlooking the Bosphorus Strait on one side and the back of the Russian Embassy on the other. You know the sort of place, flags from all the world, friendly, full of interesting people, amazing food and so so cheap. We nicknamed it base camp and used it for breakfast, working and even had a meeting there with a potential agent for Turkey. It's called the Varuna Gezgin (or Varuna Traveler), and if you are ever in these parts I can highly recommend you come here and rub shoulders with world-travelers, digital nomads, local hipsters, Russian spies and possibly even the odd gift trader.


Today we have meetings with Gemstone traders, cotton towel manufacturers, sock manufacturers.. yes socks. Socks as gifts, we think we have a new slant on gift socks.. There is a whole world of gift opportunities here. We are working on it.

We have always focused on the product and let the products sell themselves, as you know we don't have sales people on the road. So working hard to always find you the next best selling gift lines.. and it seems to work.  The only magic-bullet you need is the right products, and of course footfall, and if your customers don't come through the door then focus online.  We are working hard to bring you pampering products (always good when people need to destress), gemstone products, travel bags.. these things are selling well now.. and you will notice we have shifted focus away from Chinese products to UK made, Indian and Indonesian imports. Lots of new stock is arriving right now and we are busy! If your order is a bit slow in coming, I apologise... the guys in the warehouse are working hard to catch up.
Check out the deals we have for you and the back insock and new lines below.. 

More news next week.. from Kuala Lumpur. I'm on a flight late tonight, Tomas will stay here a few more days to finish some more deals on what we hope will be your best selling products in a month or so.

title: Join the Revolution
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Happy Fathers Day - Weekend.. Best wishes to all the Dads out there. 
Hope you don't get replaced, recycled or refilled.. because I learn that today is World Refill Day.  More below.
It's summer proper, and time to kick back and enjoy the sunshine and that.. with the right approach should be good for business.
Last week I was telling you about all the news from around AW around the world..  if you missed it you can catch up here.

Our man in India, Mr Chatterjee was telling me how unbelievably hot it is in the Kolkata area - but since then it has gone from hot to inferno level HOT. He tells me it's hitting 45c and almost impossible to work even with air conditioning, three of his staff fainted. He is doing his best to look after people.. they are praying for the monsoon rains to come and cool things down. 
In Gujarat coastal area of North India a massive cyclone is hitting.. this is an area many of our gemstone and crystal companies are based. I'll get updates.. 

Last week I asked you for help and feedback - and we got hundreds of feedback responses.. THANK YOU so much.. I have been checking them carefully and learned so much. It seems that some people are busy but many are suffering from a strange drop off in trade.. Comments like "People are more careful with money" or "Sales just dropped off a cliff" - are quite common... But others said the interest in metaphysical or esoteric products has never been higher.. and we can see that crystal products are a boom area.. The feedback link is still open (until the end of the month) here is the link.. FEEDBACK .Your feedback is very valuable (we will give you a shipping voucher for your time) and your feedback helps everyone.. I'll make a full detailed report when it closes.
In the meantime - think about stocking Crystal items (if you don't already) - obviously summer stock can sell now - see below for ideas - and self indulgent  - bath bombs are coming back strongly.. and bath bombs with gemstone bracelets inside hit two hotspots in one product.. 

Let me tell you about some Ancient (personal) History.. 


1980's those were the days!
Many moons ago, a long time before the internet - back in the days when Prince and the Revolution were singing "Purple Rain" and Tina Turner was asking "What's love got to do with it?".. I was just starting out as a very young business person. My first big success was a company that encouraged customers to refill.. it was called "Weigh & Save" - the first shop opened in Harpurhey market in Manchester (I think in 1983). It was the first of its kind.. and a huge success, and with a team of enthusiastic very young people we opened over 100 shops across the UK very rapidly. The idea that you could avoid packaging, buy the amount you actually needed and save money - at a time of severe austerity it just caught on and we grew like crazy. Customers just scooped what they needed from big barrels and at the till we weighed and saved for them.  We sold dried foods like rice, sugar, coffee etc.. Looking back there were fundamental problems, like hygiene and contamination - but in 1985 nobody cared. Do you remember those shops?  Some still exist and lots of people copied the concept. The point is even then I knew that packaging was wasteful and (don't like to brag) but my team and I were truly ahead of the curve. 

Anyway.. moving on.. today is World Refill Day.. now we are much more aware of the devastating impact of global warming, (with awful heat and storms in India happening now) and also folk having to watch the pennies more.. It's time to refocus on reuse and refill. I have been pushing my teams for a long time to get a nice refill station system for you to use.. In Bali a while back I had a refill station display stand designed and made (suitably) from recycled wood from old fishing boats. The pandemic disrupted shipping costs and the cost of shipping them was prohibitive.. we ended up with a warehouse in Bali full of them.. but now we are back to normal.. and we have them arriving in Europe.
At AW-Aromatic.com  where we produce soaps and stuff we are in an ideal position to supply you directly and your customers.. We are calling it the Refill Revolution.. and there is so much more in the pipeline to do with this.. are you joining the revolution? THE REFILL REVOLUTION. join here what better day to join than World Refill Day.. 


Working on the original Refill Station Design.. back in the pandemic days when I was trapped in Bali. We had wanted to use refillable metal canisters - to avoid plastic altogether, but that proved to be impossible, the taps don't really work well and the canisters are too expensive. But anyway we can do it..  Also from Indonesia are refillable Coconut and Teakwood soap dispensers that also make great gifts and look beautiful in your customers' bathrooms. And made specially to fit in the Refill Station stand.
In the 1980's lots of people copied us and "weigh to save", "weigh & pay", "weigh ahead", "natural weigh".. haha so many bad puns got turned into good businesses.. and many survived.. now they are been reinvented as Refill Shops. Not just food, but everything. 
Come and join the revolution..  REFILL REVOLUTION HERE
Next week I will be off travelling again.. we are going to revisit a favorite (very Ancient Wisdom) place.  
Have an absolutely wonderful (Father's Day) weekend. 
Take care.

David

title: David's AW News: From Sheffield with Relish… and Rainsticks
content_html:
Hey.. I hope you guys are doing well!

Greetings from Terminal 2 at Manchester Airport .. Because yes.. I'm on the way again.. It's pretty busy here, I had a job finding somewhere to work. 

Last week I was telling you about my crazy trip.. through Kathmandu, Kolkata to Mumbia and to Sheffield.. If you missed it you can catch up here..


I found Queen Victoria in a Sheffield park… very like the statue in Kolkata where I was only a week ago. Strange really, because Queen Victoria never actually visited India — or (when I checked) Sheffield for that matter. Yet somehow her presence still lingers in both places. It reminded me how connected the world became during that Victorian era… Sheffield steel, Indian trade, railways, industry and empire all somehow woven together. One week I’m passing the Victoria Memorial in Kolkata… the next I’m passing a quiet statue in Endcliffe Park under Yorkshire trees. History has a funny way of following you around.

Well, it’s been an interesting week back at AW HQ in Sheffield. The timing was not ideal with the Bank Holiday in the middle of everything, so I didn’t get nearly enough time with the team… but we made every second count.

I managed to catch up and have lunch with some of the crew over the break, while the Snooker World Championship was in full swing at the legendary Crucible Theatre. Sheffield always has a certain atmosphere during snooker season — the cafés, bars and restaurants buzzing with visitors from all over the world.

I also took the opportunity to wander around a few local gift shops looking for ideas, trends and inspiration. I always enjoy doing that. Sometimes the best ideas don’t come from meetings or spreadsheets… they come from quietly observing what catches people’s attention in the real world.

Meanwhile, back at the warehouse, deliveries were arriving from India and Indonesia, including our latest shipments of Rainsticks and Pangi Seed natural sound products. Holly has just made a new YouTube video all about them — and how retailers can really turn these kinds of products into display magic in-store. If you haven’t seen it yet… You can watch it here. 




And everywhere I went this week — hotels, cafés, restaurants and even street art — I kept seeing the unmistakable Sheffield icon: Henderson’s Relish.


Growing up in Sheffield, “Hendo’s” was simply always there. You didn’t really question it. It sat on café tables, chip shop counters and kitchen shelves like it had always existed. But this week it got me thinking… how does a small regional product become genuinely iconic?

The story actually starts back in 1885, when Henry Henderson first blended the sauce in Sheffield. More than 140 years later, it’s still made in the city to a closely guarded family recipe.

What fascinates me is that Henderson’s never really tried to become a flashy global mega-brand. In many ways, it did the opposite. It stayed proudly local, proudly Sheffield and stubbornly authentic. The packaging barely changed. The recipe stayed secret. The brand became woven into the identity of the city itself.

And somehow… that authenticity became the marketing.

People in Sheffield genuinely feel like it belongs to them. Musicians, artists and local businesses reference it constantly. It became cultural, not just commercial.  

There’s probably a lesson in there for all of us. In a world where so many brands try to look bigger, louder and more “corporate”… sometimes the strongest brands are the ones that stay true to where they came from.

Meanwhile, things have been super busy at AW. So busy in fact that order processing times slipped back a little this week — apologies if you were affected. Thankfully, the team have been pushing hard and, hopefully, by the time you read this, we should largely be caught up again.

Now I’m heading off to Spain for a while to connect with Toni and the team there, check on the house, deal with some administration… and no doubt drink slightly too much coffee while discussing new ideas, new products and new opportunities for the months ahead.

At times like this, travelling between warehouses, suppliers and teams across different countries, I’m reminded how unusual our business really is. One day felt artisans in Nepal… the next rainsticks from Indonesia… then logistics meetings in Sheffield… followed by incense discussions in Málaga.

It’s never boring.

As always, thank you for your continued support, patience and partnership. We genuinely appreciate it — especially during the busy periods when everything seems to happen at once.

Until next Friday…

title: David's AW News: Unveiling New Indian Treasures! ✨
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

There are lots of moving parts at AW right now.. all frantically moving whilst trying to look cool and calm. 
Coco (my wife and your China agent) is here still, keeping an eye on the guys reforming our pool terrace. Whilst practising more and more advanced Yoga moves whilst placing orders with China suppliers, organising candle production (in our factory there) whilst supervising remotely container loading. Whilst knocking up a tasty China food stir fry. I'm always amazed at her energy levels.. and endless skill sets. As I write this she is in the garden re-designing a cactus garden. Alas soon she must go back to China. 
But all of AW is similarly engaged these days.. it's Christmas in full swing.. and Black Friday on the way to boot. Rodrigo in the UK has been going a bit crazy with the offers..  50% off lots of perfectly nice stock. 

Last week I was telling you about Tomas in Bali, not only looking after AW-Advantage.com (our digital marketing company in a beach bar) but doing deals with artisans for new products.. And feeling a bit (ok very) jealous because that's my favorite job.. I also mentioned our terrace revamp after storm damage.. If you missed it you can catch up here. Now Tomas is back in Europe, currently in Slovakia.

Our pool terrace is coming on nicely, but the two week schedule seems unrealistic. Marcelo, father and his son (who speak nada English) are working really hard, but after one week it seems (to me) like there is still a lot to do. 
Ten years ago we brought lots of stone statues from Bali, they are like old friends and we don't want to lose them.. so now they are getting re-deployed and we are designing (and re-designing) the terrace around them.. communication from Coco to them is via google translate.. with occasional help from Toni (our man in Spain), who Whatsapp's them when needed. 


Meanwhile Toni apart from helping us with communications is also dealing with lots of moving parts. Some days I go to the office at AW-Artisan.eu to work from there and connect with one of my favorite teams.. 
This week they had a major Indian container, a China container and a large shipment from AW-Aromatics.com (the UK aromatics factory). Last week I was telling you that the warehouse was basically full, now our hero warehouse manager, a very capable lady called Juani, is actually on the verge of losing it.. She is looking at me as if to say enough is enough.. actually lots going out as well as coming in, but it seems like we need more space than we have.. 
And on top of that Toni is fighting a huge battle with bureaucracy - importing anything these days is increasingly hard work. It feels like a battle, no matter how perfectly you do everything EU regulations are so complex and open to interpretation that customs officials can always find something pedantic to trip you up with. I feel like it is a kind of obsession to prevent imports. We have similar problems in Slovakia..

For example.. We are often accused (without evidence) of under invoicing. That is doing a dodgy thing like putting a fake low price on the import invoice to avoid import tax. We have never done that.. but they make us pay tax on what they think the price should be. So let's think about this.. ok we pay.. next time we import, do we have to put a fake higher price to keep them happy. Of course the money going to China also has to be balanced.. So what do we do with the extra money in China? It's like they are forcing us to be dodgy. They asked Tomas for a letter explaining why we buy cheaper than other importers.. He asked me, do you think they will accept because.. the boss's wife is our China agent and very good at her job? Because she avoids dodgy commissions. Most China agents take a commision from the customer and a secret one from the supplier - thus ultimately increasing the price. 
We are often in trouble for Gemstone Power Bracelets, they often question these. 

And Toni is becoming quite an expert at dealing with customs agents, beyond patience, but when he puts down the phone - I can see the steam coming out of his ears..
Sorry for the rant.. must focus on positive energy..

So it's AW's birthday next week.. on the 16th November we will be 28 years old. It all started at an outdoor market stall in Sheffield town centre. Yes - I suppose I'm still a market trader deep down. I was raised in Sheffield markets, the old Castle and Seaf Markets. The family business was a bakery and shops. Even as a teenager I loved the hustle and bustle of the market. The art of making "a flash" - what we called an eye catching display and creating some excitement. There is a page.. called The History of Ancient Wisdom.. It starts by describing the first day of trading..  
"It was a wet cold Thursday morning a long time before Google and Facebook, and as I laid out my market stall on a Sheffield street I was more than apprehensive about what people would think. But I was ready by eight, my humble offering laid out on that simple stall.. and stomping from foot to foot I awaited my first customer."
Haha I remember it like it was yesterday.. a lot has happened since then.. check it out if you have time.. 
Stand by for more exciting news on our Birthday. 

I just discovered that the Indian container has also just arrived in UK.. with the same stock items as we have here in Spain. I was particularly impressed with the wooden Ritual Bowls  Lots of other items also... These all came out of Epic Indian/Nepal Trip last February (regular readers will remember).. and I think almost the last stock to arrive from that trip. It's a circle of life.. that right now I'm planning the 2024 Epic Trip... as usual trying to think outside of the box.. and speaking boxes.. lovely Indian ones just arrived.. 

Hope you are doing good business and all is well.
Let's hope for a peaceful weekend.

David
