She is looking at me as if to say enough is enough.. actually lots going out as well as coming in, but it seems like we need more space than we have.. And on top of that Toni is fighting a huge battle with bureaucracy - importing anything these days is increasingly hard work. It feels like a battle, no matter how perfectly you do everything EU regulations are so complex and open to interpretation that customs officials can always find something pedantic to trip you up with. I feel like it is a kind of obsession to prevent imports. We have similar problems in Slovakia.. For example.. We are often accused (without evidence) of under invoicing. That is doing a dodgy thing like putting a fake low price on the import invoice to avoid import tax. We have never done that.. but they make us pay tax on what they think the price should be. So let's think about this.. ok we pay.. next time we import, do we have to put a fake higher price to keep them happy. Of course the money going to China also has to be balanced.. So what do we do with the extra money in China? It's like they are forcing us to be dodgy. They asked Tomas for a letter explaining why we buy cheaper than other importers.. He asked me, do you think they will accept because.. the boss's wife is our China agent and very good at her job? Because she avoids dodgy commissions. Most China agents take a commision from the customer and a secret one from the supplier - thus ultimately increasing the price. We are often in trouble for Gemstone Power Bracelets , they often question these. And Toni is becoming quite an expert at dealing with customs agents, beyond patience, but when he puts down the phone - I can see the steam coming out of his ears.. Sorry for the rant.. must focus on positive energy.. So it's AW's birthday next week. . on the 16th November we will be 28 years old . It all started at an outdoor market stall in Sheffield town centre. Yes - I suppose I'm still a market trader deep down. I was raised in Sheffield markets, the old Castle and Seaf Markets. The family business was a bakery and shops. Even as a teenager I loved the hustle and bustle of the market. The art of making "a flash" - what we called an eye catching display and creating some excitement. There is a page.. called The History of Ancient Wisdom .. It starts by describing the first day of trading.. "It was a wet cold Thursday morning a long time before Google and Facebook, and as I laid out my market stall on a Sheffield street I was more than apprehensive about what people would think. But I was ready by eight, my humble offering laid out on that simple stall.. and stomping from foot to foot I awaited my first customer." Haha I remember it like it was yesterday.. a lot has happened since then.. check it out if you have time.. Stand by for more exciting news on our Birthday. I just discovered that the Indian container has also just arrived in UK.. with the same stock items as we have here in Spain. I was particularly impressed with the wooden Ritual Bowl s Lots of other items also... These all came out of Epic Indian/Nepal Trip last February (regular readers will remember).. and I think almost the last stock to arrive from that trip. It's a circle of life.. that right now I'm planning the 2024 Epic Trip... as usual trying to think outside of the box.. and speaking boxes.. lovely Indian ones just arrived.. Hope you are doing good business and all is well. Let's hope for a peaceful weekend. David

title: David's AW News: The BBC called me in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia

August Bank holiday is behind us.. and it's almost September..

Soon I will be moving on.. but it's been nice to be back in Bali even if just for a short time. 

Last week I was telling you about Indonesia's 80th Independence Day.. and the very special way they celebrate this here. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Quite big news.. I took a phone call from an unidentified UK number last week, around midnight Bali time. I thought it was the usual scam call... But it was a journalist from the BBC. They had seen our endless rant about Temu and Shein undermining British Retailers. Finally getting attention.. I chatted with the friendly guy and gave our point of view. Later, he contacted Katka in the UK, and a week later, this article came out...You can read it here... I'm really hoping that Keith Starmer will finally take action and take this massive loophole down.


A Cool Wave.

This week it has been strangely cool in Bali.. while UK, Spain and even China bask in heatwaves.. here has been a relatively cool wave. Well, cool as in 24c - but that's enough for the locals to be donning jackets and scarves. I was amused to see people wrapping up this morning on my way to the office. 

It reminds me summer is soon over.. and the next big thing is Halloween.. It's coming guys.. time to get spooky - time to get prepared.. 

Holly and Alex have been preparing the showroom in Sheffield.. and having fun doing it, I think. You can watch the video here.


Lots happening this week..

Bali is a volcanic island.. Mount Agung always looms somewhere in the distance. It's considered to be the navel of the earth by locals, shrouded in magic and mystery.

Inspired by the volcano and the spirit therein, we bring you: The Essence of the Volcano Necklace Collection


Made with volcanic stones and symbolic decor - in gift boxes with texts explaining the story behind each piece.

The packaging was designed (in colab with the jewellery designer) by our man Bondhan. 

Bondhan is an accomplished musician - he plays in a next-level Heavy Rock band called - Kanibal



a little bit loud for my liking.. haha but that hard rock trash style is big in Indonesia. 

He can also play a mean Ukulele - and is the designer behind our range of artisan Ukuleles made in a music mad village in central Java.

The other day in our small office/showroom at our Bali warehouse.. I was telling him that we had some feedback from a customer who said it was hard to tune.. and I agree I was struggling to tune myself.. Bondhan explained that because they are artisan-made by hand, as you tune each string the tensions change inside the instrument.. you need to tune each string, then start again and re-tune.. when it comes good, you are rewarded with a lovely sounding.. and really easy to play instrument. 

We made a YouTube video to celebrate... where I interview Bondhan and explain the interesting details and exactly how to tune.


We also ask: Can you sell this?.. Find it in our Can You Sell This? Playlist.

Check the Can You Sell This Playlist if you are looking for ideas of new products to sell.. here you can scroll through a selection of popular products and get all the info you need to market to your customers effectively.. also get to know the people of Ancient Wisdom. 

New stock arriving in the UK.

Lots of lovely new stock!!  - See below for details..

Spain has a space crisis.. 

Regular readers will know we have been struggling for space in our Spain warehouse for a while, we even have second-hand containers in the car park.. that helped a bit.. then we found a local fulfilment warehouse where we could store a few hundred pallets.. but not ideal because every day you are shipping stuff there and bringing stuff back, you need. Very inefficient. 

It all came to a crisis the other week, when the fulfilment company told us they were closing down and gave us a month's notice to take back our 500 pallets.. (and we cannot find a replacement) on top of that, we have like 6 container loads of stock arriving.  Toni (our man in Spain) is in a flat panic.. Tomas went there to find a solution.  

Well, it seems we have to bite the bullet and move to the next level.. 

But there are not many large clean warehouses in Malaga.. We found this warehouse this week, close by.. and got excited.


Big & Beautiful.. 

Other warehouses are big and crumbling.. or damp and poky. Modern builds are a rare beast. So we expressed an interest in this, only to find another tenant had just signed on the dotted line the day before. All week, Tomas and Toni have been visiting various options.. none very good.. my WhatsApp is full of video guided tours. But we have to do something quickly!

I'll update you next week.

 Meanwhile, Halloween is creeping up behind you...

Time to get stocked up!!

 Next week in a new location..

 Take care

David

title: Not many people know this..
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Already here one hectic week.. it's all go. Raul followed me here from Kuala Lumpur a few days after me.. Tomas is already here.. so the team is together.
Last week I had just arrived from Asia and I was telling (in a jet-lagged state) about all the lovely people in my life.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Now I'm over my jet-lag and have been working at the Artisan offices in Malaga.  As usual it's almost always party time ... we had one office birthday party already.


It was the birthday of Carmen, the young lady on the right.. she brought a big cake and made a speech about how much she loves working at AW-Artisan. And next week we have a staff beach party organised.. The weather is unnaturally hot for the time of year.  27c yesterday.. so it still feels like summer - so beach party it is.

New department in the pipeline.
I was also telling you last week how Coco has become Yoga obsessed and posting all her moves to Chinese TicToc.. well she has been shopping and upgrading her kit.. new mats and stuff. So this week we decided to develop a Yoga range of eco-friendly Yoga products.. We already sell a lot of singing bowls and healing gongs to Yoga studios. In Ubud, home of the legendary Yoga Barn - there are lots of Yoga obsessed shops.. so we (Coco and I) were already checking out the type of things that might sell well.. It's really time we make an AW Yoga supplies section. So our awesome designer in Spain Graciela is already on the job..
We can find supplies in Indonesia, India and China.. and Coco is our chief tester. 
This clearly a big growth market, and a natural fit for AW.. many of you (our customers) will already relate to this.. so any feedback, ideas and suggestions are really appreciated. 

I'll tell you something that not many people know..
I had a huge problem.. my passport is almost full.. I'm not sure what happens if you turn up at passport control and there is no space left to plonk a stamp.. but I'm pretty sure in some countries that is not a good thing to do. Everytime I pass a passport control I ask nicely if they can avoid stamping on my one empty page.. the guy in Malaysia was great. He said he understood perfectly and searched until he found a gap big enough for his stamp on an old page.. 
Another time on entering Slovakia after a trip to Turkey, a swaggering passport guy - inspected my Spanish ID card and informed me that I still had to be stamped into the EU (not actually true) and smashed his dirty big stamp with an evil smirk on my precious second to last empty page. 

 Last time I was in the UK they told me that new passport applications could take 10 weeks, and I was travelling in 2 weeks.. and no-one was helpful on those help lines.  Then I remembered someone telling me years ago it was possible under certain circumstances to hold two UK passports.. I came across an agency in London that claimed to be able to help, they could get appointments and with a photocopy of my current passport apply on my behalf (plus lots of other stuff) for a second passport. (If you are interested, message me - I can pass you the details).  I really wasn't 100% sure if it was legitimate and the agency fee' are not cheap - but I was getting desperate.  I seemed to meet all the criteria, ie travelling at the time of application, being a businessperson who needed to travel and apply for visa's at the same time.. 
Well to cut a long story short.. After lots of work and a great deal of coordination from Katka in the UK.. and Ringo in Bali helping me find the right type of photocopy and the right type of passport photo paper.. 
Yesterday my passport was delivered to my UK address (my Mum's house) - so now I am the proud owner of two UK passports. 

With lots and lots of lovely empty pages :)

Agnes & Cat open days at AW
Following the huge success of the AW showroom open days last week.. we are doing the same for our premium Agnes & Cat brand.. 
If you would like to join us - feel free to pop along.. see details below.

If I survive the parties.. This time next week I will be in the UK. So updates from there.
Have a great weekend.

David

title: One year on. Indonesia Report.
content_html:
22nd February 2013

Hi ,
Greetings from Bali, where it is the monsoon. Which is great because it's low season, the hotels are cheap and between downpours it's cool enough to work.
Last week's news was from India, and I was telling you about our Soft Art Cushion Covers and Having a Blast in Bangalore. Read it here.
The beaches I have hardly seen, but I can tell you even in the rain Bali is the most beautiful place on earth. Those volcano and rice padi vistas all those exotic temples, trailing vines, moss encrusted bridges and so many stone statues.
In the hinterland of Bali outside the main tourist zone a huge handicraft industry growing rapidly and collaborations between the islands artisans and western designers are producing a wealth of gift ideas. It's just over a year since I was first here, in fact this is my sixth visit, and like a lotus flower slowly opening I'm discovering more beautiful things each time. Also slowly and gradually coming to know the secrets of doing successful business in Indonesia... believe me it is very different thinking to India or China.. like a whole new world.
So this year between Java (the main Indonesian island) and Bali, we are about to ship our seventh container, have started trading relations with over 30 companies (all small family businesses) and have listed over 600 products. The plan now is to establish our own permanent office and warehouse similar to our set up in Yiwu, China. I'm here this time with Eric our QC and re-order guy from the UK office and Carlos from our Spanish sister company to look into this.
Interesting fact. Bali planning laws dictate that no building should be higher than a palm tree (only a few hotels built in the sixties are high-rise). Balinese Hindu culture is all about balance, so our agent Ringo tells me. Balance between, humans and God, between fellow humans and between humans and the earth. Hence the palm tree planning laws.
More news next week. Off to Java shortly.
Take care.. and happy trading.
David

categories: Snake Wine | Mandrake | ancient wisdom | aromatherapy | China
content_html:
Meanwhile in a far off province I found a market dealing in herbs and remedies.. The coastal region of China is very developed in every sense and also up to speed when it comes to eco-matters or ethical trading.. very much like the west. But head inside to the real China and such concerns hardly seem to matter. I found one little shop proudly selling African elephant and lion bone products, with pictures of the owner doing ivory deals in the dark heart of Africa. In this market.. I found musk dear anklers been chopped and crushed, pickled snakes of all types (you drink the vinager), and whole variety of dried animal private parts for heaven knows what purpose. Mandrake, half animal half plant is common, but also many strange unnamed plants and strange sea creatures. I couldn't help thinking how many endangered species and how much exploitation was involved...


   

But in the same market I found traders dealing in floral rememedies and aromatherapy products... just like Ancient Wisdom.

title: David's AW News: Christmas Seriously!!
content_html:
Greetings from Ancient Wisdom HQ in Sheffield.


Yes I'm back from Spain in the UK.. My schedule this time of year is a little crazy, but it's Christmas and it is what it is. 
Last week in Spain it was mission accomplished, I went with Toni to view potential new warehouses and was able to do a deal on a new place not too far from our existing warehouse. Huge offices and a much larger warehouse already racked out, so we can move quickly.. we will actually start moving over Christmas. So exciting times at AW-Artisan.eu in Spain.

We had the Spain Christmas party on the private terrace of a central Malaga hotel. Very posh, everyone dressed smartly looking amazing. From the terrace we could see the ancient cathedral in the old town light up with a festive laser show and a massive street party below as people come to see the famous Christmas lights. After a formal meal around one large table, I gave my traditional speech (translated by Toni), thanking everyone for their hard work this year, jokingly telling them they are my favorite team (our in joke) and wishing them a happy Christmas etc etc.. Lots of laughter and big Cheers.


So serious, then.. 



 Then Toni, and all his management team had speeches prepared.. OMG.. so serious - it was more like a management meeting or staff review.. Spanish people are supposed to work hard and play hard.. But I guess that is how it is.. then when formal dinner was over.. they wanted to take me to a bar in the Old Town - it's already midnight I protested.. Well then we had a serious party. I made it back to my hotel room (I'd booked just in case) at 4am.. seriously I'm too old for this.

Well that was last Friday night. On Thursday early morning I headed to Malaga airport and caught an EasyJet flight to Manchester, James picked me up and once more back over the Pennines to Sheffield. So once again at AW HQ.. It's crazy busy here still and the team is starting to look exhausted.. Katka told me it's been hard work.. but finally the end is in sight. Another week of madness.  
This year has been seriously busy.. and Dropshipping is smashing all records. 

Dropshipping Update.
We have some super customers who have really cracked the dropshipping game and are shipping thousands of orders. Well done guys (you know who you are!!)  - Well I think the online retailing world is in a state of flux, the big Chinese offshore companies - (those dastardly loophole traders) are getting their wings clipped across Europe. The main platform: Shopify is on a roll with innovations coming thick and fast. More and more traders are mastering the API that connects AW products to their stores for more automation. This is the time of the Independent  trader online. 2026 - I see huge growth and massive opportunities.
We were expecting two containers this week.. one from China with exclusive dropshipping products. Only available for you online. Unfortunately both containers have been delayed, but by the new year we have so much in store for you.

Meanwhile in the UK.. 


Its Tea Time!!

Yes it really is.. this has been a project that Toni (our man in Spain) has been working on for more that a year! With help from Sandra on designer.. beautiful labels, specially made brass Tea tins from India (land of tea) and a fresh and exciting range of herbal teas - mixed and blended in Spain - the ancient melting pot of tea culture. 

Basically Andalusia is a natural melting pot for herbal teas.  Andalusia became a centre for herbal and mixed teas because it combined a perfect herb-growing climate with Roman science, Islamic botanical mastery, and global trade—creating a continuous culture of herbal blending that survived long after empires fell. Seriously herbal tea! 

So here it is.. seriously steeped in the Ancient Wisdom of Tea Heritage..
Introducing our latest labour of love.. 

- Mandala Leaves - Herbal Tea.


Meanwhile.. 
Hope you are busy and enjoying the Christmas season. Not long now. 

Tomorrow night is the UK AW Christmas party.. 

Full update next week. 
Have great weekend 

David

Huge offices and a much larger warehouse already racked out, so we can move quickly.. we will actually start moving over Christmas. So exciting times at AW-Artisan.eu in Spain. We had the Spain Christmas party on the private terrace of a central Malaga hotel. Very posh, everyone dressed smartly looking amazing. From the terrace we could see the ancient cathedral in the old town light up with a festive laser show and a massive street party below as people come to see the famous Christmas lights. After a formal meal around one large table, I gave my traditional speech (translated by Toni), thanking everyone for their hard work this year, jokingly telling them they are my favorite team (our in joke) and wishing them a happy Christmas etc etc.. Lots of laughter and big Cheers. So serious, then.. Then Toni, and all his management team had speeches prepared.. OMG.. so serious - it was more like a management meeting or staff review. . Spanish people are supposed to work hard and play hard.. But I guess that is how it is.. then when formal dinner was over.. they wanted to take me to a bar in the Old Town - it's already midnight I protested.. Well then we had a serious party . I made it back to my hotel room (I'd booked just in case) at 4am.. seriously I'm too old for this. Well that was last Friday night. On Thursday early morning I headed to Malaga airport and caught an EasyJet flight to Manchester, James picked me up and once more back over the Pennines to Sheffield. So once again at AW HQ.. It's crazy busy here still and the team is starting to look exhausted.. Katka told me it's been hard work.. but finally the end is in sight. Another week of madness. This year has been seriously busy.. and Dropshipping is smashing all records . Dropshipping Update. We have some super customers who have really cracked the dropshipping game and are shipping thousands of orders. Well done guys (you know who you are!!) - Well I think the online retailing world is in a state of flux, the big Chinese offshore companies - (those dastardly loophole traders) are getting their wings clipped across Europe. The main platform: Shopify is on a roll with innovations coming thick and fast. More and more traders are mastering the API that connects AW products to their stores for more automation. This is the time of the Independent trader online. 2026 - I see huge growth and massive opportunities. We were expecting two containers this week.. one from China with exclusive dropshipping products . Only available for you online. Unfortunately both containers have been delayed, but by the new year we have so much in store for you. Meanwhile in the UK.. Its Tea Time!! Yes it really is.. this has been a project that Toni (our man in Spain) has been working on for more that a year! With help from Sandra on designer.. beautiful labels, specially made brass Tea tins from India (land of tea) and a fresh and exciting range of herbal teas - mixed and blended in Spain - the ancient melting pot of tea culture. Basically Andalusia is a natural melting pot for herbal teas. Andalusia became a centre for herbal and mixed teas because it combined a perfect herb-growing climate with Roman science, Islamic botanical mastery, and global trade—creating a continuous culture of herbal blending that survived long after empires fell. Seriously herbal tea! So here it is.. seriously steeped in the Ancient Wisdom of Tea Heritage.. Introducing our latest labour of love.. - Mandala Leaves - Herbal Tea. Meanwhile.. Hope you are busy and enjoying the Christmas season. Not long now. Tomorrow night is the UK AW Christmas party.. Full update next week. Have great weekend David

title: David's AW News: Cotton Wool to TikTok
content_html:
Only problem was… I seemed to have brought something back with me besides supplier samples. A very painful ear. Agony it was literally bringing water to my eyes.Hello Rodrigo,

Hey.. I hope you guys are doing well!

Greetings from Spain…

Last week I was writing to you from T2 Manchester Airport on the way back here… talking about Queen Victoria, Henderson’s Relish and a whirlwind week in Sheffield. If you missed it you can catch up here…

Well… I made it home at last.


It’s actually been almost three months since I properly stayed in my house here in Spain, and I have to say… it’s good to be back. The jasmine is starting to bloom, the mornings are warm again, and after airports, factories, warehouses, trade shows and far too many hotel breakfasts… even making coffee in your own kitchen feels like luxury. 


Only problem was… I seemed to have brought something back with me besides supplier samples. A very painful ear. Agony it was literally bringing water to my eyes.

I went to our local clinic here expecting antibiotic drops, but the doctor took one look and smiled.

“No infection,” she said. Apparently all the flying had pushed wax deep into the inner ear.

Well… What followed was slightly traumatic.

First: ear drops every hour for five hours to soften everything up. Then back to the clinic for peroxide bubbling away in my ear (ouch).

Then some sort of hot water pressure pump and suction machine contraption that honestly looked like something from a 1970s science-fiction film.

But in the end… after an hour of pumping and prodding, and getting soaked in hot water.. 

Relief.

The pressure vanished, the pain disappeared… and suddenly I could hear like never before.

So next time you’re on a tiny aircraft crossing the Himalayas and the stewardess offers you cotton wool for your ears.


Take my advice. Use it.

Anyway… once partially reconstructed, I went to visit Toni and the team at the new Spanish warehouse.

The showroom is really starting to come together now, the warehouse is organised, systems are improving… though still plenty to do of course. Best moment of the day, however, belonged to Graciela—Toni’s right-hand girl.



As part of her wage review we arranged a lease car for her… and the very day I visited it arrived brand new at the warehouse.

You know that unmistakable “new car smell”? She was pleased as punch.

And honestly… moments like that are one of the nicest parts of building a business.

Meanwhile…

Some very big news for our Dropshipping customers.

After what felt like forever… the TikTok API integration finally received approval and we launched it last week.

And…It’s gone crazy.

Orders are flying in, the team are adding more pickers and packers, and we’re working hard to catch up and keep everything flowing smoothly.

But this is still only the beginning.

The volumes already look exciting… yet I genuinely think we are only scratching the surface of the potential here.

I think of it like this…

With a traditional retail shop, your potential customers are limited to:
• the people who walk past your door
• the percentage who come inside
• and the percentage of those who buy from the stock you physically have on display

But with AW Dropshipping…

You suddenly have access to over 7,500 products (plus endless bundle combinations)… and potentially 60 million customers in the UK.

And in Europe? Closer to 450 million.

That changes the game completely.

If you haven’t explored it yet… this is becoming a very exciting time to dive in.

 
Holly has just made a new YouTube video related to the Wedding Season, in this video, Holly explores the Ancient Wisdom Wedding Collection - a versatile range of wedding favours.



Meanwhile, lots of stock is arriving in the warehouse, including a container from China the other day.. LOT back in stock.

We are only weeks away from Father's Day. The time to plan is NOW.. and Wedding Season is in full swing.

Anyway… there’s still far too much to do, too many ideas on the table, and apparently I’m now under medical instructions to “rest my ears” — which feels wildly unrealistic in this business.

Have a wonderful weekend wherever you are in the world.

And if someone on a Himalayan flight offers you cotton wool…

Don’t try to act tough.

title: It's Bigger Than Christmas - SOL
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Hope you are enjoying life in the 2020's. It's a new age for sure.
Last week I was telling you about "Dreams coming true" in Spain and how to make big plans that happen, you can read about it here.

I'm in Spain for several reasons, one of which is helping to get our new Spain company up to speed.. AW Artisan in Malaga. It's so much fun starting new ventures.
SOL - what is it? It's big in the gift trade..

They have those TV programmes about Brits starting businesses in Spain, I often think life at AW would make great TV drama. One time I was in a local restaurant with Raul (our IT guy) and we found ourselves in a TV programme, we were actually the first customers of a new British owned fish restaurant.. if you search hard enough.. we are still there on Channel 4 - A New Life in the Sun.  
I sometimes think that life at AW would make a great drama..
The new team at AW Artisan are bedding in well, and two of the customer service team will shortly go to the UK for intensive training.
Meanwhile our man in Spain - Toni is fast getting to grips with the products at AW and understanding the system whilst making friends with all the AW customers.
We finally got the new signage for the warehouse.. 



Meanwhile in the UK, new stock for Spring and what we like to call the "Season of Love" is arriving in swathes.. 
I'm so excited to see the new gemstone jewellery - especially the Gemstone Friendship Bracelets.  Gemstone bracelets are seriously back in fashion, and since we (re) introduced the Power Bracelets a year or so ago the sales have grown and grown until they are our best selling jewellery range. These new Friendship Bracelets designed by Tomas (with some input from me - OK, mostly Tomas) - if you follow this newsletter you will know how much blood sweat and tears we put into developing this range. Perfect for friendships of all types not just sweethearts.. but perfect in your store ready for the "Season of Love".
Also we have a new range of Soap flowers in natural baskets - perfect for wedding gifts. (see below).

The Season of Love.. it's bigger than Christmas.

We call it the SOL - the Season of Love..
It officially kicks off with Valentines Day on the 14th February - which is a Friday, so the main shopping will be the weekend of the 8th - less than 4 weeks to go.
Then Mother's Day on 22nd March (only 10 weeks)  
Then in April is Easter and all things Chocolate and fluffy bunny's (yellow candles and home fragrance).
Then Mother's Day again in Spain on 3rd May
Then it's the full blown Wedding Season - right through the summer.. wedding favours.. etc.
Which brings us to International Friendship Day on July 30th. (Did I mention the new Friendship Bracelets?) This is huge in India and Southeast Asia.. and growing more and more in UK and the EU.

So get ready for the SOL.. it's absolutely what the world needs more of.
And at AW - (we don't like to toot our own trumpet) but you can't find a better place for those fast moving gift items - AW is your go-to-wholesaler for SOL goodies.
Check our deals below.

Spread the love. 
Have a great weekend.

David

title: Edge of History
content_html:
Greetings from the edge of history.

We are in Istanbul, Turkey. Tomas, Raul and I took the trip pretty much on impulse because we heard about a huge textile trade show happening at the expo centre there. And since exchange rates are spectacular we thought maybe some bargains could be found for our customer... So on Wednesday we took Pegasus air from Manchester (not recommended) to Istanbul and a taxi to our hotel.
First impressions.. this is a massive city, modern and huge. It feels a little bit like a Chinese city. The next striking thing was the amount of flags, huge building sized flags draped everywear. The National flag of Turkey is everywhere, even over Mcdonalds. Was it National day? I started to google why so many flags?..


I have been to Istanbul before, it was maybe 20 years ago and boy has it changed. If you thought London was the biggest city in Europe (10m) then behold majestic Istanbul it has grown up to be a mega city of Twenty million. 
Of course the pedantic person might argue that this city is not quite in Europe, strangling the Bosphorus which divides Europe from Asia. It also sits in the midst of geopolitical earthquakes, as the Bosphorus is the only sea link into the Black Sea across which is Ukraine. Turkey is almost bankrupt, with a currency crisis, zero reserves and it is up to its neck in the Ukrainian conflict, trying as a Nato member to contain difficult neighbours. 


Historic time to be here. I thought we might find a city in despair.. but this place despite (or maybe because) of everything going on is alive and busy. 

Yesterday we went to the exobition centre, it's big, well organised and massively busy. I don't think I have seen a tradeshow with so many visitors, quite extraordinary. It was actually quite hard to get the attention of a salesperson. They are clearly doing epic business deals. In the evening we switched to tourist mode and went to the famous Grand Bizarre, which is a huge indoor market in the old town area. It's a spectacular place and not at all stressful,  not the aggressive traders I seem to remember. But friendly innovative retailers wheeling and dealing as they do but not out to con you.

Dates are important. May 19, 1919  was the start of the war of independence for Turkey. So the 19th of May is now Atatürk  Day and Youth and Sports Day, an annual Turkish national holiday and major flag waving day. 
Kamâl Atatürk you will know was the founder of modern Turkey and is much revered in these parts, his picture is also made into flags and banners.


Here is a Kamâl Atatürk banner in the heart of the Grand Bizarre. 
I love old markets, we also visited the old Spice Market and the backstreet wholesale markets around the old town.
 

We were particularly impressed by the tea shops selling colourful special blends of tea. Lots of inspiration for extending our top selling tea blends.
Later we made it to a restaurant on a bridge close to the port to watch the sunset and take in the hussle and bussle of downtown Istanbul. Lots of Russians here because there are few other places to holiday for them. We heard Americans and Chinese voices, and who knows what is going on. Turkey won't allow wareships through its waters, not Russian anyone else..  A feeling of a city in the midst of history. Lots of wheeling and dealing going on.
I'm writing this early in the morning.. Now it's time for breakfast and another day in the city on the edge..


Take care. After here we go to Slovakia, where our epic move to a much bigger warehouse is almost complete.
More news next week.

David

title: Is this the strangest village in Bali?
content_html:
Greetings from the rice fields of Ubud.

The only actual tourists in Bali are Russians, today (I feel) keeping a low profile.

Last week I was telling you about our big problem in Bali, if you missed it you can read it here. 

Tomas is in our Slovakian distribution centre.. we are moving warehouse and he tells me they can feel the tension in the air - Ukraine is a next door country. There are plenty of Ukrainians in the area anyway, now many more crossing the border into Slovakia. We can only hope and pray this thing works out with the minimum of bloodshed. 

The way I see it playing out economically is in tit-for-tat sanctions that will impact the whole world. For example if Russia cuts the gas supply (after we cut access to the banking system) then power prices will spiral upward driving already excessive inflation.

How this affects the gift trade is anybody's guess, but I do know.. when times are tough then affordable gifts are an essential comfort. 
If hyper-inflation sweeps the world like a financial pandemic.. then who knows how this will unwind, I'm still trying to get my mind around that.

Meanwhile as the deadly drama unfolds in Eastern Europe, I'm buzzing around the villages of Bali doing deals and developing projects and products. It's giftware heaven..

There are many beautiful exotic and strange places on Bali. The other day we went to a village famous for carving "hand shaped things". We had this idea to get the molten glass bowls poured over a lifesize carved wooden hand. And Ringo said "I know the place to find that" so off we went.. the village is known locally as "Kampon Burung" or Bird Village. Its only a small place, you enter through an arch and a few hundred meters exit through another arch. There is a temple in the middle, a couple of rice terraces and lots of small workshops with folk all busy carving hands. 

A hand carving village is strange enough, but here lives a small heron-like bird called the Kokokan Bird.
Thousands of them perched in trees on power lines, posing in the rice terrace. A bit like a tropical version of that old Alfred Hitchcock film "The Birds". They are everywhere, they are considered sacred by the villagers and treated like holy guests. But here's the really weird thing.. all the bird's nests live only in the village, pass beyond the arch and not a single bird is to be seen. 



But it gets stranger than this.. I did a bit of research and discovered something amazing..
Up until 1965 the villages used to eat the birds that came to the village, they were considered a delicacy. Then one night the village had a collective nightmare, everyone dreamed of a big monster visiting them and warning them that the birds were sacred.  The shocked locals consulted the local priest who performed a ritual of apology in the village temple. He then fell into a trance and told the village that the Kokokan bird is actually the guardian of the village

After that the villagers made a monument in the temple and as an offering cared for the birds rather than eating them. From that day they say.. village became prosperous and peaceful.
Certainly the locals were really friendly and happy, even singing as they worked. Everyone seemed busy, Ringo asked one guy if they had plenty of business.. his answer was no, not much business but they keep making for stock one day they will sell everything they made.  And here are the locals and the hands..


So many more adventures in Bali I could tell you about.. every day is a new experience. And we have a long list of projects underway. 
Next week will be very exciting.. it's Bali new year known as Nyepi where huge evil statues (know as Ogoh Ogoh) parade through the street into the night. This is followed by a day of utter silence strictly policed by an army of polite but firm temple guards known as Pecalang - even the airport is closed for this, no music, no talking, no going outside. The Pecalang of Ubud is famously the strictest in all Bali. Hope I don't get in trouble..
Plus very excited to be invited to the wedding of Ringo's niece in his remote hometown village in Bangli regency. It's rare for outsiders to get an invite, so a great honor.. and I will have to wear Balinese traditional clothes. It's next Friday so hopefully, I can report.

Next week a full update.

Take care.

David

title: The secrets of the clove forest
content_html:
Greetings from Singaraja, North Bali

In Ringo's new car we made a road trip to the north of Bali mostly to visit an essential oil guy, but also to check out the handicraft companies of this area.

We first met Pak Yogi at a wedding in Ringo's hometown - his Niece was marrying Ringo's Nephew. So now we are family he is happy to introduce us to all the craft folk he knows.
Singaraja is the second city of Bali. The forgotten city, it was, until 1974 the capital city, squashed between the sea and steep banks of mountains behind it was difficult to build an airport. So eventually the capital was moved to Denpasar (which translates as the Southern Market). Singaraja translates as Lion Kingdom.. and is famous for the wild freedom fighters who, like lions, lived in the jungles and forests above the city and fought for independence from the colonial Dutch in the 1940's.. 

We took an unusual root across the island in order to call and see a supplier on the way, this took us over one of the highest bridges in Indonesia  (we stopped to walk across it).  And then up high over the mountain range that hangs over the North coast. It turns quite cool at the top, but warms up fast as you drop down the steep windy roads through the clove forests. Ringo tells me that in the clove forests are some of the oldest villages in Bali where aboriginal people still live - the original inhabitants of Bali. I have heard that in this area farmers distil clove oil directly. We ask in a few village shops if they know about any distillery - eventually one old lady tells us her daughter collects fallen leaves and twigs and takes them to a place in a forest clearing. After asking several people and turning down small tracks we find the place. We can smell the scent of cloves heavy in the air and then see a set of large tanks filled with steaming murky liquid. Three guys are working there running a rustic but effective clove oil distillery.. they are happy to show us around, the manager is actually from Java and Bondhan can speak his local language. 
The clove leaf sodden tanks are heated underneath by a fire fed by more dried clove leaves. As the water evaporates a concentrated fluid is pipped off and drained through a series of tubs. I can't say I real understand the process but somehow they end up with buckets of sticky clove oil. This is shipped back to Java for refining before - we understood - being sold to the cigarette factories for use in clove cigarettes.


I'm not sure we can buy oil directly from here.. but it was quite amazing to find this place. Bondan has the WhatsApp of the manager, so we will see what happens, I'm hoping we can make connections with the Java boss.
After arriving in Singaraja we went to visit Pak Yogi. In Indonesia everyone uses herbal or ayurvedic oils.. Ringo keeps a roll-on in his car. Insect bites.. no problem.. sprains, backache, burns.. I have just the thing.. headache a little of this will help. There are about four main brands sold all over Indonesia, the best known is Kutus-Kutus - which means 88 in Balinese language. Pak Yogi told us the story of Kutus-Kutus.. It was a Dutch guy who was running a restaurant in Jakarta in the 1980's - he went bankrupt in the financial crash, started again.. failed again. Decided to try his hand on Bali and opened a restaurant in Kuta at the wrong time.. just before the Bali bombing and failed again.
Walking on the beach at Sanur contemplating how bad life was he slipped and sprained his ankle.. a local pulled out his herbal oil and massaged the sprain.. surprised at how quickly he felt better.. and also how the aromatics helped his negativity to fade away he started to investigate the local oils.. another Balinese friend suggested the name and Kutus-Kutus was born. 
Maybe there is a bit of poetic license in Pak Yogi's story.. but it is inspiring.. now Kutus-Kutus is a huge company one of the wealthiest in Bal owning hotels and property everywhere.

But maybe Pak Yogi's story is more interesting... his grandfather was one of the lions - the freedom fighters living in hiding in the jungle. He developed a special herbal compound used to treat injured fighters, this recipe passed down the generations and gradually refined and improved. It's not a blend of oils.. rather a blend of raw herbs combined, treated and turned to oil.. Pak Yogi has painstakingly acquired the safety standards and licences to sell his product on the open market. Earlier this week he was at the G20 handing out samples to the great and good.

But unlike Kutus-Kutus and the other main brands (I have tried) Pak Logi is happy to give us a UK and EU distribution agreement and willing to work with us to make it work. 
This will take sometime.. maybe six months so don't get too excited. But I'm excited, this is something I have been keen to do for a long time.

While we are are here in North Bali we have seen lots of interesting local.. I will maybe update you next week.
For now here is a small Road Trip video made on the fly by our man Bondan..


This week at AW was our 27th birthday.. and like every year we had a celebration..  I'd like to thank everyone who sent good wishes.. so many people have started businesses after being inspired by the story of AW.. to them I'd like to send extra special positive thinking vibes and greetings.. Actually I had a small epiphany regarding  Positive Thinking / Problem Solving.. I'll tell you about it next week.
And thinking positive we have some on the trend products and deals for you..

Take care - much love and peaceful vibes from Bali.

David

title: Year of the Tiger
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Extreme weather everywhere, snow in Athens and Jerusalem. Here there has been a howling wind buffeting my house for the last three days. Only just calming down now. As they say "It's an ill wind that blows no good"..
Katka in Slovakia office.
And so I'm getting itchy feet. It's time to get moving again, after Bondan (assistant to Ringo in Indonesia) went to east Java and discovered two towns making homeware products. I started to get excited about travelling to a new place and making new contacts. My business visa for Indonesia came through.. within minutes I'd book a flight.  

Last week I was telling you about the sad day we decided to retire our EU websites operating from the UK. It's become impossible to serve EU customers well, and so now at least we can focus on serving the UK 100%.
Thank you for all the messages of support and encouragement, it really helps because we really didn't want to lose that fight. 

Tomas and Katka flew to Slovakia yesterday. The other side of the coin is that inside the EU - we are busy and most of the customers that used to buy from AW UK, now buy from our EU distribution warehouses. So much so that the Slovakian warehouse is far too small and we are in the process of making a move to a much larger warehouse. Tomas and Katka are there to help the team make a decent plan. 


Katka in Slovakia office.

Meanwhile back in the UK.. things have been picking up as new stock comes in and Valentine's Day gets closer. Containers from India and China this week.
Lots of changes going on in the UK as mask wearing and travel restrictions are loosened. It really feels like the covid era is drawing to a close.

Coco in China is officially on holiday, it's almost Chinese New Year and all of China closes for about a month. She sent me pictures of previous years when I would be there and we would travel to the hometown. It brought back all the memories. I remember one year we drove, it's normally a six hour drive. But at CNY everyone is moving at the same time and the G60 from Yiwu to Dongxiang which is like China's Route 66 was crazy. The day we chose to travel the government in their wisdom decided to make a free day with no tolls. So everyone in clapped out motors and rusty pickup trucks hit the road, it was like Mad Max with endless minor crashes and cars breaking down. It took 14 hours with me doing most of the driving, it was an experience I will never forget. 
Last time I went the hometown was 2019.. it was also falling on Coco's grandmothers 88th birthday. The whole village came to a party in the street. A brass band came from the local church and played awfully and someone let off a massive firecracker that lasted for ages. Then we all got a bit drunk playing drinking games, fond memories.. I found some pictures.




The world has changed a lot since then.. Coco will take a fast train this time, it's like flying business class with comfortable seats and cabin service and the journey time is less than 2 hours.
That village now has a new road with a landscaped garden area and the houses have been painted. It's changed dramatically.
It's the Year of the Tiger. A quick google tells me.. The tiger is known as the king of all beasts in China and is associated with bravery, confidence and strength.. this is worrying. 
How are things going to pan out in the year of the Tiger?  Well who knows?. what we really need is a Crystal Ball..
Heavens above we have one right here.. Back in stock Crystal Balls.. 


And because the container from China had lots of display stands on it.. lots of starter packs are back in stock.
It's all systems go as we move into the Season of Love.

Take care everyone.

More news next week or I should say next year.. in the year of the tiger.

David

title: Oh Happy Day!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain    

 

Hope you are doing well and feeling a bit more upbeat.

It was a good day on Wednesday as the vaccine approval came in. But it seemed like everything came right on Wednesday. 

Last week I was telling you about some Hugs & Incites @ AW you can read about it here.


So on Wednesday, the warehouse deal finally, finally completed. If you have been following the story you will know it's been a bit complicated. And if it had gone to pot it could easily mean that AW are out on our ears looking for a new warehouse.. but all the moving parts miraculously came together this week. On Monday the funds arrived from the USA pension fund, on Friday the last details of the ten year lease were resolved - Katka signed the lease, funds went to the aerospace company selling the building, and the deeds changed hands and the lease came into being at that moment and AW has official secure tenure. Affinity Park is ours!!



On that Wednesday morning I'm driving to Malaga to do some interviews with our shortlisted candidates for two new jobs at the Spain warehouse. On the way I have to stop at the car hire company, they asked me to bring my car back - said I couldn't extend the hire anymore. I must get a new contract. I'm not into flash cars particularly, so I usually hire a modest car. The car I wanted wasn't available.. the girl on the desk asked me if I need a bigger car? I said no, a small car is fine, she asked if I had a family. Strange question? Yes I said, but it's a long story, my wife is in China. I haven't seen her since the 15th of January last year. "It's a long covid related story, I'm alone here" - I told her. Behind the mask I could see warm concerned eyes. "It's only two seats but I'm going to give you this car for the same price". A really nice bright Santa red SLK soft top Merc.. Small but super sporty. I'm even more happy. It's the bargain of the year.

 

In the car I'm tuned to "Times Radio" - have you tried it?, there is an app or webpage. I love it. Friendly chatty news.  And on that morning all about the new vaccine. Lockdown officially over in england, plenty of tiers anyway. But still good news: lots of shops can re-open.  Are you opening up? We decided to help our customers with a mega shopfitting deal, check out the beautiful product enhancing furniture below, unrepeatable deals to celebrate the re-opening. (See below)

 

We put a Christmas tree up at AW HQ, and also had a light dusting of snow.. so it's official - it's Christmas. Plus Rodrigo is wearing his "Let it Snow" top.. so it must be. 

This week's apt.. xmas lyrics.. no place to go.. pubs are closed.. can't travel.. so let it snow.. 

 

Oh the weather outside is frightful
But the fire is so delightful
And since we've no place to go 
Let it snow, let it snow, let it snow  


At AW-Artisan in Malaga, the whole team spill out of the office and warehouse to check out my car..  taking selfies with the car. They are all happy, because we just had a record month and everyone has a big bonus. It's all-go in the office and they are doing virtual showroom visits all day. Via whatsapp they take the customers on a tour of the showroom explaining and demonstrating products. Spanish people love to chat no? 

Whilst this is going on Toni and I do interviews - we have one booked every half an hour.. and not one misses, everyone turns up.  

When you see a lot of people, they can get mixed up in your mind afterwards, so to help me focus - I use this old trick..  I give them all nicknames, which I scribble on the notes. Then I like to sleep on it, think carefully about how they will fit in the team, what talents they can bring and try to visualize the team dynamic. I just chatted to Toni and it seems we both settled on the same two people. Jesus, who lives in Benalmadena and Attila who was originally from Hungary. 

So Toni is calling "Jesus of Benalmadena" and "Attila the Hun" right now to give them the good news..

 

Meanwhile we are working hard to get your orders out. It's absolutely peak time, and with some shops reopening and restocking it's putting some pressure.  We slipped a bit behind, but are doing our best to catch up.. there are more orders being shipped that ever before at AW, this week three containers came. Two from Indonesia and one from India.. so lots back in stock.. and lots selling out. Exports to the EU are up 800% as customers panic about getting stock after Brexit. So it's a bit crazy. I know James and his team are working flat out.

Dusan the Aromatic's factory manager is also stressed, taking on lots of extra staff. He is doing his best to up production of bath bombs and shower steamers enough to meet orders. But Greenman soaps are now back. The beast from France is in full production.. next up guest soaps will be back soon. 

 

More news next week.. There are lots of things happening.

 

Take care and stay safe.

 

David

title: One day in Ubud
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud,

We are back in buzzing Ubud. Honestly I have never seen the place more busy. More and more young Russian runaways every day.

Last week I was telling you about Flores and the area known as Labuan Bajo. Most people go there to visit Komodo island to see the fabled dragons that live there, but to get there is a day (at least) sailing through the most beautiful sea, past spectacular islands along with a whole flotilla of other boats making roughly the same trip. 
On the first of August the local government increased the entry fee from about £10 to £200 person to see the dragons.. to fund conservation they said. As we left for the airport a huge protest was taking place, we almost didn't make it. The protesters clearly think the price hike will destroy the local economy, especially the back-packer end of the scale. But we made it into the airport and back to Bali.. so many problems in the world these days. You can read last week newsletter here.

I was telling you last week about the pearls.. in a small fishing village we had bought a pearl necklace for about £10.. the quality was clearly not amazing but.. real pearls at this price, we had to investigate. Anyway to cut a long story short we spent a day dashing all around Labuan Bajo meeting various old ladies with small pouches of pearls which the poured out onto small towels for our appreciation.   Black pearls, pink pearls, grey and pearl coloured pearls.. How much? 
These pearls are not farmed, but found by pearl divers in the remote islands. One lady whose husband was a sea captain explained he bought them on his voyages and she traded them. 
The farmed pearls come from controlled sources and maybe the village lady was getting rejected from a farm.. we are still investigating.. Anyway in the end Coco bought two pearls from the sea captain's wife which later we will make into earrings.


Back in Ubud catching up with all the suppliers who have samples for us to see, and deals to conclude.  Always looking to find the next mega selling product, I keep saying to Ringo and Bondan we need to find the next Molten Glass Bowls, or the next Coconut Lamp.. 

A typical day in Ubud.. This morning we woke up to find a rather entitled monkey sitting on our balcony helping himself to a snack of my wifes cigarettes. 


At 9am meet Ringo and Bondan in a local cafe for extra strong Bali Coffee. One of our oldest suppliers joins us to discuss new projects. One involves this intricately carved mandala design.

title: David's AW News: Crazy in India, Plans & Protest Songs
content_html:
Greetings from a hot and humid Bali.


I don't know if you want to hear this but it has been almost too hot to work. I know the UK has been getting some spring-like weather and blue skies - so Spring is in the air. 
I'm still getting over our man Ringo wanting to retire..big news in last week's missive, if you missed you can catch up here. I spoke to Ringo the other day in his village, we miss you, I told him, and he said he was missing Ancient Wisdom also, so maybe.. 

Well Mother's Day is almost upon us, and focus moves to Easter.. Spring is in the air and it does feel more lively.. things are happening!!
And it's St Patricks day on Monday.. Guinness and Green Ties Day.

And I'm still angry about Temu and Shein. The more I think about it the more unfair it seems. I was very sad to see that an old established wholesaler, a brilliant company run by lovely people, has been forced to close down.  And Temu is a big factor in this.  I have some updates on this below.. 
Remember that bus.. it inspired me to compose a protest song..

And some disturbing news from China.. below.
I was speaking to Coco in China this morning. She said there is a lot of news about Taiwan at the moment, the government getting upset about all sorts of things..  She really thinks something bad will happen soon. I hope not, because another major disruption to trade is the last thing we need. You heard it hear first.

All I can say is you are safer at AW, we have more non-China stock than most, and what we do have is ethically sourced to the best of our ability. Coco spends half her life making sure products are tested for all sorts of extreme standards, labelling and certificates. This all adds to the cost. But we do it all. Temu does none of this.
OK ok I'm a bit obsessed.. haha.. sorry.

Beautiful things sell!
We have beautiful products from Indonesia, Nepal, India etc, made by artisans that care.. products that your customers will keep for a lifetime, (not end up in the landfill in weeks). 
And as we sometimes forget, Rodrigo and co reminded us (from the AW showroom this week) to display your products on wood to look good. The setting is all important.. and natural wood displays really enforce the quality aspect of the products you sell, I'm not sure if anyone has done a study, but I'm guessing the perceived value of gift products displayed on wooden shelves over plastic racking must repay the investment is displayed 1000%.. 
See our displays here.. and more cost effective than you might imagine.

We have two main suppliers for this kind of furniture in Bali.. One is a super organised and hardworking  lady boss, called Widya Dewi. Years ago when we first met she was holding a job at the local bank while her handy husband was producing furniture in carved out jungle compound. Since then they have built a large house, had children and grown the business to be able to produce container load orders efficiently. We are really happy to work with this family business. And as always we have confidence that the wood is ethically sourced, trace documents are provided and standards are good.
Meanwhile in India
It is that totally wild time of year.. I'm kind of happy to miss it.. but our Indian friends just LOVE it so MUCH.
It's Holi, a time when it is socially expectable to throw powder paint at friends and people you just bumped into.. to get stoned and party all night.. all polite social norms are shelved - go WILD guys!!
Wishing all our Indian (and Nepal) friends a wonderful fun and colourful Holi.
Our Mr Chatterjee showing us his colours!

Meanwhile it's almost time to move on.. shortly I will be in Nepal and then India and then..(wait and see)..
But I need your help!!
We will send you a survey shortly.. I'd appreciate if you could share your wisdom and suggest the things that you think would delight your customers.. or the things you can sell but find hard to get..
I need your insights from the cutting edge of retail.. 

Temu protest song..
I realised the Brexit Bus said £360 million a week.. when I asked Perplexity deep seek to carefully calculate what loophole traders are costing the UK.. it came back with £860 million a week!!
I mean WTF!! You can see the carefully calculated, verified and citated results here

I had so much fun (AI) creating a protest song.. then making a video.. Here it is..Please like and share  


I know.. I'm obsessed.. but it has to stop.
And if not yet signed..please sign our Change.org petition. Thank you.
https://www.change.org/TaxTemuProtectUKTraders

Have a lovely weekend!

David

title: Road Trip Java
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali.

The covid situation here is changing day by day, restrictions across Asia being dropped. PCR tests are no longer required for flights in Indonesia and from next week no quarantine into Bali. So great excitement that the tourists are finally coming back. There is a real sense that the pandemic cloud is passing. But also a sense that a particular era is coming to an end..

Last week I was telling you about Bali new year and the day of silence. On New Year's eve we had a little adventure in depth of the Monkey forest. If you missed it you can read about it here.
The day after we went to Ringo's hometown in the remote Bangli region, to attend a wedding ceremony. I'll maybe tell you more about it next week because it was very special.. but here are a few pictures..


It rained but was lovely. I had to wear a traditional Balanese dress. And like any wedding, I made lots of new friends. A great honor to be accepted as an outsider on such an occasion. 

The day after that wedding we flew to Java - the next island to Bali and the main island for population. 
We just arrived back, my goodness it was a hectic and eventful road trip across the island. Carefully planned by Bondan (assistant to Ringo) after a research trip a couple of months ago. He set meetings with various artisan family businesses and laid the groundwork for meetings. Bali has amazing artisans and lots of homegrown product groups, but a lot of the basic materials come from other parts of Indonesia, especially Java. Shipping costs and middlemen push those prices higher so we thought it good to go direct. Since Bondan is from East Java and speaks the local language he had more chances of gaining trust and opening doors.

Artisan skills in Indonesia are very localised with whole villages devoted to one type of production. Skills are passed down the generations and the work is very collaborative with different families focused on different parts of the process.

We visited three villages. The Seagrass Village in the east, then the Teak Village in Central Java, then near the North West Coast the Brass Village. Travelling diagonally from East to West, from the north coast to the south.


An epic road trip, Ringo, Bondhan, myself and our driver. We stayed in three big cities Yogyakarta, Solo then in Surabaya, each time in luxury five star hotels at ridiculous pandemic prices. The hotels, although empty, are gearing up for the arrival of tourists again. So we hit a sweet spot of full service and low prices. It was great fun in the evenings.. Our own private chef, staff and rock bands in rooftop bars.. But the daytime was spent out in the artisan villages of rural Java.

Very different villages but what each had in common was peace. Idyllic pretty towns with an artisan industry as its focus. Bondan has done a great job discovering these places because they are kind of secret locations jealously guarded by the traders and agents working from flashy showrooms in the city.
The first place was the Seagrass Village just an hour or so from the new (impressive) Yogyakarta airport. 

Nestled amongst rice terraces the village is quite prosperous with nice villa style houses and lush green surroundings. The first thing we noticed was the rope makers, twine of different types stretched out along the side of the road, with a kind of pulley system where runners stretch lengths of raffia and a spindle guy or machine does the weaving. Lots of small businesses simply make natural rope and twine, these are supplied to the businesses that weave the baskets and other products. Other places make the wooden frames that serve as mould designs that the baskets are first woven on. So the village is totally collaborative and interdependent on each other. Everyone works together to produce beautiful things. 

Sat on the terrace of one potential supplier discussing ideas, a cow wanders past, the occasional passer by on a bike, very few cars. Apart from the sound of birds tweeting, it is as quiet and peaceful a place as you can imagine. 
We visited six different artisan and within the day settled on two suppliers who we felt we could work with and asked for modified samples. We came back the following day and actually managed to place orders for two container loads.

Here is a video to give you an idea of how the Seagrass Village looks and feels.


The other villages we visited had the same kind of dynamic, I'll tell you about those later.
There is a lesson to be learned from these villages, that collaboration, trust and trade bind us together to create a peaceful prosperous world. 
A darker side of human nature seeks to be self sufficent, nationalistic, controling of others, then eventually wars happen. Trade (fair trade) is maybe the only vaccine against this, the peacemaker.

Meanwhile we have lots of new and interesting gifts coming in stock.. check out the details below.

Hope you have a peaceful and stress free weekend.

David

title: The Nice Guys
content_html:
Greetings from Goa, India

Last week I was telling you about the Good and Bad in India - and our trip to the city of Panipat. If you missed it you can catch up here.
After Panipat we spent a few days in the heart of Old Delhi diving down the many back lanes and wire strune alleyways that harbour some of the oldest export businesses in India. 
The area around the old Jama Masjid Mosque, is still a buzzing marketplace of traders dealing in all kinds of Indian handicrafts. Many years ago, arriving early in the morning directly from the airport, I was almost mugged there and only saved by the timely arrival to work of our supplier. So happy memories. 

After our Old Delhi days, we moved to Greater Noida not far from Deli to attend the trade show. I have said before that I'm not a big fan of the trade show, many of the traders are not much more than marketing companies subcontracting to the artisans that we would prefer to deal directly with. Anyway we weren't even sure if the show was going to be well attended, there had been talk at one point last year of it being cancelled or drastically scaled so I was pleasantly surprised to see a huge buzz of activity, and yes all the halls fully occupied. And the hotels full across the area, this is the first chance since covid receded and India opened up that a major trade show in our industry is taking place. 
There are 16 halls plus a permanent mart area. We spent the first two days just walking the halls, meeting and greeting old suppliers and checking out prospective new ones. The main hall is old school with many long standing suppliers, and I feel there is not so much innovation. At the edges of the show in the overspill halls, you find younger people with brighter ideas and a more (dare I say) straightforward approach. 


It's about the product, and when you meet young people passionate about design and great products, who love gifts first and foremost, you know it's going to be easy to do business. But when you see those pot bellies, sullen greedy eyes, when prices have to be argued at length, and deals painfully hammered out, you begin to realise that money is the main love and so it's time to run away.  After many years, you learn it's better to do business with the nice guys. 
Regular readers will know we go to great lengths to ensure that we are only dealing with the nice guys. India has come a long way since I first started coming here, in those days child labour was common and working conditions generally poor. It was hard to find the good guys. But now its far better and most exporters are generally socially conscious. I still like to go and visit the workshops and factories of the people we deal with if at all possible. 


For example this couple were obsessive about incense. We are going to their factory soon to confirm a two container order.

After the trade show we normally fly down to Goa, quiet, peaceful, beautiful North Goa - far from the party zone - where we have a base of sorts. Here we meet up with the gemstone suppliers from nearby Gujerat who bring suitcases of samples and spend a day sifting and sorting out esoteric beauties you and your customers will love.  The rare minerals, gemstone artifacts, gemstone jewellery, orgonite items and pendulums etc all come from about four or five family businesses that we have been trading with for years.  Often I was dealing with the father, now the son or daughter has grown up and taken over. They tell me proudly they are the fifth or sixth generation doing this business. Strangely none of this was to be found at the tradeshow, I'm not sure why. 


Meeting father and son in Goa.

As I write this we still have a few more days here, after this we fly to Bangalore to go and visit two incense factories and possibly do a deal for a whole new product group.. stay tuned.

Meanwhile back in the UK - the team at AW Aromatics have been busy, and this week unleashed on the world a new bath bomb range that takes bath bomb gifts to a whole new level. 
Check out the Gemstone chip bracelet bath bomb.  Take a bath, enjoy the fizz and fragrance then discover your bracelet, each bracelet has a different meaning.. I love it. For sure your customers will love it too.. the world of gemstones and bath bombs come together and a new product is born! 

More news next week.
Namaste from India.

David

title: David's AW News: Rain but no Rain.
content_html:
Greetings from the AW Warehouse, Bali.

Yes I'm back in Bali.

Last week I was in Spain, and I was telling you about Resolutions and Rainbows as the new year kicked off. If you missed it you can catch up here. I'm so happy to be back with the Indonesia teams.
Last Sunday I caught a Turkish airways flight from Malaga to Istanbul, with a tiny 2 hour connection to Denpasar, Bali. Of course the flight was delayed by two hours so I fully expected to miss the connection.. There was about six or seven people on my flight with the same connection, as we disembarked, the ground staff told us we could still make it as our onward flight was also delayed but we must run. So run we did. The new Istanbul airport as you probably know is huge, and our gate was at the opposite end.. Sweating and panting we arrived just as the last passengers boarded. I seem to be doing this a lot lately. Phew.. made it, but from experience I knew that my luggage wouldn't make it. I was right - in fact my luggage just arrived at my hotel this morning four days later.. not a big problem as I keep spare clothes and stuff here - the case was anyway mostly gifts for our teams. 

The dry spell in Spain is a big problem as I mentioned last week, here in Bali it is officially the rainy season. Except as people keep telling me - It's the rainy season - without the rain. Which means it's crazy humid and crazy hot. It's hard to work in this heat.. over 40c in the day and night time it barely drops to 30c and the air conditioner in my room chugs along barely shifting the humid air. I wake up in the night in a pool of sweat. 
I came to the warehouse to write this newsletter.. distribute new year Spanish Chocolates and every now and then another artisan turns up with new product samples or a delivery of stock.
Outside the warehouse even our pet love birds are looking a bit subdued by  the heat.


Ringo and Bondhan have been busy since the last time I was here. They have had a new mezzanine floor installed across the back section and added more racking to make better use of the space.
Production, stock of packaging and finished goods area is much better organised. It's always nice to see things progressing and getting a little better and better every visit.



But I had an important task to work on. Tomas had given me strict instructions to fix our under supply of Molten Glass Bowls. In the Slovaian warehouse these have become the number two selling product family. Before Christmas I had been told customers had been screaming for stock,   almost to the point of tears. We currently have two suppliers, a nice family business not far from the warehouse and the Godfather of singing bowls in Bali who has a huge factory out in the wilds of Tegalalang up in the hills beyond Ubud. During the pandemic when the tourist gift trade vanished and foreign buys couldn't come, I was stranded here and we were able to work with both companies and support them with enough business to  keep the staff busy. The Godfather always says how grateful he was for that support at that time and he does his best to meet our needs but even he cannot produce enough. So we figured we need maybe two more suppliers to meet our supply needs. My mission is to find them and sign them up on supply contracts. But these workshops don't have websites, some have showrooms but many just work under contract and are hard to find.

Ringo's brother sadly passed away during covid, there was no proper Balanese funeral allowed and so the family consulted a holy man as to how to make an acceptable passing. 
The holy man's house was next to a Molten Glass Bowl factory, which it turned out belonged to the brother of the holy man. Ringo noted that at the time... and so now we really need more suppliers we went along to see if we could possibly do business.  When we arrived the boss was in the process of making a beautiful hand blown cocktail glass, for a Japanese client. We had to wait while the process was completed.


Hot work in hot weather..

We got chatting and made friends.  And he showed us his specialty products.  He was proud of discovering a way to put small flecks of colours into the glass creating a nice rainbow effect. (Watch out for a new product coming soon). But he told us the same sad story as many suppliers do. The artisans are leaving for more stable jobs in hotels and resorts. He told us every time he trained a new worker after a few months he or she would be off. He'd like to supply us but that was the problem. I have mentioned this before in newsletters. The shrinking pool of artisans is our biggest supply line problem. The answer is to simply pay more no? Then they would happily stay in the home village and do what they love. Turns out the money in the hotels is not really any more than they can make, but offers a stable, reliable job.  A supply of orders to an artisan is often feast or famine. To many people a steady income is more important than the amount paid.  So I wanted to test my theory.. 

I asked if we could make a supply contract. He shook his head.. no contract please. Because those aggressive (often American) agents come with contracts in hand that are full of penalties, discounts, drawbacks and exclusivity deals and they end up losing money. No no, I said not like that - no penalties, no dodgy stuff - just a commitment to buy a fixed amount every month at a fair price. So that you can say to your artisans.. here this is a regular and safe job. He told us he would think about it.

Well we'd drafted a contract (using ChatGPT) and today we signed our first Artisan Supply Agreement (ASA). I'm so happy.. but let's wait and see how it pans out.
All day today I have been pitching my "ASA" idea to all the visiting artisan suppliers and I think it's getting a warm reception. What people want is a sense of security. 


This young lady just came, Tomas found the family last time he was here. They make masks and Elephants. She brought these samples to show us. I was impressed with how obsessed and knowledgeable she was about the finish and details.  Normally it's older ladies doing this type of job, but yes her mother and grandmother and friends work in the village. Our current supplier has trouble supplying for the same reason as I mentioned but her family would be very happy with a contract. After consulting with Mum.. she said they would be happy to make 150 a month. Not much but  it will supplement our current supplier.  And yes despite the heat she is wearing jacket and gloves.. I never understand this, Indonesians whatever the weather dress like winter to ride a bike.. and are shocked to the core to see foreign tourists half naked on bikes. It's cultural. 

So much to do.. very busy. We even have meetings this weekend. In a day or so James from UK arrives, it's his first business trip, first time in Bali and  I'm going to enjoy it :)
He will be working with the AW-Advantage.com team in the beach office.. because James is our Fulfilment manager and we need API making to improve that service.

That's all the news so far..
Meanwhile in the UK.. there has been a few containers arriving. Including Indian products (lots) back in stock. (see below). 
More updates later.

Take care.. or as they say here, Hati-Hati!

David
