title: Stuff Happens & the Biggest you have ever seen
content_html:
Greetings, once again from Sheffield..

 

It's all coming together.. slower than expected or than wished, but lots of projects are suddenly coming along quite nicely. And when I say lots.. I have almost lost track of the things the AW folk are working on.

These days everything is much more complicated, so what normally takes weeks now takes months.. everything from Brexit, to supplyline issues to covid complications, to worldwide shortages of raw materials... to rampant inflation.. is slowing us down. But nevertheless with a bit of positive thinking and bloody determination - as I always say to my guys.. "You gotta just make stuff happen!"

I have made a bit of an update below..

Last week I was telling you about one of those projects just launched in Spain (coming to the UK soon) that literally drove our man in Spain; Toni - to drink.. If you missed it you can read about the project and Toni's drink problem here.


Father's day is almost upon us.  Just over a week to go, so this is really the last chance to stock up..

In other good news, the limitation on numbers at weddings is being lifted - so wedding favours numbers go up also :)

From Wedding Favours items to Dad's Gifts - guess what? AW has you covered.

And for the ultimate Wedding Favour.. something extrodinary just arrived from India.. (we ordered it almost 2 years ago and it just came)..  see below.

 

Projects Updates:

 

AW-Fulfilment.co.uk

We went live with our fulfilment site.. if you need short or long term storage at reasonable rates we can help. Soon your stock can also link to AW-Dropship.com where you can have them dispatched to your customers.

Note how we spell Fulfilment the English way, not the american way.. unlike amazon who do things the american way. . Simple, straightforward and easy.. Call James if you need more info..

Any company looking for a warehouse.. now we can offer you an alternative.. a cost effective alternative where you only pay for the space and services you use.



 James ready for action..

 

AW-Aromatics.com

Gone live today! Finally we are getting there.. Many of you know and appreciate the importance of having control of your own brand. Take back control!!  Haha to quote a phrase.. If you don't understand why.. Read this: The Importance of a Brand. 

So our man Radek is now firmly in the hot seat.. empowered to help you achieve your dreams and goals. 



Radek ready for action..

 

New Bath Bombs.

We are delighted to announce the launch of a range of new bath bombs.. Called Funky Bath Bombs..

Also (now please calm down) back in stock after a long absence (due to packaging material issues) - Shower Steamers. Great for the aforementioned wedding favours..  (see below)

 

New Guest Soaps

Ducks and Clouds to join Hearts & Flowers.. it's taken a long time (it's a long story) but finally some new shapes.. with I'm told more on the way. (see below)

 

My Deals

I have been pushing for this, for a long time.. 

Do you wanna make a deal?  Now if there is something that you have a good market for, and feel you deserve a bigger discount due to your buying power.. maybe something you buy elsewhere but would like to buy from AW..

Chat to our customer service team in the chat box.. when you make a deal it will appear in the "My Products & Deals" tab.. once approved they will appear here..



This week we had another container from Indonesia, and a shipment from India. The gemstones and esoteric items from India have been almost two years since ordering to delivery.

The Ultimate Wedding Favour.. is this Shiva Lingam .. you can read about the sacred power here. Needless to say they are an ancient and  powerfull fertility symbol..

This is the biggest (and most powerful we have ever seen)..



Very soon it's Freedom Day - 21st of June.. Why couldn't this be the 20th.. that would be Father's Day.. so frustrating for Dad's.. but anyway it seems like freedom is on hold.. I heard a guy on the radio.. freaking out.. "I'm double jabbed, I have not seen my family in Europe for over a year, my business has been drained of cash, I have followed every rule, every instruction, every directive.. for goodness sake everyone vulnerable has been jabbed.. I'm having my Flipping Freedom Day whatever Boris says".  I understand exactly how he feels. Enough is enough..  

So STUFF is happening.. we are working hard to deliver you the best in giftware..
Hope you are making stuff happen as well.. 

Take care.. enjoy the sunshine..

David

title: Making Beautiful Things Happen
content_html:
Greetings from Spain..


Hope you are doing well.. and that August is kind to you.
Here in Spain it is hot... very HOT.. which is great if you are on holiday and just focused on cool beer and cool swimming pools.
But distinctly not cool if you are focused on work and doing a good job. 
Last week I was telling you about being cancelled, my Indonesian visa blocked and having to reschedule travel plans.
It's still not working out - as of this morning almost all foreign visa (including mine) are blocked, since I was due to fly on Tuesday I have decided to delay again, you can read it here.
But it wasn't really clear on the government website, my visa agent was saying it will be OK.. just fly.. but Bali.com said no.. lot's of Youtubers said no.. Absolutely no answer from the helplines at the Indonesian embassy in London. So I called up Ringo (our man in Indonesia) and he took a trip to the immigration office in Denpasar.


The nice people there tried very hard to find a way, but in the end suggested I rebook and reapply for a new visa.  
Now I will stay in Spain until September, and then try again to fly. Was so excited to be travelling again, but now a lot of disappointed Indonesian suppliers and a bit of pain.. where my wings have been clipped:)

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here. Over 74,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr. Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka, Rodrigo and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken.

I was also telling you about the difficulties importers face these days. Sometimes it feels as if the whole world is trying to trip us up. 
Shipping a container from Indonesia to Europe pre-pandemic would cost about €3500 - the last container that arrived in Slovakia cost €17,500 adding about 90% to the cost of the products.. We are doing our best to absorb as much of the increases as possible but this is a whole new level. 
So now we are going to extreme lengths to use every square inch of space.. Ringo sent me pictures of the current packing system..


We have staff packing textiles inside furniture and shopfittings every little nook and cranny is stuffed. This Ringo with his container stuffing team.

However, in spite of all this craziness.. or maybe because of it - we are more determined than ever to design and make new products.. These days instead of just Tomas and I making it happen, (as I was telling you a few weeks back) we have a whole team spread across the UK, Spain and Slovakia.. working to bring you new products.
The Artisan Tea range that Toni in Spain and his team (with a little help from me) spent months making, finally shipped to the UK.. and initial feedback has been great, which is reward enough for the work put in. See details below.
And Coco in China, who is our agent and also runs the soy wax candle factory there.. has been working with the Spain team on an idea that Tomas developed.. and I think it is going to be awesome.. it's kind of top secret because there are competitors that read this newsletter and find it hard to do something different.. and just like to copy.. but I can't resist dropping hints.. imagine mixing aromatics, gemstones, magic and drama to create a whole new concept in candles.. haha you're going to love them!

This is what we do. Making beautiful things, for wonderful retailers to delight their lovely customers.. as I'm fond of saying every gift is nothing less than an act of love. And at AW  we are humbled to be part of that process. And in troubled times the thing we need more of is love..  if you want to send a bit of love back our way.. you can send suggestions for products (just click reply)  or of course add a review at Reviews.com

Take care - have a lovely weekend.

David

title: Report from Delhi
content_html:
Greetings from Spain (again).


I keep rescheduling my flight to Indonesia, every week they announce the latest restrictions and every week it is extended so my visa is not valid for entry.
But this week the news from YouTubers on the spot is that the airports have been told to make ready the international terminals.. so maybe there will be a gradual reopening.
Last week I was telling you about how the cost of shipping goods is still sky high, and that I suspect a bit of unhealthy competition.. I did a bit of research and discovered some disturbing info.. You can read about it here.

Tomas (The AW marketing wizard) has been here - officially on holiday but inevitably getting involved in the Spain distribution center (AW Artisan) and of course the products that are in development here.
And when not doing that.. checking out the best gift shops to see any good ideas and developing markets that we might not be aware of..

Last week I was also telling you about the apparent opening up of a bottleneck in supply of the shipping containers.. Ringo (Indonesia) loaded two in one night, Coco (China) four.. of course these are all much delayed containers and will only reach us when we are well into the Christmas season. Everyday I check the stock levels in our warehouses, hoping to see increases, but we seem to be almost fighting a losing battle. Despite lots of open purchase orders, lots of new products on the way and under development - lots more AW people working in procurement and development than ever before we are fighting to keep goods flowing smoothly.
We are not the only ones I'm sure..Brexit, supply issues and the pandemic has disrupted many industries. - even (I am told) IKEA has big gaps in displays.
I mentioned before cash is no longer king, stock is king. These days I check the stock levels more than the bank balance. We are entering a strange new world. 

There was the Trade Show in Birmingham last week, Bryant from the purchasing department made a flying visit to see if he could find anything interesting, especially British manufacturers we could work with, but to no avail. I understand the show was a shadow of it's former self. Sadly.
In Delhi this week is also a tradeshow, and Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) went along to see.. but I think the same story. However, he went to visit some of our suppliers around Delhi and was able to forward me some new product designs.

Happy Christmas Folks.. hope that trade is going good.
Right now it seems like all of AW is running on Full Steam.. all systems go.

Christmas is approaching fast. We are already on day 5 of the 12 days of Christmas free gifts.. showcasing our most popular and fast selling products. 
Well it's almost Christmas.. when Ancient Wise Men first brought gifts and established the first Christmas presents. Since we are Ancient Wisdom - your favourite gift wholesalers.. we are bringing YOU gifts everyday.. Don't miss out it's day 5 already!!
Last week I was telling you about my arrival back in the UK.. and the shock of landing in Manchester. If you missed it you can catch up here.
It was great to see Rodrigo and Holly.. working on the next "Can You Sell This?" YouTube video.. and all see all the team working on full steam Christmas rush now full on.. Right on our Busiest Week Ever at Ancient Wisdom.. 




But this month is kind of crazy.. it's the beginning of the Christmas Party Season at AW.. and I'm expected - no duty bound to attend them all.. It's a hard life. So after little more than a week in the UK.. I headed to T2 at Manchester airport.. Which after my unfavourable review last week of Manchester arrivals.. I can report massive improvements since my last trip there.. they spent £1.3bn  on the departure T2 and it's awesome..so smooth and easy.. world class! Check in and luggage drop as easy as Vienna, Security (no need to take out laptops) better than Amsterdam, common areas better but not as good as most Asian International departures..   EasyJet flies from T2 but not Ryanair for that reason alone you should switch.  

So on Monday I flew EasyJet from Manchester to Malaga.. arriving late evening. Been so busy this year.. this is the first time in my home in La Cala de Mijas since June.. my poor house needs a bit of love and attention.. but alas not much time.. 

So here in Spain
Main job here is to help Toni make the final choice of warehouse and enable a fast move.. I went to see two warehouses on the shortlist.. and approved one of them. Agreed a deal and it looks like we could be moving to our new home in Malaga pretty soon. Maybe even over Christmas. Things can happen fast in Spain.. 
It's going to be great.. We could have done with a bit bigger but warehouses are scarce these days. This is a warehouse 50% bigger,  pallet racking already in place, offices 300% bigger, space for a huge showroom and 3 container docking bays 2 drive in bays. So a big upgrade in infrastructure.. and importantly two or three nice lunch restaurants within walking distance! 





This could be our new home in Spain.. wish us well.. The team in Spain will be busy beyond normal this Christmas.
More updates soon... 



Meanwhile in Bali
Tomas is almost on his last day.. and then he is back for Christmas..in UK and Slovakia. 
He has been working long days.. with our teams in our IT development office, (who it seems never want to go home).

He has been very busy there.. Now we have a solid key team.. we have been recruiting like crazy.
Lots of things are happening - offices revamped, an extra room for the team to work in, bigger monitors, more powerful computers, better air conditioners. There will be a big expansion soon. And several key new projects launched.. I'll keep you updated because some of them could save you money or help your business grow. 

Drop shipping Update
As part of that team we have a dedicated Drop-shipping section.. working REALLY hard to improve the AW drop shipping backend and systems. Now we have a system where bugs and issues come to the team directly from users.. and they are priding themselves on fixing things and improving things inside the day if possible. 
Well drop shipping sales are booming with some key customers making magic happen.. we have AWESOME products coming online.. Check it out here: AW-Dropship.com

In our Slovakia warehouse..
The team there has never been so busy.. again because of the great products we have right now..
But for a while we will lose a key member of staff.. Zuzana, our wonderful webmaster for the EU website: AWGifts.eu   She is going on maternity leave.

So we wish you well and thank you Zuzana for your super hard work.

Meanwhile in the UK.. stock arriving and the warehouse team are working all hours to get your orders out..
As well as lots of new products.. just coming online.. a lot this week came back in stock..

So grab it quick.. and take advantage of our 12 Days of Christmas gift giveaway..

Have a lovely weekend.
I'm off to the Spain AW Christmas party!!

Take care & adiós

David

title: The Art of Energy Flow at Ancient Wisdom
categories: Yin and Yang | ancient wisdom | Feng Shui | China
content_html:
In the last blog I was getting all philosophical and pondering the roll of Yin & Yang in business.

Sue sent this happy thought..
Hi David,
Yin and Yang, very deep philosophy true, but we all need balance in this life, if there were no 'Bad' in this world, how would you know what was 'Good'?  We need comparisons, balance....
Happy thought!
Sue

So having another happy thought, I was thinking how so many things in the gift trade originate from ancient traditions and hold mystical values. Since last week it was Yin & Yang - I thought this week I'd investigate Feng Shui. Or the art of Energy Flow...

Like me you probably think it all a load of superstitious rubbish.. we'll actually that's what I used to think. But it's worth considering that just how things are arranged in our life's affects the way our life's pan out. For example I learned years ago in retailing you can ruin a shops sales by the way it is laid out. A sales counter directly facing and overbearing the entrance can cause a kind of blockage to customers.  Just they way a shop "feels" makes all the difference. Somethings you just do things because they work, but you can't explain why.. energy flows like water and like water you can cause stagnant blockages if your not careful.
Out of this comes the eastern Feng Shui traditions with experts charging for their skills, for example most building in China are built along Feng Shui lines.
The compasses, elephants, toads, turtle-dragons and Buddahs have all been absorbed into a colourful Feng Shui tradition.  They make an exotic retail display and are natural gift lines.. especially if you or your staff can explain little things about them..

Such as.. The elephant: symbol of strength, wisdom, energy and wisdom, it also helps fertility.
Three leg toad: A figure that can attract prosperity should be placed in the lobby.
 Turtle dragon: symbolizes longevity. According to Chinese tradition is able to live 300 years.
The laughing Buddha is the symbol of happiness, good fortune and abundance.

Sorry for rambling on a bit.
Have a well re-arranged week. and if you feel inclined go see the wholesale Feng Shui stuff in the Collectable Dept at AW.

David

title: The Olive Tree
content_html:
Greetings once again from Spain

Last week I was telling you about Balance and Harmony, after visiting the gift shops in the Granada souk. This is on reflection quite important to be a successful gift trader, and you can read about it here.

It's almost the end of our summer sojourn in Southern Spain. Regular readers will know that we have a home La Cala de Mijas overlooking the sea. 
Most of the year is spent travelling between AW outposts, in Asia and Europe - but for a few weeks in summer we always aim to spend some quality time at the villa in Spain. 

Just like a business, it's important to continually invest in a home, and over the years we have done many projects to improve.. this year we bought an olive tree and a dirty big pot to put it in.
Olive trees are the Ancient Wisdom of trees! Mentioned in the Bible and the Koran.. symbolic of wisdom, peace and friendship. So we bought an Olive tree to celebrate the birth of our new Spanish business.. 



Like the business it is already bearing fruit.. but it will be fun to take care of and nurture to see how it grows.

I don't talk much about life at the casa, but for once I'd thought I'd give you a picture of a typical day..  
Usually I rise before dawn, make a cup of coffee and while answering Whatsapps from Indian suppliers or chatting with Ringo (our man in Indonesia) watch the sun majestically cresting the distant Sierra Nevada. The morning sun floods the house and the sea view is always breathtaking, this puts me in a positive mood, and great for thinking big and making plans :) I usually exercise and swim in the Bali inspired pool, decorated with Balinese stone statues. 
My wife will generally sleep in a bit, because inevitable she has been chatting to Chinese suppliers, or sorting some issues with the candle factory in Yiwu during the night. About 8 am we have breakfast together on the terrace, and I check my list of things to do.
Then it's a working day, my phone will begin to ping with messages from the teams in Sheffield or Slovakia and because the time zones are similar can easily communicate. There's always a skype or WhatsApp meeting, recently we started using Slack, which is business communication app, and it plugs you into everything that is happening in the company, I'm not sure whether in this case less is more.. I'm still getting used to it. Ping ping ping..
Thus the day unfolds, always heaps to do, Coco will be placing orders with Chinese suppliers, sorting out issues, I will be lending my brain to whatever issue is testing managers.
When the day is over, maybe we go for dinner with friends or walk on the beach. We like to play chess, and these days I often lose to Coco - I'm sure she is a borderline grandmaster. 

It all sounds idyllic right - I really don't want to make you jealous .. haha.. but it's not all sangria and roses.
One of the reasons we bought the house was that we have an investment in a giftware wholesale company in Malaga..  Our business partner and director (this is years ago) I rather too generously gave 50% shares and effective full control to.. In those days I naively believed if you invest trust you get results that benefit everyone. Sadly the trust in this case was abused, the relationship abused - for 10 years actually, and when we finally started to complain and gently demand a few rights the director basically went rogue.. not paying us for supplies, effectively helping himself to the 50% of the company he didn't own, refusing access to financial information, producing obviously fake accounts for tax purposes.  Breaking the trading relationship with AW, whist still claiming to customers that he represent the values of AW and was in fact AW. This bit hurts the most, because it's fake it's a lie and undermines the good name of AW, whist depriving customers of genuine AW supplies. 

Of course I'm mad, who wouldn't be? For the first time in 20 years I'm having to use lawyers.. and discovering that Spanish company law is surprisingly easy to abuse by bad players. The legal system whilst very firm and just, is just so incredibly slow, so you just grind it out until you get there. 

And yes of course in the meantime I keep reaching out (the proverbial olive branch), trying to make a meeting to find a more mutually beneficial solution, I think they could for example go (honestly) independent, and we could even help them achieve this. It would safeguard the jobs of an excellent team and be genuine honest competition which is good for the customer of course. But the director is scared to meet, lots of excuses, bravado and misplaced bluster.. maybe scared of having to be truly independent. Mostly I guess so he can continue to take advantage as long as possible. Who knows..?
I'm setting this out openly here in my newsletter which is widely read in the gift trade, to warn other business people about Spanish business culture, and Spanish company law. Here you need to be much more careful than in the UK (or even most other EU countries) , working with locals can of course be hugely rewarding and most people are great, but a bad player can abuse the system with ease. Bad debts that can be collected in weeks in the UK, take years here. There is no transparency, in the UK you can search Company House website instantly for free and find all the key information on any company, here you have to pay and then there is virtually nothing to know. Always get a shareholder agreement, never lose control.. just saying.

Meanwhile back in the UK, our new Spain website: AWGifts.es is going great guns, we are picking up totally new customers, some of them very good retailers indeed.. Rodrigo has been overseeing the project and working night and day to make it happen, we have new staff now to take the strain and are well ahead of target. Rodrigo messaged me yesterday that met we July target already. Well done Rodrigo!
Our plan is to find a warehouse - we are looking at some now - and transplant that website (like an olive tree) back into Spain.. after Brexit we will be ready to serve customers better.. but my plan was that our Spain company would also create and contribute gift products back to the UK.. Olive oil gifts for example, now I can see that vision finally coming true. If you know anyone who would be interested in joining us in Spain do drop me a line - it's a new adventure... like the olive tree.. can grow to great things.

Take care


David


PS
Some Indian esoteric stuff arrived.. I'm so excited :)  Check it out below.

title: David's AW News: Surprising Java Road Trip
content_html:
Greetings from Blitar City, Java


I'm on a road trip across the island of Bali with Bondhan again. I arrived the other day on a flight from Bali to Jogjakarta - up at 4am to get a 7am flight, Bondhan was in the midst of loading a container at the Giant Statue supplier. That's such hard work, but it was good to see the statues loaded and all the wasted space around the statues carefully filled with small items. Otherwise, the shipping costs would be too high. We have a YouTube in the mix about this.
Last week I was in China and telling you about the Ancient Wisdom town, not far from Yiwu - super interesting actually and some brilliant retailing ideas for you.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
I got a Grab taxi (like Uber) from Jogya airport direct to the Giant statue supplier - about an hours drive.. beautiful Java morning. 
Typical Java island view.. 

Also, subscribe if not already on our YouTube channel to see past adventures and catch the new ones.

Well, it's been a busy week... After loading the container, finishing at 8pm after a 4am start,.. a bit exhausted but we stayed overnight in Yogyakarta, a friendly and cool student city, lots of universities here and so lots of cool Indonesian kids from all over Indonesia. We managed to grab a beer in a tiny reggae bar and catch a local three piece band do their stuff.  Very friendly place. Java is big,.. and a six hour drive the next morning is the way it rolls here. 

We went to the marble city.. to see our oldish supplier. The first time we started business was in 2023, at the end of the pandemic, just as we were able to get around freely again. Our supplier was delighted we came, a nice young guy, super good at his business. We buy high quality stone soap dishes from them and petrified wood candle holders.. in three years, they have had regular good reorders, so the boss was happy and grateful to see us.. This town is famous for marble and stone,.. and our supplier has a really interesting back-story.
They actually have the most impressive showroom in town, a little strangely, he lives with his wife and kids in the showroom, well, it kind of overlaps the kitchen and lounge of his home.
He told us the story about how his father started the business. His father was the eldest of ten brothers, a humble farmer, and he had two cows, which he sold to buy a small grinding machine and taught himself to make (actually) soap dishes. He was a successful artisan, and all his nine other brothers followed into the same trade. Today, the sons and daughters all run successful marble and stone businesses in the same area. And often work together - they often joke that the whole town was built on two cows. 

He took on a tour of his workshops and store rooms around the town. This is the kind of business that needs both highly skilled artisans and mega heavy equipment. Proving 80 years later a society can be multicultural.

Anyway, have a great weekend.
Lots of deals, and back in stock.

Take care
David

title: Snow time like the present
content_html:
Hi 
Last week I was telling you about the new chat system (read it here). I'm so excited that you seem to love it and embrace it.
Greetings from Andalusia in Spain where I am working with our sister company this week.
Yes your right, it's a smart move escaping the snow, but this weekend we are facing major gales. So much for that plan. :(
Anyway shortly I'm off to India. That should definitely be warmer I think. I will be there for Valentines Day.. they call it V-Day and the tradition is to send your loved one a pair of knickers.
The traditionalist killjoys hate it of course, so it is always a running battle between the modern youth and the stuffy old guys. Should be fun.
Speaking of Valentines.. we have a great "better than free shipping" deal with bonus valentines pens to brighten up your deals for the big love-in weekend.
Hope your not snowed in where you are. We have lots of customers in remote places... at AW we are thinking about you. In the worst case you can at least plan your valentine offers and displays, until the snow clears. Snow time like the present... :) sorry about that.
Back to Spain.. where we are just introducing the chat system on the website (last weeks news). Good news here is that despite the financial crisis (which believe me is bad), things at AW Spain are at least on the up. Sales last year are just in the black, so I'm happy.
One thing I have noticed that is really good in Spain is that the corruption and black money deals are been swept away. Spain is fast sorting itself out. I just bought a small house here (with a nice view) and there was no question or possibility of paying chunks in cash to avoid taxes. This suites me, because I like things straight, but it's also a refreshing change. Practices and attitudes are changing now as rapidly as the skyline did a few years ago. I feel very positive for Spain, because when the crisis passes this country will come out of it leaner and fitter.
More good news, you may remember me telling you about my futile attempts to change the siesta culture at AW Spain - this means closing for an hour and a half at lunch. Well from next week we have managed to stagger breaks and organise ourselves to be open all day. Just like the rest of Europe. See.. pigs can fly!
More good news next week.
Hope you can stay warm and cosy and dodge those snow balls.
All the very best
David

title: David's AW News: Resolutions & Rainbows
content_html:
New Year Greetings from Spain

The first newsletter of 2024. 
Last week was the last of 2023 and I made a recap, a kind of audit of achievements of the year aw AW.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Last night it rained. Flashes of lightning and rumblings of thunder woke me up. I got out of bed and went to the terrace to witness the rain.. 
You see this part of Spain has not had any significant rain in months, we are in a dire dry mess. Bush fires in the hills. Strict water measures are in place, our garden is gradually withering away, the pool cannot be refilled and huge fines can be levied on anyone found with even a watering can in hand. Helicopters sweep down the coast looking for offenders. 
OK ok I know.. it's dry in Spain but so wet with floods and storms in the UK.. sorry I'm not trying to upset you.. stay with me..

Yesterday morning driving into work I saw a vivid rainbow.. I snapped a photo..


A promise of better times ahead.. 
Why? Because I realised for a rainbow to appear there must be water in the air.. maybe the drought is coming to an end. Literally Hope is in the air.

A metaphor for 2024. Let's hope so.

So far so good, we seem to be kicking off the year super busy, as the sales start and smart retailers restock. The only problem is delayed containers (we have eight I believe) that have been redirected to avoid the conflicts off Yemen means that Valentine's Stock could be in short supply, and probably arrive too late. The good news is that lots of best selling V-Day stock comes from our home grown aromatics factory in Sheffield (AW-Aromatics.com) so at least you can find pink bath bombs. Check out our Valentines Page for inspiration.

Here in Spain it is kind of Christmas eve.. The Three Kings will parade tonight distributing literally tons of sweets to kids of all ages. 


The Three Kings.

It's still a working day in Spain.. and that means a good excuse to have an office party.. Lot's of traditional sweet foods and good wishes.
Yesterday we did our annual staff review, talked to all the key staff in Spain one by one. Updated them with our big plans, discussed objectives,  ideas, personal career paths and enquired about wellbeing and happiness at work.. So much enthusiasm, earnest heartfelt speeches and awesome team spirit.. 


Toni and his team have done very well but soon Toni is travelling with me on this year's Epic Asia Trip.. so they will need to be more self reliant and we made a few changes to make sure everything is running smoothly and this year we continue to delight our customers.

Back in the UK.. and it's all happening. Despite everything an Indonesian container made it through... so new stock see below.. 
We have been working on a major price crash for our signature Essential Oils Range. And this week we are excited to launch our permanent LOWER PRICES..  
So I'm excited to announce..
Up to 20% Reductions on our top selling Essential Oils. 
See below for more details.
The team at AW-Aromatics.com have been working on this for the last two months and the new prices (same high quality) land on all our websites across UK and Europe from today.
Other wholesalers do it differently, charge higher prices and do big (apparent) discounts.. we are trying hard to more straightforward than other wholesalers. It's our new year's resolution to bring you the best Fast Selling Products, always the Keenest Prices. (Let us know if you can buy anything cheaper). In 2024 aim to have less gimmicks and more simply beautiful stock that sells great. 
I feel we are getting there when enthusiastic new year reviews come.. check them out here.. (and leave yours if you can, it is very much appreciated - and I promise inspires us to do better and better for you). Also check our Product Reviews (over 10,000) . It might be a good place to find ideas for your store.

Happy new year! Thank you for the newsletters I always look forward to reading, and hearty thanks to everyone at your Sheffield HQ for the patience and perfect dealings we've had so far (100%!) -- they're incredible. Hope everyone's feeling refreshed and ready to go again. What a relief and pleasure to find such a rock-solid and ethical supplier of wond'rous giftware -- it's great to get a peek into all the hard-earned progress, too -- in just one year! -- we can't wait to find out what's been planned for 2024 :D
--Alex..

Thanks Alex for that lovely feedback.. but I was actually thrilled to receive this from Cara..

They will become Like family to you. Always good customer service and quality products. Email updates on their travels too. Love it.

And so happy to read this..

What can I add to all my previous posts on this Company. They are just the best Company I have ever come across in over 50 years. They are completely Honest and exceedingly Helpful. Their range of goods is Brilliant as are their prices. Well Done Ancient Wisdom Wholesale. 100 / 100 your parcels too are always well wrapped and all the items arrive in great condition. I would like to say I Hope YOU ALL HAVE AFANTASTIC CHRISTMAS AND A PROSPEROUS NEW YEAR FOR 2024!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Thank you Peter (and all who posted) for this. You have no idea how encouraging it is to everyone at AW.. and drive us to do better and better..   Leave us a review if you can. Thank you

From me and the team at AW we wish you all the best also for 2024.. 
lots of Sweets and Rainbows to all our amazing customers!!

Hope you are off to a FLYING START this year..
I'm certainly off to a flying start.. very shortly I'm flying to Bali to catch up with Ringo and the team there (AW-Advantage.com).. news next week from there.
Hope you are coming along for the ride.. it's going to be such an exciting year..

Take care, 

David

title: Beer and Pearls in the South Seas
content_html:
Greetings from Labuan Bajo, Flores Islands.

Paradise wouldn't be a bad description of this place. We arrived via a one hour Airasia flight from Bali and a short taxi ride from the spanking new airport to the bustling port town of Labuan Bajo.
Last week I was telling you of our trip to East Java and the textile factory in the friendly city of Solo, if you missed you can catch up here.


First view of Labuan Bajo

My wife and I are on holiday.. yes actually. Regular readers will know that Coco was in China the last 30 months trapped by covid restrictions. At great expense and some difficulty we managed to find a way out of China for her on a business trip.. which it actually also is. But after sorting the business in Bali and Java we thought we might escape for a few days to see the Komodo dragons on Komodo island a day or so boat ride from here.
Most people come for this reason, they stay in town for a day or two and then head off on a two or three night trip aboard one of the many yachts or house boats floating in the harbour. I tried to book online but the price and the quality on offer from basic to uber-lux was confusing to say the least. A friend in Ubud told us it was easy to find on harbourside and you can check out the boats also.

But as we arrived at our portside hotel, we found that a G20 side-meeting had just concluded, the President himself had been here the day before. Our hotel was full of political types.. now of course all looking to take advantage of the visit and charter a boat.. so it wasn't so easy. Coronavirus lockdowns had killed off half the fleet of boats, you can sadly see many abandoned boats in the bay. Plus the local government had announced that the one day ticket to visit Komodo national park was going to be hiked from $15 to $250 on the 1st August. So also a mad rush to beat the increase.

So we decided to extend our trip a bit to discover the Labuan Bajo area slowly and have a chance to find a berth on a boat. 
Flores Islands were colonised at one time by the Portuguese.. and if you have been to Goa in India, there are shades of that feeling here, tropical white washed Churches in the jungle, friendly people with Christian names like Ferdinando or Harry.  I mistakenly thought we might be able to explore the island, but it's much bigger than Bali, and doesn't have good roads so getting around can take days not hours. 2 million people live on the island mostly in farming or fishing villages. They tell me there are 30 local languages just on this island. 


So in the meantime we made friends with a booking agent working out of a clapboard office by the port called Ferdinando who promised to work hard to find us a trip. He took us on a car trip around the area and  to a fishing village where we got a local fisherman to take us to a cave on a remote beach.  We went to view the available boats in the bay, but they were basically floating boxes smelling of fresh paint.. then on Sunday he called me and said there was a cancellation on a nice boat, if we could pay immediately we could secure the booking and have the boat just for us. We couldn't see it as it was not in port, but he assured me it was good (the pictures looked amazing). I sent him the money via Wise and immediately thought, OMG.. we have been conned.. he could just disappear with our money leaving us literally high and dry.
But good as his word on Monday morning Ferdinando was waiting in the lobby, he had said with a car to take us to the port where a launch would ferry us to the boat. Where is the car I asked? No need he said, your boat is here in front of the hotel. "I persuaded the captain to pick you up here"  he said with a grin as wide as his face.


It was love at first sight.

So that's how we ended up on a drop-dead beautiful boat with a crew of six for a ridiculous cheap price. We have never done this before, we are novice sailors.. but that's how we spent three days sailing around the South Seas.
We did so many things it felt like a week or more.. turtle spotting, snorkeling on empty beaches, watching the hundred thousand flying foxes on a dusk migration fly over the boat.. that was amazing. Shore trips to various islands, we had adventures before breakfast and much more. The crew were delightful and included a guide called Harry. I asked Harry if the crew were allowed to drink beer in the evening? Absolutely he said but we have no beer and we are a days sailing away from port. But we asked the captain anyway if we could buy beer anywhere.. There is a fishing village on Rina island we can call at and ask.. the crew were delighted and excited. 
The village was a Muslim one so the small local portside shop said no immeadiately, but suggested we ask in the village. The captain soon located the local beer runner, in a small very basic shack he seated us in plush chairs to begin negotiations, but his price was OK not much more than the supermarket, so we bought all his stock at asking price and the crew cheerfully carried it back to the boat.  


 Here's Harry with the beer guy and his stock. 


Back to the boat.

On the way back in the village we passed an old lady who had spread some local handicraft items on a trestle table, Coco spotted a pearl necklace. We asked if it was local, yes made here.. 
In Bali they sell these - I had seen for about £100 the lady was clearly delighted when we accepted her price of £10.. 
That night we had a party with the crew under the stars.. but my mind was thinking about the pearls...

The next day the captain took us to a famous pearl farm, owned by a large Australian company. It had been closed because of covid and not yet functioning, but the manager met us and suggested we meet his boss in Denpasar.
Back in port I asked Ferdinando if he knew any local family pearl businesses (more our style).. yes of course he does..

It's Friday midday now and in 20 minutes we are off to meet them.. he has five local people lined up to see, he will drive us around to meet them.
Yes I know we are supposed to be on holiday.. but this is just so much more fun.
We have to go..

It's almost August..can you believe, soon it will be September and almost Christmas.
And it seems to be getting busy already.. I have seen the first orders coming for Orange and Cinnamon candles.

Take care and more news next week.
Let's see what happens.. full report next week.

David

We went to view the available boats in the bay, but they were basically floating boxes smelling of fresh paint.. then on Sunday he called me and said there was a cancellation on a nice boat, if we could pay immediately we could secure the booking and have the boat just for us. We couldn't see it as it was not in port, but he assured me it was good (the pictures looked amazing). I sent him the money via Wise and immediately thought, OMG.. we have been conned.. he could just disappear with our money leaving us literally high and dry. But good as his word on Monday morning Ferdinando was waiting in the lobby, he had said with a car to take us to the port where a launch would ferry us to the boat. Where is the car I asked? No need he said, your boat is here in front of the hotel. "I persuaded the captain to pick you up here" he said with a grin as wide as his face. It was love at first sight. So that's how we ended up on a drop-dead beautiful boat with a crew of six for a ridiculous cheap price. We have never done this before, we are novice sailors.. but that's how we spent three days sailing around the South Seas. We did so many things it felt like a week or more.. turtle spotting, snorkeling on empty beaches, watching the hundred thousand flying foxes on a dusk migration fly over the boat.. that was amazing. Shore trips to various islands, we had adventures before breakfast and much more. The crew were delightful and included a guide called Harry. I asked Harry if the crew were allowed to drink beer in the evening? Absolutely he said but we have no beer and we are a days sailing away from port. But we asked the captain anyway if we could buy beer anywhere.. There is a fishing village on Rina island we can call at and ask.. the crew were delighted and excited. The village was a Muslim one so the small local portside shop said no immeadiately, but suggested we ask in the village. The captain soon located the local beer runner, in a small very basic shack he seated us in plush chairs to begin negotiations, but his price was OK not much more than the supermarket, so we bought all his stock at asking price and the crew cheerfully carried it back to the boat. Here's Harry with the beer guy and his stock. Back to the boat. On the way back in the village we passed an old lady who had spread some local handicraft items on a trestle table, Coco spotted a pearl necklace. We asked if it was local, yes made here.. In Bali they sell these - I had seen for about £100 the lady was clearly delighted when we accepted her price of £10.. That night we had a party with the crew under the stars.. but my mind was thinking about the pearls... The next day the captain took us to a famous pearl farm, owned by a large Australian company. It had been closed because of covid and not yet functioning, but the manager met us and suggested we meet his boss in Denpasar. Back in port I asked Ferdinando if he knew any local family pearl businesses (more our style).. yes of course he does.. It's Friday midday now and in 20 minutes we are off to meet them.. he has five local people lined up to see, he will drive us around to meet them. Yes I know we are supposed to be on holiday.. but this is just so much more fun. We have to go.. It's almost August..can you believe, soon it will be September and almost Christmas. And it seems to be getting busy already.. I have seen the first orders coming for Orange and Cinnamon candles. Take care and more news next week. Let's see what happens.. full report next week. David

title: Toni has a drink problem..
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Sheffield.

 

It's all go, lots of things are happening. As I write two (long lost) containers from Indonesia are arriving, and the guys are putting up a sign in the warehouse.

That sign has history.. (more below).

Last week I was telling you about the time I went to the wild west woodwork town of Saharanpur in Northern India.. you can read about it here.

Hope you had a good bank holiday.. and now the weather is looking good, that should hopefully help the giftshops in destination locations.. 

And with Father's Day almost upon - now is the time to market the Dad Gifts..

Dad Gifts are always a bit tricky to source although I feel in recent years there are more really good wholesalers producing better and cooler gifts for Dad's everywhere.. At AW we got you covered.. and plus this weekend to give you an helping hand we got FREE (or if you live in the sticks discounted) Shipping. 

 

Brits I read, spend over £20 billion a year whilst on foreign holidays.. that's a lot of jugs of Sangria or Italian Pasta or Greek plate smashing.. The Green List is a joke list. Of the countries on the Green list.. only two are actual letting us in - down to one - Gibraltar - from Tuesday.. and the Rock is a nice place but hardly room to swing a cat.

I mean why even put Australia on the Green list? - you can't go anyway.. When everyone vulnerable has been jabbed or double jabbed, when those countries such as Greece or Spain are delighted to have us.. something doesn't stack up in my mind. 

But when Brexit is punching a big hole in country balance sheet (that can't all be blamed on covid), why not divert some of that £20 billion to UK shores? Wow.. It's a cunning plan.. but Boris just throw the poor travel agents and airline industries under the bus to do it.

Sorry - I'm doing it again.. Ranting on a Friday.. Must try to look on the bright side.. at least it will be good for the holiday retail trade and give our hotels a much needed boost.  

 

Meanwhile at AW Spain a long term project has just come to fruition.. and it's totally a new and refreshing direction for AW.. Toni our man in Spain and his designer helper Graciela have been putting there heart and soul into it and have been drinking rather a lot recently. Actually while I was in Spain - I also was drinking rather too much.. and the fruit of all that supping has finally made it online..

 

It's not what you think...


It was a long time ago that Tomas first floated the idea.. after seeing a busy shop in Bratislava town centre, selling herbal tea as if it was aromatherapy.. you know tea to help you sleep, a tea blend that's good for stress, tea as a slimming aid.. And all the tea pots, strainers and cups to go with it. Tea is imported from China, India, Sri Lanka and Morocco into Spain and then blended with local flavours to create herbal blends.. so we have been working closely with a company based in Malaga to make our range of Herbal Teas we call AW Artisan Tea..  Check it out here.. (WARNING - DO NOT ORDER IT)..   Normally (before Brexit) it would already be in shipped to the UK and online ready for you.. these days supply lines are massively more complicated.. But it is on the way hopefully in a few weeks we can have it online in the UK.  I really believe this could be a huge gift retail opportunity - gift packs and hampers, a whole new department in your store.. and importantly... bringing repeat customers back into our store (or website) for refills.

 

The sign.. that sign now hanging at the end of our warehouse - was on the warehouse that we lost in a fire last July.. regular readers will know the story.. We lost everything except the sign and the Buddha..  our name (the sign) and our values represented by the Buddha. Now the Buddha sits at the entrance to Affinity Park welcoming everyone and the sign above us as we work.. . 



Another thing that is happening is a new department I'll tell you more later.. But if you need storage space for pallets of goods at a reasonable price we can help, soon we can even distribute your products.

Check out: AW-Fulfilment.co.uk 

 

So have a great weekend, happy (and safe) trading. 

 

David

 

PS:

Ash, our new guy in the Marketing Dept is breathing new life into our social media.. Join us on Instagram and

Facebook and let us know what you like, what you want..  give us feedback and ideas..

title: David's AW News: 80 in Indonesia and other amazing things
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


Last week I was telling you about my trip from Spain to Kuala Lumpur - not without Drama.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
I spent the weekend in KL, one of my favourite cities in the world, and then on Sunday afternoon took a Batik Air flight from KL International airport to Denpasar, Bali. 
Very smooth flight, about three hours, and very smooth through the airport. Batik arrivals stand is the one next to the arrival hall. Because I have investor status in Bali I get to use the VIP passport channel. Which I enjoy, yes ok I know maybe shallow and childish but so nice to skip the lines. I have to speak Indonesian, because they assume I can (actually not very well at all), but I wing it and like this I'm off the plane and in the luggage area in 3 minutes.. grab my priority luggage and to customs control..   here's a tip you can fill the form and get a QR code before you fly.. customs is just a scanned code and you're outside in a jiffy.  I have Denpasar airport down to a fine art.. and Bondhan is waiting outside to greet me.
We drive from the airport across the dramatic bridge across the bay to Denpasar city.. if you are very lucky you can see Mount Agung which is on the other side of the island but here seems to rise out of the sea in the evening light. A took a picture from the car window.  A nice welcome to Indonesia on their 80th Birthday.. more details below.


 

Mount Agung.. (ok I admit it I AI enhanced it a smidgen.. haha but just so you get the vibe better)
 
Happy Independence Day
So here I am arriving on Independence Day in Indonesia. 80 years so it is a bigger than ever celebration. Every company in Indonesia does some kind of celebration, Red & White flags are everywhere and this massively diverse land is united in celebration. I'm happy to be here at this moment in history.

Indonesia X factor
AW-Advantage our digital marketing off-shoot is no exception and Debbie our manager has organised an X Factor style talent show for the staff. Before work at 9am  I'm given the honor of being a judge.. Everyone has made a huge effort.. dressed in regional costumes.. they each give a little speech about the culture of the region or island of Indonesia they are dressed up in.  I genuinely learn so much from these guys.  For example I never knew that North Sumatra has a large Christian community with a uniquely developed set of traditions, dances and costumes etc merging Christian and ancient Sumatran elements.    The Batak people have an ancient and developed culture unique in the world like Bali culture is unique.. I really have to visit.


The guy on the left: Edo is wearing the Batak traditional dress. As with all the costumes every element of the dress holds a particular cultural or spiritual meaning.. these guys explained all this to me.. I learnt so much.


 

This is Vika in a Papua costume - one of our super bright developers.  He did a monologue, a dance, a dramatic makeup change and ended with firecrackers.. so he won the competition. Well done Vika!

Ok so young educated Indonesians are super social and super bright.. and our team seems to be more so. I have discussed this before.. Indonesia is an unlikely country.. made up of hugely different ethnicity, religions, traditions, languages - The original multicultural society and yet people in main get on amazingly together proud of each other's cultures.

I have only been here a few days and lots happening.. managed to see one or two suppliers.. will report more next week.

Coco is crazy hot.
Meanwhile the heat bomb in Spain they tell me is subsiding, but Coco in China tells me she has never in her life experienced such a prolonged heat wave. The candle factory really cannot operate, the warehouse is too hot to work in the day. Outside they have hit 45c.. she tells me you cannot go outside like that. 
But she also told me the notebook and journals that we ordered on the last trip finally arrived in the warehouse. Sandra, our designer in the UK has worked long hours on the journals making something truly (I think)awesome - and the dream journals.. fluffy books to write down your dreams in.. gonna be awesome.


 

Here's a sneak preview.. coming soon.

Also from China we have some Ancient (Chinese) Wisdom.. Excited to see these cultural Feng Shui pieces. 
They are beautiful and detailed, full of moving parts with masses of meaning. Take a picture and ask ChatGBT to explain each piece has a story to tell.
When Tomas and I found them we just had to get them for Ancient Wisdom. 



 More details here
Meanwhile in the UK.. Holly has been busy this week.
And following on from Interviewing the designer Emily of the award winning designer of the Crystal Elemental Soaps. She went along to see Audrey, one of our amazing artisans at AW-Aromatics, actually making those soaps and other soaps as well.   Behind the Scenes look at artisan soap production.. 

 
Check it out here.. (say Hi to Audrey in the comments)

Selenite is Magic...
Holly also gets enthusiastic about Selenite.. and with good reason.. Selenite is a bit weird and wonderful. You probably know we import from a guy with an amazing artisan business in a small town under the Atlas mountains in Morocco.. 
 

Holly talks Selenite all the details..  Check it out here.


Meanwhile..
In the UK so much new stock is arriving.. there is too much to tell you about! 
Indonesian and Chinese.. Check out the beautiful minimalist lamps here... sure to be a bestseller. 
See other NEW stock here...
Plus BH Weekend deals galore.. 

Take and enjoy the Bank holiday weekend.. 

David

title: Plan B & Some Good News
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield.

Day 21 of the road back to recovery and resurgence.

This new normal is anything but normal for me. The view from my office window is like something from one of those end of the world movies. Block B.. burned out and still crumbling down. Every now and then something comes crashing down.
It's painful to see, it looks like the biggest monster of a problem any company could face - a massive insurmountable problem. And yet, and yet the team here at AW are really sleighing that monster.
Last week I was telling you about my very strange journey from Indonesia to the UK.. you can read about it here.

We were basically closed for one week, by day 7 we had a dispatch and CS departments running, by day 14 production restarted.  Kane (our big guy) goods in manager, and James (our hardest worker) warehouse manager - have motivated and led their teams, working 12 hour days to make this very tight space work, night shifts and long hours. Everyone is pulling together!


We have containers arriving all the time, a China one just came.. with new products. It's now day 21 and we are adding more products every day. 

I have been investigating our future warehouse.. and seen some big beautiful sheds. But doing a deal will take time, and all the legals and paperwork.. well just a bit hard work.

So we have two plans.. Plan A and Plan B.. both involve expanding our production department in the three units we have here.. 
Plan A - is to find a really big place that can last us the next ten years, and think big and bold. And move PDQ. We have found three potential places.. but the numbers are huge and Brexit looms, while COVID rumbles on..
Plan B - is to find a temporary home, we have a couple of options.. and let our lovely landlord (Keith) re-create block B as big as possible.. there is the possibility to buy some extra land behind. We could be back within 12 to 18 months.. 
It's hard to plan, because 21 days after the event the insurance company still didn't brief us. Some big guy in London is still deciding..

Improving the view..
Looking out of the window is painful.. but soon the demolition company are going to take it all away for scrap.. this will make me feel better :)  and we should have a different view down the valley.
Our new warehouse I feel should have offices with a nice view.. it's high our criteria ..

We sent the money raised on GoFundme.. to Mr Chatterjee.. in India. It's probable enough to provide 5000 meals. Thank you.
Mr Chatterjee has been feeding people in his home town area.. thousands of meals. He tells me that the situation in India is really bad. Random lock-downs, panicking officials, poor people unable to find doctors.  His factory is working - under super high safety standards at least providing some employment. But only alternate days, as the local government thinks this is a good idea. 
The good news is that one of the children in the children's home we support came top of the class in exams. As we supply English, art and computer teachers.. it's an amazing and satisfying result.
No orphan has ever had such a good result. The news even made the Kolkatta news. Mr Chatterjee went to the home to personally congratulate him.

    

It's a bit of good news.. in difficult times.

You can still support the good work of Mr Chatterjee.. here: GoFundMe.

Meanwhile, back in Sheffield, we are working round the clock (yes actually) to ship your orders. I want to say thank you for supporting us.. and gradually we are catching up with the orders.
Lots of new products arrived.. see below.
Aromatherapy products are quickly coming back online.. some fragrance oils.. and some beautiful new candles.

Stay safe, have a good weekend.
Wear a mask!!

David

title: Duplicity at Ancient Wisdom
content_html:
What does it mean?

Thanks for the all the suggestions and interest in our forthcoming Lavender project in last weeks newsletter.
As Valentines day approaches (or as they call it in India V-Day) of course things are pretty busy at AW, but it's not too late to grab some stock and (honestly) we have some pretty good deals that will really your boost sales. See below..

Meanwhile I have been getting a little philosophical recently.
I was thinking about business and Yin & Yang. I used to think of Yin & Yang as a kind of opposites mentality.. light & dark, good & evil. But the Chinese understanding is more complex, it's actually about being two opposing things at the same time. A state of conflict and balance. It seems to me that in business you have to be often two things at once. Here are some examples:

Be very generous and jolly mean simultaneously.
You have to blindly trust yet keep a wary eye.
You must always think big but pay attention to details.
Take huge gambles and yet minimise risk.

Is it this ability to apparently do two conflicting things that is a key secret of success? After all the human brain is really two brains left and right each capable of different processes.
Left is logical, detailed reality based and cautious.  The Right side is where the imagination and mystical things reside, it also risk taking. We humans are actually constructed in a Yin & Yang way.

Well a glance at ancient wisdom (not us, the real thing) will find lots of such sage advice. For one all the Yin & Yang philosophy is built around these ideas. In the bible Paul talks about been as innocent as a dove but crafty as a snake.
In Confucianism the Earth is the ultimate yin object. Heaven is the ultimate yang object. They have to be mixed to work... all philosophy and religions have to deal with duality it's a common theme in any culture.

So all those nice arty gift items using the Yin & Yang symbol as inspiration have more to them than meets the eye.
Is it any wonder that the Yin & Yang makes such a popular gift theme.. and like the idea for a Lavender themed shop or department in a shop maybe it would also work for Yin & Yang..

So that's my rambling for today..

Hope you have chance to use both your brains..

David

content_text: What does it mean? Thanks for the all the suggestions and interest in our forthcoming Lavender project in last weeks newsletter. As Valentines day approaches (or as they call it in India V-Day) of course things are pretty busy at AW, but it's not too late to grab some stock and (honestly) we have some pretty good deals that will really your boost sales. See below.. Meanwhile I have been getting a little philosophical recently. I was thinking about business and Yin & Yang. I used to think of Yin & Yang as a kind of opposites mentality.. light & dark, good & evil. But the Chinese understanding is more complex, it's actually about being two opposing things at the same time. A state of conflict and balance. It seems to me that in business you have to be often two things at once. Here are some examples: Be very generous and jolly mean simultaneously. You have to blindly trust yet keep a wary eye. You must always think big but pay attention to details. Take huge gambles and yet minimise risk. Is it this ability to apparently do two conflicting things that is a key secret of success? After all the human brain is really two brains left and right each capable of different processes. Left is logical, detailed reality based and cautious. The Right side is where the imagination and mystical things reside, it also risk taking. We humans are actually constructed in a Yin & Yang way. Well a glance at ancient wisdom (not us, the real thing) will find lots of such sage advice. For one all the Yin & Yang philosophy is built around these ideas. In the bible Paul talks about been as innocent as a dove but crafty as a snake. In Confucianism the Earth is the ultimate yin object. Heaven is the ultimate yang object. They have to be mixed to work... all philosophy and religions have to deal with duality it's a common theme in any culture. So all those nice arty gift items using the Yin & Yang symbol as inspiration have more to them than meets the eye. Is it any wonder that the Yin & Yang makes such a popular gift theme.. and like the idea for a Lavender themed shop or department in a shop maybe it would also work for Yin & Yang.. So that's my rambling for today.. Hope you have chance to use both your brains.. David www.AncientWisdom.biz

title: A Strange Night in Guangzhou… and a Warm Welcome in Kathmandu.
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu,

A Strange Night in Guangzhou… and a Warm Welcome in Kathmandu. 

Last week I was in Yiwu, China. This week, Nepal. If you missed the Yiwu update, you can catch up here

My newsletter has a slightly different format this week; it's a cautionary tale.. 

Sandra and Bryant (who were in China with me) are safely back in the UK, while I took a China Southern afternoon flight down to Guangzhou, planning to connect on to Kathmandu. Except (again)… my onward flight had been cancelled and replaced with an early morning departure the next day.

No great problem, I thought. I remembered there was a rather nice five-star hotel somewhere in the airport complex. Oddly, I couldn’t find it on Trip.com. Expedia, however, showed me a hotel just eight minutes’ walk from the terminal. The room photos looked familiar. I even found the location on Google Maps. That must be the place.. 



Then came the first warning sign: the price. Seventy-five percent off. About £16. Too good to be true? Almost certainly. Did I book it anyway? Of course I did.

So off I went, wheeling my suitcase through the humid Guangzhou night, looking for this bargain luxury airport hotel. Only… there was no hotel.

I checked and rechecked. Nothing. So I went to an enquiry desk at the airport entrance, where a very helpful young lady took pity on me. She called the hotel, spoke to them, and told me not to walk there at all — apparently, I needed a hotel transfer. She gave me the vehicle registration and said it would arrive in a few minutes.

I waited at the pickup point.

And waited.

Lots of vehicles came and went. Not mine. By now it was getting close to midnight, hot, sticky, and I was starting to feel a bit stressed. So I called the hotel myself and attempted, in truly dreadful Chinese, to explain that I was still standing there and beginning to doubt the whole arrangement. The girl on the other end, calm and patient, told me I was at the wrong pickup point and needed to go elsewhere.

Eventually, I found the vehicle. It was not, let us say, a gleaming hotel limousine.

More an elderly van with hard bench seats. In the front sat a man in a hoodie, hunched over, and the driver had the kind of mafia tatooed look that does not immediately inspire confidence in a tired traveller after midnight.

Now, Guangzhou always had a bit of a reputation years ago. I remember the old days when taxi drivers sat in protective cages and hotels advised you not to wander out late at night. Surely those days had passed, I told myself. Still, as we drove away from the airport — and not in the direction shown on my Google map — I did begin to wonder.

“Maybe eight minutes by car,” I thought.

I leaned forward and attempted to ask the driver how long it would take. He responded by turning the radio volume up to full blast.

Not ideal.

Thirty minutes later we were still driving, now through what looked like a distinctly less polished part of town, and I began to think that perhaps my bargain hotel booking had not been the masterstroke I had imagined. Mugging? Scam? Organ trade? One does wonder where the mind goes at that time of night.

Then suddenly, relief.

We pulled up outside a building that looked exactly like the one in the Expedia photos.

I got out, collected my luggage, and stepped into a brightly lit lobby with modern décor and rather arty furniture. Behind the desk stood five young women in a neat row, all smiling, giggling, and operating with extraordinary speed despite patchy English between us. One handed me green tea in a paper cup. Another scanned my passport. Another made the room card. Another checked my flight time so the return transit van could be organised.

Within moments I was in the lift and on my way upstairs.

Now the room…

Large. Bright. Slightly surreal.

There were no normal light switches, only motion-sensor lights. A huge bed. An oversized chaise longue. A yoga mat. A set of weights in the corner. The shower room appeared to double as a karaoke room. At this point I did begin to suspect I had not checked into a standard airport business hotel.

And on the back of the door was a rather alarming police notice, sternly warning about secret filming, privacy violations, hidden cameras, indecent material, and various associated criminal penalties.



Haha, you can google translate the picture text, strange and unsettling.

 At one in the morning, with a 5.30 wake-up looming, this was not especially soothing reading.

Still, sleep was needed.

Unfortunately, outside the window there was thumping music, and after a while I realised I was also being eaten alive by mosquitoes. So it was not exactly a restful night. But at 5.32am the bedside phone rang: the transit bus was waiting. Downstairs they handed me a packed breakfast, bundled me back into transport, and delivered me to the airport.

And do you know what? In its own strange way, it wasn’t too bad.

Yes, I had clearly been lured in by a misleading booking. But for about £17 I got a bed, two transfers, a bizarre room, a memorable story, and breakfast. 

This is China.

From there I took the early China Southern flight to Kathmandu.

And what a contrast on arrival.

The hotel here had sent a car for me, but everything moved in a completely different rhythm. Not brutally efficient, as in China, but softer, warmer, more human. The luggage belt had broken down and apparently no one was available to fix it. In practical terms, less efficient. But somehow nobody seemed panicked. The driver was delightful, the hotel staff were wonderful — “Welcome back, Mr David” — and within moments I felt something I always seem to feel in Nepal. 

Relief. Warmth. A kind of gentle embrace.

Then Mr Padam, our shipping agent, invited me to his niece’s wedding the very next day, which was a lovely reminder of how personal and generous business relationships can be here. 

The wedding was in a posh part of the city in a White House copy building.. It was amazing. Most ladies wore red and looked stunning, the groom's side all sported red scarves. The wedding is a full day starting at 8.30am and ending late. It involves a rolling series of mini-ceremonies and rituals, plus endless catering (and, refreshingly, no alcohol). Fortunately, other than close family, the guests come and go as they wished. We stayed for a couple of hours enjoying meeting all types of people and eating from the huge buffet that had just opened. 

Then the time came when we (Raul from KL is here with me) were ushered in front of the happy couple. (I know the bride a little; she helps at the shipping agency.) We wish them well in their future life, photos op, then hand over our red envelopes (interestingly, these must go to the bride), and our job is done; we are free to leave. 




So after the hard edges, bright lights and strange adventures of transit China, it feels very good indeed to be back in Nepal.

Meanwhile, back in the UK, we have so much new stock arriving, including new stock from Nepal and India. Check out the deals below.. 

More news next week.

Namaste 

David

title: Healthy/Unhealthy Competition?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


August is over, now the month of September unfolds, who knows what will happen.
Last week I was telling you about a fraud alert and how Ringo (our man in Indonesia loaded) two 40ft containers in one night, working through the night because of the heat.
If you missed it you can read about it here.
Coco (our girl in China) doesn't like to be beaten..
Tomas is here in Spain! He is officially on holiday.. but nothing could stop him from visiting our Spain company (AW Artisan) and connecting face to face with the team. Of course he connects every day online, but actual  bonding matters. We went for dinner last night.. and invited anyone in the company who wanted to to join us after work.. Only slightly surprisingly... Everyone made it.. in honor of Tomas I guess. They like parties in Spain. Anyway we had to celebrate a record month, and targets smashed.

     Tomas on the left and Toni (Spain manager) on the right. 

Tomas is the main man at our Slovak company, so as you can imagine there is a lot of healthy competition between the two teams and Tony and Tomas.. but in a good hearted way. 

You have probably read about the supply chain problems, in India, China and Indonesia there is a huge shortage of containers. In the trade jargon they call it "Equipment" - for reasons that are beyond me all the containers in the world have ended up in the wrong spots at the wrong times, not enough equipment, not enough slots on ships, not enough drivers.. resulting in massive price hikes for the capacity that is available. Why is it taking so long to sort this out? The latest news from shipping companies is that rates are expected to keep rising.
 
I think something deeply dodgy could be going on.. the world's shipping is in the hands of only about four or five mega companies..

1 Maersk Line with 708 ships - based in Denmark and basically the countries biggest company and tax payer
2 Mediterranean Shipping Company with 589 ships - privately owned family controlled Swiss company. Secretive?
3 CMA CGM with 566 ships French owned with plenty of allegedly dodgy dealing in the past and is run by a family with Lebanese and Syrian origin. (google search)
4 COSCO with 498 ships, it is also known as: China Ocean Shipping Company, and ultimately (most likely) controlled by the CCP.

My friend Alan is Danish and owns a few shares in Maersk, if the rumors around Copenhagen are correct they are making obscene amounts of money and struggling to invest/hide the loot. Shares have increased over 100% recently.. but do the maths..
If the old price of shipping containers was about €650 (this is what the shipping part of the costs was) and they could make a profit on this.. imagine their profit margin when they can charge €12,000 per container.
These companies control more than half of all container capacity and practically all of the East / West routes. Is it possible that normal competitive markets are broken?
One hopes that healthy competition will normalize the market soon, or else governments will step in to do something, because ultimately we all pay these increased costs.

Anyway we had been fighting for weeks to even secure containers, when strangely all of a sudden we were able to book what we wanted.. hence Ringo loading two in one night and more the following nights.
Coco was offered four containers.. if she could load them the same day. All a bit feast or famine.
We have a small warehouse in Yiwu, China which can just about hold four containers of stock at a push.. so things were desperate stock loaded to the rafters.
It's a lot of work, admin, checking, decision making, packing list and invoices with all the paperworks have to be put together on the same day.. 


Coco called me excited and exhausted after an epic day. She sent me lots of pictures.. an all time record for container loading at AW.  and maybe she was just a bit pleased to beat Ringo :)
That's healthy competition..
Hopefully the stock will be in the UK in four or five weeks in time for Christmas.. but only just..

We are working hard to bring you supplies, and not just from China.. shipments on the way from India and Nepal also.. plus we are working hard to produce new and exciting products from the UK aromatics factory.

We are far from perfect at AW - we are often behind with orders, often out of stock, sometimes things go wrong, but at the end of the day we love gifts (and our customers) and try our best to be authentic.
But the tradeshow is back on in Birmingham.. exciting to see life getting back to normal. Regular readers will know that we don't exhibit at trade shows, but if you have the chance you should go, many very good companies will be there including our good friends Puckator and Something Different. In a trade show all those companies head to head should provide you with some healthy competition.
AW doesn't have sales people or do trade shows, so maybe you have to work a little harder to place an order, but I believe you will see the difference in your bottom line...

Take care, have a nice weekend whatever you do, and don't forget to be kind to someone.


David
