title: Finally good news
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


But next week (if nothing changes) I will be on the way to Indonesia - finally! 

Last week I was telling you about all the things going on at AW - it's a hive of activity right now. If you missed it you can catch up here.
In the UK everything seems to be going pear-shaped.. Fuel running out, no turkey for Christmas, electric companies falling like flies, everyone is catching strange colds but things could be looking up..
 
Certainly inflation is creeping up - whatever the government & MSM seem to tell us.. shortages and price rises are the subject of every other email I open, and it's virtually impossible to place a reorder without a supplier requesting (or demanding) price rises.
Shipping costs remain high, and packaging costs are skyrocketing. In China they are having trouble generating enough electricity.. Coco tells me that our Candle Factory only gets electric four days a week and that most factories we work with have the same problem, so re-orders are now coming much slower.

All these problems, so much doom and gloom and yet.. 

... and yet.. somehow where there is a will there's a way. And come what may - life goes on. Love makes the world go round (when nothing else works) and giving a reasonably priced gift is an act of love.. I would argue that in these times a gift is an essential item.
maybe not, but anyway we are - in spite of everything - managing to keep a good supply of gifts coming your way. Bryant, our head of ordering, tells me we have more open PO's than ever and lots of containers on the way. But he tells me we need a lot more from Indonesia, stock is coming far too slowly.

But good news is coming, visa restrictions and travel restrictions are being relaxed the world over. I really think soon I can see Coco, my wife. Even Australia just announced the opening of international borders.

More good news.. 
It's Rodrigo's (our marketing man in the UK) 7th Birthday.. 


Yes really - at AW we try to remember birthdays..  And today is Rodrigo 7th anniversary of starting work at AW.. how time flies and how much has happened in that time!
And even more good news: Halloween is on the way to cheer us up!!  Yes it's October guys.. and to prove it we have just launched a limited edition..  Halloween Bathbomb range.. see below..

Soon I will be on the way to Indonesia, after quarantine in Jakarta, next stop will be Bali. We have a 2000 square meter warehouse there. Why do we need our own warehouse? Well the artisans of Bali are not really geared to packing their products in boxes, putting a barcode on it and then packing them in a master carton. Traditionally this has been done by local Cargo Companies who charge per cubic meter to do the packing job. But not only is this very expensive, but you can only get standard packaging and quality control is not seen as part of the job. So early on we worked out that we could "take back control" (to borrow a phrase) with our own cargo warehouse, and only needed to ship about six containers a year to cover the cost of the staff and warehouse compared to Cargo Company rates. We started in a small warehouse in Ubud about ten years ago, moved to a larger warehouse nearby after three years and then realised we needed much bigger so about three years ago took over a rather dilapidated warehouse that had previously been the Coca Cola depot for the island.  We made it nice - regular readers will know the story.. 

Ringo, our agent in Indonesia runs the place, and under his calm and capable direction we have made a nice place to work and equipped an office, In the office we have a meeting area to connect with artisan suppliers, a small photo studio and mini showroom.
Our initial motivation was to streamline the packaging and despatch, but making a nice office/hub has had many more benefits than I had anticipated. Artisans drop in with new samples, they collaborate - ideas are born - improvements made. 
I love to go out and meet new suppliers and visit the old ones, but most stock arrives at the warehouse on the back of small pickup trucks driven by the boss. So spend a day at the warehouse you get to meet face to face more artisans than buzzing all over the island.


Ringo and the warehouse, the pot garden by the offices..

In the UK at our Affinity Park site - The HQ of AW.. we made new offices also. Tomas has been working on it.. one idea he had was to create a zone of the office as a kind of homage to that place in Bali. It's just finished...


My mission in Bali is to find a way to inspire the artisans to scale up - to think big. The pandemic has destroyed much of the tourist economy, and the handicraft sector has been a bit of a life-line as companies like AW have continued to order. But many artisans don't think beyond small family only business - the idea of renting a decent workshop and employing staff is just too daunting. I'm thinking of helping with funding and have a mentor/training program running. Some way to increase speed and volumes of goods produced - which would be a win/win - employing more workers, increasing prosperity. The people of Bali are amazingly creative, easy to work with, hard working and honest. But thinking big is not on the menu. 

If you have any ideas - do let me know.
I'm beyond excited to be going back to Bali.. hope you can join me in spirit via this newsletter.

Take care - be kind to someone.. more news next week.

David

Soon I will be on the way to Indonesia, after quarantine in Jakarta, next stop will be Bali. We have a 2000 square meter warehouse there. Why do we need our own warehouse? Well the artisans of Bali are not really geared to packing their products in boxes, putting a barcode on it and then packing them in a master carton. Traditionally this has been done by local Cargo Companies who charge per cubic meter to do the packing job. But not only is this very expensive, but you can only get standard packaging and quality control is not seen as part of the job. So early on we worked out that we could "take back control" (to borrow a phrase) with our own cargo warehouse, and only needed to ship about six containers a year to cover the cost of the staff and warehouse compared to Cargo Company rates. We started in a small warehouse in Ubud about ten years ago, moved to a larger warehouse nearby after three years and then realised we needed much bigger so about three years ago took over a rather dilapidated warehouse that had previously been the Coca Cola depot for the island. We made it nice - regular readers will know the story.. Ringo, our agent in Indonesia runs the place, and under his calm and capable direction we have made a nice place to work and equipped an office, In the office we have a meeting area to connect with artisan suppliers, a small photo studio and mini showroom. Our initial motivation was to streamline the packaging and despatch, but making a nice office/hub has had many more benefits than I had anticipated. Artisans drop in with new samples, they collaborate - ideas are born - improvements made. I love to go out and meet new suppliers and visit the old ones, but most stock arrives at the warehouse on the back of small pickup trucks driven by the boss. So spend a day at the warehouse you get to meet face to face more artisans than buzzing all over the island. Ringo and the warehouse, the pot garden by the offices.. In the UK at our Affinity Park site - The HQ of AW.. we made new offices also. Tomas has been working on it.. one idea he had was to create a zone of the office as a kind of homage to that place in Bali. It's just finished... My mission in Bali is to find a way to inspire the artisans to scale up - to think big. The pandemic has destroyed much of the tourist economy, and the handicraft sector has been a bit of a life-line as companies like AW have continued to order. But many artisans don't think beyond small family only business - the idea of renting a decent workshop and employing staff is just too daunting. I'm thinking of helping with funding and have a mentor/training program running. Some way to increase speed and volumes of goods produced - which would be a win/win - employing more workers, increasing prosperity. The people of Bali are amazingly creative, easy to work with, hard working and honest. But thinking big is not on the menu. If you have any ideas - do let me know. I'm beyond excited to be going back to Bali.. hope you can join me in spirit via this newsletter. Take care - be kind to someone.. more news next week. David

title: China 70th birthday
content_html:
Greetings from Hangzhou airport, just waiting to board a flight to KL with Tomas.

It's been a crazy few days, rushing around Yiwu finalising deals, checking samples pulling everything together.
Last week I was in Spain just leaving for China, it's a bit crazy right now.. I was telling everyone to just CALM DOWN! - You can read about it here.


So I took the flight from Malaga to Amsterdam..  I had booked with KLM, but my flight was very strange. It was an American plane, with staff from Florida and an American pilot - all the announcements were in American English with quotes from Federal law. The TV screens were broken, the plane rattled, some of the overheads came open on there own. Frankly a bit scary, why was an almost bankrupt airline flying me in Europe? We landed with a hell of a bump and screeched to a halt super fast causing .  As I got off the plane I heard the captain a Texan (I think) with a huge beer belly say to the hostess that was a hell of a flight - I was fighting that frigging crosswind all the way.  Why? What's going on.

I was happy to find the leg from Amsterdam to China was a proper KLM flight..

In China - had to hit the ground running - Tomas had already been there a few days and had things under control.. sort of.  I'd been there a few weeks ago and had lots of projects underway.. now we had to make it all happen. 
Working with Coco (our Agent in China) is amazing.. it always amazes me how much, and how quickly you can get things done.

It was China 70th birthday. A national holiday, so we thought everything would stop, but no.. Coco set up meetings and suppliers were happy to meet us even when everyone else was closed. 
No Plastic!!  No plastic is the plan, and now our Chinese suppliers are getting the message, we have been working hard on sourcing eco-friendly products.. I'm so excited at what we have coming..  but do calm down.. most will come after Christmas.

Yiwu is still hot, the city gets more trees and parks every-time I come.. and now even the grubby river area has been beautified.



But now it's on to KL, Malaysia. Regular readers will know that Raul (from Mexico) our IT wizard lives there, with his Malaysian wife; Alicia and his young daughter. He heads our small IT team from trendy offices in downtown KL - and I'm really looking forward to going over the latest developments - especially the up and coming new drop-shipping system. 

There is a neat IT update this week.. 
Dots appeared.. did you see, next to the product boxes, now we have a traffic light system in the websites to show you if we have good stock, in danger of running out or no stock. Red, amber & green dots.   

In the UK, it's crazy busy, but the guys are working wonders.. we still can't manage to ship next day but normal with this volume of orders we are slipping badly behind. But I can see the stats and we are keeping up.. pretty much. well done guys!
Brexit is looming.. it's seriously looming, not looking good. Shipping company's are quoting huge fee's for doing customs clearance.. so much that it will be impossible to do business. An average €300 order will cost so much that all the profit will be gone. So that's half our sales buggered. If there is a deal, will this still apply? No-one knows.. it's a shambles.. and only weeks to go. Boris makes jokes like a stand-up, tells people to think positive, accuses folk of being doomsters and gloomsters..  while my peoples jobs hang by a thread. I'm not seeing the funny side of those jokes.  Good job we have a plan.. but it's still not going to be a party.

OK our flight has been called, got to go.. 

More news next week.

David

title: Epic Days
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali. Last week I was telling you about traveling in East Java through the teak forests to find sustainable teak wood suppliers.
This week I met up with our Indonesian agent (Ringo) in Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia we were visiting two trade shows looking for suppliers. You can read it here.
Jakarta is a mega city, and I'm pretty sure there are twice as many skyscrapers than on my last visit about three years ago. But the roads are way behind the developments, it must be the worst traffic in Asia if not the world. You can really walk quicker than taking a taxi.
But the trade shows when we finally got to them were full of creativity, so much beautiful stuff. A lot of the worlds furniture is made in Indonesia, and the designers are world class. Of course the prices they want to charge at these shows are at a premium, especially the stands run by marketing companies. You might not believe this but I found plenty of products that we actually sell cheaper on our UK website, than in the show. However we found new suppliers in Bali I didn't know existed, and discovered the cities that specialise in different products. Also found lots and lots of ideas.
In the UK, you will by the time you read this have experienced an epic Solar Eclipse, and on the first day of Spring. The ancients would have read all sorts of wisdom and mysticism into that double occurrence. Here on the other side of the world it is Happy New Year.. or Isakawarsa - it is Balinese new year today. Ubud is the place to be for this.. but not the best timing for doing business, as pretty much everyone is ensconced in making the epic monsters that will troop round the streets tonight. Yesterday was the beach offering day for Ubud, whole villages piled into the back of trucks, set off in long convoys to the coast to make offerings on the beach, then later back to the village temples, bells clanging to make more offerings.



Tonight will be a riotous party in Ubud. There is massive competition to create the most amazing monsters. The creativity of local artisans is really let loose, and even though this is in essence a hindu religious ceremony, many images are sensual, some ribald and dare I say almost pornagraphic -much to the consternation of the many conservative Indian hindus who visit. There will be mock battles in the streets, later some monsters will be burned, the evil chased away for another year.

This is actually my personal third new year this year :) Once in Spain, of the regular sort, then Chinese New Year in China and now Bali New Year in Ubud.
But tomorrow is different, very different. It's called Nyepi or the Bali day of silence. I have been in Ubud once before for this.
Everything is quiet, peaceful. No cars, strictly no driving. You are encouraged to stay in your hotel. The airport closes, yes really. There are zero flights in and out of Bali. Last time the electric was off, and only cold food available. For some reason, you whisper rather than speak out loud.
So shsss... until next week.
The day after Nyepi I have a flight to Calcutta, India. So next time News from there..
Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: Historic Event!  Gen Z overthrew the government..
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal.


Last week, I was debating whether to make this scheduled trip. The airport was closed and protests were turning to riots and reports of police brutality.. and all happening right in the business area around my hotel where I had booked to stay. Also in last week's news, lots of drama everywhere. Nobody has noticed Temu is a channel for Russian goods into the UK. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Well, I was being well informed by my friends and suppliers in Kathmandu. The situation had changed rapidly, massive drama going on, including the flagship Hilton hotel being burned down. But the army restored order, the government resigned and collectively went into hiding, the Gen Z protests actually worked with huge impact. Historic times. Well, my flight was not cancelled, the airport was open again.. so I stuck with my plan and went there.
The first thing I did was to find actual Gen Z protestors and interview them.. I discovered something interesting..
Watch my YouTube video here.

The journey.
So on Monday evening, I took a flight from Yiwu airport to Chengdu airport, which is Panda central, so many pandas in that airport.  I had an 8-hour connection but found a rather plush airport hotel actually in the terminal, got a few hours sleep and then strolled over to international departures. Very organised place with lots of Panda statues, no hassle at all. I'm sat in the business lounge with a cup of coffee, catching up on some work, when a young lady found me to tell me the flight was leaving early. Could I hurry to the gate.. 

The flight was very sparse, only three people in business class, took off early and arrived over Kathmandu after about 2.5 hours. They actually announced the landing and said we would be on the ground in 15 minutes. But then, rather alarmingly, we spent a long time in a holding loop over the airport - more than an hour, maybe 90 minutes - I was actually getting worried that beneath us something had kicked off and wasn't able to land. The only information from the flight deck was a sorry about the delay, and there are traffic control issues. 
Back to normal in Nepal

But after landing, the notorious stressful passport control was almost empty, no queue at all.. and a very polite immigration officer actually thanked me and said welcome back to Nepal, we are glad to have you. No clue why we were delayed.. could have just been the weather. 

I took a car to my hotel, which was right in the heart of the unrest area, opposite the Grand Place and not far from the burned down Hilton Hotel, which we passed on the way to my hotel.

I soon connected with the Gen Z, son and daughter of our Shipping agent and the staff of our Lokta paper supplier.  Watch the video above to find out why the Hilton was burned down.

There is something about the young people in Nepal - they seem to have a lot more agency and independence than the youngsters of India or China. Somehow pretty cool.. very like the Indonesian or Malaysian youngsters. And in Nepal, they changed a corrupt and greedy government with mass protest pretty much overnight. 

Meanwhile, in the UK.

There is a Gold Reward Amnesty.. on right now - Ends soon. Great time to stock up, ready for the run up to Christmas.

What is the Secret of Soap Flowers?

Also in the UK.. Holly made this excellent informative video - for our "Can You Sell This?" series about Soap Flowers.. 

If you ask me, this is one of our most underrated under the radar products. We have a handful of customers who have discovered the secret to selling this line and literally buy pallet loads; one customer bought half a container load. In Europe, we sell them really well to many more customers than the UK.. Come on, Britain, find out how you can make money with Soap Flowers.
Also happening!

Massive discounts on our Backflow incense and a Can You Sell This? Info video also..


Drop-shipping Update.
I finally feel happy to report that our Drop-shipping website is coming good. This was a lot more difficult than we imagined and has taken a monumental effort by a big section of AW people. Raul has been co-ordinating the developer team in Bali, Tomas has literally been working day and night to get stuff designed and functioning.. I have been testing and reporting bugs until those bugs are totally eradicated. Martina in the UK is full-time on uploading products and crafting deals..  The APIs that connect Shopify, eBay, etc have been born, tuned and tamed and made to perform for our customers..(More API's are on the verge of being unveiled)..  And a special thanks to some particularly long suffering dedicated customers (you know who you are!) have been immeasurably helpful with feedback and suggestions. 

AW-Dropship.com  - now is the time to dip back in.. and carve out your online sales profits. 

So get yourself a nice cup of tea, glass of wine or hot chocolate.. sit down and start by reading this guide:  ADVICE & TIPS 

Wishing you a lovely weekend.. 

Peace and love.
David

title: Trust is an Investment
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ Sheffield


I trust you are well..

It's really getting busy, and the challenge of working out of limited space is beginning to stretch AW people to the limits.
Last week I was telling you about our 3X plan and the possible move to a big new warehouse and showed you the time-lapse video of the old one being pulled down, you can read about it here.

Last week I was telling you about the complex deal to acquire a lease on this beautiful big warehouse that will take AW and our service to you to the next level. I was hoping to tell you today the deal has been done, but alas we keep hitting stumbling blocks. Lawyers, bankers, insurance and agents all complicating things.. In the old days, not that long ago deals were deals, find a rapport, look the guy in the eye, strike a bargain, shake hands and get on with it. With Parkwood Business Park, our home now (what remains) I met Keith the owner/property developer, a canny but straight talking Yorkshire guy and we kinda clicked. He flies helicopters for fun and he scared me witless by taking me for a spin and buzzing over nearby Chatsworth House.  We did a substantial deal on a handshake, and we didn't bother with lawyers.. much to the horror of our bankers and accountants. 

AW has always been built on a foundation of trust and personal relationships. In twenty years we have never used a letter of credit when importing containers of products from India, or Indonesia or China. Deals done on an exchange of emails to clarify points, I might snap a picture of my notes made during negotiations, then we shake hands and give a PO and immediately a decent deposit. Trust. But not without a bit of due diligence, it is important to know the people you are dealing with are decent people and we always check our suppliers are ethical, good to staff and compliant with local laws etc. The most important thing is that relationship. 

Meet the AW agents:


Mr Chatterjee - our man in India. And one of the kindest humans on earth, he spends his spare time feeding needy people and helps with the children's home we support.


Coco - our girl in China. And one of the hardest working people you will meet, endless energy and enthusiasm. She is also my wife :-)


Ringo - our man in Indonesia. And one of the humblest and gentlest guys alive. But resourceful and totally in control.  
We trust our agents a lot, with lots of money, millions of pounds. They have to work in the interest of AW, but of course they have endless conflicts of interest and many potential areas for corruption. For example a supplier could offer kickbacks for extracting a higher price, there are lots of ways to undermine the agent relationship. In the past we have had one or two bad relationships where (a well paid agent or manager) has abused the trust invested in them. What happened was that the relationship became strained, broke down, and was in the end no fun for anyone. You know who you are.. Some people are naturally prone to take advantage of trust, psychologists think it could be as much as 20% of people - so many business people don't risk investing in trust. Instead they become control freaks, have endless complex contracts etc. I learned however that blind trust is not good, build in a little accountability and some KPI (targets), don't naively trust.. but don't get obsessive.  

Good people respond well to trust. The system works well and business can grow, everyone has fun, everyone benefits. 
When you trust in people - sometimes for years - and they just take advantage of you again and again.. it blinking hurts.. but trust is risky and the way I see it that hurt you feel is the price you pay for having other great relationships.

So we didn't get the keys to our new warehouse yet.. because all those bankers, agents, lawyers, insurance bods are all there to implement systems that control risk, negating the need to trust. And that takes eons.. slows everything down.
At the end of the day, someone has to hand over the keys to a 8 million pound asset. So you can't blame them for being obsessively careful. 
I wish they would just trust us on a handshake (or elbow nudge) because we have five containers stacked up at the port, hundreds of pallets in storage and people working themselves into a frenzy trying to cope.. 

The big news is that Bath Bombs are coming back on-line.. See below.. lots of new lines, back in stock.
We are a long way behind with orders, working this weekend to catch up.. I will go and help myself.
Thank you for trusting us with your orders.. we appreciate your trust. And we are doing our level best to repay it.

Take care..

More news next week.

David

For example a supplier could offer kickbacks for extracting a higher price, there are lots of ways to undermine the agent relationship. In the past we have had one or two bad relationships where (a well paid agent or manager) has abused the trust invested in them. What happened was that the relationship became strained, broke down, and was in the end no fun for anyone. You know who you are.. Some people are naturally prone to take advantage of trust, psychologists think it could be as much as 20% of people - so many business people don't risk investing in trust. Instead they become control freaks, have endless complex contracts etc. I learned however that blind trust is not good, build in a little accountability and some KPI (targets), don't naively trust.. but don't get obsessive. Good people respond well to trust. The system works well and business can grow, everyone has fun, everyone benefits. The big news is that Bath Bombs are coming back on-line.. See below.. lots of new lines, back in stock. We are a long way behind with orders, working this weekend to catch up.. title: David's AW News: Taking on the Mafia
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal, where I am taking on the mafia.


Last week was crazy, we kicked off with our 29th Birthday celebrations.. AW is 29 years old. 29 years since I sold my first bottle of Lavender Oil on a Sheffield Street market. 
Since then it's been beyond busy in all our warehouses, the elfs are struggling to keep up - but we will find a way.

Anyway I'm on the way home for Christmas (Erm the long way).. On Wednesday I said goodbye to Ringo and Bondhan as they dropped me off at Denpasar airport, I took a Malaysian airways flight to Kuala Lumpur arriving late evening, slept in the most comfortable bed you can imagine at the Sama-Sama airport hotel (short walk and a buggy ride), and early morning checked in for the flight to Kathmandu. Just about the smoothest, trouble free, friendly people, nice food.. best experience ever. Sometimes I love traveling in Asia.  Even as we approached the airport it seemed like the wings were almost touching the magical mountains.
Last week I was telling you about 29 years of AW.. and how I almost gave up on the first day.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Well, nice Mr Paddam (our gentleman Shipping agent) was kindly waiting at the airport to pick me and my extremely heavy luggage up.  We caught up with things as he drove me to my hotel. Then I managed to drop in and see three of our suppliers with showrooms nearby. One of which came back to my hotel to collect the content of my luggage. Lots of hang tag labels..

Mafia label man.
You see we have an order for 14,200 items of a new product we have been working on for a while. This thing needs a hangtag, attached label and barcode label. Labels in Kathmandu are ridiculously expensive, last time I got into an argument about it. It seems there is one guy who makes all the labels for all our suppliers. I ask Mr Padam if there is anyone else and apparently not really. I went to this guy's print shop and asked why what costs 1.5p in India or Indonesia costs 10p here. It's crazy, making products more expensive than they need to be. The guy is jolly (and shall we say well fed) and smartly dressed.. I sense corruption. And so many implausible excuses why it is so expensive.  I tell him that I think we will get labels made in India and ship them. But he tells me that it is difficult, customs, duty, delays etc.. Anyway the guy gets my Whatsapp number and starts messaging me.. "Sir I want to meet you, I need to talk to you". 

In the end I agree and we meet in a coffee shop. "Sir I want all your business and if you deal directly with me I can give you better prices". He pretty much told me he has to pay commission to the suppliers in cash back. I didn't tell him he already makes all our labels (as far as I can see)  but asked how much cheaper it would be if we ordered and paid directly? That hangtag he could do for 7p. Do the maths that's 14,200 x (7p-1.5p) = that's £781 on just one product (excess profit). 

So I got those hang tags printed in Bali, and booked a business class flight with lots of luggage allowance - stuffed two suitcases full of labels. Had a very pleasant flight and saved enough money to pay for the flight and hotel on the way. But I still need to fix this issue if our Nepal products are to be competitive. . and that guy keeps messaging me asking who I bought the labels from?
I just found one street on the edge of Tamel with several print shops selling hang tags and labels for manufacturers, off the shelf I can buy North Face and Uniqlo labels, barcodes and everything to make your own fakes..very dodgy.  I asked for a quote but it was even more expensive.

Chinese live streamers.
Last time I was here I noticed them, this time I can hear more Chinese spoken than Nepali or Hindu. One of our suppliers explained the business model to me. These young people come, very cool and trendy looking, they have cameras and lights. They ask what ready stock you have and if they can sell it for you. They often live stream in the doorway or window, so life going on can be seen and noises of Katmandu provide a backdrop. Selling on live streams to China.. packing and labeling orders on the shop floor, and Chinese shipping companies have sprung up all over Thamel just to ship these orders. 
Christmas is coming, and I managed to catch this year's big Christmas movie: "Red One".  What a fun movie! Action, fantasy and comedy. Dwayne Johnson plays Santa bodyguard when Santa gets kidnapped. Apparently Santa staff are all mythical creatures who travel the world via hyperloops hidden in the broom cupboards of the world's gift shops. There is a running joke in the movie. Every time they loop around the world and pop out in another gift shop, there is some shopper who turns to her friend and says "I can't believe they have sold out of essential oils!".. so funny. 29 years ago when I started AW I had to explain what essential oils were now they are mainstream. 

I don't know if it's related or not but Essential Oil sales (always our top selling range) are up by quite a bump at the moment. Trending again I guess.

Nepal products
Yes last time I was here only a few weeks ago, there were lots of blockages and goods were not getting shipped. I sorted it out and we managed to get things moving.
So those things are arriving (by air) in our warehouses now. I noticed you like the Little Felt Sheep. 
Selling fast.. which makes me happy :)

Have a lovely weekend, hope you escape Storm Bert and if it snows it is pretty not painful.
Take care!

Namaste! from Nepal. 

David

title: David's AW News: Shock in China
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China.

Everyday is a wild adventure here, far too much to report in an update you will want to read quickly.

Tomas and Sandra are here. Sandra is our talented designer from the UK the genius behind our best selling Hop Hare Brand. So we brought Sandra here to see what possibilities are here and give her a major inspirational boost.  See below.


Last week I was telling you about the crazy journey to get here from India and more about that Mad Honey.. if you missed you can catch up here.


Sandra and Tomas - in Yiwu!

It's hard work!

Everyday we are working long hours, seven days a week.. it's full on. Sandra is a little bit in shock - but this is normal in China. People work hard.

The other day we went on a factory visit to one of our old suppliers, soap flowers - in the next city. Coco drove us there and we arrived a huge complex, warehouse / factory with seven floors. The boss who we have known a few years met us on the entrance to the complex and directed us to his place.  We have delt with them for years, soap flowers sell well (in some markets very well) but it's highly competitive and price and quality - and all the compliance papers etc have to be spot on. 




We asked him about the Trump tariffs and like many of our suppliers he played down the effect, he said only 10% of orders go America and these days big growth from South America and Africa can make up the slack. Anyway their main market by far is Japan. In the showroom we found some strange Japanese things.. including bouquets of soft cute toys.


Haha fun but we decided not really an Ancient Wisdom thing. Shockingly bad taste :)


We had a tour of the factory, and found really good working conditions, spacious and organised. Happy smiling staff and really helpful designers keen to work with us.

We buy a lot of soap flower bouquets from here, and these are becoming increasingly popular, similar price (maybe less than) a real flower bouquet, but will keep for a long time, and should you tire of it can be used in the bath. 

So Sandra was a little bit shy at first, but soon got into the design process - she came equipped with idea and with the help of the inhouse designer quickly made a new range of bouquets. 



It's great to see creativity and collaboration in action, and this company so easy to deal with, keen to meet our price expectation and nothing too much trouble.

If I get time I'll upload a YouTube video about the visit. You can register for our channel and stay up-to date here.

Actually our suppliers this time seem to be super happy.. to see us.

One supplier (our Atomiser supplier) declared it was eight years we had been trading with them and insisted on taking us out for a nice meal. They took us to a ridiculously lavish restaurant, like an indoor landscaped garden, with a river and live classical Chinese music. We had our own private room with three staff (and a musician) to serve us. But the food was mostly shellfish with the speciality giant spider crab. Neither me, Tomas or Sandra are fans of this kind of seafood. But we enjoyed the company and experience. But quite shocked at the things you could eat here!




Nomad Sari- brand T-shirts are finally here!

Back in the UK - Rodrigo and team have been enthusiastically getting into fashion photography and seems like all AW staff want to be models - haha!

Well the Stonewashed Mandala T-shirts arrived.. and everyone loves them. Which makes me so happy, because I put a massive amount of work into this product. Designed by our Bali designer, Bondhan, produced in Kathmandu, with co-ordination between the factory (we checked good working conditions), the stonewashing house, the screen-print workshop and our Mr Suman finishing, packing and all the co-ordination.. this is not fast fashion.. it took forever. 



Selling fast! Stock up now.. See below for more details. 

Lots of products arrived recently.. and the team are working hard to get everything online asap.

Also a major BACK IN STOCK!

The long awaited Satya Incense - is BACK and online. Best selling - Best price - Best stock up now!!

Anyway - lots to do!!

Enjoy your weekend.

Hope business is good.

Take care, more updates next week.

title: I found a huge problem in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Bali..

Yes I made it. Lots of hurdles to cross but I finally made it back to Bali. 
Last week I was just starting my four days quarantine in Jakarta after an exhausting 26 hour journey from Malaga. At least I met an interesting Thai lady.. you can read about it here if you missed it.

I hope you all brave the bad weather in the UK without any dire consequences. Storm Eunice is coming..

I was showing Ringo and Bondan the news from the UK about extreme weather, I told them it could be the worst for 40 years. Oh really they said not particularly impressed.. In Indonesia, storms, floods, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tornadoes and tsunamis are all to be expected.  But as we drove up past Tegallalang, with the famous rice terrace view, turned right towards the higher ground on the way to visit Mr Pak Man, (one of our oldest suppliers) we were practically in paradise. Here beyond the tourist zone farmers live gentle lifes tending the rice terrace adorned with small temples and statues. The young rice has just been planted and the terraces are being gradually flooded, trickles of water with the sun glinting off the pools. Lush green trees and huge tropical plants adorn everything. "You might have extreme weather conditions sometimes but you also have paradise" I pointed out. 


It might be paradise but  AW has a BIG problem right now in Bali.. and I am being shown the consequences.

First job of course on arriving in Bali was to go and visit the team at our warehouse in Ketterwell, after my last visit in November last year activity has ramped up hugely and we have already shipped several containers. Two of which just arrived in the UK this week. The problem is we need to ship far more containers than are actually available, finding a shipping company with accesses to containers and shipping lines with space on a ship is a daily battle. Make a booking and it gets cancelled, or you get gazumped and the price can go up even after booking because somebody else is willing to pay more. It used to cost 15-20% of the value of the goods in shipping, these days it costs 80-90%. 

It's not that there is greater demand for containers, it's that the capacity has been strangled by shipping companies who are doing a terrible job but making obscene profits at the moment.  
Google made $20 billion last year, the top ten shipping companies (and full details are hard to get) by some estimates made eye popping $300 billion - dwarfing not just Google but Facebook and Amazon combined. We are all paying for it in increased prices or reduced profits, I'm not even sure our partying ruling class even notice this problem - a major factor in the inflation spiral we are about to hit us. Big money like that finds it's way to political party funding as a way to influence those who could put a stop to it. 

Gosh sorry for the rant.. but we are at the sharp end of the consequences.. 

Ringo had been complaining that the warehouse was full, but I wasn't quite prepared for how full. 
I arrived at the warehouse see the carpark full, the staff room full, the packing are full. Ringo led me through a warren between stacked high cartons and piles of stock awaiting QC and packing. "Oh my God Ringo.. how can you work in such circumstances?" my head is spinning this is certainly not the H&S standards that we aim for at AW. Ringo's like.. no problem, we can find away. He is always so stress free on the surface and never wanting to bring any stress to me.



What the Bali warehouse looks like now.. 


"Why don't you leave the stock in the suppliers warehouses?" I asked him.. "Until we have a container to load and bring it then." Already doing that he told me, and today we went to see.

First the guy who makes the Coconut Lamps, his factory was floor to roof full of stock for us. At least two container loads in just that one product. 
Then the lady who makes the display stands for bath bombs (amongst other things), her factory full, and borrowing space in several other workshops nearby. 

Then we went to see Mr Pakman I have mentioned him before. He is the head of his village and contracts out work to all the families, we gave them an order for natural log stools and those Plant Holders.. 
His family and extended family live in a typical Bali compound, houses surrounding a temple and shared outdoor living area. Pakman and his wife live in a nice villa with roof terrace open views to Mount Agung the live volcano. The workshop are is full, the shared living spaces are full of stock, the roof terrace has been filled, and the wife was complaining it was hard to get to the bedroom. Even the office area was full so we had to meet on a step.
And he told me the whole village was full. I'm so sorry I told him, no problem he said we understand. We have been paying them before delivery, otherwise not only would they have no space to live but money to pay the workers.
Ringo is calling rould the shipping agents everyday chasing possible containers.


So despite the fact that two containers just arrived in the UK and we have lots of things back in stock, and some new stuff coming online.. it won't last long before out of stock items start to appear. 
Our grand plan to be Europe's best (and possibly biggest) importer of Indonesian home and giftware products is hitting a serious glitch right now. This damn container shortage is a nightmare. I'll keep you posted.

Meanwhile Tomas is in Slovakia where we are moving to our new distribution warehouse. Our current one is not far behind the one in Bali for spare space.
Big milestone this week, we got early access - the offices are still being built but we can use the warehouse part. First job to construct the racking. 



Our architect and contractor who can make anything happen. Tomas says they are great guys full of positivity and really getting on with the project. We want to be operational by end of April / May time. By which time I'm hoping we will have shipped the backlog of orders from Indonesia - to fill it up..

That's all the news for now, I just heard from Ringo that he has secured one container possibly two for the 25th for shipping to UK. Yesterday we despatched one container to Spain, so maybe things are looking up. But we have lots of wonderful new products that I am just dying to see on the market.. some.. just a little.. arrived in those two containers.. see below.

Take special care everyone, especially you guys in the UK, Storm Eunice is coming. 

More news from Indonesia next week.

David

title: Christmas - The Last Day
content_html:
Greetings from Affinity Park, Sheffield

So this is Christmas and what have you done?

The Last Day
It's the last day at AW, and as usual I'm at the HQ to wish everyone a Happy Christmas. 
Apart from last year which was pretty much cancelled, the last day at AW has become a kind of family tradition. Like any family we do the same things, traditions that have become baked in.
Lucy always orders the pizza, Ula always distributes the secret Santa presents, we always exchange Christmas greetings with other parts of AW, everyone is tidying up to leave things spick and span for next year.
Later this afternoon we will open a few bottles of wine and gather for pizza and toasts, a group photo must be taken and then I will make a short emotional speech - in which I will thank everyone for there hard work and contributions to AW.  In dribs and drabs everyone will leave clutching a small gift box of chocolates and wine from AW. Usually the last to leave are Tomas, Katka and Phillippe (Katka's husband). Another year at AW over.

Another year over, a new one just begun.

Message of Hope.
This year is of course like that but also nothing like that.. half of the team are not here, Omicron has taken lots of people (into isolation) this year..  fortunately no-one is seriously ill, most have no or very mild symptoms. I don't know what your experience is like, but I hope the same.. maybe Omicron is a good thing, distributing antibodies like a natural vaccine with only minor side effects. One can imagine the flat panic in the board-rooms of the vaccine companies.
Let's hope and pray that this is nature's Christmas Present to humanity.

And so this is Christmas, I hope you have fun,
The near and the dear one
The old and the young

Thank You
Of course it is always important to stay humble, and thankful, and be grateful. 
On behalf of everyone at AW, we thank you - our lovely customers - for being with us, supporting us and contributing to the story of AW. And so we would like to wish you all a peaceful, safe and very Happy Christmas.
Whatever traditions you and your workmates, friends and family have developed at Christmas... they are a kind of gift to ourselves.. a way to express our love..  enjoy them!

A very merry Christmas
And a happy new year
Let's hope it's a good one
Without any fear

And so lets hope it's a good one..
Happy Christmas from myself and everyone at Ancient Wisdom.
Here is our Christmas Card to you..

David

title: Inside or Out..?
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

It's day 97.. 

Last week I was telling you lots of things, including the evolution of face masks in Indonesia.. you can read about it here.
I'm feeling like I really need to go, Europe is opening up, super Saturday, 1 meter rule, pale ale - a new normal. China (where my wife is) is looking isolated and impossible to get to.  So here is nice, working with Ringo is great, the weather is always perfect, I can find and develop new products, but time is coming when I need to move. Can I really just stay holed up here until this pandemic is over.. will it ever be over? What happens then.. will I ever come back to Asia?  Today I feel confused and emotional and a little lonely.
Anyone I talk to has a different perspective / different opinions & advice / at different times. Now I can see flight options, it's becoming possible.. Do I stay or do I go now..? In Bali or out?

The skies are full of kites. Every day more and it seems higher. Thousands of them. t's a sign that folks have nothing better to do but engage in a cheap hobby. Shops that sold tourist gifts are turning out kites, some huge some tiny, all shapes. Ringo says normally there are restrictions but now because only a few local flights no one is controlling the kites. Maybe it's a subconscious wish to fly away.. driving people to send their creation to the skies... to be free. 

Even here things have been opening up a bit. The beach reopened so I can walk again for exercise. Sadly all the hotels are still closed and the few small businesses.. bars and restaurants are now bankrupt or given up. So very few businesses trading there. 
There is an English owned restaurant on the main road, and I had heard they was serving English Sunday Lunch.. roast beef and Yorkshire puddings.  It's about 40 minutes walk, normally I'm not to bothered by the expat bars, why travel if you just want to recreate home. But the thought of Sunday lunch with all the trimmings.. (oh yes!) It was lovely the owner is friendly, and he was totally surprised to be full.. and like old times.. no, or little social distancing that I could see, staff masks had slipped under chins. People chatting, children running around.  I guess the same will be happening in England this weekend. 
Here it Covid rates are (officially at least) very low and few deaths for the size of the population. Just 16 in a population of four million. But the infection rate doubled in 2 weeks since lock-down rules relaxed. Let's hope the same doesn't happen in Europe.

Ringo's niece got married. He comes from a village inland in an area called Bangli.  I was formally invited to the wedding and then uninvited by the village elders. Regulations only allow twenty people, and Ringo explained that I was off that list. Don't worry I told him, I understand. He took pictures.. Only 20 people in the wedding compound, but outside the walls of the compound the family paid for a roast pig meal and the disgruntled uninvited held their own party. Life in coronavirus Bali..

The 20 people rule clearly got bent.. Ringo moved from one event to the other to take these pictures. 

    
   Inside....


  Outside...

Meanwhile back in the UK..
Everyone has been working incredibly hard.. we shifted more order in June than ever in the history of AW.. these are crazy times, normally our quiet month of June gone mad. The same in Slovakia EU warehouse and Spain also. 
Of course we are thankful for the business, a few weeks ago it seemed like the world would fall in. Who know's what the future holds.. 

Stay safe please, wear a mask.
Enjoy the weekend.

Take care

David

title: The Rice People Saving The World
content_html:
Greetings from lock-down in Bali day 22

How are you doing?

Last week I was telling you about the bird that followed me. And also added to my review of webshop systems that can help you do drop-shipping.  You can read about it here. 
Mostly I fill my day by working in the mornings, the afternoons I go for a (social distancing / mask on) brisk walk along the beach nearby. Evenings (when Europe is awake)  I interact with the AW teams. But each afternoon as I walk I literally see the same few faces ,we nod to each other but rarely speak. It's really beautiful, maybe because the air is cleaner, maybe because it is so quiet. To the left is a view across to the volcano, sleepy and exotic.  Mount Agung the locals believe to be a sacred mountain, the centre of the universes home to Gods, there is a temple on the banks of the volcano, Bali's most sacred, parts of which date back 2000 years. 


The last time people wore masks in Bali. Only in May 2019 it was erupting and delaying flights and a real concern that a major eruption could bring Bali to a halt. I was here at the time and experienced more than one earthquake.

It was a huge worry in 2019, many people cancelled holidays, parts of the island were closed to visitors for safety and the people of Bali prayed and held continuous ceremonies until eventually, the volcano calmed down. Did it just calm down, or did the ceremonies and prayers to the gods do the trick? Rationally of course it calmed down, but spiritually maybe it is possible to draw (simultaneously) a different conclusion. At that time, tourism was badly effected, ironically people were issued with face masks to protect them from breathing in ash-laden air and Agung anxiety created a heightened spiritual awareness.   

Yesterday afternoon I passed a ceremony happening at a temple near the beach, I didn't take pictures because I realised it was a cremation ceremony. A kiln in the shape of a dragon was spewing smoke from it's nose, as people prayed toward mount Agung.  They wore masks and social distanced, but I know the event was probably illegal. People are scared - not just here but the world over. I noticed some offerings I had not seen before..

The drum was heard.
There is a drum in a temple at Puri Klungkung, very rarely it sounds by itself, once in 1963 just before the volcano had a major eruption, once in 2002 before the Bali bombing.. only certain holy men across the island can hear it. On the eve of the Silent Day called Nyepi 25th March, the bell was heard again.  As a result of this, the holy men of Bali asked people to make a special devotion and make a nasi wong-wongan. It's a figure made of rice - nasi is Indonesian for rice and wong-wonga means people. 
  
 
 Rice People to protect the island and the world from the virus.
Meanwhile.. back in the UK.
Tomas and Katka, continue to keep AW on track, we are still shipping orders, our hero's working safely working hard. Many of our customers have an on-line presence and are doing well despite the lock-down. So our drop-shipping department is busy.
 We are working like crazy to full-fill the orders, this week we will increase shifts and put more people on drop-shipping. 

Be unique..
Also, we are trying to make specific bundles of products just for Drop-shipping. For example an Oil Burner, a Selection of Essential Oil and  6 nightlights. The advantages of bundles are threefold.. 1. Convenience for your customer, one click, don't need to think too hard.  2. A higher value deal, (more £'s per sale) meaning it's maybe possible to offer free shipping (this boosts sales every time) and..  3. Price comparisons are harder to make, so you don't need to worry about been undercut by Amazon. Your unique combination is unique right?  Remember at AW we only sell B2B - we don't list on Ebay or Amazon or run our own retail websites, so you can be sure not to run into unfair competition.
So - do you have any ideas? Ideas for bundles that we could set up for you.. product pictures ready etc. Do let me know..

Take care, stay safe, wash your hands, talk to someone.

Until next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Java find. This is Amazing!
content_html:
Greetings Bali, where I have just landed after a week of absolute adventure.

Wishing you all the best for Valentine's Day.. Hope your day is full of Romance, Love, and Fun. 

This week Bondhan and I have been criss-crossing the island of Java on a mad road trip.. and had some absolutely amazing and unexpected adventures.
I'm beside myself with excitement about what we discovered.. I'm sharing the secrets below..
Last week I was telling you about the surf in Bali and how it's connected to beating Temu, if you missed it you can catch up here.

Now check this..
Do you see the red leaves on this tree? Our first sight of a mystical blessed tree in the jungle forest of Java.

So Bondhan and I took a flight from Denpasar, Bali to Yogyakarta in South central Java. A neighbour from Bondhans hometown, kindly lent us his car - he met us at the airport with the keys. Instead of turning right from the airport towards the city, we turned left along the coast road. A few hours drive and then turned inland heading to higher ground, where we stopped the night in a small town where the only highrise was the hotel we stayed in, which marketed itself as a wedding venue. Packages starting at 85,000rp - about £4 per person. We were the only guests. But a very friendly hotel with a totally wasted breakfast buffet just for us. The next morning we went to see our Coconut craft supplier up in the hills... and spent an interesting time learning about coconut crafts (and gave him an order).. but I was keen to press on - because quite by accident we had discovered something utterly amazing. We asked the coconut man if it was true...
..he said yes but be careful... that market is controlled..

So this is how we found ourselves deep in the lush mountain forests of central Java. After bouncing along unpaved roads for a couple of hours we arrived at the surprisingly nice village of the Genitri trees.
A mural on the side of the village office depicted members of the six religions of Indonesia, and a slogan saying all people are welcome here. Given that Java is predominantly Muslim this is at first sight surprising, but all these religions use the fruit of the Gentri tree within their artefacts.. Our contact met us in the square and we followed him on his motorbike another twenty minutes to his farmstead.
So remote, there was no internet, even the electricity was limited to so many hours a day here.  
Those trees with distinctive red leaves falling like tears produce ripe dark blue berries with chunky seeds that are the Rudraksha beads much sought after in mala jewellery, rosary beads etc.  Each tree brings a unique shape, the number of segments of the bead reflects in the meaning and value of the bead. The rarest is the 16 section eight plus eight (the Gauri Shanker twin bead), worth around $500 per bead. Sought after by Hindu and Buddhist monks from India and China. The lucky farmers who find these trees live in luxury villas hidden in the hills. The guy we made contact with, a farmer who showed us his humble farmhouse and workshops. He explained the painstaking process of harvesting and making the beads, carefully drilling the holes to thread the beads has to be done one by one. He told us that local legend has it that Hindu monks came to these mountains a hundred years ago and blessed the area with the tears of Shiva and taught the locals how to harvest.  He showed us his small collection of special beads, these valued at around £50 per bead. The quality and quantity from here far surpasses the Nepalese and Indian harvests. But he also warned us to be careful of the Indian and Chinese traders, like a mafia they try to control the trade from the area by loaning farmers money in exchange for exclusive contracts.  
Most people believe that the mala beads come from India and Nepal, the truth is the best quality and volume comes from these secret hills in central Java. Indian and Chinese traders try to keep this a secret, even ChatGPT didn't know about this area. Of course the Bali folk knew, and even they kept it a secret, but now we know. And so do you! 
We have secured some supplies ahead of the next harvest, and are thinking of supplying bulk in Europe for people who like to craft their own jewellery. 

But as it happens, we have Bali Mala bead Necklaces recently arrived in the UK.. 108 beads, gift boxed (perfect for Mother's Day) with spiritual guidance details on the box. 
They are good value compared to similar Nepal or India sources (Google it) simply because they are made nearer the source of the Mala beads.

From India.. a container just arrived today.. Rodrigo and Team are working hard to get beautiful new boxes online.. 

But that was just one adventure.. more to come. I'll update you next week on what happened next..
Take care, have a lovely Valentine's Weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: IN CHINA
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu in China

Hope you are doing well and ready for the weekend. It's very hot here, as hot as I can ever remember being.. 

Last week I was telling you about life in Bali and how a BBC journalist called me around midnight (Bali time) from the UK.. if you missed it and want to find out why you can catch up here.

On Sunday evening Bondhan (Our man in Indonesia) drove me to the airport, my time here seemed far too short and lots of jobs not really finished.. but anyway I had a night flight to Guangzhou China to catch. 

Bali airport these days is super efficient, and like a dream to drift though, everyone is so kind and thoughtful even the security and passport control.. Bought some last minute gifts, a glass of wine in the lounge and then ambled to the gate to board a China Southern night flight to Guangzhou. 

On board there are only a few business class seats, so get very fussed over.. more wine and more food than I can eat. Really delightful friendly service.  I managed to sleep a little on the 5 hour flight and we arrived in Guangzhou at 6am with a connection to Yiwu at 8.20am.. 

From calm to chaos.. I wasn't expecting this.. last time I was in China it was not busy in the airport.. but now thousands of people in long winding lines for passport control and only one young guy struggling to control the mass of Indian's, Russian; South Americans and Turkish - all sorts of odd people including me.




From relaxed Bali to Chaotic Guangzhou - Culture Shock!
That culture shock I don't usually get inside Asia.. and the staff I interacted with on a stressful trip though the airport, addressed me (annoyingly) in Russian, snatched my passport off me. Refused to help or look at my ticket when I requested a fast lane since my connection was very short.  Anyway I just rolled with it.. and made it to the gate midway though boarding.. 
A short flight to Yiwu - 90 minutes and a much more relaxed airport experience.. and Coco is waiting for me as I leave the airport.. It's not so bad.

As I step outside... WOW! this is hot.. it's stifling. Never have I known this stonking heat. The sky is blue and the sun is hot.. the heat is dry.. this is not normal.
The next day Tomas arrives from Spain on a flight from Spain (where he has been looking for a new warehouse urgently - see last week's news)  we meet at his hotel.. where staff are putting reflective shields on the cars in the sun - so helpful to stop everything melting. 

The Heat Problem

Tomas had brought some candle samples for us to work on, and he brought an apple from the breakfast buffet. After our day in the Yiwu market.. back at the car in 43c the apple had stewed and turned black and the candle wax had turned to liquid and run away.
This is a worrying problem because we have loaded a few containers with Candles in them.. Coco has been careful to make sure they are loaded upright and not at the edges of the container.. but I fear between China and the UK there will be some heat.  Anyway.. we just got news that the EU and the UK are imposing (Trump like) tariffs on candles of 75% from this month. So candles anyway are going to be off the menu. (hint - stock up).

The Temu Problem. 

We have done our usual round of visiting some of our old suppliers and seeing what's new.. But apart from the heat in China.. We have another major problem. And this is related to the reason the BBC guy called me. So yesterday we went along to see one of our old suppliers.. We buy amongst other things.. Chakra Gemstone String Bracelets.
It's a lovely family business, like many with a lady boss. Her husband, Son and daughter-inlaw are all hands on sorting, making, labelling and packing jewellery. As hardworking and enthusiastic about the gemstone jewellery family as you can get.
But then I spotted this label.. this label had been supplied by Temu - the lady boss told me.. she speaks no English, doesn't understand it anyway. I asked her if she knew what EC REP means.. she said maybe a customer - has no idea. Coco explained that it's the person in the EU who is supposed to represent your company if there is any problem with the product.. Blank look. The company name at the top.. is not their company at all.. who is it.. Shrug.. she has no idea. The thing is I recognise those names.. we made test purchases from Temu and had the same names on the labels. If you find those addresses on Google maps they are Pizza parlours or something. Last time I checked.
She then went off on a total rant about Temu.. they demand stock at prices impossible to supply.. so cut quality to the minimum, use fake or glass beads.
Then explained, if stock sells too slow Temu will charge "rent", if goods are a day late they are fined. They are fined so many times. It's hard to make a profit.
But she went on to explain, American trade has gone, business is not great and to fill the gap they end up using Temu even if it is hard work. 
Temu have very persuasive reps who call none stop promising the earth if you trade.. but the reality is different. There have even been street protests about it.


With Temu nobody wins, only Temu.. and the only silver lining is our lovely supplier lady absolutely assured us our products she would never list on Temu.
The Temu problem is huge.. and we have already met quite a few companies who list on Temu and we have had to  reject the product. The first thing we do is a Temu search now and if the product is listed we say sorry we cannot buy. Sometimes actually quite often though a nice product is simply listed with stolen pictures and a poor replicure is sent instead..   it's a dog eat dog world here in Yiwu.

Anyway rest assured we are doing our best to bring you family business ethically produced - and beautiful gifts..
Meanwhile back in the UK.. Halloween is creeping up.. are you ready for the big day.. check out the scary and mystical gifts below..


So wishing you a lovely weekend.

Take care

David.

title: David's AW News: Crazy Trip?
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal


Happy Halloween October!

Did you see the news? They said I was crazy to come here. 
Last week I was telling you about some strange things going on in China. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Floods decimated the Kathmandu plain and even the city has been hit badly. But I had flights and hotels booked, because this was a leg on the way to India. I spoke with Mr Padam, our lovely gentleman shipping agent. "Namaste Mr David, you are very welcome to be here." Our suppliers all told me not to worry.. so on Wednesday Tomas and I took a China Southern flight from Yiwu to Guangzhou. From there he caught the connection to Bali, and I took the evening flight to Kathmandu. Arrived at 12.30am local time but the captain said we had to wait for a slot so we circled the city for a while, the airport is probably one of the most disorganised in the world. It took me two hours to get through the airport. Unnecessary security checks to get into the baggage area, long queues and then a long wait for my luggage, which came off almost last despite the priority tag and me being the only business class passenger on the flight. 
When I finally made it out of the airport. A familiar face was waiting for me.. my hotel driver from the last visit. Welcome back Mr David. On the drive through the night streets to the hotel he told me the roads had only just been cleared and that it had been pretty bad and many customers had cancelled trips, so he said the hotel was very happy to see me. The staff welcomed me but explained there were still issues following the floods.. no running water in the room, actually it was running like mud. But it would be fixed by the time I woke up. 

And the next morning (yesterday) during breakfast the manager, who I actually knew from another hotel (we had recognised each other on the last trip).. came to see me for a chat and catch up and thanked me for coming. Then I ventured out into the maze of streets that is the Thamel area and home to most of Nepal's giftware exporters. 
I was lost in no time..
My first stop (when I found him) was to see Mr Padam, our shipping agent and old school gentleman never seen without his Dhaka topi, an old fashioned formal hat. We have five orders outstanding from February, a bit of a performance disaster and I wanted to find out why? But of course since I was coming to check all the problems - had been magically resolved and almost everything was in Mr Padam's warehouse. 
Then I went to see Dipendrea, we call him Dip.. the trendy young guy that owns a small factory making many of our hemp bags. He told me his hometown had been badly affected and they were still in a mess. The casualties are much higher than the government admits. Infrastructure in Nepal (see the airport) is woefully maintained. This small country is stuck in a power struggle between its two mega neighbours, India and China - (unlike much of SE Asia) it doesn't quite seem to get its act together.  
But the people are humble and nice, easy to do business with and as you know the handicrafts of Nepal are practically a brand in their own right. So AW must do its bit in Nepal.

Geopolitics at play
I'm partly here because there are no direct flights between China and India.. The two biggest populations on the planet earth and neighbors have zero direct flights. Strange no? This is geopolitics at its worst. Despite this in Yiwu there is a whole Indian neighbourhood where Indian shipping agents and Indian business people are doing good business with China.  Anyway we need to be in India for the Delhi fair.. and since this issue means we have to go somewhere on the way.. I went to Nepal and Tomas Bali.. we will meet up in India in a while. 

Speaking of India.. 
Did you watch the recent Bald and Bankrupt Youtube in Delhi entitled - I visited India so you don't have to..?
It's caused an absolute storm in India (30,000  comments). In it he visits parts of Delhi I know well - and (like Thamel) home to handicraft exporters. Regular readers will know that Delhi is NOT my favorite city in India and that Youtube episode is no exaggeration. I love India and most of its people but it has to be said (as Mr Bald fearlessly points out) parts of it are terrible.  Even the most hectic backstreets of Katmandu are clean and people are relatively honest and calm. All SE Asia improved over the last ten years.. except.. Well, let's not get in trouble. I'll be there soon.
Meanwhile back in the UK..
Lots of new stock coming online.. lot's back in stock.
It's the Halloween month of October.. scary deals abound.. Including Free Magic Candles to all our customers (over £200) and a double discount - now 20% off that fast selling range. Don't miss out. Candles generally sell better from October (though to Mother's Day) - so now is the time to get your candle offering in tiptop shape.. Lot's of deals below.

Namaste from Nepal.
Have a lovely weekend.
David

title: It's all happening
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal. Where Tomas and I just landed.

Last we were in China just on the way to Kuala Lumpur where our IT is based and I was telling you about my short time in Yiwu, and just how nice they are making this once very scruffy city. You can read about it here.

We arrived at about 10pm - the airport looks like 1965, apart from hi-tech visa machines for foreigners it's seen no investment in years, the people are friendly though and finally we stumble out of the airport. The air feels cool and clean, a driver from the hotel is waiting for us, we drive to downtown Kathmandu. The streets are deserted, there are no street lamps, roads are pot-holed - it really feels 3rd world. Made worse by groups of police with guns and army check points. We are stopped and our driver breathalysed. All this security I ask the driver, but hardly any people - what's happening? He explained the festival of Dashain has just concluded, 2.5 million people descend on Kathmandu and they have just all gone home, I get the feeling we are stepping into the aftermath of a giant party.

Big posters line the streets of President Xi of China.. why we ask? We are having a state visit from Xi Jinping, he arrives this Saturday for three days. Apparently he is here to sign a trade deal. It's all happening in Kathmandu.
Last time I was here the Indian PM Narendra Modi was here, traffic was blocked for motorcades and it was almost impossible to get around the city. Should be interesting.

So we spent the last few days with Raul our IT wizard, basically preparing for Brexit. Raul works from trendy shared space offices, but for a couple of days, we decamped to the 49th floor of our hotel which is a penthouse loft-space with gobsmacking views of the famous KL skyline. If you ever go to KL, stay at the Lanson Place, massive suites, stupendous views and lovely staff. And cheaper than a travel lodge in London.
It's amazing how productive you can be in a good working environment. It's the monsoon season and the afternoons in KL turned electric with crackling lightning and thunder. Tomas, Raul and I were literally brainstorming in a storm.. high in the sky.
Haha.. Sometimes I really love my job.

Meanwhile back in the UK, its getting to the mad crazy time. We have weekend shifts on, have managed to squeeze in some extra packing bays. And (it was my idea) persuaded the courier company to park a trailer in the car-park.. So now we just load up your orders on pallets and forklift them onto the trailer. Makes lots of extra workspaces, and when the trailer is full they just hook up and take it directly to the depot. It's working well, means less time loading vans, more time packing orders.
Bryant the warehouse manager is stressed, he messaged we have 9 containers (mostly 40 foots) arriving in the next few days, how are we going to manage? I point out that as fast as stock comes in it is going out, so we should have space.. but this is no easy job, Bryant for sure has his hands full, but he has a good team. Pray for him and his team :)

So now we will go and meet Mr Padam, a real old school gentleman, he is our shipping agent and possible sourcing agent in Nepal. Nepal has a lot of products to offer, we have only just started here, I noticed that Nepalese hemp products are really popular in Spain, and increasingly in UK so I'm keen to develop our ranges.

Full update next week.

Take care

David

title: David's AW News:Vivá España! The Heat is on.
content_html:
Greetings from Malaga, Spain


I'm here at AW Artisan, the Spanish base of AW.  
It's always a pleasure to spend time with Toni and his (always ready for a party) team.
Last week I was telling you about The End.. the end of the Spring Asia sourcing trip. And my day in cool Copenhagen on the way here to Spain. Also my slightly bizarre fellow passengers on Thai airways flight who looked like aging cartel members.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Toni was travelling with me on that Asia trip, part of which we spent with Mr Chatterjee in Kolkata.. I just spoke with Chatterjee and his son.. "We are finished," he said. "it's mad hot here, feels like 50c - we are struggling to work - and the heat wave will last at least two weeks more".  He is installing extra fans, cold water on tap and cut working hours. We sent our sympathies..  Chatterjee sent some pictures.

Even in Kathmandu, Nepal our suppliers report the hottest temperatures they can remember. So far the heatwave didn't hit Indonesia so badly, but it's coming soon. In China they have severe flooding, but it's not affecting Coco although it's getting warmer by the day. 

In China we have now fully moved to our new larger warehouse.. And already dispatched three containers.. Tomorrow another will leave. Coco tells me it's a good job we have the extra space. And we also made a nice AW-China office.. still being decorated..  the sign is up but we have to find room for the Buddha statue..
Welcome to the new AW-China office.

It's not so hot in Spain, but the heat is still on. There is a looming problem that needs to be addressed. You see whilst in India we ordered rather a lot.. got a little over enthusiastic.. I'm blaming Toni, haha but maybe it's also my fault.. There are around 850 new products (on top of regular reorders) and that translates into lots of containers on the way.. and the warehouse (I mentioned this before) is already bursting at the seams. AW-Artisan has been growing fast for the last few years and has already outgrown the warehouse. We had this issue in the UK and Slovakia before we moved to bigger warehouses, so have some experience on how to deal with this kind of problem.. but they need to move quickly.. because all that stock IS COMING!! and we need to get a grip on this..
Juani is our super capable warehouse manager in Spain. She is amazingly well organised, and her team are always ready to meet any challenge. But this looming problem is on another level. We could rent containers and put them in the carpark, we have space, but I know from experience that's not ideal. We will need to use fulfillment storage services to store excess stock and bring it in as we need it. But so far we didn't find the right place near enough. Ultimately we will need to move to a big shed warehouse like we have in the UK and Slovakia.. but we have another year to wait for the lease to end.
We have a tradition at AW of big Buddha statues outside our warehouses.. So Juani jokingly went to get inspiration from our Buddha statue. 
Try not to stress, stay calm and we will find a way - we always do. 

Back in the UK.. Indian stock is arriving already.. We are delighted to add to the Hop Hare Brand a new range of bags and pouches.. Perfect for the spring and summer seasons. 
Lots of Indian and Indonesian products back in stock. Lots more on the way..

Anyway, my visit to Spain is very brief. Next week I will be in the UK.. I'm excited and looking forward to seeing the team. 
Somehow I don't think I'm going to have a heatwave problem there :)
But there are huge happenings - lots of exciting products in the pipeline. Stand by for updates.

Take care, have a lovely weekend.

David
