title: David's AW News: Strangely Peaceful
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


This week has been strangely peaceful in Bali, partly because of a drop in flights from the Middle East, partly because it's almost Eid (they call it Eid al-fitr here) so lots of people left Bali to go back to hometowns on other islands to celebrate the end of Ramadan with family. Also because yesterday was Bali new year and the famous "quiet day" (see below) lots of Gen Z types run away to Lombock or Gili Islands so they can party as normal.  So Bali right now is like the old days, strangely peaceful..
Last week I was telling you about my busy week.. and updates from Nepal.. if you missed you can catch up here.



Peaceful..

As promised I finally managed to upload the content we collected in India, on our trip to the gemstone artisan town: Khambhat.. which also holds some other Cricket related surprises..
You can check it out here.. It's a totally Off the Grid - kind of place.. and we met some amazing people and well just check it out..




Anyway I was telling you how peaceful Bali is right now.. 
This week was Nyepi — Bali’s famous Day of Silence.

I'm writing this in the coffee shop after just emerging from what felt like a kind of enforced reset… no travel, no lights, no work (they told me), no noise. You know even the airport shuts. The whole island goes still. Mobile internet is cut. Only tourist hotels have internet access. Now at 8am people are just emerging blinking into the real world.

The idea of a quiet day is, I understand..  a moment to reflect, reset, and some say to trick any wandering evil spirits into thinking the island is empty.

And I have to say… this morning as I type this.. is something special. The air feels lighter. Like the whole place has taken a deep breath. 

But the Night Before OMG!!… after I finished work and grabbed a bite to eat..  I ventured out..  the streets already darkened, many shops closed.. I'm going looking for Chaos (the Good Kind). Because the night before Nyepi is the complete opposite. I went out in search of the Ogoh Ogoh…someone told me to head to the road junction near McDonalds..  and more by luck than judgement found myself right in the middle of it. I brought the Insta360 camera.. 



Huge crowds, proper energy. And these incredible, slightly terrifying, larger-than-life monsters being carried through the streets on bamboo platforms. It was hot! The crowd got super dense, and as the Ogoh-Ogoh kept coming, drums playing, the crowd pushing.. a little bit alarming at one point I thought if someone goes down we all do.. 

But the creations are amazing.. Each one handcrafted by local youth groups — the Banjar — who spend weeks building them. And this is where it gets interesting… because they are more Than just monsters. These figures are based on Bhuta Kala — characters from Balinese Hindu mythology representing chaos, negative forces, ego, imbalance… all the things we carry around but don’t always face.  Here, they don’t hide them, they bring them out… make them big… make them loud… shake them about… even stage mock battles in the streets.

Then… they take them to the beach and burn them. And then after the madness and noise.. next day — silence.

Why Bali Is So Creative. 
Watching all this, it really clicked for me… maybe this is why Bali produces such incredible artisans. From youth creativity is encouraged. Because creativity here isn’t a “job”… it’s part of life. From a young age people are: Building things together in their communities, working with their hands, learning skills passed down through generations.

Creating for ceremonies, not just for sale. And later I guess the same hands that build those wild Ogoh Ogoh… are carving wood, shaping shells, weaving, painting… creating the products we work with every day. It’s the same energy — just expressed differently.

And you can feel that connection in what they make. In Bali artisan products are not mass-produced… not purely functional…
But made with a sense of story, spirit, and pride. 

Which brings me nicely to what’s coming next…

Easter… But Maybe Not As You Know It

Easter is just around the corner — and while for many it’s tradition, chocolate, and family time…
Check out our Easter pages..


There’s also a growing group of customers looking for something a little different.
A bit more natural. A bit more meaningful. A bit more artisan.. Here's my Alternative Easter Gifts Picks....

Bali wind chimes & bird boxes — something for the garden, bringing a bit of calm and nature into the space


Hand-carved wooden Buddha statues — for those leaning more towards mindfulness, reflection, or simply beautiful décor



And Holy made a really informative video about them..
Not everyone wants bunnies and bright colours…
Some are looking for something quieter. More thoughtful. Easter is Afterall about renewal.

And actually… that fits quite nicely with the whole Nyepi feeling.

Season of Love Rolls On
And of course — Easter is just one moment.
The Season of Love continues…
Easter → Father’s Day → Wedding season is warming up nicely already.

Each one a little reminder of what we really do in this business:  Help people give small acts of love.

A Thought to Leave You With
Watching Bali switch from full chaos… to complete silence… in the space of 24 hours… It  made me think.
Maybe we all need a bit of both. A time to create, express, build…
And a time to pause, reset, and appreciate.

Take care (or as they say here)) Hati-Hati!
More news next week.

David

PS
Almost forgot Hati-Hati Angels are perfect for easter..

title: David's AW News: Festival VIP - I don't like.
content_html:
Greetings from Kolkata, India


I just arrived last night, flying down from Kathmandu by Air India. I spent Thursday morning tying up the loose ends on two (maybe three) interesting deals, after a hectic week sorting out delayed orders and shipping problems.  Then saying goodbye to our sweet, delightful and kind (if a little slow) Nepali suppliers. 
My timing in Kathmandu turned out to be good, as I leave a big festival, a ten day holiday, is kicking off: The Dashain Festival which seems to consist of many mini fairgrounds, loud music and big red splodges on foreheads..  Factories and shops close, it's festival time guys!
As I land in Kolkata the famous Durga Puja is in mid-flow. Mr Chatterjee met me at the airport in full festival dress, as we drove to his hometown an hour away on the banks of the Ganges we pasted many brightly lit garish LED signs, banks of them, buildings banked in them. Passageways are vivid with festival lights. My pictures all came out a blur..  but I got a shot of a pandal (a kind of temporary art installation). Last week I was telling you about the crazy idea of a trip to Kathmandu just as massive flooding hit the city.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
 
Mr Chatterjee  at the airport.

New trends in Nepal.
Last time I was in Kathmandu, I kind of had the feeling we had seen everything (in artisan giftware) worth seeing. But this time I feel a new wave of creativity has swept the showrooms of Thamal. I didn't schedule enough time, so I think we need to come back soon. The Japanese and certain kinds of hippy Chinese traders have come here recently en masse, and I think their ideas and styles are influencing ideas and trends.  

Factory Visit
Mr Padam (our gentleman shipping agent) in his non-pushy way tentatively suggested I visit a new felt factory that he had recently become aware of. He said he was hearing good things and I should go see. So it was arranged and the other day two young people. Brother and Sister - good looking, but humble and sweet appeared in the lobby. "Mr David.. so pleased to meet you - please come".
We drove about an hour to the very edge of Kathmandu valley right under the foothills of Himalayan range. There I was shown a factory workshop where mostly ladies worked producing felt items. They told me due to the approaching festival many had left for mountain villages, so only about 50% of the staff remained. 
I have been to these places before and they are generally well organised and care for the workers and have good working conditions. All prerequisites of doing export business to Europe or the US. But this place with open views to the mountains and happy smiling workers was the best I have seen. I was surprised when the children introduced me to one of the ladies working on the factory floor.. this is our Mother, she's very hands on. 
We haven't quite finalized the deal.. although I'm confident we will, later I'll introduce you to this lovely family.

I have been working all day with Mr Chatterjee and his team - who are supposed to be on holiday - at his factory, connecting with our talented designer Sandra in Sheffield HQ and Tomas in Bali.. between us we finalised an exciting new product range.. after a long day.. Chatterjee took me to the festival to see some of the local famous Pandals.. which I can only describe as art installations with a loose religious theme. The main one had been curated by a local artist who is quite well known.  Everyone was happy and chatting, making selfies, dressed up in their festival best clothes.. the queue stretched for a long way.. maybe an hour wait all the way along the LED flashing light light street..

Chatterjee strides to the front of the line.. What's happening? I say as we are whisked around a curtain into a small VIP area.. where the local bigwig politician - who I have met before - is waiting to gladhand me then after some chit chat escorts us inside.. It's actually quite impressive, the theme is female empowerment. The centre piece is a giant crocodile eating a naked girl. And the Goddess is depicted with huge erm well you know.. well the artist wouldn't you know it is the same politician guy turns up for more selfies with the only white face in town.
We actually gate-crashed two long lines and entered as a VIP.. I'm asking why we can do this, I'm feeling a bit guilty.. so far no straight answer. I think white privilege still exists.
Chatterjee tells me that the all powerful Goddess Durga Puja is the most famous festival in Bengal and celebrates the Goddess fighting and killing the devil, and saving the world.

Hapi Drums - a happy medium. Drum up some happy sales.
Meanwhile in the UK - Indian products are rolling in.. lots of new stock online this week. Including (by popular demand) Hapi drums. We tried very hard to buy these in Java, Indonesia. There they produce relatively expensive musically tuned ones - too expensive for gift shops in China they have much cheaper but not nice sounding ones.. in the end we opted for Indian ones. We tried many producers, and our trusty old supplier in the heart of Old Delhi came up good.. approved by Bondhan (in Bali), our resident musical expert via Whatsapp.   

Halloween is fast approaching. Scary thought, not many days left..
We have special deals with FREE Magic Spell Candles & BIG Discounts. Plus Halloween Bath Bombs are an easy sell right now.

Wishing you an amazing weekend.
Remember to be kind to someone and look after your self.
Namaste 

David

title: Making Things a Little Better
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 Hope you are well, it's just a week on from Valentines day... but seems longer.

Last week I was telling you about the Year of the Ox, you can read it here and why I think everything is changing.. more on this below.

I have been working with our man Toni who manages AW Artisan in Spain.  Lots and lots of projects coming to fruition. The office there is buzzing and we are taking on more staff to cope with the extra business that has shifted from the UK to Spain.

One thing we did was make a nice rock and garden in front of the warehouse, it's not really our land but no-one seemed to care for it which seemed a shame. So my friend Clive (who can do anything handy) came and made it happen.. he tanked it with a liner and filled the space with three tons of nice white stones. Then Toni, Mario and I went to the local garden centre and bought lots of aloe vera plants.. I have them in my garden and I know they grow quickly and don't need much looking after. 



It's only a little thing, but it is improving the situation. and this makes me feel better.

Like Coco says if you can just make something a little better no matter how little, every day, every week.. then the world gets better. And the good news is - the next door neighbors already started something similar.

 

In the UK a much more substantial investment is taking place. If you are a regular reader you will know we moved to Affinity Park late last year. A huge 100,000 sq ft complex. And we just invested in 6000 racking locations. 

Some would say we are mad.. first of all even moving to a warehouse this big right on top of brexit ... and then investing in this much capacity. On top of this we have been expanding and kitting out our factory at the Parkwood site. Are we mad? 

Rodrigo likes to make time lapse videos and he made this.. 



Not so little.. but we made it better.

The world is changing.. and we might be mad,making big investments right now, but I feel that however it changes we need to be ready and agile and think positively.  

In June 2016, after the referendum. I really had gut feeling this was a huge mistake, and from that very week we started making plans for EU warehouses. Thank goodness we did, Brexit is a huge disaster - it's not project fear, it's reality. 70% of our EU customers have fled.. but at least they have somewhere to go for AW stock. And while we have a way to go before we recover all that lost trade - we have a plan and so far it is working. 

We continue to try to operate our Brexit trade bridge, and it's kind of working. But I'm not convinced we are giving our EU customers the best service possible. We will review the system at the end of March.

 

We really don't know what 2021 will bring.. but as I was thinking last week.. big wheels are turning. Things are going to change. We will see what unfolds.. I still feel that when the whole world prints money to solve problems then this macro event has to have consequences. Maybe we will enter a kind of Alice in Wonderland world.. 

 

Anyway, back to reality.. the next big thing is Mother's Day.. this year it is 22nd of March so only a few weeks away. We have been preparing some great deals and offers - see below.

It's unlikely that mother's will be taken for expensive lunches or taken away for a luxury break.. sadly.. but at least the gift trade can provide much needed pamper products to give Mum a bit of me time she deserves.

So get prepared for a bumper Mother's day.. especially via online trade and dropshipping.  check out.. AW-Dropship.com

 

So wishing you a safe and peaceful weekend.. 

Make something little.. anything.. a little better..

 

David

title: Opposite to what I expected
content_html:
Greetings from Morocco


We are in a small town almost at the feet of the mighty Atlas mountains. 
On Tuesday Toni (our man in Spain) and I took a very short flight from Malaga to Fez in Morocco. Short but from one world to another.. from Europe to Africa in an hour. 
And yesterday we made a epic road trip inland across all sorts of terrain to reach fabled the gemstone area..

Last week I was telling you about what I thought was an April fool but wasn't and also about what's happening in India - you can read about it here.

In Fez we had decided to spend two nights to check out the town and see what handicrafts might be found. Research suggested ceramics.. but we had no idea if that was all and even where to start.
Fez they claim has one of the world's biggest Medinas', a maze of market streets, narrow passages and hidden secrets. There are over 9000 streets and more shops than you could count selling everything imaginable. I chose a Riad hotel in the heart of the Medina and they sent a car to the airport to bring us to the hotel.

Fez airport is the total opposite of Manchester airport. Modern, small, friendly and very efficient. From the plane to the Passport hall directly where our covid checks where done in the queue by friendly efficient staff. After passport control our luggage was waiting, and a friendly guy with a board with our names greeted as we emerged. The car ride to Fez was also a surprise, beautiful villa's line the streets and new Fez is a modern city with a park style avenue though the centre, green tidy and with impressive fountains.  

Fez is really twin towns, the new and the ancient. Totally opposite places. The car dropped us at a carpark on the edge of the walled city where a porter was waiting with a trolly for our luggage, it's five minutes walk into the Madina to the Raid where we were staying. Down tiny passages between massive high ancient walls, out into wider passages lined with traders selling shoes, ceramics, musical instruments, leather.. back into another alleyway, round dogleg bends and finally arriving at an ornate heavy wooden door. Inside.. again totally opposite. 

From the stark mud coloured passage ways to a beautiful sunbathed courtyard, birds singing in trees surrounding a small pool. A lovely French lady was waiting with sweet mint tea and a warm welcome. Watch out for the tortoises she said they come indoor as well, and then she explained the secrets to not getting lost in the Medina and gave us tips on how to behave during Ramadan.
My room was two floors up with a balcony looking over the courtyard, and full of the type of homeware and handicrafts that we would love to stock at AW.  I would highly recommend this small hotel.. check it out here: Ryad Salamanda 
My sense is that in ancient times successful traders in the souk buying and selling goods along the trade route into and out of Africa made fortunes which for the sake of modesty they hid behind huge walls and built these opulent hidden worlds. 

Fez is relatively gentle compared to the hustle and hard sell of Marrakech, or maybe it's just the after effects of the covid era and or Ramadan.. but people are polite and peaceful greeting each other as they pass in the street. Even the informal street guides who help the lost find their way didn't demand tips or argue for more like we found in Marrakech. It's cool this time of year and lots of local guys where a kind of wooly monks habit with a peaked hood. It seems that when you wear this you walk differently arms straight down and a kind of staggered gait as though moving with important purpose. See our small first impressions video, spot the habit guys more interesting than the famous Blue Gate.. Go to Fez it's nice these days.


The nice French lady told us about the Ceramic Village near Fez.. so we went to see. She kindly advised us to get past the tourist trap showrooms pretending to be factories and seek out the artisan workshops in the back streets. 
And yes we found beautiful stuff, but one day is not enough time to make anything happen, we need to find the right kind of people (we can work with) and products (you will love) to make this work. 
But here are a few initial items we liked.. feedback is welcome.


Indian update.. Last week I was telling you about Mr Chatterjee & Son in Delhi, now they have moved to Jodhpur and checking out Rug and textile suppliers. 
And doing a good job, we will try to make a range of new rugs, cushions and possibly wall hangings..


Then yesterday we hired a car made a road trip across Morocco to the foot of the Atlas Mountains - across several very different terrains..  Morocco is more varied, dramatic and beautiful than I had thought. And HUGE!!
As we finally approached the town where we are staying though a vast open valley that felt like the wild west from a cowboy movie and on the side of the road we started to see traders selling fossils and minerals.. we stopped at one stall it was rough and ready and no-one to be seen.. But this is what we have come to find. Yesterday late afternoon we meet our supplier who gave us a whirlwind tour of the town (quite incredible), and right now, shortly after breakfast we are going with him to visit a mine. 

Our guesthouse is practically the only one in town.. and lets just say it is the opposite of the Riad in Fez.. 

I'll give you a full update next week.

Take care.

David

title: Bali Startup Ceremony
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

A lot has happened in the weeks we were in Nepal & India.. I'm excited to see our new office here. We call it the "Beach Office" to differentiate from the "Warehouse Office".

Last week I was telling you about our last days in India. Our first days in India we found ourselves in an goddamn awful hotel, the last days in India's finest: the Raj West End in Bangalore, rubbing shoulders with the rich and famous. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Whilst travelling from place to place, we have been receiving daily updates from Ringo and Bondan (our guys in Bali) as to the renovations progress.. our plan is to make the most beautiful place possible to work - and each evening we had a progress report and pictures. Hopefully we can attract the cool talented young people to come and work for us (and maybe for you).


Introducing our new office. AW-Advantage.com

We are recruiting staff right now, all day everyday interviewing young bright people. We will train a team of young people to understand the marketing methods of Europe.. to give careful consideration, attention to detail and with genuine passion - we believe that takes time and talent, and that is simply difficult to find in time pressed Europe.  A successful online business is a battle for attention.. of course you need excellent products, without that you have nothing, without good (cost effective) marketing your perfect products will not sell.. 

Today I dragged myself away from the new office to check on progress at AW warehouse, just up the road. I'm introduced to the latest recruits, we are expanding and the warehouse is totally crammed again. A container will be loaded to go to the UK this weekend and next week another to our Slovakia warehouse.  All the staff here are interested in the new business starting nearby, they wish us well.. But that's not all. In Bali a business must officially start with a ceremony.. and that ceremony must be on an auspicious date. All the key people must be there, the local village head person, staff and priest. 

Ringo and Made (our export manager) consult the Balinese calendar to determine which is the best date.   Every office in Bali has this calendar and we often have to consult it.






It's very complicated choosing a date. On the 9th there is a risk the business might suffer a fire in the future, on the 11th it is not good for the structure of the building.. but the 10th which is also Easter Monday and a good day for new beginnings.. seems to be perfect. I tell Ringo that this is important to do - and seems right to me... and he is absolutely delighted. Right now he is scribbling down a list of things to be done and joyfully calling the priests and people that do this kind of thing. 3pm in the afternoon is deemed the best time.. so now the wheels are in motion.. All very Ancient Wisdom.

Apparently, we will have to wear traditional dress, it should be interesting.. Full report next week

Meanwhile, it's Easter in Europe.. 

I trust your business is running well.. and wish you all the best for the future. Of course, this is a good time to reflect on new ideas and new beginnings.. why not check out our new products, these beautiful Natural Teak Display, and our unique Bamboo Display, this bamboo display will look amazing with the Hop Hare Socks. and if bathroom products are your niche, you can't miss out on Bath Salts in Vials.

Lots of deals to inspire you to grow your business to fresh heights.

After all (Ringo tells me) it is a great auspicious time to start something new. We will ask the priests to make offerings to bring blessings to the business but also blessings on you our customers.

So from everyone here in Bali, we wish you a wonderful Easter.. lot's of blessings, love, cute bunnies and of course copious amounts of chocolate!

Thanking you as always for your support (and reviews if you have time).

Take care

David

title: Getting Creative
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ Sheffield. 

It's now 41 days since the fire at AW, and still no meaningful response from the insurance company, although they are starting to thaw.
Banks, local council, insurance and property agents.. all seem to be moving slowly, soooo slowly. 
While on the other hand, our suppliers and the staff at AW have moved like the wind. Under immense pressure they have made so much happen - I'm proud of them and impressed.
Imagine one minute working out of 45 thousand square feet, and the next 14 thousand square feet.. and needing to do twice as much to recover.
Last week I was telling you about Gentle Giants and Angels at AW - you can read about it here.

Every day some new equipment arrives for production, the electricians are here full time wiring things up, every day another product group goes into production. Dushan and Neil are running around like demented bee's organising people and machines. 
See below for all the items back on line this week. This my friends is a really heroic effort, you have no idea how many stops have been pulled, all of them and then some more.
Meanwhile at the other end of the building James & Kane are trying their level best (and succeeding) in getting blood from stones.. whereas before we had twelve packing bays and a dropship department, now we have two bays and a dropship corner. Running shifts is part of the answer, but lots of problems are addressed with creative thinking, containers outside, persuading the shipping company to leave us a trailer we can fill with finished orders. Jacob is a superstar, he is the dispatch coordinator and another guy working crazy hours and looking frazzled. Goods in are no less stressed, some of Indian shipments arrived, the team are juggling space to find picking locations, inventing new racking configurations.. I'm impressed at the inventiveness. 
All this has been done, whilst wearing face masks and social distancing.   Well done guys.
Visitors that come here are genuinely flabbergasted at the pace of progress. 


So you can imagine, it's kind of distressing (for us all) when a customer posts two bad reviews for the same order - not because of anything we did, but because the courier company was slow.  (You know who you are!).
If you would like to encourage the team and lend us your moral support (and many of you have sent amazing messages already) why not post a good review Reviews.co.uk - Thank you :) 

When people pull together it's amazing what can be achieved. Take heart from this. 
Good news for the gift trade.. face masks are selling like hotcakes, and we have just received another shipment.. 
In other news Netflix new documentary "(Un) well", features Essential Oils, the essential oils themselves are given good press but some companies' dodgy MLM methods are exposed. AW essential oils are mostly in stock. Maybe a good time to stock up.

A new idea!
Hopefully we will be moving to a new warehouse soon. For the first time in years we should have more than enough space.
Which may well enable one of my pet ideas to happen. I'd be interested in your thoughts on this..
It's called: AW-Community  - basically it will allow you to (show and sell) your own products to Ancient Wisdom's (considerable) database of customers across Europe.   Say you have something you make, or import yourself, that you know sells well - send us the stock in bulk, we will store it in our warehouse and ship it when customers order. Every-time someone orders, you'd get an email notification and we'd send you money less a commission. Customers could order whilst ordering other things.  It would be B2B only, so you would need to be able to offer your products at wholesale rates. Obviously there would need to be some T&C but you get the basic idea.  I suspect there are thousands of great products out there just waiting to be given wings. 

Lots of new products from India here this week. When India went into lockdown, all these products got blocked, now they are starting to flow again.. 
It's a similar story with all our Nepal shipments - we are expecting lots to arrive in early September. 

So I hope you can have a nice weekend, take care, stay safe, wear a mask (an AW one!), be kind and stay calm.

David

title: Children Day
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about house hunting in Malaga...
Greeting to all.. here from China where almost no-one has heard about the Queens Jubilee, actually today is Children's Day and a day off from school, and a day that many parents are given as a day off.
They call it "Értóng jié" - it means, games, candy, holidays.
In the UK we are one of the only countries worldwide that doesn't have a children's day. Why? well you can blame that old skinflint: Gordon Brown who said "There is no positive need to the day, other than to add an unnecessary day off school or work. We have bigger things to think about". Whoops, bet that lost him a few votes. Here in China where they don't have votes they do have children's day. Go figure.
Interestingly in Spain they don't miss the chance for another fiesta, this date is celebrated on the 2nd Sunday of May, and it's called "Día del niño".
Anyway I don't want to spoil the fun and garden parties.. happy Jubilee weekend to all the UK and throughout the British Empire. I'm a bit jealous since I'm missing all that bunting and buttered scones. :( I'm sure it will be the most glorious full on fest of Britishness.
One things for sure, even though kids day has officially been ditched.. this year at least they will be having as much fun as anyone.
Hoping you have a great long weekend. If you are trading, don't work too hard and I hope you have time to join in the fun.
More news next week.. from somewhere else.
Regards
David
AncientWisdom.biz

title: Indonesia Says Thank You!
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


I really hope you are well and business is going well.
Last week I was telling you about the rampaging monkeys invading Ubud town, you can read about it here.
This week it's been all going on, far too many things happening to report on everything. But I will do my best..
In the UK more stock is arriving (all much delayed and/or in short supply) and this means we have been super busy as folk attempt to restock. Don't panic, we do have plenty more stock on the way.
The only problem is we are slipping behind with shipping times, the warehouse team are working flat out, overtime and weekends. Please be a little patient we are doing our best. 

Normally at the busy times we would take on lots of temp staff, but as you know even temp staff are in short supply. 
Now plenty of products are coming to fruition, samples made and approved, packaging sorted, prices and terms negotiated. So everyday this week we have been raising Purchase Orders and sending substantial deposits to much depleted bank accounts.
I have a sense of workshops, factories, home production all over Bali and also Java.. springing back to life on the back of our orders. In fact many artisan companies have been ticking over surviving on local trade or occasional re-orders from regular customers abroad. 
Some have gone, closed down, but nothing like as bad as the tourist trade in Bali which has been devastated. The pure tourist area around the Monkey Forest area is a broken down ghost town. Whilst the wholesale showroom area of Ubud still supports cool coffee shops and lunch stops. Our favourite is Starbaxo.. which serves the best Bakso in Bali - simple street food with a cool Bintang beer and superfast internet. 


Starbakso.

We had placed an order with one of the Molten Glass on Wood companies we deal with.. and since we hadn't visited in several years decided to go and visit and go over the product specs, packing etc.
The village is miles from anywhere almost on the banks of the volcano - the whole town seems occupied making the same range of products. The boss told us that he had an American customer that had boosted his business, but no orders recently. He had ninety people working with only a trickle of orders. So he was delighted to get our order, all ninety people working on it.. an absolute hive of joyful activity. One of the few businesses in Bali where the boss thinks big.
 


Meanwhile in Bali we are still in the midst of the Galuwan day festival period.. 10 days of the spirits coming down to earth to walk amongst us - tomorrow is the leaving day when the spirits go back to their realm and a big day of ceremonies.  
One tradition is the Barung boys.. groups of young kids wander the streets banging drums, two or three in Barong costume. Ringo told me it evolved from the Chinese dragon dancers many years ago and adopted Bali mythology. The Barong is the mystical king of the spirits, if he dances for you you'd better hand over a little cash. The Barung boys have been draining my small change for days.. In Ubud alone there must be ten troops roaming the streets. I tried to escape into a small warung (cafe) but they found me..



So much more I could report on, it's all happening especially since Bondan joined the team.. we have upped the activity level and are really making things happen like never before.


Bondan with one of our suppliers and Ringo.  We call this guy Mr Win-win, because he is always thinking up creative ideas to make products cost effective. He will message me everyday with "Hello Boss.. come and see me I have a win-win solution" followed by pictures of his latest designs. Like many of the artisans here he comes from another part of Indonesia, and his home village is really the back-up production area. Ubud is actually a hub of artisans from all over indonesia with different cultures and religions. We have suppliers from Java, Sulawesi, Kalimantan, Madura and Lombok. The way it often works is raw unfinished goods arrive on trucks and the finishing is done here to the specifications of the customers.
 
I know you are busy..so more updates next week. But on behalf of all the artisans and small businesses of Indonesia I want to say a big thank you for your support. 
You have no idea how much difference your regular orders make.. 

Take care.

David

One tradition is the Barung boys.. groups of young kids wander the streets banging drums, two or three in Barong costume. Ringo told me it evolved from the Chinese dragon dancers many years ago and adopted Bali mythology. The Barong is the mystical king of the spirits, if he dances for you you'd better hand over a little cash. The Barung boys have been draining my small change for days.. In Ubud alone there must be ten troops roaming the streets. I tried to escape into a small warung (cafe) but they found me.. So much more I could report on, it's all happening especially since Bondan joined the team.. we have upped the activity level and are really making things happen like never before. Bondan with one of our suppliers and Ringo. We call this guy Mr Win-win, because he is always thinking up creative ideas to make products cost effective. He will message me everyday with "Hello Boss.. come and see me I have a win-win solution" followed by pictures of his latest designs. Like many of the artisans here he comes from another part of Indonesia, and his home village is really the back-up production area. Ubud is actually a hub of artisans from all over indonesia with different cultures and religions. We have suppliers from Java, Sulawesi, Kalimantan, Madura and Lombok. The way it often works is raw unfinished goods arrive on trucks and the finishing is done here to the specifications of the customers. I know you are busy..so more updates next week. But on behalf of all the artisans and small businesses of Indonesia I want to say a big thank you for your support. You have no idea how much difference your regular orders make.. Take care. David

title: Happy Scary Halloween
content_html:
Greetings from Sunny Sheffield


Yes, I'm still here in Sheffield the birth place and home of Ancient Wisdom. The action this week is at AW-Aromatics where we are just completing our move into our brand-spanking-new warehouse and production home.
Last week I was telling you about the dreadful weather in our Indonesia home base on Bali. If you missed you can catch up here.. 
One video of a guy rushing to rescue a motorbike getting swept away went viral on social media, (you can see in last week's newsletter) - turns out that guy is one of our suppliers.. a new guy who is making a nice range of ceramic vases for us. He Whatsapped me while reading the newsletter.. That's me! 


Here is the bike rescue hero.. and his vases.. coming soon.

Speaking of extreme weather.. Here in Sheffield it was a warm balmy 20c the other lunchtime when I popped out to get a  sandwich. Seems very strange to me that it feels like summer in Sheffield at the end of October..
Well it's almost Halloween, a time when we enjoy scaring each other in a fun way.. and usually this is jolly good for business in the gift trade.. I hope so! Soon it will be time to set the clocks back, darker nights and Bonfire night set the starting gun (or rocket) for the Christmas season to seriously commence. And that is when the gift trade really moves up a gear.. We are already very busy.. and generally, stock levels are good. 

The main reason I am here is for AW-Aromatic's move into the new factory.. step by step - organised by Erik and the team production lines are dismantled and reconstructed in our new place. One of the biggest hurdles was moving the beast - the huge soap extruding machine we bought from a French company a couple of years ago. It needed a special forklift truck that can lift six tons.. they tell me only one such machine is available in Sheffield.. but the job was done without drama and today I can see the soap being produced again.

It's not been ideal moving production at our busiest time - in the runup to Christmas.. but as they say often in Yorkshire.. "It is what it is". We were supposed to move back in April.. but we live in difficult times and delays happened. Our growth plans had to be set back.. but now, finally it's time to think positive and all hands to the deck to move forward. 

We can easily double production and more.. 
My idea is that we choose our future customers carefully - our dream customers are our partners in this adventure, have similar values and are creative..
If you would like your own brand developed.. or need raw materials or direct supplies of bulk essential oils. Then head over to AW-Aromatics

Meanwhile, at our main warehouse it's all go..
New stock arrived from Indonesia, including some beautiful new oversized Dream Catchers.. which are hot selling. These are special next level.. merging the decorative Balinese umbrella known as a Payung with feather free dream catchers.. We developed them with one of our old suppliers.. as far as I know, totally unique to Ancient Wisdom. 
I'm also delighted to see our Macrame Angels catching on fast.. beautiful for Christmas but not exclusively a Christmas line.. you can sell all year round. 

Check out the deals we have below..

Next week I might have a big surprise for you.. you might be slightly shocked and surprised.. :)

Have an enjoyable, safe and not too scary Halloween weekend.

David

PS
Don't forget the clocks go back this weekend.. it always gets busy after that..

title: Brexit, the Ox and a new world order
content_html:
Greetings and Happy Chinese New Year!

 

Today is the first day of the year of the Ox (or the cow depending on who you ask), to your Chinese friends you can say: Xīnnián kuàilè.. (shin knee hen q-why le).

It's also almost Valentine's Day.. on Sunday.. probably the saddest loneliest Valentines day in history.. or at least the most Virtual Valentine  Day ever. Haha it's VVD..

It's been one year and 25 days since I said goodbye to my wife at Malaga airport, the plan was I would go to Indonesia and India (for business) and get to China to see her and the family by Valentines Day. 

But this year has not been normal and things didn't work that way.. if you have been following this newsletter you will know all the details.. 

Last week.. which already seems like another age.. I was telling you about how nothing is normal.. and a quick round up of AW life around the world. you can read about it here.



Last year was the year of the rat.. rats, those nasty creatures.. bringer of plagues. Kind of fitting in retrospect especially when it seemed like the reckless rats were in charge. The Ox on the other hand is the symbol of steady hard work, rebuilding and regrowth. Let's hope 2021 is a year of rebuilding. A year in which the steady sensible hardworking types take over from the reckless rats.  

But let's face it  the world has changed, everything has changed.  I have been thinking about this a lot lately. The marco events that have hit the earth like meteorites from space are.. 

1. Tribalism fueled by social media. Symptoms of which are nationalist leaders around the world causing things like Brexit, trade wars and reducing productivity money like crazy.

2. The Pandemic. Has affected the world in all sorts of terrible ways, including the cost of fighting it. Less obvious, but important is the reduced productivity as people sit at home not producing anything.

3. QE. Quantitative easing. Basically means governments are printing money and buying stuff with it.. to fix the world's problems (whilst making super rich people even more rich), but risking massive inflation. It worked in 2007 because everyone got busy with that extra money.

4. Global warming needs to be fixed and at some further cost.

 

Some say QE without increased productivity is going to brew the mother of all economic storms.

 

Let's hope we can weather the storm.. it's already cold enough in the UK.. But one thing is for sure, in times of trouble folks still give each other comforting gifts, they increasingly want to make their homes more homely and safe.

And stuff.. (gold, houses, crypto, giftware stock) as opposed to money cannot be devalued. Well crypto currency is a gamble it could go down, but at least the governments of the world are not messing with it. 

Stock and crypto is probably better than cash right now, well stock that doesn't have a date life. Obviously fresh fish is not a good investment.  

 

So at AW we have been buying stock like mad. Five containers arrived this week.. To house it we are building 6000 racking locations in our Affinity warehouse in Sheffield, which will be finished on Sunday. Next week another five containers are expected.

That means lots of items back in stock.. even some new products coming from India. In our EU warehouses also we are stocking up as trade diverts from the UK to the EU.. 

 

We are still doing our best to ship to our loyal long suffering EU customers direct from the UK using our "Brexit Bridge". This is where we sell a whole truck load of orders from AW UK to AW Slovakia, who pay the duty, vat and import charges.. and then we deliver to the EU customers.. easy.  NOT easy.. yesterday Tomas was almost crying, Katka was stressed.. as quickly as we fix the problems customs in the EU find more for us. You have read the news about the number of forms being filled in, and if you don't use black ink are rejected. That's nothing, it is much worse.  Fortunately we have been importing from outside the EU for 20 years so we know how it works. 

Four uniformed customs guys turned up at our warehouse in Slovakia, aggressively demanding to check individual products. 500 cartons, how do you find the carton with the particular product in it they wanted to see? Well Raul our IT guy quickly wrote the software to identify the carton requested.. they were determined to find something with the wrong tariff code, something under valued, something miss described. One guy said to the staff the directors (that's me and Tomas) will be facing criminal offences. Tomas had travelled to the UK was self isolating and had to deal with all this from his bedroom.  They of course didn't find anything but to be called a criminal is another level of stress. At AW we are whiter than white, we pay all taxes, we use the tariffs always as suggested by customs whatever the duty charged. Tomas almost cried last night, he told me he doesn't want to do this crap. He wants to be productive, design and make great products to make our customers happy. And I agree.

 

Lots of companies have already given up shipping to the EU, we will continue, for now. But it's not the best service we can give our customers.

 

Anyway peace, love and forgiveness are the antidotes to this kind of nastiness affecting simply doing business.. and as it is practically valentines day let spread the love..

Hope you can have a best possible weekend and survie the Beast from the East 2, and whatever else you need to deal with. 

 

Take care, stay safe, virtual hugs.

Happy Year of the OX.

 

David

title: David's AW News: An Important Announcement
content_html:
Greetings from Bali


Hope life is treating you well.. and business is booming.
Last week I was telling you a little secret from AW history.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
In Bali it's the wet season, plenty of rain.. I have spent half the week seemingly driving up or down roads that have turned into rivers..
But every now and then the skies clear and the air is fresh and clean and you catch beautiful views.. 
The other morning Mount Agung appeared like magic across the bay in Sanur.


Snakes Alive!!
So yes there has been big rain in Bali again.. disrupting things. And it seems like various animals are moving indoors. The other day we found a huge lizard hiding in the curtains in the office, and then minutes later found two big snakes exploring our meeting room. Arya (one of our developers) and Bondhan bravely captured him and took him somewhere far away.  The other one escaped and is still at large.


Long time suppliers..
The other day Bondhan and I went to the Sukawati art market, where we have a few suppliers. All lady bosses.. I don't know why but many of our best suppliers it's the wife who is the boss.



This is Wayan who makes these kinds of products.. She was telling me that it's been 10 years we have been doing business and I checked if it's true.. How time flies.. the fact is there are many people, staff, suppliers and customers who have been with Ancient Wisdom literally for decades. Wayan since she has known us has had two children, grown her business substantially.. moved into a nice house. Recently invested in two substantial laser engraving machines, (imported from China) and doing good business engraving for other artisans. I'll upload a video about the artisans of Bali soon.

30 Years Anniversary
Yes it was almost 30 years that I founded AW on a street market in Sheffield. If you didn't read the story.. it's here.. Story of Ancient Wisdom. It starts like this.. and on that first day I almost gave up..

The Very First Day - 16th November 1995

As I recalled it...  

It was a wet cold Thursday morning a long time before Google and Facebook, and as I laid out my market stall on a Sheffield street I was more than apprehensive about what people would think. But I was ready by eight, my humble offering laid out on that simple stall.. and stomping from foot to foot I awaited my first customer.

A few months earlier, I'd been reading a book called "Ancient Wisdom" - now out of print. The book highlighted many things that seem out of place in history - the pyramids, Stonehenge etc. At the same time I'd been researching aromatherapy. It struck me that essential oils had been used for thousands of years and ancient people must have known more about them - (healing and enchanting) than perhaps we did. So I put the two together and devised the brand of "Ancient Wisdom" slowly (very slowly, no Internet remember) I found supplies of oils. I found a potter down in Stoke who made me my own design of oil burner, and invested in a pallet load of candles.

The truth was I was stone broke, every penny and more I put into my unusual retail business. In those days no-one had any idea what aromatherapy was, oil burners were a new fangled thing and this was Yorkshire!
The first person to approach was a well built lady of colour with a broad Yorkshire accent. Picking up a bottle of Lavender oil she asked me bruskly "what's it good for lad?" Oh I said recalling my Julia Lawless quotes.. "it's good for relaxing, will help you sleep and if you burn yourself it's an amazing healing oil".

Well I can remember it clear as day.. she looked at me, took me in with big brown eyes, and in a low voice said; "You are completely bloody bonkers". And wandered off to the fruit and veg.
You can imagine how I felt. That first day I sold one lavender oil and gave some tea tree away to a spotty teenage girl. I went home and almost packed it in.


But I didn't give up.. and here we are 30 years later.

As I type this all of AW are having a low key party..



Te3
he actual day is on Sunday.. 
On Sunday we are planning to make an important announcement.. 
Please subscribe (if not already) to our YouTube channel to get notified.


There is also a new "Can you sell this?" Video from Holly who has been taking a deep dive into the world of Agnes & Cat.

Our Lake District inspired brand has been growing and finding many new fans recently. Check it out!



 Discover Agnes + Cat today..


It's almost the middle of November.. getting so busy.

Soon it will be Christmas.. (again) - the years go past so quickly..


Wishing you an absolutely lovely weekend.

David

title: Can you guess the banned word?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 It's that day already.. Happy Black Friday! 

Were we continue to get to know our new Spanish team, training them, preparing the warehouse and getting ready to launch the new AW concept in Spain & Europe.
It's all go I can tell you.. everyday a whirl of activity. There is so much to do, and so much to make happen and make happen quickly.. that Tomas (who is working round the clock poor guy) has come up with a new policy.. and banned the use of a popular Spanish word.. Can you guess what it is? Answer below, see if you can guess the banned word before the end.

We have a list of things to make happen, and our team is quickly taking the various tasks and making them happen one by one.. I love this part of company forming / team building / 
Last week I was telling you about a bombshell that hit us (figuratively) you can read about it here.

Today the racking company will deliver the racking, on Monday and Tuesday they will install it. And... actually I just arrived at the warehouse and huge truck is already here, early morning with all the racking our man Toni's first folk-lift job is unloading racking for 600 pallet spaces (later we will double this).. It's another first.. there are lots of firsts.. first customer registration, first happy customer, first re-order, first company lunch.. 


We all make unconscious (possibly irrational) prejudicial assumptions based on nationality.. eg.. Irish people are a bit thick.. Swedish totally blond.. French cheese eating communists..   Politicians are all dodgy and always bending the truth..  all obviously wrong on so many levels, erm except the last one possibly.. but we still laugh when a joke is made along these lines.   Spanish people are known to take things easy, to never rush, to never manage to finish a job, never answer an email - they are lazy and more interested in a party than working hard no?...  And yes I can think of particular people who might fit that description. But hey you can find that type of useless dipstick person in any country in the world. But I want to say categorically it certainly doesn't apply in Spain anymore (if ever) as a generalisation.  We are working with a awesome fantastic group of companies and people who are totally tuned to get things done.
I'm seriously impressed with the professionalism of the Spain companies and people we are working with. But still .. as we sort things out occasionally that banned word crops up... did you guess..?

Meanwhile back in the good old UK at AW HQ - things are beyond busy - everyone is picking and packing orders - everyone and their auntie. It's all hands on deck.. it's none stop running. Katka (our main girl in UK) is doing her level best to keep everyone sane and balanced. We are almost always a bit too busy - but this week and next are peak way-too-busy-weeks.. 
If you need stock for Christmas (and you do we know, we know you do) then my only advise is get it in as early as possible.. 



Here the warehouse is been painted white, the racking was delivered, offices are been made cool and trendy, the team are been trained in all things Ancient Wisdom - its all happening here today.. and that word that is banned..if you didn't guess it's: mañana.. well no-one dare use that! It gets done now - today..  or as we say in this office.... Lo quiéro para ayer!!    - I want it yesterday!! 

And yes I know you want / need your orders like yesterday.. we are working on it..

Take care - hope you survive Black Friday.. now it's all onward and upward to Christmas and beyond.

David

And... actually I just arrived at the warehouse and huge truck is already here, early morning with all the racking our man Toni's first folk-lift job is unloading racking for 600 pallet spaces (later we will double this).. It's another first.. there are lots of firsts.. first customer registration, first happy customer, first re-order, first company lunch.. We all make unconscious (possibly irrational) prejudicial assumptions based on nationality.. eg.. Irish people are a bit thick.. Swedish totally blond.. French cheese eating communists.. Politicians are all dodgy and always bending the truth.. all obviously wrong on so many levels, erm except the last one possibly.. but we still laugh when a joke is made along these lines. Spanish people are known to take things easy, to never rush, to never manage to finish a job, never answer an email - they are lazy and more interested in a party than working hard no?... And yes I can think of particular people who might fit that description. But hey you can find that type of useless dipstick person in any country in the world. But I want to say categorically it certainly doesn't apply in Spain anymore (if ever) as a generalisation. We are working with a awesome fantastic group of companies and people who are totally tuned to get things done. I'm seriously impressed with the professionalism of the Spain companies and people we are working with. But still .. as we sort things out occasionally that banned word crops up... did you guess..? Meanwhile back in the good old UK at AW HQ - things are beyond busy - everyone is picking and packing orders - everyone and their auntie. It's all hands on deck.. it's none stop running. Katka (our main girl in UK) is doing her level best to keep everyone sane and balanced. We are almost always a bit too busy - but this week and next are peak way-too-busy-weeks.. If you need stock for Christmas (and you do we know, we know you do) then my only advise is get it in as early as possible.. Here the warehouse is been painted white, the racking was delivered, offices are been made cool and trendy, the team are been trained in all things Ancient Wisdom - its all happening here today.. and that word that is banned..if you didn't guess it's: mañana .. well no-one dare use that! It gets done now - today.. or as we say in this office.... Lo quiéro para ayer!! - I want it yesterday!! And yes I know you want / need your orders like yesterday.. we are working on it.. Take care - hope you survive Black Friday.. now it's all onward and upward to Christmas and beyond. David

title: David's AW News: Next Level / Meet James
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ Sheffield.

Hope you guys are doing well and getting busy in the run up to Father's Day.

 

It's another Bank Holiday weekend - hopefully with just enough sunshine to bring out the crowds. 

Last week I was telling you about our beautiful showroom (this week open week) full of AW products and my stories.. Almost every product has a personal story behind it. I shared one or two, if you missed it you can catch up here.

Almost everyone I talked to likes to read this newsletter so it felt like meeting old friends. And when you chat you learn.. and I'm all ears.. thankyou guys for the pointers and ideas.

A big shout-out to Rodrigo, Martina and Sandra who have put so much work into the showroom. And welcomed our friends and customers with open arms.and cups of tea. 

 

We have to make a special mention for Sandra who is the designer behind many of our products, but more particularly the mastermind behind the Hop Hare concept product range. We have a Hop Hare corner of the warehouse, and once folks understand that this is actually special.. and then begin to understand the magic, manifestations and cast of characters woven into the products... you can't get them away.  This month Sandra's Hop Hare brand was chosen for the cover of Gift Focus Magazine.. that''s next level!

In Other News.. 

I'd like to welcome local boy James to the AW board of directors. The first such appointment in over 5 years.. (we take these things very slowly). James has worked for AW for just over ten years starting as an order picker / packer and moving to warehouse manager, and then operations manager. He successfully took our AW-Fulfillment business from zero to a million pound business in short order. He has helped to organise the AW warehouses in Spain, Slovakia and even Indonesia.. and so much more.  

Katka, Tomas and myself welcome today James to join the AW board of directors. It's the next level!

 

Fun facts about James.. he flies helicopters (up to very high levels) when he has the chance, loves travelling to the USA, hails from Barnsley, can fix anything mechanical with just a glance, a proud Yorkshireman (like me)  and last time I checked (ladies) he is still single - and so young - not yet 30. I'm sure you will wish him continued and growing success as he joins the team effort to deliver the best in giftware and services to our customers.  For sure he will play a part in taking AW to the next level.

 

Meanwhile...

Lots and lots are back in stock this week.. including (back in fashion) Crystal Balls and Money Cats..  just the tools we need at Ancient Wisdom to take us to the next level!!

 

The other thing we need is a next level artisan herbal tea.. and you will be happy to know that's also back in stock.

Next Level - Helping YOU Think Big!

New this week.. organised by Tomas and Raul.. we have the PastPay credit system installed to help you think big and expand this summer. 

If you are a registered company (sorry sole traders, later we will help you) and thinking-next-level-big you can check HERE (then via the shopping cart) to see if you have been allocated a credit - up to £16,000 is available for many regular customers of AW.

 

A little sad & annoying news.. 

I mentioned before that Coco (my wife and your agent in China) would be coming to Europe on an epic six week trip, with all her family. Her Mother and Father (first time out of China), Coco's son and wife and George & Elly the two grandchildren. Coco has a Spain ID card but the rest of the family needed passports and visas. So we paid the best visa agent we could find to make sure all our paperwork was correct and in place, lots of work, expense and a group trip to the Spanish consulate in Shanghai. Yesterday the passports came back and all of them had been rejected. No visas. No reason given. It seems so brutal. I can tell you we are one depressed family.

Oh well, usually when something bad happens, something good comes.. 

 

Next week I will be somewhere different.. see you there..

But some good news.. Ula, who you will remember badly strained her leg on a bouncy castle at our AW garden party two weeks ago.. is back hobbling a little, but bravely back to work.

Have a lovely (Next Level) Bank Holiday weekend - hopefully the free shipping will makes it even better!

 

All the best David

title: The Chapatti Redeye to Delhi
content_html:
Greetings from Delhi, where I have just landed. Last week I was telling you about out hot it was in China (read it here). Last week in Yiwu the word was a plane had crashed in the little airport there. Impossible to find what happened initially, the web was quickly blocked. It turned out that the heat and direct sunlight on the end of runway had melted some of the tarmac, and the plane landed and sunk into the runway like swamp water. No one was hurt fortunately.
I'm writing this with slightly jet lagged brain power, so please forgive any typo's.
I've just come on the Midnight Shanghai to Delhi Air India flight - the Chapatti Redeye. Always an experience. Before now I have been one of a handful of passengers on this infamous night run, able to sleep peacefully across three seats. But last night was almost full, mostly Indian businessmen heading home, a few brave Chinese businessmen and women heading out, and for the first time a number of Chinese families on sightseeing holidays to India. India like many countries has just woken up to the fact that Chinese tourists are big spenders, and there's a lot of them. They represent a significant boom in tourism revenues, so they have recently made it relatively simple recently for Chinese to get a visa - so the flight is full :(.
India is home to some of the best airlines in the world! Air India is not one of them. The Chapatti run (as I call it) is delightful in an archaic chaotic kind of way. Flight safety demonstration? Not that I noticed? Use of mobile phones and electronic devices prohibited during take off. No issue. The Indian sari clad ladies have long given up trying to control the Indian businessmen, and barely had a word of Chinese. Instead barely at cruising altitude the ladies were pouring super large whisky's and delivering them to the Indian guys almost without asking. I asked for a G&T and was thrust a handful of mini bottles and three cans of tonic. Get the buggers nicely sozzled and they will be less trouble, is clearly the policy.
After the fastest meal distribution, and half hearted tidy up, that's the last of the we saw of the stewards on the 6 hour flight. I could see the Chinese tourist were not happy with the food, what do you do with a chapatti?, and what no chopsticks? Early stage culture shock setting in.
A rather relaxed captain came on the tannoy to announce our imminent arrival in er.. Delhi, a slightly worrying pause as he obviously checked - in fact - where we were going. Your luggage will be on belt 12, and the local time is 2.40am. Luggage was on belt 10, and it was 1.40am.. but only minor things. I read recently about an Air India captain who went to the toilet, and locked himself out of the cockpit. He was rattling and banging on the door trying to wake the sleeping no.2 inside.
Landing in Delhi at 2am local time, is not such a bad idea, you can breeze through the immigration and customs without any trouble. Everyone is half asleep. My hotel had sent a car to pick me up. They remembered me. Then it struck me, how come in such a hectic, crazy place like India they can produce the best run, and elegantly calm hotels in the world?
Only a few days in India, and so much to do... must get on.
Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: HEATWAVES & Opportunities
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.


Hope you guys are doing well and enjoying the weather. For once it's HOTTER in the UK than Spain. Enjoy!
Last week I was telling you about my journey from Indonesia to Spain, Father's day and our summer BBQ in the UK.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
Sadly I don't have much time in Spain.. shortly I'm travelling again.. I'll miss the sunrise in Spain. As I sit down to type this it's 7am and this is the view.. 


 I love my house in Spain, but never get much time to stay here.. 

June here is a time of long, warm days (not as warm as the UK) and some lively local festivals. Last weekend I went along to the Marbella feria and had a wander around.. It didn't seem so busy. Spain  seems to be getting its knickers in a twist about over-tourism with demonstrations everywhere.. So yes there is a delicate balance between visitors and community. But it's more complicated than blaming tourists for everything. 
I did get time take our man Toni for a beach lunch to celebrate his birthday, so I have been soaking up the atmosphere - white wine and sardines - while keeping tabs on Ancient Wisdom. Perfect summer!

This week, Spain is gearing up for the Noche de San Juan, it's on Monday.. and I won't be here.. It's when they have bonfires on the beaches some say to welcome the summer solstice others to celebrate John the Baptist. .But I'm off somewhere else.. you'll find out next week.

Volcano trouble in Indonesia. More trouble in Java. And an opportunity.
Bondhan called me from the Ukulele supplier in central Java.. It seems the locals are protesting there also. Truck drivers are on strike over something (I don't understand) and the container he went there to load has been delayed by ten days. Meanwhile (you will have seen the news) a volcano on the island of Flores is erupting, disrupting flights. 
So our export lady Made cancelled her flight from Bali and Bondhan is stuck in Yogyakarta.. 



I just had a long chat.. I think it's a good opportunity for him to visit the Rudraksha bead farming area, it's a few hours drive away in the mountain forests.. but now is the harvest season and a good time to buy the Tears of Shiva beads. I was thinking if he goes now he could secure some rare shapes. 


We discovered the area quite  by accident back in February..  I wrote about it here.  
Then it was the wrong time to secure supplies, but we made some good contacts and now might be a good time.

Yes, everyone assumes that the  Rudraksha beads come from India and Nepal..they are associated with Indian culture and used in jewellery and bangles and of course the 108 bead malas. But it turns out the best quality comes from this mountain forest area in Java.  The locals told us that Chinese, Indian, Nepalese and Balinese are the biggest buyers. With Indian and Chinese behaving like mafia trying to corner the market.  We had a super interesting trip there.. I really want to go back. 

Meanwhile in the UK.. lots of great stock arriving at the moment.. all those travels, deals and hard work finally coming to fruition..
And it's always so satisfying when the guys in the office love the products and get enthusiastic. Rodrigo is very enthusiastic about the new range of copper and magnets jewellery that just arrived. We worked hard to get these designed and organised, and our guy from Agra, India has done a really good job. (see below).`


Wherever you are, I hope you’re finding moments of inspiration and connection. And grabbing those opportunities when they crop up!

Have a lovely heatwave weekend. Enjoy!!

All the best

David

title: David's AW News:  The Longest Day, Father's Day & A Suitcase Full of Soap
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Last week I was telling you that summer was gathering pace. Well... this weekend it officially arrives. It's midsummer today is day 10 of our Midsummer madness promo.
The Summer Solstice is almost upon us. The longest day of the year. Father's Day. Football. San Juan beach parties here in Spain. And somehow, as often happens at Ancient Wisdom, lots of other things seem to be happening all at once. Big news from our corner of the world... Coco has arrived in Spain. Quite a journey, too. Yiwu to Beijing to Munich to Malaga. Air China with Lufthansa codes on the European leg. She tells me they flew over Russia, and her rather futuristic new Huawei foldable phone seemed keen to confirm it by greeting her with a "Welcome to Russia" message mid-flight. The phone itself is fascinating - one of those China-first gadgets that makes you realise the future sometimes arrives there before we ever see it in Europe.

And speaking of arrivals... Tomas has just landed in Malaga, too.

This time of year has quietly become an Ancient Wisdom tradition. Both Coco and Tomas celebrate birthdays around now, so whenever possible, we gather part of the team together here in Spain. A little work, a little planning, some good food, plenty of ideas and usually just enough chaos to make things interesting.

The timing couldn't be better because we're already planning the next wave of sourcing adventures.

Coco is particularly keen that we visit China's famous Crystal City. Apparently, if you are in the crystal business, this is a place you simply have to see. Knowing us, this will probably involve several flights, a road trip, a wrong turn somewhere, and hopefully a few exciting discoveries along the way.

Meanwhile, something else has caught my attention.

More and more of Coco's family and friends are asking her to bring Spanish olive oil soaps back to China. Every year, the requests seem to grow. At this rate, she may need a suitcase dedicated entirely to soap. An elderly woman in Coco's hometown was given a slice of the Donkey Milk soap (from Coco's mum) and claims her lifelong skin condition has been cured! Looking at the enthusiasm, perhaps they are onto something. (See Olive Oils Soaps here).

Back in Malaga, I was trying to show Coco the famous purple Jacaranda trees. Sadly, we were a week or two too late. The blossom is mostly gone now, with only a few last splashes of purple hanging on before summer takes over completely.

Talking of summer...

Our Midsummer Madness promotion is sizzling along nicely. Like a beach barbecue with someone constantly adding more charcoal, it seems to be gathering momentum every day. The deals have become slightly more enthusiastic than originally planned... but then again, it is Midsummer Madness.

It's all about Love Magic in Poland!

If you missed last week's newsletter, you can catch up here and see how all this seasonal chaos started.

And now we head towards the big.. BIG.. weekend.

Father's Day.
The Summer Solstice.
Football fever.
San Juan bonfires lighting up the beaches across Spain.
Perhaps even a new star rising in Makersfield.

On a different level, a new product from Agnes + Cat - Bath Fizzer Gift Sets has arrived. The warehouse in the UK has never been so busy, with lots of stock arriving this week from China, India, Indonesia and Nepal!   A summer storm of midsummer madness orders and dizzy rush or arrivals.. It's all go. 

Whatever you're doing, I hope your shops are buzzing and fizzing, your customers are smiling, and a little bit of midsummer magic finds its way into your business.

The deals continue... but not forever. 

So grab them while they are hot.

Wishing you a wonderful weekend, good trading, and all the warmth, light and opportunity that summer brings.

Peace, Love & Midsummer Magic, and Happy and Chilled Father's Day to all!

David

title: Have yourself a merry little Christmas
content_html:
Greetings from Ancient Wisdom HQ
Let your heart be light
From now on,
our troubles will be out of sight
Have yourself a merry little Christmas,
Make the Yule-tide gay,
From now on,
our troubles will be miles away.  
So goes the words of the song, and so here we are dancing merrily as we work.. before breaking up (literally) until the new year.
Tomorrow is also the winter solstice, deep mid-winter, the shortest day, so Yuletide Greetings!! From now on the days get longer and warmer, that's a good reason to celebrate no? Make the Yule-tide gay :)
Friends, customers, readers of this newsletter.. it's almost the end of the year, Heavens! the decade even! 2020 will bring many rewards and many (I feel) challenges - but for now Our troubles will be far away.. as we look forward to the festive season. A warm heartfelt thanks to all our customers for all your support, feedback and trade in 2019 . And now on-wards - and upwards - together. It's the end of the decade, and for a second join me as I glance back 10 years to 2009.. 
10 years ago.. AW had just moved to a new modern warehouse (we are still here much expanded taking over most of the business park) we had 30 employee's (now almost 100) We had a partnership with a Spain company that (despite huge effort) ended in tears, but now we have just launched AW Artisan - from a new warehouse in Malaga.. and it's going great guns. 
Two years ago we founded AWGifts.eu  from a Slovakian base and this is growing like a weed supplying all Eastern Europe.
 
In 2012 we started our adventure in Indonesia, regular readers will have heard stories about our man Ringo.. who has helped AW expand it's range and suppliers of Artisan products. We moved from our small Ubud warehouse to a new 1000 sq meter warehouse just outside Denpasar this year.


Pictures from the Bali warehouse yesterday..

In China, on the back of all this expansion our small candle factory (making soywax candles) is busy busy, and our Agent - Coco.. has shipped a record number of containers.. Coco took over the job in 2006 and this year shipped 30 containers (up from 8 in 2005). Well done Coco.. There are other corners of AW - like our IT team in Kuala Lumpa or new agents in Nepal and Morocco.. but a special mention for our India agent Mr Chatterjee.
In India we continue to invest in the orphanage we support. Mr Chatterjee (our agent in India) has worked hard and unstintingly to support the children's home. After fixing the buildings and making it nice (when we found it in 2013 there was no running water, electricity the roof was broken in the kids in little more than rags). Recent years we invested in teachers.. an English teacher, a computer teacher, and an Art teacher. Now as they come of age the kids are getting decent jobs..they can chat to me in pretty good English.. and this Christmas they are even holding an art exhibition of their work in the local town centre.
Merry Christmas from India! 
Back here 
The guys are unloading an China container, it's stuffed full of eco-friendly bamboo toothbrushes and lots of other non-plastic items.. I'm so happy and excited.. Perfect for Spring 2020..
It's the first of several containers that will arrive during the Christmas season the early part of next year.  So expect lots of new Spring stock right of the bat in 2020 the Eco-Friendly Year at AW.. we have lots of lovely earth-friendly products coming your way..
The goods out and customer service teams are having a little mad rush working to dispatch the last of the orders, tidying up all those loose ends and last minute jobs, but they are having fun I can see. Party hats, boxes of chocolate everywhere, and Xmas music drifting in the air.. Very much a party/work day today.. this spirit of Christmas, peace and goodwill. Fun and festivity and we'd like to spirit this jolly feeling to all our customers, and readers.
The way Christmas falls this year means our customers (You) have a few more days of retail rush.. which we hope is fun and successful. We'll be back on the 2nd Jan 2019 working hard to get your orders off as quick as possible (despite our hangovers).. you can order anytime over the Christmas period, and we'll be dispatching orders in rotation.. first in first out.
It's been a wonderful year, an incredible decade.. a roller-coaster, a party, an exciting ride. If you have followed along by reading this weekly newsletter, I hope you have enjoyed been involved.
Who knows how 2020 will pan out, (don't mention Brexit), but for sure it will be exciting. Big Retail is in a bigger mess than ever.. and I firmly believe now is the time that the independents (like you) can shine..
Come all ye.. Artisan Retailers, Innovative Independents, The Enthusiastic Specialists, Ethical Traders... you guys are in the antecedent 2020 and the next decade will be awesome!
Finally ..

On behalf of everyone at Ancient Wisdom I'd like to wish you a relaxing and peaceful Christmas and let's hope and pray.. bright positive new year.
With Fun Festive Greetings, Have yourself a merry little Christmas, now... 
See you next year :)
David

title: AW Christmas Greetings
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield.

I'm home for Christmas - at AW HQ in Sheffield. Actually writing this from our production company (AW-Aromatics) - last day today so this morning is a big deep clean, tidy up and leave everything perfect for next year.
I always feel a bit guilty because I know most of our customers are crazy busy at this time.. and here we are gently winding down.

We have a Christmas tradition where when the work is finished we order in pizza and wind-down wishing each other all the best - before heading off..
Shortly I'll drive across Sheffield to Affinity to HQ and do the Pizza thing again..

This is my last message in 2022. It's been another strange, sometimes challenging but anyway a wonderful year..
A year ago almost everyone at AW was down with covid after having a mask free party for the first time.. a year later it seems like everything and nothing has changed.. lots of staff off with covid or flu - get well quickly guys.
But in one year a lot has changed at AW.. Many many new products came online over the year.. this week alone - New Konjac Sponges, Hop Hare Bamboo Socks and a range of Feng Shui water fountains. Three amazing product groups I'm sure you can make money with in 2023. Anyway, much more to come next year.. we have big plans. Hope you are coming along for the ride..

Last week I was telling you about arriving in the UK to lovely snow. (If you missed it you can catch up here) Oh.. I thought that's nice... we are in for a white Christmas!!

They said there'll be snow at Christmas
They said there'll be peace on Earth
But instead it just kept on raining

But it seems like it's not a White Christmas at least here in Sheffield. But who knows it could snow yet..
This morning I checked in with all corners of AW - our teams all over the world all working hard until the last minute delivering great gifts for your business. From different worlds but all have one thing in common..
We are all immensely grateful for our customers - we are honored and happy to serve you and the support you give us is appreciated - worldwide!!

From HQ and all around AW - in Slovakia (AWGifts.eu) - in Spain (AWArtisan.eu) - at Aromatics ( AW-Aromatics.com). From India (Mr Chatterjee and the Children's home we support), Indonesia and China (My wife and the grandkids)..



A BIG thank you for your support - your trade is very much appreciated and it's been a pleasure and delight to work with you.

Our message is to wish you a wonderful peaceful Christmas - and hopefully a wonderful new year.

We wish you a hopeful Christmas
we wish you a brave New Year
All anguish pain and sadness leave your Heart and let your road be clear
Maybe there'll be snow this Christmas
Let's hope there'll be peace on Earth
Hallelujah, Noel, be it Heaven or hell
We wish you the Christmas of your Dreams.. and maybe a white one..

(apologies to Greg Lake)

Enjoy your Christmas

All the very best from David and all at AW.
