title: Incredible Indian Banking
content_html:
They have a tourist advertising slogan in India, you will have seen it: "Incredible India"  as much as I love India a more apt slogan would be "Incredible (but oft infuriating) India"

The other day I visited a bank - where we have a old dormant bank account (long story), but there was a small balance that was worth withdrawing. In fact it's a tiny branch in a village in rural south Goa. There were only two cashiers and a line of  waiting customers sat on chairs along a wall like a doctors waiting room. An ancient framed sepia picture of a bearded Jesus decorated with a marigold wreath watched over us from one side and a wall mounted Ganpati elephant god statue from the other presumably to keep transactions honest. A cranky roof fan wafted warm air around, and piles of dusty journals lay piled randomly on a second line of desks behind the cashiers. It's 2012, but I felt like I just walked in to a 1950s Graham Greene novel.

Everyone turned to look at the Englishman. "Come come.." cried an amiable clerk from the second line and gestured to me to come round to the back office and sit on a little chair squeezed between desks. Everyone nodded to me and smiled, the cashiers swiveled round in their chairs to chat to me ignoring customers, who also smiled at me. 
I find all this faintly embarrassing, why should a white face drop in to top slot on the cast system so easily? It's not even as if I had a heap of money deposited, and what was there was soon to go. "I'd like to withdraw money from this account" I said waving my  cheque book (remember those). "No problem sir, I'll check the balance" - which he did on an ancient cathode ray screen - and helped me write the check the correct way, which was handed to cashier number one. Then what happened?

Pretty much nothing.. I watched my check being passed from one cashier to the other, each struggling to call up the account, then a patient customer would push a passbook in front of them and they got distracted, my cheque got shuffled around the place. I really didn't want to cause a fuss - especially since I'd just jumped the queue, so I waited. After half an hour the amiable clerk turned to me like I'd just materialized and said "can I help you?" 

This is what I mean about India, so charming but often so infuriating. 

 "I'm waiting for my money" I pointed out trying not to sound grumpy. He said something to number two in local language, who swiveled and promptly gave me a large well rubbed brass coin, cira 1900, with bank insignia on it.  "What's this for?" I asked, "it's in lieu of your money sir," 
By now I am getting grumpy, "I'd rather have the money" I snapped.  I sat rubbing my brass coin like a worry stone, and waited a while longer.. until the money finally arrived - which was ceremoniousness exchanged for the coin. 

Over an hour to get my cash. As I left the bank, I realized for all the antiquated bureaucratic systems in place, no-one had actually checked my identity, I could have been anyone with a stolen cheque book. But of course that would never have happened, not with Jesus and Ganpati watching.
 ___________________________________________________________________________

More travels next week..

title: David's AW News: More behind the scenes.
content_html:
Greetings from the Island of the Gods.


It's not a good time to be a tourist in Bali.. it's raining everyday and sometimes huge electric storms with crackling thunder so loud the windows shake. 
It was Chinese New Year this week, and the locals like to celebrate this, as they do across all of SouthEast Asia, with fireworks and dancing dragons. But the stormy weather put a bit of a dampener on it.. at least three locals told me that wet weather at Chinese New Year is normal, every year like this.. I said how can that be? Because CNY changes date quite a lot can be upto 14 days different.  This year is very early. I'm reliably informed (by several locals) that the more it rains in CNY, the better and more prosperous the coming year will be. 
I was in central Denpasar with Ringo yesterday and the whole town around the market area was decorated with red lanterns.. 
Happy Year of the Snake Guys.. whatever that might mean.. lets hope it's good.
Last week I was telling you about our very dedicated admin department here in the AW warehouse, I'm amazed at the level of detail and control our two young girls have - never a question they can't answer in minutes with a spreadsheet and backup file of papers.. if you missed it you can catch up here.  

Actually the admin team is very important to the success of AW indonesian operation. By keeping things under control and with tight efficiency we can I believe export from Indonesia at least 10% cheaper than our competitors and still pay our artisans a good and fair price..   So yesterday as a token of appreciation I suggested the admin team should have a team lunch. Where would they like to go?
There is no shortage of high class dining in Bali.. but they wanted to go to a local restaurant.. about 20 minutes from here. It's un-marked from the road in a small village. Actually a fish farm with lots of lakes descending in pools down a hill-side. The gimmick is if you want to come and catch your own lunch with a rod and line you can get 10% off your meal. Very rustic, no tourists here. Fresh fish served with rice salad and super sweet and spicy sauce, it was finger licking good!
All Bali is abuzz it seems.. well at our suppliers are. Mr David is here... and they are all keen to present the latest creations. So this week I have been inundated with new products to evaluate.. not an easy job - because not everything is suitable for UK & Europe, and many items were basically more of the same.. but, I think we found some good ideas..
Anyway as promised more behind the scenes. Last week you met our Admin accounts team. 
Right now we have an ace packing team, three containers packed and dispatched this year already. Delaku (a local lady) is our veteran super skilled and knowledgeable lady who teaches the team.  Always hard working and reliable she has been with us for years. And the rest of them working well. 
Here is the whole team, many from Nusa - Timur islands. And after loading the last container.

I hope you find this interesting! Next week I will show you some artisan suppliers at work in the villages of Bali.

Well it's only two weeks until Valentine's Day and now is the time to stock up. We have the deals and the good stuff.

A container actually arrived from Bali yesterday.. with long awaited stock of Molten Glass Bowls - lots more fast selling lines back in stock.. also something new.. 

Year of the Snake - let's hope it's good! ..  Greetings and best wishes. 
Take care.. more news next week.

David

title: Malaga to Marrakech
content_html:
Greetings from Morocco

Last week I was telling you about "Moving on" - sometimes business relationships just don't work out well, you can read about it here.

A special Hello, Hola!.. to our new Spanish customers who are subscribing in droves to the latest AW website.. AWGifts.es - the only authorised AW site for Spain. 
We are busy adding products to the site, more everyday.. soon we should have the full range of Ancient Wisdom products available for our wonderful Spanish customers - now you can buy direct from AW - please patient as we add products and finish the website. We are interviewing for staff, (Spanish speaking) in Sheffield - it's surprising how many Spanish folk there are in Sheffield if you know anyone that would like an interview, applications close on Tuesday.

Our plan is to later open a distribution centre in Spain.. it's all happening.. 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over eight years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here. 
Over 50,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here  I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka and the whole team from the UK.  Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken.

Meanwhile.. finally after so many years of planning to go.. my wife and I finally made it to Marrakech.  When I was really young, maybe 16, I read a book about someone buying an old Riad in Marrakech and turning it into a small hotel - what a fantastic adventure it seemed to be and it always stayed with me. So it's always been on my dream list of places to visit. And more so now.. since it has a rich culture of artisan crafts, plus aromatics and gemstone products - such opportunity.. and everyone loves that stylish Moroccan look and feel. Ancient Wisdom really should be trading there. I suppose one of the reasons I never made it before was that I had offered this opportunity to Carlos our partner in the Spain company, he never found the time.. so now that partnership is over - an opportunity opens up.. as one door closes another opens as they say.

The flight from Malaga to Marrakech is surprisingly stressed free and super fast, a really short flight and you actually arrive before you leave because of the time zones. The airport in Marrakech is modern and very efficient, the hotel sent a driver to pick us and the trip downtown (we wanted to stay practically in the souks of course) was only 20 minutes. The boutique hotel (also a Riad) served mint tea in a cool and beautiful courtyard. All so trouble free...

OMG.. so many shops, so much stuff, so many guys wanting you to buy their wares.

title: Fooled Again
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Last week I was telling you about the gloomy weather in Spain and the calima or sandstorm that turned everything muddy brown.. well the big clean up has begun and the sun started to reappear. So hopefully we can get back to normal.. the transport strike is also winding down.. it was all doom and gloom (but getting better now) - if you missed it you can catch up here. 


The clean up begins.. our man Clive on the job. Returning our Spain warehouse to pristine whiter than white. 

Well it's the first of April. And the cost of living shocks are no joke, it's no April fools joke this time.
And like I have been saying for a long time, this will turn into hyper inflation.. the massive worldwide printing of money to pay for the pandemic was bound to cause it.. but now the war in Ukraine and supply chain problems are making it much worse, like the perfect storm.. but calm down everybody. These times will pass and even in the darkest days (or especially) humans need the means to comfort each other. Since ancient times, we humans have brought gifts as offerings to our loved and respected ones. 
In difficult times people turn to more spiritual things.. think candles (Magic Spell Candles), incense (Smudge Sticks & Nag Champa), aromatics (always stock  essential oils), sing bowls and anything in gemstones and esoteric.
Now is the time to pivot to the spiritual and esoteric.. and you know the best supplier don't you?

I should have been in India right now, there is a trade show happening in Delhi, and many suppliers are ready with new products to pitch to us. But for some strange geo-political reason e-visa for UK nationals are unavailable.  If I was Russian or Afgan or even Spanish I could make it, but for some reason the British are blocked for now. Fortunately we have Mr Chatterjee and his son Dishanta (our team in India) on the ground in Delhi and around, and by the power of Whatapp still doing business. I can see from the stream of pictures that the creativity in India is unbounded. Those guys have not spent the pandemic doing nothing.. they have been making magic..


Father & Son team in India..  and few pictures of potential products coming to AW..


Our new AW-Aromatics production area in Sheffield was supposed to be ready to move into on the 1st of April. And obviously given the supply issues generally and shortage of Polish plumbers it has been massively delayed. Now we are hoping to get in by June or earlyJuly in order to ramp up production in time for Christmas. But this morning despite almost nothing else happening on time.. a sign writer seems to have been.. and put up the wrong sign.


Ancient Wisdom moved to Affinity Park 18 months ago, this was our old warehouse (which you will recall burned down) now almost rebuilt ready for production to move back into. Nobody knows anything about this sign.. It should say "AW Aromatics" and a different colour logo. As of writing this newsletter - I still don't know if this is an elaborate April Fool, a monumental error or an honest mistake..Somebody tell me!! 

Next week - I'm off to somewhere exotic.. travelling to visit a supplier in another country where Brits are actually allowed to go.
Can you guess where? 
More updates next week.

Take care

David

title: Something Strange in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from my Bali lock-down day 41.

There is something really strange going on in this island.. maybe it holds a clue to escaping Covid-19 - anyway it's becoming clear something is spectacularly odd. I'll explain below.
Last week I was telling you about all the free food here on offer as the local government scramble to prevent starvation and avoid civil unrest. In India, there is less help for poor people - but good people like our agent Mr Chatterjee are working to help in many ways - I was showing you last week Mr Chatterjee's efforts and a message from the orphanage we support there. You can read about it here.
Since then many people emailed me offering support and donations to Mr Chatterjee to enable him to do more. It's amazing how kind people can be even in such difficult circumstances.  Maybe I will set up a go-fund page or something..

Today as I write it is a New Moon day in Bali, that means everyone gets dressed up nice and makes offerings in every place, and then troops off to the temple for exotic ceremonies. The wife from the family that owns our warehouse came with a tray of offerings, there is a small temple in the corner of the car-park which she cleaned and refreshed and placed incense and offerings, she came in the office and placed offerings around my new photo-studio, she went in warehouse placed more amongst our packing benches. Ringo said it's all Full Moon offerings, praying success for our business and protection from the virus. When she had finished he went and at distance thanked her profusely.


Full Moon Offerings.
 
So here's the thing. Six weeks ago Bali was a bustling tourist resort. 740,000 tourists in Bali and a maybe 100,000 of those were Chinese including many arriving on direct flights from Wuhan. Many others from Europe, including not a small amount of Italians and Spanish people busy hugging and kissing everyone they meet. This is a small island with 4 million local population, it is densely populated. It had all the ingredients for a major corona-virus mega-disaster. 
And yet.. here are the stats as of today: 287 cases to date, 183 recovered, 4 deaths - 2 of which were Europeans. No new cases yesterday.

Compared to other parts of Indonesia (with very few tourists).. compared to Europe it's simply astoundingly low. Why? 

Are they faking the figures (thinking it will protect tourism).. I think it's possible to a degree - but the hospitals are normal, and I know that from Ringo who knows doctors in the central hospital in Denpasar. The mainstream media is not covering this story, but I think they should because whatever the reason it's so low here right now is a mystery. The local spiritual leaders would have you believe the same Gods that calmed down Mount Agung two years ago from a predicted massive eruption, acted again and protected the island.

Maybe, let's keep an open mind.. but perhaps it is something else local to here. Diet for example, the particular level of heat and humidity.. erm I can't think of anything else.
Critics argue it can't be the humidity because Singapore is suffering and it's not so far away and the same weather. Other tropical countries are also bad (eg Mexico) so why on earth is Bali immune?

In Europe and America the curve is past its peak.. just.. and already an un-holy rush to relax lock-downs..So you would think here they would be ultra relaxing now. Some days there are no more cases.. the argument for getting back to normal is strong. And yet.. everyday more stringent rules come, more police and army on the streets. Check points on all major junctions. You must wear a mask at all times outside your home, even in a car. Beaches closed, no public meetings (although I have seen temples open), detergent is been enthusiastically sprayed everywhere with gay abandon.  Cars have to drive through detergent washes - streets are drenched twice a day. All ports and airports remain closed, even travel from one part of the island to another is prohibited without reason.


   Police check everyone. 

Someone, please explain to me what the hell is going on?!!

Meanwhile, in Europe things seem to be picking up.. next week we are getting more people back to work because we need to  - although it is a major challenge to keep everyone safe. Tomas and Katka have been tearing their hair out devising safety plans.
  
We had a container - the first of many - arrive from China so lots of things are back in stock. Including some Soap Flowers.. They have to be the perfect lock-down gift right?. Flowers you can actually wash your hands with!
See below for other stock items.

Here in Bali, we will be dispatching a container in two days... so it's all go.. packing and labelling and QC jobs from morning to night.. Ringo and I are very busy.
Oh yes and another strange thing in Bali.. it's normal that every now and then - every few days you get an earthquake.. mostly little - occasionally a little more scary - I have experienced a few whilst here. Regular readers will recall the worst ones..  
In 3 months of corona time.. guess what? - None at all..  it's like the very earth it'self is at peace.
Something strange in Bali..

Take care - stay safe.
More news next week.

David

title: Heavy Rock & Tea in Java
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Hope you are well and surviving the sandstorms, prestalance and wars. 
It's all levels of stress at once it seems.. In Spain, apart from being sandblasted, the nation's drivers are on strike, so nothing is getting delivered.
Here in Indonesia everything is peaceful and calm by comparison.. although we have been super busy developing the next ranges of products - working day and night with our artisan suppliers to bring you something new.
Last week I was telling you about our road trip to Java.. and our exploration of three artisan villages discovered by our man Bondan. I was telling you about the Seagrass Village.. if you missed it you can catch up here. If you are interested, I'll tell you about the Teak Village.. if not skip ahead to the business stuff below.


We spent a couple of days in the Seagrass Village (last week's news), and could have spent much longer. But time is short so we had to move on - on our road trip across Java.
There is a brand new motorway to the city of Solo in central Java. Recent years have seen huge infrastructure projects completed across Indonesia, much to the pride and joy of the population. For Ringo it was his first time on a proper motorway, and he was delighted and impressed. After spending the night in Solo, we headed up into the Teak forest area of central Java. Now driving on small country roads winding up to the higher ground.

Teak wood is strictly controlled by the government, and as far as I'm aware the artisan producers are all compliant. Trees can only be cut with approval and must be over a certain girth. A system to protect the teak supply and ensure that forests are maintained was developed with the EU a few years back it's called the SVLK.. importers like AW have to hold a FLEGT (Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade) license, and we are obliged to ensure all our wood imports meet the standards. Ringo is always on the job chasing up papers and getting the correct stamps and paperwork to make sure our products meet the standards. 

I read that over a million people work in Java producing teak furniture for the world, not all the teak is grown on Java, some comes from forests on other islands - but the main artisan area is in central Java. Bondan had discovered one particular village that specialised in giftware and furniture.. As we arrived close to the town, the side of the road was made up of small showrooms practically nestling in the edge of the forest. 
Small businesses each with a particular speciality with people actually living and working right inside the forest. Later we went to the town - a neat organised place, nice houses and a feeling of prosperity. We met earnest, thoughtful business people very hands on and creative, working with all types of teakwood. The roots, branches, heart of the tree all for different purposes. Wow, I was very impressed.. a wide range of items from fine high-end furniture - to funky coffee shop designs and arty giftware items. 
We made a video.. 


So I think we found a couple of businesses that we will work with, and Bondan will return in the next few weeks to finalise a couple of container loads of orders.
After the teak village we went to visit the hometown of Bondan, where we met his Mother and Father.. his father a musician (like Bondan) and a very cool guy. In the back of his house they had built a small recording studio where local aspiring rock stars can come and practice. All over Java, people love 1970's Rock.. I was surprised at the number of radio stations playing soft rock (even English language stations here), every hotel has a resident band, even at the motorway service station a band played for tips. The immensely popular president of Indonesia known as Jokowi (his nickname) is an avowed heavy metal fan. And in Indonesia there is a huge rock band culture. I don't know what your perception of a Muslim country is but I bet you didn't expect that ..

This was another idyllic peaceful village high up on the side of a mountain with rice terrace views below and tea plantation views above.
We went to visit the tea plantation, where locals go to a picnic area with dramatic views. In a small workers village one or two gift shops sold the local produce including the tea. A nice lady gave us endless cups of tea to try.. the local tea is supposed to improve your eyesight.. it was nice - looked a lot like "gunpowder tea" and even without sugar it had a sweet floral taste. However, we do have some Artisan teas from Spain...


Next week more news from Indonesia.
Don't panic.. but only 10 days to Mother's Day.
If you still need to stock up we have just the things you need.

Take care 

David

This was another idyllic peaceful village high up on the side of a mountain with rice terrace views below and tea plantation views above. title: 25+ Reasons to be Cheerful
content_html:
Greetings on our auspicious day.


I don't usually write a newsletter on a Monday, but this is a special day.
It was Twenty Five years ago today that Ancient Wisdom was born.
On Friday I told you the story of that first day of trading. You can read it here.


Thank you so much to all the people who wrote in with congratulation messages, it's a great encouragement to me and all at AW.
One kind person mentioned that 25 years is actually a "Silver Anniversary"  - So we thought we would like to celebrate by issuing a Silver Voucher to all our customers.
It's worth £25 - and you can redeem it with any order over £200+vat within the next 25 days. See below, plus we have free shipping for the next 25 hours.
Plus some very special anniversary deals thrown in for good measure.



In Friday's newsletter I also made a call out for "Ben" to make himself known, as he was the first person to come up with the name we like best for our new warehouse address.

Ben had just posted anonymously to our blog site. 
Below is his email.. I'm sure he won't mind me sharing it with you.. 
We are sending him Champagne today.. and I have invited Ben & Chloe to our official naming and opening party as guests of honour when this whole horrid covid thing is in the past.


If your covid depressed, or just fed up - Ben will cheer you up. Plus check out the deals below..


Anyway hope you have a great week.

 

David



Dear David,


I have this afternoon been arranging our most recent order received from Ancient Wisdom this week in our shop, getting ready for when lockdown ends here in Ireland (hopefully on 1st December). I had come home intending a quiet night in (as usual during lockdown) and just before I closed the lid of my laptop, I remembered it was Friday and I had not yet seen your newsletter, I always love to read your newsletters and reading them usually results in an hour or so browsing through your website filling up my cart :) I opened your email and read through it, as I scrolled down I see the picture of your new warehouse, imbedded the text "Affinity Park" I thought to myself "Oh look, they have called their new warehouse Affinity Park, I suggested that" Of course I thought someone else must have also suggested the same name... I never win anything! It wasn't until I had read the text surrounding the picture for the second or third time that the penny finally dropped... it was ME!! I jumped up and punched the air above my head... Frightened the life out of my partner Chloe! Haha.


WOW!!!! I am actually speechless!!! This is amazing!! I can not begin to explain just how happy we are!


I remember when my family and I woke to the news that you had had a fire at your warehouse, we assumed it was nothing serious as we had received an email from you guys, and then when I saw the gruesome images on the news I felt sick to the pit of my stomach, I could not believe it. The sense of loss I felt was immense. I remember pacing up and down the kitchen, a million thoughts going through my mind. Throughout my journey with Ancient Wisdom I feel I have been made to feel like one of the family, and that is genuinely a great feeling!! Of course I was concerned as to whether anyone had been hurt or worse, and the relief I felt once I had learned everyone was OK was great - but short lived. My thoughts then turned to the AW business, gutted by flames. I guess I underestimated you and Ancient Wisdom! I was sad for the people who might be losing their jobs and the businesses that would face disruption, all in the midst of the pandemic - it really could not have happened at a worse time! And then I thought of yourself, stuck out in Bali. I imagined how you might be feeling. Needless to say, as you will know only too well, that was not a good day! Like I said, I really have been made to feel like one of the AW family, so felt an incredible amount of many feelings, all of them sad at that time. 


Since then I have read in awe your newsletters. You have spoken about hope and determination throughout. Frankly the way you have dealt with this has been inspirational! I am sure many may have curled up in a ball and given up! But not you or the AW Heros. WOW!


I spoke to Mauro a while after the fire, he told me of the "nightmarish" scenes he faced when he went to site. I can not even begin to imagine how yourself or any  of the AW heros felt right then. I think myself and many of your customers shared somewhat in your grief.


And now look at where you are and what you guys have achieved... A new bigger warehouse, not only have you got much of the stock lost back in stock, but you are also adding new and fantastic lines regularly, your dispatch is currently the quickest I have ever known! What you and the AW Heros have achieved is amazing and to be naming your new warehouse "Affinity" has well and truly overwhelmed me! I won't bore you with my life story, But like you I also started off on street corners at markets selling bits & bobs, this and that. My family and I have had to overcome some real difficult times over the past few years and then in January when we moved here to Ireland, we felt like we had found our "Affinity" and then when we started our business again we found "Affinity" in that and then when we found Ancient Wisdom we found "Affinity" in our supplier...


Needless to say the word "Affinity" and its meaning is very dear to our family and from the bottom of our hearts we would like to thank you for using it to name your new warehouse!


Whilst here, can I please bring your attention to one thing? Mauro... What can I say? This man is an absolute LEGEND! The customer services I have received from Mauro, time and time again has been second to none! I call myself his very own pest! However he is always extremely helpful and obliging. No issue to small, no problem too big. It seems Mauro can sort anything. He is a true credit to Ancient Wisdom. I always hope there will be a way I can thank him for all of his help. Please pass on my thanks, and hopefully once the lockdowns ect are all over and we get back to some sort of normality I will come to Ancient Wisdom and thank him and yourself and all the AW Heros personally. 


Thanks once again soooooooooooooooooooooooooooo much!!!


Yours,


Ben & Chloe.

title: Peace on Earth
content_html:
I hope you find your peace this Easter  

Greetings from my very peaceful quarantine hotel room in Sheffield.  Hope you are well, feeling like a spring chicken and ready for the long weekend.

I am able to work the same way I did in Spain: via Wechat, Whatsapp, Slack & Zoom. With Ringo in Indonesia, Coco in China, Mr Chatterjee in India and all the AW offices in Europe. The only difference is now I have a nice view of the car park, rather than the sea.

Oh but at least I brought the sunshine with me, it's a lot more sunny and warm than I expected. 

 

So this week since it's Easter, a less business and more reflective newsletter with some amazing news and memories from another age..

 

Last week I was writing from Malaga airport as I prepared to leave Spain. I was telling you about how I could see those mega container ships pass by our house there, and an update on the container ship blocking the Suez Canal. You can read about it here.

The flight should have been fully booked, it was the only direct flight from Malaga to Manchester in a month. But quite a few people failed to negotiate the complicated passenger locator and booking covid tests system.

Even though the online guidance said you could show pdf proofs on your phone, the easyjet guy checking papers in the queue wanted to see printed off papers. Covid tests needed to be valid within 72 hours and there is no guidance of which types of tests are valid or not. In short it was a complete (insert expletive) mess. It was not peaceful.. it was very stressful. Once on board maybe 20% of seats were empty - so many didn't make it.  


Regular readers will remember the story of Rodrigo. He is our main marketing guy in the UK, (although he involves himself in all sorts of projects). He is from Brazil and married to Jess, a lovely Yorkshire lass. In the age of Teresa May and her hostile environment for immigrants Rodrigo got trapped in a bureaucratic mess and was almost deported back to Brazil, even though he was (very happerly) married to an English girl. It seemed crazy and heartless that they would force him to leave his wife indefinitely to go back to Brazil and reapply for UK residency from there. We fought tooth and nail, and many of you signed a petition.. it was stressful. Finally we got a slight compromise that Rodrigo could go to Spain and reapply from there. So Rodrigo went to live in and work remotely from my house in Spain.  The story wasn't smooth.

From there it took seven months and seven day, many protests, great expense and a lot of forms, tears and mixups. Although there were visits from Jess, I was there some of the time, and we shared tapas and tears. Many evenings drinking wine on the terrace listening to Guns and Roses and discussing life. And I remember the day Rodrigo was finally granted leave to remain, and his passport was returned to him.  Within hours we got him back on a flight to the UK to be reunited with Jess. 

Well the big news is that Rodrigo & Jess have an announcement to make. Meet Frida, a beautiful baby girl. Frida, Rodrigo, tells me Frida.. means peace.

What do they say?  pictures speak a thousand words. If you want to message Rodrigo & Jess and you can here: rodrigo@ancientwisdom.biz

 

In Europe it's Easter, a time of chocolates, rebirth and more chocolate... 

In India it is also that time of year, they call it Holi. Holi is the most popular Hindu festival, also known as the "Festival of Love", the "Festival of Colours", and the "Festival of Spring".

You probably know about the colours.. this thing with dancing and playing Holi. It's as though all India's social norms are abandoned, people dance with strangers, lose their clothes, smear paint on each other. In Mr Chatterjee area they drink a kind of intoxicating yogurt drink and everyone gets stoned. It's quite normal. Coronavirus seems to have passed in his area, and everyone is more relaxed. Mr Chatterjee was even able to go on holiday to a mountain resort with his family and friends this week.

Here's some pictures of the local kids getting in the vibe, that's Mr Chatterjee on the left picture in the middle. 

It brings back memories.. It was a long time ago almost in another age.. five years ago in Goa it was Holi time and Mr Chatterjee took Coco, me and Tomas, to a posh Holi party.  

It was mad, totally wild..a kind of Holi rave come pool party. Later on it became too crazy and we had to escape.. It took weeks to scrub off the paint. But the memory remains.

Those were the days. Hopefully one day we will all be able to go out and live our lives in multi colours again.

Wishing you fond memories and a peaceful Easter.

 

Take care

David

title: Epic Happenings at AW
content_html:
Greetings from the twilight zone..

It was peaceful, productive and green in Indonesia, but circumstances forced me to leave and return to Europe. I'm in Spain now.
Here in Europe it seems the exact opposite.. war in Ukraine, transport strike in Spain and a weird mud storm turning everything brown.

Swimming pools turned to mud baths overnight.. 


Our normally white warehouse this morning. Epic and strange Weather in Spain.

Yesterday afternoon was gloomy and muddy, the air quality turned three times worse than Delhi (according to my AirVisual app) and it really felt like I was living inside a sepia picture. 

Last week I was telling you more about our Java Road Trip to the Teak Village - you can read about it here.

Amazingly I managed to get an international flight out of Bali, before departing the captain came on the tannoy to assure us that this plane would not be flying in Russian or Ukrainian airspace.
It's a strange world at the moment..

But at least we can celebrate Mother's Day in the UK. - To all mothers out there, wishing you a peaceful and happy Sunday. Hope and pray for a normal happy day.

I'm in Spain now but my heart is still in Indonesia.. With so many projects still on the go, I'm still finalising products and deals today. Bondan and Ringo and the team loaded two containers yesterday working late into the night. Both for the UK.. so lots of products on the way..


Every inch of space is used, we even stopped using master cartons to save space, products are packed inside furniture and textiles packed in any void space. Shipping costs are still sky high, so every possible packing solution is essential. An Epic job by our Bali team..

Last week I was telling you about the teak village in Java.. after that we went to a village where brass products are produced. Again I was surprised at the peaceful collaborative nature of the place. Small artisan workshops each with it's own specialist items, our main contact took us to see his brothers place and his uncles, between them they can make an interesting collection. The items are cast in wax first with some details hand carved in the wax, then the wax is packed in fine sand with a straw hole through which the molten brass is poured, melting the wax and creating the brass figure.  It's far from industrial, artisan workshops with people working to the sound of 80's soft rock music and the people we found to be all studious and gentle.  
Bondan compiled a video of our day in the Brass Village.
Meanwhile in Slovakia we are in the midst of moving to our new warehouse. The efficient and hard working team are making it look easy.. but I know from experience it is anything but.
This is a major step forward for AWGifts.eu and I can't wait to go see the new place.
It's an EPIC move.. Tomas and James (the UK warehouse mystro) are there keeping everything running smoothly.. we had to halt shipping orders from Wednesday.. but we should be up and running from the new warehouse by Monday. That's an awesome and absolutely EPIC achievement.



So one way or another it's all happening at AW..

Have a wonderful Mother's Day weekend.. (don't forget the clocks change as well this weekend)
More news and updates next week.

David

title: Bangkok and a game called Dakon
content_html:
Greetings from big bad Bangkok. The city has such a reputation, which on I'm beginning to think is not totally deserved. The traffic is relatively organised and relaxed compared to any Chinese or Indian city, the air is definitely cleaner and the sky is actually blue. The people are unremittingly polite, and invariably smiling. Smiling and bowing, bowing and smiling, like a city wide travel ad sponsored by a teeth whitening clinic. In many ways Bangkok ain't so bad.
But I have had just one day here, just time to go and see a new wholesale Silver market - which was interesting with very professional companies, great designs and (surprising for Thailand) realistic prices. Tomorrow it's off to Chiang Mai - a whole new city for me. After that it's Indonesia.
Meanwhile.. Our first container from Indonesia washed up in Ancient Wisdom home base in Sheffield. Lots of goodies, but I'm particularly excited about a game called Dakon. Which I have to tell you about.
When I first saw this board games, I thought how beautiful.. and you can have fun playing with them. The more I learned about them the more I thought they would make an interesting and unusual gift line.
It was outside the city of Yogjakarta in a steamy rainforest on the banks of a volcano where we found a small sleepy village, the cultural home of Dakon. Where the inhabitants are invariably skilled artisans spending their days creating beautiful batik decorated Dakon boards.
The history of the game dates back to forth century Egypt and it is thought that the game was brought here by traders and then adapted by Malacca merchants and developed into this very popular Javanese game. Here on the mountain where the wood, heritage and skills come together a mini industry has developed producing these beautiful intricately decorated sets.
The sets are made in the shape of various animals, rabbits, fish etc. The most prized and carefully decorated are the signature standing dragons. I think they are not just a game but a work of art, that anyone with an ounce of cultural appreciation would simply love to own.
Dakon is a simple and addictive game, to win you need to think further ahead than your opponent, be quick at calculations and a good judge of numbers of shells in a hole.
More info and the rules read more here..
More thoughts and news next week.. from Chiang Mai in North Thailand.
Regards
David

The history of the game dates back to forth century Egypt and it is thought that the game was brought here by traders and then adapted by Malacca merchants and developed into this very popular Javanese game. Here on the mountain where the wood, heritage and skills come together a mini industry has developed producing these beautiful intricately decorated sets. The sets are made in the shape of various animals, rabbits, fish etc. The most prized and carefully decorated are the signature standing dragons. I think they are not just a game but a work of art, that anyone with an ounce of cultural appreciation would simply love to own. Dakon is a simple and addictive game, to win you need to think further ahead than your opponent, be quick at calculations and a good judge of numbers of shells in a hole. More info and the rules read more here.. More thoughts and news next week.. from Chiang Mai in North Thailand. Regards David w ww.AncientWisdom.biz

title: David's AW News: Baking Buddhas
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia.

Yes, I am here on my way back to Europe. Raul, our IT wizard, is here and there are lots of things happening. The marketing world is changing so fast..

Last week I was telling you about my one day delayed flight and the conspiracy guy who managed to almost cause a riot. If you missed it you can catch up here.

My observation is this..  That guy who kept coming up with conspiracies (they cancelled our flight to consolidate it etc), became the natural group leader by making people feel angry and untrusting. There in action was the simple truth.. Conspiracies are the way to hack democracy.. so that's why we have Trump.02.

All changes in marketing.

But maybe I was a bit unfair to the guy.. 

An apology.
The next day in the Red Fox Hotel near the airport.. they gave us a coach transfer back to the airport. Everyone on our flight was milling around in the lobby. I had decided from experience to avoid the coach transfer. Too many mosquitoes, smells and damp seats for my liking. So I called an Uber, only £2 to the airport - and a nice big new car turned up. So I popped back to the lobby and invited a couple of English ladies I had met who had also made friends with the Conspiracy guy.. and so we all crammed in the taxi for the 6 minute transit to the airport. 
At the business check-in it was me and this guy. We bonded, then in the business lounge we sat and chatted about marketing for two or three hours. Exchanging notes and ideas.. he was the owner of a wellness retreat, and faced similar challenges reaching out to potential customers. 

Oven in Bali
Yes it's hot now in Bali, and that is good for one reason.. When carved wooden items like the Hand-carved Buddha's arrive in our warehouse they need to be checked for quality, and one thing we do is check the moisture level of the wood. If the level is too high, chances are the Buddha will face some bad karma on the way as the container moves around the world.. and arrive with big cracks. So the regular solution is to put the statues in the sunlight to dry out - usually for several days.. 
The problem with this is two fold, firstly someone has to run around every few hours moving them back into the sun, and the really big problem is the rainy season.. which these days can be anytime. Waiting for dry days can set back shipping these items by months. So we bought an oven.. (some of our more advanced suppliers have ovens for this purpose),  most of the artisans that do wood carving cannot or don't want to spend money on this. Our oven took almost a week to be built - today they finished it. So now we can gently cook our own Buddha's until they are ultra dry.
Ringo with our new oven.

Satya Incense - update
The Satya brand from the same home as Nag Champa has become a major brand over the last ten years. Do you know the story? The business fell to the control of two brothers, when the old guy and founder died. They fought over the business and the direction it should take.. I don't know all the details, but a lot was involved because Nag Champa is the world's best selling Incense brand. Basically to cut a long story short there are two factories producing almost identical products.. One (the original) in Bangalore and the (rebel upstart) factory in Mumbai. 
So Tomas and I on our India trip met with the boss of the Bangalore factory and we managed to negotiate good terms in return for a commitment to a rolling contract. The purest retailers always buy Bangalore incense because this is the original and still the best, and I think I agree. Because of this we have always stocked Bangalore made.
So this week we were able to dramatically slash the price of the Satya range of incense. This is a major profit opportunity for you!  

Now Satya can cost you as little as 32p per pack. Sell at any 4 packs for £6 or £2 each.. Happy Days!
We have a limited amount of display stands (made in Bali) you can get super cheap in our starter pack deal. Grab while you can.
Online retailers - might want to sell as 12 pack assortment for £12.. fast selling and we have a dropship deal to help you do this.. Just add to your shop now. For sure sales.

So back in the UK.. there is still a backlog of products to get online. But the warehouse team is on it, and Rodrigo and the marketing team are updating pages.

Only a few weeks to Christmas.. 
Plus we already have HUGE Black Friday Deals for you.

Hati-hati - Take care - I have to go and watch some Buddha's gentle cooking.

David

title: Gentle Giants and Angels
content_html:
Greetings from hot and sunny Sheffield.

Now 34 days since the fire at AW, and still no meaningful response from the insurance company.
Thank you for all your suggestions, tips and advice on how to deal with insurance claims. It's amazing how helpful and supportive the AW community is.. it's really encouraging and keeping us going.


Even our competitors have been in touch offering help and advice. The gift trade is amazing.
Not knowing is more stressful than even knowing that they just want to escape liability on some technicality. At least we can plan accordingly. You can read last week newsletter here.
We have been searching for a big new warehouse, the biggest of which we couldn't really commit to without the insurance company support, so currently in a kind of frustrating limbo.

But anyway it's all go in here, a maze of activity. We are quickly adding new production items - something new every day. Also new products arriving - it's all go. See below.
Dispatch and warehouse guys are working round the clock. They are seriously hero's.


The demolition guys came, a team of old timers - all gentle giants led by a lovely guy called Charlie who told me he had destroyed some of the biggest buildings in the UK in his 40 year career. These old timers wield massive equipment that can rip tons of metal girders from the burned out building and dump them in massive skips. They remind me of marvel superheros with special powers.

From our office in the remaining block we can watch their progress, and every now and then feel it.. as something comes crashing down and the floor shakes. While they get busy destroying our old warehouse we are getting busy rebuilding our company, it's products and supply chains. We have a grand plan.. Ancient Wisdom production department will remain here - in the three units remaining, so three times more space than before. We will rename it AW Aromatics, and they will not only supply AW but anybody that wants their own label or white label products. The distribution will move to a new big warehouse. We should be much more efficient with enough space to stock and ship everything from one place.

So our future plans are gradually coming into focus. Meanwhile, I'm quite excited because some of the Indonesian products I was working on whilst in lock-down in Bali are starting to arrive here. 

Regular readers will remember the story about the coco lamp supplier, and the teething troubles we had with production. They are here now and look beautiful, all the staff want to buy them, this makes me happy. I'm hoping we can quickly give that family business a decent re-order.

Also Hati Hati angels are finally back.. this was one of the first products we developed in Indonesia. Hati hati means "take care" or "be careful" in Indonesian - they became a firm seller and a much copied item. The family that carved the angels, simply couldn't make enough and supplied whoever gave them cash - they are found in local gift shops in Bali now, so our orders never got completed. Recently we trained another supplier, the one that makes soap dishes for us, and restarted production. So now we have some of that stock starting to arrive. It's another small family business, Wayan is a young energetic lady - another lady boss - who leads a small team of artisans all organised by her good looking husband, but Wayan is clearly the boss and really caring and giving attention to detail. She learns how to make any product herself, then sits and trains the artisans in how to make it personally and sets the standards. The artisans who carve the angels are usually older ladies earning extra money for their families.


It doesn't seem that long ago that she was sat in our office at the warehouse in Bali, showing me the traceability documents for the wood used to make soap dishes. And the invoices from government approved companies logging companies. All our wood is double checked by me or someone at Ancient Wisdom to make sure it comes from sustainable sources, and Wayan is as keen to be fully compliant. And always with plenty of Hati Hati.

 

Check our what we have back in stock..

 

So take care.. Hati hati!

 

More news next week.


David

title: Good and Bad in India
content_html:
Greetings from Greater Noida, India

The AW buying team (Tomas, Bryant, Chatterjee, Drishanta, and me)  are travelling in India - seeking out a swath of amazing new products for you. Right now we are attending the huge Spring trade show at the exhibition center in Greater Noida.. To be honest, I'm not always impressed by the tradeshows, preferring to seek out the independent family businesses directly, but this year is different.. details below.
Last week I was telling you about our last days in Kathmandu - the journey to Delhi and then onwards to Panipat - a major textile area in North India. If you missed it you can read ti here.
Since then we have spent a few days in the heart of Old Delhi connecting with our regular suppliers and some new ones, then onward to the trade show.

Panipat was interesting, we stayed in Days Inn.. close to one of our suppliers. Probably one of the worst hotels ever. From the sullen un-smiling staff, to the super-slow and patchy Wi-Fi to the ripped wallpaper and stained bedsheets - it was all sub-par. It sold itself as a luxury wedding venue and indeed it had a vast wedding hall, where the staff played banging Bollywood music at all hours. The lobby was reasonably grand and the building not old, but somehow everything was shabby and dusty. When we checked out the manager came and asked me if everything was good.. I gave him my feedback as you can imagine.. after much apologising they went on to charge my credit card twice.. and until today despite many promises and daily phone calls not refunded the "mistaken" charge.  

India, as you know is a land of extremes. Extreme poverty/wealth, extreme squaller/beauty, extremely unkind people / amazingly good people.  If the hotel in Panipat was bad the opposite could be said about our supplier. The family business is run by Raj, the eldest son and an absolute gentleman, his father and younger son also gentle people, but absolute professionals of the textile business. We had placed one order with them semi-remotely. Last June I had met Chatterjee in Kuala Lumpa (at that time India was closed to British people) and he brought suit cases of samples from Panipat. And so from a hotel room in KL we had an online meeting with Raj in India with samples spread all over the floor and so managed to negotiate a deal and kicked of our business relationship.  We bought a range of the hugely popular Indian Rag Rugs.. which came in stock and sold out rapidly.. (actually more due in a week or so).  Also stocked are some round jute and recycled cotton rugs and some nice classic cotton rugs, which can function as yoga mats - excellent quality and value - you can compete with Ikea with these. And some posh tasteful cushion covers... 
So now it was time to meet the family.. and see what else Panipat has to offer. The city has a slightly wild-west frontier town to it.  Lots of what we call alcohol shops.. selling strangely "English Wine". I mentioned to Raj that English wine was quite hard to come by even in England.. turns out in these parts any imported drink is classed as "English".  Large textile factories dominate the industrial parks and the area has a cultural heritage in rug manufacturing and recycling.
Raj took us to there factory, sadly closed because of the Holi holiday, and showed us the impressive showroom.. a surprising amount of textile items come from this town.. probably quite a few items from here are in your home.
Raj and Tomas clearly had creative chemistry, within an afternoon we were putting together some exciting ranges.


    We had a tour of the workshops where some production was happening despite the Holi holidays.




After surviving Panipat.. we moved to central Delhi and spent four days in-depth visiting suppliers..
Now we are busy in the trade show.. and I think we have some amazing deals and products in the pipeline for you. Esoteric products, amazing new incense, notebooks, scarves.. it's all happening!! 
Full report next week..

It's Mother's Day this Sunday (in the UK).. so wishing all Mothers an absolutely lovely day..
Take care.

David

title: Easter Message and Freedom Project
content_html:
Easter is a time for bunnies and chocolate and eggs, or even chocolate bunny eggs. So I hope you are not too busy working and retailing and have some time for both chocolate and your family. Without wishing to sound like the vicar - Easter is also a time of renewal and reflection... and chocolate of course.
Speaking of renewal, after landing in Kolkata I scooted over the Hooley bridge up the Ganges a bit to Serampore where our Jute supplier is located. Regular readers will know that it is one of the poorer areas we do business, and that we have tried to help a little by adopting a childrens home there. Mr Chatterjee our supplier has worked as hard on this project as on our export order. Just scanned my emails to see he has sent more correspondence about that than business. Much more.
When he first took me to the childrens home, it was in a sorry state. But I was impressed by the couple who ran the place, they had been given the ramshackle house by a lake as a gift, on condition they look after the area's homeless children. They ran the place on occasional donations from local businesses and people, but only barely. The roof had pretty much collapsed, in the monsoon they couldn't keep anything dry and even though the children looked healthy it looked desperate. The local chief of police told me the guy and his wife have big hearts. When they find abandoned or lost children they take them until they can find the parents, if they can't, then this where they stay. Without this facility, these children could well end up in the begging gangs working the big cities living on the streets.
This is before and after.. now twenty seven children are been cared for here. On the back row, from the left: Babita, the lady who comes to cook every day, Mrs Kundu who is a local school teacher and teacher to the children, her husband Mr Kundu who looks after everything. Then the guy with the badger hair is Mr Chatterjee our supplier and finally the chap who organised and help redecorate and a put a new roof on the buildings. He is called Sailen Das.
All the children go to school everyday, one smart guy is in the top pupil in the school. We went to visit last Sunday evening and arrived to a delighted and excited crowd. We were shown round all the improvements and shown the new roof. Then I had to inspect all the school reports and nod as if I could actually understand Bengali. I asked to see the top pupil and shook his hand. I think he was pleased.
Then it was tea and biscuits time, and I chatted to the family and cook. Then we had to pose for lots of pictures like it was a wedding. Finally we went to the dorm, all the guys sat crossed legged on the beds. Mr Kundu lead everyone in a rousing rendition of the hymn "We are not alone" which brought tears to my eyes. They had been practicing for weeks, and it was pretty darn good to say they are Hindu and don't speak English.
Here are a few more pictures:
Actually they are really happy, and didn't ask me for anything. Mostly the hymn summed it up, they felt happy because quite simply some cared about them.
Still there is a lot to do, the kitchen was far from satisfactory, not even a sink. And washing and toilet facilities are pretty basic. After that we plan to make a small garden / play area by the lake.
Support us by stocking Freedom Fund items.
The real hero's here are Mr Chatterjee, his helper and Mr & Mrs Kundu.
If you give money to a charity, you don't really know what happens how much really gets put to good use. Not that you shouldn't donate (I'm not saying that).. but when we give money to Mr Chatterjee every single rupee is accounted for on a spreadsheet, backed up with a folder of receipts.
They don't really have Easter in Kolkata, but it was just the Bengali New year on the 16th. So if you'd like to send Mr Chatterjee and The Kundu family a New Year greeting you can buy just replying to this email. I'll pass it on.
So that's my Easter.. er Bengali New Year Message. One of renewal and hope.
..and chocolate bunnies of course :)
Now I'm in Delhi.. I'll tell you about it next week.
Have a great Easter
Take care 
David

title: The Critical Stage
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Last week I was telling you about our trip to Marrakesh and adventures in the Souks.
You can read about it here. 
Our new man in Morocco (I introduced you to last week), a young guy called Aymen has been messaging me regularly and seems to be making good progress. I gave him a short list of target products and prices and he has found some suppliers that can actually manage this. But this is only stage one I tell him, and thankfully he seems to understand. Next is samples to check quality, then we have to figure out how to ship cost effectively to our warehouses. The critical stage is what bankers call KYC.. It's not a rip off fried chicken chain.. haha.
KYC means Know Your Customer.. in the case of banks, it's to make sure that customers are not using bank accounts for dodgy purposes, because governments worldwide have made banks take this responsibility.  
So it looks like I'm on the way back to Morocco when I get chance, to do a spot of KYS.. Know Your Supplier - a friendly ethics check. I'll explain.. 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over eight years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here. 
Over 50,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here  I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka and the whole team from the UK.  Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken.

We my friends are in the Gift Business.. the act of giving (I am fond of telling anyone who will listen) is nothing short of an act of love. Thus: We are in the business of facilitating love.. Therefore, and most giftware traders our customers especially,agree we have a moral imperative to ensure there is nothing dodgy in the supply chain. Obviously child labour is an issue, but in developing countries with cash economies it is relatively easy for bad players to pay pittance piece work rates, or even slave labour. And quite rightly our customers.. that probably you, hold us to account to make sure the gifts we sell are not tainted by dodgy practices.
So my job is to go and check, meet the suppliers, find out if they are decent people, talk to workers tour the factory where possible, draw my own conclusion.

I remember in the early days of travelling to India meeting a fashion jewellery supplier, they had a spectacularly nice trade show stand with smart young sales people. The besuited bossed bragged about supplying some well know high street brands, and bullied us into placing a (for us at the time) a mega order. But before confirming I insisted on a trip to their production facilities which were in the heart of old Delhi.. we were taken by rickshaw down winding back lanes, draped with random electric wires and rubble underfoot. Lead through a maze of go-downs and ancient souk like shops. In a dingy below ground mud floored room we found a hundred ladies in dim light threading beads and packing and labelling jewellery.  And lets not be fooled, in India a lot of production is done in villages by organised outworking gang-leaders, this was just the finishing part. If this was finishing, what was the rest like. I canceled the order.

I learned not to trust the pushy guys, the ones that make impossible claims, the false image. In my chat with young Aymen I told him how important this is... Deal with gentle folk I told him, anyone else will be trouble in the long run. We found Marrakech to be stuffed full of pushy guys (not many ladies)  so I worry that in there we can find gentle folk, but Aymen told me that away from the tourist zone you can find honest humble business people.. 
What happened in India? That boss guy didn't give up he chased me for the order for weeks if not months. I told him straight the reason why. He dropped the prices, I still said no. Eventually (maybe) he got my message, and sent me photos of ladies working at tables with good lighting and smiles. But an image is one thing a good heart is another. 
Maybe we did some good I don't know, but we never confirmed that order.

Of course there are many people who don't believe. Who think that just the image is good enough, you don't really have to have real integrity, that's for fools. Many times I have been told, honest business people never get rich, you have to be dodgy to succeed. Our ex-business partner in Spain was sadly like this, and that relationship couldn't succeed, despite many years of trying to persuade on the benefits of going straight. Seth Godin, is a marketing genius, I subscribe to his always apt micro blogs.. today's words of wisdom explain why dodgy doesn't work, and even more so in today's world.  Read it here.. it's called: Don't Pee in the Pool.  We are all connected even if we think we are not.

Of course I don't always get it right, I'm human and can make poor character judgements, but I believe we have a moral duty to try and do our best. Trading fairly is a powerful way to change the world for the better, YOU are part of this process, selling gift products, that help other humans be kind to each other, we all in the circle, it's like karma.. 

Speaking of Spain, we have been interviewing for Spanish staff for the new Spain website in Sheffield. I can't believe how many people applied for the job, and so many likable enthusiastic people all so keen to work for AW.. I spent an hour debating with Tomas, Katka and Rodrigo over the list of candidates. It's hard work trying to decide which ones to employ, who understands the AW ethos, who will fit in. It's a new adventure.. I'll keep you updated.

Next week I'm the UK..

Take care

title: Don't Worry
content_html:
Greetings from Euroland,

 

Last week I was telling you about how upbeat everyone was feeling with the news about the vaccine and a heap of other good news.

It was a Happy Day.. you can read about it here.

This week it's back to a regular level of stress as hopes of a Brexit Deal this Christmas diminish. By Sunday we might have some more firm news one way or another.

But it's not looking good as the ports are already jammed, booking a container from Asia is like trying to get tickets to the Queen's last garden party.

Coco was telling me even after getting a booking, they can increase the prices an hour before loading and tough luck, take it or leave it attitude.

It's a bloodbath.. add to this a self imposed Brexit mess on top of a looming recession, on top of Christmas, on top of covid. What the jeepers is happening!!?


So annoying when the glib government ministers keep saying British business needs to be ready for Brexit, and how much money they have spent on educating us. Websites with bad links, unanswered questions, changing scenarios, confusion and useless webinars. 

Good job we have been getting ready for Brexit for the last three years. Making our own plans. 

 

In Slovakia Tomas is busy negotiating extra warehouse space, he managed to get 200 pallets in a warehouse across the road. In Spain we just this week racked out another 1000 sq meters of warehouse space.

Plus two new jobs in Spain and several in Slovakia.. are you sure you are taking back control Boris?

All that business that used to come from the UK to Europe will now go from Europe to Europe.. this must be happening across many companies and industries.




Not bad.. this is one days work. There is still blue sky in Spain. The English and French versions of our Spain websites are 90% ready. AWArtisan.eu  and AWArtisan.fr   If you are outside the UK, and worried about getting  supplies.. DON'T WORRY!!   We have Plan A  and B and C..  whatever happens we have ways to keep you supplied.

Tomas, Katka and Raul (and me) have been devising plans like mad. The shipping companies have plans.. but could be expensive.

 

My favoured plan is to load a lorry once a week with all the export orders and take it to Slovakia.. to the shipping depot.. AW Slovakia imports it and then reinvoices to you our customers. Since shipping from Slovakia is cheaper than UK, and the cost of the truck would be about €1.50 per carton.. it could even cost about the same to ship. Watch this space.. but don't Worry!!

 

Despite the container congestion, miraculously we are still receiving containers.. This week Salt Lamps came from  Pakistan.. so lots back in stock.. see below. On this shipment.. a new product.



This is Bryant's baby. Normally Tomas and I devise, develop and design new products.. Normally this is best done face to face but these days it's been done remotely and slowly.. 

So Bryant our imports manager fancied having a go.. he is the proud father.. of a set of salt lamp shot glasses. 

A bit more about the container crisis.. I know some readers like to know about the business nitty gritty. 

Normally it costs about $2000 to get a 40ft container from Asia to the UK.. give or take $500 depending on supply and demand. This week the market price hits $10,000 and prone to change even after booking. 

So that's an extra $8,000 - and since an average container of gift products might hold $80,000 of stock... you can do the maths - it's adding 10% to the cost.  

With bulky or low value products (like food basics) which won't be anything like this value..  the percent increase could be 30% or 40% in some cases. Scary.

On top of massive spending by governments, I can't see how hyperinflation can be avoided. 

 

So on that bombshell.. let's move on to something more cheerful.

It's almost Christmas. What do you want for Christmas?

I want the best ever Christmas song.. the one that really cheers you up.. and since I didn't see Coco my wife, since last Christmas.. it has to be..



If that doesn't put you in the mood, nothing will.

 

Take care, stay safe.

More news next week.

 

David

title: David's AW News: NO DRAMA - KEEP SMILE
content_html:
Greetings from Frangipani Warehouse Bali. 

Hope things are good with you guys, and that September is off to a good start..
Last week I was telling you about Teak tails in Java, and the new Baby in the Baby Home we support.. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Here in the AW warehouse we got off to a good start with the first container of the month loaded and on the way from Bali to Slovakia.
The Container arrives at 8am and is finally loaded by 6.30pm - very busy day, last minute stock arriving and being packed - every inch of space must be used. If anything has empty space inside like furniture then stuff is packed inside there.. It's hard work. Our two accountant girls check every single box item, papers have to be provided for different items like wooden stuff.. Packing list has to be made. Everything is labelled and barcoded. Export papers prepared..  it's a lot of work, believe me.
Well done team.. awesome job! 

There is a local local election in Bali soon. People are voting for a new Governor. Posters are starting to appear on the roadsides. I noticed this guy.. 
I'm always amazed that politicians here have no problem using English.. This guy calls himself "Big Daddy" and "De Gadjah" The Elephant.. His personal catch phrase is "NO DRAMA - KEEP SMILE"   - (in English) and his Instagram of course is full of him working out in the gym with British heavy rock background music. Ringo says he can't win the election, maybe he will come in third place, but he is a popular figure in Bali.   I can see his appeal, the strong guy you don't mess with who will stick up for the island at the national level.
 
Anyway so it's No Drama - Keep Smile.. Kids are back to school and holidays are over. It's time to look towards Christmas. And I can already see that folks are getting organised in that direction.
Usually this time of year our Christmas stock has landed or is landing in the UK.. but the container situation is dire.. We were calculating current shipping times from PO to delivery, China came in at 90 days which I think is impressive, whilst Indonesia despite heroic efforts clocked an average of 160 days. India we haven't calculated yet but I feel it will be longer. This means of course that heaps of stock that should be in our warehouses is stuck bobbing about on the water somewhere on its way around Africa. Unfortunately there have been some heavy shipping charges, which you might have noticed we have had to partially pass on.  But today we have a long awaited Indian container so lots and lots back in stock..

But the good news is.. you will notice many more Volume Discounts across the website. And always matching Gold Reward Discounts. Because if you order more from a family of products, we can pick and pack those items more cost effectively (hence the discount). We also believe that the more of a range you stock the more you will sell - so a WIN WIN. PLUS.. if you reorder within 30 days you automatically qualify for the Gold Reward Discount - basically the same as Volume discount (but without the need to buy the volume). So you can top up at the discount price. 
You know years ago when I was a retailer (Story here) we used to say.. Be loyal to your stock, and your customers will be loyal to you. I believe that is more true than ever. We know our most regular customers are the most successful businesses.. So if you are focused and professional, reorder within 30 days to maximise profits.. But get this.. BIG NO DRAMA BONUS.. some of our customers don't realise that we give Gold Reward Discounts not just on the stock you bought before.. But on EVERYTHING (almost everything) across the range. 
So just to recap guys.. Buy a decent range, reorder regularly even to top up.. and working with us like this helps us to help you.. WIN WIN. Or as Big Daddy would say.. No Drama - Keep Smile!

Some products we have been trying to source for years, and never quite find a supplier that meets our standard or can give us the right price. Some products you just can't find. One of those things is Reindeer Moss.. ok calm down it's not from reindeers.. it's what (allegedly) your average reindeer loves to forage for lunch.. But crafty folk, the same ones that buy Molten Glass Bowls for Terrariums or Soap Flowers - have been requesting this item for years.. So.. I'm so happy that we finally have a  supply line. 
Sandra in our Sheffield Showroom have been getting quite creative with the moss... 
Speaking of the Sheffield Showroom..
We have another OPEN WEEK coming up.. from the 30th September.. of course you can come anytime.. (just make an online appointment) but on the open week lots of things will be happening. 
It's all happening lots back in stock.. something new also.. 
Take care.. have a lovely weekend - remember NO DRAMA - KEEP SIMILE.. and all will be well.

More news updates next week.

David

title: Did you win? Karma from Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

It's been a pretty full week, running around Bali like crazy sorting out issues, trying to find new stock, developing ongoing ideas.

Last week I asked you for help in naming our new warehouse.. you can read about it here.
The response has been overwhelming hundreds of suggestions rolled in, with some pretty free-thinking ideas, and some nice iterations on the theme of our old warehouse.. that was called: The Yellow Coconut Depot, after the name of the village.

Now we have moved to what is basically a fishing village (called Jack Fruit Village) on a rugged stretch of the coast.. there are big blue doors so blue cropped up a lot.. I liked the idea: Blue Coconut Depot.. also to reflect the being near the sea.. lot's of people liked the temples connection, near by is a Sea Temple.. so lots of ideas using that theme, but I feel we need to be careful not to offend religious feelings.. not that Bali folk are remotely snowflakish.. so it was hard work choosing a winner.. after long deliberation.. and consultations with Ringo and the staff.. who have to live with it.. we decided on a very popular suggestion that came up a lot.. the first person that made this suggestion obviously wins the prize.. everyone else will get the consolation prize of Free Shipping.. read on to find out what it was.. 

eanwhile Ringo and I have been running around Bali, Sukawati, Dempasar and Ubud and places in-between - they say up to a million people are employed in the handicraft production on Bali, and much of it is in this quarter of the island.  Sukawati is home to the art market, and one area houses a colony of artists.. all living in small studio / flats painting there own particular flavour of art on canvas. These find there way to the showrooms in Ubud or the large export companies on the main road to Dempasar.  Ringo had an idea that we could find an artist here that could come and paint the warehouse to make it beautiful. In our lease there is a clause that we have to donate one 100kg sack of rice to the Temple each year and keep the property "Indah" ie not just maintained but beautiful. And since we are in the business of finding beautiful things for lovely people.. it seems perfectly logical that we should make it as nice as possible for the staff that work here. 
So we set of in the maze of back avenues draped with frangipani trees that make up the artist colony. Inside small compounds are stacks of ready canvases, and lined up against walls - work in progress.. We find the Buddah painting, the one painting that sells constantly and well in our art range.. That's ours I say!!  Turns out this guy supplies the export agent who carries a huge selection, and we have ordered from in the past. Actually it's a two guy partnership, as you'd expect pretty cool guys, artists have to look the part - they turn up our warehouse to give us a quote for the artwork. 

Meanwhile in Slovakia, Tomas and Anton have taken the chosen name and come up with designs, we show them to the artists who you can see are seriously into this project, taking pictures on their phones, disusing with Ringo and coming up with modifications..
So it's about time I tell you the winning name.. it had to be a name with deep Ancient Wisdom connections, and it turns out this is very apt. 
Roll of drums...  Simple and easy..   the name is:  "Ancient Wisdom Frangipani Depot" 

Frangipani is very AW: 
Frangipani is used in offerings in Bali, those little trays of offerings made to the gods every morning, often contain frangipani petals. The gnarled trunk and branches, shows determination and strength, while the flowers are spectacularly elegant and beautiful. All over the world, the Frangipani has spiritual ancient wisdom meanings.. here in Hindu Bali - the "Strength to overcome challenges" some people believe the spirits reside in the branches looking over us. The flowers come in many colours, and it is a national hobby (Ringo tells me) to keep a tree at home and keep grafting on branches that produce different colour blossoms, so in the end, you have a multi-colour tree. This also seems apt for AW..  
So we planted a young Frangipani tree near our little temple in the corner of the car park.. 
The flower is also closely associated with Spa's and aromatherapy.. and since many of these are our customers is also fitting. We don't yet sell real Fragipani oil.. right now trying hard to find a direct supply.. 
The other day the head holy man called by, he was very happy with our Indah.. he told Ringo so happy in fact that he told us the 100kg of rice was not mandatory, no need - he said you are doing enough. It's all good Karma:)

       Our young Frangipani tree, next to the temple, and a big pot with Frangipani petal motif. 
      Frangipani lines the streets of Bali

Vicki Bonass - was the first person to suggest this and wins the prize!  Plus heaps of karma and goodwill all the way from Bali. Congratulations Vicki.. Vouchers on the way to you :)
well done Vicki - Ringo and the team say thank you.


   Everyone else we will send free shipping vouchers to.


This is just the artist impression.. not done yet.. (Thank you Anton) The office are will look like this, but will also paint the external wall in a similar way.

Meanwhile in the UK.. it is a Bank Holiday weekend, which means we have been extremely busy. Ula has been in charge and doing an amazing job getting the orders out - it's been manic but, but Ula and her team have been like the Frangipani overcoming obstacles with stubborn determination and.. still looking beautiful. Also, I know the warehouse team have been total hero's dealing with in-coming containers (including one from Bali), whilst getting the maximum orders out. Well done guys.

Hope you have a wonderful Indah weekend  I read it should be hot & sunny :)
Next week I will be in China. 

Take care 

David
