title: David's AW News: It was 20 years ago today..
content_html:
Greetings from Delhi, India

I'm with Toni (our man from Spain) travelling in India and right now we are at the Delhi Fair, India biggest B2B trade show for the gift trade. 
What can I say my first impressions are its cold (for India) and very quiet. The usual first day registration hall hustle and bustle just never happened with just a trickle of visitors and barely a queue.


It's a little earlier this year and clashes with other trade events around the world (including the Birmingham faire) and CNY so maybe just a case of bad timing. However the creativity and competition to innovate is off the scale, so much of interest.. Toni is loving it and getting a little over excited.
Last week I was telling you about our arrival in India and Toni's first impression of India, and how I was here 20 years ago.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Toni, Chatterjee (our India agent) and I flew from Kolkata on Monday via Vistara - the smartest most comfortable budget airline you can imagine. Comfy seats, legroom, complimentary drinks and snacks. Very polite and helpful staff. Even our fellow customers all seemed to be gentle and polite. Nobody wanted to sell us anything extra, not even a scratch card. Ticket fee included 15kg luggage and hold bags. Our luggage was over weight by 3kg, the check in girl just smiled and said no problem. My new favourite airline.

It's slightly comical to see how Delhi folk react to the cold.. cold being around 20c jackets and big fluffy scarves wrapped around the head and under the chin. While in the UK, Sheffield is actually very cold with snow falling.. So I hope the weather is not causing you too much disruption.

Year of the Dragon.
Coco has finished work now - dispatching 3 containers in 3 days, before breaking for the CNY holiday. She drove back to her hometown normally a four hour drive, but the traffic was horrendous, access to the motorway blocked when it became too congested so came mostly on the back roads. 14 hours drive.   Now she is in the home town exchanging red envelopes with her family and celebrating the Year of the Dragon. She tells me this year the ban on fireworks has been lifted because so many people complained, and the government realise folks need cheering up.

Children's Home Update
Last week I was telling you it was 20 years since I first met Chatterjee and came to Kolkata. Chatterjee is one of my oldest friends, and together we have made a lot of good business happen.
Before we left for Delhi we took Toni to see the children's home that AW supports in Chatterjee's home town. Now Mr Kundu has 28 children, twelve years ago when we started the youngest is now the oldest, many have been taught English and moved on to work and others have come and joined the home. 


We brought chocolates for the kids from Bali - they were so polite and grateful Toni said they broke his heart. We pledged more donations to help refurbish part of the home and promised to find other ways to support them. Then we did the traditional high-five routine which the kids love.. The kid who was little came top in his class for years, he has become like a son and righthand man to Mr Kundu helping to run the home. Recently he got a good job in a bank and gives most of his salary to the home. It's always an emotional experience to visit.

20th Birthday of Alan.
Anyway 20 years ago I met Mr Chatterjee and around the same time Alan came to work at Ancient Wisdom in Sheffield. Today the team at AW UK are celebrating Alan's 20th Birthday in AW..
Many of our regular customers may have interacted with Alan over the years, I'm sure you will join with me and in wishing him well and all the best for the next 20 years... Big Congratulations to Alan!

Meanwhile..
A container from Indonesia just arrived in the UK.. so there is lots back in stock, and some new items perfect for Valentines or Mother's Day. See below.
There is FREE SHIPPING all February as our Valentines gift to you!!

I wish you a lovely weekend especially if you are celebrating Valentines early over the weekend. 
Next week we are on a Road Trip north to some interesting rarely visited places..
Full report next Friday.

Take care and Namaste

David

title: We Need Your Help 😀
content_html:
Greetings from India, I'm at the Denmark Pub, a restored heritage hotel on the banks of the Ganges in the town or Serampore near Kolkata.

It's early morning as I write, I can hear dogs barking, a crow, people on the street calling to each other, horns honking.. cars and boats..  it's India it's noisy.
Last week I was telling you about our new dog Happier, who has adopted us at our Bali warehouse, you can read about it here.

On Wednesday I took a Malindo air flight to KL airport. 80% of people wearing masks, many latex gloves, the business lounge was all but deserted. Strange times right now. Then a 4 hour flight to Kolkatta, arriving at midnight. Crashed at the Swiss hotel near the airport  (welcome back Mr David). The next morning met up with Tomas who had arrived earlier and our man in India Mr Chatterjee. After breakfast we drove to Sermpore, spent the day checking work in progress at Mr Chatterjee factory, where his team produce eco-friendly jute and cotton bags for us.
Regular readers will know I usually stay at the Royal Hotel, which has to be the worlds worst, my last visit was bad.. very bad! - with stained sheets, cold water and assorted insects as fellow guests. Fortunately, it's not the only hotel in town anymore.. The Denmark Pub has just opened, it's a restored heritage building previously occupied by the local police, it was discovered that the building had been a Danish Tavern in olden days when the Danish people occupied the area in 1755 and probably traded opium and such along the river.
The building has been restored with money from Denmark, it's a living museum, and run by the Park Hotel group, so excellent staff. They are still painstakingly restoring it, it will take years, so far only two rooms are available, but I have to say they are palatial. I'm in one and Tomas the other.. so haha we have block booked a whole hotel..

    

The view..

Later of course the British via the mercantile skills of the East India company come to rule all India, and this Englishman is back trading much more respectable goods. Jute and cotton. 
After checking the stock and then going over our ideas for new products and commissioning a range of samples that will be produced in the evening we retired to the Denmark Pub. Ravi who is Mr Chatterjee's business partner showed me news feed on his mobile that claimed that drinking whiskey protected you against coronavirus - Fake News! me and Tomas cried.. then after a seconds thought.. oh well it's worth a try, so we opened a bottle of Black Label. 

We need your help!

Meanwhile back in the UK, the new drop-shipping site is really kicking off.. it's still in beta mode and so we are asking users for suggestions.. but it's working good. Simply add your customers details and then click "New Order" - you will need to know the product code but is easy to add products if you have the info to hand - and if you have an order to full-fill then you will. Here is a quick User Guide

So dear reader we need your help, feedback and suggestions. In any event aw-dropship.com for any gift business is a no-brainer, it's an extra string to your bow, another way to serve your customers (and to make extra money). At the very least if a customer asks you for something you don't have you can say "No problem" I'll get it shipped to your home address today. Two minutes job to make extra sales.  Register today  Anyway it's the future.. more sales are moving online all the time, this helps you be part of that trend.
On the page footer, you can see the link for feedback and suggestions.. this going direct to Raul and the development team in KL. Thank you so much for your help.

Tomorrow Tomas and I will visit the children's home we support here in Serampore. A full report next week. 

Hope you have a lovely weekend. 

Take care.

David

title: David's AW News: Why Independence is fun..
content_html:
Greetings from a traffic jam in Bali


I'm on the way to work in the AW-Advantage office (we call it the beach office). It's 10 to 15 minutes of normal traffic, but these days it can take an hour, the traffic in Bali has reached crisis proportions.
So I open my laptop in the back of my Grab taxi and get some work done, including writing to you. 
Last week I was telling you about Angels & Babies and how we are supporting a young charity here that is saving the lives of babies and helping single moms in dire-straits..  if you missed you can catch up here. The streets are lined with Red & White flags, because tomorrow is Independence Day in Indonesia, a big thing around here. 

I just arrived at the beach office. The team are enthusiastically dressed up as historical or mythical figures of Indonesia culture and then do cosplay acts. All before work.. so I have to be here early because I'm the appointed judge, it's like an episode of AW got Talent. 

So much enthusiasm and energy, so early in the morning.. it's quite exhausting! 


Then after much good humour and entertaining each other, and making content for personal social media... its back to work.

But I learnt a few things about the culture and mythical history of Indonesia. Incredibly diverse, so many very different peoples, languages, religions and sharply different cultures.. yet cheerfully united and comfortable with being Indonesian together.  A different kind of nationalism, totally at odds with the nasty thuggish British nationalism that makes me depressed these days.
I learned how the port city of Surabaya got it's name.. The story began, as these things often do, with a pair of friends: Sura the shark and Baya the crocodile. Basically they had a big fight over food, until in the end they worked it out and became friends, got together and the city is named after them.. Surabaya. The symbol of the city is the shark and the crocodile. 

These two young guys bring the story to life with slapstick humour and energy.

Later the warehouse team - who yesterday loaded a container bound for Slovakia warehouse..believe me that's really hard work..
 ..they certainly deserve some independence day fun and join the beach team. 

For party games...

Meanwhile in the UK.. Rodrigo and his team have been hosting a showroom open day in the Sheffield HQ. This is so important, not just so we can showcase our latest products.. but because we can get first hand face to face feedback and great direction from our lovely customers.. the last open day - I was around and it was absolutely delightful meeting customers. Rodrigo says a big thank you to everyone who called by, and an extra big thank you for all the super useful feedback and ideas.

It's a bank holiday creeping up on us.. the BIG one.. time to get stocked up.. and we have heaps of deals, some amazing new products.. and Halloween bath bombs from the AW-Aromatics team..
A new range of Gemstones figures has just arrived.. a lot of work went into this - I'm personally very happy to see them.. we have been trying to nail this important product range for years.. 

Wishing you a magical and delightful weekend. Hope you discover your independence!
Next week's news may be from a different place.. exciting no?

David

title: Discovering The Angel Number
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield and AW HQ.

 

It's been 48 days since the fire at AW, today as I type this the last part of the burned out building has been dragged to the floor.
So the old AW HQ is officially no more.
I just calculated how many days we occupied the building from being given the key in May 2008 to the day of the fire is 4444 days.
In China 4 is an extremely unlucky number, but in other ancient wisdom it means different things. Numerology is interesting, since biblical times numbers have powers. Last week I was telling you about the creative solutions we are using at AW to cope. If you missed it you can read it here.


On Tuesday, (that's just 44 days since the fire) things definitely changed, like the ground shifted. We got a call from the insurance company saying basically they would support us, the warehouse we want to move to - our potential new landlord called and wants to meet us and move things forward.
Yes.. and in goods-in, in despatch, in customer service, and in production - I could feel the mood shifting. AW is back, we are starting to win battles, people smiling and getting stuff done. Andy - one of our long standing order pickers stopped me between the racking, "It's going to be alright isn't it?" - "I think so Andy, we can do this!" Behind his mask I could feel his relief and smile. "I don't mind telling you I cried for Ancient Wisdom, I don't want to lose this"



Difficult times anyway what with covid and all, but in difficult times people pull together. And everyday we make some new steps forward, new products, better ways of doing things, arrival of new equipment. It's getting better - AW is officially back.
The encouragement everyday from you our customers has been amazing working like a magic hand. Of course we thank you for supporting us with your orders, kind words and not least a wave of good reviews on Reviews.co.uk feel free to add your encouragement :)

 

The number 4 in China is considered seriously unlucky, even buildings don't have a 4th or 14th or 24th floor, often just missing out those numbers - it also make's the upper floors seem higher I guess. But a bit of googling and I find that in China 4444 is actually super lucky.It seems when 4 is presented repeatedly as 4444, it gets rid of the ominous connotation and takes on auspicious meaning. The reason being is that the look of 4444 resembles four rockets neatly shooting towards the sky. It is a very good sign that signals your fortune to be like the rockets shooting high into the sky. In western numerology in tarot reading this number is the ultimate guardian angel number. The number contains a message from your angels that your spiritual guides and protectors are close at hand and are ready to intervene on your behalf. The Angel Number - check it out..

 

So the number 4 can be both bad and good luck.. just like the phoenix effect..

 

Maybe it's all mumbo jumbo, but sometimes you can feel forces at work you just don't understand. It seems to me AW has always bounced back from major setbacks (several of them) - always stronger and better than before. From the very beginning of AW it has been a pattern. On our company's 21st birthday I wrote a piece about this called The Phoenix Effect. You can read about it here.

 

It's another week of new products coming back on-line, or brand new products arriving. Check out the new stuff below. AW is back!

 

Take care.. I hope your guardian angels are not working from home.. have a great weekend.

 

 David

title: Keeping my Cool in Spain
content_html:
Hola Amigos and greetings from Spain

Let me tell you, Spain is sizzling hot right now! My house is perched on a hill with a view of the Mediterranean. Normally, the sea breeze keeps things cool, and I've never been a fan of air conditioning. I mean, who needs it when you can just open the windows and let that sea breeze work its magic? So, no AC for me, ever! But, guess what? This summer is putting me to the test! I'm sweating buckets, more than I ever did in India or Indonesia. The nights are so steamy I might as well sleep in a sauna. To cool off, I've practically turned into a fish in my pool!

But guess what? I chatted with Coco this morning in China, and she's dealing with an even bigger hot mess! Seriously, what in the world is going on? We've got our own little global warming party here! And you know what's even crazier? I had a court date in Spain recently, and let me tell you, Spanish law operates on a different time zone altogether! No speedy resolutions here, folks. More below..
Last week I was telling you about Istanbul and when Coco met our lovely agent Hatice. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Now, here's the juicy bit: I wasn't supposed to be in Spain this week. I really need to be elsewhere, but a stupid legal dispute dragged me back here. I totally wasted a day in court. Because zero, nada, nothing happened. For reasons totally beyond me the whole shebang got delayed until.. July 2024! I wanted to write about it here mentioning no names of course.. So I wrote a really funny upbeat newsletter describing the whole ridiculous thing. After writing it - I felt so much better!!. It's good to get things off your chest as they say..  I sent that newsletter to my team yesterday... and...

They won't let me tell you..  "Nooooo.. David don't say that.." and "Customers are not interested" and "It's hilarious, it's true but don't say it". Blar blar blar.. So sorry folks we just have to move on.(I do listen to my team). They are right, I suppose, we have bigger fish to fry, and we sure don't need that mess adding to the heatwave. We have to see the bigger picture, right? 
So enough of my rant! My sweet grandfather from Yorkshire always said, "If you ain't got anything nice to say about someone, just say nowt!" Wise words, indeed. He also used to joke, "In this world, there's only me and thee that are sane, and I'm not so sure about you!" Haha, makes me smile every time! So, despite all the crazy fudged-up people in this world, let's try to see the best in 'em. It might just cool us down a bit!

They say the world is the hottest it's ever been. Extreme weather everywhere.. yet the whole world is getting obsessed with a Pink Barbie Movie.
And what's wrong with that? If you want pink things to follow up on this trend at AW we have lots.. including our new whipped soap in Pink.. Check out the PINK LINKS.


Speaking of which we are giving it away for free.. FREE Whipped soaps with every order this week.. if you are lucky you might get a pink one :)

Lots and lots back in stock in the UK.. plus new and better deals.
And did you know at AW-Aromatic it is Christmas already?. (Yes, realise I used the "C" word in July, I do apologise).. but you have to plan ahead if you want the best trends in Xmas fragrances.. check out the brand new range here. Exclusively available only at AW. 

It's so hot in Spain we are changing the working hours, starting early morning to avoid the afternoon heat. It's a good idea. In Bali, Ringo and his team always load containers at night because it's cooler. One of those containers arrived in Spain a few days ago, and the team almost wilted away in the heat unloading it. Everyone from the office came to help the warehouse team to ease the load. What amazing AW hero's we have here.. So this afternoon work we are having a beach party with MFT (My favourite team in Spain)..  They have done a fantastic job this year so the least I can do is take them out for a party.


Stay cool, everyone, and stand by for news from a different part of the world next week.

David

title: My Black & White Idea
content_html:
Greeting from Spain, where we have a sister company. Last week I was telling you about the strange conversations you can hear in Ancient Wisdom's customer service department. You can read it here.
I'm really excited, besides my self.. because this week my baby has finally arrived. Conceived in Bali, gestated in Bangalore, and birthed in Blighty this week. I'm talking of course about our new incense range: Dark Arts & White Magic.
It started like this.. I'm in Bali with our agent Ringo (who knows everything there is to know about Bali) and he is explaining to me why many of the statues are dressed up in black and white checked clothes. All over Bali you will see black and white chequered cloth draped over trees, statues, and worn by people in ceremonies. This special cloth is called saput poleng in the local language and is considered somewhat sacred. Often trees are wrapped in the cloth, this means that someone believes the tree is the home to some mystic spirit. Ringo told me that if you look carefully the material is black and white and grey. The pattern reminds us that good and evil are woven together. To truly know good you must also touch evil, we humans are the mixture, the grey in the cloth.
We were at one of our suppliers (the one who makes the mosaic turtles), businesses often burn incense for good luck but the incense I could smell was just really nice, evocative and fragrant. I went to check which incense it was and discovered a pack Darshan incense. I'd not heard of this company, based in Bangalore, where as luck would have it I was headed the week after. I'm pretty sure this was the moment of conception. That chequered cloth of Bali gave me an idea for a new brand of incense. I resolved to visit Darshan in Bangalore.
So as soon as I got to Bangalore I called them up and went to check them out. In total that week I visited maybe eight companies. Only two met our criteria for good working conditions, one of them was Darshan International.
A lovely company run by two brothers. South Indians, very gentle but very smart. They showed me round the factory, without any qualms and I was really impressed. Nice well ventilated working areas, and staff that seemed happy and motivated. What's more when I floated the idea of a new incense brand, they were hugely enthusiastic and offered up their in-house designer a guy called Vinod to work with our designer Helen, to put my concept into action. They both worked really hard on it, as did Carlos (our man in Spain), and you can see the packs are designed to be bilingual.
Here's the boss, just after we signed a deal to be exclusive distributors for Spain and UK.
Well that was back in October 2012, so the project has taken eleven months to fruition.. I hope you think it's worth it.. please check it out below.
One foot note to the story, I was back in Bangalore to to check on the projects progress in July, as it happened the Bali distributor was visiting the same day. Actually a family of six had all come, an old guy with his wife his son and his wife and their children. All very smiley and happy a real family business. We showed them the new incense range.. they were just absolutely delighted. I told them it was actually a packet of their incense that had started it off. The old guy took me to one side and pumping my hand with tears in his eyes he just thanked me for promoting Bali culture.
More news next week.

title: A complete dog's breakfast...
content_html:
Greetings from Spain
Where I just arrived, last week I was telling you about the magic packaging man in Yiwu China. You can read about it here.
Last Friday was Brexit day.. or Brexit day that never was :)
Since then we have also survived April Fools day, moved into British Summer Time (officially) and discovered that after all that talk of Brexit being immutably fixed on 29th March, that it now could be 12th of April, 22nd of May or even an extended Flexit date sometime in the future. So much for Mrs Mays immutability.. What a dog's breakfast, what a mess, nobody knows what the hell is going on.
Meanwhile, we are getting on with updating our websites.
You might have seen our Europe website: AWGifts.eu it's been up and running over a year now, solidly tested and bedded in. Our customers across Europe seem to love it.
So this format we are rolling out on all our UK based websites. In the early hours of this morning, Raul (our IT wizard) in Kuala Lumpur was switching over our French site. A big job, lots of links to fix, pages to reformat, behind the scenes we were all fixing things in the early hours. Check it out:(our IT wizard) in Kuala Lumpur was switching over our French site. A big job, lots of links to fix, pages to reformat, behind the scenes we were all fixing things in the early hours. Check it out: AW-Cadeaux.com it's mobile friendly and all that and hope easier and more fun to use. )AW-Cadeaux.com it's mobile friendly and all that and hope easier and more fun to use.
The French site is our busiest after the main UK site almost 10,000 active customers in France. Now I hope all our work is not wasted.. Brexit could cause friction and quite easily disrupt and destroy the trade overnight - our French team are understandably worried.
So the only remaining site to convert to the new format is the main UK site..
Coming very soon, watch this space.
I'm in Spain to fix some problems with our Spanish company.
It's a long sad story, maybe one day I will tell you. Needless to say, trusting people is always a risky business, mostly trust enables better business, but sometimes, sadly it is abused.
Anyway I don't worry anymore, out of every bad thing comes good, you just have to do the right thing and keep a positive attitude.
Brexit is also a worry, but we made our plans the best we could, now all we can do is wait and see how it works out.
A complete dog's breakfast.. is a very British saying. In America they probably don't know what you are talking about.. but I think it's a jolly descriptive picture.. you are making a meal and it all goes wrong beans get burnt, eggs spoil etc- a big mess - the only thing it's good for is pet food.. So at least the Dog gets breakfast.

title: David's AW News: Return to Kathmandu!
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu


Hope you are well and didn't get fooled on April fools day.. I did! 

Yesterday morning I took a Batik airways flight from Denpasar to Kuala Lumpa, changed there for Malaysia air to Kathmandu. Arrived about 10pm local time. 

Toni from Spain arrived just before me and was waiting in the lobby in our hotel in downtown Kathmandu. We went for a late night beer to catch up. 

Last week I was telling you about the Melasti Ceremony, which was taking place right by our beach office, no tourists allowed, but we got a pass. If you missed it you can catch up here. Or check the Youtube video here. 

This morning we went to see our delightful shipping agent, Mr Padam. He told us our orders from the last visit are being shipped right now.. and as we progressed to visit one of our other suppliers, we saw our products being loaded on to a truck.. Toni, who has lots of energy, got stuck in to help load. I'm a bit tired from the travelling and Toni is seriously jet-lagged, but it's great to be back in Nepal and the people so happy to see us and welcoming. The maze of alleyways and back streets that is Thamel and home to many giftware artisans is like a land of opportunity; anything could happen.
Back in Kathmandu!

After the Melasti cleansing ceremony I was telling you about last week, I went up to Ubud to see the magnificent Ogoh-ogoh parade and dramatic show.. Wow, it was epic. The town was crammed to capacity, and amid fireworks, incense and light shows, the monsters were carried through the streets by youngsters with huge energy. 

After the excitement, I checked into a local hotel, because at 9pm they already start closing all the roads and lights are going off - ahead of the Day of Silence, which starts at 6am the next morning. 

During this period, after the Ogoh-Ogoh and before the Day of Silence, secret, mysterious ceremonies take place in hidden temples. I know because four years ago, in the pandemic, I was here with our guy Bondhan and his wife Debbie, staying in the same hotel. 

This was the pandemic, the Ogoh-Ogoh parade had been cancelled - but we heard something was happening in the heart of the monkey forest. So despite restrictions we clambered over a fence and in pitch black sneaked into the Monkey Forest, we could hear gambalan music and chanting and drums..right in the heart of the forest is an ancient temple, weird things were going on there we sneaked as close up as we could.. boy it was scary.. if we got caught I don't know what would have happened. I remember seeing a fire, leaping shadows, incense smoke, and strange dressed priests ringing bells.. I joked it looked like a human sacrifice was happening.. 

Then a security guy spotted us or heard something and came to see, and we scarpered back to the fence, hearts pounding and escaped. 

Anyway, this year, after the parade excitement, I'm back in the hotel. So from 6am on Saturday until 6am Sunday, there is no internet, access to outside is not allowed, I can walk around the hotel grounds, and that's all, they tell me if I talk to any other guests, it should be in a low voice. But I only see a couple of people by the pool reading books. No one talks. One day alone, in total silence - overlooking the Monkey Forest. Actually, it was amazing, I was kind of sad when it was over, but I went for breakfast in a local cafe and several local people I met on the walk there remembered me from the time in the pandemic. So nice in Ubud. 

Thanks for your help! 
I have to say thank you to everyone that filled in the questionnaire so far.. So many useful suggestions and insights. I'm studying everyday, you still have time to have your say.  Link here. 

Upheavals.. If you don't have enough drama in the world with devastating earthquakes and volcanic activities. Now the Trump tariffs are shaking the world financial systems, who knows what the fallout will be and how it could affect us. 

Big News! 
And now we have a major product launch.. 
We finally got the Zodiac Bath Fizzers from the team at AW-Aromatics. Next level awesome.

Wishing you a wonderful weekend. 
More news and an update from Nepal next week. 

Take care

The town was crammed to capacity, and amid fireworks, incense and light shows, the monsters were carried through the streets by youngsters with huge energy. After the excitement, I checked into a local hotel, because at 9pm they already start closing all the roads and lights are going off - ahead of the Day of Silence , which starts at 6am the next morning. During this period, after the Ogoh-Ogoh and before the Day of Silence, secret, mysterious ceremonies take place in hidden temples. I know because four years ago, in the pandemic, I was here with our guy Bondhan and his wife Debbie, staying in the same hotel. This was the pandemic, the Ogoh-Ogoh parade had been cancelled - but we heard something was happening in the heart of the monkey forest. So despite restrictions we clambered over a fence and in pitch black sneaked into the Monkey Forest, we could hear gambalan music and chanting and drums..right in the heart of the forest is an ancient temple, weird things were going on there we sneaked as close up as we could.. boy it was scary.. if we got caught I don't know what would have happened. I remember seeing a fire, leaping shadows, incense smoke, and strange dressed priests ringing bells.. I joked it looked like a human sacrifice was happening.. Then a security guy spotted us or heard something and came to see, and we scarpered back to the fence, hearts pounding and escaped. Anyway, this year, after the parade excitement, I'm back in the hotel. So from 6am on Saturday until 6am Sunday, there is no internet, access to outside is not allowed, I can walk around the hotel grounds, and that's all, they tell me if I talk to any other guests, it should be in a low voice. But I only see a couple of people by the pool reading books. No one talks. One day alone, in total silence - overlooking the Monkey Forest. Actually, it was amazing, I was kind of sad when it was over, but I went for breakfast in a local cafe and several local people I met on the walk there remembered me from the time in the pandemic. So nice in Ubud. Thanks for your help! I have to say thank you to everyone that filled in the questionnaire so far.. So many useful suggestions and insights. I'm studying everyday, you still have time to have your say. Link here. Upheavals .. If you don't have enough drama in the world with devastating earthquakes and volcanic activities. Now the Trump tariffs are shaking the world financial systems, who knows what the fallout will be and how it could affect us. Big News! And now we have a major product launch.. We finally got the Zodiac Bath Fizzers from the team at AW-Aromatics. Next level awesome. Wishing you a wonderful weekend. More news and an update from Nepal next week. Take care

title: David's AW News: Let's make 2026 a GREAT Year.. together.
content_html:
Greetings from Sunny Spain


Happy New Year!
Hope that Storm Goretti is not causing you too much disruption. 

This is my first official Friday newsletter of 2026.
 This time of year is all about making plans.. looking forward and getting in a positive frame of mind.
Yes 2026 will be amazing.. we are already off to a great start with a swathe of new products landing already and more to come.
It's all happening this year.

In Spain, Toni and his team are in the midst of moving our warehouse.. Here's Toni pretending not to be stressed..


The racking is being assembled and repositioned today.. and some stock already being moved..

So a big welcome to 2026 at AW.

A new year always feels a little bit like  a fresh notebook. Clean pages. Big possibilities. And thinking Yeah!, “This could be a good one.”

At Ancient Wisdom, we’re choosing to believe exactly that. We have made a bold plan for 2026.. hope you are coming for the ride!!

This year already starts with some lively momentum.
Our new, larger warehouse in Spain is coming together — giving us more space, better flow, and better service for our customers across Southern Europe.  We will shortly expand our incense range in Spain.. the new warehouse will have a larger Tea packing / mixing area. The warehouse is bigger, but the offices are super spacious.. offering lots of possibilities for expansion..  hope you are coming for the ride!!

See before and after AI inspired .. (in process) of our new Spain warehouse. 

At at the same time, an Indian container has just landed in the UK, full of colour, craftsmanship, and the kind of products that remind us why we love what we do. An Indonesian container is due any day.

Behind the scenes, we’re also investing heavily in something less visible but hugely important — our Bali development and digital marketing team. Brilliant people, building better systems, smarter tools, smoother connections… all so doing business with AW becomes easier, faster, and more profitable for you.

And this is just the beginning. You will see all our websites dramatically upgraded over the next few weeks.. AW-Dropship.com in the UK is already using a new backend system that is already opening more possibilities for our customers.. With MUCH MORE.. to come. 

Coco came from China to Spain..

She has not stopped working whilst she is here.. constantly on the phone or WeChat with suppliers.. and remotely monitoring container loading in our China warehouse in the early hours here. 

And we have a new "Can You Sell this? From Holly, taking a deep dive into Greenman Ritual Bath Salts & Soaps..

These are new Bath Salts - Epsom Salts based and going to be great in 2026.. 

Check out the Video here..

Travel Plans 2026.. 

 Follow me on my travels this spring as I move between the UK, Nepal, India, Indonesia and China — not as a tourist, but as a product hunter with a notebook full of ideas and our 2026 wish-list in my pocket. I’ll be sharing real stories from workshops, villages, factories and markets, meeting the real people behind the products, spotting trends before they arrive in Europe, and quietly shaping the next generation of Ancient Wisdom ranges. I'm planning to make some more Travel Style YouTube videos.. (please follow me) If you enjoy discovering what’s coming before it becomes mainstream — and like seeing how craft, culture and commerce connect — then I’d love you to come along for the ride.   Any suggestions or ideas are gratefully received.. 

Anyway wishing you all the best for 2026.

So this is my gentle nudge to you:

Be curious.
Be bold.
Test something new.
Back yourself a little more this year.

We’ll keep doing what we’ve always tried to do — source honestly, price fairly, innovate quietly, and support you as best we can along the way.

Thank you for choosing to trade with Ancient Wisdom.
Thank you for trusting us.
And thank you for being part of our story.

Let’s make 2026 a year we’re proud to remember.

Warm wishes,
David

Founder — Ancient Wisdom

title: Dancing in the Dark and other Happy Cats
content_html:
Greetings from China.. where the temperature is really racking up into the mid forties. In the day it is getting too hot to work and it's not unusual to see people asleep in any shade they can find.
The late the other night I took a short cut across a local park and was amazed to find it packed, about five hundred elderly ladies were doing formation disco dancing almost in the dark, families were playing badminton by torch light. In the gloom I could make out all sorts of activities, painting clubs for kids, tia chi by moonlight. Most bizarre to my eyes, but when you consider the asian fear of sunlight and the shear heat of the day, only at night can you go out to play.

Meanwhile back in England the temperature in AW offices and warehouse is also rising, but is less to do with the weather as the volume of stock starting to roll in ahead of the forth coming (dare I mention) Christmas season. On a recent container from China we shipped some of those Money Cats. You will have seen them in Chinese restaurants, they wave at you.. and according to Chinese feng shui they attract money. Since so many businesses employee the waving cats maybe there is something in it.. It's a big business in this town several large factories do nothing but make these cats. I was there selecting which models to buy and I noticed that one of the cats had a big smile on it's face. Why is that one with his eyes closed smiling? I asked the boss. "Ha.." he said, "That one is not a money cat, no good to make you rich.. this one make you happy".  You see you need to keep your eyes open to spot the money, but you can always close your eyes and be happy.
Can you see the smiling one?

I'm thinking of having the happy cat in our reception.. maybe it will bring more happy customers.

_________________________________________________________________________________

title: The Last Artisan?
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

I'm writing this from our beautiful beach office in Keterwali, Bali. Our young very dedicated team is beavering away to make sure AW websites are more visible to the world.  There are teams working on SEO, PPC, SM and PD. Yes I know. I have spent time this week bonding with these super bright young people, full of ideas and enthusiasm. So nice to work with them and they are all falling in love with AW.  I'd like to say they are my new favorite team... haha but I'd get in so much trouble....



To be honest I'm really happy working on new products like an incense burner or a beautiful carved Buddha. But in today's cut throat online world you have to work hard to stay ahead of the competition. And these young guys can really help.

But I have a big rather different problem to fix...It's the artisans.. they are in short supply.. so making products is getting a little difficult here.. I'll explain more below.
Last week I was telling you about wizards and that pool boy.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Usually when I arrive in Bali, Ringo will give me a little list of issues that he cannot fix.. usually excessive price rises making a product uncompetitive. But this time the list is long, not just price rises but problems in supply. We have slow supply issues with even some of our oldest and best suppliers. Something is going wrong. So I went to investigate..
The area above Ubud running upto the foothills of Mount Agung is full of small villages each specialising in particular crafts. One of my favorite things is to buzz around those villages with Ringo finding artisans and contracting them to make products for AW. These guys don't have websites, many don't even have a business card. Family businesses that in many cases are generational, with skills passed down from father to son. Often they are rice farmers tending the rice terrace.. but that job is intermittent, so they use farming downtime to make crafts. Crafts that find their way to good gift shops around the world.


I snapped this view of Mount Agung from right next door to one of our suppliers' places.


A workshop with normally about twenty people sat crossed legged on the floor carving albasia wood items.
The boss told us that normally he has ten guys just making the carved sitting Buddha.  But today he just had one.


This carved Buddha product is made by this guy..


The Last Artisan?
The route of the problem is that Bali is booming with record numbers of tourists arriving. The hotels and restaurants are offering higher wages to attract staff, so many have left the villages to work in the resort areas. Added to this problem is that local gift shop owners turn up with cash in hand and buy finished products which the artisans think they can replace later. Thus orders get delayed. 
What's the solution? The other day I spent time with Ringo visiting five different suppliers with basically the same problem. I argued that during the pandemic we had been there for them and placed orders when no other buyers came. But that didn't work.. Of course everyone is really sorry for the delays but what can they do? 

In the end, the solution is (as always) a combination of things. 1. Pay more to attract artisans back, and they are more happy in the village. 2. Offshore some production to other parts of Indonesia. 3.. Cancel the products that just cannot be made now and focus on the ones that can. 

Despite all the problems, as Ringo pointed out to me we still load a container every week or so. Shipping more artisan products to Europe than ever before. 
I think eventually the market will fix itself. Lots of folk from other parts of Indonesia are coming to Bali for work. Even in our warehouse we have people from Sumba, Java and Flores. Our digital marketing team hail from all parts of Indonesia. Hopefully artisans will find their way back to work and be better paid.

Back in the UK.. we have FREE shipping (UK mainland) all August. Plus lots of other deals and new products. It's all go..
From our Aromatics team new products are coming... (with lots in the pipeline) - the bath bomb kits are getting a great response and selling well. See below.
Also we have a new product that is, I promise you going to literally BLOW YOUR MIND... yes.. Smelling Salts with a modern twist.  And with aromatic benefits to take this ancient product to the next level. 
While I was in Istanbul recently in the tea and herbal shops.. they all sell smelling salts. The old fashioned type (and quite expensive), as you are paying for your herbal tea they offer you a smell, which of course makes you jump in surprise and causes much laughter.. I don't know what percentage of customers buy a bottle of smelling salts but I guess it's quite high. 

I'm planning my next trip to India with our man in India; Mr Chatterjee.. I will go and visit the new factory in Serampore, near Kolkata. The last time I was there was just before the pandemic, so I'm looking forward to catching up with the team there.. but first lots of jobs to get done here.

Have a wonderful weekend. 
Take care.. as they say here Hati Hati. 

David

title: Ancient Wisdom is Reborn!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Where the holy week is set to begin, I have been to Malaga city a few times recently and the Holy week excitement is building. There is a BIG question in the air. And the Question is this: Is the City's favourite son coming home for Easter? he often does.. and will he, has is his custom take part in the majestic and solemn Holy Week processions. Speculation here. I'm talking of course about Antonio Banderas - the famous actor and major investor in this part of Spain. All those guys looking like the Ku Klux Klan with the peaked white capes look scary to me.. even if one of them is actually our Antonio. Scary.


Last week I was rambling on about how some people: "Bring more to the table" and others.. a small percentage of people.. take from the table, and how this, in the end, destroys relationships. You can read about it here.
It's Easter!  So lots of Easter wishes to all our customers, past future and present - especially those who keep up with this newsletter :)

Easter, of course, is a time for Bunnies & Chocolate (yay!).. sorry scrub that.. I should say (serious face, deep voice).. it's a time for Reflection and Renewal..
It's about .. you could say.. bringing more to the table.. giving more than you take.. our big example of this at Easter is Jesus who we learn laid down his life for his friends.. (and all mankind we are told) the very definition of love.
Anyway it's globally culturally accepted that this is a good thing..  all world religions have it that it is better to give than receive and those that do will prosper.. somehow this is ingrained ancient wisdom (see what I did there) in all humans worldwide. Instinctively we know this, evolutionary biologists think it is even hard-wired into our DNA.  Of course, there are a few (is this what they call a psychopath?) who can't help but take advantage of this element of human nature... Judas in the Easter story..

The buzz this week at Ancient Wisdom.. is that the Company.. AW has been Reborn!!
Apt at Easter no?
Why?  Well the old website with the angel and horse.. has died, is no more, has gone to the server in the sky.


Goodbye, rest in peace.

Long live Ancient Wisdom.. a NEW website is born.. 
After almost two years of hard work and development, (mostly by Raul our IT wizard in KL) we have finally taken the plunge and switched to a new mobile-friendly, customer friendly - all new version of AW.
We have actually been gradually changing all the sites starting with our Polish version, then Italian etc.. and the response has been generally good if not great.. and we keep learning as we move forward.
Changing the Big Daddy site (the UK one) was always going to be nerve racking - lots of things could go wrong.. but on Monday in the dead of night.. we did it..  since then we have been fixing things like crazy that don't look right..
Please check out the new look site: AncientWisdom.biz   - all feedback greatly appreciated. 

I know a lot of you in the gift trade will be working your socks off this Easter.. but I hope you get time to spend with your friends and family. 
Wishing you a muchochocalato Easter.. with fun, laughter and love.

Take care.

title: David's AW News: Dad's Day & Dropship Update
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Happy Father's Day Weekend!

Hi guys, hope you are doing well.
Yes I'm back in Europe after 6 months of travelling. At my home in La Cala de Mijas. 

It's kind of strange because it doesn't seem that long ago I was here and also so much has happened it simultaneously seems like years. 

Last week I was telling you about our updates that are coming from the IT development in Bali and my thoughts on AI.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

I took a Turkish Airways flight from Bali to Istanbul business class, but already culture shock with grumpy staff who snatched my ticket, no eye contact, no real human interaction. 

Even on the most budget Indian or Indonesia Airlines nothing but friendly gracious contact. But the food is nice and they give you a romantic (fake) candle when you are served food. Then a short change over in Istanbul to Malaga Spain.. 4 hours later in the airport we landed with an almighty crash. I feel the landing gear must be damaged..but the captain never mentioned anything, just welcome to Spain etc..

 Malaga airport.. wow so busy.. and the non EU queue for passport control was horrendous. Backing up beyond the arrivals hall into the terminals.. with announcements saying please respect the staff, and we are working hard to resolve the delay. Fortunately (for me) .. I have a Spanish ID and skipped the line, only about four people in front of me. And super efficient Malaga airport had my luggage on the belt before I got there.. so was out of the airport PDQ.  
This is terrible and hits home.
This morning Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) messaged me about the Air India crash.. Before the news broke on the BBC. Oh my God.. that's a shock and so depressing. An Air India flight from India to the UK crashed just after take off. In the last year I had three dreadful flights with Air India in a row.. cancelled, massively delayed, or bumped off the flight to the next one.. and useless communication. please be patient.. lots coming soon.

Lots of peace and love, and happy trading.

David

title: Pink Rabbits & Thumb Prints
content_html:
Greetings from the AW warehouse in Bali.

 

In the village of Ketewel, east of Denpasar and not far from Sukawati you will find the warehouse of Ancient Wisdom.

Named the Frangipani Depot, every day a steady stream of artisans arrive with small trucks loaded with handicraft products.

It's my Happy Place..

 

Last week I was in Malaga at our office there telling you about some game-changing ideas.. It was my birthday (on Friday 13th) and if you missed the fun you can catch up here.

Since then I have traveled via Istanbul on Turkish airlines to Kulala Lumpa to visit our IT wizard Raul (who lives there) to work on our plans for one of those Game Changing ideas.. and from there I took a short flight on AirAsia to Denpasar Bali.


The flights went smoothly, until I arrived in Denpasar - it was late at night and since now is low season so I'd expected to drift through immigration without too much delay and meet Ringo outside pretty quickly. But I arrived to see the arrival hall stuffed full of thousands of people waiting to buy visa on arrival tickets and then queueing again for passport control. I soon realised that the majority of the people were young Russians. There are rumours swirling of a general mobilization and the borders closing. It feels like anyone with a little money is running away... and Bali is a favored escape with established Russian communities.

I have a business visa so I skipped the first queue, but it still took more than two hours to get out of the airport. 

 

It was 3am by the time I got to bed.. but Ringo had arranged an important meeting the next day so no rest.. We had a meeting in Ubud with our lawyer Cory and assistant, a Notary from Denpasar, Ringo, Bondan and myself.

We have been going through the process of setting up a PT/PMA a foreign owned Indonesian Company. This will allow us to do many more things in Indonesia including advertising for staff, employing more people and owning property. 




Job done!

There is a digital nomad hotel and co-working space that belongs to a friend of mine, so we met there. (It's called The Onion) I signed lots of papers, Ringo signed them as our local director,  Cory our lawyer signed them.. then when everything had been signed, the Notary gentleman - explained everything and he stamped and signed everything.

Then apparently it is only legal with the application of my big English thumb prints. I duly inked my thumbs and plonked them on the legalising paper.




The beginning of another adventure at AW.. in a few days Tomas (marketing wizard) and Raul (IT wizard) will arrive and we will progress this big idea.. you will understand more later.. but as an AW customer we hope to give you a game changing advantage.. 

 

Meanwhile it is almost a New Year.. the year of the Tiger is passing and an altogether more fluffy year of the Rabbit is beginning.. 

In Kuala Lumpur the shopping malls were decked out with pink rabbits.. 


Let's hope the year of the Rabbit is cuter and cuddly and less trouble than the last one.

Coco tells me this year is unusual, because it falls so early.. and the official holiday season has to be extended to end in February. Which for some complicated reason I can't quite understand means that there are two Februarys in China this year. This apparently is very unlucky.. let's hope not.

 

All the best from Bali..

More news next week.

 

David

title: David's AW News: Back to Bali / Top Picks
content_html:
Greetings from the AW warehouse in Ketewel, Bali

Our pet love birds.. remind me of something beginning with "V". See below for my personal top picks.

I just arrived. On Wednesday  I took Turkish airways from Malaga to Istanbul arriving at 7pm then at 2am (Thursday)  took a 12 hour night flight to Denpasar, Bali. Arriving because of the time difference 7pm Thursday evening.. Ringo and Bondhan were waiting as usual at the arrivals and escorted me to the villa - on the way giving me a full debrief on what's been happening. I slept immediately..  because I didn't sleep much on the flight, it was full of families with excited small children running about. Then wake up excited to get to work.. but first things first.
Last week I was telling you my very positive plans on thinking big in 2025 without asking Mr AI.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

But first things first in Bali.. before work it's time for breakfast. And Ringo likes to prepare a real Indonesian traditional breakfast.
This is Nasi Goreng.. Chicken Fried Rice with an egg on top, served with a spicy sambal sauce, two mini kebabs, salad and decorated with prawn crackers. Then ice cold fresh watermelon juice and a very strong black sweet Bali Coffee.. which I can tell you absolutely sets you up for the day. I love it! 

Then down to work. Checking the schedule of containers to be loaded. See how they are getting on with packing delivered products. Here in Bali the artisans don't do packing. We take deliveries of "finished products" off the back of trucks or in big bamboo baskets. The quality control, barcoding, wrapping and packing in boxes and cartons ready for export is all done in our warehouse. The empty container turns up and all the packing staff become container packers loading the container, usually in the evening because cooler to work. 

Indo Update.
Ringo and his team do a vast amount of organising to make it happen. Then our office team do lots of export document preparations and admin stuff to enable the export to even happen. 
Check out our Indonesian imports page. As the Homeware - Spring Clean - lets make the house a home - season is upon us.. the natural and beautiful products of Indonesia are perfect. Historically Indonesian products have been most popular in two European countries, but I can see from our sales stats that's changing fast. (see below for the countries).

Valentines is only weeks away.. My Top Picks.
We have so much! AW is definitely your Valentines Supplier of Choice. Not just from Indonesia, we have heaps of fast selling beautiful products perfect this year for Valentines Day.
My picks include.. old favourites (but selling like crazy): Soap Flowers. We also have new Zodiac Candles -  the perfect gift (they include a gemstone bracelet). Hop Hare Candles (especial "The Lovers") and Gemstone Friendship bracelets - great value - two matching bracelets one for your valentine one for you. When visitors see this in our showroom always a good reaction.
For a totally unique Valentines Gift - how about Artisan Ukuleles. Trending now.. buy one as a gift and learn to play.. "Love Love me Do" - it's easy. This product is so easy to sell if you can demo it.
Check our Valentines Page.. but almost everything at AW is a potential "V" gift. Don't forget to make pick-up gift pouches..

New Stock this week.
There is so much.. containers from Indonesia and China just arrived. Rodrigo and the team are working hard to add the new stuff.  

New Year January Sales is also in full swing.. where you could grab some lines for Valentines also.

Anyway I'm sure you are busy.
Wishing you all the best.. more news from Indonesia next week.

Take care.
David

PS
FYI .. Holland and Germany were traditionally the best countries for Indonesian imports. But recently Spain and UK have seen a boom.

title: David's AW News: A personal message for 2025
content_html:
Greetings and a Very Happy New Year from a bright sunny Spain.


All the other wholesalers are sending you bright and breezy new year messages... but at AW let's just for a second face reality.

Well here we are, it's 2025. Is that really already a quarter of the way through this century? 

You know it seems the world is full of problems, bad news and depressing things seem to surround us. Who the heck knows what the year ahead will bring?

For sure though we are all going to face business challenges in the UK especially as the increase in National insurance and ever increasing costs bite.  Pesky companies like Temu and Shein continue to steal trade from under our noses. Compliance and regulations complicate and cause unnecessary drag.. 

Sometimes in Business it just seems like hard work. 

Sorry to depress you. 

Friends, one thing is true and remains true. If you don't face the future with Bright Optimism and Positive thinking then you have already failed.  

So thinking positive.. Here are my.. 5 Ways to Think Big in 2025! - and have fun doing it..

1. I know what every retailer needs.. that's fast selling products with VERY GOOD profit margins. Products you and your customers love.

Our New Year's Resolution at AW is to deliver more of these types of products. 

We had a huge (and continued) success when we brought you the popular Sataya Brand of Incense 28% off (with Gold Reward) meaning you can buy Incense for 32p you can sell at £1.50  (or 5 packs for £5) - I know you need lines like this to survive. You can actually find many retailing opportunities at AW..  And this year we PROMISE to deliver more like this.

Artisan and Esoteric products from India, Nepal and Indonesia. Not tatt made in China but beautiful products carefully and ethically sourced. 

Sidestep them further by selling Made in UK high quality aromatics. Essential Oils for example are trending big time once again. If you don't sell AW Essential oils then you are really missing out. (nobody will seriously trust Essential Oils from Temu) Kick off this year with our Starter Pack of top selling Essential OIls. And this year we PROMISE to bring you more beautiful Artisan products.

3. BE A GOLD REWARD CUSTOMER.. it's easy and a great way to boost your bottom line. It's how we look after and reward our regular customers. You can see on our website that most products have discounts for quantity.. when you are a Gold Reward customer you get those discounts ANYWAY.. upto 28% OFF.. How to get a Gold Reward.. easy just order within 30 days of your last order.. be regular - look after your stock and customers will keep coming and your margin will be higher. And this year we PROMISE to deliver more BIGGER Gold Reward Discounts.

4.  Check out our NEW YEAR SALE.. Yes, why not grab some stock for your sale items - or boost your magins - Lots of stock up to 50% Off..

Now.. hold on to your hats.. the BIG ONE is dropping right now.... because dear fellow giftware traders.. For the next ten days we are having a massive.....

===================================================================================================================================================

5. GOLD REWARD AMNESTY.  It means order now and whether you are a member or not, you are getting MAXIMISED discounts upto 28% off. So now is the perfect time to stock up and grab those discounts.. PLUS we are adding some crazy DOUBLE DISCOUNT DEALS..  including off Essential Oils.. and fast selling Soap Flowers. Perfect for Valentine's Day and Mother's Day.

The thing is - Think Positive - kick of 2025 with your refreshed Gold Reward membership.. you can top up with small orders and get those discounts.. and keep your membership. But early Feb when you stock up for Valentine's Day you can take advantage again..

So guys that's the big news.. start the year with our Amnesty..

Thank you again for your support, it's an honour to be in the gift trade, and an honour to work with retailers like you. If you are a regular reader of this newsletter, you will know how hard we work to bring you the best in giftware.. soon I will be travelling and you are invited to follow my stories in 2025.  I always appreciate your ideas and feedback.  

Thank you for trusting us in 2024 - let's together make 2025 awesome!

Take care - much love

David and all at AW.

title: David's AW News: Happy New Year - it's 2082
content_html:
Greetings from Delhi, India


Happy Easter, hope there are lots of fluffy things and chocolate coming your way!

Meanwhile it's been Happy New Year in Nepal.. we were fortunate enough to be here on the Nepalese new year. It's the year 2082 which seems a bit surreal. All the restaurants and bars in Kathmandu were throwing new year parties, it was very jolly - Toni (our man in Spanish) who is always up for a party, had the full experience.. I was in bed by 10, because well, just too busy.. too much to do. The tradition is to decorate everywhere with balloons.. It does seem rather strange to see Happy New Year 2082 everywhere.


Toni and I took an Indigo flight from Kathmandu to Delhi on Tuesday morning. We got through Kathmandu airport (the world's most bureaucratic airport) in good humour. All the ridiculous security checks, and stamps you need to get, my half bottle of Whiskey was taken off me by the pre-security check before the check in desks. A jolly security guy was so happy to find it, I didn't want the hassle of an argument (because I know it's not their task to catch whisky), so for good Karma I just handed it to him and said Happy New Year!.and slapped him on the back, he waddled his head and gave me a toothy grin and the bottle disappeared into his backpack under the desk in mili-second. 
Big queue for check in, big queue to get a stamp before the immigration, surprisingly fast, then security with all sorts of odd requests and stamps. Then before boarding the plane yet another security check, male and female segregated in a kind of portable box actually on the steps of the aircraft.  Crazy.

We arrived in Delhi and Drishanta, Mr Chatterjee's son, was waiting for us with a nice comfortable car to ease the stress of Delhi traffic. We are now at the Delhi Fair for a few days catching up with our old suppliers that exhibit here. Soooo busy, I can barely walk a few yards without a supplier or old contact shaking my hand and pulling me towards his stand. I'll update you next week.

Mad Honey
This mad honey thing is crazy, since it was on the Joe Rogan podcast.. this honey from Nepal made with the world's biggest bees in super remote mountain locations.  It's supposed to give you weird dreams and even hallucinations.. and it's (for now) legal.  I don't want to try.. but I have been having fun persuading Toni to try.. check it..

Surprising visit to the Felt Factory


Then while we were in Kathmandu - one day we went to see one of the felt factories we deal with.. as it happens some of their products have just arrived in the UK.. see below.
We managed to make a YouTube video about the visit.. This is only my third (or maybe forth) at making a proper YouTube publication.. Check it out, subscribe and I'd really appreciate any feedback and comments. You know I really didn't want to do this, I'm very shy.. but actually I'm beginning to enjoy the process..


You can watch the video here: Check it out, subscribe and I'd really appreciate any feedback and comments

Wedding in Kathmandu
On New Year's Day.. in Kathmandu. That was Monday, we were honoured to be invited to the wedding of one of our suppliers' daughters. It was totally different to a British wedding, but somehow the same.. Groom sporting rock and roll beard and sunglasses, happy bride, stressed parents, old ladies loving it, guys acting cool,naughty kids, broad smiles. The priest had a sweater with "Magic Happens" on it. This wedding was due to carry on for three days, we dropped in for about three hours and witnessed a stream of traditional ceremonial things going on..




Here we are with the bride.. 

Meanwhile in the UK.. lots of things back in stock.. including a rare supply of Dinner Candles.. there is a massive shortage, grab them while you can.. 
Anyway, have a lovely Easter break!
.
Take care.

content_html:
Greetings from AW-Aromatics. Sheffield.


It's warming up nicely in the UK.. both the weather and the creative juices. It's all go at AW.

Let's get this PARTY Started!

We got the best range, and certainly the best quality / value bags range. This week you can really BAG a BAG bargain..  

Father's Day is coming.. and we have I believe we have some of the best gifts going.. check out Father Day Products here.. 

In Spain.. they like to party.. and here in the UK the teams also (they tell me) like to mingle, so this afternoon Tomas and the team at Ancient Wisdom are hosting an afterwork BBQ and garden party.
So I'm off to Mingle with my favorite UK teams! We have to get the Party Started..


Hope you have a lovely weekend. Enjoy the warm weather and I hope you get to party a little too.
Take care.

More news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Bali Baby Home
content_html:
Greetings from Bali Indonesia

This week James (operations wizard) arrived from the UK. His first business trip to Asia. Also the other day Raul (the IT wizard) came from his home in KL to take care of the AW-Advantage team.
James looks after AW-Fulfilment.co.uk  (before that he was AW warehouse manager). He is keen to work with Raul to develop more functionality for our fulfilment customers and get more efficient use of our warehouse spaces across AW. He started by helping our man Ringo here in Bali reorganise the warehouse here.
Last week I was telling you about arriving in Bali, and discovering we are in the Rainy Season but without Rain.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Well it was my birthday last Saturday. A day I was hoping to let it pass without much fuss. But in Bali that's not allowed. It started early morning I'm just about to take a shower.. and the villa door bell is ringing. I'm thinking's maybe it's the pool guy or the gardener. I pull on a t-shirt and pants to let him in.. I open the door and all the staff are standing there with a birthday cake singing happy birthday.. 
They are old friends actually, in the early part of the pandemic from March 2020 I was stuck here with them all for few months. Well the day continued the same, flowers and cakes and birthday wishes, from all the staff at our warehouse, from the staff at the beach office from several suppliers. It was a full days programme organised out of my hands. 



With the AW-Advantage team and the Warehouse team.. can you spot James?

On the morning of my birthday Debbie our office manager thought it would be a good idea to visit a local charity and offer support. She knows that at AW we do this kind of thing.. 
I came across this picture from 2008.. it's the Indian children's home we took under our wing.. this is from the day we found them.

All they were asking was help to fix the roof.
This is them at Christmas time now..


So we went to visit an abandoned babies home, not far from our warehouse.  It's called Bali Baby Home.
Sometimes unwanted babies are abandoned, sometimes the mother and child are abandoned.. it's terrible but the founder of this charity established a home to look after babies and then works to persuade the families to reunite with the baby. He travels all over Indonesia, collecting abandoned children and then works tirelessly to get them back home. 
They requested baby formular and nappies, so we went and bought a car load and took it there. The founder wasn't there (he was on a mission to reunite a family in Java), but his very enthusiastic young staff gave us a tour and told us the heart breaking stories behind each little person there. 


At any time they have twenty or so abandoned babies and some mothers who help out  along with volunteers to care for the babies. So much love and broad smiles, these little kids are desperate to love and be loved and the wonderful people here it seems to me doing a vitally important life saving job. It was hard not spend the morning in tears. 

The remainder of the day I felt a feeling of devastation, quite upsetting that these young life's can start like this.
Anyway it is not far from our warehouse and we will visit again and see how we can practically help. I hope  you feel like you can support this cause also.

Last week I was telling you about making contracts with artisans to give them a more secure income. This week we signed contracts for Hati Hati Angels, and a Molten Glass Bowl guy. The Hati Hati angels are out of stock more than they are in.. I'm hoping that we can change this. We also placed an order for the coloured glass bowls I was telling you about.

Coming soon..

Meanwhile back in the UK.. it's very very cold and large parts of the country are snowed under.. 
I hope you can stay safe and warm, and that the weather is not too disruptive to your business. 
Lots of new products and back in stock items.. 

Take care
More news from Bali next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Dreams do come true.
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia

Hope you guys are doing well and the Spring trading season is blooming for you.
I'm here in Bali with Tomas (products & marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard from KL) and Peter (SEO wizard from Slovakia). 
So we have been working with our enthusiastic digital marketing team in our famous Bali beach office.
Last week I was telling you about being zapped all ways by electrical storms.. if you missed it you can catch up here. 

As you drive along the coastal road from Padang Bay towards Denpasar close to the village of Ketewel you might just spot a strange sign on the side of the road. No name. No advertisement, no nothing.. just a symbol.  The AW symbol, you might recognise it, but only because people, like you who know AW know this.
Turn left at that odd sign. Trundle down a rough track past fragrant water meadows and an old abandoned hotel you come to a rarely used almost secret beach. A stone plinth with a rock circle on top marks a holy spot for the local temple. You can see a single rustic beach bar frequented by a few hard core Japanese surfer dudes. But walk a little just beyond the shack and you will spy an office packed full of earnest young folk studious bent over laptops.. 
It's the home of AW-Advantage  and just a year ago was only a dream.. but this week was our 1st anniversary. 

So after work, and after dark (so the muslim folk could join us to eat) we drove to Turtle Island. Actually it's no longer an island as reclaimed land has enabled a bridge to this newly developing corner of Bali. It seems like all the businesses here are little independent fish restaurants and all the customers are local Balanese.. It's good fresh food and very cheap.. Debbie, our highly organised office manager organised everything. And called on me to do a speech.. nobody warned me.. haha so I had to wing it.. the best way because then the words come straight unfiltered from the heart.. I told them 18 months ago this project was just an idea, a dream. And even though this company is still a baby, only one year old today.. It is a dream come true. You guys, I told them, are my Dream Team.. come true. 
The mandatory group photo notice one finger signifying one year.. Dream Team!

Anyway.. as much as we love the Dream Team.. there is also another thing that we love (a little bit) more in Indonesia.. and that's finding the Dream Products. At AW we love the products! Here in Indonesia it is giftware heaven. .. 
But there are many challenges, nothing that can't be overcome but our team here has heaps more to do than in the old days. Compliance paperwork to make exports is a full time job, and new rules and tests and complications land everyday. 
Our lady Made does a valiant job.  

Also other issues like we just don't get the stock as quickly as we used to. There are less artisans available and this impacts supply chains. We have been countering this by finding multiple suppliers for the same products, giving long term contracts so artisans can feel more secure and making more professional binding contracts. I discovered they like a contract here.

The warehouse is busy busy busy... trying their best to dispatch more containers. Ringo is taking many people on from the island of Sumba, young people coming to Bali to find work. It's all go!
Our guard dog Apim has also been busy.. and the AW team has two brand new members in the security department.. 
 Very cute!

Meanwhile in the Uk.. it seems to be getting busy. Lots of best selling items are back in stock.
And the new Crystal Elementary Soaps are creating a massive buzz.. Shower Steamers are really trending now - I noticed a few big orders coming (not sure why)..  and the new Chakra Bath Fizzers Sets are.. well just next level!
It seems like anything Chakra is Next Level right now.. see our Chakra Inspirations page for ideas..
Oh and did I mention the (rather generous) Spring Gift Give Away we have going on right now..

Details below.

So have a wonderful weekend. Dream big! 
Because if you don't have a Dream.. how you gonna have a Dream come true..
More updates next week. 

Take care..

David

title: Happier and Happier - see why?
content_html:
Greetings from Sukawati Bali.

Last week (it was Valentines day) and I was telling you about my arrival here in Bali and the slightly odd journey from Kuala Lumpa. You can read about it here.
You can also discover the main reason I was in KL below..

It's been a really hectic week, every morning meeting Ringo (our man in Bali) for breakfast then heading out to meet various suppliers deal with issues and seek out new stock.
In the day it's stinking hot, and working in the heat drains energy, in the evening there are tropical storms, so a bit trapped in my hotel.. don't worry I'm really happy to be here - it's one of my favourite places whatever the weather.
In Bali (like India) there is always some festival kicking off, this week it is Galungan - a celebration of the gods coming to earth to fight - and beat - the evil king (some say the devil. So it is a celebration of good over evil. 

The streets are lined with penjors - highly decorated bent over or bowing bamboo poles. Homes, businesses, temples all have to have at least one. And richer people can show off with more elaborate ones. Everyone is dressed in their sacred best, and the ladies looking particularly smart also balance offerings on the heads as they process to the gatherings. Everyone is so happy and seem to be having enormous fun.
It's caused us some disruption because many of our suppliers close for the ceremonies but Ringo calls ahead and suppliers are happy to meet us anyway. It's been interesting and an honour to be in the midst of family ceremonies.


The other big news is that AW in Bali have adopted a dog.. or I think the dog has actually adopted us. Ringo told me that a Japanese family sold up and moved out of a big villa. They had a number of dogs and dumped them one morning all along Jackfruit village where we have our warehouse. 
One of them just settled in our warehouse yard like he'd been there forever.. As soon as we laid eyes on each other, I could tell he sensed I was the big boss, I stroked him and looked happy, he looked ecstatic and spend a good deal of time licking my toes..haha. So  I named him Happier  - after the song, because he is always super happy. 


He seems so happy to just live in the yard, sleeps by the plants, is house trained and is so happy to greet us every morning when we arrive, we open the gates and there he is wagging that tail so much his whole body wags. Even better a local stray dogs charity call every morning with dog food. I told Ringo to tell them we would look after the food from here on in..  because we always happy to help :)

Meanwhile back in the UK, storm Denis has been lashing the country, but has not dampened the excitement over new stock arrivals. See below.. we are preparing for the summer already.. 
The other big news.. and this is HUGE, and I'm very Happy! And we hope your are even Happier!!- Finally after huge amount of effort by Raul and his team (in KL) the new AW Drop-shipping Site is officially launched. It's still in Beta mode but it works :)


dropship.com  So Drop-shipping is finally GO :)

Next week I will be going to India, to Kolkata, will catch up with our agent in India - Mr Chatterjee and meeting Tomas there.. so anything could happen..

Hope you have an amazing weekend, stay safe..

David

title: Free Moon-cakes
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Today is a national holiday. It's Mid-autumn Festival. So nobody is working today. 
We live in an apartment on the 26th floor of building number 1 (of 12) in Oujing Village. Europe style Village is how it styles itself.

There is a swimming pool, tennis courts, gardens and lots of rather cheesy statues and fountains all surrounded by these huge 45 story buildings. It's closed community with it's own security, school and regular social events.
Mid-autumn festival is the biggest. I call it Moon-cake Day.. It’s time to grab the smudge sticks and crystal ball. It is Friday the 13th and also a full moon — the first full moon to fall on a Friday the 13th in 13 years. Spooked? Don’t be. According to some witches and astrologers, the number 13 is auspicious — we have 13 full moons and 13 menstrual cycles in a year. And Friday is associated with the goddess Venus. So a full moon that falls on Friday the 13th is a special, powerful time.  Calm down dear.. it's all going to be OK.

Drinking rice wine? No.. they are quite happy stood round the dinning room table packing a consignment of gemstone jewellery ready for the next container. I complain to Coco that she is making all her relatives work on a national holiday. What did he say? they ask.. Coco translates and they all fall about laughing.

Next week I fly to Spain, I have some jobs to do with the new warehouse and interviewing staff. So should be interesting.. then back to China with Tomas. It's all go.

Hope you survive Friday the 13th in one piece.. see you on the other side.
I'm going to have another moon-cake and find out what's for dinner.

Take care
David
