title: David's AW News: Trust Me Posters
content_html:
Greetings from Frangipani Warehouse in Bali

We called it the Frangipani warehouse because at the time we moved, the streets around were bedded with frangipani flowers, the pretty frangipani petals are used in offerings as hair decoration and can be processed into perfume. The same perfume that is made to make Nagchampa Incense in India. Now in Bali the Frangipani trees are in full bloom. But it is also the time of a full blown election and Indonesia will choose new national and local leaders soon. They get very enthusiastic about these things - there are wall to wall posters and flags across Bali, and I assume, all Indonesia. 
Last week I was telling you about the Bali Baby Home we went to visit and the arrival of our man James from the UK.. if you missed it you can catch up here.


Frangipani Warehouse.

James has been busy, working with Raul (IT developer) on improvements to the fulfillment software we use at AW-Fulfillment. Now Raul and his small team of developers are focused on this project. Then he is spending time with the AW warehouse team implementing new systems to the warehouse here. Big changes are happening.. including re-organising the warehouse here.  Now we have a goods-in racked out area, after goods have been QC'ed and packed they are booked to locations in racking from which they can be loaded on the next container leaving.. It's all getting much better organised. To get experience James (the other morning) even helped load a container destined for Slovakia. It's very hot and humid. It's a job that's not for the faint heart of heart.. after a four hour shift I think he was sweating..


So James is very busy but we still found time to go and visit some suppliers up in the hills and villages beyond Ubud where many of the artisan craft workers live. 


Artisans of Bali.

I'm fascinated and worried by democracy. In Indonesia it seems complicated but reasonably healthy.  Fresh lively debates, and as far as I can see the process hasn't been hacked by bad actors like in many (so called) democracies. In the way that Raul can hack a computer.. political operators hack the human brain.. using religion (India, Turkey), using fear of outsiders (UK, Hungary), changing constitutions and controlling the media to stay forever in power (Russia, China).  

Here.. every billboard, spare bit of land, side of houses has political posters.. not with campaign slogans or political arguments.. but with what I call "Trust Me Posters". The faces of innocent, competent and trustworthy (looking) people stare out at you. Silently saying " You can trust us to run our country fairly for the benefit of all".


The current super popular president is stepping down after the maximum two terms, his young son and an ex-general are running mates..  one popular hack on the human brain to instil trust is cuteness.. babys, puppies, cats and toys all employ an innocent cuteness to seduce the human brain to trust. 


So I was fascinated to see this cute version of the political "trust me" poster. See the two guys above in blue shirts.. The general and the president's son who is so young, the constitution was rewritten to allow his name on the ballot. You can trust us.. we are lovable cartoons. 

So anyway, on a slightly different note.... you can trust AW.. we are doing our best to bring you level, honest, straightforward deals. Products that simply sell well. Sourced fairly and carefully designed and researched to sell well. Don't need to trust me - check our reviews!

Smart independent traders use AW to build their business by pleasing customers consistently. All the (often) fake discounts, free shipping and other brain hacks that some wholesalers use to persuade you to order may not be as good a deal as it seems.  

And we have lots of perfect for Valentines Day and Easter and beyond Giftware.
A China container just arrived.. new products and important back in stocks.
Check out the deals below..

Next week I will be in India..
Toni arrives tonight from Spain.. and we will travel together to India.
The next stage of the adventure unfolds.

Take care, hope you have a lovely weekend.

David

title: Balance & Harmony
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I hope you are enjoying the summer, long nights, Wimbledon and drinking beer outdoors in a country pubs. It's almost mid July and I have seen the first evidence of customers ordering for (alert the "C" word is coming)... Christmas. Woops sorry I said it.. Well it's only two more weeks and it's August bank holiday weekend, and then the focus seriously turns to the upcoming festive season. In the gift trade you really are part of the circle of life. You need to be planning ahead.

This week I have been planning our main sourcing season, it's imperative we find and develop the next set of amazing products to delight your customers with. Tomas (marketing and development wizard) and I will be spending time in India, Indonesia and Nepal - oh and a quick trip to Morocco where. Later we will go to China, where it's always possible to make things happen.

Last week I was telling you about the three-fold harmony ceremony at our brand new warehouse in Indonesia, you can read about it here.. 

Since the ceremony at our new AW warehouse in Jackfruit Village, Ringo (our man in Indonesia) has been working hard. Not only have we shipped all the holding stock and packaging materials from our old warehouse, but loaded and shipped a 40ft container to UK, and by the time you read this probably another one to our Eastern Europe warehouse in Slovakia. He likes to send me pictures on a container day, starting before dawn with an empty container being delivered to our (new) loading bay, and ending after sunset with the container loaded, packing list made and the guy who comes to the necessary fumigation. 

Then the driver returns hooks up the container and trundles off to the port, a bit like your DPD parcel the container will go from depot to depot, in this case to Surabaya port, Java, then to Singapore, where it will transfer to a container ship that brings it to Europe.  



Ringo, early morning getting ready to load. Carefully using every square inch. Almost full and last picture see the fumigation tank. Next time we see this container will be in Sheffield in about six weeks.

So last week we learned a little about three-fold harmony.. and in the giftware business Balance and Harmony are important. This is why we work hard to bring you stock from India, Indonesia and Nepal as well as China. Of course, China is the easiest place to work in, all the infrastructure is there, big factories (you can scale up easy) and most giftware companies buy the bulk of items in China. We also buy in China and have a warehouse in Yiwu, but try to focus on smaller family businesses and try to avoid plastic tat and mass market stuff.

Last weekend Coco and I went to the city of Granada, we had tickets for the Alhambra - a truly Ancient Wisdom location. And of course, we made a full tour of the gift shops (of which there are many), being in the gift trade you recognise where stuff comes from. That's from India, that's from Bali, that's Chinese. The best shops, the busiest shops have a Balance and Harmony.. something local, in Granda - Indian products look good, plus lots from Indonesia and we even spotted our Nepal hemp bags on sale. The shops with all China stock lacked a sense of authenticity, although there are good things just a bit of that can really destroy a shops zen and harmony. We loved the shops in the South Area.. lots of shops with Leather Notebooks (from India).




Granada gift shops.. 

This is why (blowing-own-trumpet-moment) at AW we spend more time than your average gift wholesaler sourcing the harder to get items, making sure it is ethically traded and making sure the prices are right. 
What's in Ringo's latest container.. mostly Molten Glass Bowls some recycled wood furniture, coconut dragons (and old favorite) now specially boxed to prevent breakages and more.. 

Wish you a weekend of Balance & Harmony :)

More news next week..

Take care 

David

title: David's AW News: We found an Ancient Wisdom town in China
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia


Yes, back on the island of the Gods.
Well, after a couple of hectic weeks in China, Coco dropped us at Yiwu airport, said goodbye, and we took a China Southern flight to Guangzhou, where we transferred to a flight to Bali. It took like 16 hours, with transfer times, and somehow we arrived absolutely exhausted in Denpasar. But happy to be here, and it's Sandra's first time. It will be interesting to see Bali fresh through her eyes.
Since we just arrived, I'll give you updates later.
Last week, I was telling you about some Culture Shocks in China, and all about one factory visit. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Yiwu Update - strangely quiet.
Yiwu was great, our suppliers were happy to see us and full of new ideas. But it's not normal - the hotel that Tomas and Sandra stayed in, a nice 5 star attached to a shopping mall, and usually fully booked with a high proportion of western foreigners, was almost empty, in the breakfast buffet area, only a handful of customers. Also, all our suppliers say western buyers are not coming.   
And the buyers that come from South America, the Middle East or Russia tend to stay in as cheap as possible hotels.
I was a little distressed to find Russian products in the supermarket.. Coco even bought these for the grandkids.
 Russian chocolates in China.. It's a sign of the times.

Ancient Wisdom Town
Even though Yiwu is a business city, a little out of town along the river is a tourist area that's been developed in recent years. We took Sandra to see it, so at least she has seen something of China on her trip other than suppliers and factories. I have been before, but this time I discovered some things I didn't appreciate..
Fotang Ancient Town, as it's known, is actually an ancient Buddhist trading post on the river. And still retains a lot of ancient Buddhist buildings, which are only now being recognised as important and finally being restored and cared for. It's really popular with local tourists; it was very busy with lots of people there, but as far as we could see, we were the only foreigners there. 
There are two ancient bridges... One is made of boats strapped together, and at night, there is a spectacular laser show and music. 
One of Fotang’s most striking sights is this floating bridge - a line of boats, lashed together, carrying streams of visitors across the Yiwu River. It struck me that it's not just a bridge-it’s a metaphor for Yiwu itself: a place where old and new, tradition and innovation, meet and mingle.

We wandered the old streets just as it was going dark... and found whitewashed walls adorned with bold calligraphy-“佛堂” (Fotang), meaning “Buddha Hall,” a reminder of the town’s spiritual roots. Fotang was once a Buddhist centre, a place where merchants and monks crossed paths, and where the wisdom of the East was traded alongside silk and tea. 
But today the shops are aimed at tourists, and some really innovative retailers.. I was impressed by this store.. selling only gemstone pendants and bracelets. The shop was long and thin, all painted black, with only backlights shining down on the products. Two rows like this facing. Simple and effective, and actually very busy. 
This style - I thought you might be inspired by it. We can definitely supply you with all those types of products, even the display trays. 

Speaking of innovative retailing.. I believe we glimpsed the future in China also.
I was so impressed.. I made a YouTube short about it..
You can find it here:
More retailing ideas to inspire you!
Subscribe to our YouTube channel if you want more ideas..

Back in the UK
Meanwhile, we have lots of products coming online.. Another Bank Holiday is almost upon us.. so it's all go!
Hope you are ready to rock and roll!!

And next up is Father's Day..


All the best.
Take care, and have a lovely weekend. 
David

title: Buzzing in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia

I arrived here from India a few days ago, and this is a flying visit.. next stop China.
I was in Goa after spending a few days in Jaipur - The Pink City.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
From Jaipur we flew down to Goa.. I didn't know but there is a brand new airport in the north of the state. The airport feels like a holiday camp, very sunshine festive, totally designed for holiday makers.
After a short stay, I took a flight from Dabolim airport in the South of Goa to Mumbai (the most beautiful airport in the world), where I took a very pleasant Thai Airways night flight to Bangkok and a connection to Bali. It's quite hard work getting from Goa to Bali and I arrived exhausted...


North Goa Airport 

Even though I arrived in Bali exhausted and feeling jet lag much more than 3.5 hours difference... so much to do I had to hit the ground running.  I was telling you last time I was in Bali about some issues we are facing with a shortage of artisans, most of those problems are fixed but a couple remain and need me to make visits to suppliers and find solutions.. today made those visits. And I can report.. I think we fixed everything.
But then I went to our warehouse to see how it is going.. We have lots of new staff and Ringo and team are really stepping up the pace. I was so impressed the place is buzzing, absolutely buzzing. Artisan actually queuing with trucks to make deliveries.. Sunday we have a container to load (and another next week) and are racing to pack everything in time.

We made a video to introduce the new staff and show you how it works in the Frangipani Warehouse.



Our new marketing office on the beach (not far from the warehouse) is also Buzzing.. Raul (our IT wizard) arrived just before me from Kuala Lumpur and Peter (our marketing wizard) arrived from Slovakia a day later. We have to plan the next stage in development.. and believe me it's BUZZING down there.. Every morning this week we start the day early with a breakfast meeting on the beach near my hotel. title: Making it Happen
content_html:
Hello from Yiwu, China

Last week I was telling you about some family business success stories from Indonesia and ladies that make it happen. You can read about it here. 
So I have been in China just over a week, and a lot has happened. Its like that here, ridiculously easy to make things happen...


Coco, my wife and our agent in China remembers the Yiwu man coming to her home town village (350 miles from here). Not wanting to give her age away (haha, but this is of cultural importance) in those days the village had little communication with the outside world and the arrival of the Candy Man with his bong bong bong hand drum was an exciting day. She told me she would be collecting fallen chicken feathers for weeks ready for his arrival along with the other village children to trade for candy cane. (it was the late 1970's). Even today if you venture out of the city you will find fields of sugar cane and road side vendors offering sticks of cane or sugar cane juice. The sugar is part of the Yiwu story.
Then the Candy Men of Yiwu came to need more than just sugar cane to trade, and a lively market developed in Yiwu with other goods, sewing needles, cotton and ribbons to start.  


This is a photo from the museum. 1980 - Yiwu city market. The father of a friend of mine - now wealthy - started trading in this market, sitting on the floor with goods laid out on a mat. 
In 1982 this jolly guy - now immortalised as the father of Yiwu (in the centre) dared to ask the communist party if he could let people trade independently, possibly even (heaven forbid) make a profit.

This was 1982.. and he got permission to build this market.



It would take you a full day to walk from one end to the other.. and this is just the main market. It's hard to find a photo that fully captures the scale and scope of Yiwu market.
I can quote all sorts of stats - but nothing prepares you for the full on experience of stepping into the Yiwu world. We have an office and warehouse here, and trade with lots of the family businesses in this area. 

All over the city are trading area's that have grown up for different product groups, some in back streets and fairly informal with traders coming and going from all over the world. One of the most diverse and interesting is the gemstone jewellery area. Indian's, Africans, Brazilians and people from all over Asia and China bring gemstones and trade.. There are a grid of backstreets, tumble-stone machines rumbling on pavements, huge piles of rocks, different shops specialising in lapis (from Afghanistan) or  turquoise (from Iran)   or tiger-eye (from Africa).. Shells of every kind (from Indonesia) every walk of life, every nationality is mingling here..  out of which great beauty comes... and fortunes are made.
Lots of people came to Yiwu looking for a good living - starting with next to nothing and made things happen.

Things happen fast here.. so who knows what can happen this week..

Next week more news..

Take care

David

title: The Team is amazing!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

We are here in Spain launching the new Spain distribution company: AW Artisan.
I was telling you how contrary to popular believe not everyone on Spain is a mañana person. Things can really get done very quickly in Spain.  You can read about it here.

Here in Spain it is a Bank Holiday - it's The Constitution Day: Día de la Constitución - celebrating Spain's move to democracy in 1978.. 
So today we are working at our home (our new Spanish colleagues get a day off).

Yes in a very short time we seem to achieved a great deal. My previous business experience in Spain had always been a bit frustrating, slow and lots of excuses why things couldn't be done. I learn that the solution is to surround yourself with the right kind of good people, taking the time and effort to put a team together that will work together well is seriously worth the effort. 
Since last week, the warehouse outside is painted, the racking all constructed (in 2 days), the walls knocked down and new warehouse constructed, we have a full functioning website, lots of people registering one every few minutes. Contracts signed for all sorts of things.. from shipping companies to water cooler machine. Even though we have very limited stock orders are coming.. over Christmas we will get fully loaded and ready for action in the new year. 

But one thing you need in Spain is a Stamp.. we had to get a stamp made, because a signature is not good enough.. you need to stamp & sign all official documents. 
Why do you need a stamp for your business in Spain but not in the UK.. (or other countries come to that)? 
It's the trust factor. 
One thing I have noticed from travelling around the world doing business in different places, is that the "Trust Factor" is almost a cultural thing, different places have different trust levels.
In India for example trust is very low, people really don't trust each other much. If you buy a new phone or toaster for example, they will take you to the testing room, where you sit with a tester person to make sure everything is functioning correctly before you can take it away. People want to be sure what they have works, and companies want to make sure goods are not switched and returned later.  Although in recent years trust has improved a lot.. it's still not great - why? I don't really know.
Whereas in Indonesia trust is so high, small companies do business on a handshake, shops are left open and unattended (call if you want something).. it's really easy to do business and quick and easy build up a trusting relationship. 
We leased a 1000 meter warehouse with minimal bureaucracy in Bali, the land registry and legal stuff all clear and easy. Compared to Spain.. a breeze.

Spain.. I never realised until now.. but it's a low trust country. Maybe because the legal and company law system is very slow and very weak .. it is possible to run up credit and not pay and get away with that for years. It is simply not possible to find who owns a company, in England or India you can search online and find out - all is open and clear. Here you have to work hard to find such things. In UK you would have to work hard to hide such things. Think about that for a minute, it means no-one really knows who they doing a deal with, or if the contractor who gets to build the new town hall is really owned by the brother of the Mayor. 
So trust is low.. this translates into bureaucracy in government, companies wanting deposits or bank guarantees before trading with you - all barriers to starting a business that don't exist in the UK. 
Now I understand why Spanish people spend so long being nice to each other - developing a bond, kissing warmly, enquiring about each others families, having endless business lunches.. it's all about establishing a degree of trust though relationship. Oh and you need a pretty company stamp.. that helps :)

It's Christmas no? 
Even here the poinsettia christmas tree's are everywhere, the supermarkets are playing "Last Christmas" on loop. Black Friday and Cyber Monday are behind us.. only Christmas Day to come.. 
In Sheffield at AW HQ - Katka (the acting CEO in there) is bravely marshalling the troops and ever optimistic and happy and is leading the effort to get all your orders out.  
I know she is in the thick of it - picking orders and encouraging everyone to keep moving.. only another 10 days to go..


Katka has worked for AW for over 15 years, she is from a small village near Brno in the Czech republic.. we used to joke she was our company Russian spy, but now her accent is more Yorkshire than Easter Europe. There is nobody more clear thinking - positive and perennially cheerful than Katka - and an absolute asset to AW. Married to Philippe the French guy (also helping out today - thanks Phill!) with two charming kids - Katka manages a family and our business amazingly.  She is the commercial director at AW but will deal with almost anything that needs to be done..  And with Tomas, Rodrigo and me in Spain - she is extra busy.. 
Today picking and packing orders..

Oh did I mention a container of new wonderful stuff arrived.. it's really stuff for the Spring season - but we are working hard to get some of it onlne. See below..

I know you are busy also.. 
Take care.. have a great weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: Heat Bombs, Bureaucracy & Bank Holiday Trading
content_html:
Greeting from Sunny Spain

Ironically, parts of the UK have actually been hotter than here this week… but don’t get too comfortable - Spain is next in line for the heat bomb… and it’s coming fast. Last week I was telling you about my trip here and why you should stuff cotton wool in your ears..

I’ve spent part of the week with the Spanish team in the new Malaga office and warehouse. Always good fun. The showroom is taking shape nicely, stock is flowing, and there’s a real feeling that Spain is beginning to hit its stride for us now.

But alongside warehouse visits and meetings… I also had the pleasure of tangling once again with the famous Spanish bureaucracy.

Ah yes… Residency Card Renewal time.



I needed to renew my residency card before it expired. In theory, straightforward.

Years ago, the system involved turning up at dawn outside a local police station, joining a confused crowd shuffling about on the pavement. Every so often a very important-looking policeman would emerge clutching a clipboard and shout out names in an accent so strong that even the owners of the names struggled to recognise themselves. For some reason they always call me by my middle name which they can't pronounced - it's Lloyd. 

It was chaos… but somehow charming chaos.

Now Spain has embraced modern technology.

You can book a very precise online appointment.

Mine was at exactly 10:16am.

Not 10:15.
Not 10:20.
10:16.

I had also been warned very firmly that the appointment MUST happen before the card expired. With my travel schedule resembling a badly organised world tour, getting the slot was stressful enough. My agent Carolina finally managed to secure one in Fuengirola—exactly one day before expiry and perfectly fitted into my travel plans.

So I arrived Thursday night.
Appointment Friday morning.

Perfect.

At exactly 10:16am we marched confidently up the steps. A policeman ticked my name off a list and guided us to a booth where a lady carefully checked all my papers… typed into her computer… frowned slightly…

Then, with what I thought was just a touch too much smug satisfaction, informed Carolina:

“Oh… the rules have changed.”

Something about Brexit was muttered with an elegant Spanish shrug.

Now apparently… I had to attend AFTER the card expired.

All the paperwork was handed back and, almost as an afterthought, she added in English:

“And by the way… you cannot travel outside Spain until your new card is issued.” 

That was the moment I got the “wings clipped” feeling.

Poor Carolina looked close to tears.

I was strangely calm.

“These things happen,” I told her. 


Part 2…



Carolina somehow managed to get another appointment this week - this time in Marbella.

2pm sharp.

A quick Google search beforehand revealed the Marbella office has developed something of a reputation online… phrases like “most unfriendly office in Spain” and “bureaucratic nightmare” appeared repeatedly in the one star reviews.

Excellent.
This should be fun.

Parking was impossible, so I arrived only slightly early. Carolina was already outside bouncing nervously from foot to foot.

“Quickly! Go in!”

“But the appointment is 2pm…”

Yes… but there was one small complication.

A giant sign on the door clearly stated the office closes at 2pm sharp.

Only in Spain could you be given an appointment at the precise moment the office closes.

Anyway… in we went.

And honestly?

Everyone was lovely.

The man at the desk was cheerful, papers all checked, fingerprints taken, forms stamped. I was fully expecting them to hand over the shiny new card there and then.

No chance. The office was closing.

“When can I collect it?”

He smiled warmly. “We will let you know…”

“How long?”

“Maybe three… maybe four weeks…”

But I need to go to the UK.. well you just need a permission letter - ok can I get one.. Turns out you need an appointment to apply for a permission letter; the earliest is in three weeks, and then there's another week's wait for it to be issued. 

Ah yes.

The famous Spanish bureaucracy lives on after all.  No point in getting hot and bothered.. it's getting hot - Heat Bomb - hot already.. 

Meanwhile, the Spring Bank Holiday weekend is nearly upon us, Father’s Day is creeping closer, and the season is definitely heating up - literally and commercially.

New arrivals continue to land from India and Indonesia, including some exceptionally strong-selling gemstone gifts and jewellery lines that are already flying out of the warehouse. There’s definitely a growing appetite for products with meaning, story and a little soul behind them. 

So wherever you are this weekend - whether trading hard, relaxing in the sunshine, or wrestling with paperwork somewhere in Europe - I hope you have a brilliant few days.

And if you happen to have a government appointment booked for exactly the same time the office closes…

Good luck.

Have a great weekend and happy trading.

David

title: Bulging Bags & Bankers
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about "Dancing in the Dark"... the incredible energy your average Chinese person has. No wonder they have so many gold medals.
It's been very busy in the UK, three containers as well as numinous smaller deliveries. The warehouse guys are getting a little stressed. But it's that time of year when all the stock rolls in ahead of the Christmas season. I was delighted to see the Mosaic items from Indonesia appear, they represent a huge amount of work, not just for me, but the small family business that has produced them. Our order gave them three months work. I like doing business with this type of small business, because I feel that we can make a difference. The world is changing, and some really good things are happening that is bringing rapid changes in standards of living to these type of people. Let me tell you a little story.
It was a hot sticky day in June when I set of with our man in Indonesia Ringo (yes that's his name), to accompany him on his errands. Today we were delivering barcode labels to our small but growing band of suppliers. On the back seat of his small 4x4 is a bulging bag, because Ringo has already been to the bank and drawn quite literally a heap of cash. We are making stage payments against orders to help fund production:10,000 rp notes are worth about 70p each, so you soon get a big pile. We get to the Mosaic producers little showroom on the mountain road, spectacular views of paddy fields with steaming jungle back drops. No-one home so Ringo gets on the phone.
More news next week.
QC system...
Turns out today is a local special ceremony day. There are lot of those, and the family are all on the farm, which is also a production area, can we go there? After half an hour of bouncing along rutted tracks and turning down ever tighter roads we finally find the farm yard. Actually part farm, part temple, part factory and today half party. There are incense offerings been made by an ancient teak skinned grandmother, who is topless, she doesn't mind me and grins a toothless smile, scrawny chickens run around my legs. The boss a young man is sat surrounded by his small team of workers, all stripped to the waist - as we arrive they are smoking and raising a toast pouring something home-made looking from a plastic bottle. They are so happy to see us, he leaps up and pours us both some of his home-brew and offers smokes (both of which I manage to decline), and rushes off to proudly show us samples from our order.
Today they are a very different couple to the ones we gave the order to. Then humble and attentive, now boisterous and excited. The boss guy knows just enough English to make a sale and negotiate a price, beyond that he was struggling but he knew the word "quality" and he was inordinately proud of his quality. From what I could gather his quality had got them a big French company order the year before. But being a bit drunk, he was emboldened, he picked up one of the mosaic turtles (coming soon) ripped off the brown paper packaging and rubbed it vigorously. See smooth and no paint coming off. title: David's AW News: Guinea Pigs & the New Dropshipping Website
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ - UK


I'm in the UK, in Sheffield, at the heart of AW. 
Tomas is here, Raul (the IT wizard) has flown in from KL, I'm here. Working on something amazing..
It's all happening here; we are working 24/7 on the new Dropshipping website. Which will be launched very soon.
I'm hoping it will be a game changer for YOU!   (more details below)
Last week I was telling you about my short time in Spain at home, and our guy in Indonesia stuck in Java.. if you missed it, you can catch up here.
Well, it's all happening here.. and I quickly got involved with Rodrigo and the team.. we already made a "Can you sell this? Video.. about the Indian Rag Rugs.. did you see it?
Update from Indonesia.
Our man Bondhan went to Java to load another container of the Big Statues (they are selling faster than we can ship them) - they are good but very complicated because the only way to ship them cost effectively is by filling the void space around the statues with small, expensive items.  We actually made a Video all about it. Well, Bondhan went there, and the truck drivers of Java went on strike.. and everything got delayed. But we have confirmation a container will arrive on Monday, and we can get more of the Big Buddha Statues on the way to you. Please be patient. Although we still have some stock. of some of the sizes. 

New Dropshipping Website update.
It's very close.. standby - hopefully we have a beta tester launch shortly.. if you'd like to be a tester (and forever in our debt), message me and we can add you to the team.. to try out the things.. We have so far.. including API's for Shopify, eBay and WooCommerce, ready to test - please let me know if you'd like to be a Guinea Pig.. Just reply to this newsletter with your name and WhatsApp / Phone number.. and Raul the IT wizard may connect with you. 
Here is a little teaser.
If you have been following this newsletter you will know about the Beach office in Bali, and our team of developers there.. they are working on the backend of the website and need feedback and ideas..  we were there only three weeks ago pulling it altogether, now in Sheffield to get this end of things polished. It's a worldwide team effort. I really believe it will be a game changer for our customers. aw-dropship.com - you can register on our existing site, and when the new site is fully ready, you will already be a member. And be able to use the same login. If you are an invited Guinea Pig  (see above) - you will get access to the Beta version. 

Just Arrived!!
Meanwhile.. today we have the Lokta Paper notebooks from Nepal in our warehouse. And available for the first time in the UK.
In the giftware market eco friendly stationery is a fast growing sector..  I personally use a nice notebook, and there is something low tech about making a handwritten list that focuses the mind and has more power to manifest that list into reality.. than just digital, with that concept in mind, we designed this range of notebooks.. 
Here you can actually see the artisan process of making the Lokta paper. 
I'm very excited!!  Because it's a new family supplier, and I'm really hoping we can develop more business with them. 

They tell me a heatwave is coming.. if it's true, enjoy the sunshine (responsibly) or maybe not!
Have an awesome weekend.. 

More updates next week.

David

title: Big Wheels Turning
content_html:
Greetings from Jakarta (again).

Early Friday morning in central Jakarta, I can hear protestors in the streets, horns and whistles - complaining about fuel price rises. Open the news and see that the Queen has passed away.
Today Coco should return to China.. It is one of those days.

Last week I was telling you about the horrendous covid hoops that they make you jump through before returning to China. Four tests over two days with different clinics in different parts of the city.
If you missed that newsletter you can catch up here.
We went to the first test.. just after I sent last week's news...

Groundhog day.. After the first test within a couple of hours Coco receives a message that there is no need to do the rest of the tests, she has tested positive... again.  I'm dubious.. let's get our own test done now.. Next door to our apartment complex is a hospital with a testing place.  Again (same as last week) our independent test comes back negative. 
This has really messed up the plans, cancelled flight, quarantine hotel.. it's a mess. So we extended our apartment booking and figured out what to do.

I speak to Bondhan who is from Java and ask what we can do.. he asks me if we have been offered an "agent" yet.. Apparently that's how it works.. an "agent" - for a "fee" - can fix things. Then I remembered that the helpful guy in the hospital had given me the personal phone number of the China guy in charge - "just in case we needed help" .. I found the business card with the mobile number scribbled on the back.
Maybe I'm getting paranoid.. is someone messing with us? 

Coco is very active on Chinese social media - her views of her whimsical uploads can be over 30,000 views with hundreds of commentators. I worry she is bringing the wrong kind of attention. A large subset of her followers are also going through the same process of leaving Indonesia for China. 


Should I call the number? Pay a bribe maybe and get Coco back to her family in China. Well no.. in 25 years for doing business we have never paid a bribe, and not planning to start now. But what to do, wait a week and go though the whole expensive process again?

But big wheels are turning and things change quickly.. Hong Kong announces shorter quarantine and more flights into mainland China to reduce a huge backlog. One of Coco's followers recommends a travel agent who can arrange everything, flight to Hong Kong, quarantine hotel for three days and a flight to Xiamen in China, from where Coco can do the seven day quarantine and then get back to Yiwu and her family. The agent assures her that PCR tests in Hong Kong are free of corruption, and non of her clients has had an undue problem. 

So yesterday morning we went for another PCR test within a few hours it came back.. negative of course.. and the China Embassy green card, flight, hotel and flight out of HK all confirmed. 
If all goes well, by the time you are reading this Coco will be on the flight. 

When will I see her again? I don't know.. we are hoping at Christmas and New Year, if (and there are a lot of if's) those big wheels keep turning and things come back to a better kind of normality.
It's has been wonderful being back together with Coco, lots of adventures over the last couple of months.. we went to East Java, Floris Islands, all over Bali, done lots of business.. sorted lots of things both in in Indonesia and China. It's been productive and great fun..  but now I come to say goodbye, I worry that... well you know.. 


Live is an adventure.. and Coco always says.. Let's see what happens come.

Meanwhile - I'm informed it's all happening in UK.. very busy now with lots of deliveries coming. 
Who knows how the big wheels will turn but even at a hint of a power-cut candle sales will sky rocket.. and word from our main supplier in Germany is factory prices could double again soon.
So think about stocking up on candles, anything that keeps you warm and I still feel we are going to need some extra pampering this winter.. 

A little good news from Indonesia.. those big wheels have turned and the cost of getting a 40ft container from Indonesia to Europe has suddenly dropped from €15,000 to €8,000 (it used to be €2,500).
This is great news because we have a warehouse stuffed full of products too bulky and thus too expensive to ship.. we immediately booked three containers and Ringo is working round the clock getting ready to ship next week. 

I'll update you on the latest happenings next week..
Take care.

David

title: Round and Round
content_html:
Greetings from Delhi, India
I'm in the worlds most polluted city..

I arrived from Kuala Lumpa on an evening flight, arriving around 10pm, as we came into land I could see the city below. Draped in a gossamer blanket of mist, the car headlights piercing it the occasional high building rising out of it. That's pretty I thought, then realised that the mystical mist is just the city fug, the dirty soup that you live with in Delhi. Welcome to India.

Last week I was telling you about Yiwu in China, in the aftermath of Chinese New Year, and why you don't need to panic (too much) over Brexit. You can read it here.

Actually, as I exited the terminal looking for my name on the arrival boards of the line of waiting drivers, I had an unexpected surprise. Mr Chatterjee's bright and smiling face... he had made the hour long journey from Greater Noida personally to meet and pick me up. Mr Chatterjee is our long standing supplier of jute and cotton products, and also our India agent. 

India is a country you can love and hate all at the same time. It's all extremes of beauty and ugly, gentle kindness and brutal bullying, ancient mystical wisdom and deluded religious madness.

So I'm here for the Spring Trade Show, now India knows how to organise a trade show. They actually have the best five star hotels in the world in India, period. You cannot beat India for perfect hotels.. and the same people must organise the trade shows these days. Everything is laid on for the buyer, film crews follow you around, welcome entertainment, free lunches and buyers lounges to relax in. Good no? 

No.. it's not good. The problem is most of these stands are run by marketing companies, they don't really make the stuff. Sure they add value by innovation and great designs.. but they also get carried into a fantasy world of what price to charge. 

So I fire up the VPN on my mobile, this gives me google like I'm in the UK.. open up Amazon UK - search for the product I'm interested in. In some cases, I can buy cheaper in the UK then the trade show here. So it's actually hard work.. so I tend to meet the companies where we already have a good relationship. In any event, I need to know we are dealing with actual producers.. we need to know those companies are treating their workers and contractors well because India is a country still riddled with human exploitation. To do that you have to get beyond the trade show you gotta go to real India.
One useful thing about the trade show is that you can see the trends in action. Round bags.. everywhere round bags.. this follows the rattan round bag craze from Bali.. actually made on the island of Lombok these bags became Instagram-cool and container loads were being shipped to America. Designers started to make round bags in lots of natural materials.. in this trade show everyone is at it. I picked up a bag made from jute and cotton on one stand.. how much? Six dollars..SIX DOLLARS!! I try to be polite.. but we have our own bags on sale this week in the UK from £3.95.. 

It's the last day of the show.. I need to get along and finalise some deals, I'm getting Whatsapp messages from 6am.. come to my stand, we can get close to your target price.. 
Tomorrow Mr Chatterjee and I will go and visit some factories in Delhi, later will go down to Kolkatta - I'll give you an update next week.

Take care have a great weekend.

David

title: Adventures in Java 🌍
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

 

But by the time you read this we will be on a different Indonesian island..one I have never been to.. I'll tell you what happens next week.

It's hot there right? Very hot.. hope you are managing to enjoy the heat responsibly. Here in Indonesia close to the equator it is very pleasant weather not too hot never too cold. For sure it's hotter there.

Last week I was telling you about our trip to East Java to an artisan village where almost everyone is involved in making beautiful marble and stone items. If you missed it you can catch up here.


From the stone craft village in East Java we drove west to the city of Solo. Solo has it's own distinct culture and style it's famous for textiles. Bondan told us that a massive factory here produces army clothes and supplies to the Americans, the Russians and the Ukraine Armies. It's famous for being the home town of the much loved Indonesian president Jokowi and the most hated Bali bomber: Known as the smiling terrorist. 

Actually Jokowi and Solo are nick names, they like nick names in Indonesia.. Jokowi real name is Joko Widodo and Solo's is Surakarta City.

 

The Solo people are the happiest and friendliest people in the world, we went to the wholesale textile market in the town centre just to see what happens. We arrived a little too early before everywhere had opened up and witnessed the staff arriving, laughing and joking - it was like a party. Batik fabrics are famous here and you can buy batik shirts in the wholesale market for £2 or £3 for decent quantities.  We had an idea we might be able to source Spa Robes here.. but most of the designs were for the Indonesia market. Bondhan had a friend from university that had started a textile business  - we went to see.




Solo wholesale market.


The textile factory was very interesting. The screen print on fabric on a huge scale, then iron and seal the fabrics ready to go to the production factory to be cut and stitched into whatever.

Interestingly they use different grades of material and different types, the boss showed us a viscus (or rayon) material.. made from bamboo he told us. Soft and silky to touch.

Bondan's idea is that we can make our own pattern design unique to AW and then send it to the stitching factory to produce our own Spa robes and matching products. 




From Solo we travelled into the countryside and deep into the teak forest to visit a village producing teak handicrafts and furniture.. I have been here before and we already had some products in development we wanted to order.

After a day with the teak folk we headed back to Solo and from the airport there Ringo, Coco and me came back to Bali. We left Bondan there to continue with the projects, plus he will visit his home town which is close.

 

So you can see we have been quite busy.

Next week we are officially on holiday (kind of).. but I will update you.

 

Meanwhile back in the UK - despite the heat - we have been very busy also.. lots of great stock arriving all the fast selling stuff you want right now. 

Things that seem to be on fire right now.. Incense items including back-flow burners.. Aromatherapy - Essential Oils are flying. Gemstone Bangles.. we can't ship enough..

title: Mooncakes & Reflections
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu on Mooncake day.

It's Mooncake day (Or mid autumn festival) , a big holiday in China. So I kind of have a day off. Strange weather.. it's supposed to be autumn now, and when I have been here at this time of year it can be quite cool, jacket time. But today it is 33c and high humidity.. My phone tells me a record high temperature for Yiwu at this time. It's shorts and flip-flops weather.
All week beautifully packaged boxes of mooncakes have been arriving at our apartment or office. It's a thing, you do, send all your good customers a Mooncake gift.


That would be amazing - except a) we have too many to eat, b) can't easily re-gift because everyone else has too many already.. and c) I cannot eat those stogy mooncakes.. I really don't like them. But apparently they do have ancient wisdom in them.. Long ago, during the Tang Dynasty, an uprising against the ruling Mongols was being planned. To communicate their revolutionary plans, the local Chinese came up with a clever idea: they hid secret messages inside mooncakes. These messages helped them coordinate their efforts without alerting the Mongol rulers. Later the festival also came to honor the legend of Chang'e, the Moon Goddess who resides on the moon.
That's all you need to know about Mooncakes.. last week I was telling you about arriving in China and discovering that the vast wholesale market is a little placid these days.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

This week Coco and I have been super busy, buzzing around our suppliers, adding a few products to old ranges, and finding a few new ones.  I was telling you how sad and depleted the market seems, but since then we have found other parts of Yiwu actually pretty busy. There is an area that specialises in jewellery components.. I have no idea what many of the shops actually do.. you go and see tiny components, used in who knows what.. and people sorting, packing, selling online sat on the floor, talking live to some distant audience.. this stuff can be shipped by air, so there are few barriers to trade. I guess they trade amongst themselves and the whole world buys its tiny little things in Yiwu. 
Many showrooms have become online streaming venues, selling virtually via the Chinese version of Tiktok, resourceful as ever the small Chinese business people always find a way to trade.


Coco is a keen jewellery designer and understands this market. She is often making jewellery for friends and family. Some of those designs have found their way into AW products.. 

Some producers have given up their showrooms in Yiwu altogether and just sell online.. We went to see a supplier in a nearby city who makes backflow incense burners. The lady boss showed us her showroom, set up a bit like a TV studio. Interestingly prices are coming down, she re-quoted us, some keen prices which we will pass on to you as the stock arrives. I can see from past sales that the simple classic style designs sell best, so we have picked a few more like this..  


A very nice lady she told us about a village in the hills nearby that is a local beauty spot.
Since the weather was so nice and we had done our jobs for the day, we decided to explore.. This village showed up on the map as a five star tourist resort, the road to it maked by multicoloured central lines.. I don't like this centrally organised tourism, where some faceless official decides what area is worthy of tourism. We found the village, a sign said Welcome to Tongyu Village. A beautiful place surrounded by mountains with a pretty pond in the centre square, but appeared abandoned almost a ghost town. There was no restaurant open, nothing much to do. An old man told us up the hill was a temple and a local restaurant. We stopped for lunch and actually it was pretty tasty food, after a while a few local customers came and it was quite jolly, we learned that nearby was a reservoir which you could climb up to.. 


We didn't see another soul, there was 108 steps to climb and at the top the place was absolutely peaceful and pristine, just the sound of cicadas in the trees. It's our ten year wedding anniversary and this spot found almost by accident is a prefect place to be and reflect. 

OK it's almost October.. things are buzzing, so much stock has arrived our warehouses are bursting.. the plan (I believe) is coming together. If you have been following this newsletter you will know how hard we have been working to bring you the absolutely best in giftware. Not just from China, but from India, Nepal and Indonesia (and more). Plus lots of new products from our Aromatics factory in Yorkshire.. I really think this Christmas we have the best product ranges we have ever had. At the end of the day (as I keep banging on) it's 90% about the product.. If you want authentic products then AW is your best source this season and beyond.. 
Check our New for 2023 Christmas fragrance range. The care and love that went creating these fragrances was ledgendary. 

Take care, have a lovely weekend, watch out for that full moon.
More news next week..

David

title: Having a Blast in Bangalore
content_html:
5th February 2013

Hi ,
Greetings from India, last week I was telling you about the Grand Bazaar in Delhi.
You can read it here.
I hope the Valentines Day trading was a success, and you had time for a little romance.
This week I met up with Carlos in Delhi, our Spanish MD, to check out the Handicraft show.
The trade show was good, many new designs on show. We was surprised at the growth in the digital print cushions. From one company (on my last trip) to perhaps twenty producing this product and I have to say fabulous designs. When you see so many companies jumping on the band wagon, you know it's a product that sells through. And the wholesale price has dropped by half, but I'm happy to say still nowhere near our prices for our Oh-so-soft cushion ranged launched today. Digital prints on high quality cushions are major gift trend. Remember you read it here first :)
Oh but Delhi was smoggy and the air quality poor, so many people with hacking coughs, we were glad to escape down to Bangalore. The garden city they call it, and high on a plain it is relatively cool, with old colonial buildings and ancient huge trees arching over the wide roads. Traffic is bad, but it's mostly clean and cared for, the cops are cool in their cowboy hats and always helpful. I like Bangalore.
The airport is about forty kilometers out of town, so you have an hours taxi ride down the smart landscaped motorway they have built. Normally no problem, but we hit a road block and a huge crowd of people blocking the way. It was the Bangalore air show, and the city had ground to a halt.
With our taxi driver practically begging us to stop and watch the show for a bit, and standing traffic, it seemed like we might as well. So we pulled over and joined the excited crowd, as fighter jets roared over head, whizzed past in formation and did spectacular twirls. The jets were great but I also loved the people, hanging from walls and poster hoardings and wherever just to get a better view. These were the cheap seats, well free seats and the people of Bangalore had turned out in mass to watch. Of course two western guys soon make lots of friends in such circumstances. As they say in India "We had a blast!"
Click to enlarge picture
Yes I know.. but we finally we did some work, working on a secret new product range.. so can't tell you too much just yet.
More news next week. Next week I'm in Indonesia.
Take care.. and happy trading.
David

title: Creativity in Chiang Mai
content_html:
For a long time I have wanted to visit Thailand's second city - people keep telling me it is the place for giftware. Indeed we have one supplier there who make the rock shaped soaps we sell, and it's one supplier who's factory I have not yet visited.
Leaving Bangkok and flying to Chiang Mai is like making a trip to see a country cousin. Where Bangkok is fast and flash, high-rise and serious money. Chiang Mai is up country. The highlands of Thailand, and altogether slower paced. It's a low-rise city, old temples, ancient city wall and a lazy river. Streets full of sleepy shops, old hippies and orange robbed monks. Built on a plane with distant mountains rising on all sides, it feels like a small town even though it boosts a population of two million and is home to a highly active giftware industry. They call it: The Creative City.
First stop with my agent (Fredy the Peruvian) was at a freight forwarder to check out the costs and complications of shipping from this city. We learned that most producers don't do packing and labelling the shipping company acts as a packer. Second interesting fact: Holy images of Buddha can not be exported, at least not before they have been un-holyfied. Naturally this costs money. You have to get a license and stamp for every model and shipment.
Then onward to Bann Twai creative village on the outskirts of the city. Here the local government has encouraged producers to set up showrooms and factories. It has grown to the size of a small town, you can get lost in a maze of wood carving, ceramics and table lamp producers. The main streets all showrooms, the back alleyways workshops and small factories.
One showroom had such spectacular glass lamps, and huge carved statues, I couldn't believe anyone would buy. A small Chinese guy with squeaky english and thick round glasses explained that his business supplied five star hotels with artwork for the lobby, designed to impress. We ship to every corner of the world he told me proudly, very good business he said giving me his card.
Chiang Mai is like another world, nothing like the rest of Thailand. So much to be discovered here so little time to do it. It's a seriously arty place with a highly intelligent and entrepreneurial population. A real melting pot of cultures. Local Hill tribes, Burmese (not far away), Thai and Chinese people, not to mention an old British colonial influence. After four days I had reluctantly to move on, but I will be back. Next stop Bali in Indonesia.
More news next week.
Regards
David

title: David's AW News: Spring is in the Air
content_html:
Greetings from Bali,

Last week I was telling you How Strangely Peaceful it was in Bali... and then abruptly not..  If you missed it you can catch up here.. 

Well, the clocks go back this weekend.. SPRING is in the air.. It's time to get your bunny & bounce on!  


Bondhan and I bounced over to the main wholesale market in Denpasar Bali. See below.. as usual spilling the beans on where to go if you fancy importing yourself from Bali.. this is a good starting point.

Meanwhile this week I’ve found myself deep in the world of leases… but in two very different worlds. 

Back in the UK, we’re in the middle of a rent review on our main warehouse—about 9,000 square metres of it. It’s all surveyors, technical arguments, comparables, yield calculations… the kind of conversations that can go round in circles for weeks or months..

Meanwhile, here in Bali, we needed to renew our 2,000 square metre warehouse. A completely different experience. You won't believe the cost comparison, see below!

Last, I sat down with the father and son who own the property. We had a chat, a coffee, a bit of back and forth… and agreed to extend for another five years. Price-wise, it’s kind of understood what the market rate is—and to me, it felt more than fair.

A few days later, we met the notary. She wrote everything up, we all pressed our fingerprints onto the agreement, took a few photos… and that was that.



High trust. Straightforward. Everyone smiling. 

Out of curiosity, I worked it out:

UK = about £110 per square metre per year (all in)

Bali = about £2 per square metre per year (signed and sealed)

It does make you pause for thought. And in Bali, folk are actually complaining about increasing property costs. 

Alongside that, Bondhan and I have been out on the road again—visiting suppliers, looking for those next products that will really work for you.

We’ve just come back from Kumbasari Market in Denpasar. If you’ve ever thought about importing from Bali, this is where it often begins. For decades, Kumbasari has been the wholesale heartbeat of the island—small traders, artisans, middlemen, all under one roof, supplying shops across Indonesia and far beyond.



It’s not glamorous. It’s hot, humid, and the aisles are narrow and busy—but it’s full of energy and ideas.

Interestingly, it was also one of the first places COVID really hit in Bali. Tomas and I were walking those same tight corridors the day before everything changed back in early 2020… it felt very different this time, but also strangely reassuring to see it fully alive again.

Next stop for us is Ubud—always a good place to find something a little bit different, a bit more creative.

And I suppose that’s the thread running through this week…

Two warehouses, two completely different worlds.

One built on contracts and calculations… the other on relationships and trust.

Both are important in their own way.

But at the end of it all, it still comes down to the same thing—people.

We have a couple of new Youtube videos for you.  One of me is walking on the beach near our office and doing my best to persuade you that being a Digital Nomad or Dropshipper is NOT easy.. with the advent of AI you don't need intelligence to succeed.. now to be competitive you need 6 personality traits.. Check them out here


Also here is a new YouTube video from Holly, explaining all about our Nomad Sari (the spirit of travel) Brand.


CAN YOU SELL THIS? Nomad Sari Collection.

Wishing you a totally Happy Spring! Hope that trade is good.. if not amazing!  We have so many amazing products to make it that way. Just check out below.

Take care (as they say here, Hati-Hati)

More news next week and from somewhere NEW..  (it's time to move on)..

David

Last week I was in Slovakia at our EU distribution center, telling you about the Secret Soup of Life. You can read about it here.

Since then Raul (our IT wizard) took the Ryanair flight down to Malaga - we have been working on improving the software systems... lots more improvements are in the pipeline.

In the UK it's all happening.. a flow of containers from all corners.. Indian, Indonesian and Chinese deliveries, so lots of things back in stock.
The warehouse team is working flat out to book in all that stock.. and doing a great job. Well done guys!

Over the top flowers. There is something about the Spring that puts a spring into everyone and things just seem to happen, so maybe May is a good time to make things happen, to get creative.. to spring to life.
Let the inner flowers just bloom..

It's another Bank Holiday almost upon us, so now is the time to stock up ready for the rush.. check out the special May madness deals below.
It seems to me that Bank Holidays are getting ridiculously busy, this picture from the Yorkshire Post shows the mad rush in one of my favourite places on Easter weekend: Whitby. 



It's the instagram effect.. like everyone goes to the latest trending place all at the same time.
Is it good thing? 

So here's wishing you a blooming marvelous weekend, wherever you are :)

David

title: Coco has gone
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Yes I'm back in Ubud for a short while. Last week I was telling you about the dodgy goings on in Jakarta with Coco and her return trip to China. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Coco left Indonesia (and me) on the same day the Queen died. We took a taxi to the airport and checked in to the Jakarta Airport Hotel which is inside terminal 2E - because Coco flight was at midnight and we could rest there until her time to leave and I could sleep there until my flight back to Bali the next morning. If you are ever in Jakarta I would recommend this hotel if you have early or late timings.. super helpful people, quiet rooms and good lounge.. plus they will make sure you get to the right terminal, even by car - which they did for Coco. At 9pm I went with Coco, a porter and the luggage outside where a car was waiting to take her to the International terminal. 
The moment we said our goodbyes, a hug, she jumped in the back seat and the door slammed shut, smoked glass, I couldn't see her - and she was gone. 

We are closed on Monday in respect for the Queen's Funeral - hope your day is peaceful and reflective, whatever your views this event marks the passing of an era. That is something to reflect on.

The next morning I took the sky-train to the Air Asia terminal - and on an early flight back to Bali, Ringo was waiting for me in arrivals. "We have a lot of work to do Ringo" - I told him.. 
Coco arrived in Hong Kong, spent five hours in various queues before being taken to the quarantine hotel downtown for three nights.. after she flew to Xiamen on a very short flight but now inside China - inside a government quarantine centre being tested two times a day for seven days. The room is large and clean with a good supply of water and snacks. Room enough to practice the yoga moves she learned in Ubud.. she is getting to expert level.. and posting her moves on her social media channel in China. After Xiamen she needs to get home to Yiwu.. could fly or go by train, and it's not clear if she will have to do further quarantine in Yiwu, she thinks three days. So much trouble, so many tests.. it will have taken basically a month to get back inside China. You can't help thinking this is designed to stop Chinese people from travelling, a travel ban in all but name. 

Here in Bali my first job was to go and see the three wise incense men of Ubud.  They are incense obsessed and produce a very special incense made from over 30 herbal ingredients developed over three generations and now tweaked and perfected for Ancient Wisdom.. They call it simply: Healing Incense and it has to be burned in a particular ritualistic way..  I went along to smell the modified fragrances. My idea was to make the aromatic element more dominant and create a cleaner recognisable fragrance. So because of the delay in Jakarta they had more time to work on getting the blends perfect. And I have to say I was pleasantly surprised, I have a very good nose.. and almost all fragrances products have to get past my nose before they can be listed at AW. And these guys had listened closely to my brief and delivered.


We gave them a decent sized order, and in thanks they had to make offerings.. in fact before each business meeting they make an offering. Before each batch is carefully blended which I understand has to be done according to the Balinese calendar.. they make an offering. All this mindfulness and focus I believe will make an excellent product. 
We asked how long it would take to complete our order.. and before giving us an answer they had to consult the Bali calendar.. because timing is important and there are days you can and cannot start a project.


There are 210 days in a Balinese year, and that overlaps with other local calendars.. it's very complicated.

Anyway the deal is done and now I'm working on packaging and presentation with Bondan.. our designer here.
Lots of other projects are underway and have to finalised over the next few days.. so a busy time.

I'll update you next week. By then Coco should be back home in Yiwu.
Have a restful weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: Discover the ancient secrets of Lokta paper.
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu.


I can't believe I have been here a full week, so much has happened it feels like a month.
Easter is almost upon us, just time to get fully stocked and ready for trading action.

Here, yesterday it rained, which believe me.. was a major relief, because Kathmandu valley has been experiencing some of the worst pollution levels in its history. Actually they tell me it is worse than Delhi (and that's where we are off to next), and this week Kathmandu actually claimed the dubious crown of the world's most polluted city.  But after the rain the gloom lifted and views to the mountains appeared.  Kathmandu is a basin city, head out and up and you can quickly leave the smog behind, so naturally we took every opportunity to get out to see our suppliers' workshops and factories outside.
Escaping Kathmandu smog.

Last week I was telling you about the journey here, and secret mysterious ceremonies of Bali.. if you missed it you can catch up here. 

I'm here with Toni from Spain, he has been here with me before and already has good relations with a number of our suppliers, it's so nice to be back and our friends here are so welcoming. We have even been invited to a wedding party this weekend. One thing I have wanted to do for a while is the Lokta paper products. They make notebooks and lanterns and even incense from this special paper.
Last time I tried to find the actual artisan producer but couldn't get past the middleman traders.. this time we got lucky and found the son of a family business. 

Lokta paper is totally Ancient Wisdom.. traditionally made for over 1,900 years in this area. Made from the fibrous inner bark of the Daphne shrub, which grows naturally in the high altitudes of Nepal, this paper has long been revered for its quality and resilience. In ancient times, it was used to record and protect sacred Buddhist scriptures such as the Karanya Buha Sutra.

Interestingly the Lokta plant regenerates naturally within just 4–6 years of harvesting, making it an eco-friendly alternative to conventional paper. No trees are chopped down to make this type of paper.  In fact these days they have blends of Lokta paper made with blends of lemongrass and eucalyptus leaves. Every sheet of Lokta paper is painstakingly handmade by skilled Nepalese artisans using age-old techniques passed down through families, keeping this traditional craft alive and thriving in local mountain communities.

So went to see the small workshops in a village on the outskirts of the Kathmandu valley about an hours drive away.
It's was fascinating and lovely to meet his team of workers and his father. Really interesting to see the notebook making processes, in the corner of the workshop was a huge stack of the Lokta paper and I asked where it came from and if we could go and see it being made..
So the next day we went to a different village to see paper production..
I managed (with a little help) to put together a Youtube video for you! - please give me a little encouragement - like and subscribe (well if you actually do)..


Actually we are so busy here - need to dash, got a meeting with another supplier in a few minutes.
I'll update you more next week.

Meanwhile back in the UK we have had a container from Indonesia with lots back in stock and some new beautiful windchimes from one of my favourite suppliers.
Also they tell me Dinner Candles finally in stock.

Take care,
Have a wonderful weekend.
David

title: Tornadoes & Mangos 🌪
content_html:
Greetings from a still rather grey Sheffield.

 

Everyone, myself included, is complaining about the UK weather, and with some justification it's been one of the wettest and coldest May on record. 

 

I called Mr Chatterjee for an update on his oxygen for the poor of his town mission. (you can still donate here) - he was telling me that they had already bought the oxygen and given it to three families in dire straits. There is also a local volunteer force of young people that own cars who are bravely taking people to hospital and back because there are not enough ambulances and taxis refuse to carry ill people. These people also can take the oxygen where it is needed. 



If this situation wasn't bad enough - the region was hit by a massive storm earlier this week, some coastal towns almost washed away, along the Ganges tornadoes raging.. He sent me a video.. check it out.



So now not complaining any more.. counting blessings instead. Last week I was telling you about "The Ultimate Gift" and the "Trial of Tomas" - if you missed it you can read about it here. 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 73,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka, Rodrigo and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken. 

 

So it's almost June, and the weather forecast is looking up. As it's a bank holiday and I know many of you are ready for retail action. So trade is looking up.. 

Getting supplies is hard work, disruptions on so many levels. If covid issues don't disrupt things, then Brexit issues will, and if that doesn't there is the world-wide shortage of containers and crazy prices being demanded.

Coco in China is managing with great difficulty to book containers. When we try to book with UK agents they are regularly cancelled at short notice, and we are told to rebook at a higher rate. It's marginally easier to book containers to Europe, but to the UK prices are inexplicably higher and more prone to be cancelled. I'm trying to find out why.. 

 

In spite of all these hurdles to overcome, two containers made it and arrived this week. One much delayed one with just Soap Flowers. I know a lot of people have been waiting for the Luxury Soap Flowers.

 

And amazingly a container of mango wood products from the city of  Saharanpur in Northern India. It's the woodwork craft city of India.



Years ago it used to mainly produce Sheesham wood, sometimes called Indian Rosewood.  You will remember those brass inlaid ash catchers..  But Sheesham wood is a hardwood and grows too slowly to be sustainable, a few years ago the Indian authorities regulated Shesham making it very expensive and almost impossible to export without all the proper paperwork. So it was a big upheaval for the craft industry in that city. 

The solution was mango wood..  basically mango trees produce a crop of mango's but when they get old the crop is poor. So mango farmers cut down old trees and plant new ones on a rotation basis. Hence fast growing mango wood is a by-product of mango production (a big favorite in India) and totally sustainable. Dried and treated properly this wood is also very beautiful.



I went with Mr Chatterjee from Delhi to Saharanpur by sleeper train to sort out this transformation of products from Sheesham to Mango. 

Our supplier Rashid met us at the station.. the contrast from Delhi to Saharanpur was a culture shock.. I'm sure it has improved these days.. but that time I really thought I'd landed in a lawless province of Afghanistan. There were men with machine guns, muddy streets, camels pulling cart loads of huge logs. Rashid took us to his surprisingly organised factory with a large team of in-house artisans.. it was a massive job re-inventing a range of products from hardwood to softwood.. but we did it. I always remember being invited to Rashid's home at the end of a very long day, and sitting on the floor in a circle eating the most amazing biryani cooked by his wife. 

 

Some importers still do dodgy things and mislabel illegal sheesham wood (on shipping documents) as mango, and especially in Europe you can get in a lot of trouble doing this and it is very easy to lose the license importers need to import wood.  So if anyone tries to sell you that old fashioned sheesham wood, you should question it's provenance. 

This delivery means we have some stock of mini display stands used for starter packs, as many of you are just re-opening and revamping.. maybe this is good timing. 

There is another container being loaded in Saharanpur very shortly, but local lockdowns could easily disrupt that. Already the problems in India have had a massive disruption on supply lines. I don't see it getting better anytime soon.

So heads up, Stock up on indian products when you can.

 

Wishing a lovely Bank Holiday weekend.. stay safe and I hope you get a chance to enjoy some time in the sun.

 

More News next week.

 

David

 

PS

You can still help Mr Chatterjee and his team help people in his town. Even if you only share these links in your social media it will help. Help Mr Chaterjee - or.. More info here

title: Getting over the Brexit Bump
content_html:
Getting over the Brexit Bump..

Greetings from Sunny Sheffield
Yes, I am here at Ancient Wisdom HQ - and it's such a delight to be in amongst the home team.
Last week was the Easter newsletter (I was in Spain) and was all about re-birth - right at the time AW main UK website was being reborn. You can read about it here.

Since then I have made the hop from Malaga to Yorkshire, and strangely and very unusually it was warmer in here than Spain.. 
Must be global warming, no wonder everyone is protesting down in London. 

The awful news from Sri Lanka was particularly distressing as I was just there a few weeks ago, as regular readers will know. My wife and I visited at least one of those churches and stayed in the hotel next to the Shangri-la - our friends had lunch in there.
We have an IT team based in Kuala Lumpur, and one of the team is from Sri Lanka - he was visiting his home town when it happened. It all seems so shockingly close. Now the foreign office has advised against travelling there. I was planning to go back sometime soon.. this time to do business - gemstones are good - and I will not be changing my plans...  why should we let them win?

It's all go at AW - so many projects underway.. lots of beautiful new products all bubbling away and so much enthusiasm - it's intoxicating :)
The new revamped website has got everybody excited and somehow even more motivated, it's quite exhausting.. and so much love and positive feedback. Although I keep finding broken links or formatting errors.. I'm fixing them at 4am when I can't sleep :)
You won't realise this but the backend of the website was also revamped - the part that enables us to process your orders and run everything from the warehouse to the website - it's all new and improved and I hope will enable us to serve you faster and better. The old system has gone to the server in the sky, it's dead and gone.. our customer service team are on a new platform and still finding out how everything works, so I hope you can bear with them if they seem slightly hesitant when you call them.

This next week there is quite a few deliveries expected.. tumble stones from South Africa, a container from Indonesia, an Indian shipment and a Salt Lamp container.. then there are three containers from China to arrive pretty close together.. 
This week Singing Bowls from India came.. so they are back in stock..
There was a bit of a lull in incoming shipments because we were stocking up ahead of the Brexit day that never was, now we are bit back to normal.. getting over the Brexit Bump..  and getting ready for the wedding season.

How many weddings are you invited to this year?
Are you stocked with wedding related items - things for wedding favours, church etc? Now is the time to keep those wedding bells in mind..

Next week I will be in Slovakia at our AW Gifts outpost. We have a distribution warehouse in the pretty town of Trnova not far from Bratislava.. 
So updates and news from the Eastern Europe front next Friday.

Take care.. have a great weekend.
