Last week was the Easter newsletter (I was in Spain) and was all about re-birth - right at the time AW main UK website was being reborn. You can read about it here . Since then I have made the hop from Malaga to Yorkshire, and strangely and very unusually it was warmer in here than Spain.. Must be global warming, no wonder everyone is protesting down in London. The awful news from Sri Lanka was particularly distressing as I was just there a few weeks ago, as regular readers will know. My wife and I visited at least one of those churches and stayed in the hotel next to the Shangri-la - our friends had lunch in there. We have an IT team based in Kuala Lumpur, and one of the team is from Sri Lanka - he was visiting his home town when it happened. It all seems so shockingly close. Now the foreign office has advised against travelling there. I was planning to go back sometime soon.. this time to do business - gemstones are good - and I will not be changing my plans... why should we let them win? It's all go at AW - so many projects underway.. lots of beautiful new products all bubbling away and so much enthusiasm - it's intoxicating :) The new revamped website has got everybody excited and somehow even more motivated, it's quite exhausting.. and so much love and positive feedback. Although I keep finding broken links or formatting errors.. I'm fixing them at 4am when I can't sleep :) You won't realise this but the backend of the website was also revamped - the part that enables us to process your orders and run everything from the warehouse to the website - it's all new and improved and I hope will enable us to serve you faster and better. The old system has gone to the server in the sky, it's dead and gone.. our customer service team are on a new platform and still finding out how everything works, so I hope you can bear with them if they seem slightly hesitant when you call them. This next week there is quite a few deliveries expected.. tumble stones from South Africa, a container from Indonesia, an Indian shipment and a Salt Lamp container.. then there are three containers from China to arrive pretty close together.. This week Singing Bowls from India came.. so they are back in stock.. There was a bit of a lull in incoming shipments because we were stocking up ahead of the Brexit day that never was, now we are bit back to normal.. getting over the Brexit Bump.. and getting ready for the wedding season. How many weddings are you invited to this year? Are you stocked with wedding related items - things for wedding favours , church etc? Now is the time to keep those wedding bells in mind.. Next week I will be in Slovakia at our AW Gifts outpost. We have a distribution warehouse in the pretty town of Trnova not far from Bratislava.. So updates and news from the Eastern Europe front next Friday. Take care.. have a great weekend.

title: 3 Fold Harmony & 2 Wild Boars
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Last week I was telling you about how "Authenticity" matters in the gift trade. But what does authenticity really mean? .. you can read about it here.

Soon it will be time to move on, time to travel, time to discover some beautiful things, things that hopefully will delight your customers and enhance your business. If on the way we can help nurture small businesses in developing countries it all adds to the karma and (that word again) authenticity of the offer. So making plans for a return trip to Morocco (a lot offer from there, especially perfumes and florals), then Indonesia - we have a new warehouse (more below), then India, China and maybe a quick trip to Nepal. Hope you will follow along for the ride, and give me your ideas, suggestions and comments. It's your feedback that has shaped AW and made the product range what it is today.

Here's some boar-ing news from Spain.
You will have seen in the media it has been epically, biblically hot in Spain! But here in La Cala de Mijas near the sea, it has been actually quite pleasant. Head inland just a bit and the temperature rockets up and wildfires are raging. My friend Clive's home was almost in a ring of fire, helicopters scooping water from the sea and dumping it in relays to save them. Coming home late one evening we were shocked to find a wild boar and it's cub not far from our house, munching on our comuninial flowers. Clive tells me they run away from the fires and the heat, head towards the coast to cool down.



Wild Boars in town - a sign of global warming.

Here's some less boring news from Bali.
Regular readers will know about Ringo, our man in Indonesia. He a hard working guy, but recently he's been very busy. In between despatching containers, we have been moving warehouse. I signed the lease on Jackfruit village warehouse earlier this year, you can read about it here. that in itself was an interesting experience.  Our old warehouse on the outskirts of Ubud, close to the famous Monkey Forest had in recent years become too small to cope, and loading containers more and more difficult as the area got more congested. Our new home is five times the size not far from the main Denpasar highway, has a big yard for loading containers and (pleasantly) within walking distance of the sea. The village area it falls in translates as Jackfruit Village.  The warehouse had in a previous life been the islands Coca Cola depot. It was pretty dilapidated, so in return for some rent-free time we spent money to bring it up to a good standard. 

One condition of the lease was that after renovation and before use we would need to have the property properly blessed. It was contractual, but Ringo would have done it anyway.
Ringo was so enthusiastic he was live streaming the events to me.. some of the village folk nearby brought goodwill offering, the local holyman laid out a blanket in front of the offices, and the ceremony was made. I really don't understand the details, but it is something to do with three-fold harmony. Harmony with the spirits/God, with the earth/environment and with our fellow humans. Out of this balance can come prosperity.. Here is more information if you are interested.

The ceremony happened this week.. here are a few pictures.




Check, our actual car park temple, locals coming to wish us well.

Hopefully, I will go there soon, we are planning nice offices, a design studio, a QC area and a place Ringo can greet and meet with local artisans. It's a good central location, many of the artisans we work with are in the area and can bring work in and be paid on the spot. Packaging, labeling and quality control in the old warehouse was done in cramped conditions, here we can get really organized.  I'm looking forward to working there.. don't worry you will get full updates.

Meanwhile, in sunny Sheffield, a container (from Indonesia) came, another from China and some Indian shipments.. so it's been pretty hectic there.
Tomas is delighted (by the way he reached the epic age of 35 today) because one of his recent creations came to fruition. A range of ready to retail Soap Flowers, absolutely perfect pick up gifts for lots of occasions, and a fresh new slant on the hugely successful Soap Flower range. Maybe he would like one as a birthday present..? haha.
I'm also happy because my range of leather journals came into stock from India. All very "Game of Thrones" style, gothic and stylish at the same time. Ideal for any historic gift shop location and perfect gifts for many an occasion. I seen these first in a gift shop in Portugal last year, a customer of AW, the owner told me of all the products she stocked the leather journals generated the biggest sales. She had a big old table in the centre of the shop opposite the entrance piled high with books. 
See below, for more details.. we have more designs coming soon and I believe our prices (as usual, sorry to blow-own-trumpet again) are the best... if not let us know, we always price match on a like for like basis. 

Anyway I don't want to boar / bore you anymore :)   More news next week.

Wishing you all the best three-fold harmony!

Take Care

David

title: Something Strange Happened
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

Hope you had a wonderful Easter, now onwards into the spring..
Last week I was telling you about selecting the auspicious date for a ceremony  to launch our start-up in Bali..The date was carefully selected as the 10th of April. If you missed the reasons why you can catch up here.
I'm delighted with our new office, the objective to create the best possible work place, a dream location, swimming pool, air-conditioned,surf view.. who wouldn't want to work here?
Well it seems like no-one wants to work here.. Debbie our HR has been interviewing six or seven people a day, we have hundreds of applications, the best ones are invited to a second interview.. we then offer people jobs to find they have already found another job, or changed their mind or just don't answer.. we thought this would be easy but it seems lots of companies are recruiting for digital marketing professionals right now.

Meanwhile I have been doing what I love to do, and that's buzzing around the villages of Bali visiting artisan suppliers and developing new and beautiful products. While driving I asked Ringo about the ceremony.. 
We had the ceremony for our new business on the 10th of April as planned.
It was amazing.. the ladies that work in our warehouse and the wife of our security man, came dressed beautifully in traditional Balinese clothes. They constructed an offering table that was stacked high with allsorts of things.. then the local holy man came, sat crossed legged and started to ding a bell in front of the offerings.. At one point the ladies taking a bowl of specially blessed water joyfully with much laughter and energy swooped and whooped to every room and corner of the office, splashing water all over the place... 


Ringo came with a big bag of traditional clothes, and Tomas, me and Peter (from Slovakia) changed into Balinese mode.  After we were all called to sit crossed legged on the floor behind the holy man, he started chanting some mantras and we all made the namaste pose with our palms together. In front of us a colourful basket of flower petals.The temple bell was hypnotically dinging away.. then we paused and Ringo said now take some yellow petals inside your fingers and the process was repeated..  then again we did it again green leafs, then again with blue petals, then with a handful mixed petals and finally nothing between our palms. I felt that spiritual power flowing, when somehow you touch the divine. Then it was all over, we had pictures with the priest, lots of laughter and then special food came.. Nasi Champor which was delicious. 


Don't worry I have not converted to being a Balanese Hindu.. but the whole mystical  experience was undeniably uplifting. Even if I had no idea of the symbolism of the various elements..
So whilst driving around the villages and rice terraces of Bali I quizzed Ringo about what it all means..
I took notes..
Doing Namaste with empty hands to start - means unconditionally asking for blessings but not expecting.
With yellow flowers - means asking the sun god to warm us with energy and to watch over us.
With green leaves - means asking the god of the land. Ask for our building to be safe and secure. (important in a land of earthquakes and volcanoes)
With blue flowers - to the goddess of the sea. To all to be safe, positive and happy..and to secure a prosperous catch of fish... ie to be successful.
With mixed flowers - is to all gods - for protection from evil and to smooth the paths before us.
Empty again - thankfully to everyone, to the earth, to the gods, to nature. 

The chanting.. was this..
Om santi santi santi om .. Good inside and all outside. 
Damai di Hati damai di dunia ... Peace in the heart, peace in the world

Nice no? 
Ok you might be sceptical, but all the Balinese people we connect with are super happy, the whole thing cost including the food, penjars, offerings and donation to the priest was very small money. So I'm happy.
Bondhan made a video for Youtube.. 


Meanwhile back in the UK.. lots of stock arrived from India.. including some tie-dye cotton bags that I'm excited about..
During that ceremony the priest asked for blessings for our customers - that's YOU.. so I hope they are flowing nicely to you..
Next week I'll be in China!! so News from there..

Wishing you a beautiful and peaceful weekend.
The day after the ceremony.. Something strange happened... people started enthusiastically accepting our job offers.. six people so far..so it's all happening..

David

title: David's AW News: Guitar Village Collab!
content_html:
Greetings from somewhere in central Java


Happy Bank Holiday Weekend! 
Hope Storm Lilian gives you a bypass.

Collaboration. That's a good, profound and important word. I'll explain below something I learned this week.
Last week I was telling you about being Independent in Indonesia, if you missed it you can catch up here.

So earlier this week Bondhan and I caught the morning Lion Air flight from Denpasar, Bali down to Yogyakarta in central Java, the main island of Indonesia. Lion air has a reputation of being bad, but our flight was up there as the most perfect and beautiful ever. The seats are the tightest gap you can imagine, but our air hostess spots my cramped long legs and moves me and Bondhan to the emergency exit row with views just before the wing.  Taking off and banking around over beautiful surf, overflying our beach office then flying west over all Bali and seeing the straits between Bali and Java. Spectacular views of the Ijen mountain with a vivid acid blue lake near it's peak but also live lava flow burning down a flank.
Fly down the north coast over the fabled Madura Island of the coast near the port city Surabya, then we bank left and fly across the island and land at the new Yogyakarta airport. It's a short but dramatic flight. This week in Java is the same.. in just a few short days way too much to report..

Right now we are in the beautiful city of Solo famous for textiles and clothes production.  It's in central Java and the people here are the most open, happy and friendly you can imagine. But there is one village nearby where that friendliness reaches a new level. Bondhan who is the right hand man of Ringo, our agent in Bali.. in another life is also a musician in an (occasional) heavy rock band. We actually met in the pandemic when he was trying patiently to teach me to play guitar. And since his hometown is near here naturally he knew about the Guitar village.
Despite it being very hot, we decided to walk the streets and see what we could find. People smile and say good morning and it seems quite natural to just walk into peoples homes, all of which are artisan home industry places in full swing. A guitar is quite a complicated thing and here no one person makes a guitar from start to finish, each street does a particular process. The frame shape is formed and glued on one street. Another fixes, treats and polishes the fret boards, another specialises in the necks.  It's fascinating and the friendly, open people invite you into their workshops and homes. We learn how many years and generations a family has been doing a process.. and they tell us openly how many they can produce in a day, and how much they sell on the part they do. One guy made just the body of Ukuleles and sold them for amazingly for about £7 per dozen.. a stack by his front door waiting for fellow collaborators to pick up.
Gradually as we move through the village, past Jackfruit laden trees. Lime groves and low hanging mangos, the place seems blessed by nature, we find the finishing part of town where artisans put everything together, string up the instruments, add all the details and deliver a finished product. There is music playing everywhere as people work, and people even playing guitars on a break.
Even though Java is Muslim, they have a huge love of music. Especially Heavy Metal and 1970/80's music. The President of Indonesia known as Jokowi is famously an AC/DC fan and plays a mean electric guitar. In a local BBQ restaurant in Yogyakarta we were entertained by buskers playing music from my childhood. Blur and the Beatles. 

By popular request we had been planning to add ukuleles to our musical instruments range for a while, but the prices and quality we found in Bali didn't make sense.  The cheapest quality are mainly for decoration and get finished in Bali for the souvenir market.  Back in Europe they would not compete at the bottom end of the (Chinese factory made) market. Whichever way I sliced it the product didn't add up. But here we can buy much better quality direct from the artisans and sell into the mid market - a nice product.. Bondhan had found the best selling Ukulele brand on Shopee (Indonesian Amazon) with top reviews and impressive sales figures.. We happened upon a household making just Ukuleles and it turned out to be the very same. 
Bonhan made this video of our experience.. with a glimpse of some of the other projects we have been working on.
The father was very proud of his young daughter who had set up the Shopee online store and direct sales to end users, clearly a big boon to the family business. Bondhan road tested their product, nice sound, great details, very playable.. he entertained us with a pretty good Bohemian Rhapsody rendition..   We asked how many they could make for us a month - turns out they have extended family who can help and we can get not a huge amount but enough to get started. Bondhan asked for better strings, an improved tuning mechanism (a little more cost) and he will redesign some of the details. I think we can get a damn good Artisan made product to the market at around £35 retail. But it will take time.. a few months before they start to arrive.
The Ukulele Family

The thing that impressed me most is how this village all works together.. in a beautiful friendly collaboration. Each playing their own part just like in a band to make beautiful music together.. but in this case beautiful musical instruments. More news from Java next week..

Meanwhile in the UK..
.. it's all happening. More new stock keeps arriving.. I'm very excited to see the Gemstone Planets online.. so much work and a serious Collaboration to make this happen.. Packaging designs by Sandra, text input from yours truly, range selection and design by Tomas and Coco organised everything including the printing of the boxes and packing the product.   
Also lots back in stock this week.. including.. Now please stay calm.. Luxury Soap Flowers  LSF-02  .. last time we had a shipment it sold out in a few hours.. be quick if you want to grab some!

And what better time than when we have a FREE SHIPPING WEEKEND.. (until midnight on Monday).
Check out the rest of the main back in stocks.. and the other NEW PRODUCTS.

Hope the weather treats you kindly and you have a lovely weekend (working or otherwise)..
We just dropped in to see Bondhans family in his hometown - Ngrambe - where I'm finishing this newsletter and Bondhan is editing the video above.. (check it out)...yes we are Collaborating :)
Take care.. as they say here Hati Hati!

David

title: Beyond the Gates of Heaven
content_html:
Greetings from Amed, Bali

Hope the heatwave is being kind to you.. 
Here in Bali the weather is not too hot, we came East - the far east of Bali under the looming Mount Agung to a spectacularly beautiful but not really well known area. 
Last week I was telling you about a typical day's work in Ubud, and trouble with monkeys.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

The village of Amed is basically a coast road stretching about 10 kilometers with small guest houses and little hotels dipping their toes into the warm sea. The main reason to come here is diving and diving schools and dive shops make up half the businesses. French people discovered the area years back and the locals seem to know as much French as English. 
This sleepy part of Bali suffered badly in covid lock-downs and basically closed, now Bali is booming but the tourists (mostly French) are only just rolling up here, and Amed is not ready, only two ATM's in town are functioning. I stood in a queue of complaining French folk at the only working ATM trying to explain the Indonesian concept of "sabar".


Sleepy Amed with Mount Agung the volcano in the back.

The internet is on and off and when working - pretty patchy, which for my wife Coco is stressful because she spends most of the day communicating with the AW China office in Yiwu. She is getting a little agitated because Yiwu has gone into zero covid lock-down again. Yesterday we were due to load a container, Coco thought it would be fine, the last lock-down business was allowed to flow with some strict restrictions.. the driver couldn't leave his cab. But this time it's super strict.. everything is closed. At the last minute even as the empty container was enroute to our warehouse, everything was cancelled.  How many cases are there I asked. 131 she said. Here in Bali it is similar but no-one is panicking. In Yiwu now, there is full lockdown, and daily testing.. for at least a week. So a container of stock for Christmas is delayed. Sabar.

You can snorkel straight off the beach into the most spectacular tropical sea filled with every kind of fish and if you are patient and have enough "sabar" it's entirely possible a sea turtle will bless you with company and swim alongside.
The dive shops will take you further to dive on sunken Japanese ships from the second world war or in search of sharks, but I'm happy inshore just with a snorkeling mask and flippers. 
We came here seven or eight years ago and Coco wanted to revisit.. hence our trip. Ringo brought us here, he likes this area also -- high on the mountain looking down on Amed is his favorite temple. Known as the "Gates of Heaven" it's an instagram spot. A Balnese gate frames a mountain view of mount Agung. To get to the temple complex and the gates is quite a walk up 1700 steps up the mountain but Ringo explained that the real temple is small and sacred and can only be approached on foot, another 2000 steps higher up the mountain, he was there on a pilgrimage recently but would be happy to be our guide and take us up. Basically beyond the Gates of Heaven.


Before covid this spot became super popular with the insta crowd, the queue to get this shot could be upto two hours. 

Anyway with all the trouble in the world, it's nice to escape a little. Back to work tomorrow.. back to Ubud and the AW warehouse.
Lots of jobs to do.. not least sorting out our bulging warehouse and streamlining container dispatches.

Meanwhile back in the UK it's definitely getting busy, and it's nice to see so many Indonesian products selling. The Marame Hati Hati Angels.. these were so long in the making I can't tell you.. are selling very well and this makes me happy because I can report to the young enthusiastic guys making them that a re-order will be forthcoming. When? they ask... Sabar sabar I say.. 

But not all is good, here and in the UK raw material prices are rocketing. Shipping costs are still through the roof. At AW we work hard to absorb price increases, and I know that every product has an optimum price at which it sells best.. It worries us when products start to look expensive because it disrupts the all important flow of goods and good karma.

So here is a heads up guys.. shortly we will be increasing some prices.. 
The combined effects of supply issues, raw material increases, raw material shortages, inflation, fuel cost, and energy price have pushed cost prices much higher than we would like.
At this stage we are focusing on the products produced at AW Aromatics.. our own production items.

That's the bad news , but the good news is as a valued customer and reader of this newsletter we are giving you advance warning to enable you to order ahead of the increases.
The price rises will come into effect in the first week of September. The rates vary from 10% upwards and in some cases much higher - because horribly some raw materials have doubled in price.

I hope you can understand, despite many increases over the last 11 months this is the first material increase we have made in a long time.
I can assure you that we remain focused on being competitive in the market, so even after these price rises we aim to be your best value supplier, if you should find "like for like" products cheaper then please let us know.

The good news is there are some stunning new products available - Massage soaps - wow and considering everything the guys in production have achieved a good price point.
Other good news - if you want to stock up now ready for Christmas and ahead of price rises.. we have more payment options available.. including 60 days credit subject to status, (you can check in the check out stage) and also pay in 3 is enabled in Paypal.

Take care.. have a lovely hot weekend and if anyone stresses you .. just smile, hold your palm face down and push gently away and say softly "sabar my friend"
I think you have worked out what it means.. be patient, be kind.
More news next week.

David

title: Lost in Bangkok
content_html:
Usually when in Bangkok I make a visit to Chatuchak market. According to reports the market has been flooded and so is closed, but I will go and see anyway.
There are lots of markets in Thailand but Chatuchak Weekend Market is the undisputed king of them all. It's big - it covers an area of 35 acres, contains more than 15,000 shops and stalls, has over 200,000 visitors each day . The range of products is huge - handicrafts, art, antiques, live animals, books, music, clothes, food, plants and flowers etc... the shoppers are locals and tourists but there are also many serious importers looking for deals. Lots of these shops double as the Bangkok showrooms for craft producers and gift manufacturers, so it's a great place to find suppliers. But there are problems.. many tourists claim to be importers to try and get good prices on "samples", so they may not believe you are a serious buyer. Some shops are just traders, not actually manufacturers so they bluff. The most serious problem is simply getting lost, finding a shop you have seen before might be impossible. Anyway all this is just part of the fun. In any event this is a pretty cool place to do business, hip bars and relaxing foot massage places are stumbled on and you often find strange colourful people who just want their photo taken. Here's a few pictures to give you a feel:


So assuming I survive - more reports next week.
Take care, happy trading.

title: By George, that's confusing
content_html:
Greeting from China. Where it is also very hot.
Last week I was telling you about the "Bad Lands of Java" you can read it here.
I believe it is a jolly time in the UK. What with the royal birth and all. Now I'm guessing half the males born this year will be Georges, and a good proportion of the girls will be Georgette also.
Can you imagine the classroom roll call in a few years time.
I just got back to China having been in Bali (and Java), whilst there discovered something about Bali names I never knew.
I'd noticed that high proportion of the people we work with there are called Wayan. I mentioned to Ringo (our agent there) how popular this name is. "Of course" he said "all first born men and women are called Wayan". After a little more questioning it turn out that most Balinese have one of four names. One name for the first born, another for the second born, another for the third and one for the forth. And, get this, if your the fifth, then you just start again with Wayan.
The name Wayan is derived from “wayahan” which means “the most mature.” The title for the second child, Made or Nengah, is derived from the word “madia” which means “the middle one.” Nyoman, the third child, is taken from the word “uman” which means “remains” or “last.” According to traditional Balinese belief, a family should only have three children. After the third one, parents should be wiser. However, many families have more than three children. As such, the fourth child, Ketut, means “little banana” or “the outer edge of a bunch of bananas.” This child is considered the “bonus” child. More than four children, the name cycle repeats itself.
To make it more complicated there are no sir names.. although modern Bali folk have taken to inventing one, and of course nick names are common. Our agent; Ringo is really called Nengah a second child. This system if I understand correctly is all wrapped up in the Hindu Balinese believe in reincarnation and that people are reborn again in the same families. On the way to the airport we passed a ceremony, lots smartly dressed people in the street having a very good time, laughing and singing. "Ah, said Ringo, looks like someone very important has died, it's a funeral". Turns out Bali funerals are happy occasions, you are only allowed to mourn for a day or two, beyond that they celebrate rebirth.
By George, so confusing.
More startling revelations news next week.
Until then.
Take care..

title: Goodbye Everybody
content_html:
greetings from a surprisingly warm Sheffield.

 

Last week I was telling you about the "Biggest we have ever seen" Calm down, it's not what you think.. it's a Shiva Lingam stone that arrived from India.. if you missed it you can read about it here.

It's all happening at once, almost Father's Day..on the 20th - so to all Fathers reading this - Happy Dad's Day.. this is your time.. nobody can stop you watching the footy.. 

On the 21st it's Solstice Day.. day of the hippies and druids.. longest day of the year.. and the day the sun stands still. It is the day when the sun reaches its northernmost position, before reversing its direction.

So it seems to me a good day to stand still, and think of all the stuff in our lives that need to start to change, and the day when those changes can start to be real. 

Also it is the 1st day of Summer! Happy summer folks.. 

 

So this is a good time.. The time has finally come.  It's been great being here, but now it is time to move on. So I must say goodbyes.. 


I'm leaving on a jet plane, don't know when I'll be back again..
Yes, by the time you read this I'm probably on the way to Spain, with a grand travel plan ahead. Being double jabbed definitely helps, but Brexit has made further hurdles to jump.. the 180/90 rule for third country nationals means I couldn't yet travel back to Spain as I have already burned up my 90 days.. But Mario, our man in Spain, managed to acquire me a visa of sorts - which I just hope Ryanair will recognise.. all being well I will be back in my house in La Cala de Mijas shortly.

 

The plan then is to spend two or three weeks working with Toni and the team at AW Artisan.. they have been rocking it recently, very busy.. so we need to make big plans to take them to the next level..

From there I will fly to Bratislava - to see the team at AW Gifts - last time I was there (heavens.. it was exactly two years ago) .. they had 8 employees, now there are 28 - so I have a lot of people to get to know. By then Tomas will be there, and we seriously need to make plans. Big plans. AW Gifts is Tomas's baby.. we are based in Trnova which is the hometown of Tomas.. It's certainly time to move to a new warehouse, so we will be checking out new locations.. our lease is coming to the end, and the warehouse now is stretched beyond capacity. So it should be really exciting and interesting..  

 

Then the plan is.. all things being equal.. (pandemic permitting) - I'll fly from Vienna via Amsterdam via Singapore to  Jakarta, Indonesia. I have a business visa, so should be able to access. In Jakarta will still need to self isolate for 5 days - then a domestic flight to the island of Bali.. where I'm sure our man in Indonesia; Ringo - will be waiting for me at arrivals.  It will be just over a year since I was there.. 

Demand for Indonesian stock has skyrocketed.. we have orders in with Ringo for 20+ containers - so there will be a massive job of work gearing things up in our warehouse there to cope. Should be exciting.. 

I'm so looking forward to seeing Ringo and the team there.. 

 

My visa is for 60 days.. but can be extended.. so we will see what happens.. Hopefully at some point it will be possible to go to China and finally see Coco (my wife) who you will know runs our China warehouse and purchasing office. If not then maybe Coco can come to Bali.. we will have to see what is possible by then.  I'd like to go to India and Nepal.. but it's not looking so good.. but as Coco would say.. "We will see what happen comes". 

 

So I hope you can come along with me (in spirit) for the ride.. I will be updating you as always every Friday..

 

Lot's of projects that I would have liked to have seen completed have not quite happened yet.. These days there are always delays, but nevertheless the excellent team here in the UK can and will make STUFF happen. 

Right now the joiners are banging away, making our new office space at Affinity Park come to life.. next time I hope to see it in operation.

 

Today is a tearful farewell - it's been an amazing time.. I have to go now, because I have lots of people to say goodbye to.

The Summer Solstice, day of change.. this travel blog.. will finally change and become an actual travel blog.. 

 

Take care, have a wonderful Father's Day weekend.

 

David

title: David's AW News: Getting High in Nepal
content_html:
Greetings from the Top of the World


Happy Mother's Day weekend. And special greetings from the top of the world. Wishing all Mothers reading this a wonderful Sunday with love and laughter.

Coco and I just arrived in Pokhara for a  short break and checked into the Rainiban Retreat. 
It's high up above the lake side city with breath-taking views of the Annapurna mountain range. Peaceful, quiet and still as it gets. 
We said our emotional goodbyes and left Toni on his own in Kathmandu. His Epic Asian trip is coming to a close, in a few days he will head back to Spain. We arrived in Pokhara by a short Yeti airways morning flight, just 30 minutes and spectacular mountain views landing at the infamous new International Airport (no international flights yet). From the airport we took a taxi through the city and then up a very steep mountain road, then off-road bouncing along a precarious track, the underside of the little taxi being crunched and scraped. "No problem," said our jolly taxi driver beeping to wakeup the staff as we approached our mountain retreat...
Last week I was telling you about arriving in Nepal with Toni and Coco joining us the next day flying in from China. If you missed it you can catch up here.


Here is the view from our room.

In Kathmandu we had a busy week, visiting our existing suppliers and seeking out some new ones. It was of course it was Toni's first visit to Kathmandu and the slightly manic wholesale area known as Thamel. It's a maze of narrow streets between ancient crumbling buildings and a traditional trading area. Since last time I was here it has had many more streets pedestrianised and more boutique hotels and cool restaurants opened. It's still a bit dodgy with drug dealers muttering as you pass by and scary looking dodgy dive club opening late at night. But here handicraft traders have showrooms, export agents and shipping companies work from upper floor offices. And all sorts of esoteric and exotic Nepali products find there way to gifts shops all over the world from Thamel.


Toni took to it like a dog to water.. navigating the alleyways making friends with traders and getting (a little over) excited at the variety of products being traded. All manner of brass items including singing bowls, incense, teas, beautiful and fun felt products, hemp fabric and much more. It's giftware heaven.
Our shipping agent, Mr Padam, an old school gentleman, whose office still sports a fax machine introduced us to some new traders, the ones that he knew well and were not simply middlemen. He took us to a small place hidden away in a back-street specialising in prayer flags. It was super busy and very well organised suppling all the giftshops, temples and monasteries in Kathmandu and a few exporters like us. We figure if you want to sell Singing Bowls and the like you need to get the look and feel right.. prayer flags are the answer to your prayers. Coming soon to AW.


Toni and I went to visit a felt factory on the outskirts of Kathmandu. The boss picked us up from our hotel and drove there explaining the complicated politics, the corruption, the reasons why most Nepal people are still poor. India and China tussle for influence, and dodgy deals abound at the top. But the ordinary people of Nepal are hard working, gentle and honest. He told us most dream of leaving for Australia or Canada where their hard work is apricated and they can send money home.


The suburbs are scruffy and disorganised, although the boss told us they have a mayor for the first time that seems to be improving things. He didn't have much hope he would last long in the job. 
The factory was spread-out over two large houses on three floors, each room focused on a different process or product. It was clean nice working environment and the mostly ladies working there were really happy to see us and certainly working hard. 


And making beautiful products. 

Meanwhile back in the UK..

With Mother's day upon us it's been pretty busy, but also our new Hop Hare products are causing quite a stir and flying out.
Easter is coming and so that's the next focus.. and of course the wedding season creates many opportunities for the wise giftware traders.
Plenty back in stock this week and some brilliant deals to keep your customers happy and you busy.

Namaste from Nepal.
More news next week.

David

title: Are creative people more kind?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain..

Welcome to December.. I hope you are starting to feel festive vibes..

Last week I was telling you about Weird & Wonderful Ubud, Bali.. and your latest venture into the decorative umbrella - or Balanese parasol - business.. If you missed it you can catch up here.
It has been a world-wind trip to Indonesia and yesterday I said goodbye to Ringo and the team and took my return flight with Korean airways back to Europe. 
Masks all the way, but delightful and charming staff. The chief purser in a formal suit, came and did a deep Korean bow, arms straight at the side bending from the waist.. Thank you Mr David for flying with us today. You don't get that on Ryanaire.. Seven hours from Denpasar to Seoul, 16 hours from Seoul to Amsterdam, then two hours or so down to Malaga with Ryanair.- with transit times almost 40 hours   
Coming home for Christmas... I'm a little frazzled and tonight in Spain we have an AW-Artisan christmas party.. Next week I will go to Sheffield.

Actually we have lots of projects underway in Indonesia - Raul was there last week, (our IT wizard from Kuala Lumpur) - and we are working on a potential new project that could revolutionise how you market your business.. but more on that later, let just say there could be interesting developments. Exciting times ahead.
As I was flying back to Europe, Bondan (Ringo's righ-thand man) flew to Java for meetings with some furniture companies  - another big project hopefully coming soon. It's all go. 


 Bondan is working on a range of folding teak furniture. He just sent me a video of his meeting with a guy very proud of how strong his stools of mini tables are..


Indonesia is where I have been making some things happen.. But all over Ancient Wisdom things are happening.. Tomas has been in our Slovakia company and traveling to Poland recently working on an exciting new partnership that hopefully will bring a whole new range of health supplements and the like to AW.  Our teams in the UK have been busy also - will report next week. Mr Chatterjee, our man in India has been out and about visiting craftware villages..
So you can see.. at AW we are always trying to innovate and create and serve our customers better. 

My thoughts for today on toxic people.
I love Indonesia because there are so many creative people.. who also tend to be gentle, kind and humble. People who create good vibes who are a pleasure to be around and make life generally better. The same kind of people can be found in India, in Europe, everywhere actually. Our kind of people at AW.. the people we choose to work with - suppliers, team members and customers.. are all creative and collaborative and kind.. making a better world.
Sadly though there are toxic people in the world.. (you know who you are) the non-creative who are happy to make money without creativity - not kind, not collaborative.. for whatever reason sometimes we find ourselves falling into their traps and having to deal with them. They can undermine creativity - disrupt mental health - destroy positivity. My advice: deal with the issues in the minimum time (or delegate to professionals) - turn away and celebrate the good and creative things.  Don't sweat bad stuff - I learned from my Balanese friends - don't get angry, don't stress, just turn your back to the toxic people and cut them from your life as much as possible. Karma will find them; you don't need to even care. I'm lucky to be surrounded by good and kind people.. I am grateful for this every day.

Light a candle today - think about creative positive things.. fresh ideas - just one good idea can change your life and the people around you for the better.. 
There is a lot to be said for lighting a candle, finding a moment of peace and letting go of things that depress your spirit - focus on joy and friends and creativity instead - allow the good to flow..

Speaking of Candles.. it's almost Christmas and Candles are a big part of Christmas - and beyond (Valentine and the season of love coming soon).. We have put together some special deals..
All things candles see below..

Also our showroom in Sheffield is open and ready for you to visit.. Rodrigo, Katka and team are taking bookings already.- they are excited to meet you.

Have a great weekend. Be creative, be kind, light a candle and find your great idea..
More updates next week.

David

title: Hero's Hiccups & Hope
content_html:
Greeting from Spain

 

It's all go at AW!  So much drama at AW. So much to report this week . Lots of happenings involving.. heroes, hiccups and hope - I have no idea where to start.

But first if you missed last week's newsletter about two grand announcements - an anniversary and a christening - you can read it here.

And our special Monday newsletter - 25 reasons to be Cheerful - you can read that here.

I'd just like to thank the hundreds of people who took the time to write congratulations to us for being 25 years old, and to Ben in Ireland for naming our new warehouse.

You are truly an amazing bunch of people, at AW we are proud to be part of this giftware..erm.. what are we? a club? a cult - heaven forbid?.. community I suppose but that word is too dry.

Lets use Ben's word; Affinity, when people have an affinity that's when they come together with a common purpose. So we are so happy to call our new distribution and HQ site in Sheffield - Affinity Park.

 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 66,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken. 

 

So here's a roundup of happenings at AW.

 

1. Katka and the lease of Affinity Park

This is more complicated than Brexit, if you have been following the story you might just follow this.  So we are in a warehouse that is being bought and will be rented to us by an American investment fund, they are buying the warehouse from an aerospace company for almost £8 million. That process is long and complicated, so we persuaded the nice people (who are selling it) to let us occupy the warehouse in the interim on a license.. So it's like a three way negotiation that has to conclude at a moment in time. Three sets of lawyers, a stressed out aerospace company, an American investment fund and a bunch of Yorkshire hippies selling incense and Buddah statues. I'm spending half the day juggling issues between them. 

Katka is due to meet the lawyer and sign (on behalf) of AW the lease today. Early next week the property will be sold to the Americans.. and Affinity will be officially our home for the next 10 years. 



2. Ringo is too hot  in Bali, Indonesia

So we gave our Indonsian agent a huge purchase order, so he has heaps of work to do. Only problem he has is it's unbearably hot there, they are sweating. I miss that heat. 

But I also learned that it is possible to get a business visa and travel via Jakarta back to Bali. There are rumours that the international airport in Bali might reopen in December, with strict double testing on departure and arrival to prevent covid coming. So a glimmer of hope. Ringo also need's a bigger warehouse.. I asked him to look into taking on the one next door, it's been empty a longtime. 



3. Coco's heroic idea and containers..

A couple of weeks ago I was telling you about the stress Bryant (our import manager) is having booking containers. And it's getting worse.. you might have seen the BBC reports. Even before Brexit, Felixtow port is in meltdown. There is a massive shortage of ships, but a thousand containers of PPE equipment getting priority, and half the workforce off isolating or down with covid. We are booking containers one day, and them just not turning up or getting cancelled the next.

But Coco, our China agent, came up with a partial solution.. Instead of us being the shipper, she could do that from her end, and being close to action to find and book herself.  She managed to book four containers yesterday and is loading the first today. So well done, but we still have to get them into the UK.  Stand by for huge shortages of stock in the coming months. 

Coco is also looking for a new bigger warehouse, ours is being converted to apartments next year. More news on this to follow.



4. Dusan and the Beast.

The Beast from France is in full swing.. back in Parkwood, Sheffield our aromatics factory got the soap making machine (we bought it from a French guy). First day we made 750 Greenman soaps - but day by day production is increasing. So soon plenty of soap soon back in stock. We are recruiting staff like crazy for the factory.. We need at least six more people.



5. Matej, our man in Slovakia.

He is definitely the biggest AW Hero. He is the manager at our Slovakia distribution warehouse. In his younger days he was a professional tennis coach in New York, today he is batting problem shots back over the net one after the other. Last week, one of the warehouse staff came down with Covid, all the warehouse guys had to isolate.  On that day a container arrived from Bali.. he unloaded with the help of one agency person. Normally a five man job.. and then went on to pick and pack orders. 



This week most of the office staff got track and trace messages to isolate.. just two people left.. and yet Matej found solutions to get most of the orders out. So Love all to Matej. 

 

I could go on and on.. more updates next week from around AW. 

 

But the next big thing to focus on I suppose is Black Friday.. approaching fast. Are you loaded and ready to roll? Lots of major deals below.

I don't want to panic you but it's worth stocking up if possible .. there will (it's unavoidable) be stock shortages coming..

 

Thank you for your support (as always), for being part of the AW story.. and being part of the AW affinity..

I'd love to hear your AW story, how AW has been part of your life, and business..  Ben was kind enough to share his story.  If you'd like to share yours please (if you have time) write to me.. directly if you like at david@ancientwisdom.biz, or reply to this email.

Special rewards to all those we reprint here, plus publicity, kudos, good karma and kindness points..

 

Take care..

 

 David

title: Fair Trade with Love
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield

I'm still at AW HQ and also spending time with the team at AW Aromatics - the aromatics factory. Or maybe it should be called the ideas factory, they are just bursting with ideas - so many new products in the pipeline. Of course not all will come to fruition but I can see that in the next few months exciting things are happening. 
Plus the move to our new factory and warehouse is going to happen soon, within two weeks we should have access to the warehouse area which means we will have enough space to pick and pack white label products for immediate dispatch. It's happening guys! AW-Aromatics.com  is your new secret source. It's all happening.. Just today we are launching a funky range of hand and body lotions. I have been testing the product and I can tell you I have the smoothest, softest skin and OMG.. I smell fabulous :). Of course as you would expect from AW they are free from Parabens, Sulphates and other nasties. Check below.
Today is Friday the 13th..  but Tomorrow is Fair Trade Day. I know which one I prefer. 

Fair Trade day.. who knew there was an awareness day for that? Of course everyday should be fair.. and at AW I don't like to blow our own trumpet too much.. but we have been trading fairly for over 20 years. I notice these days there is more awareness of climate change issues as well as treating artisans in developing countries fairly, check it out at Fair Trade Day.
Check our Indonesia products page.. Check our India Products page..  It's all fair trade. also our Cotton products page.. saving the planet since 1995.



I'm so excited because a container arrived from Indonesia full of the products I was working on a few months ago, if you are a regular reader of this newsletter you will recall my last visit to Java and Bali in Indonesia.
One product that we developed from scratch was Bee & Insect boxes, made with driftwood and eco-friendly albesia wood.
Also from the same family comes delightful garden bird boxes. 
It's from a nice family business in Sukawati not that far from our warehouse. Kadek is the boss, a very switched on lady and her husband is the artisan and creator.. we gave them the basic idea and over the space of a few weeks the samples were developed.. every now and then dropping off new designs at my hotel. Eventually we gave them a substantial order. That was November last year, this week we have some of the range (more on the way) in our warehouse in Sheffield and on sale.


This Kadek with the first attempt..

Unfortunately I don't have more pictures because they are a delightful smiley enthusiastic couple. Anyway the thing is I believe the deal was life changing for this family and together we made a product that your customers will love, and the bees and insects in their gardens will love, you will love it also.. it all good. What could be more fair trade?
See below.

It's all going on at AW.. I love it all.

Hope you have a lovely weekend - (free shipping to celebrate Fair Trade Day)

David

I notice these days there is more awareness of climate change issues as well as treating artisans in developing countries fairly, check it out at Fair Trade Day . Check our Indonesia products page.. Check our India Product s page.. It's all fair trade. also our Cotton products page.. saving the planet since 1995. I'm so excited because a container arrived from Indonesia full of the products I was working on a few months ago, if you are a regular reader of this newsletter you will recall my last visit to Java and Bali in Indonesia. One product that we developed from scratch was Bee & Insect boxes, made with driftwood and eco-friendly albesia wood. Also from the same family comes delightful garden bird boxes. It's from a nice family business in Sukawati not that far from our warehouse. Kadek is the boss, a very switched on lady and her husband is the artisan and creator.. we gave them the basic idea and over the space of a few weeks the samples were developed.. every now and then dropping off new designs at my hotel. Eventually we gave them a substantial order. That was November last year, this week we have some of the range (more on the way) in our warehouse in Sheffield and on sale. This Kadek with the first attempt.. Unfortunately I don't have more pictures because they are a delightful smiley enthusiastic couple. Anyway the thing is I believe the deal was life changing for this family and together we made a product that your customers will love, and the bees and insects in their gardens will love, you will love it also.. it all good. What could be more fair trade? See below. It's all going on at AW.. I love it all. Hope you have a lovely weekend - (free shipping to celebrate Fair Trade Day) David

title: David's AW News: I'm Sorry Mom / Visiting the loom ladies / SO ANGRY
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia. 


Where it is still raining everyday, but still beautiful.
Yesterday I spent time at the beach office, our digital marketing team workplace. I was a little bit surprised to see a warship floating just off the coast. I sent a picture to ChatGPT and it told me it was a Russian warship equipped with hypersonic missiles. It's a strange world we live in. Wheels turning not reported in western media, but Erdogan the Turkish president was in Indonesia. Last week when Bondhan and I flew back from Java, as we came into land our captain announced there had been VIP movements and that we and 15 other planes had been put into a holding pattern and for more than an hour we circled on high, coming into land so late I missed my appointment at the immigration office in Denpasar. (that's another story).
Presidents and warships in Bali.. big wheels turning.
Last week I was telling you about our trip to the mystical forests of the Genitri trees - where the natural beads known as the tears of Shiva originate - and doing business that we was warned could upset the Chinese and Indian mafia. If you missed it you can catch up here.

After that adventure, we drove back along the coast to Jogjakarta stopping off to see our giant statue supplier. Discussed adding more products, what do you think about life size dinosaurs? 
Can you sell these? You can find them in our drop shipping site, prices include UK mainland shipping. It's possible to earn £200 plus per sale. Check them out here.
Next stop Pekalongan
Then we crossed the island on the almost new motorway, eventually arriving at the small city of Pekalongan. This area is famous for textile production, with hundreds of small home industry type operations often specialising in a particular craft. We booked into the towns Aston hotel, always a safe and good standard hotel, like a Premier Inn in the UK. Except we were in for an interesting surprise. 
This hotel was a unique concept hotel, a Syariah concept hotel for strict pious religious types.. in practice this was 24/7 prayers piped to the lobby from the hotels mosque, in the lift, in the corridors and I discovered even in the room. There was like a dimmer switch by the bed where you could turn the sound down.. but not completely off. All night long that sound rattling around in my head, very strange. But the staff were delightful, couldn't do enough for us. The rooms were really high standard, even an AI assistant you could talk to in English and order room service, the hotel had a swimming pool and gym.. but of course strictly segregated. Other guests were wandering around in full religious dress with multiple wives in tow.  Interesting. Even Bondhan (who is culturally Muslim) said it was the strangest experience. 
Bondhan had lost his room key card and they charged us £5 for a new one.. but when we checked out this lady apologised and gave us back the money.. she said she was so happy to have a foreign guest in the hotel, and did I have any feedback. So smiley and nice, picture? yes no problem.

We spent two days with our supplier there, he already supplies us with Mandala Sarongs, and when we placed our order for the summer season 2025, he prompted him to open a new factory space. And invited us along to see the very first production item, considering it good luck to have a guest at the birth of production.
Me with the boss and two of his artisans, and the very first production pieces. Good luck guys!
We ordered a number of new items.. including some woven scarves, which he finished with dramatic colours in his home production. His son and an ex-con work in a upper room, skilfully producing artisan designs. 
His tattoo says "I'm Sorry Mum" - the boss told us he is a reformed bad boy and gave him a job. He was a nice guy taking great pride in his work, showing us the whole process. In a day they can make about 120 pieces. 
The boss was delighted, his face lit up when we told him we wanted to order because he said the village collective where he sources the woven material had no orders right now and desperately needed the business. Would we like to see? Yes of course.. lets go.

The Loom Village
We drove out of town to a village area, he explained that the village had five little loom shops, where all the ladies of the village worked. The head of the village received orders and distributed the business evenly around. He led us down a little alley way and an empty loom shop to show us what it was like.. Like nothing had changed in a hundred years, except now instead of cotton they weave with pine tree pulp rayon. Making a super soft and light material. 
After showing us the loom workshop, he took us to a little store and showroom, after a while lots of ladies started appearing. Then started to get excited and very jolly. Our guy had told them we had come to order and give them work. They all gathered around wanting to take pictures with me. One lady explained that in 50 years I was the first foreign person to come into the village and want to see the looms.  They were so grateful and happy to be given a chance.. a few days later they was already joyfully in production and the village head sent us videos of the production in full swing. 
I hope when the products finally arrive I guess by June or July you will support these ladies by stocking there scarves.

It's Outrageous!
Meanwhile, I learned something truly terrible.. did you know that TEMU sends to the UK alone around 1500 cargo planes a month?. The carbon footprint experts say is 100 times that of goods sent by shipping container. And the goods are sent using a tax and standards loophole known as the "de minimis loophole". They pay no import duty! And no taxes! Yes TEMU's parent company, PDD Holdings, is headquartered in Ireland for international operations, which means that UK revenues are processed through Ireland rather than being taxed directly in the UK. 
Do the maths and I figure they are stealing around 15-20% of your sales. Thus reducing your profits and the taxes you would have paid on the.. a double whammy for the exchequer. It's not just taxes, Trading Standards give us ridicules hoops to jump through almost every week something new.. whilst TEMU and the like can literally fly 777's around those standards.

  • 100x Carbon Footprint 
  • Billions of your lost sales & our taxes  
  • Dodgy substandard totally uncontrolled goods in the hands of our children. I'm mean WTF!!!

I got myself so angry I started a petition.. maybe if enough people sign.. we can get some publicity and get something done. Here in Indonesia, they banned the app almost as soon as it launched here. Other countries also stopped it or tariff taxed it. Slow and dopy Britain.. needs to wake up and act fast. PLEASE SIGN MY PETITION  Tax TEMU protect UK traders.

OK calm down.. I need to do some breathing exercises and a touch of Yoga.. 

Gift of the Year!
Delighted that one of our products has made the final of Gift of the Year..
Although I can't believe our Hop Hare products didn't make it also.. in my humble opinion much better than other finalists.. 
So while you are in a signing things frame of mind.. PLEASE ADD YOUR VOTE.. Thank you so much!
Today I believe is the last day of the Double Discount Launch offer.. on Glass Candle Holders. Nice Mother's Day gifts..
Don't miss out..

Wishing you a lovely stress free relaxing weekend.
More news next week. 

David

title: Lockdown Bali Style
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

Hope and pray that you are well and safe.
Last week I was telling you about Tomas and I in Bali, a lot has happened since then. You can read last weeks news here.
Tomas managed to get the very last Emirates flight out of here.. he was stranded in Dubai 16 hours but finally made it to the UK on Tuesday.. since then he is self-isolating in Sheffield.
My plan was to finish the jobs here and then try to get a flight route to China (although very hard) - now this morning the announce no foreign people allowed to enter, not even with quarantine. 
So looks like I am self-isolating in Bali. These are truly terrible and testing times for all of us.  

Mr Chatterjee is in total lock down in India, if you follow this newsletter you will know that Tomas and I was there just a few weeks ago.. not a mask in sight. Coco in China sent a carton of masks and sanitiser by DHL to Mr Chatterjee, only to have it returned when all flights were cancelled. Raul is in enforced lock down in central Kuala Lumpur, with the army paroling the empty streets below his apartment. He's slowly going nuts he tells me.. 

It was heartwarming to see the support for our NHS staff on Thursday, they were even talking about it here. Today's super hero's if you ask me. In the UK we are still trading.. and trying to do it as safely as possible - everyone that can work at home is doing so.. those that have to be in are taking all measures.. they are our hero's - and for now we are confident the measures we are taking keep our staff as safe if not safer at work than home. Your orders might be a little delayed because we have the absolute minimum in at any one time, Tomas is working from home to minimise the numbers further so that people can have large chunks of space to themselves whist they work. Mostly what we people are ordering soaps.. and essential oils and atomisers (do they help?) . And I guess all for on-line stores.. Our relatively new (thank you Raul) drop-shipping website is proving to be a godsend for many of our customers enabling them to stay in business and keep afloat.
I spend every evening until the early hours talking to our people.. and working out how best to handle this. Katka, Tomas and I have a daily conference on-line..  Katka at HQ is doesn't like to be publicly praised.. but she is handling levels of stress way beyond the call of duty.

It's a fact that of all the places in the world Bali is uniquely placed to organise a lock-down, they already have police departments for it, trained and organised volunteer force in place, and a complete set of recognised and respected rules. You may have heard of Nyepi - It's Bali's New Year. Every 210 days according to their calendar is a complete day of silence - a spiritual day of reflection.. airport, roads are closed, everyone must stay at home and reflect. So it's same as a lock-down right?  It was on Wednesday, the night before parades and parties all cancelled but the quiet day went ahead.. with one last-minute amendment... it would last for two full days not one, and that further instructions would follow. It seemed to me a smart move.. already a total lock-down.. extend it and then extend it more (with allowances for going out for food and stuff) until like Malaysia a virus halting lock-down is imposed. But alas rumours that it would be extended, were fake news and today (Friday) Ringo and I were allowed out to finish of a few jobs, however, the place is like a ghost town. Everything is closed.
Now who knows what will happen.. looks like I'm stranded here.. I have been one step ahead of the virus in Spain, UK, Malaysia, India.. finally like all of us it is catching up with me.  

I know you all have your own sets of problems right now.. I'm praying that soon things will improve. But please please don't relax being careful.. stay at home if you can.. wash your hands now.
Take care, be kind and be careful.

Updates next week

David

title: David's AW News: Help! I've Been Kidnapped
content_html:
Greetings from Trnava, Slovakia


Yep, I'm back at our EU office and warehouse: AW-Gifts.eu. Actually I had planned to stay in the UK until after Christmas, but everyone kept on asking me to attend the AW Slovakia Christmas party.. Tomas had gone there already and I pointed out there were no flights available and made my apologies.. But Katka, found a (convoluted) route.. and booked it and told me I had no choice.. So you see I have been kidnapped and taken to Slovakia.

The Kidnap Trip.
Yesterday morning I was forced to wake-up at 5am. Katka and her husband Phillipe, were waiting for me.. Philippe kindly drove us to East-Midlands airport. Where we took a Ryanair flight to Prague. I can't say I really enjoyed it.. East-Midlands airport is a dump, they have better airports in the wildest parts of India. Speedy boarding basically meant we had the privilege of standing outside in the cold, dark and drizzle waiting for the incoming plane to off board. On the plane we were actually shouted at to listen to the safety instructions or not be allowed to fly. Thankfully it's not a long flight, but in Prague airport there was only two or three people stamping passports and huge backlog of people waiting.. and in our line the guy was moving at a snail pace, taking two minutes per person.. We had to catch a train to Slovakia, and started to think we might miss it. Eventually after about an hour they opened more booths and things started moving.. Katka (who is Czech) asked why there was so few people working, and was told because everyone was working from home today.


Waiting to enter the Czech Republic.
Last week I was telling you about coming home for Christmas - back in Sheffield.. and meeting with our amazing team.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

In other news we finally got the new sign put up at the UK office.. there is a long story behind this, maybe for another day. 

Last Saturday was the UK Christmas party.. the theme was 1970's and everyone except me was dressed up as hippies and glam rockers from the 70's.. Since that's my authentic era.. I came as myself:).. 
It was fairly wild and good fun was had by all and I think it was a big success..

     Tomas Katka and me.. 

 This Saturday it's the Slovak Christmas party.. that's why I have been kidnapped.

So once we got through Prague airport, things improved dramatically.. Katka had organised a nice car and driver to whisk us to the train station.. a happy chap who was keen to show us his city. Prague is an iconic city, and very friendly - it's a few years since I was last here with Coco and it brought back memories. We got to the train station with time to spare for lunch and happened on the most amazing restaurant, built in an old bank with decorative high ceilings, delightful staff and authentic Czech food. Katka was so happy to be eating the traditional food of her childhood. I love it too. 


Prague train station.
 After lunch we ambled into the train station found North platform 5, just as our train rumbled into view. A little bit old fashioned, Katka had booked us a business carriage, leather seats and a glass of fizz included. Very Orient Express.. we was able to work and chat for a few hours.. while we trundled our way across the Czech Republic over the border to Slovakia and eventually arrived at Trnava station at 8pm. A friendly host brought snacks and good wine, and time passed in a very pleasant way.. Travel Regiojet trains.. it's the total opposite of Ryanair, slow & relaxing not fast & stressful... I have never been in the train station in Trnava and yet it seemed very familiar, I instinctively knew where to go..  I realised it was the exact same layout and design as the train station in Yiwu, China. Some communist connections there.
Matej our man in Trnava was waiting at the station and took us the hotel.. It seemed like a long day travelling, all good fun but exhausting. I slept like a log.

This morning it is an absolute delight to see the awesome team in at AW-Gifts.eu  - organised and efficent to the next level.. we had the tour of the office and warehouse. 
Erica and Matej our managers here have worked for AW-Gifts.eu since day one and over the years seen us grow and thrive. Katka was there at the beginning helping to establish the original team. We started out in june 2017, those six and half years have passed in a blur.. and from scratch they have become established as one of Europe's main gift
wholesalers. 


Well done guys (the original team).

Toni (from Spain) is also here in Slovakia. The planning for the spring sourcing trip for Toni and I is ongoing.. day by day, new meeting set up, hotels booked, flights booked and a strategy for the product groups we want to focus on this time round. If you have any suggestions or ideas please feel free to email me directly. We will be in Indonesia, Nepal, India and China.. Last time we focused on Singing Bowls and  accessories, Incense and next level aromatic products, Crystals, Gemstones and Esoteric products. And I feel that we (don't like to brag but) we have become wizards in these areas.. adding to your specialist list of products any one of which would make excellent Pop-up Shop ranges. Now there's a thing.. Pop-up shops are trending more than ever - are you opening them? I'd love to hear from you..

So another week another AW Christmas party.. yes I have been kidnapped - but it's not all bad..
Full report next week. 

Christmas is coming.. and it's still busy.. we are working hard to despatch all your orders as quickly as possible.
Hope you are finding trading good and all is well with you.

Have a magical wonderful festive weekend. 

David

title: David's AW News: It's Christmas Pizza!
content_html:
Greetings from a very blustery Sheffield

 

It's the last day at work at AW, and I'm back from my quick trip to Slovakia in a wet and windy Sheffield at our HQ. If you missed that story last week you can catch up here.



The Christmas market in Slovakia..

Tomas, Katka and me.. enjoy mulled wine in Trnava..

Driving to work this morning in Sheffield, I was dodging empty wheelie bins blowing in the road and fallen branches.. arriving at work feeling a bit like the end of the world, not just the end of the year..

 

Yesterday news was filtering in.. there is a shipping problem, all the containers we have on the way or about to be loaded are being hit with a $3000 contingency charge.. and potentially long delays. 

Heck if it's not one thing it's another.. and yet..

 

It's officially Christmas and like you and your family, at AW UK we have our Christmas traditions on the last day.. and nothing.. the windy weather or shipping crisis will stop our last day Christmas traditions..

We have a pizza party, the pizza gets delivered from Domino pizza - everyone gathers in the office. We play Christmas songs and wish each other the best for Christmas and the New Year.

Everything will be left spick and span, clean and tidy, all the orders sent, desks cleared, everything organised and ready for a fresh start in 2024. The Pizza has been ordered.. I'm in AW-Aromatics.com right now.. when the pizza arrives I'll give a little speech and wish everyone all the best.. then head across town to Affinity Park and AncientWisdom.biz  our HQ.. for the pizza party there.. 


All around AW..

In the Spain office (AWArtisan.eu) they will be playing  Feliz Navidad  .. they have different holidays to the UK, but will still be joining the party.. 

In Slovakia (AWGifts.eu) they have their own version of Jingle Bells, here in the UK I think we will be playing Fairytale of New York.. Ringo and the Team in Indonesia, Coco from China, Mr Chatterjee from India.. all wish you heaps and heaps of season's greetings.. 

 

Whatever your Christmas traditions are.. myself and everyone at AW - WISH YOU A WONDERFUL CHRISTMAS and truly peaceful and happy New Year. 

We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your support and trade during 2023.. and we wish you great success and many adventures and 2024 may it be an exciting and fulfilling year.

 

I'm off for a slice of pizza and good cheer..

See you next year..


David

title: Bol Bam & other Madness
content_html:
Hi 
Last week I was telling you about my trip over the Hump and arrival in Kolkata, India. You can read it here.
After arriving and recovering from the overnight flight at a good hotel near the airport, our supplier picked me up and we drove out of Kolkata over the Hooghly bridge and onto the old GT highway along the banks of the Ganges river. This year the monsoon has failed to come and everything is sticky and hot, the river is like chocolate, flowing languidly odd lumps here and there breaking the surface. I'm here to buy jute, a new range from a new supplier and his office and factory is in a town really at the back of beyond.
Today it turns out is Independence day. Shrines of Indian flags have sprung up, cars are sporting pendants, TV's are all switched to the big-wigs big speeches. 65 years on, and India has changed, boy has it changed. Except that is.. in this sleepy backwater I have found myself in. As far as I can see nothing has changed.
Yards from the river, tiny lanes, shops in holes in the wall, draped wires, stand pumps where people wash, wandering cows and runaway chickens. Nothing is new, a stone carving over an arch tells me it was built in 1952. The place has a feeling of madness about it. On the way here we'd passed several naked holy men and a old lady made up like a tart and topless. "Mad", confirmed my contact sagely each time.
I'm taken to a first floor office, where I'm left alone while my man goes to find his business partner. Outside I can hear Hare-krishna type chanting and tambourines. I open a low balcony door to see what is happening, and find myself looking down on a dead body held aloft on a stretcher by four bearers, a small retinue of musicians follow. The blackened head of a young girl lolls back and forth almost at my feet. I close the door recoiling in horror. Later we walk down the lane to the crematorium. Relatives sit in circle chatting while the body is burned on a pyre. After the ashes will be scattered in the Ganges beyond. Death is the main industry, thanks to the sacred river in town.
I have spent three days here, developing some new products and got to know some of the people. They are dignified and intelligent, thoughtful and kind. And to a man, eccentric as they come. The place is poor but without the squalor you often see in India. No beggars, no-one asked me for money and folks only showed me kindness. I took heaps of pictures to try and capture a feel for the place..
Here are some.
Apart from Independence it was some special festival called Bol Bam, I was taken to see. At this special place on the banks of the river people come to do the Bol Bam. This involves swimming in the river, filling two plastic pots with sacred water, and then walking 35 kilometres bare foot, with the pots hanging on a pole across your shoulders in the stinking heat to a particular shrine where you pour the water over Shiva. Hundreds of people do it every year. Madness I pointed out to my man. Surely the gods would rather you did some good for a fellow human than this. He told me when he was young he'd done it, and it took him three weeks to recover his health. But I pondered maybe superstitions run high, when life offers little else.
The communist party ran the place in to the ground for many years - that's my assessment anyway. Recently voted out of power, maybe things will change. I hope it does, maybe our business will help in some small way. But you have a feeling that when it does an old way of life will have been lost.
More news next week.
Take care and enjoy this Bank Holiday weekend
David
