title: David's AW News: Holes, Bowls and a Big Beautiful Launch!
content_html:
Greetings from heatwave Sheffield. 


I hope you are finding time to enjoy the beautiful weather here in the UK.. I'm so lucky to be here at this time.. but so busy.
It's been a crazy, mad, crazy week. The main focus has been the launch of the new big beautiful dropshipping website.. full honest update below.
Last week, I was telling you about how we almost lost our shipment of Full Moon Singing Bowls from Nepal.. and how our man James tracked them down and recovered them. If you missed it, you can catch up here..
We are so happy to get them back, our new social media girl, Holly.. enthusiastically got into the world of Singing Bowls (including the Full Moon Bowls).. and made an info YouTube video for your enlightenment, entertainment and inspiration...  actually, Singing Bowls are a booming (pun intended ) business.. lovers of singing bowls - that includes me.. are obsessed with them.. will pay big money for the more exotic bowls and spend hours practising to make the spine tingling sounds. We have an excellent range.. retail from £25 to £300. Check out the video..
They will look amazing in your shop.

Hole in the Road in Bali.
Bali, with its flashy beach clubs and huge tourism.. sometimes we forget it's still an underdeveloped country.. with barely functioning infrastructure.. This week, a sinkhole appeared on the main road on the northern side of the island, the road that brings heavy trucks, including empty 40ft containers on the way to our warehouse for loading.
And they tell me there is no other route that can accommodate a 40ft container trailer. It will take up to three weeks to fix the road, even though according to the local news, they will work 24 hours a day.. and just when we have three container loads of stock ready for loading. I can't help thinking there must be some other solution.. This means stock for Christmas will come later than expected..

AW-Dropship.com, the Big Beautiful Website you will grow to love.. 
So here in the UK.. everyone has been hands on.. working like crazy.. Plus Dev guys in Bali working long hours, Raul the IT wizard pulling all nighters..
A massive effort from the team.. Well done, guys!!  

It happened we had a soft launch of the NEW Drop-Shipping site.. API's are working for Shopify, Ebay, WooCommerce and manual uploads.. 
And of course, lots of things went wrong.. and our amazing customers stepped in with huge amounts of feedback.. as we find glitches, we are fixing them.

THANK YOU GUYS for the super helpful constructive feedback - it's been amazing, this is a real team effort.. with you, our customers an important part of the team.

We are still having some issues with the Ebay API.. but hopefully we will fix it shortly..
Head over the aw-dropship.com and check it out.. NOW is the time to get on board, there are thousands of retailing opportunities.. with a little imagination, you can start a new business this weekend! 

And stand by.. As soon as all the bugs are ironed out, we will bring you some spectacular early bird deals. 

Meanwhile..we have some brilliant deals below. 

Take care, enjoy the sunshine 

More news next week. 

David

title: Joyful reunions in Asia
content_html:
Greetings from Kuala Lumpur

Yes I'm back in Asia, and back in KL for the first time since the pandemic struck.
Last week I was telling you about the return to Istanbul, where I met up with Tomas and we pursued quite a few interesting new products. I was telling you about the best backers restaurant in Istanbul.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Tomas stayed for a few more days, but I had to leave to meet up with Mr Chatterjee and his son (our India agents) in KL.
I was writing last week's news just before departing.. I'm writing now just before departing for Bali.

Turkish Airways are pretty good, I would recommend them. And the flight from Turkey to KL is only 10 hours or so. There was a tropical storm at KL airport and the landing was dramatically aborted at the last second. The captain pulled out of the landing and roared upwards at an alarmingly steep angle. Finally he came on the tannoy and apologised that adverse tail winds had forced us to abort. I can tell you that in the meantime there were some concerned faces in the cabin. Thoughts of hijacking or something else.. 

Anyway after the drama I was happy to see Mr Sugar, my regular KL taxi driver waiting for me at gate 6.  How are you? How is your family? Great to see you sir! A reunion.. but not the last.
On Saturday Mr Chatterjee and his son Dishtanta arrived via Airasia from Kolkata.. along with excess luggage stuffed with product samples, plus a carton had arrived via DHL to our hotel. 
I was delighted to see them after more than two years. Another joyful reunion..
It was their first visit to Kuala Lumpur (Dishanta's first out of India) and they were wide-eyed and excited to see this very modern tropical city.  I suggested we have Sunday off and take Mr Sugar's city tour and see the city like a tourist. I have been to KL more times than I can remember but never been to the Batu Caves or seen the Royal Palace. 
Mr Chatterjee particularly liked the Batu caves because it is actually a major Hindu shrine, at the top of 272 steps and inside a huge cavern. Not many tourists here but lots of Indians on pilgrimage. Some barefoot, walking the stairs, some shave their heads and apply a layer of henna.. strange. We climbed the stairs in 35c heat and humidity with hundreds of monkeys playfully leaping around.. which I suppose is also strange behaviour. 
In the 27 months since I have been here, a couple of things have changed.. lots more street art in the old Chinatown area, and new buildings including the stupendous Merdeka 118 building, which dwarfs the other skyscrapers.. It's officially the second tallest building in the world. It can be seen from everywhere in KL..

Huge tower, Entrance to Batu caves and Mr Chatterjee with street art.
I was also happy to see Raul again and see his cute daughter - now two years older and twice as cute.
Most of the last week though has been spent holed up in Mr Chatterjee's room checking samples, calling suppliers, tweeking designs and negotiating. In the end I think we have placed orders for about three container loads of new products, some of which I'm very excited about - I think you will love what's coming.

Mr Chatterjee was upset. Beyond angry. A shipping company had stitched us up, here's what happened:
A container had been despatched to Mumbai docks, on the invoice and shipping documents you have to quote the total weight of the goods, the containers get weighed and if within 1000kg then no problem. Chatterjee had carefully checked all the paperwork and submitted everything in duplicate, some dipstick in that shipping office (the same one that is charging us) had made a typo and entered 240,000 kg instead of 24,000kg and the container was stopped for examination. The inspector didn't turn up for 4 days.. that's $200 per day rollover ferr, change of weight fee $600 plus a long list of other rubbish charges. $3,500. Of course Chatterjee complained a lot.. but the shipping company basically has us over a barrel, pay or the container stays portside racking up more charges by the day. Pure extortion, and massively unjust. Angry is not the word.

Now this is not an isolated incident. Everyday we are getting stitched up by unscrupulous middlemen, it's like an epidemic of dodgy practices.Tomas spends half his life arguing with agents, as does Toni in Spain and Bryant in the UK. It's very stressful, poor Tomas really is losing his hair over this. I'm sure those of you that import or export are experiencing this.. it's almost as if the mafia has taken over.  Tomas, Toni and Bryant tell me the same kind of stories. At the end of the day  the price of the products increase because of it adding to inflation.. Oftentimes it is dodgy agents, other times over zealous government officials determined to disrupt imports. It's a serious problem. I'm not sure what the answer is?

Sorry to rant..

The really good news is I managed to acquire a business visa for Coco (my wife) to visit Indonesia and also managed to secure one of the rare seats on a plane from Guangzhou to Denpasar Bali via KL.  
Lot's of things could go wrong.. allsorts of rumours about Chinese officials discouraging outside travel... but fingers crossed we could be having a reunion soon.
I'll keep you posted.

More good news, our amazing girl Lenka, who was our customer service advisor for over 4 years and now is Agnes and Cat account manager, will be off on maternity leave. AW team across the globe wishes her good luck. If you want to pass on your wishes you can email her on ondrisovalenka@gmail.com

Next week's news from Bali.

David

title: Is Creativity The Key To Wealth?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Happy Mother's Day weekend! It might not be a usual Mother's day, but at least we have Zoom and Whatsapp. So all the best to Mum's everywhere.

 

Hope you guys are well and thinking positive thoughts.

Last week I was telling you about beating the bully - and I told you a shocking story about how some people try to control markets.. you can read it here.

That story really touched a nerve and hundreds of people wrote in support of our actions, some with long (and interesting) stories of similar abuses. I'm sorry guys I can't answer you all..

I also told you I would explain my plan this week on how you (and AW) can fight back and make the world a fairer place.


But first an update on the backflow trademark issue.. I have been in contact with some fellow importers/wholesalers who are also upset that anyone could try to hijack a market like this, and so we got legal advice. The lawyer is very confident that the trademark is not legal so is taking the action needed to block it, meanwhile we will reach out to this black marketing company to try and resolve things amicably. The massive moral support we have received from all corners of the gift trade will definitely add weight to the case.. so hopefully this thing can be sorted. Thank you everyone for your help and support.

 

But in a way I can see the problem this guy has.. he was, after all just trying to protect his market. 

 

Here is a sad but common story..

Say you trade from a gift shop in a small market town, and build up a good trade in (for example) dinner candles.. a nice range of colours and accessories and you have amazing candle gift packs and your display is super attractive.. you put a lot of work in and over the years sales creep up nicely. Then the shop at the other end of town see's your success and basically copies everything.. and a tiny bit cheaper. Sales drop off the cliff.. That's so annoying, what can you do? Well it's annoying but normal.. the good way to respond is to do the job better, go upmarket, stock better colours and designs, be more friendly. Or just look for other products to develop.. The bad way is to send your cousin Vinny to threaten to smash in this guy's windows if he doesn't stop selling them.. Because this is against the law. More sneaky but not nice or moral would be to bad mouth your competitor, lobby the council/landlord/supplier to change the rules somehow.. or I guess get a dodgy lawyer to send him a fake scary legal letter.. but this just leads to bad blood, and bad karma.

But it could be even worse than this..

Imagine how annoying it would be if that competitor had access to all your customers details, and all your different product sales performance. They could really take full advantage of all your hard work.

 

Yikes!! That would be bad.. but this my friend is happening already, right now, right under your nose in broad daylight..  if you trade on any of the major retail trading platforms (you already know the worst offender I'm sure). This is exactly what happens.

If you find a great niche market on Amazon (for example), don't be surprised if the competitor who steals your trade, undercuts you and has better visibility is...  actually Amazon.. a few years back Amazon made a huge effort to buy directly from AW.. We said but we don't do retailing and compete with our customers, their argument was in this case it would be Amazon buying just like any other retailer. But it didn't feel good. In the end I stopped the project, before it really got going.

 

There is an answer.. and it involves a little hard work and investment.. but the upside can be huge and almost limitless.. It's called Branding.. Own your own Brand and you have a lot more control over the market. If you can develop trust and goodwill in your brand, if your brand has some unique properties, if your brand is pretty cool or quirky.. maybe you can even charge a premium.   

As long as you control the Brand that you develop (not just appropriate it like our blackflow friend) then you have control.. and who knows if it is very successful the brand will have a value of it's own - you can possibly sell the brand in the future.

 

So the question is are you CREATIVE? This is the question? Everything else can be subcontracted out.. design (to a degree), manufacturing / importing, distribution even marketing and sales.

But the creative spark is what creates something new, and that ultimately is what creates (good, honest and ethical) wealth.

 

So if you are a creative person, listen up. Things are changing at AW, and we might be part of your plan.

 

After the fire last July.. we moved the distribution part of AW to Affinity Park, a big 100,000 square foot distribution warehouse just across town. The aromatics factory of AW we left in our remaining warehouse, and have been working hard to expand it using all the 15,000 square feet we have left there.. As a customer of AW you will know how hard it is to keep up with production of our own items, but now we are investing a lot in expanding..and going hell for leather. Soon we will even out grow that space.. 

Well the good news is the 35,000 square foot warehouse that burned down is in the process of being rebuilt (even bigger), our amazing landlord Keith has been doing a valiant job and expects to finish rebuilding it a few months ahead of schedule. So we have the opportunity to expand exponentially when that space becomes available. 

 

Check out: AW-Aromatics.com  it's new and not yet fully functional. But it will be the portal for Branded products. Soon any products you develop with us with your own brand will appear here (for your eyes only when you log in) - and you can order just the same as at AW. Alternatively we will have a range of "White Label" products that you can order and brand up yourself, if you enjoy that kind of work. 



I wanted to give you the heads up - basically our capacity has to be shared fairley.  We already have a few branding partners we trade with and the factory supplies AW UK and AW in Europe. Because of capacity issues, for a while we can expand but eventually we will need to limit the number of branding partners. We are open now for registration, if you register we can keep you updated as the plan comes together.  

 

Then.. I hear you ask.. so I make a product, with my own brand.. How do I distribute it? Especially if I don't have a chain of shops..

So check out: AW-Dropship.com  - from our distribution warehouse of course. Soon you will be also able to add your own products to our dropshipping platform. Also in the future you will be able to ship your products to our EU distribution warehouses and using Dropshipping there: AW-Dropship.eu (Eastern & Central Europe) and AW-Dropship.es (Spain, Portugal & France) 

 

Here is a graphic that kind of explains the possibilities. 



Anyway that's enough excitement for one newsletter..

Hope you have a wonderful Mother's Day.

 

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: Crazy Journey!
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Wishing you a Happy May Day Weekend.. hope you are both busy and enjoying the weather!

Wow! I just landed after a crazy journey from Goa to Yiwu.  Feeling a little battered.. not sure why. 
It's crazy that the two most populous nations on earth, who are also neighbours, have zero direct flights. And to make it worse, there are hardly any convenient connecting flights.

So on Tuesday afternoon, I took a taxi to Goa Dabolim airport with Mr Chatterjee, he took a flight to Kolkata me to Bengaluru (Bangalore) - we said our goodbyes - Mr Chatterjee, emotional as usual. I stayed overnight at a local hotel and the next morning caught a flight to Kuala Lumpur.  It's the first time I have flown from Bangalore's newish International terminal, I was very impressed. The city is known as the Garden City, and the terminal is an extraordinary garden with a huge hanging flower bed and what seems like a river running through.
Gardeners have to work in the sky.
In Kuala Lumpur, I had an 8 hour connection for my China Southern flight to Guangzhou, 2 hour connection to Yiwu. Actually, this 2 hour connect was not stressful because the transfer terminal was completely empty, only me. Something very strange in China. I arrived in Yiwu on Thursday at 10am, and Coco was waiting for me with the grandchildren and Tuan-Tuan, a new family addition, a pet dog.
Tomas is already here.. He left on a flight from Budapest at the same time I departed Goa, and somehow arrived one day before me.  

More Hard Core.
Last week I was telling you about our Hard Core India experiences - if you missed it, you can catch up here.
Before we left Delhi, we made a trip to Paharganj, the backpacker, trader area and all round chaos zone. Lots of gift traders venture here to do their first India export trade, but this really is a buyer beware zone, we (or I) made a few mistakes here. Yes, for sure you can do business here, but in these days of massive compliance and standards - be very careful. I'm planning to make a YouTube video explaining all the things that can go wrong and how to avoid them. Join the channel here if you want to know the trade secrets.

Mad Honey part 2
Toni and I had finally finished the Nepal - India leg, a lot of hard work (hard work and non-stop), so I figured it was time to relax a little, we took the Mad Honey we had acquired in Kathmandu to our regular beach shack.. and tried it out. It was light hearted fun.. spoiler alert nothing discernible happened, but we made a fun YouTube short anyway.
Part two here.

So I just arrived last night in China.. 
Tomas, Coco and I went to the main market to catch up with a few suppliers.
It was really interesting.. I'm making a YouTube video about it.. Trump tariffs are upending the market. But maybe Trump is underestimating how much the China suppliers depend on American trade, it's a big world and lots of other markets are growing rapidly. 
Tomas and Coco - ready for action.
On our first day - I can tell you we already found some super interesting products, at prices hard to believe, so I think we will be bringing you next level goods soon..
Full report next week.

Meanwhile, back in the UK..
Lots and lots of new stock pouring into our warehouse. May is going to be awesome.. stick around for some major retail opportunities.
And I'm so excited to see our Nomad Sari T-shirt online.. these are from Nepal, double stonewashed, cotton and with mandala style designs with hidden details..
It's not fast fashion! These have been in the pipeline a long-time.. Great for the warm weather, and make all your customers look like seasoned rather cool travellers. 

Anyway.. so busy here - no Bank Holiday weekend for us.. too much to do.
Enjoy your weekend!! 

Take care.. more news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Good News & The Goddess
content_html:
Greetings from  Malaga, Spain 

There are a lot of Banging of Drums this week, hope you can forgive me.

I'm writing this from the AW-Artisan.eu office.. where everything is in full swing. 
A container just arrived from Indonesia, and all the team were here very early in the morning, before sunrise.. to unload it. 


Yes, a pre-dawn container..
Here in Spain it has never been so busy.. fresh stock arriving and orders flowing out.. the team (MFT) are literally running around like crazy to keep up.
The container unloaded the old fashioned way, because unlike UK and Slovakia warehouses we don't have container docking bays.. it's hard work. But they still managed to dispatch a record number of orders the same day.
With one thing an another.. lots of new customers recently.. We are really going to have to face up to the fact we need a bigger warehouse in Spain as soon as possible. 
Last week I was telling you about our trip from Bali, to Jakarta to Istanbul to Malaga.. not as stressful you might think.. if you missed it you can read about it here.

My wife Coco is here.. and the good news to share is that she was granted Spanish residency.. in a couple of weeks she will get a TIE card giving right to remain in Spain.. which is amazing.. we went to our local chiquito for a fish lunch to celebrate... and other things have been resolving also - it seems to have been a week of good news.


We have to thank our man in Spain Mario and his assistant Laura, who put in a lot of hardwork and organising to make it happen. Thanks Guys!

Meanwhile in the UK an Indonesian container also just arrived.. and lots of amazing new products are coming online..
I really don't like to bang our own drum too much.. but in this case I feel I have to.. because the Shamanic drums arrived.. with unique designs to AW making them not only a great gift, but we put a lot of work into finding actually good sounding drums.. all carefully approved by Bondhan, our musical guy in Bali.


Also arrived this week (in the UK) is a new range of ceramic vases, made on Lombok Island and finished artistically on Bali.  Some really cool designs with a hole in them. Do-nut vases are (I'm told) on trend.. 
Also just came in time for the winter season .. Indian Boho Scarves.. and I'm happy to report that they are selling really well, stock up now while we have stock guys. I believe they are really good value for the quality. Not exactly high end fashion, but every world traveller can throw on this kind of scarf to look cool. I have my own collection. 

I just realised we were working on the Drums and Ceramic Vases at the same time we started work on the AW-Advantage.com Digital marketing office back in February / March. Tomas is still there with the team.. and it's another product that can help your business and is just launching now.. we are able to take on a few clients.. Banging the Drum again.. we have an amazing team there.. really keen, talented and motivated.. they would love to chat..


If you want a team to bang the drum for your business.. Check them out here.

Talking of India.. Mr Chatterjee is celebrating the famous local festival of Durga Puja.. I have been there at this time.. it's amazing. All the streets are turned into a living festival of Indian Gods and especially the Goddesses....


There is a lot of banging of drums and chanting and herbal drinks.. incense and ceremonies.. Durga Puja is the best Kolkata festival of the year. It's a riot of a carnival, with beautiful pandals (special immersive displays) throughout the area, the sound of the dhaak drum (very like our drums from Bali), folks dressed in their best clothes and a whole special feast! It kicks off today.. and lasts for four days. I'm sure you will wish Mr Chatterjee and his family and team all the best.. 


It's all for the Goddess Durga.. (don't ask it's a bit gruesome).
Which reminds me - we now have (I believe)  absolutely the best range of Incense of any wholesaler in Europe (banging the drum again).. and all the next level Incense.. Check out our Incense department... 
There is lots more new stuff coming online.. check more below..

Anyway, enough excitement for one week. Or maybe not.. because there is more Good News.. 
The new Rolling Stones album is also out today!  I'm planning to kick-back and soak it up along with a bit of Spanish sunshine and vino (hopefully).

All the best, thank you for your support, take care.
If Storm Babet is causing you any disruption, please take extra care.

Wishing you a lovely weekend.

David

title: We have been Robbed!
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I'm shocked. A shipment of AW products has been stolen.. details below.

August in Spain.. it's the first time I have been here at this time of year. It's crammed with tourists like a normal year.. and the roads are full of people who can't seem to drive, overcome by sunstroke, unsure of which side of the road to drive, getting confused and has to be said probably a little tipsy.. a trip to the supermarket is an adventure.. Within ten minutes I have seen so many near misses, a car going the wrong way round a roundabout, someone attempting to join the motorway in the wrong direction, people parking in random locations. Now I know why the locals leave for August..

Last week I was telling you that despite all the problems these days of shipping and importing products, we are still determined to make beautiful things happen. If you missed it you can catch up here..
Just when I thought importing couldn't get any harder than it is... it did.. 

Container no. AWC-74 has had a difficult time.. from the loading being cancelled several times, to delays at export customs, to extended time at sea.. not to mention the crazy shipping fees, some $12,000 more than pre-pandemic.  Then getting from Felixstowe to Sheffield.. you have probably read there is a shortage of drivers.. more delays..
The driver - who does not apparently speak English - ran out of time on his tachometer and didn't make it to the truckstop. Had to stay in a layby off the A14.. while napping somebody with a bolt cropper broke the seal and made off with a load of cartons from the back of the container. Yes.. I agree with you, and the Police are investigating

Normally every inch of space is used, so you can see quite a few cartons missing.
This has never happened before, in twenty years of importing we never had anything stolen in transit from a container. Google Map ref.
What has been stolen is mostly Aromatherapy Soywax Candles.. quite a few. It seems like 90 cartons (cartons are small but high value) Some - Mini Ceramic Baths for Gifts and eight cartons of - Natural Soap Bags from Rami and Sisal.
In total about £10,000 of products.
So.. 


STOLEN!!  If you get offered any of these items cheap.. Please let us know!!

That is not the only problem.. I spoke to Coco in China this morning.. Another problem. The giant port of Ningbo is in lockdown, apparently a single case of covid is enough to close the port.

Ningbo Port News

There is not much news about this in Western Media yet.. but I found this on DW. 
Coco says we have two containers in there, one queuing to get in, and one about to be loaded on a ship. The numbers are huge.. millions of containers go through Ningbo every month, the effect could be vast - much worse than the Suez canal blockage. 
No news yet how long it will last.. but hopefully days not weeks.. meanwhile they will invoice us storage charges. 

In other news.. I have had a few emails from customers, suggesting I travel less to help save the planet. I want to address this.. yes of course I agree with that. Already I plan to stay in Indonesia for two or three months, if and when it is possible to enter the country. 
In 2018 (I keep a log) and I'm not proud of this, I took 57 flights, often staying a few days dashing to the next place and frantically trying to do hundreds of jobs in a crazy merry-go-round. This has to stop.
Also, some customers say we should be buying more locally. Well we are doing that as well, as much as possible. You can't get more local than our own aromatics factory.. New products this week include Clay Face Masks. We have many more products in the pipeline. Recent (more local) products include candles from Poland and amazing high quality Loofahs from Egypt. Tea blends from Spain (which I love).  We are working hard on all fronts to find you products that sell well and keep your customers happy.

Yes it's hard work these days.. but we still love it.

Take care, stay safe and hope you are enjoying the summer.

David

title: Retro Xmas with Chopsticks
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about Fast Feng Shui... 
It might be Father's Day in the UK (Happy Dad's Day to all who qualify!) but here in China it is Christmas. You see I'm still in Yiwu, seeking out new products to ship to Europe. It's June so therefore it's Christmas and now is the time to get in the festive spirit and figure out what Xmas stock we need. Order now and it will be arriving in the UK warehouse early September.. with a bit of luck.
I'm thinking along retro nostalgic lines. So if you have any ideas for Christmas stock lines please let me know. Actually nostalgia not what it used to be (I always wanted to say that).. seriously the retro look has become a theme of it's own borrowing old styles and reinventing new ones. I love it actually and especially since the theme fits well with our AW style. Some of our best selling lines are in the retro / steampunk style. Your not with it, unless you are old fashioned.
I have been hanging out in the festive halls of the Yiwu market. It's the busy time here for Christmas trade, the market is buzzing. All dancing Santa's and flashing Christmas tree lights. Smiling Chinese salesmen eating lunch with chopsticks. Miles and miles of tinsel and endless Rudolf soft toys. Chinese lanterns and red tassels for luck. I have done this job before but it always seems altogether surreal.
Next week I'm off to Chiang Mai the northern city in Thailand famed for it's handicrafts and growing gift trade. A few days there and then on to Indonesia to further develop our sources in this hugely growing area.
More thoughts and news next week.. from the East.
Regards
David

title: New Products in Java
content_html:
Greetings from East Java

Last week I was telling you about the arrival of Coco (my wife and your China agent) to Bali. After 900 days separated by covid.. If you missed it you can catch up here.
After a few days in Ubud seeing things I never see, because who goes to tourist attractions on their own, it's time to get back to work. 
A long-planned trip to East Java.. we took a packed and very cramped Lion Air flight (not recommended) from Denpasar, Bali to Surabaya, Java. Ringo, his assistant Bondhan, Coco and me.. 
The first mission to an area where marble, granite, onyx and million year old fossilised wood is found. Bondhan had discovered a village deep in East Java beneath the mountains where almost everyone was making stone crafts..
Since it is very difficult to buy pestle & mortars in China these days we thought at least maybe we can find it here.. 

But Java is a big island with only a few fast roads, so from the airport to the area we wanted to visit was a four hour drive. The only decent hotel was in a town called Tulungagung, famous for three things.. 1. The world's largest cigarette factory which we drove past for quite a while. 2.  The beautiful marble and onyx mined locally - our hotel was made of the stuff from top to bottom. 3. It's cheap here.. the hotel is less than £25 a night including an excellent breakfast buffet. We ate out at the Steak Barn restaurant for four people including steak for £15.. 

Bondan who speaks the local language had done the groundwork, he had discovered the place a while back and already made some contacts. So we could just take it to the next level and do the business. 

From the hotel to the village was still quite a drive.. but as we arrived you could see it was geared for business.. the Stone business.. huge stone lions, showrooms full of every kind of statue.. small and large workshops. We spent two days exploring getting to know the locals
and discovered that quite a lot of production is made for export to the USA, Australia and some European companies.  Friendly people.. one guy with a beautiful showroom and a well organised warehouse with a container loading dock even offered to consolidate orders and load them in his warehouse, no problem if we buy from the competition.  Later he told us that his grand-father had been one of ten sons that all got into the stone craft business, the second generation of those ten sons now made up most of the businesses in town.  Each one specialising one particular stone craft. Stone Birthday Numbers
From huge Buddha statues to every type of stone soap dish, to bathroom basins made from huge river stones..  they even make jewellery from onyx beads.. so lots of possibilities. Gemstone Bracelets 


We managed to order from one business and have another couple in the process. Still hoping to secure a deal    for supply
of rare petrified wood - which is claimed to be over a million years old, it can be fashioned into candle holders and interesting bowls


This is the grandson son of the village founder and his wife with some of that petrified wood. 

A couple of months ago I was in Morocco, also miles from anywhere, in a village in the shadow of mountains where gemstones were found. Here are different stones but the same type of craft workshops and creativity.
Regular readers will recall.. 

We will definitely come back, lovely gentle people - small family businesses easy to do deal with and a wealth of local craft skills. So well done to Bondan for once again opening up a new source of beautiful craft items.
After the stone village, we hit the road again this time travelling to Central Java and the city of Solo.. where we are today. 

The teak craft villages are near, but also this is a major area for textiles.. so let's see what will happen..

Meanwhile back in UK.. it's hotter than here I understand. So I hope you are enjoying the weather. Things are really hotting up.
Sales of many items are also hotting up. we have your fast-selling summer stock right here right now..

Some other good news at our Aromatics factory.. AW-Aromatics new factory and warehouse is nearing completion. We are already using the warehouse space.. 
This means we can supply many products directly from the aromatics factory.. if you are interested in making your own branding. What we call white label items. Or you need bulk supplies, or want to chat to us about contract packing your brand we are here to help. Head over to AW-Aromatics.com to buy even more direct. 


Take care. Have a great weekend.
More news next week. 

David

title: David's AW News:  Trade Secrets, Teak Tales, and a Special Thanks from Bali 🌸
content_html:
Greetings from AW Frangipani warehouse, Bali

Yes I'm back from Java, where last week I was telling you about the most friendly people and the village where everyone collaborates together to make beautiful guitars.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

There seems to be a bit of a crisis inside Indonesia with airlines. Prices of tickets have rocketed and every flight seems to be full. I used to even turn up at the airport and get whatever flight was next to leave, now you have to plan well ahead.  I need to get back to Bali from Solo and discovered that no seats were available for the next four days.. so I ended up flying to Batik airways to Jakarta, business class (crazy for a one hour flight - but I enjoyed it), strolled through the rustic but friendly domestic airport to departures, sat in an ancient but comfy business lounge at the one gate terminal just for Batik. Nobody checked my ticket..  As I came out of the lounge I was directed to take the business class mini bus to the plane.. on the plane I took my seat.. I realised nobody had looked at my ticket on my phone, or even scanned the QR code. Well such trusting folks at Batik air...

Whilst in Java we went to visit a supplier deep in the Teak forests of central Java. 

I was keen to reinvent our teak fruit bowls collection having seen an impressive range at one of our Spanish competitors.. nothing like a bit of competition to get you motivated!

There is a town in the middle of the forest, which is a bit like the guitar colab village I was telling you about where everyone is focused on the same things. 

Actually before you reach that place (I can't tell you the name.. it's a trade secret).. we have one long-time supplier. Husband and wife, they have a small showroom on the side of the road and workshops that actually abuts  into the forest..  The husband was actually working on re-order when we arrived. You can see the teak display pad the is making.


These are carefully managed teak forests, this area actually just planted two years ago. I was surprised at the height they grow in two years. Our supplier lady explained that they don't cut the tree's until the trunks reach a certain diameter and some parts of the forest have trees that won't be harvested until they are fifty years old!  That's a hell of a supply line. More trees are planted than cut and conservation is a serious business. The big trees are cut and harvested and shipped to the mega factories near the port that produce the world's garden furniture. The roots, branches and offcuts find their way to the local artisan community.. where tremendous creativity produces beautiful things. Check out these..


The boss of this place employs dozens of local artisans, he showed us his beautiful house and several large workshops with people beavering away. The guy was very happy to see us, actually all the family came to say hello. It seems his best customer (I think American) has never met or has even talked to them. They just get regular emailed orders, and send truck loads to the cargo house every week. Hense so happy to meet potential customers in person. 

We didn't order anything yet.. because the current shipping rates would triple the landed price of such things, but do you think we should?

Meanwhile I'm back in Bali and Ringo has been showing me the garden that surrounds the loading area of our warehouse. He has green fingers.. and really proud of his multi coloured frangipani.

Green fingers..

And a big thank you. 



THANK YOU!

 

Finally news from Bali Baby Home. With our donation (made possible by you.. our amazing customers) they were able to fund the rescue of three more babies in the Yogyakarta branch..

The founder called us with very emotional thanks and his media guy made a little video.  


He also told us that another two babies have been taken into the Bali home. So lots happening right now.

You can help by donating here.. but just being a customer will help us help more. Thank you. 

If you donate, you can be sure 100% of it goes to the causes we support. 

 

It's September very soon.. and that means CHRISTMAS IS COMING.. not to mention Halloween.. so the Backend Giftware Season officially kicks off.

Wishing you all the best for the upcoming trading season.. let's make it Happen!

 

Have a lovely weekend, more news next Friday.

 

David

 



PS: This is today.. baby born lunchtime in Bali Baby Home...

title: Hugs & insights - What's Trending
content_html:
Greetings from Spain    

 

Happy Black Friday.. hope it's going well.
Cyber Monday is next, and this year is where it is at.

 

Here in Malaga we are recruiting warehouse staff, not surprisingly (perhaps) in the space of a few hours, we had 200 applicants for two jobs. 
What is surprising is the number of be-suited hopefuls who apparently don't trust emails, preferring to turn up in person to deliver their CV.  It's a pretty clever trend in job hunting techniques. You have got to be impressed.
Last Christmas (and it now seems another age) we were training the AW-Artisan team after an intense recruiting round.. now it's time to expand the team.
Last Week (also a long time ago) I was telling you about: Hero's Hiccups & Hope. Happenings in the far corners of AW.. you can read about it here.

 

To put you in the mood for Christmas congour up in your mind's eye the amazing (late great) George Micheal and mates in the ski lodge, broken hearts wooly jumpers.

 

Last Christmas..
Last Christmas, I gave you my heart
But the very next day, you gave it away
This year, to save me from tears
I'll give it to someone special...

 

That is.. Save us all from tiers :)  level one, two or three. 
Sorry, so sorry but I had to get in a tiers pun 
But the big question (in the gift trade) is... what are people going to give each other this Christmas?

 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 66,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken. 

 

Last Christmas - was a different world. For sure it's a strange time we live in. All the popular usual gifts from a year ago are out of style. Who wears perfume or lipstick these days, my go-to gift of theatre tickets are practically off the table. Skiing trips a big no no.
But since we are spending more time in the home, things that make us feel more at home. Homely things are what sells and we can see it in what's trending at AW.. Candle sales are sky high. Dinner Candles 214% up Soy Pot candles 128%.
I can spend all day looking at stats, checking the trends and sometimes strange unexpected things happen. Essential oils of course you will know already are booming right now (unbranded up 69% - everything up at least 40%) and could be higher if we could get the supplies it's hard secure stock right now.
Unexpectedly Smudge Sticks are up (351%).. is everyone sat around in lockdown doing weird stuff at home.. yoga and meditation.. wafting herbal aromatics and chanting incantations? New stocks due in shortly - I'm told.
Gemstone Face Rollers..  are newish, we didn't have them last Christmas but sales are 50% month on month. Home is Home Candle Pots are also new - and this year's perfect candle gift. 
I won't bore you more.. but if you have any surprising trends in your business and would like to share them with the AW affinity inner circle - drop us a line.

 

In Spain we just launched a new "English language" site: AW-Artisan.eu  - ahead of Brexit. Check it out, if you are in Europe and speak English you might find it useful. 

 

So no hugs (sorry gran)..  we are told this Christmas.. but at AW we have lots of things your customers can give instead. Thoughtful and kind gifts are the next best thing to a hug.
Check out the deals below.

 

Wishing you all the best, remember to stay safe, give virtual hugs, wear a mask, and hopefully it won't all end in tiers :)

 

More updates and Christmas lyrics next week..

 

David

title: I have been Cancelled
content_html:
Greetings - unfortunately from Spain

Hope you are doing OK.. 
Last week I was in our distribution centre in Slovakia, and telling you about my upcoming trip to Indonesia. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
I was due to fly on Tuesday to Jakarta, but over the weekend the Indonesian government canceled all foreign visas throwing all my plans into confusion. 
Last week I possessed the question: Should I stay or should I go?.. and was genuinely feeling anxious about traveling to a covid hot spot.  Quite a few kind people wrote to me telling me not to go.. anyway folks.. for now the option is off the table.
I have a visa agent working on possible solutions but don't hold out much hope.

Romance is in the air at AW... 
Graciela, who works in the Spain office, announced her engagement and was flashing an impressive engagement ring.
In Slovakia Mirriama (who looks after the AWGifts.eu website) was wed, in traditional Slovakia style.
And many of you will know Kristy from UK customer services (now she works in the purchasing dept) who is finally able to have a lovely English wedding.. 

  
We wish them all a wonderful future and lots of happiness.

Meanwhile since I'm back in Spain I have been getting involved in AWArtisan - lots and lots of stock arriving.. I have to say long awaited stock. 
Stock that has cost vastly more to get here and involved massive amounts of arguing and stress. Containers from Indonesia, China and shipments from India in the last week or so.. plus two 40ft trucks from UK production.
Previously we have shipped from UK to Slovakia and then to Spain (Slovakia office having mastered all the customs import regulations there) - but clearly ridiculously inefficient sending stock on a merry-go-round through Europe.
So we had to bite the bullet and find a way to ship directly to Spain, and Spain has an extra layer of rules and bureaucracy - especially when it comes to soap - they hate soap imports.
Post Brexit we already knew would be difficult... so we already had a plan.. last month we shipped two mixed pallets of stock just as a learning curve to see what issues might arise - and there were lots. so having learned what tariff codes make the customs people happy, what changes to labels, what declarations need making, what country of origin forms to fill.. etc etc etc.. we were ready to scale up.. and so crossed our fingers and despatched two 40ft trailers with hopefully enough stock for a few months. 

We used to load a truck and it arrived a couple of days later.. now from leaving Sheffield to finally arriving in Malaga a full month.  And what used to cost a few hundred pounds and say 5% of the shipment, now costs tens of thousands and a lot of stress. 
A customs person who clocks off at 2pm, makes petty unreasonable requests and seems to be unable to reply to responses, thus delaying clearance again and again.  customs officials are waging an unofficial trade war against imports..
Toni is a hero.. our man in Spain has become a world expert in importing in this new age.. sorting the issues one by one and then.. cajoling, persuading, and making official complaints until it is sorted. 
 
Maybe they feel they are doing their patriotic duty to disrupt trade, but even without them there are enough problems.. the cost of shipping containers from Asia is still $10,000 per container more than it should be and shows no sign of coming down. Raw material costs in Indonesia, China and India are spiraling out of control, every purchase order we make is returned with a request for a price increase, or worse - unable to fulfill orders right now.  

So they say CASH is KING.. in a crisis it's good to have money to get you out of a hole. 
But this is a strange new world we live in.. I'm now telling my team that things have changed. 
Now.. STOCK is KING..  
That money in the bank is losing buying power day by day like a melting iceberg.  Whilst the stock you hold could well be appreciating in value dramatically.
Anyway, without stock how can we do business?

It's almost August.. 
And that means the start of the Christmas season is getting closer and closer.
We do have stock arriving in the UK, an Indian container just arrived, with lots of Indian cotton items from Mr. Chatterjee factory in Kolkata.
Salt lamps and Hymalian salt products also recently arrived.
Plus we have a new range of candles from a new supplier in Poland, our regular German supplier is complaining that raw material is in short supply so there will be delays.  

Hope you will enjoy the end of July, and manage to relax a little in August.
Take care and stay safe.

For the minute I'm stranded (not unhappily) in Spain at my home.
Next week I will update you with any developments.

David

title: David's AW News: India rage bate / Whiskey drama
content_html:
Greetings from Vadodara, in Gujarat


Gujarat is a dry state - alcohol consumption is banned even carrying alcohol is against the law. And both Toni and I have expensive whiskey we bought as presents for friends. Hope we don't get in trouble.. It was a little stressful at the airport..  but so far no problem. Yes, I never heard of Vadodara either.  And it's a surprising place. I'll tell you why later. 

So this week we have been crazy busy, at the Delhi fair - It happens twice a year, this is the Spring fair where many of our suppliers can be found. 
Last week I was telling you about our last days in Kathmandu, and my thoughts on Gifting Opportunities.. There's lots!  If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Well… Delhi doesn’t do things quietly.

It's been a whirlwind few days at the trade show — reconnecting with suppliers, shaking hands, doing deals, devising products and trying (unsuccessfully) to be in five places at once. Wow, they did a great job this year.. Musical entertainment, free quality lunchtime food, clean toilets, and even Like India generally, this tradeshow is getting better and better.

The big news?
We finalised a distribution deal with one of India’s major incense brands for the UK and Europe. Also opened up two, maybe three, new artisan suppliers. I'm quite pleased, actually.

We also did our usual trick of meeting suppliers in a hotel room. This way, we see products that have not been exposed to the whole world. Finding original designs.
After the trade show, we took a car to central Delhi, staying close to Connaught Place, convenient for the shops, bars and cafes.. but also not far from Old Delhi and Parahaganj .. where we met up with some of our oldest suppliers. 
Our main Singing Bowl supplier, Kamran, who runs his artisan export business from the depths of Chawri Bazar, a stone's throw from the Jama Masjid - one of the oldest and largest mosques in Delhi. Our guy Bondhan from Java, Indonesia, was super excited to see it. After we finished work, Kamran gave us a VIP guided tour.
After Chawri Bazar, the next morning we visited another hectic and iconic trading area.. the legendary Paharganj main bazar. We have a few suppliers there.. It's a favourite with a certain type of YouTubers who come to mock the scammers (and there are some), and great for content.  It is a high-energy, crowded, and often noisy area.  A true, raw, and busy, hectic Delhi experience. 
David's Rant! (sorry)
The thing is, while it's suddenly fashionable to make those rage-bait videos.. upsets Indians (who hate their country being shown badly) delights smug (I dare say possibly racist) westerners.. and therefore gets views and comments boosting the algorithm..  But you know I have been coming to India for twenty-odd years.. A lot has changed for the better. Even Paharganj is cleaner and safer; the mud and potholes are gone, and people these days are polite, not pushy.  Delhi sproosted itself up in 2023 for the G20 meeting.. and carried on getting cleaner and greener. Heck, the other day even the sky was blue. Our hotel was full of delegates. India AI Impact Summit 2026.. happening now.. and lots of bigwigs here.. 20 heads of state and of course Narendra Modi, Emmanuel Macron, UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. It's a big thing here. The whole city is abuzz with it. 
So, of course, you can make shocking content in India, but they are unfair in the bigger India.. which brings me to..

Trip to Vadodara
In Delhi, the traffic is epic because that huge conference is going on.  But despite the traffic, yesterday afternoon we escaped the city, made it to the airport and took the short flight with Indigo air down to Vadodara. I don't know what I was expecting.. but not this.
The airport is not huge, so we walked into the terminal, the luggage already on the belt.. and the luggage hall opened out with no fuss directly to the taxi pickup area.  Calm, peaceful, no hassle at all, Uber and a choice of other taxi systems. In no time, we had a cab (no scamming), a friendly driver to our hotel. And wow, a clean, tidy city. And big, two-million-person flash shopping arcades. And so far, all the people we have met are polite and friendly.  If you came to Vadodara to make rage-bait content, you'd be disappointed.  

We just checked into our hotel, tomorrow morning we will travel by car to Khambhat, a famous gemstone artisan area on the coast.. I'll tell you about that next week. This should be super interesting!!
As we checked, a gentleman appeared at the lobby asking if we'd like him to secure us a government licence to consume alcohol.. As foreigners, we qualify. How strange.. we declined a few days alcohol free, and embracing local norms will be good.

Meanwhile..
Back in the UK.. It's all happening.. 
Mother's Day is coming. And so much stock is arriving at the moment. 

India continues to unfold — intense, inspiring, exhausting, brilliant.

Grateful for the friendships, the artisans, the graft behind the scenes — and for all of you who make this journey possible.

Next update from Khambat… assuming we don’t get whiskey busted and accidentally feature in an Indian drama.

Thanks for being on the journey.

David

title: Emotional Decisions...
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

We have been here in Spain just over a week.. and a lot has happened. Last week I was telling you about why we are different, I even suggested we might be sub-normal... which upset one reader, you can read about it here.
Last week we got the keys to our new warehouse, taken our first delivery, organised a racking company, ordered a folk-lift truck, sorted the insurance, alarm, electric, CCTV, internet, printer etc.. but all that is easy compared to the job of recruitment.  
The important, delicate, careful, life-changing task of selecting a team to take AW Spain forward and forge future careers. Rodrigo (our Brazilian webmaster & fixer) has done a magnificent job placing ads, and then sifting through the 900+ applications and scheduling appointments for interview.  In the UK it's depressingly common that people don't make it to the interview, you can expect 30% not to turn up, sometimes even more.. here we have been interviewing 12 to 15 people each day.. and so far every single one has turned up. Amazingly and almost to a person a few minutes early.  It seems that good jobs with a respectable companies are hard to come by. The education levels are very high (even warehouse staff applicants seem to have university degrees) so it's not surprising that lots of young Spanish people move abroad for work. 

We had a surprising number of Antonio's - one or two Jesus's and lots of Juan's... One Juan after another Juan, "not another Juan!".. I joked - no-one thought that was funny..  thankfully not one Carlos. But all to a boy or girl really high standard and very polite and keen. All had done their homework and researched AW - some were massively enthusiastic to start working for us.
Interviewing staff is hard work, we specified that applicants should have some English language, but a few turned out to have limited English so we had to do it in Spanish.. which was interesting. The nervousness and stress rubs off on you and after a day of interviews, Tomas Rodrigo and I were just emotionally exhausted. After a week of it we are knackered.. 
Actually it was a humbling experience.  Listening to peoples stories, it made us all feel more appreciative that we have secure jobs that we love. 

One gentle guy, came happy to take a warehouse job, he was currently working for a big olive oil co-op. A major producer supplying supermarkets around the world. His job was a responsible one in the buying department - he'd just moved there (after a promotion) and within a month Donald Trump had destroyed it. The USA have recently introduced a tariff on EU olive oil and he told us that; that just wiped a massive chunk of business off the sales, putting the whole co-op into crisis. Visibly emotional and almost shaking he explained he couldn't support his family without a proper income and he had been told by his boss that his job could not be sustained for long and he should find something else. Hundreds of other people were also effected. It all seems so heartless.

It was "World Kindness Day" and it seems the world needs more kindness than ever before.

Now we have a short list of about 12 people, and from those we are trying to decide which 4 or 5 are going to be the founding staff of our new Spain company.  There are talents that are needed in the team, will the team gel together? is there a good balance of youth and experience, etc etc?.. We feel like the Strictly judges.. In this case the winners will take an all expenses paid trip to Sheffield to spend three weeks in intensive training, meeting all the AW people, developing relationships and making friends - they should even make it to the AW xmas party - before returning back to Spain to unleash AW products on the nation and beyond.  But honestly it's an incredibly difficult to decide.. Tomas, Rodrigo and I each have different feelings about how the team should work, and not forgetting these are life changing decisions not to be taken lightly. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. Black Friday approaches.. and thus many deals are available.. also new stock arriving..see below.. we are MEGA busy so please beware it's taking a few days to dispatch. At one point this week we was 900 orders behind.. but I am assured it is all under control, extra people extra shifts, and everyone possible person picking and packing.. we should get through the backlog.. I'll keep you posted.

I know you are busy. Do take care and remember to be kind.. to yourself.. and also to others :)

David

title: David's AW News: Drama and should I go?
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Where the temperature has fallen to around 30c much more comfortable.. I was telling you about the heat (40c plus) in last week's news and much more.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
This week we have been running everyday. Tomas, Coco and me.. running round our suppliers making things happen at pace as only they can in China - and especially in Yiwu.
If you can make it here you can make it anywhere! It's a Yiwu state of mind...I'm sure there should be a hip-hop song about it.


Yiwu City - you can make it here. Actually you can make almost anything here.

Correction. Re - Tax on candles..

Slight correction on last week's newsletter.. where I mentioned: we just got news that the EU and the UK are imposing (Trump like) tariffs on candles of 75% from this month... well the UK is not imposing this (so far) just the EU.. I understand that the EU is trying to protect candle manufacturers from cheap Chinese imports.. but have they thought this through? TEMU can still ship and no doubt will ship even more candles using the de minimis rule and pay zero taxes. At least when we import, we are paying taxes on sales and profits and some duty on import. All that the EU will lose. The candles will still flow via online marketplaces even more disruptive for EU manufacturers - so actually shooting themselves in the foot.  WHAT A BIG MESS.

Russian Shungite & Temu

We often get asked for Shungite gemstones.. I have seen it available in India and China. But Shungite is only available from one geographical location in the world. That's a town called Shunga in the Karelia Region of Russia - so of course we cannot and will not offer this product. However, go to Temu and search for Shungite and you will be swamped with listings.. Now it's possible that what's shown there is fake Shungite (Tourmaline would pass), but not everything can be and anyway Russian products are widely available in China these days - so supply would be easy. Think about that.. Temu is a backdoor for sanctioned Russian products using the de minimis rule. I'm notifying the guy at the BBC.. if this Russian product can arrive though the Temu back door what else can?


Meanwhile... Denpasar Drama

If it's not one thing it's another.. title: In Delhi's Main Bazaar
content_html:
8th February 2013

Hi ,
Greetings from India..
Last week I was telling you about my Mystic Mission in India. You can read it here.
Well it's all go as the big V day approaches in many countries. In Asia it's almost Chinese New Year and in India the Kumbh Mela is under way - possible the biggest human gathering ever.
While most young Indians have embraced Valentines day, in China they have their own version which falls on the 7th day of the 7th month.. in the lunar calendar, so that's not until august.
Today I'm off to Delhi, there is a well organised trade show where we can connect with a number of our suppliers quickly. But Delhi is one of the oldest trading cities in the world and has a wealth of ancient often chaotic wholesale markets, catering both for the domestic and the export trades. Paharganj district is one such area close to the New Delhi Railway Station. Just across the road from the station you'll see the entrance to Paharganj's main trading area, they call it the Main Bazaar and it stretches for about one crazy hectic kilometer teeming with people from all over India, cows and camels, bikes and rickshaws.
This market is definitely not for the feint hearted. It's chaotic, noisy, dirty, and full of crumbling buildings. It's been on the Hippy trail since the sixties, no doubt you can buy anything in those dusty back lanes. However, some of the big wholesale traders have showrooms here, and there are odd things that we buy here.
If your in Dehli and like a bit of adventure you should visit. It is possible to buy and export even small quantities back to the UK (lots of shipping agents) and many a retailer does just that.
But it's so old school, be prepared to haggle for hours and because they are basically traders, you have no idea if the producers are operating ethically, plus be warned.. quality control is purely hypothetical.
Take care.. and happy trading.
David

title: David's AW News: Back on the Road.. 1st Stop Kathmandu!
content_html:
Oh my goodness, I can't tell how good it is to be back in Nepal.

I left Sheffield in winter mode, to Manchester airport T2 over a sunny and snow-sprinkled Pennines. Then a night flight (via Turkish airways) through Istanbul (always slightly surreal at 1am), a little bit delayed but landed in Kathmandu early afternoon local time.  Kathmandu airport is one of the worst organised in the world, but redeemed by the most lovely people. After the chaotic but jolly baggage hall experience, I emerge to that familiar mix of incense, traffic, prayer flags and smiles. If you’ve ever been here, you’ll know what I mean — if you haven’t, it’s a place that gets under your skin very quickly.

Coming in to land at KTM, caught a spectacular view of the mountains above Kathmandu. Then land at the famously disorganised KMT airport.

Last week I was writing to you from Sheffield, my hometown and AW HQ. Talking about plans, people, and movement. I gave you my Top 10 picks for the SOL (Season of Love) - starting with Valentine's Day pretty soon! If you missed it you can catch up here.   

This week I’m right in the middle of it. Catching up with our delightful band of suppliers, some like the airport (super friendly but badly organised) - so a few cockups to sort out, but it's almost a pleasure fixing the issues.  Gosh, I just realised that we started trading in Nepal 8 years ago.. It's taken a long time to develop the relationships that deliver. 

One thing that always strikes me when I’m here is just how strong the “Made in Nepal” Brand is in the gift trade. 

Nepal isn’t about mass production or shiny factories. It’s about hands, skills, patience and heritage.  Lokta paper is made from Himalayan bark. Felted wool shaped by eye, not machine. Incense rolled slowly, bead by bead, stick by stick. These are products with time in them — and customers feel that. 

If Nepal had a creative heartbeat, it would be Thamel.

It’s the artisan hub — a maze of workshops, tiny shops, tea stops and suppliers who’ve been doing their craft for generations. You come looking for one thing and leave with five ideas, three samples and at least one unplanned conversation that maybe turns into a long-term partnership.

And the people… genuinely lovely. Warm, curious, welcoming — and always ready to help, even if it involves walking you halfway across town to make sure you don’t get lost (which, let’s be honest, I still manage to do). 

I had a few days on my own to gently dive into this world.  Calling on our regular suppliers, eating with my good friends, catching up with our lovely (and organised) shipping agent, Mr Padam. Then yesterday late afternoon, Toni from Spain arrived. I wasn't sure he would make it.. He is lucky to be here! If you have been following this newsletter, you will know that they have been moving to a new warehouse in Spain.. with much drama and upset. But this job is almost done, and the rest is on firm tracks, so he has escaped to join me on the adventure. 

Spain Update

Toni found a new racking company.. and they are on it! 

Almost finished..

Meanwhile, I’m here, we’re working on new ideas, strengthening supplier relationships, and shaping future products that fit perfectly into the Ancient Wisdom world — authentic, ethical, and commercially strong. Today we visited the factory of a potential new supplier.. factory high up on the sixth floor. 

They are making beautiful designer patchwork-style clothes from recycled materials. Watch this space!

Back in Europe, the calendar keeps moving — and Valentine’s Day is almost upon us 
It’s the first big moment in our Season of Love, and we’ve got great stock ready to help you make the most of it — gifts with meaning, margin, and a story your customers can connect with.

It's almost Valentine's Day.. and also Chinese New Year. And as luck would have it, a China container arrived with a new range of Lucky Waving Money Cats. We have sold these for years..and anything with cats is trending.. Money cats are back in fashion.. so we bought a whole new range.. We even designed our own Money Cat's Playing cards (see below)

Well, Holly got into the lucky esoteric business and made a very enthusiastic and (I think) informative video.. Check it out.. I'm sure you will see how easy it is to sell Money Cats.. And they bring you money as well!

Have a browse, get inspired, and make sure you’re stocked up.

More stories from Nepal very soon.

Warm wishes from Kathmandu,
David
Ancient Wisdom

title: David's AW News: Civic pride, new products & SOL.
content_html:
Greetings from Spain,

Well, as I write this.. It’s raining — proper Spanish rain — the kind that makes the coffee taste better. Yesterday, though, was sunny and bright, and we found ourselves in Mijas town hall doing a little admin job. I have to say… what a beautiful building. Calm, proud, elegant. It reminded me how much civic pride still matters here. It left me quietly inspired — and feeling grateful to be part of something that’s grown with the same kind of care. Mijas Pueblo is high up on the mountainside, looking down on the Costa del sol.. I'm sure most of you have been there at some time, but we were there early in the morning, just after sunrise and before the tourists.. the only folk around were gardeners and street cleaners..  underlining that sense of civic pride.

Coco sorting some papers at the town hall.
Last week I was telling you about our plans for the new warehouse in Spain and our ideas to make it a beautiful place to work.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Spain Warehouse Update

Well, in a week, a lot has happened.. (not without some drama) the offices are taking shape, racking has been moved, lots of stock has been shifted. We are building our Mandala Leaves Tea packing and blending vasility.. Toni's hair has turned slightly grey/ginger colour.. the team are working like crazy to make the move a success.. this weekend, they plan to move all the picking locations PLUS the picking benches- then Monday be ready to pick to pick (a big backlog) of orders from the new warehouse. What can I say, guys - AW heroes - an awesome effort!!

Now… back to the business at hand..— and what a lovely moment in the calendar we are entering.

Valentine’s Day is just around the corner, and from there we flow straight into what I like to call our Season of Love: (SOL)

Valentine’s - Mother’s Day - Father’s Day - Easter - Wedding Season

My AI graphic to remind you and inspire you of the upcoming opportunities.. :)

It’s a wonderful run of opportunity for independent retailers — and Ancient Wisdom has you very well covered.

We have heaps of fresh new stock just arrived, across multiple ranges, and right now we are also running a Gold Reward Amnesty (until the 26th January)— which means it’s the perfect time to:

• Reap or restart your Gold Rewards (reorder within 30 days, and you get to keep those discounts)
• Rebuild healthy margins (we like to reward our regular customers)
• Refresh best-selling lines 
• Add new products without stretching cash flow
• Prepare properly for the busiest emotional buying season of the year

Love sells. Gifting sells. Meaningful products sell.

And when you combine that with Gold Reward, your margins quietly smile too.

Let’s get this SOL — Season of Love — officially started.

This week we have so many new products - Tarot Card designs, Tarot Card storage and reading boxes.. They are amazing and selling fast.. 

Also, a container from Indonesia came with new products.. It's all happening.. 

Holly has been busy making some new Can You Sell This? YouTube videos.. Including this one about the Tarot Boxes, Cards and Crystal Balls - all things Esoteric.

As always, thank you for trusting us with a little part of your business journey.

We don’t take that lightly. Ever.

Wherever you are reading this from — rainy Spain, sunny England, snowy Europe (it's very cold at our Slovak office) or somewhere warm — I hope you feel the quiet momentum building for the year ahead.

Let’s make this Season of Love a beautiful one.

Warm wishes,
David

Founder — Ancient Wisdom

PS. Gold Reward Amnesty won’t be around forever (ends 26th January)… but good margins always should be  Plus
