title: George & The Crack Buying Team
content_html:
Greetings from a sunny and warm Sheffield.

 

Hope you are able to enjoy the blue skies and warm weather. Perfect for celebrating St George's Day.

But George is not British.. Lot's of countries around the world celebrate it. There is actually a country named George, and a US State named George (or Georgia). Then there are chaps and some gals called George - all like to celebrate St George's Day. He might be the patron Saint of England, but he is absolutely not English. It's such a big day that Google has updated it's logo.. strange to me why St George is claimed by the British.. he never came to Britain, that dragon slaying stuff is probably fake news and he was certainly no saint. 

 

Rodrigo just told me in Brazil.. they rather cruely call ugly girl friends Saint Georges.. why? He has no idea..

Haha, that's my thoughts..  

Last week I was telling you about my lucid dreams and our dream AW offices... you can read about it here.

 

If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011.. You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 73,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka, Rodrigo and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken.   

 

By George it's back to basics time..

Back in the day.. in 2006 when we moved into our first decent sized warehouse in a bohemian part of Sheffield. It was actually called Lancelot Works and way back in Sheffield's industrial past it had been a silver works. There was something kind of poetic about Ancient Wisdom trading from Lancelot Works, and the landlord did have a beard and something of Merlin the wizard about him.  Standing in this vast empty space with some big abandoned machine (we never knew what it did) plonked in the middle with the landlord trying to convince us to rent the place.  "But it's huge" I protested, "much more than we need".  



Sadly they changed the name, to a rather bland and unromantic Sheaf Bank Business Park, but it is full of vibrant start ups and artisan businesses.. 

I will never forget the wise words he came back with.. "But all you have to do is find out what your customers want.. fill this space with that." as he wafted his hand Merlin like across the space. 

It was like Authur pulling the sword from the stone moment.. kind of blinking obvious and yet most businesses don't actually do this. Especially in those days. 

 

Product is King. Forget everything else until you have products that your customers actually want.. so from that day I spent most of my time just finding out from customers what they want. then finding and developing products. Our mission was to have the best of everything that a gift retailer could ever want. Of course our heritage and origins are in aromatherapy products so we have gradually grown on top of that fertile base into all sorts of areas..

 

Now we have moved into Affinity Park, our 100,000 square foot warehouse. And with 6000 pallet racking spaces available.. we have lots of space again.. so time to find products..




Normally Tomas and I  would be travelling in India, China, Indonesia etc finding and developing those products. Face to face this is the best way to get exactly the right product..also able to check that companies are ethical and treat their workers and subcontractors well.  In the age of the pandemic this is practically impossible, so I have been rethinking the system. We still need your feedback and suggestions, your ideas have shaped AW since the early days..

and we still need you just as much.. If you or your customers are asking for something.. do just reply to this email and let me know.

 

So here is the plan.

My job is to reach out to all our existing Indian and Indonesian suppliers via Whatsapp to find what new products they can offer us. All night long from 1am my phone vibrates with hundreds of pictures arriving. It's disturbing my lucid dreams, and often I end up chatting with our Indian or Indonesian friends at some ungodly hour..

Once we get a product range that has potential, Bryant and Kristy (his new assistant) follow up requesting samples, organising labelling, packaging etc.





Radek, our Polish webmaster, spends some of his time researching Polish companies including candle companies.

Rodrigo, who is from Brazil is in touch with a couple of very promising gemstone companies who have some fabulous items..

Toni (our man in Spain) is doing a major deal with a local tea company for an upcoming magical range of herbal gift teas. He is also working with our Palo Santo guy who is currently in Mexico and it seems discovering a whole new world.

Tomas is spending every morning at the AW Aromatics factory developing new home grown and designed products.. with help and ideas from Dusan, Neil and Alan.

Tomas also has designed some fantastic products working with some real nice eastern European companies, Latvia especially.

And of course there is Coco in China (my wife) who is working incredibly hard, checking companies out, making visits, coming up with ideas.. 

 

So this is the AW product sourcing/designing/making crack team.. working hard to find you products that can boost your business and delight your customers.  

But one key team member is missing.. and that is YOU!




Do send your ideas to me and the team..

 

Meanwhile.. we have some amazing magical deals :)

 

Take care and have a safe and lovely weekend.

 

David
content_text: Greetings from a sunny and warm Sheffield. Hope you are able to enjoy the blue skies and warm weather. Perfect for celebrating St George's Day. But George is not British.. Lot's of countries around the world celebrate it. There is actually a country named George , and a US State named George (or Georgia). Then there are chaps and some gals called George - all like to celebrate St George's Day. He might be the patron Saint of England, but he is absolutely not English. It's such a big day that Google has updated it's logo.. strange to me why St George is claimed by the British.. he never came to Britain, that dragon slaying stuff is probably fake news and he was certainly no saint. Rodrigo just told me in Brazil.. they rather cruely call ugly girl friends Saint Georges.. why? He has no idea.. Haha, that's my thoughts.. Last week I was telling you about my lucid dreams and our dream AW offices... you can read about it here. If you are new to this newsletter - I have been writing it every Friday, from wherever I happen to be.. for over nine years.. the first was from Thailand during Chinese New Year 2011. . You can scan a selection of old blogs here.Over 73,000 people subscribe to this newsletter, all customers and fellow giftware traders - Here I tell you the trade secrets, the gossips, the adventures and mishaps. You will meet Ringo our agent in Indonesia, Mr Chatterjee our man in India. Coco our agent in China.. and of course Tomas (product and marketing wizard), Raul (IT wizard), Katka, Rodrigo and the whole team from the UK. Join me as I travel and work.. and feel free to email me your ideas and suggestions, over the years the readers of this blog have really shaped the direction AW has taken. By George it's back to basics time.. Back in the day.. in 2006 when we moved into our first decent sized warehouse in a bohemian part of Sheffield. It was actually called Lancelot Works and way back in Sheffield's industrial past it had been a silver works. There was something kind of poetic about Ancient Wisdom trading from Lancelot Works, and the landlord did have a beard and something of Merlin the wizard about him. Standing in this vast empty space with some big abandoned machine (we never knew what it did) plonked in the middle with the landlord trying to convince us to rent the place. "But it's huge" I protested, "much more than we need". Sadly they changed the name, to a rather bland and unromantic Sheaf Bank Business Park, but it is full of vibrant start ups and artisan businesses.. I will never forget the wise words he came back with.. "But all you have to do is find out what your customers want.. fill this space with that." as he wafted his hand Merlin like across the space. It was like Authur pulling the sword from the stone moment.. kind of blinking obvious and yet most businesses don't actually do this. Especially in those days. Product is King. Forget everything else until you have products that your customers actually want.. so from that day I spent most of my time just finding out from customers what they want. then finding and developing products. Our mission was to have the best of everything that a gift retailer could ever want. Of course our heritage and origins are in aromatherapy products so we have gradually grown on top of that fertile base into all sorts of areas.. Now we have moved into Affinity Park, our 100,000 square foot warehouse. And with 6000 pallet racking spaces available.. we have lots of space again.. so time to find products.. Normally Tomas and I would be travelling in India, China, Indonesia etc finding and developing those products. Face to face this is the best way to get exactly the right product..also able to check that companies are ethical and treat their workers and subcontractors well. In the age of the pandemic this is practically impossible, so I have been rethinking the system. We still need your feedback and suggestions, your ideas have shaped AW since the early days.. and we still need you just as much.. If you or your customers are asking for something.. do just reply to this email and let me know. So here is the plan. My job is to reach out to all our existing Indian and Indonesian suppliers via Whatsapp to find what new products they can offer us. All night long from 1am my phone vibrates with hundreds of pictures arriving. It's disturbing my lucid dreams, and often I end up chatting with our Indian or Indonesian friends at some ungodly hour.. Once we get a product range that has potential, Bryant and Kristy (his new assistant) follow up requesting samples, organising labelling, packaging etc. Radek, our Polish webmaster, spends some of his time researching Polish companies including candle companies. Rodrigo, who is from Brazil is in touch with a couple of very promising gemstone companies who have some fabulous items.. Toni (our man in Spain) is doing a major deal with a local tea company for an upcoming magical range of herbal gift teas. He is also working with our Palo Santo guy who is currently in Mexico and it seems discovering a whole new world. Tomas is spending every morning at the AW Aromatics factory developing new home grown and designed products.. with help and ideas from Dusan, Neil and Alan. Tomas also has designed some fantastic products working with some real nice eastern European companies, Latvia especially. And of course there is Coco in China (my wife) who is working incredibly hard, checking companies out, making visits, coming up with ideas.. So this is the AW product sourcing/designing/making crack team.. working hard to find you products that can boost your business and delight your customers. But one key team member is missing.. and that is YOU! Do send your ideas to me and the team.. Meanwhile.. we have some amazing magical deals :) Take care and have a safe and lovely weekend. David

title: India and Freedom Project
content_html:
Greetings from the island of Java, Indonesia.

Last week I was writing from South Goa. India. A favourite spot to chill and think, you can read about it here. 

Since then I flown across India from the west coast to the east coast to visit Serampore and the hometown of Mr Chatterjee (our man in India). After a night flight to Kuala Lumpur, a day interviewing staff for our IT team there and then a 3.30am start to get the flight to the port city of Semarang on the island of Java.

Serampore is where all the jute and cotton bags and packaging products come from. Mr Chatterjee runs a factory with his longstanding and loyal team of workers, beavering away making products for AW and others.

It's one of the poorest places I visit, although little improvements are seen, better street lighting, an actual park, albeit very tiny and new high rise property development being built with apartments advertised from 7 lac - about £8,000. The people are lovely and despite the obvious poverty, there are no beggars and I understand crime is very rare. 
Regular readers will know about the orphanage we support in the town, I, of course, have to go and visit, they love it when I come and always put on some kind of production where the kids can demonstrate their improving English with renditions and singing. 

This time I said - no need to do all that stuff - I'll just come for a cup of tea and a chat. Thinking I could see day to day life at the home. I'd got Mr Chatterjee to phone, whist we was in Delhi to request a no-fuss visit. 

We arrived late because of traffic, and in the outdoor canopy area I find all twenty-four children sat patiently in neat lines cross-legged on the floor, small ones at the front bigger at the back. A line of chairs a small table and a cup of tea. "Welcome Mr David" they all say in unison as we enter. 

Mr Chatterjee and I sit down, we are given cups of milky char and Mr Kundu (the orphanage owner) and the art teacher we hired stand looking at us. We sip the tea, the kids all watching us and smiling, Mr Kundo and the teacher watching us smiling. "This is not what I had in mind" I hiss at Chatterjee under my breath. So I ask Mr Kundu what they normally do on a Sunday evening.. "Yes sir, they do homework, play games and watch cricket on television". 

"Oh!" I say.. "That's good.. let's do that then". Mr Kundo is wobbling his head from side to side. "Oh no sir, Mr David sir, all that is cancelled because you are coming for tea". 

So embarrassing.. they really got me here.. then I remember the kids are entered in a local art competition been put on by the town temple. "Mr Kundu could the kids show me their artworks?" They don't need much encouraging before Mr Kundu can tell them - they all run off to find drawing pads and lining up to proudly show me the art one by one. There are one or two kids with clear talent. Then the traditional group high fiving, a few pictures and everyone are relaxed and informal.



It's always hard work in India, but almost always rewarding.. 
In Kuala Lumpur I met up with Tomas - the Marketing director/wizard at AW - and yesterday flew to Semarang, Ringo (our man in Indonesia) met us at the airport. My first impression, well the airport wasn't what I expected - it's as modern and slick as any in China and busy. The first thing you notice is the smell.. coffee.. Java haha.. smells of coffee!
So now we are in a totally new area in Java, it's early morning time for breakfast. Time to explore. First I need that coffee :) Full report next week.

Take care.

David

title: Lovely People
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I have just arrived in Spain after five days in Kuala Lumpur. 
Please forgive any typo's or rambling - because I'm writing this while jet-lagged..
Last week I was in Bali and I was telling you about Coco finally making it home.. and a little about Bali ceremonies.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Since then I had a few frantic days in Bali. Said goodbye to Ringo, Bondan and his wife with a fresh fish lunch on the beach near the airport. 

It's become a little bit of a tradition.. on the way to the airport we stop off at Jimbaran beach very close to the airport.. where.. at the far end of the beach there is a locals fish restaurant..  it's not posh, plastic tables,  wobbly chairs, no menu,  but a friendly smiling lady and the best fresh fish at reasonable prices.. help your self to cold beer from the fridge.. pick the fish from a chilled display.. we sit and chat.
We go over what's been achieved on this trip and make a plan for improvements and missions before my next visit. Bondan's wife works for a marketing company in Denpasar city not far away.. she managed to escape early and joined us just as the fish was served. After we take the 10 minute trip from there to international departure's.. and it's good bye hugs and best wishes all round.. I feel so grateful to be working with lovely people, say goodbye and I'm on my way to KL..

The flight was delayed (of course) and I arrived in Kuala Lumpur airport very late at night.. but Mr Sugar my regular driver was waiting for me in KL arrivals and takes me to my regular hotel on Bukit Ceylon. We chat on the way into the city.. he updates on his family news and asks me about Coco and how business is. Mr Sugar is a South Indian guy and a like most people in Malaysia or Indonesia (or in Asia generally) he is super nice, very gentle and always happy to help. We arrive at the hotel at about 1am the night porter is waiting.. welcome back Mr David..  lovely people everywhere.
Next morning I have breakfast with Raul (our IT wizard) he lives with his family on Bukit Ceylon in a very pleasant apartment. And we catch up with all the projects under development.. I explain my ideas in detail, I have some ideas for our Aromatics business in Sheffield. And over the next couple of days we plan it out.. and with a little gentle persuasion he agrees to come to  Europe in a few days.. 

On Wednesday evening Mr Sugar takes me back to the airport. Turkish airways via Istanbul to Malaga.. it's more than 24 hours journey from Bukit Ceylon to my house in La Cala de Mijas. But I enjoy the travel and always meet interesting people along the way. The business lounge in Istanbul is huge.. but it was very busy, it was hard to find a seat. A lot of Russians - wealthy ones I guess - going somewhere. Istanbul is one of the few airports they can still fly to, so a major escape hub right now. From Istanbul it is a 4 hour flight to Malaga.. it's not busy in Malaga, and I'm through the airport and in my hire car pretty quick. 
Tomas is here in Spain, and comes round to visit with some friends.. we go to eat at local beach restaurant just as the sun is setting. Tomas and his friends are lovely people.

Coco.. made it back to Yiwu.. last week I was telling you how difficult it was to get back into China. She had to do a final three days quarantine in Yiwu.. and as I sent last weeks newsletter she was about to get free.. and they cancelled on her and told her because there were new cases in Yiwu, she would have to stay longer.. She was so distressed poor girl, just when she thought she would see the grandkids, rug pulled. I told to start shouting and argue.. surprisingly despite Coco's doubts.. it worked and they let her out one day later. The regulation was that a bus would take that days batch of released people directly to their homes.. where they are expected to do more home quarantine (it's obsessive no?). It was going take hours driving round the city dropping people off one by one.. She called me from the bus.. I told just to get off when it stops and get a taxi home.. she asked the driver, and he basically said he was sick of this stupid job.. and yes everyone could get off now.. So Coco's son came and picked her up.. and she was finally home.. about a month after I said goodbye in Jakarta. 

Now she is teaching the kids the yoga moves she picked up in Ubud..


Meanwhile in Sheffield, we finally got showroom up and running and this week has been open days.. no appointment needed.
A steady stream of visitors have been popping in to meet the team and check out the show room. Rodrigo says he really enjoys meeting our customers and getting feedback and suggestions. He tells me all our visiting customers are lovely people.
From next week - it's best to book an appointment. Showroom details. There is a Whatsapp link there.. you can but the appointment there. 


It seems like an age ago - that Toni and I went to Morocco and visited our supplier in a small town in the middle of no-where in foothills of the Atlas mountains.. It was in April actually.. here is a link back in time.. to: In search of dream stones. Regular readers will recall..


Our man: Ismail  in Morocco.. 

Well the stock we ordered finally arrived in the UK.. and it is magnificent.. I'm so happy to see this arriving. Lot's of beautiful items see below for details. And I can tell they are selling very fast..

A note about financial crisis in the UK. Seems like UK government have everything under control.. (or maybe not) what a good idea to borrow lots of new money just at the point inflation and fuel bills are are spinning out of control.
A while back I predicted this situation.. it seemed to me that when the whole world was printing money to deal with covid, that inflation was inevitable and now the Ukrainian situation has made everything worse.. but this was coming anyway.
Cash is not king anymore.. money is now shrinking in value fast. Whilst stock, my friends is appreciating in value. . 
And affordable, aromatic, comforting, mystical... the type of GIFTS we have at AW are the type of gifts that people buy in difficult times.. because lovely people love beautiful things..

I just want to say.. That I'm so grateful for all the lovely people in my life.
With that thought.. I wish you a happy and peaceful weekend.. 


David

title: Heaven & Hell
content_html:
Greetings from the wet season in Bali.

Hope you are doing well and trade is rocking..
Here in Bali when it's not raining it's stinking hot, I didn't know it could rain so much! Whenever I have been here this time of year it could rain pretty damn heavy but usually not for so long or so hard as it has this week.
I'm not complaining, in fact I'm loving Bali more and more.. here covid is almost zero, very high vaccination rates and fastidious mask wearing have squashed the virus into submission. In a population of 4 million only a few people are in hospital and no deaths for days.Here in Bali still no tourists at all, the government is still only allowing business or family visas.. so no-one is really coming. So Ubud has become calm and bohemian again - just like in the "Eat,Love Pray" movie.. It is maybe selfish because so many businesses are suffering but it's nice to frequent the few cool places that remain and see familiar faces everywhere. I'm making lots of friends including three retired giftware exporters who chose to retire to Ubud.. who knows maybe I will do the same. It's Heaven.

It's very different in parts of Europe of course.. our team in Slovakia (AWgifts.eu) is under huge stress, it's back to dark difficult days there. New lockdown and about 5 staff off with covid. It's hell. And this right on top of the busy trading period. I'm sure your thoughts and prayers are with them. They are AW hero's and we stand strong with you in spirit.

Ubud is giftware heaven.. and where giftware entrepreneurs go to die. 
But not yet! There is so much to do.. we have been working like demons, developing product lines - revamping, renewing, re-visiting old products.. it's all go! in Bali.  
Last week I was telling you about the visit to the Molten Glass on wood factory where you via AW have put 90 people back to work.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

One guy who has a small family business painting the Buddha pictures we sell, also does sign writing as a sideline. We decided to give him a few days' work and revamp our warehouse in Bali.
Ringo (our man in Indonesia) said that the old sign was a bit confusing anyway. A couple of years ago we had a customer competition to name our new warehouse - and it was christened "Frangipani Depot". Which is lovely as the whole street is lined with frangipani trees. Since the Ringo has been taking cuttings and planting frangipani branches in every spot and pot possible around our compound making it fab frangipani land. 
The problem with the name is the term "depot" - in Indonesian this is another word for warrung or cafe.. and a few none-locals keep popping in asking what's on the menu. 
So hence a slight revamp to "Frangipani Warehouse" and the addition of the new AW logo - which you will be seeing more of soon.


Bondan - our new designer and PA to Ringo - wanted to add his mark.. and came up with the " Do what you love" - " Love what you do" signage to go above the office windows.. I like it :)

There is a village not far from our warehouse that specialises in carved Buddha statues. We have never really visited it although Ringo has been mentioning it many times. So this week we went to visit a windy road weaves between workshops and rice paddy and artisans sit even by the road chopping away at lumps of wood until like magic mythical figures appear. Part of the business here is making statues for temples..
 ingo likes to just knock on doors and say hello until we meet people who are happy to work with us.
A lot of the export trade gets filtered through "marketing" people.. who present themselves as artisan companies. It's these people who have the instagram accounts and websites. When you give them an order the actual work gets shunted around different artisans in villages like this to find the best price, so ultimately quality suffers and the artisan works for the minimum. I'm not saying all "marketing" companies are bad.. they can add value with better or new designs and organise and coordinate lots of different family workshops to enable the volume orders to happen. But at AW we always like to get close to the artisans themselves. 


We spotted this guy carving a huge statue..
We asked if he was the boss, he looked amused but pulled out his phone and called the actual boss. 
After a few minutes a couple and young child appeared on a scooter.. at first they were a bit wary of us, but Ringo explained to them about AW and how we work. They didn't even have a business card, and had never dealt directly with exporters.
In normal times they would get regular contracts from agents plus supplying local tourist retailers. And this would be enough. Now the tourist trade has gone and the agents don't call. So they were very happy to talk to us.. 


This is Novita Dewi and her husband.. Because they are not far from our warehouse, they keep turning up with samples, offering different finishes and new designs.. 
There is nothing like a bit of enthusiasm to endear you to people and for sure they love their art a lot. Here are some examples..


These are all what they call "unfinished" pieces. Often another place will do the finishing, sometimes even the retailers in the tourist areas do the finishing giving the impression that they are making on the spot.


Here you can see the different finishes that Novita brought to our office.

But my time in heaven is coming to an end. Soon I must return to Europe. It's not bad.. I'm looking forward to seeing my family and friends for Christmas.. and that first pint of pale ale in a cosy Yorkshire pub.
Other good news is that Coco (my wife) has applied for a UK visa and may be able to travel to the UK for Christmas. But there are complications.. so let's see. Fingers crossed.

By next Friday I will be in Spain, later to the UK. Before I have lots of work to do.. we seem to be working long days.. I have tasked Ringo and Bondan with a target of shipping at least one container a week. 
This will be a lot easier when shipping rates normalise, because many low value bulky products - like bamboo wind chimes - are simply off the list because they cost too much to ship. 

In the UK it's really rocking.. now containers are turning up everyday, new products from our aromatics factory coming online. We are running a little behind with orders, but our warehouse team is working like demons, and putting in overtime and weekend shifts to make it happen.

Hope you are trading well and keeping safe.
More news next week..


David

Ubud is giftware heaven.. and where giftware entrepreneurs go to die. But not yet! There is so much to do.. we have been working like demons, developing product lines - revamping, renewing, re-visiting old products.. it's all go! in Bali. Last week I was telling you about the visit to the Molten Glass on wood factory where you via AW have put 90 people back to work.. if you missed it you can catch up here . One guy who has a small family business painting the Buddha pictures we sell, also does sign writing as a sideline. We decided to give him a few days' work and revamp our warehouse in Bali. Ringo (our man in Indonesia) said that the old sign was a bit confusing anyway. A couple of years ago we had a customer competition to name our new warehouse - and it was christened "Frangipani Depot". Which is lovely as the whole street is lined with frangipani trees. Since the Ringo has been taking cuttings and planting frangipani branches in every spot and pot possible around our compound making it fab frangipani land. The problem with the name is the term "depot" - in Indonesian this is another word for warrung or cafe.. and a few none-locals keep popping in asking what's on the menu. So hence a slight revamp to "Frangipani Warehouse" and the addition of the new AW logo - which you will be seeing more of soon. Bondan - our new designer and PA to Ringo - wanted to add his mark.. and came up with the " Do what you love" - " Love what you do" signage to go above the office windows.. I like it :) There is a village not far from our warehouse that specialises in carved Buddha statues. We have never really visited it although Ringo has been mentioning it many times. So this week we went to visit a windy road weaves between workshops and rice paddy and artisans sit even by the road chopping away at lumps of wood until like magic mythical figures appear. Part of the business here is making statues for temples.. ingo likes to just knock on doors and say hello until we meet people who are happy to work with us. A lot of the export trade gets filtered through "marketing" people.. who present themselves as artisan companies. It's these people who have the instagram accounts and websites. When you give them an order the actual work gets shunted around different artisans in villages like this to find the best price, so ultimately quality suffers and the artisan works for the minimum. I'm not saying all "marketing" companies are bad.. they can add value with better or new designs and organise and coordinate lots of different family workshops to enable the volume orders to happen. But at AW we always like to get close to the artisans themselves. We spotted this guy carving a huge statue.. We asked if he was the boss, he looked amused but pulled out his phone and called the actual boss. After a few minutes a couple and young child appeared on a scooter.. at first they were a bit wary of us, but Ringo explained to them about AW and how we work. They didn't even have a business card, and had never dealt directly with exporters. In normal times they would get regular contracts from agents plus supplying local tourist retailers. And this would be enough. Now the tourist trade has gone and the agents don't call. So they were very happy to talk to us.. This is Novita Dewi and her husband.. Because they are not far from our warehouse, they keep turning up with samples, offering different finishes and new designs.. There is nothing like a bit of enthusiasm to endear you to people and for sure they love their art a lot. Here are some examples.. These are all what they call "unfinished" pieces. Often another place will do the finishing, sometimes even the retailers in the tourist areas do the finishing giving the impression that they are making on the spot. Here you can see the different finishes that Novita brought to our office. But my time in heaven is coming to an end. Soon I must return to Europe. It's not bad.. I'm looking forward to seeing my family and friends for Christmas.. and that first pint of pale ale in a cosy Yorkshire pub. Other good news is that Coco (my wife) has applied for a UK visa and may be able to travel to the UK for Christmas. But there are complications.. so let's see. Fingers crossed. By next Friday I will be in Spain, later to the UK. Before I have lots of work to do.. we seem to be working long days.. I have tasked Ringo and Bondan with a target of shipping at least one container a week. This will be a lot easier when shipping rates normalise, because many low value bulky products - like bamboo wind chimes - are simply off the list because they cost too much to ship. In the UK it's really rocking.. now containers are turning up everyday, new products from our aromatics factory coming online. We are running a little behind with orders, but our warehouse team is working like demons, and putting in overtime and weekend shifts to make it happen. Hope you are trading well and keeping safe. More news next week.. David

title: David's AW News: 12 Days in China
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China


Hope you survived Storm Dave, enjoyed the Heat Wave and are ready for whatever weather comes next. Here in China, we are also suffering/enjoying dramatic temperature changes—one day 15°C, today 32°C. But cracking on with work regardless.  
Last week I was telling you about my journey here with an unexpected detour in Guangzhou.. our quick trip to Coco's hometown.. if you missed it, you can catch up here..

Now we are back in Yiwu..And the thing about Yiwu.. There’s a certain energy here that’s hard to explain unless you’ve been here. Not chaos exactly… more like momentum. Everything is always moving, everything is possible. No time wasted, competent people - who get things done without fuss. 

Bryant and Sandra arrived via Hong Kong a few days ago — It's Bryant’s first time here — and you can see it in his eyes… that mix of curiosity, excitement, and “blimey, this place is big”. And it is. Properly big. But also full of opportunity if you know where to look. We’ve come up with a big plan. Ambitious. Slightly mad if I’m honest. And just 12 days to pull it together.
Bryant and Sandra.. the first day.. and Bryant outside the main market entrance..  

But… I think we’ve got the right team here to do it.
Coco — absolutely unstoppable. The kind of “can do” attitude you just can’t teach. Between her contacts and the relationships we’ve built over the years, doors just open.
Sandra — design maestro — sketching, refining, reworking… often still at it well past midnight. You can literally see ideas becoming products in real time.
Bryant — straight into it. Packaging, positioning, thinking commercially all the time. Loads of ideas, and not afraid to push things.
And me… somewhere in the middle of it all, trying to keep up.

Every day has been a bit of a whirl.
One minute we’re sat in a tiny office surrounded by packaging samples…
Next minute we’re in a showroom full of teapots…
then across town with our tarot card guys…
then back with our favourite gemstone jewellery lady (still as sharp as ever)…

And then our packaging guy — honestly, next level.
Design something in the morning… and by the next day, there it is in your hand. Real. Physical. Done.

That speed… that responsiveness… it changes how you think about product development. You stop overthinking. You start doing. And that’s something I keep noticing here…
Perfection isn’t always the goal. But they just get things done. 

The gemstone market area… not actually in the organised market - it's a maze of streets that pre-date the modern market. It is a place I love and as mesmerising as ever.
Exotic shops, folk from all parts of China, gemstone community built around a love of stones.. But what I like is the people behind it. The familiarity. The trust built over the years. Conversations that pick up where they left off last time. It’s not just buying and selling. It’s relationships. Really, I could spend the whole time very happy in these streets, creating and doing deals.. 

And then today — something a bit different. We’re off to visit the glass and metal décor factory that makes our Bottom Up shot glasses (you might know them already — if not, you will soon… Father’s Day written all over them). I always enjoy these visits. You see the process. The skill. The little details you’d never think about, sitting back in the UK.

What strikes me most, halfway through this trip… Is how much this all depends on people.

Not systems. Not strategies. Not spreadsheets. But people.

The supplier who says “yes, we can try that” instead of “no”.
The designer who keeps going when everyone else would stop.
The team that just gets on with it, no fuss.

We’re thousands of miles from Sheffield… but in moments like this, it feels very connected. Every day, we upload all the pictures to a WhatsApp group for the AW teams from Sheffield, Spain and Slovakia. They all give feedback, ideas and encouragement. We are missing Tomas here (our old China hand).. but he is just too busy in the UK right now.. but he is watching us closely

Same goal. Same push. Same belief that we can make something better.

Let’s see where we get to by the end of the 12 days… 

More news soon.

Take care
David

title: David's AW News: Criminals in Malaga
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Hope you had a lovely Bank Holiday weekend, and hopefully successful trading. 

Yes, I upped sticks and moved back to my home base.. at least for a while.
Last week I was at AW HQ in Sheffield, and was telling you about our man James who has just been elevated to a director of Ancient Wisdom.. If you missed it you can meet James here.
We had an open week in the showroom in Sheffield and between my other jobs, I was able to meet and chat with a number of our delightful and always interesting customers. (more later).
Very early Tuesday morning Raul (the IT wizard from KL) and I drove over the Pennines to Manchester airport.  We took the route via the pretty town of Castleton and through the Winnats Pass, which was particularly dramatic and beautiful in the morning light.  

It's worth going that way just for the experience and beautiful views. Then we took a packed Ryanair flight down to Malaga. Arriving early in the afternoon, and amazed at how efficient Malaga airport is these days. Through passport control in minutes and luggage on the belt as we got there. Ten minutes from the plane to Sunshine. 

It was lovely to meet some of our customers face to face and everyone I spoke to - so generous with ideas and suggestions. I was really inspired. People telling me their secret best sellers, tips and tricks to sell more. Such as wearing gemstone bracelets whilst serving customers - and ideal price points. Apparently £10 is a good price for our Cedarwood and Gemstone Chakra bracelets.. We have recommended prices from £4.50 - £8.00 (cost from £1.92) if you buy a starter. Yesterday I was in Malaga town centre for a meeting and after we called in one of the esoteric shops to see how it was going..  They had taken our Cedarwood bracelet, repackaged it and had it on sale for €25.. in a basket by the till. There are lots of opportunities at AW!


In the same shop I was surprised to see a Palo Santo heater on sale. Not ours but a copy.. that's been done amazingly quickly.  It wasn't teakwood, and didn't have esoteric engraving but the same shape and concept.

It doesn't seem long ago I was designing and developing this product in Bali with one of our old suppliers, in fact our UK shipment only just arrived. (Along with lots of other new items.) see below...

We spent ages getting just the right height and size to take the Palo Santo sticks and heat them just the right way to release the fragrance without the stick catching fire. You can use them for Smudge sticks also.



These arrived in Slovaka a AW-Gifts and sold very quickly. 

In Spain, it's been a bit cloudy, but now the sun is coming out and it's time to think positive and make plans for the future in the AW-Artisan warehouse. I was telling you that we have rather too much stock on the way and nowhere to stock it. Our guy Toni had this idea to buy three Shipping containers and stack them in the carpark and use them for backup storage. He found a local company that sells refurbished containers for this purpose and we paid for them.. but the day came for delivery and they didn't come, so Toni chased the company.. and found the email and Whatsapp numbers stopped working. Website down.. Have we been Conned by Criminals?  So he called the police and the bank to stop the payment. Lot of drama and it may be too late.. but yesterday we got a random WhatsApp reply that was just a delay and they will come next week.  If they don't we will be trying to track them down in the dockland area.. I'll let you know what happens next week. 

Meanwhile, Summer is Here! And Father's Day is not far away.. Consider stocking up.. we have so many retailing opportunities.. Also we have PastPay offering many of our customers £16,000 lines of credit.. So stock up!

Take care
Have a lovely weekend. 

All the best David

title: Buzz word: Authentic
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Last week I was telling you about KYW  (know your wholesaler) and some wedding customs from Slovakia.. you can read about it here.

Since then my wife and I took a short break on the island of Rhodes, we just got back to our home in La Cala de Mijas at 3am last night.
On the flight, I was thinking about "authenticity" and what it actually is? It's a buzz word right now, and whatever it is - everyone is after the authentic experience. 

Here's my top travel tip for the week, avoid Volotea airline like the plague. It's a budget Spanish airline, and we were never so ripped off, delayed without explanation, incompetently organised, left on the tarmac waiting in 38c heat, left on a bus for 30 minutes no aircon. Any company in this day and age that charges €20 to print a boarding card, or another €20 if your hand luggage is 1cm bigger than allowed, and that is almost everyone's.. they waive this if you buy speedy boarding.. except there is no actual speedy boarding system (at least on our flights). Dodgy as they come, you can entertain yourself by reading the one star Tripadvisor reviews for the airline.. the thing is the image is amazing, company presentation is super cool, staff with fashionable uniforms, beautiful looking website, planes in fresh clean livery. Looks good - doesn't deliver. The name "Volotea" originates from the Spanish verb "revolotear," meaning "to fly around.. my travel tip.. fly around this company if you can.. they don't authentically care.. 

Anyway back to business, the gift business. In Rhodes old town.. which is a truly ancient wisdom sort of place with history oozing out of the stones, also has a lot of gift retailers, some of which are top class retailers offering a fantastic range of authentic giftware.. some like that airline offers a more fake experience. You can tell instinctively which retailers love gifts and which just want to rip of the customers with any old products and sneaky tricks.. I seen plenty of Indonesian and India imports in Greece, but thoughtfully presented to in keeping. Of course, fridge magnets are almost always made in China, so does that make them an authentic gift? mmm - I'm not sure?.. We found a guy in a mountain shop selling his own olive oil products, he had our China bamboo boxes with his company logo stamped on them. and cotton bags from India again personalised. Is it still authentic? Yes I think so, gift packaging adds value to the product, and this kind of stuff only comes (cost effectively) when imported. He obviously loved his products, and what he offered was an authentic experience.




So what is authentic? How do you define an authentic gift? Is the difference in love of the product?
I like to think so. But what about gift wholesalers.. how do you tell how authentic they are..
My old friend Terry (now retired) a true gentleman gift professional, once told me about a London wholesaler he was thinking of investing in. Naming no names here.. but they had an obsession about removing any label that might give away the manufacturer or true importers. Needless to say he never invested. At AW we hide very little, (only commercially sensitive information) - if you are a regular reader you know all the trade secrets of importing, I tell you everything!  If we can't add genuine value we shouldn't be in business.

So here are 5 tests of authenticity for your gift wholesalers?
1. Are they actually importing or manufacturing the majority of the products on offer?  - if not they are just a middleman adding no actual value to a product.
2. Do they have warehouses and agents on the ground in the countries they import from, who care about trading fairly and track the source of products? 
3. Does your wholesaler retail as well? Do they sell on Amazon, or own retail sites (online or high street). Because if they do, they are competing with you unfairly. That's not love.
4. Do they add value, buy creating authentic original designs, and/or by buying big enough to get economies of scale that they can genuinely pass on to their customers?
5. Are they trying to pass themselves off as being something they are not? Beware of fakes.. believe it or not, there are people who even pretend to be associated  AW wholesalers. 

We are far from perfect at AW - we are often behind with orders, often out of stock, sometimes things go wrong, but at the end of the day we love gifts (and our customers) and try our best to be authentic. 
We don't have sales people or do trade shows, so maybe you have to work a little harder to place an order, but you will see the difference in your bottom line...  

One of the things I love about Spain is the food. Many restaurant owners (especially around here) love what they do so much, they would never compromise on quality, the product comes first even before making a profit. You can feel that love, that distinctly Spanish passion, that authenticity in a restaurant before you even eat right? You know what I mean? On the other hand the fake tourist paella joint still lives on.. conning its customers selling tarted up boil in the bag paella.  There are boil-in-the-bag wholesalers as well :)

It's super hot in Spain.. forecasts of 40c plus.. hopefully if I don't wilt away more news next week.

Take care.

David

title: David's AW News: To Many Culture Shocks
content_html:
Greetings from Northern India

Hope you guys are well and business is good. I'm travelling with Toni on our Epic Asian Adventure seeking out new exciting products to boost your business. I'd say "elevate to the next level," but that would mark me out as a lazy AI user. Is it just me or is all the world descending into an AI generated (empathy free) sameness. The same vocabulary and turn of phrases everywhere.  I was a big fan of AI a year ago but now I'm not so sure. It has it's uses but not every flipping time. Use your brain please.
Sorry about the rant, even here in India I can see adverts composed by it and I'm thinking the whole world is losing creativity. And India is a country famous for it's creativity. Last week I was telling you about our visit to the major giftware trade show in Delhi. So much concentrated creativity and beautiful things in one spot it was overwhelming. If you missed it you can catch up here. 
Wow this week has been mad. After the trade show we spent some time in central Delhi - the old parts where artisans trade.. 


I'm seeing India fresh through the eyes of Toni on his first trip, for me it's familiar territory (and I can see things are slowly improving) for Toni there is that culture shock thing going on. Between visits to old suppliers in those ancient areas we squeezed in visits to the epic India Gate, and the ancient and hectic Jama Masjid mosque. Where we were lucky to be given a personalised tour by one of our suppliers local to the area. Total culture shock.

After that we planned to travel north to Panipat, the fabric recycling capital of India famous for Rag Rugs. But there was a problem. You may have read in the news about thousands of revolting farmers angry at price guarantee reforms descending on Delhi to protest. That was all happening between us and Panipat, our car driver cancelled on us. But Mr Chatterjee had a solution and acting quickly managed to secure three tickets on the express train out of New Delhi train station direct to Panipat. Another level of culture shock, the hectic station, the mad rush and scrum to get aboard . But then the next level culture shock.. You see these days since the G20 meeting last year Delhi has been made relatively pretty, it's been cleaned up, painted nicely, lots of murial type art and by simple blocking of anything ugly with huge walls of blue and green corrugated metal fences. But off  the main roads or behind those fences the slums of Delhi still exist. As our "express" train trundled out of Delhi at a snail's pace, we saw the other side of Delhi. Another culture shock even for me.


Our very green train and the sad views.

Our guy in Panipat, Raj met us at the station in his nice brand new hybrid car, and drove us through the ramshackle city of Panipat to our hotel. The best he could find us in town, over a rather scruffy shopping centre a sprawling hotel and leisure centre has been built (or still being built it seemed). A monument to bad taste, but at least happy cheerful staff, clean large rooms and good food. There was a large roof terrace restaurant with a big screen playing old Bolliwood music videos, where on Valentine's evening they decorated with pink banners and hearts and a family saxophone band played. The towns relatively well off came with their whole families to enjoy, small well dressed kids running around. Parents and grandparents on big tables. Not many romantic couples, which was a relief for me Chatterjee and Toni. 


This part of India has low alcohol taxes and Panipat people like to drink, so it was a jolly affair.  Raj explained to us there was a local (dangerous) moonshine culture that the government solved by making good quality drinks cheaper and available through smart clean shops.. all called "English Wine and Beer Shops" of which in this town there are a lot. Why "English" I asked? Because I'm sure you don't actually have English wine in there. It's because the word "English" denotes quality. Good to know 


English wine in India!

Panipat products.
After Panipat we took a car with a driver further north to the wood craft city of Saharanpur..
Last time I was here was 2016, and it has improved somewhat... but you know still that culture shock. 
More news about that next week.

Meanwhile...
Back in the UK.
A quick thank you to everyone who has filled in our Feedback form to help us improve your ordering experience on the website. It's actually a huge help thank you!
If you didn't contribute yet you can still do so in the link below or here.
Note.. we still have FREE SHIPPING in UK so don't miss out. Plus quite a lot of new stock coming online from India.. 

Wishing you an amazing weekend (we will be working as usual).
Take care and Namaste.

David

title: Homeward Bound
content_html:
Greetings Malaga airport, I'm waiting for EasyJet flight U2 1867 to Manchester. 

It's a bit stressful at check in, busy because stupid Brexit is causing a lot people to leave at this time. And a surprising amount of people don't have Covid certificates or have not filled in the passenger locater form. Tears and tantrums, old folks that can't cope, French people claiming they don't speak English. But I have made it to the gate.. 

 

By the time you read this I should be in quarantine in a hotel in Sheffield.

Last week I was telling you about Spring bursting forth here.. the warm weather has just arrived, and I'm leaving.

The Spring is a time of hope and rebirth.. none more than this year. You can read about it here.


I have a spreadsheet, where I record my travel and which country I'm staying in. It's usually a fairly hectic schedule, as regular readers will recall. 

Normally, and I'm not particularly proud about my carbon footprint, I will make between 40 and 50 flights in a year and spend time in about 12 countries. My second home is KL airport, and I know my way around most airports without thinking, I'm like a regular customer in a dozen business lounges.. and there are familiar faces.  Some of whom are other buyers for retail or wholesale companies. So today is a bit strange.. I'm taking my first flight in six months. 

Yesterday I had to get a Covid test, a friend told me where to go to do a saliva test.. there are lots of test places you can go, but I, like you are not particularly fond of the nasty nasal swab. So I gargled some salty liquid, spit in a tub. Hey presto.. a few hours later by whats app I received my negative result paper.. I have also booked another test as instructed in the UK and filled all the online forms in. More complicated than normal but not difficult.



We had to sit at separate tables, as a maximum of 5 per table still applies. 

It was slightly emotional saying goodbye to everyone, but it is what it is.. and of course I realise I'm luckier than most. Even so there are friends in the countries I usually visit I miss.. I have good friends in China, India, Indonesia, Nepal not to mention Slovakia and the rest of Europe. Yes. One day when this is all over there will be some grand reunion parties full of tearful emotional hugs. 

But travel now (even on business) is very difficult. So my travel blog has been a bit stagnant, for a while. 

 

Anyway it's almost Easter so at least time to chat to friends and family.. remember that this weekend the clocks will leap forward. It really is Spring.

 

That ship stuck in the Suez Canal, it could cause an almighty blockage, for sure we have a few containers caught up in that. From my house in Spain I have a good view of the Mediterranean, and big ships are often on the horizon. This one with Evergreen written down the side I have seen a couple of times. There is an app called.. Marine Radar, which I use to check what the ships are. I have checked it before with the app.. Check these screen shots from the app. This is pretty serious you can see the congestion building at each side. 



Heads up.. Might be worth stocking up now before big shortages hit. 

 

Anyway take care stay safe. 

 

David

title: My Top Importers Tip
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China.
Last week I was musing about differing asian reaction's to the Scottish bid for independence. Bad idea! I thought I was offering a few views from different perspectives, and being careful not to take sides. I just upset lots of people on both sides of the argument. If you promise not to get upset with me you can read it here. Note to self: Don't discuss politics in newsletters.
To make amends I'm going to let you in on my top importers tip.
Here in Yiwu (regular readers will know) is the worlds biggest wholesale market for small goods. That includes gifts, and at the last count 90,000 small and big business display their goods here and are up for doing a deal. We have a warehouse and office here so I visit very regularly to find the latest trends in giftware and all the stuff we stock.
First I just wanted to share with you my day in Yiwu.
Mark, our agent here has a young son he is bright as a button and has just started at junior school which happens to be close to the market area. So to save Mark taking his son to school, traveling back to the outskirts of the city to pick me up and then going back into the city all in the rush hour. I have been going on the school run, Chinese style.
Thousands of kids go to this school, so thousands of cars descend on one set of back streets. 7.30am is big breakfast time. Lots of long tables on the street outside bustling kitchens pumping out wonton soup, dumplings, fried eggs and something like crispy nan-breads. It's all jolly friendly and communal. Everyone is so well dressed, Mum's and Dad's or Grandparents and the also the trendy kids (no uniforms I note), I think it is pretty competitive here. So I'm at the middle of the table tucking into a delicious wonton soup, Mark has gone to the kitchen to procure more dumplings. Young Loui turns to the whole table (who are clearly interested in the foreign guy) and announces proudly; "My Father has lots of Lǎowài (foreign) friends.. this tall one here is just one of them" this is apparently a high status thing for a young boy. And very embarrassing for me.
Lǎowài is a word you hear a lot in China, people often comment at seeing one. Even in Yiwu which full of them, I often get asked for a picture along side someone. There are Lǎowài who make a living out of renting themselves out to business meetings to enhance the importance of a company.
Breakfast over and young son despatched to school, we head to the market. Mark has learned that one of his old school friends now runs a very successful scarf manufacturing business. They have some big orders from a huge Russian company. Naturally they have a showroom in the mega scarf market. Think of the biggest shopping centre you have been in, double that and imagine every store selling scarves. It's like that, I like to imagine just the sample scarves on show, put end to end would reach to the moon and back :)
So here's my top tip. It's called: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants.
You know the company has a very big order, you have a good connection. You ask nicely if it is possible to get the same rates if you buy from the big buyers range.
Usually you get a yes, because it is easy additional business.
It's been a good day, I'm delighted to have sourced some very tasteful rather posh, but surprisingly good value scarves which should arrive well in time for Mother's Day next year.
It's creeping up on us, don't be scared. Halloween is only a few weeks away. See our deals below..
Until next week.
Take care.
David

title: Camels and Cows and other Hero's
content_html:
Easter Greetings from India..
The last few days I have spent in Delhi seeing old suppliers and finding new ones. There's no trade fair on so it's back to basics finding new suppliers ie pounding the streets. As luck would have it a friend of mine who is a fully qualified OIH.. that's an "Old India Hand" was also in Delhi and he introduced me to a couple of wholesale handicraft areas I wasn't aware of. Found supplies of all sorts of things I have been seeking for years.. with the added advantage of my friend speaking Hindi which opened more doors. One particular warren of streets street was great, a piece of real India.. complete with camels, holy cows, holy men and buffalo carts. Right in the heart of Delhi. Some pictures below.

It's Easter - which is a time for thinking about renewal, and this time in India I can really feel a fresh breeze of renewal blowing away the dust of self interest and corruption. I can see it in little things like cleaner streets and less hassle from street vender's. Even the business deals are more straight-forward. There is an old man called Anna who set himself up in a Delhi public park and started to starve himself for better anti-corruption laws in India. Even before the hunger pangs had set in, the Indian government had capitulated to all his demands. Democracy in action. Now Anna is the biggest hero in India since Gandhi.. no exaggeration.

Talking of democracy - while checking out the central Tibetan market (not very good), I found myself in the midst of a huge Islamic anti-America march. Demanding that America stay out of Libya. My man in Delhi was panicking as he thought the mob might think my white skin was white Yankee skin.. but I just kept smiling waving and taking pictures. Since mine was the only camera around they seemed delighted to be photographed and although angry they were good natured. I stood in the mid-flow taking snaps - until my man dragged me away.
  Down with America!
  On the streets..
   Product ideas what do you think?

Take care.. and have a great Easter. If you are trading, I hope you can find some time to relax.

title: The creative heart of the world
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali, Indonesia

Yes I'm back in giftware heaven, Ubud the creative heart of all things esoteric, artistic, handicrafts and the yoga capital of the world (don't tell India).
Last week I was with our man from India (and his son) Mr Chatterjee in the city of Kuala Lumpur , a reunion after more than two years.. if you missed it you can read about it here.
Ubud sits in the Gianyar regency of Bali, and whilst you will find folk all over Bali and other parts of Indonesia making things by hand, Gianyar is ground zero for handicraft exports. Some claim the most creative people on earth live here.. people who almost can't help themselves making things day and night. Villages often specialise in strange things, I have told you about the hand carving village before, but there are towns that just make bamboo items, a whole town making silver items a glass blowing village. 

Mr Chatterjee went back to India and I cam to Bali.. but while this maybe a Yoga capital, India likes to claim they are the home of Yoga and now every year they have an  international day of Yoga day... but mostly in India where President Modi loves to show off his moves. The children's home that with the help of Mr Chatterjee AW supports got in on the act.. here are the kids doing Yoga.


In more good news one of our older kids achieved top marks in all the town schools.. it seems we have a super smart guy.. Mr Chatterjee went to congratulate him.


Mr Kundo is the home manager here with our Super-star and Mr Chatterjee.

Meanwhile back in Ubud I have spent the last few days visiting suppliers, checking work in progress and reviewing potential new products. 
Ringo, his assistant: Bondhan and me buzzing round the villages  meeting up with our old suppliers and friends.. it's one of my favourite things to do.. 
Bondhan and I had an evening out in Ubud, we went to see a band that we know.. what I can tell you is Ubud is busy again and by far the biggest visitors are Russians, and all the ones I have chatted to are not really on holiday, they claim to be digital nomads and are not planning on going home anytime soon. 


Ringo & Bondhan in action.

I was last here only a few months ago.. last time Bondhan who is a trained graphic designer worked on a range of Mandela inspired cushions..I fed him the ideas he drafted them up and working with our supplier we developed this luxury range of linen cushions with mandala designs.


OK simple I guess, and maybe just an idea who's time had come.. But our idea has been copied and now you can see pretty similar cushions  in showrooms and gift shops everywhere. We went to the main city market in Denpasar, a large multi-storey craft market in the heart of the town.  Every other textile store has our cushions..same look and feel.. Stores in Ubud have them selling to Russians and Australian tourists.. I said to Bondhan.. look your work has gone viral.. It's not the first time this happened.. years ago I developed the Hati-Hati angel.. and now you can find it in most gift shops. 

So already have a few ideas in the pipeline, but you have any suggestions - I'd love to hear from you.
At the end of the day new products are what your customers want and drive better profitable sales for your business.. 

Hopefully Coco will be here by the time you get next weeks newsletter..

Take care, 

David

title: Kindness in Troubling Times
content_html:
Greetings 

The times they are a changing.. these are an unprecedented and difficult time, the best we can do is love and support one another.

Last week I was telling you about the strange and troubling flights from India to Bali. You can read about it here. It was Friday the 13th, but that seems more like a month ago than a week.
Here in Bali, I'm with Tomas we have been keeping as calm as possible and carrying on. In the last few days Bali has emptied like a plug has been pulled.. people are leaving.. no-one is coming.. flights are cancelled wholesale.
Suddenly Tomas and I are rare foreigners, certainly in the areas where our suppliers are. I understand how the Chinese people in Sheffield were feeling in early February when this news was breaking.. Now we are the one people run from, turn away, try to stop breathing near us. It's understandable, I don't blame anyone. Anyway, they are still kind and nice to us.. not mean. We wear masks, use the Namaste greeting - everyone does now - and keep a good social distance. I'm sure you are doing the same.
Here there is no lock-down as yet - officially there has only been one case. But almost no-one believes that everyone is taking it seriously. Though no-one is panic buying, masks and sanitisers are sold out. And I'm told turmeric, both fresh and oils have rocketed in price. Turmeric is a super food as you know..  and locally they believe it boosts the immune system.. which I believe is true, but whether it helps protect against covid-19 who knows.

We are doing our best to carry on. I was here before the India trip and had a number of projects underway. At that time I was ramping up orders to cover for stock not coming from China.. now the whole ball game has up-ended. Who knows what stock we will need in Europe in two or three months time when our orders here land in Europe. Do we call a halt to everything? I thought about it.. and decided no that was wrong. Firstly this island is 60% dependant on the tourist traded, it's just dried up over night. If we pull our business also it will severely effect the families of our suppliers - because there is no safety net nothing else to fall back on.. And I can tell you they are surprised, grateful and thankful that we continue to support them.
Normally busy streets are empty.. it's happening the world over..


Secondly in times of trouble people's instinct is to support each other, in these isolating times it can't be done with a hug, but a gift is still an option. With online ordering so much easier and doorstep deliveries the norm, then I believe and have faith that the artisan products from Bali when they arrive in Europe will still wing there a way to a loving home. It will be online trading.. more than likely.. are you prepared.

In times of trouble - people help each other more - there is an out break of kindness, kindness is going viral - from the brave and heroic Doctors and nurses risking there lives to protect society, to the neighbours checking on the old folks, calling up the lonely, We will get through this together and many will suffer, but lets hope in the end at least the world will be a kinder more loving place.  It is stressful, every night after finishing work here I spend until the early hours dealing with rapidly changing situations. Almost everyone despite problems and worries is a hero.. pulling together for the greater good. 

You must have your own set of worries and stress. Take heart - this too will pass - I wish you all the kindness and goodwill - the more you give the more karma will flow..

Shortly I will be self-isolating here in Bali - it's nothing new actually - they do it every year Nyepi or Bali New Year is the famous Day of Silence. The night before is normally a big carnival with huge fantastic Ogoh-ogoh statues paraded through the streets and wild parties - but all that has been cancelled of course - the day of silence will remain. And why not.. they close the airport for Nyepi (it's already 80% closed), all roads are out of use, all Bali people stay at home, hotel guests stay in the hotel and are not allowed out. Speaking is by whisper, TV and internet is cut.. it really is so quiet you can only hear the birds. It's a day for reflection. And that's something we can all do with.

Our new drop-shipping department came online just in time.. have you signed up yet? AW-Dropship.com   this is your route to staying in business even if your store is closed. No need to stock anything - just sell online and we can do the rest, so you can still get organised and trade.


Take care please.. call up your friends, be kind, wash your hands.. 

As they say in Indonesia.. Hati Hati - it means take special care.


Hati Hati!

More news next week. 

David

title: Game Changers at AW
content_html:
Greetings from Malaga, Spain

 

I'm in AW-Artisan warehouse in Malaga, and even though it is Friday 13th they still find an excuse for a party. (see below).

Meanwhile it's preparation time for our up-coming trip around asia..  the first leg starts tomorrow.

Last week I was telling you about Catching the Zeitgeist and catching sweets in Spain.. lots of people responded to that.. if you missed it you can catch up here.


It's Friday 13th…but don't panic. After all (as they say) Friday the 13th is unlucky for some... and if you think about it every day is unlucky for somebody somewhere...   numerology says… the sacred number 13 is considered to be a very karmic number in numerology. It is associated with the divine, and is said to bring good luck and prosperity to those who embrace it. In fact, many people believe that the number 13 brings about change, which can often lead to a positive outlook. 

Yes, so here is some Ancient Wisdom.. when bad luck comes (and it will) then embrace it as nothing innately bad but an opportunity to learn, maybe to change, to grow as a human. Remember what doesn't kill makes you stronger..

The Ancient Wisdom story is like that.. we had more than our share of bad luck and despite that have thrived..  if you didn't read our back story you can find it here.

 

Some strange problems in India.. relating to the banking system. For planning trips around India I often use MakeMyTrip.com - it's like Expedia in India. When I tried to login to my account.. I got this message.



Slightly worrying. Even with VPN enabled I cannot access.

OK so let's just use Expedia.. I can set up bookings but every credit card payment fails for Indian airlines..

I try booking directly with the individual airlines (I have a total of 12 flights to book for our tour) - every one gives error messages.

So I use the Airasia app - it's really easy to use and for outside India is working fine.. as soon as I try to book an India flight I booted out of the App.

Something big (and bad) is going on.. I hope this is not another bad luck event in the offing.. 

Anyway once I realise the problem there is an easy work around, Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) books all the flights for us. 

I called my friend in Goa, who is well connected and owns a hotel there.. He has no idea, has no British customers these days, all his guests he tells me are crazy old Russians. Ermm.. is that a clue..

 

Anyway - onwards and upwards - thinking positive.. 

We have some great products this week just arrived.. including some new Singing Bowls - from India. I'm always excited when a product I have been involved with arrives. 

But these days there are plenty of products at AW that are created, developed and arrive without my help.. I was pleasantly surprised to see these Spell Candles - launching today (Friday the 13th) .. especially since this was one of the most requested products by our lovely customers.

 

Game Changer

At this time of year - I start to think out-side-of-the-box.. and encourage everyone at AW to think of something that will change the game. "Guys!!" I say - we need a game changer product. Something that is going to supercharge our customers' businesses, something that will take everyone to a new level. Last week I was telling you about Chat GPT.. and everyone is now on it.. That' is anything is a Game Changer.. how can this be used to change the game..

It's brainstorming time.. 

At the end of the day (as I tirelessly repeat myself) it's about the product. a product is the most important part of any business. Yes every part of your business is essential, but without amazing products you have nothing..

We are working hard to find you those products at AW..

 

Today might be an unlucky day for some but actually for me it is a special day.. and the team at AW-Artisan Spain surprised me just now with a cake.



Yes, today is my birthday :)

 

The years go by.. and time moves on.. but I'm lucky and immensely grateful to be surrounded by young, enthusiastic, good hearted and talented people at AW..  it's a pleasure everyday to work with all the good folk of AW.  I heard something the other day I want to share..  (I asked Dall-E to make me some art to express it)..



Take care and have a wonderful weekend.. 

 

Next week's newsletter is from somewhere in Asia.. 

 

David

title: David's AW News: Another Gift Opportunity. Team India.
content_html:
Greetings from Aerocity, Delhi.


Happy Valentine's Weekend!

We have just arrived in India from Kathmandu. Toni and I took an Indigo (very short) flight down to Delhi T3, landing at 3pm. Bondhan, our man in Indonesia, braved Air India and flew from Denpasar to Delhi T3, also landing at 3pm, although a much longer flight. The plan was to meet in the luggage hall. What could possibly go wrong? Amazingly, it worked, and we easily found each other. It's Bondhan's very first trip to India. So this should be interesting, especially since later we will be going hardcore India. 
But the first evening is at an airport hotel - in an area called Aerocity.. Basically, all the hotels in the world have built a hotel here. We are staying at a Lemon Tree Hotel, a lovely, well-loved Indian brand that famously employs disabled and disadvantaged people. Recycled water in the toilets, etc. It's very woke.. Trump would hate it. We loved it.

This morning, Chatterjee (our man in India) came, and because it's Chatterjee's (big) birthday and Bondhan's first trip, I said, let's go and visit somewhere special.. So we went to a real Ancient Wisdom place, the Qutb Minar complex.. Where we took some promo shots (kind of) for our up and coming Travel Blessing Scarves (see below)..
Team India.
Bondhan (our man from Indonesia), me, Chatterjee (our man in India) and Toni (our man in Spain).
Last week I was telling you about arriving in Kathmandu. And all the great people there.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Kathmandu Update

Well, this week has been a rolling development of ideas, samples and redesigns.. we have been working in three main areas, and I feel quite pleased at progress.. 

Progress in Kathmandu, I have to say, there is a feeling of things happening in Nepal, a certain buzz.. in Thamel, two new smart hotels opened, lots of cool cafes and hip bars. After the Gen Z protests and the overthrow of the government, (elections will be held next month..) It seems to me they were getting on better just with an interim government, but what do I know?

Since we were last here, a new hotel opened in the heart of Thamel, twelve stories high, inside it is as traditional Nepali wood carved almost old fashioned, take the lift to the 12th, and they have a restaurant and event area built inside a four-sided glass box. Ultra modern. Mr Padam (our gentleman agent) invited us to visit.

While we were there, a local event was in full swing..  An event I have never heard of - a Weaning Party.
I mean, what the heck is a Weaning Party… Nepal Style

Flowers everywhere. Pink drapes. Bright cushions. Traditional dress.
A small child at the centre of it all — dressed like royalty — marking that cultural milestone: first solid food. Family gathered. Laughter. Photos. Pride.

In Nepal, it seems life’s transitions are celebrated properly. Community and ritual are important.

And I’m standing there thinking… It's another GIFT opportunity.. 

We talk about “storytelling” in retail all the time.
But this — this is storytelling in real life.

Every object in that room had context. Symbolism. Craft.

Which brings me neatly back to why I’m here. There’s something else here, too.

You see young people everywhere — ambitious, creative, restless. Some dream of leaving. Some dream of building things right here. It’s a city in transition.

And maybe that’s why I love it.  It’s not polished or predictable. But it’s alive. And the artisans are really on it.  All sorts of bright ideas we can work together on. 

This trip, Toni and I We have been focused on three artisan suppliers. One new Felt Supplier (cute things sell) we like.. developing more artisan Lokta paper notebooks (stationery is a growing gifting area), and with our old friend Mr Suman, our textile guy, we are working on Blessings scarves.. 

Talking about gifting opportunities.. (my theme at the moment) - here in Nepal, so many young people dream of leaving - go to work in Dubai or Türkiye - they can send money home and have an adventure. At the airport, families all turn up to see their loved ones - seems like a whole village saying goodbye to one young guy. And they drape him in a Blessing scarf. There is tremendous Ancient Wisdom in this..

Here are some guys at the airport, and here's Toni in our version. Perfect for our Nomad Sari (spirit of travel) brand. The world is actually bursting with Gifting Opportunities.. for example, sold right with a story could be a great gift for travel stores, airport shops, etc.

OK, so talking about gifting opportunities..  Valentine's Day is upon us - hope your weekend is full of love and romance!  Next up is Mother's Day - and at AW, we have the goods!

Meanwhile, by co-incidence as we arrive in India, in the UK, an India incense container arrived. With beautiful products from one of our favourite family business suppliers.. your customers are going to love this.. 

Holly has been busy.. focusing our newish fashion jewellery brand, NYMPH brand. Sandra designed and is selling wonderfully well. Honestly, a super Gifting Opportunity! A really well-explained video, well done, Holly! Please check it out and leave a comment and like ..

Well, Valentine’s week kinda started in Kathmandu… and now we’re continuing in Delhi.

From prayer flags to big city vibe and traffic honking. Different rhythm. Same energy.

I just want to say I’m grateful — for the friendships, the artisans, the ideas taking shape… and for your support that makes all this possible.

After all these years, I still feel lucky to be doing this. Thank you.

Stay tuned for next week’s update — India continues to unfold.

Happy Valentine’s.

David

PS 

The awesome pictures above are thanks to this nice security guard.. he knew all the best places to get a good shot.
