title: Hidden Danger
content_html:
Greetings from Sunny Sheffield

Last week I was telling you about some good news and tales of our road to recovery. You can read about it here.
It's now been 27 days since the AW inferno, and what the team here has achieved in that time is almost impossible to believe. Everyday we are putting more products back on-line, everyday finding better ways to ship more orders, everyday everyone is pulling all the stops out. The spirit of recovery is burning on full power. Everyday we pass a small milestone, everyday we recover another few steps.

Thank you for your support, both with continuing to place orders and with the continued messages of good wishes and encouragement. The AW community spirit is fantastic and really holding us together.
Almost everybody has been supportive, for this I am grateful, because the ones that are not really break your heart.


Yesterday I spoke to the fire officer trying to get a copy of the forensic report, like everyone, I want to know how the AW inferno happened. The two insurance companies involved and the fire service have commissioned forensic reports but no-one it seems is prepared or able to give me a copy as they say it is only available to interested parties! I'm keenly interested I protested, nobody is more (insert expletive) interested than me!.. I told the fire officer, and he said yes I can see that. I cannot give you the report but I can tell you what it says.. then he said "This is a one in a million chance accident, followed by a perfect storm of events". What happened he thought, and he thought the other reports would agree - is that a particular residue of oil had reacted with the cotton lint inside used face masks in the bin creating a slow burn chemical reaction. We had been told by health and safety to keep IBC those large containers of the non-flammable oils outside, and the bin was near an IBC.. the reaction started at 23.23 in the evening - six hours after it had been last touched, within 20 minutes the even the non-flammable oil was hot enough to burn and the fire big enough to reach the building , within the hours - even though the fire brigade came quickly the whole block had burned down in an hour. It's all on CCTV. It's monumental, like a biblical disaster.

 

So the insurance company are sitting on this report, to try and protect their legal position, they are, it would appear trying to riddle out of liability on a technicality. This makes me really angry, because surly that fact that FACE MASKS CAN CAUSE FIRES.. should be big news no?? Anyway they are down in London and don't reply my calls, they don't rush to inform us of anything after 27 days I finally received a call from a "private number" to apologise for not calling us back, from a guy who would only give me his first name.

So we are getting on with the recovery, AW is big enough to recover without help from the insurance, but we will fight them until we get justice. This kind of uncaring hanging us out to dry is incredibly distressing on top of everything else.
If anyone one has advice on large insurance claims, because me or anyone I know has any experience of this. Yes we have a lawyer who specialises in this lined up, but not engaged yet.


Please spread the news, dispose of those medical face masks carefully, not in contact with any oily substance, put them in a plastic bag when disposing of them.

title: David's AW News: 7 Surprising Surprises
content_html:
Greetings from....yes surprise! (I'm back) in Bali.. 

Hope you guys are well, enjoying the heatwave and the Olympics - last week I was telling you about how HOT HOT HOT it was in Spain and how we almost melted on our team bonding beach meal. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Surprise number one.. Since then I have been travelling... first to Kula Lumpa for a few days. Mostly to work with Raul (AW IT Wizard) and then to get my annual body check up.. 

Well Coco flew back to China (she is very busy). And then to get here I took a KLM flight from Malaga to Amsterdam. After a pleasant sojourn in the updated KLM lounge I took the flight to Singapore. I just had time to wander around that beautiful airport - check out the gardens.. then a short flight to Kuala Lumpur international airport. Finally a Grab taxi downtown. I arrived a little bit jet lagged.. sleep hardly at all and then have an early appointment at Gleneagles Hospital KL. I checked out the view from the breakfast room of my hotel (Lanson Place) on the 48th floor..  since I was here last they have built what they call a Megatall building called Merdeka 118. It's SURPRISING! Get your mind around that thing!



Compared to the other skyscrapers it's just stupendous. Actually the second tallest building in the world. Not officially completed yet..
So that was Surprise number one..


Then I went to the Gleneagles Hospital - about 15 minutes by taxi for an 8am registration. The lobby of the hospital is like a five star hotel.. it's a bit confusing. There are uniformed staff, valet parking and I guy in a tux playing a grand piano.. I mean that's quite surprising no? (No.2).  Imagine if you got this on the NHS! - on the 5th floor is the health screening department. They can do about 30 people in a four hour sesion. The lady on the reception remembers me from two years ago.. welcome back Mr David, I have your previous report and records.  I was given a face mask and asked politely to wear it.. felt surprisingly like I was back in the pandemic. Everyone without exception customers and staff wearing a mask. I'm given a number TK014 and it pops up on the monitors with the message "go to room 5" - I go from room to room for the next 4 hours with barely a minute to sit down. Xrays, blood test, stress test, eye, ear and skin tests.. CT scans, poked, prodded and pricked and heaven knows what else they did. And through it all the staff are absolutely delightful, kind and chatty. 

I have been told not to eat for 8 hours before coming.. at a certain point after the scans they tell me I can visit the breakfast buffet.. The jolly staff are a mix of Malay, Indian and ethnic Chinese.. They speak between themselves a curious mix of Malay/English/Mandarin.. which I seem surprisingly to be able to pretty much understand.

They gave me a voucher for lunch in the posh DOME restaurant just by the lobby.  And was told to come back for consultation with Doctor Wong at 3.15pm. Doctor Wong, a nice lady, tells me everything is Surprisingly good.. I'm given a fat folder containing all the results nicely printed and presented, a CD with more data. Same DAY! For goodness sake.. She talks me through everything, doesn't even attempt to sell me anything and answers all my questions. I drink too much, but my liver and kidneys are surprisingly pretty.. she says I'm lucky, probably genetic. I'm so happy.. 

How much does it cost I hear you ask.. well I had the male premium package (check absolutely everything) - about £250.. Surprising no? That was Surprise no.3


Spend some intense days working on a deep dive into the details of a web update (see below).. Then I fly on Batik air to Denpaser, Bali. Bondhan and Ringo meet me at the airport. Bali has got crazy busy, don't come now.. it's just a log jam. They are complaining about over tourism in Spain.. it's happening in Bali also. I even struggled to find a decent hotel room. 

 

But today I visited the warehouse, I'm surprised to find a lot of changes since I was last here. Now we have a solid dedicated team. A specialist QC lady called Atiek who administers checks at all stages of packing. The warehouse is better organised, the office has been cleaned out and redecorated and we have a brand new revamped Showroom. Wow.. I'm very surprised (no.4) how much things have changed. Then Bondhan takes me across the road to the small warehouse we acquired last time I was here..



A Surprising New Venture (No.5)..

Our warehouse is called Frangipani Warehouse locally. Did you know that the fragrance of Nagchampa incense comes from the yellow frangipani flowers? Here in Bali the frangipani grows everywhere, streets are lined with trees. The flowers are used in offerings and young girls wear the flowers in their hair. The frangipani is totally embedded into the culture of Bali. 

Ringo told me a story.. about a Japanese company that came to this area a few years back. They put a big poster on the side of the road saying "We buy Frangipani 40,000rp per kilo". Ringo said everyone and their aunty was out early in the morning collecting the freshly fallen frangipani petals.. it was like free money, get them weighed in and walk away with hard cash.  

So as a new venture I wanted to try and distill our own frangipani oil.. but this is not easy.. first step Bondhan and his wife went on a training course in Solo Java.. learning all the tricks of the trade. Last year we went to visit distillers of clove oil deep in the clove forests of northern Bali.  Last time I was here we acquired a new warehouse. Yesterday our first mini still came.. If we make it work then we will buy a larger one.. if that works we can fit maybe 24 of them in the space we have. My vision is guys in lab coats in a spotless space looking after rows of gently stewing machines and a heavenly fragrance coming drip by drip.  I can't wait to put up our sign " We buy Frangipani petals".. probably on Facebook.. 



Bondhan waiting for the first drop to appear. Update next week.

 

 

Finally the BIGGEST Surprise (no.6).. perchance you visit an AW website today.. like AncientWisdom.biz  you might discover something quite SURPRISING.. that is Gold Reward Discounts are massively back.. and right across the product range now more than 6000 products have Volume and Gold Reward Discounts.. Eg order 4 from a family range and get a 20% discount.. or if you are a Gold Reward member you can order just 1 item and get the same discount.. Discounts range from 5-20% and on almost everything. PLUS  - there will be more ways to qualify for Gold Reward Benefits.. and many MORE SURPRISING BENEFITS are in the pipeline..



New format order box is already there.. more stuff coming over the next few days..

So that's Surprise (I'm losing count).. I think it's phew.. No.7

 

And surprise surprise we have a couple of containers booked into the UK warehouse - more new products.. Rodrigo and his team are working hard to get them on sale for the weekend.

Since we started rolling out the Gold Reward revamp.. it's getting Surprisingly Busy.. the shipment of Soap Flowers (LSF code) almost sold out within a few hours.. Orders flooding the warehouse. 

I'm proud of our team in the UK.. we actually shipped a record number of orders in July..our best July ever. And pretty much keeping the orders flowing for same or next day despatch.. 

Well done team!

 

Plus have you checked out our Surprising New Search bar? Try it.. customers are telling us they are discovering surprising things they never knew we stocked. 

 

Wishing you a wonderful and surprising weekend!

More updates next Friday.

 

David

title: It's a Summer Shake-up
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 

Welcome to June, it's officially Summer and the sun is shining.

 

Yes back in Spain after a long time, we arrived yesterday evening on a rawkus hen and stag laden Ryanair flight from Manchester to Malaga. All good humour and long (endless) queues for the toilet, I'm not sure everyone made it haha... it reminds me that this is full on wedding season - and the greatest gift to gift traders everywhere. At AWGifts (our EU distribution) they just had their busiest month ever and totally driven by wedding season gifts, Soap Flowers used by craft people selling next-level.

Plus Father's Day is almost upon us - and happy that our range this year is (don't want to brag) is the BIG DADDY range - the best we have ever had at AW. After a few weeks at HQ - it's nice to leave on a high and head home for a bit.

Last week I was telling you about how if you just join the dots, amazing things can happen, and I'm encouraging our AW teams to do that.. if you missed it you can catch up here.


This week has been a bit of a whirl, a bit of a reshuffle (in fact), after chatting to all the key people at AW, applying a smidgen of radical thinking and a dollop of team reshaping.. I'm hoping that the summer shake-up will inspire more creativity and ultimately more amazing products for your business. The stuff in the pipeline is great, but I want everything to be what you think.. is WTNL! (wow-thats-next-level!) If you have been following this newsletter you will know about the epic tour of Nepal and India (almost 500 new products on the way) my time back in China (another 200) and the steady stream of beautiful things from our team in Indonesia. Add to that our home grown aromatics, soap and bathroom items from AW-Aromatics in Sheffield and you can see why I'm excited about the next few months. Stay with us if you want to be first with the good stuff.

 

In the summer shake-up you might like to welcome Daniella to the Dropshipping team - she has lots of ideas and is excited to take over. Lucy has moved to customer service at AW-Aromatics and is likewise keen to shake things up (in a good way).. 


We just received an Indonesian and China container this week.. with lots of popular things coming back into stock.. (including perfect for Father's Day) Mens Bracelets Sets.  (see below).

Summer-Shake-Up continues..

At AW you will know we have always done things differently. For example you know that we don't do trade shows or employ salespeople. Back in the day, rather than sales reps we used to mail mini catalogues. Then we were the first to start email marketing,  then we were the very first B2B wholesaler to offer online ordering and next day delivery. Amazingly no-one copied us for a couple of years.. and at that time we grew like crazy. 

This newsletter and other email marketing has always been our main way of connecting with our amazing trading partners like you. But I feel most people get their updates from social media, and anyay there is far too much happening around AW for one newsletter on a Friday. Of course we have all the social media accounts.. but we are experimenting with other ways to keep you informed with new deals, product launches and news of currently fast-selling stock. 

Are you following these social media accounts?  


INSTAGRAM  - FACEBOOK - PINTEREST - LINKEDIN - YOUTUBE



Also watch out for breaking news via your What's App account, we are experimenting with this media now.. if you'd like to be first and be included (and can chat with us directly) just click on the What'sApp icon and request adding to the AW news group. 

 

Hope you feel inspired to do your own Summer-Shake-Up.. 

Anyway, have a wonderful weekend. Thank you as always for your support, feedback and ideas.

More news next week as I visit the fun-loving team at AW-Artisan at our Malaga warehouse. 


David

title: From Simple To Simply Crazy
content_html:
Greetings from Bali

90 days.. I can't believe it. 
Last week I was telling you about the sacred oils of Bali.. you can read about it here. 

It's 90 days in one place, 90 days I didn't wear socks or shoes, or trousers. 90 days in shorts and flip-flops. And maybe you are in shorts now in Blighty as June 2020 hits new highs. But for me it's 90 days of developing new products with Ringo.. the first batch of which has just arrived in the UK. See details below.

Well it's 90 days not just in flip-flops but also a mask. Unlike the UK, they quickly made it mandatory to wear a mask out-doors... anywhere out-side of your own residence. And plenty of police, army and local security people to check this is happening.
And I believe this and the travel lock-down has made a difference, the infection rate in Bali is very low for the population. In the beginning you could only buy masks in the pharmacy, and mostly they were sold out. Then gradually the local producers stepped up and made masks, pretty soon everyone is selling masks and mask fashion is evolving at a rapid pace.

I was here in February if you remember, then went to India for three weeks with Tomas, just as the pandemic really started to cause waves. We came back to Bali, because it was impossible to go to China as planned.  The fruits of the first visit are just landing in the UK. So from February to now I have witnessed the changing fashion of masks.. and pretty much bought them all.. gone from simple, to cotton plain, patterned, to batik traditional designs to simply crazy. Even the police and security guys are sporting the crazy ones..


    Ringo and I sporting the latest fashion in masks.

Last week I was telling you about the herbal oils of Bali, which turn out to be big business. My back went.. not badly, I could still walk but quite stiff and painful. Ringo gave me local herbal medicine, and one of our suppliers, pulled out his bottle of Kutus Kutus and insisted on treating me. He massaged my feet, insisting that the oil would work via my feet best, but the pain is in my back I told him.. yes I know, then he rubbed it in my forehead, behind my ears, and the back of my neck very gently. Finally, he applied to my back.. amazingly the pain and the stiffness - at least for the next hour or so gone. He opened his mouth and squirted some in the back of his throat and swallowed it.. erm .. no thanks I said, I'm feeling much better already.

    Traditional back treatment.

title: Problems with Whales
content_html:
Greetings from Spain where I'm working with Toni and the team at AW-Artisan.

As England enter's lockdown for the second time and Liverpool gets totally tested we enter unknown territory.
Last lockdown, the things that were selling fast at AW flipped dramatically.. seems totally different things sell online than in shops.
Keep reading for some potentially profitable insights and what I like to call - retail opportunities. Plus we have a growing problem with whales..


First I have to report that the "A" team in the AW warehouse have been really making things happen. Packing all time record numbers of orders - catching up and even getting on top of the flow of orders. For the first time in months (if not years) we can actually quote 1-3 working days dispatch time. It's been a huge team effort, from everyone including tweaking software (thanks Raul in KL) to devising impressive systems (Tomas on form) to making it happen (James & Kane), but thanks must go to our all star order picking & packing teams.. Great work.. 

 

Last week we had two containers arrive from Indonesia with Natural Coconut Lamps on them. Lots of people had registered to be notified when they came back in stock.. so the automatic system sent out the messages and within minutes orders were coming super fast. Both shipments sold out within the day of arrival. Most of those orders were from legitimate AW customers.. but I worry that some were from "Whales" - these are ticket tout type traders who buy up stock to take it off the market, and thus get to control the onward supply. I think it's not nice.. I'm looking into how to control this. It's great when a product is well accepted but unfair played like this. You can read last week newsletter here.
One person who is really happy (and I'm delighted for them) is Pak Odang from Ubud. We gave him a reorder that is basically called.. we will buy all you can possibly make.. 



A happy man.

With his wife - in charge of the shades and his eldest son - in charge of shaping the leaves, they can produce quite a bit of stock. But one thing I learned about the artisans of Indonesia, they don't want to go too big, there is no way they will take on a factory and lots of staff. As long as they can make enough for a reasonable lifestyle they have no wish to upset their work life balance.  And maybe there is something to be said for that.


Other products that are being hit by "whales" I feel are Dinner Candles, Atomisers, Soap Flowers and some Essential Oils.. all things that seemed to sell well in the last lock-down. If you want to be notified when stock comes back online - you can click that little envelope next to where it says out of stock.


Now that we are getting on top of the orders - it's worth noting that you don't need to panic buy to get stock.. anyway if you order small and often - our Gold Reward system applies automatically and discounts - Gold reward applies when you order within 30 days of your last order. If you are particularly pushed for stock quickly - we have just switched back on (by popular demand) priority shipping. We switched it off when it became apparent if simply wasn't fair when only priority orders were getting shipped and everyone else had to wait. But now it seems we can handle it fairly. 


Trouble in China. Lack of containers..
It's been an ongoing problem all summer. It's like this.. at the beginning of the pandemic the shipping companies panicked and mothballed a percentage of ships. Then it turned out that they overdid it and now there is a worldwide shortage of slots on boats. In the past as soon as Ringo (in Indonesia) or Coco (In China) had enough stock in company warehouses to fill a container they would message Bryant (our manly import manager in the UK) who would get quotes and book a container with a shipping agent..  The shipping agent's local guy would call our agent to say the truck will arrive with an empty container at 7am Thursday.. and you can get organised with a loading team, packing lists and last minute deliveries. The truck would arrive on the dot and you load it.
Now even an hour before it comes our agents are getting calls to say no container is available, and asking us to rebook. Bryant has been asked to pay "guaranteed booking fees" which we have paid and then had containers - even so - cancelled. It's like a bloodbath out there.. the big boys are pulling strings and stealing our containers. Coco was even asked for a bribe to get our actually booked container to actually arrive. She was hopping mad.. at one point last week she had four containers of stock in our China warehouse, (it's designed for two) even the offices were full of cartons, the candle factory full.. and even had to leave some stuff in the carpark overnight. 
Of course at AW we never pay bribes, but Coco's fury and anger, Bryants persuasion eventually got us some containers. Needless to say we are going to run out of some faster selling stock because of this.



Meanwhile.. we have some magic new stock coming online.. some great deals. Dropshipping is adding new stock also.. check out AW-Dropship.com  (also almost on next day delivery) .


Have a peaceful weekend, don't stress.. stay safe.


David

title: Last day / Goodbye Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Bali - this is my last day here.

Last week I was telling you about my last day with Coco before her return to China, if you missed it you can read about it here.
Coco's journey back home has taken a ridiculous amount of time and trouble. After being delayed for 22 days in Jakarta she finally got a flight to Hong Kong, where she was obliged to spend 3 days in quarantine before she could fly to mainland China - city of Xaimen , where she was taken from the airport to a government quarantine centre - 7 days. Then she took a train (seven hours) back to Yiwu.. where she was met and taken for 3 days of quarantine. As I write this she is waiting patiently for a knock on the door to say she is free to go. 
Despite all this she remains positive, has been working everyday, placing and chasing orders with suppliers and twice a day practicing Yoga. Soon she will see her grandchildren who I know she has missed dearly.

Listening to Putin ranting and raving, you do wonder if we are living in the last days. Ubud is practically Russian, lots of young and not so young Russian runaways settling in here. There are Russian play groups for kids, there is something called the Ubud Club out in the sticks practically a small village for Russians. Are we living in the last days?
Who knows? But I know this is my last day in Indonesia for a while. Living and working with the most gentle, kind and humble people is an honour and pleasure and I really don't want to go.

I think I have told you before one of my favourite things is driving around the rural villages with Ringo, seeking out artisans to produce products for AW (and your customers). As we drive from village to village, we often pass local ceremonies - almost everyday something somewhere is happening. And Ringo will explain to me the particular event and what it all means. I learn quite a bit about the unique Balinese Hindu  traditions. Which I feel are the least religious and the most ceremonial. Almost nothing is restrictive, everything is to be in balance, acceptance and tolerance are built-in. 

Some ceremonies are little, maybe just locals making offerings for the Full Moon. Others are grand and impressive.. This ceremony in Ubud I wanted to share with you..



Ringo would often explain about the Tri Hita Karana the philology underpinning the daily life and attitudes of Balinese people.  In a nutshell:  Tri Hita Karana means..  Tri= three, hita=happiness, karana=elements. The elements can be summed up as: God-Humans-Nature. Finding balance between these three leads to happiness and well-being.  These ideas of balanced relations between God, Humans and Nature.. is literally woven into the art of Bali. 
So it was going to happen.. working with a young local Balinese designer and with help from Bondhan and produced by a family in one of those villages a range of bangles inspired by the Tri Hita Karna. See below.
Made  with aromatic wooden beads and elements representing the three elements, each bangle is inspired by a different element of the Tri Hita Karana - with information in each gift box. Lot's of work has gone into making these.. so I hope you can stock and support.

Also just arrived - Coconut Fruit Bowls - sets of three.. How more natural can you get? The same guy and his family who makes the Natural Coconut Lamps, produced these and also a range of Coconut leaf wind chimes.
It's all arriving in the UK - just as I'm leaving. Of course the next wave of products that we have been working on this time will not arrive in Europe until Spring 2023..  It's like the cycle of life.. round and round.

From here I will go to Kuala Lumpur to meet Raul (our IT wizard) then to Spain, where I will see Tomas and Toni, and be reunited with my favourite team (well in Spain). 
Then I will go to the UK - where lots of stuff is happening - there will be a lot to report.. 

Stay tuned.. the journey continues.

Have a wonderful calm and balanced weekend.

David

PS Coco just messaged me - her phone turned green and she is finally free to leave quarantine at the end of her month-long journey back home.Then  minutes later she gets the news that there have been cases found in Yiwu and the city is to go into lock-down.  When will this madness end?

title: David's AW News: Drama and should I go?
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Where the temperature has fallen to around 30c much more comfortable.. I was telling you about the heat (40c plus) in last week's news and much more.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

This week we have been running everyday. Tomas, Coco and me.. running round our suppliers making things happen at pace as only they can in China - and especially in Yiwu.

If you can make it here you can make it anywhere! It's a Yiwu state of mind...I'm sure there should be a hip-hop song about it.



Yiwu City - you can make it here. Actually you can make almost anything here.

Correction. Re - Tax on candles..

Slight correction on last week's newsletter.. where I mentioned: we just got news that the EU and the UK are imposing (Trump like) tariffs on candles of 75% from this month... well the UK is not imposing this (so far) just the EU.. I understand that the EU is trying to protect candle manufacturers from cheap Chinese imports.. but have they thought this through? TEMU can still ship and no doubt will ship even more candles using the de minimis rule and pay zero taxes. At least when we import, we are paying taxes on sales and profits and some duty on import. All that the EU will lose. The candles will still flow via online marketplaces even more disruptive for EU manufacturers - so actually shooting themselves in the foot.  WHAT A BIG MESS.


Russian Shungite & Temu

We often get asked for Shungite gemstones.. I have seen it available in India and China. But Shungite is only available from one geographical location in the world. That's a town called Shunga in the Karelia Region of Russia - so of course we cannot and will not offer this product. However, go to Temu and search for Shungite and you will be swamped with listings.. Now it's possible that what's shown there is fake Shungite (Tourmaline would pass), but not everything can be and anyway Russian products are widely available in China these days - so supply would be easy. Think about that.. Temu is a backdoor for sanctioned Russian products using the de minimis rule. I'm notifying the guy at the BBC.. if this Russian product can arrive though the Temu back door what else can?



Meanwhile... Denpasar Drama

If it's not one thing it's another.. In Indonesia.. if you didn't see the news - following the riots sparked by the hashtag #NEPOKIDS  - extreme weather has descended on Bali - horrendous rainfall then massive floods throughout the island and in Denpasar city.. Bondhan and Debbie who work for AW in Bali have had their home flooded, as have many people in the area. Mudslides, flash foods and fallen trees have caused havoc with a serious death toll. It's pretty bad.. I almost feel guilty that our warehouse and offices so far have been spared any damage. Our prayers go to those affected and we are helping where we can. Debbie sent me these pictures.



Kathmandu Chaos. 

Also in Kathmandu - where we have many suppliers.. is facing the worst crisis in 20 years.. You must have seen the news.. A couple of our supplies that are also friends and live in that area have been updating me.. It's been horrendous. This started with the #Nepokids hashtag in Indonesia - the sons and daughters of the corrupt elite living flashy lifestyles while  ordinary young people are struggling to even find work. If it's bad in Indonesia this phenomenon is much worse in Nepal. The government in Nepal (heavily influenced by China) used the same playbook and closed down social media under some pretext. That was a massive mistake because 70% of Nepali households have a family member working abroad.. cutting social media was like cutting off family.. people got very angry.  The city and other parts of Nepal have been in chaos.. the last few days.. one of our suppliers sent me these pictures.



Police attacking people even in a temple.

Well here's the thing due to go to Kathmandu next week.. before travelling on to India.. stay tuned.. Should I still go? Or cancel?


But we have a GOLD REWARD AMNESTY week coming up.. It means if you didn't order for a while.. you can get maximum discounts.. and then keep ordering within 30 days and your all good until Christmas.

Lots of amazing deals - Including 38% Gold Reward discount on Backflow Incense Burners.. By far the best deal in the UK.

Lots of things back in stock and some new products coming online!

Wishing you a drama free peaceful weekend.


David

title: Missing in Shanghai
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

Yes, I'm finally back in China after more than four years. It's a bit strange, the same but very different.
I took the China Eastern night flight, from Denpasar to Shanghai. A very sparse flight, a selection of sad Russian refugees (moving to the next place they can), some wealthy Chinese and me. In Shanghai the airport was almost empty. Very strange, only a few international flights arriving. Coco (my wife and AW China agent) needed to be in Shanghai to apply for her Schengen visa so we arranged to meet at the hotel.
Last week I was in Bali, and we had the local priest come to performed a blessings ceremony for the latest AW start-up. Something strange happened.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Shanghai is full of flashy high-rise hotels, but I choice to stay in a slightly odd boutique hotel in the heart of the French quarter. Moller Villa was built by an eccentric Englishman to a fantasy design provided by his small daughter. The shipping magnets home was commandeered by the communist party and later converted to a hotel, everything has been preserved including the serving of a pretty dreadful English Breakfast.

But we love the area, Julu Road is near by and leads deep into the French Quarter. Here trendy gift shops, hip coffee places, cool vintage clothes stores.. the bright young things of Shanghai open small businesses in the dappled leafy streets. Massive high rise office blocks house the financial elite and there is a lot of wealthy clientele to support the small businesses.. Shanghai has always been the most cosmopolitan city in China, the most stylish and the most westernised.. In this area the old and the new mix, the local old folk and the young incomers, and before west and east.. there used to be a lot of foreigners.. but now hardly any. We ate in packed western style restaurants where I was the only westerner. I have to say I was made super welcome, and many locals want to chat or just say hello.


The creative buzz is still alive.. and some things have improved, the sky is blue, birds sing in the trees, the traffic is mostly electric (or super cars) so the roads are whisper quiet.. Springtime in Paris they say is beautiful, but Springtime in Shanghai is special. But something is missing... the foreigners. And you can sense the locals are slightly on edge, it's not normal.
Eric Moller completed his lavish home in the 1930's it was a time of massive change.. the Japanese invaded, the second world war, and the upheaval that followed..

We took the fast train from the humongous Hongqiao Station, so vast it boggles the mind.. the only foreigners I noticed where on the same train as us.. going to Yiwu. Home to the worlds biggest small commodity wholesale market.

Did you know, At our HQ complex in Sheffield we produce, aromatherapy products, home fragrance and scrumptious bathroom items such as bath bombs and soap loaves. You can smell us from miles away, the sweetest smelling company in the north. Click on some of our newest products here. We are delighted to see our new and existing customers. Whether you're collecting your order or visiting our showroom, you will always be greeted with a smile.

I'll tell you more about that next week...

I hope you have a peaceful and gentle weekend.

Take care.
David

title: Trip to Afghanistan
content_html:
Greetings from an unnaturally hot and sultry Spain.


It's August and since many people are on holiday, I hope you're enjoying it.
Last week I was telling you about the robbery, how a container from China was broken into on a layby on the A14 and a hundred or so cartons stolen.. about what would fit in a large transit van.
In last week's newsletter I listed the products - should you get offered then cheap you would know - you can read about it here..
A big thank you to the many people who wrote expressing sympathy and support! 

The good news is the shipping company has accepted liability and is negotiating a settlement with us. The bad news is we will have to reorder that stock and won't be here for a few months.. 
We keep asking for sight of the tachograph reading, if there is any cab CCTV footage, and surely there are CCTV cameras on the A14 that can be accessed at that time. The crooks had offloaded a lot of stock before they found something high value they liked, a few boxes that remained had been opened, and the Aromatherapy candles were on the base of the truck, so it must have taken quite some-time to sort out what they wanted. Very suspicious. 

I almost went to Afghanistan.. If you have time - I'll tell you the story.
Otherwise skip ahead to the deals below. 

The stunning awful pictures and news from Kabul has shocked us all.
For hours I have watched the news unfold, and listened horrified at the pathetic disconnected rhetoric coming from our own government and the Americans. It all seems a big tragic mess.

I have always been absolutely fascinated by Afghanistan.. 
As a teenager one of the first travel books I read was:  "A Short Walk in the Hindu Kush" Book by Eric Newby - a madcap journey to the badlands and highlands of Afghanistan.. For sure it changed my life and instilled in me a desire to travel to far flung exotic places. 
Since then I have soaked up any book I could find on this seemingly dangerous and fascinating country. Have you read Rory Stewart's book: "The Places In Between" where he walks on foot across the country? - The account is hairraising, honest and totally mad. But despite the bad and crazy guys he meets (and escapes from) you get the feeling there are many warm real humans there. He talks a lot about the kindness of strangers. 

In the early days of AW (it was 2007) at a dinner party I met an Afghan guy called Sadiq who was working at Sheffield university. He had contacts in the tribal areas where Lapis is mined and showed me some impressive tribal jewellery made from local brass plate and gemstones including beautiful vibrant blue lapis gemstones.

 The thought of being able to support a local business in such an area was so in line with our trading mission we were delighted at the opportunity and knew our customers would be supportive.
As you can imagine I was very excited to import it but as you can imagine it wasn't easy.. lots of issues but in the end we received about five pallets of stock.. I think it was about £20,000 of stock which was a decent investment at the time. 
When we opened the cartons it was amazing, beautiful - exotic and fabulous. We also received a note from customs asking if the jewellery was nickel free.. as you know nickel can cause nasty reactions on caucasian skin. Yes it should be, our supplier had assured us it was.. and we sent off samples to the lab to check and you guessed it..  it wasn't brass plated, the metal part of the jewellery was far from nickel free. Basically, it was nickel so we couldn't sell it at all. 
Sadiq was mortified and promised to resolve the issue but ultimately it was impossible.. he suggested we go to Afghanistan and meet the producers and find a solution.. and that seemed like a good idea to me.. 
Sadiq told me I would be safe with him, I would meet him in Peshawar in Pakistan where he would get me local clothes and we would drive over the border to Afghanistan.. It seemed like a grand exciting plan.
Of course, they way things developed, something bad happened and trouble escalated and I had to cancel the trip.

We had those pallets of tribal jewellery for years - didn't want to throw them out, couldn't sell them. In the end they burned in the fire at AW last year.
But I have a few samples in my house in Spain - at one time we were trying to find a way to re-electroplate them. I just found them in a bottom drawer..


Nice no? 

Our trade - if we could have sorted it - could have given one village or family a decent income.. and maybe encouraged others to not rely on drugs or guns to provide a living.
It never happened because  on 27 December 2007 the assassination of Benazir Bhutto took place, the former female PM of Pakistan - a leading liberal femanist whoes views you can imagine those extremist thugs didn't like. 
So this is how violence is never the answer.

Trade of course is the only solution, when humans trade, they build relationships that overcome even bigoted religious attitudes and gradually good values and trust has to be built to prosper. Not trading with people you don't agree with on principle in some cases is the right thing to do to bring pressure to bear.. but mostly not, because what happens when you stop trading.. They just go and trade with other dodgy people who will reinforce their world view. It's a very complex problem, with a lot of grey areas.. 
Charles Hoskison the founder of the crypto currency Cardano.. is actually one of the clearest thinkers in the world today.


Check out his thoughts on Afghanistan here.

After all the ancient silk road carried more than silk, it spread culture, civilization and wealth along it's routes that changed the world mostly for the better.

But we live in difficult times, global warming and the pandemic are bad enough.. As I write, a big yellow seaplane swoops low over my house - it will scoop up sea water and then fly to a forest fire burning not far away. 
Right now I should be in Indonesia working with any number of suppliers, but the pandemic put that on hold. If the world didn't have enough problems we have nationalism causing trade wars and things like Brexit. Enough. 

But still, life goes on..
Our office is finally taking shape. One of the things we have in all our offices is a wall or two turned to a chalkboard.



So big ideas can be made visual.. Ula (from customer service) has artistically drawn up the AW values.. I drafted these many years ago, and we include them in the induction for new employees. 

Here's that board, some other pictures of the office in Sheffield and the values.. 

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: End of an era
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia

I hope you are doing well and life is treating you well. 
Last week I was telling you about our trip to visit "Pacman" one of our long-time artisan suppliers in Bali. We made a Youtube video about it. I'm planning a series called: Meet the Artisans. If you missed the newsletter, you can catch up here.

Yesterday was a sad day. The end of an Era.


So only a week ago, Ringo came to see me. He sat in front of me looking incredibly nervous, I could see his hands shaking. What he told me rocked my world. Rocked all of AW. 

Ringo has been our Indonesian agent for almost 14 years. Not only that but a good friend and wise council. I can say hand on heart, I don't know anyone as humble, hard working, diligent and caring as Ringo. He taught me so much about the Bali Hindu philosophy, about the Tri Hita Karana which is all about balance, Three way balance between the spiritual, humans (community) and nature.  
Now he is sat in front of me telling me it is time for him to return to his small village in the Bangli regency and ultimately to become a village elder. Long story short his elder brother died about a year ago the village will hold a big ceremony which is his job to organise, after this he must take up a position as village elder to give balance back to the community.  He is, it seems to me, kind of retiring.

Such a shock! It feels like I am losing one of my oldest friends. Of course I fought against it, tried to persuade him to take a few months off and then come back. But he patiently explained why he cannot come back (maybe but unlikely). After telling me - he personally contacted and told everyone he interacted with in AW and then his staff, wishing everyone good health and success in the future.

In retrospect I can see he was planning this a long time, teaching his able assistant Bondhan everything, building a strong accountant team, and an excellent packing team. It was preordained, time to move to the next phase of his life. But it has taken me a week to process this and come to terms with it. 

Yesterday was a day of ceremonies, prayers, hugs and tears. We had a meal with the team and everyone wanted to say something for the record. Ringo also.
And at the end without fuss, when no one was looking Ringo quietly slipped away.. 

The end of an era.. 

ctually I should not have been here, but fate works in mysterious ways. I needed to renew my KITAS (Indonesian Investor visa) in order to legally run businesses here. Normally a 10 day job, but they just changed the rules and after the local immigration office approves the visa it has to be approved by the Jakarta office, and this coincided with the introduction of a new government digital system that promptly broke down.  They told me I couldn't leave Indonesia whilst in process because that would invalidate the visa. OK, but how long until fixed.. the immigration officer here told me at least a month, maybe two. So that's why I'm still here and not back in the UK as planned.. but that's not so bad (as you can imagine).. and this thing with Ringo.. Thank goodness I'm here to oversee the transition.

So Bondhan, who is pretty good at video editing.. made a record of Ringo's last day. I just uploaded it to our YouTube channel.


Fighting Temu & the loophole traders.
It's actually ridiculous that Temu can fly in 1500 planes a month, sell junk to your customers and not pay taxes in the UK.

Awful carbon footprint, zero trading standards control and they dodge taxes.
Ask your other suppliers if they are supporting this? - word on the line is some are scared to sign.. because well.. China.


You can support here (thank you)

Sooner or later they (our government) have to wake up..and tax and control closing this unfair loophole...
Until then we can fight back by refocusing on quality, UK made and artisan products that people like Ringo are working hard to bring to you.
Check out the deals we have for you below..

Also new stock arriving..
Only 3 weeks to Mother's Day.. and we have the best Season of Love Deals for you.

Wishing you a great weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: Behaving Badly & Goldfish
content_html:
Greetings from Indonesia

I hope you guys are doing well!
It's Friday the 13th - Don't panic.. What could possible go wrong?

Shortly I will be moving from here. Which is both exciting and sad.. but the circle of life at AW must continue.. standby for fresh adventures.
The thing about all Indonesia (in my experience anyway) is the stress free nature of the people. The calm, gentle, no drama approach to life and other people.  Maybe because of the many diverse peoples on many different islands.. that this relatively new nation (slogan: Strength in diversity) had to learn how to get along. to accept others as they are. I'm going to miss this..
Last week I was telling you about the "No Drama Keep Smile" jolly bodybuilding politician of Bali.  And I also explained a bit about the complex process of loading a container in the AW warehouse.. if you missed it you can catch up here. 
Our Digital marketing team is the personification of Indonesian friendliness in diversity.. AW-Advantage.com.. (BTW these guys can help you grow your online business).
Between the office and warehouse we have six very different cultural groups.. that all get along without stress and with total (as far as I can see) acceptance. This week we launched (or should say relaunched) the AW Gold Reward Amnesty.. it's my plan for rewarding our loyal customers... like you :).. more below.

Behaving badly in Bali.
Let me tell you not every visitor to Indonesia appreciates or responds well to the gentle culture here. There is a certain type of annoying swaggering, excess testosterone, overly privileged, low IQ foreigner who thinks it's ok to behave like a prat. For example to ride around without a helmet, under-dressed, over-tattooed and with zero respect for traffic rules.  They can do this (and much worse).. because in this country the locals will just accept them as they are, so there is no check on bad behaviour. There is a social media genre in Indonesia called Bule (which is slang for foreigner) Behaving Badly. The locals don't get upset or angry, they just shake their heads in disbelief and post to Tiktok or Facebook. Search: Bule behaving badly in Bali.. in any social media for some light entertainment. 
Sadly some of those folk are fellow Brits, but many are run-away Russians as locals are happy to point out. 

Fortunately these types mostly frequent only pockets of Bali best avoided (which I do). So anyway that gentle, accepting, trusting nature - the culture of Indonesia.. is what makes it relatively easy to do business. Artisans even often openly share their product costs and ask what is an acceptable price. Is this under threat from over tourism?.. Yes I see some locals learning to be mistrustful because of bad experiences. Sad but I hope the good will prevail.
There is a village in south Java (which springs to mind) where we buy traditional woven place mats.. the locals are open and kind and invite you into their homes.. . It would be awful if this way of life was destroyed. By the way, the natural vetiver place mats and runners they make are very special in that they are naturally scented. An amazing gift for Christmas.
So let me tell you about the Gold Reward Amnesty.. You will have noticed we give volume discounts in most families (or ranges) of products. This is to encourage retailers like you to carry a good selection of a similar product range, because a good selection means you will give your customers confidence and thus sell more.. It also means your order can be picked and packed more efficiently, so the savings can be passed on to you.
All good so far right (I know this because I used to be a retailer many moons ago).. except that for sure you will sell out of the most popular lines quickly and then need to restock. Restocking is expensive.. so our system is that you can restock (within 30 days) and still get the discount. We call this the Gold Reward Discount..   
It's all good if you can remember to order regularly.. if you are loyal to your stock your customers will be loyal to you.. but life gets in the way.. and well you know what happens..
SO.. that's why we invented the Gold Reward Amnesty.. what with covid and Brexit it kind of got forgotten.. but this week we are delighted to bring it back..
Rodrigo and Sandra and team.. came up with a fresh look involving a Goldfish..
Plus we are actively dreaming up many more benefits/gifts we can bestow on our lovely regular customers - helping you to sell more, boost your profit margin and have more fun. 
After all we are all in the Gift Trade - our business to help people love other people - no less! Gifts are a profound and deeply meaningful part of human nature. I believe we should be humbled and grateful to be part of this process. So you might be pleasantly surprised to find a gift in your order for your personal use - from AW to you..

Lots of new stock is rolling into our warehouses right now.. Christmas season (gifts for all) is approaching. Now really is the best time to get stocked up.

title: David's AW News: Find what you need.. / FREE BAG
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Spain


Put that Mick Jagger voice on and let's sing (in your head at least).. bare with me I'll explain later..

No, you can't always get what you want
You can't always get what you want
You can't always get what you want
But if you try sometime you find
You get what you need

Hope you guys are well and trade is good. Welcome to a new UK - new management, new blood. a fresh broom.. as predicted Sir Kieth and the labour government are back in the driving seat.
So let's hope for more sunny days ahead..  let's hope Britain finds it's mojo and we all find what we need.
Last week I was telling you about my idea for a new AW catch phrase.. and wave of new products landing in AW land.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

Tomas arrived from Slovakia on Tuesday. Coco arrived on Wednesday morning.. well just after midnight on Tuesday.. I went to the airport and waited for her to arrive.. It was so busy streams of people arriving and lots of emotional reunions on a warm (25c) night. Like that scene in "Love Actually". I  was a little early and waiting and waiting for ages. Streams of folk of all types and styles.. I'm searching the faces trying to find.... but then she arrived looking cool and beautiful.. as though she had just stepped out for the evening.. and not been travelling for 36 hours.

She has a bag of samples of products we are working on.. and Tomas came the next day to see Coco and the samples.. Then we went for lunch (including Coco favorite, grilled Sardines) on the beach nearby. 

Finding what you need..
Our big news this week is after a surprisingly huge amount of work.. Raul (the IT wizard) and Tomas with some help have launched a NEW SEARCH BAR.. 
It's been a longtime coming (like Coco) but might spread light on parts of AW you never knew existed. Try it out and see what you can find.. We are hoping you can find things more attuned to your customer base..Now you can search by price range, from low to high or vice versa. By category and search comes as you type.. so you can feel your way around the world of AW in a  whole new way.
Try it out.. HERE.
Try searching for Pink or Blue.. if you want to theme a part of your gift shop..it kind of worked before but now to a whole new level.. hope you like it and find it useful.

Today is Tomas 40th Birthday.. and we are celebrating today a little lowkey with friends and family BBQ this afternoon. Feel free to send birthday wishes.. he will appreciate it.. Tomas.

If you have time.. I'd like to tell you a little story.. 
In Bali.. a while back - Ringo and I travelled to the north coast one day to see if we could find some new suppliers..The second city on Bali is Singearaja, a port town..The name means Lion King.  one place that our contact recommended was an artisan tye-dye factory.. making super cool products - everything from scarves and t-shirts to wall coverings and bags. Their best selling product was a slouchy low slung casual linen bag, with bright colours running to pastel in a unique shape. We tried hard to make a deal to buy them for you.. but the usual problem was that the quantity we wanted was unrealistic for them to make. 
They were selling them in the attached gift shop for the equverlant of £30.. which seemed reasonable.. but the retail price in the UK (even if we could have bought it) would be £60+ - which is steep even for a posh tote bag... 
Later in India I told our man Chatterjee about the concept.. and we thought he could develop something out of washed (soft) jute. He had a contact not far from his factory where two brothers beavered away making tye-dye materials - (I actually wrote about them) 
The Tye-dye bro.. and artisan worker. 
We spent ages working with the guys to get the material to come out right.. then lots of attempts with the pattern guy in Chatterjee factory to get the shape and feel right of the bag.
Finally we made it.. a nice slouchy summer bag.. A year later it arrived in the UK and Europe..  
See it's quite big and nicely sloachy.. RRP at £12 - seems reasonable to me.. £18 would be fine. Check here.
I'm more disappointed than a conservative minister who lost his seat today..
Very disappointing these bags are simply not selling like they should..everyone loves the much more expensive Hemp Bags from Nepal.. people go crazy for the Ethnic Sling Bags (also more expensive) the Hope Hare Tote bags.. are just flying out.. But no love so far for these.. Please tell me why? Mr Chatterjee and the Tye-dye guys keep asking me how they are selling and I don't know why we are not selling enough, not even enough to re-order. I know they are a summer thing.. so maybe their time is just coming.. 

FREE BAG!
SO.. I have asked that we send all our lovely customers* a free bag.. for your personal use.. if you like it great.. if you don't please tell me why.. so I can give honest feedback.
*On your next order (over £200) you will find a little gift from me.. and now you understand the backstory maybe you can help find out why.

Take care, have a lovely weekend.
We are off to Tomas Birthday BBQ!

David

title: Times of Trouble
content_html:
Greetings from somewhere in the sky over India. 

Happy Friday the 13th. Since last week the coronavirus situation has changed a lot both in Europe and here in India. 

Tomas and I are on an almost empty flight from Bangalore to Kuala Lumpur. Gosh.. It's almost a ghost flight. Most of the two dozen or so people and the crew are wearing face masks. This is like something in a movie.



Last week I was telling you about taking an ancient boat across the river Ganges and visiting the children's home we support, you can read about it here. 

Since then we took a flight to Delhi and spent a few days doing deals. We have been trying to secure a particularly nice range of incense, a beautifully designed incense, for sometime now. 

I'd almost given up hope of achieving a workable deal but Chatterjee our man in India managed to organise a meeting with the big boss actually at the incense factory, about an hour's drive from Delhi. Turns out the boss a stylish gentle guy is married to a French lady..who is the inhouse designer. When two cultures mingle and new products emerge something special happens. 

We pitched that AW was the best company in Europe to market their lovely products.. and that our company ethos and values matched. 
We were pleased to see the best working conditions in a modern factory you could imagine. Clean and tidy, ventilated and super organised. Just the sort of family company we like to work with. 


After a while and some bonding, the boss admitted that his current distributor in the UK had some internal issues and hadn't managed to deliver on promised volumes so he would work with us.. Plus the prices magically came into line with what we had expected. 

We got up to so many adventures in old Delhi, discovering a whole new area full of artisans and traders down tidy little back lanes with huge go-downs and mazes of showrooms. Not only amazing products but some amazing characters, we quickly made some new friends and hope to do more business here. 

Even though riots and rumours of riots in Delhi were rife we managed to stay out of trouble. 

It's a time of trouble for sure but life goes on. 
After Delhi, we flew down to Goa to catch up with old friends and also meet up with one of our gemstone guys who came to meet us there. Very few tourists in Goa.. And it was a bit of a shock when the Indian government announced all tourist visas were suspended. 

Next stop was supposed to be China.. But a change of plan we are going to Bali, virus free Bali (they claim). Where at least we can focus on more artisan products and work with our man Ringo. 

With Italy in lock down, Slovakia in semi lock down and governments across Europe announcing increasingly strict measures.. Who knows what this week will bring. A time of trouble. 

Stay safe. More news next week.

David

title: David's AW News:  This Town Changed Everything
content_html:
Greetings from India


Hope you are well. 
Last week I was telling you about our whiskey drama and how India is not so bad these days. If you missed it you can catch up here.
We had made it to the city of Vadodara in Gujarat - a dry state from there our friend the mine owner picked us up (you can see him in this video I made about his mine).. and drove us to the famous gemstone artisan town Khambhat which is an unbelievably historic and otherworldly place.


Khambhat.. woah this place!

Not exactly on any tourist maps. No yoga cafés. No mountain views. Not even a proper hotel (We stayed just out of town at a highway stopover.). Sadly the sea coast silted up and the sea is 10 kilometres in the distance, but they still have a seaside promenade. Many ancient British buildings. And we were taken to a place of epic history totally abandoned.

The place is just heat, dust, narrow streets… and history that runs deep. The old town part still has tiny trading stores that look a hundred years old. We have several suppliers in this town, people we have worked with for many years, in two cases over two generations.  If you ever wondered why AW has the best value and range of gemstone products, this place is one of our "trade secrets".. whoops another secret I tell you about. 



Once upon a time this was one of India’s great trading ports. The Gulf of Khambhat carried ships from Arabia, Africa, even Rome. Spices, silk, beads, ideas — all moving through this town long before the word “globalisation” was invented.

And stones.

Khambhat became famous for agate. Carnelian. Jasper. The earth here gives up these treasures, and for generations families have shaped them by hand. Not factories. Courtyard workshops. Fathers teaching sons. Now daughters too. The sound of cutting wheels, polishing drums, the rhythm of craft passed down quietly over centuries. Now the town imports gemstones from all over India, our friend the gemstone mine holder brings truck loads here.. right across India from Jharkhand. 

There’s something very Ancient Wisdom about that.

You walk through the lanes and see rough stones in sacks on the floor. Dust everywhere. Then you see the finished pieces — spheres, palms, geodes — glowing like captured sunsets. Transformation. Raw to refined. Earth to the object of meaning.


But then our mines guy, told us about a place of astounding history. So special they made a famous movie about it.. maybe you have seen. On the edge of town close to what would have been a beach in the old days..  He showed us an abandoned Cricket pitch and pavilion.


The pitch is overgrown, but the pavilion still stands.

In 1721, sailors of the East India Company played the game near Cambay (as Khambhat was then called), watched by locals and noted in the journals of Lieutenant Clement Downing — that seaside moment is often pointed to as the very first glimpse of the “gentleman’s game” in India. 

Can you believe it!! We found the birth place of Cricket in India.. legend has it that the locals learned the game. A movie was made about it.  Lagaan — the epic, Oscar-nominated drama about a drought-ravaged Indian village in 1893, where farmers challenge British officers to a match of cricket to win relief from oppressive taxes. It captured the imagination of an entire nation around cricket as a symbol of resistance, unity and transformation.


It's a great movie! If you have never seen it I can highly recommend it.

And standing there — between the gemstone workshops and that forgotten cricket pavilion — you realise something beautiful.

In Khambhat, stones are shaped by hand, and games once shaped history. The British may have brought cricket, but India made it its own. Just like the earth gives up rough agate, and local hands turn it into something luminous.

That’s what we try to do at Ancient Wisdom.

Find the raw. Honour the story. Work with people who carry skill in their blood. Then send something meaningful back out into the world.

From dusty pitches to glowing spheres — it’s all part of the same journey.

And somehow, it feels like we’re still playing our part in a much older game.

Take care

More news next week..

David

title: David's AW News: Hot Hot Hot!
content_html:
Greetings from a hot hot hot place..

Hope you guys are doing well.
In Spain it was the hottest day ever, and the hottest point actually not far from our AW-Artisan warehouse.. the local government issued a decree that if your working environment is over a certain level you can just go home and still get paid. Toni (our main man in Spain) organised giant fans and cold water.. but the temperature was HOT-HOT-HOT! but our AW heroes warehouse team just kept on working regardless.. getting orders out to our customers as normal.. so we decided to take the team out for a meal on the beach as a reward... more later.
Last week (we had the blue screen event) I was telling you about the empty containers - (for more space for our over full warehouse) finally arriving in AW-Artisan carpark.. If you missed it you can read about it here..

Those containers arrived in the nick of time as an Indonesian container just came the next day, we were able to store backup stock and create space for new products picking area.
So the other day we finished work a little early and all the AW team got changed into their smart outfits, girls in pretty dresses, guys looking cool in white with shades.. we met a large popular chiringuito on the beach not far from us.. We do this once a year (at least) and it's become a bit of a tradition.. 

It started so well..Toni takes an awesome selfie!

But the hottest day of the year.. and those parasols had gaps where the sun came through.. the staff tried to keep us all in the shade, but the damn sun kept moving and slowly someone was a pool of sweat..
I did my speech and our new girl; Molly (second on the left) who is from Bath in the UK - and very posh - volunteered to translate. Her Spanish is excellent. title: David's AW News: The End. Next!
content_html:
Greetings from Copenhagen' Kastrup Airport, Denmark.

I'm on the way to Spain, on route to the UK. But I decided to stop off for one day to see my pal Allen (a slightly mad but brilliant Danish inventor, and expert in patent law), it is his birthday so we had lunch and later played chess in the hotel bar. He beat me again. But we made friends with those very friendly Danish folk who came to watch. 

Last week I was telling you how Dreams can come true, from Bali, Indonesia. If you missed it you can catch up here.

From Denpasar airport I took a Thai airways flight to Bangkok. Then spent five hours working in transit and then a midnight flight to Copenhagen on a very old  creaky Boeing 777. 
A very strange experience, most of my fellow customers looked like veteran Thai versions of breaking bad characters.  One old scruffy dude I think tried to sell me something,  on the way to the toilet he stopped next to me mumbling something and showing me some small envelopes.. no no thank you and I nudged him along. 
Later at immigration they looked like a group of retired mobsters, I heard one  guy with long lank slicked back hair, Gucci bag and gold chain being quizzed what he was doing in Denmark. Holiday he said (unconvincingly I thought), how long will you stay? Oh, (shrugging shoulders) erm 7 days..  why so short? For a second he looked a bit lost for an answer.. then started laughing, slammed a hand down on the counter ..your country haha.. its very expensive! Yes sir it is, said the immigration officer and stamped his passport. 
Up at 5am and a short stroll from the airport hotel to terminal 2, this is a very low stress airport. My impression.. calm, quiet, arty, low lighting very organized.  Virtually no queues and polite friendly people.  
Next stop is Spain,  where I need to catch up with Toni and the team, I'm continuing to write this on the early morning Norwegian air flight down to Malaga. 
My last days in Bali I spent grappling with our dreadful supply lines issues.  It's hard work, we had several meetings with suppliers who all tell me the same thing, a shortage of artisans.  Even increasing prices doesn't seem to impact much. Contracts help because they create long-term more secure jobs, so we have been signing a few more.. Ringo and Bondhan, our guys there are doing their best. But I fear for the future of Indonesian Artisan crafts.
Anyway we had a fish meal near the airport where I gave them an encouraging speech.. and we brainstormed some ideas.. said our goodbyes, and after they dropped me at the airport.
Ringo, Bondhan and Debbie, our office manager at AW-Advantage.
So this is it. The END..  I'm at the end of the Spring 2024 Buying Trip. I started when I left my home in Spain on the 8th of January... and traveled to Bali, after India, then Nepal and on to China.  Then back to Bali and now 103 days later full circle back to Spain.. 

Traveling part of the way with Toni (our man in Spain), James from UK, Coco (my wife and your China agent) and Tomas, Peter  (from Slovakia ) and Raul. It's been a grand amazing adventure.  Thank you for being part of it, your ideas and suggestions are always valuable. 

We have 847 new products in the pipeline, opened up lots of new suppliers in India and Nepal, probably created jobs for hundreds of artisans. I am very excited about quite a few ranges on the way- a huge amount of backroom stuff is done and being done, four designers are busy making packaging and adding details..  And so I'm pretty sure some of those products will be great for your customers and a big boost to your business. 

So its the epic END.. and every end is a new beginning.. the circle of life continues...  Next up.. soon to UK.

Lots of products from previous trips and from our Aromatics factory are landing almost every week. This week we had big shipments from India and Bali.. so lots of fast selling products are back in stock.
Crystal Balls seem to be back in fashion.. we are selling out fast. Also anything gemstone related is buzzing.. Maybe its that: Feel the Power of the Gems Start to Cleanse..    Trending on TicTok.. did you see it?
Our new Crystal Soap I told you about last week.. Sold out in seconds. Good news is they have been working shifts to get it back in.. Back in stock right now..
To celebrate we have a Free Shipping Weekend!  
I'm just landing in Malaga.. so I'm wishing you a lovely weekend.. 
Thank you once again for your support.. 
And remember.. it's never the end... MORE News next week!

David

title: Bonding with a Thai Lady
content_html:
Greetings from Jakarta, Indonesia.

Yep - I made it, finally arriving in my quarantine hotel after 26 hours of travel late last night.  I just woke up feeling a bit blurry and worse for wear. As they say on Strictly it was quite a journey.  
And they just bought me a full Indonesian breakfast and pastries with a message.. which should bring me round. I'm typing this and eating breakfast :)


It's the same hotel and same room as when I was here in October. Then it was supposed to be 8 days now I only have 4 nights quarantine and one has passed already.

Last week I was telling you about a kinda magic in the gift trade which means we don't need to panic when the economy crashes. You can read why here (if you missed it).

So from Malaga to Amsterdam to Singapore to Jakarta.. and after "enjoying" the quarantine.. if all goes well I should arrive in Bali on Valentine's day evening.
Hope your Valentine's trade is going good, it's the start of the season of love.. the season everyone in the gift trade loves :)

It was slightly stressful in Amsterdam where I thought I had a tight but manageable hour and half transit time. Some mistake with the time difference calculation, when I checked my flight to Singapore on the screen, it was already boarding and only 30 minutes to spare. Departing gate E1 on the other side of passport control, I arrived and found a big queue. So I asked a guide if I could skip the queue due to the short connection time, he barely glimpsed at my ticket and shook his head. I asked another guy, same response.. third time lucky - got some sympathy and a pass to the front. Panting I arrived at the gate to see a "Gate Closed" sign. Oh OK I thought, it's not my fault they will have to put me up for the night and book me on the next day's flight. "Come quickly sir" a security man waved me through, "we just need to check your papers" you can still make it. It's actually quite cool being last to board. 
I figured my luggage wouldn't make it so I resigned myself to having to wait for it to come after a day or so to the hotel. But some angel at KLM baggage handling made the connection and it was sat there by the belt when I finally passed all the multiple processes to get through the airport. 

Getting through Jakarta airport was also a journey in itself. First they issue you with an ID barcode then document checks then the PCR test. That all went fairly smoothly, the passport control only had two rather sleepy people working and it took 2 hours to get through that. I grabbed my luggage and went to the secure area where you meet the quarantine hotel reps. Everyone had someone waiting for them with a name board, except me.. and a lady holding the same hotel reservation paper. 
The other reps were super sympathetic and tried to help us by calling the hotel, one even knew the guy who was supposed to be there. "Please wait, he will be here soon". 
An hour later he turned up apologising, in the meantime the lady and I had bonded.. She was from Thailand and was in Indonesia to meet up with her British husband who she hadn't seen in two years. "Stupid pandemic" she explained. Snap I said.. I haven't seen my wife in two years either.. so we exchanged pictures and stories. She had a 16 year old daughter, very cleaver who she was hoping would go to university in the UK. 
Outside the airport we had to wait again for a car to come to take us to the hotel, my car came and I suggested rather than wait for the next we could both go together. After we set off I noticed our taxi driver was driving ridiculously slowly.. he didn't speak any English. My Indonesian is very rusty but I asked him, "why so slow?" - it turned out his sat nav system wasn't working, he didn't know the way and was going slowly hoping it would start working soon. 
A 20 minute journey took 90 minutes.. 

The quarantine check-in desk is in the underground carpark, the staff were waiting for us in rather unnecessary hazmat suits Because we came out of the same car they assumed we were a couple, and in our frazzled and travel weary state didn't have the energy to argue. They took us to a room and sat us down at a makeshift check-in desk, "We are not married" I said to the check-in girl.. "It's no problem.." she said with a 'we are not that type of Muslim country' look, "..there are no restrictions here".
Honestly.. after that journey, I almost gave up. 

We have to wear quarantine wrist bands - the type they put on dead bodies at the morgue. And according to government regulations, the hotel has to take a photo of you wearing it. So we had our photo taken together holding up our bands. I said goodbye to the lady in the lift, "maybe see you in four days, if not I hope your reunion goes well", thank you she said, touching my arm, "very nice to meet you".

Next week I will be in Bali..

Hope you have a lovely Valentines day.
Take care.

David

title: So Emotional
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I'm actually on the way to the airport now. Last few jobs to do from the Malaga office then onwards to Jakarta.
I seem to have been saying goodbye to friends and the team for the last few days.. 
This morning I awoke to a beautiful sunrise, and realised that as excited as I feel to be traveling to asia finally.. I'm also sad to leave my home in Spain.
Very mixed emotions.. sad at leaving, excited at a new adventure, apprehensive about the journey... I don't know why I'm feeling so emotional.. 
If all goes well.. I will fly from Malaga (KLM) to Amsterdam then change for the night flight to Singapore. I won't be allowed to leave the plane in Singapore, we drop off and pick up passengers.. then onward to Jakarta.
Then I will have to undergo a PCR in the airport and will be taken to a quarantine hotel for seven nights. After that I will be free to travel to Bali.
Wish me well!!

Last week I was telling you about all the good news at AW.. and about our, Bali inspired office space in the HQ in Sheffield.. if you missed it you can read about it here.

This week has been very busy on many fronts - it's all go.. and in the UK, fuel shortages, facebook deleting itself and panic buying everywhere.
Last week I was telling you it was Rodrigo's 7th birthday.. it's true..(seven years at AW) this week he tells me he is running in the Manchester Marathon.. to raise funds for Weston Park Cancer Hospital in Sheffield. I'm sure you will wish him well.
Here is a link:

                                https://www.justgiving.com/fundraising/ancientwisdom


Well it's only weeks to Halloween.. which always seems to kick start the Christmas season.. the clocks will go back, the mornings are darker - it's time to plan for Christmas.
Are you planning well ahead?  
We have lots of amazing deals - candles - could be in short supply if the lights go out (and I think it could happen). We are doing our best to secure good supplies, but it's not easy.
Talking to Coco in China this morning.. our candle factory there is facing electric shortages and soywax increased in price 25% this week with more increases warned.

There is always a reason for a party at the AW Artisan office in Spain. And today as well as me leaving for Asia, it was also the leaving day of one of our founding members, Luis has been our warehouse manager since day one in Spain.
But after lots of heartache and emotionals discusions he has decided it is time to move on.. I believe he planning to start a business. Over a spread of very sweet snacks everyone made emotional speaches and we said our goodbyes to Luis. I told him that we wish he all the best and whatever happens he will always be a member of the AW family. 


Goodbye Luis and good luck! All very emotional..


David

We have two main arms to the AW business in the UK. Our Aromatics production unit, and the Ancient Wisdom distribution warehouse. It's hard to be in two places at the same time, as much as I would like to be.
I visited the Ancient Wisdom warehouse, and said hello to everyone on Monday.. checked out the revamped Showroom there.. and totally blown away by what the guys there have achieved. Maybe I'm biased but that showroom is awesome, it's as though all the hard work and creativity of everyone at AW is distilled and on show in that one spot. I was quite overcome with  a mixture of pride and excitement.  And the customers visiting recently certainly seem to be impressed. Getting really good reviews lately. 
On Sunday in Malaga I dropped my hire car off at the stress free (no dodgy tricks) place I use these days. Here's a tip..Malagacar.com - I highly recommend them if you need car hire in the area. It's not inside the airport but a short mini bus to the terminal from a big shed place near, and friendly helpful people. I took a Ryanair flight to Manchester along with the hungover stag and hen party groups returning home.  Manchester Airport wasn't too stressed, although 7c was a little shocking for me after 3 months in tropical climbs. But I enjoyed a pleasant homecoming drive over the Snake Pass to Sheffield. 
Home at last. 

I have spent most of this week at AW-Aromatics with the team reviewing the new products in process.. As always there is awesome stuff on the way.. top secret at this stage but very exciting.. Our designers Sandra and Emily are totally on it - creativity and ideas spilling forth like a magic fountain. The Hop Hare Brand, conceived and developed by Sandra..    is coming along nicely. We just added to the range bags, tote bags and pouches. 
Other items from India also came in and also back into stock.. Indian products are having a massive resurgence these days.. I believe at  AW we have the best range and prices.. especially incense.

Happening Soon..
Father's Day is approaching fast.. We have a good selection to inspire you here.
We also have a big stock of Buddha items  arriving.. it's Buddha Day coming up soon.. so might want to consider this. 
Apparently it's International Bath Bomb Day soon..

This weekend we have some vouchers to help you stock up for all this and the Spring / Summer / Wedding season..  DON'T MISS OUT!!


Anyway I know you are busy or getting ready for the long weekend. Late May Day Greetings.. Enjoy!!
Hopefully we will have nice weather..  

Take care.. more updates next Friday.

David
