title: Introducing the Beast from France
content_html:
Greetings from Sunny Spain

Last week I was telling you about the new warehouse and updates on progress.also introduced you to some of our China suppliers. If you missed it you can read about it here.
Since then, things have moved on quite a bit.. We installed ten packing benches, started a lot of new guys who are being trained and brought up to speed right now.
The number of orders shipped per day is now more than we are receiving (at least most of the time).  It's really "All systems Go!"
I took an early morning Easyjet flight to Malaga on Saturday morning.. been visiting our Spain company who have been left a bit to their own devices during the last few months. It was really nice to catch up things, and brilliant to find the office and warehouse quite buzzing with activity. Toni and his team all looking good, the showroom is beautiful, I couldn't be more happy with their progress. Toni says his only problem is getting enough stock quick enough.. Check them out: AWArtisan.es. Meanwhile The Beast - is on the way.. 


Let me explain about the production department. As you know we make bath bombs, artisan soaps, aromatherapy products and home fragrance stuff. After the fire we had to remake the production from scratch. Dushan and Neil the production managers and their team worked round the clock and rooted out the equipment we need and amazingly made it all happen. Absolute AW hero's!  We were forced to work from about 15 thousand square feet in Units 1,2,3 at Parkwood Business Park with lower floor of unit 3 used for production. If you have following the story you will know how we managed to move the distribution to Europa way. Our plan is to use all three units for production, effectively increasing capacity threefold. 


So we have been making SLS free soaps using what is called "a plodder" - what it does basically is mince up the soap noodles with the aromatic additions and then extrude the soap through a dye. Our old machine had served us well for many years, and we had hoped it might have survived the fire, but even that solid bit of kit was destroyed. We began to look for a new machine, they make them in Korea, India and China.. but in the age of corona, and worldwide high demand for soap all the manufacturers where quoting six months lead times.  So we turned to the secondhand market.. after much casting around, one of our contacts knew someone who knew someone in France that had a machine to sell. The only thing is this machine is big, it can produce 10 times what we used to produce a day.
A charming French guy, with impeccable English gave us a whatsapp tour of the machine, he assured us it will do the job and he has a UK contact who can commission it for us. The price wasn't negotiable, €30K - 40% deposit, after a refurb the balance on collection. We collected this week. The Beast from France is on the way.. it is coming from Île de Ré  an island close to La Rochelle. He kindly sent pictures of it been loaded. 





So that's quite exciting we expect to receive it next week.
Last week I was also telling you about the Nepal container that finally arrived. It was a year ago Tomas and I was in Kathmandu placing those orders. The airport closed due to covid and the lockdown there delayed production also. Eventually our agent there found away to get the goods out over land in a container to Kolkata port in India. Actually two containers, one shipped to our Slovakia warehouse and one to UK. 
I thought you might like to meet some of the delightful suppliers from Nepal..


Mr Suman, súper organised and enthusiastic hemp and cotton bag supplier. Attention to details is his pasión.

This is Dome Sherpa, a super humble guy managing a team of metal work artisans, they are producing singing bowls, and the new copper and brass jewelry - see below.


This is Babu Chaudhary, who organises a woman's collective making natural felt products - his input is the tremendous fun designs that reflect his jolly character.

 

So things are coming together finally.. we are still short of stock, and still behind with orders.. but it's getting better day by day.
One other thing to report.. we are changing our working hours. Now we will start from 8am rather than 9am, and finish at 4.30pm - this is has worked well in Slovakia warehouse and we hope to get off to a flying start in the mornings thus serving you better.


Take care - stay safe.


PS: Discover a wide range of high-quality wholesale soaps and indulge in a luxurious bathing experience - Click on the link now to explore our collection!


David

title: Mystic Mission
content_html:
1st February 2013

Hi ,
Less than two weeks to Valentines day.. so it's all systems go at AW. Lots and lots of new stock and brand new Retail Displays & Stands Department. See below.
Welcome to all the new readers to my newsletter. I travel a lot seeking out ever more unique (and hopefully salable) gift-ware, some of our customers like to read my ramblings.. but feel free to skip to the business stuff below.
Last week I was telling you about our sister company in southern Spain... and how you can get a pretty decent English breakfast there. Yesterday I landed in Mumbai, India and this morning had the finest English breakfast east of Scarborough. One thing you can say about good Indian hotels is that they really are the best in the world, where coffee is heaven, service is world class, bacon crispy and HP sauce is treated with respect. Could be my last for a while.. outside of the big city hotels it will be a real Indian breakfast, spicy masala dosa, milky tea and no HP..
I'm in India on a mission to find some seriously esoteric and exotic gift-ware. Sales of Tibetan singing bowls, exotic incense, mala beads etc keep on getting more popular. India is the place for all things magic and mysterious, probably the most spiritual country in the world. You have probably read about the Kumbh Mela - the worlds biggest spiritual gathering, expected to draw a hundred million devotees, really.. the biggest human gathering on earth ever. It's just warming up now.. so maybe my mission timing is auspicious.
The mission has gotten off to a great start. Just had a meeting with our long time supplier from Ahmadabad, our new designs of gemstone and crystal wands are.. well what can I say.. they are just magic.
More news from India, next week.
Happy trading.
David

title: 🙏 Can You Help?
content_html:
Greetings From sunny Sheffield

 

Things are looking up, very soon we can go to a restaurant or pub without having to hope for clement weather.

Very soon we can hug our loved ones. 

Last week I was telling you about some street art that struck a chord - "We are all waves in the same sea" - you can read about it here.

While things are getting better here, we have to remember that no-one is safe until we are all safe... We are all in this together.


China

Coco called me to tell me she was finally having the vaccine..   send me pictures I said.. I want to see what the Chinese vaccine experience is like.

She told me the system is very different there, everyone of every age is being vaccinated at the same time. Whole factories or whole apartment blocks are called up the same day. So two coaches came to pick up Coco and her staff, and the workers in the same commercial area to ferry everyone to a purpose built vaccination centre. The second jab will be in 28 days, after which - she tells me with a degree of national pride all of China will be vaccinated.  



Indonesia

Ringo in Indonesia called me to say he has had a vaccine. In Bali they are trying to vaccinate everyone as quickly as possible so that the island can be opened to tourists again, presumably vaccinated tourists. Meanwhile I applied for a business visa (via an agent) for Indonesia and I was surprised to actually receive it. It's an e-visa which I present on arrival. If I use it (I'm still waiting for my second jab) I would still need to fly to Jakarta, quarantine there for a week before being allowed to fly onward to Bali. But I'm excited to finally get the chance to go back to Indonesia and ramp up new products. Heaven knows we need them, and the artisans and their families certainly need the work.

 

India

Chatting with Mr Chatterjee, it is very bad there.. his two sisters contracted covid, but have now fortunately recovered. But many friends and local people he knows have not, the Ganges is nearby and it's true what you hear about dead bodies drifting by.

It was only February last year that Tomas and I were there, we took an early morning ferry with the locals just for the experience. 



While we were there we developed quite a few products with Mr Chatterjee. One was trendy cotton mesh bags.. See below..  Stock Indian Cotton bags.. this will really help with work in that town, when the factory can reopen. 

 

Lots of readers and customers are also asking me if they can help with donations, which is really really kind. So I was just chatting with Chatterjee, he says now his family are OK he can focus on helping others. Oxygen is the problem - the hospitals don't have so people buy their own supplies and take them to the wards. Of course those without work cannot afford to pay the market price, a cylinder costs about £200 - and Chatterjee says he has a contact at a factory that can do refills for about £5 

I have set up a Go Fund Me page.. Here is the link,

 


It's bad in India in many places, even Goa where we have a company apartment (bought many years ago), I spoke to my friend Alex who told me the local hospital ran out of oxygen - I have been there it's a modern very well equipped place with top doctors..  and before they were resupplied 75 people had passed away for lack of oxygen. 

 

If India is bad, Nepal it is worse still, and after speaking to my friend there Mr Uphindra - who was the manager of the hotel in downtown Kathmandu where I used to stay.. I was in tears. He and his wife and children are in lockdown, he is also trying to support a hostel with seven kids, where he is the official carer. He only goes out to find food for his family and the kids, and yesterday to get to the market had to step over dead bodies in the street. I sent money to help, but will see what other practical help we  can give.

 

So things are looking up in the UK and most of Europe, but we are not safe until everyone is safe.

I'm sorry to depress you.. it's just what's on my mind right now. 

Anyway..

 

Enjoy your weekend.. but stay safe. 

 

More news next week.

 

David

title: David's AW News: Magic happened
content_html:
Greetings from Spain..

It's the day after our 28th Birthday. Ancient Wisdom's started by me on a market stall 28 years and one day ago. I can hardly believe where that path has led.. and where it will go..
As part of the celebration, we had a quiz to see how many of you know AW well enough.. I am humbled and happy by the number that entered the quiz and delighted that so many 53% got 100% correct.. you are amazing guys.. you know who you are.. and I think you should be given special status at AW.. a big thank you to our super fans
It's in the DNA of AW to be always making plans and always aiming to grow. And this time of year we start making those plans for next year.
So last week I was telling you about some of the moving parts of AW - lot's happening.. if you missed you can catch up here.

One very moving thing.. is that yesterday Coco went back to China.. as I write this she is still on the way. She must go back, because of work commitments (lots to do before the Chinese New Year shutdown) and also her grandchildren miss her a lot. 

Our last day together in Spain was special. Sunny and warm, so we went for a walk along the beach boardwalk. It's mid November but still 24c and the sea is warm enough to swim comfortably. Most of the beach restaurants have closed for the year, but one place called the Garden Bar, stays open and we stopped there for a spot of lunch. We are semi-regulars and many times have enjoyed the view and a spot of lunch here. 
Then it happened! I spotted them first!!


Coco's last day. Magic happened.
I have lived here (on and off) for over ten years. It's the first time I have seen dolphins from the shore. I saw something over Coco's shoulder and said.. look, something is there. We squinted out to sea and.. just then two beautiful dolphins only meters from the shore leap clean out of the water. I screamed.. wow look! Then a whole pod of dolphins did that thing where they synchronised broke the surface in a smooth arch.  All the customers are on their feet, everyone trying to catch a picture.. it's hard to do.. but there is something magical about seeing a pod of dolphins really putting on a show for us.  Great excitement and joy, it really lifted the spirits of everyone there. 
After a while they moved on along the coast, but left behind in the Garden Bar some kind of magic. Everyone now bonding and friends, groups on different tables making friends. It felt like a special blessing for Coco's last day.

So yesterday I took Coco to the airport. She was booked on the only (kind of) reasonably priced business class flight I could find. Finnair: Malaga to Helsinki - 8 hours transit time and then on to Shanghai. Actually I feel scammed by Finnair.. it's the only business class flight I have ever booked that doesn't include any luggage or lounge access. Only realised the day before and had to book the very expensive extras online, they even wanted €150 just to select a seat, I didn't bother.  Finnair my advice - don't bother.

She arrived safely - I just spoke to her - it's Friday evening in Shanghai as I write this. The flight was only so so she said.. comfortable but not worth a review. Shanghai international arrivals is very quiet, she said.  Last time I was there is was like that.. It's not the same in China.

Thanks once again to everyone that filled the quiz.. we are so happy that you engage with AW - it's magic to have you onboard. Thank you also for the recent lovely reviews. We always appreciate your feedback.
If you have time and want to give us a little love.. or just a little gift.. nothing would be nicer than a sweet (but honest) review.

Review AW Here.


Singing Bowls Suggestion.

Last year this time we made a plan (one of many) to be the best at Singing Bowls in the UK and Europe. We have actually been importing Sing Bowls for over twenty years, so have a fair amount of experience and a good selection of suppliers. But recently noted a BIG trend in Singing Bowls sales.. Yoga and Healing folk use them.. and lots of people are collecting them. High end top quality seemed to be in demand. On the last epic trip to Nepal and India (the first since before covid) we made a huge effort to boost the depth and range of supplies. Almost everything is online in the UK (some more exciting things still on the way). Check this page to see most things Singing Bowls Central with links there to other pages.   

I just wanted to suggest that maybe a Singing Bowl corner in your shop or section in your website - might work very well. Super fun, easy to engage customers, and healthy sales values. And I believe even though these artisan made items can have supply delays, we have enough depth and range to always have enough items to keep you stocked and your sales healthy. I really feel a Singing Bowl Pop Up shop in the right place would be magic.  


Soap Flowers Gift Boxes

This product is a little under the radar, but Soap Flowers generally have been selling well for years.. what we have noticed recently is higher end (but good value) soap flowers taking off more and more. So Coco working with one of our old suppliers, put together a posh range, Bondhan (our designer in Bali) designed the gold embossed packaging and I made the final selections. And I came up with that bad kind of French pun.. so they can be used as a "Thank You" gift.- that was last spring. 

Check Soap Flower Gift Boxes.  In Europe they are selling like hot cakes.. we just reordered full containers just of these in Slovakia and Spain. In UK.. selling great but I feel still basically undiscovered in the uk. So consider them also.. I think could also make a Pop Up shop on their own..  We re-took the pictures this week to give you a better idea. Good time to start.. will sell through Christmas to Valentine's day and Mother's Day to next year's wedding season. Magic... Go for it!!

And this time of year we start making those plans for next year. So last week I was telling you about some of the moving parts of AW - lot's happening.. if you missed you can catch up here. Sunny and warm, so we went for a walk along the beach boardwalk. It's mid November but still 24c and the sea is warm enough to swim comfortably. Most of the beach restaurants have closed for the year, but one place called the Garden Bar , stays open and we stopped there for a spot of lunch. title: David's AW News: Behind the scenes / SOL
content_html:
Greetings again from the AW Warehouse in Bali.


Ringo and his team are working so well, they are crushing it like never before (as Pres Trump would say).. another container shipped every week almost. One just despatched to Slovakia, and in a couple of days another to the UK. A container holds about 69 cubic, and everyday the team tot up how much cubic they have packed into cartons ready to despatch. Ringo can tell me exactly how many cubic we have packed for UK, Spain or Slovakia at the end of every day. When we get to about 60 cubic meters he starts asking EU offices to book a container. We have two young girls in the "accounts" department who not only keep track of the money but chase up artisans reminding them to get orders finished and delivered to the warehouse. They also organise the barcodes and hangtags providing everyday what the packing team needs.  Nuru, Ari are AW heroes of the week. 

Working together with Ringo (big boss) and Made (who looks after all the export documents, and compliance stuff we need). Together an amazing team, I'm very proud of them.
Last week I was telling you about my trip from Spain to here and my typical breakfast in Bali. Also my personal top picks for Valentines Day. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Last time I was here, we went exploring the Silver area of Bali not so far from our warehouse that is a maze of small WFH type workshops where families of artisans work producing silver and some gold jewellery. Showrooms on the main road sell the work of the locals. Many are tourist commission system places. If your tour guide or taxi driver wants you to visit such a place you can be sure they are getting a healthy commission and prices are double or triple local prices. But some are legitimate export businesses and some artisans are happy to work directly for people like us. 
The best way to do the jewellery business is to design your own components and own the molds used to make the shapes, then buy the silver by the kilo from a government office - you need an artisan licence to do this - and let the artisans make for you directly. 
Anyway down an alleyway (last November) we found a new place..
The new items we ordered just arrived today, and I'm very impressed with the quality. Really beautiful, nicely packed, proper silver stamps, all paperwork in place.
And just in time to pack in the UK container. You should see them in a few weeks.

Valentine's day is almost here!
We call it the start of the Season of Love..(SOL) Valentines, Mother's Day, Easter, Father's Day and the whole Wedding Season lies before us.. 
We have lots and lots of perfect products at AW.. dare I suggest AW is your best V-pick. And romantic gifts need to be quality, artisan and beautiful. A gift from TEMU is seriously not going to impress the wife.
So at AW you can compete with those dodgy guys..  Check out our Valentines Page, and don't be scared to stock up - the more you stock the more you will sell throughout the Season of Love.

2 New in stock lines that I'm excited about..
First.. very happy to see the Flat Pack Gift Boxes arriving.. finally. If you want to offer Hamper style gifts these are perfect. Ideal for the SOL.. smart design that means you can erect a posh box in seconds. And create hampers and gift packs to fulfill the dreams of your customers. And if you want something fast selling and highly profitable (to put in them) you can't beat our range of Wholesale Craft Soap Flowers - ideal for creative people.

And Secondly from the Agnes & Cat - team.. something new and available at AW and directly from A&C. 
Great pick-up lines in the shape of cute little house gift boxes. Ideal RRP's of around £15 & £25 makes for a perfect SOL gift you can sell all day long.

And lots more new stock in the pipeline..
OH my God!.. so exciting these days it's all coming on-line.. many new stock lines arriving. You have no idea how much hard work has been put into these things!

Dragons Den AW style..
And I'm working on more from Bali.. we had this idea to make an open day where all our most trusted suppliers can come along to our warehouse office and present their best new products that they feel AW customers (that's you) will love. Next week I will update you on how this goes.

Hati Hati (Take care) and have a lovely weekend. Take care in stormy weather!

David 

PS I almost forgot to include our head of security Opim.. 
He says woof! More AW Heroes next week.

title: David's AW News: So Many Stories
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield. I'm at AW HQ.. 

 

And it's so much fun. It's all happening in every department. AW Aromatic's have some exciting new products in development. Hop Hare designer Sandra has new products coming online now.. (love the pouches) and more beautifully detailed products in the pipeline.  

Our Hop Hare department is growing nicely.

Last week I was telling you about festival time in the UK, and we even kicked off the season with our own mini festival in our AW garden. If you missed it you can catch up here.

That party was supposed to be an afterwork event, an appreciation and thank you to our hard working teams.. but somehow it went on all evening and late into the night. I left relatively early, but the team had a great time into the early hours.. Unfortunately Urzula (our customer service manager) bounced a little high on the bouncy castle.. and suffered a nasty strain leg.. she has been bravely working from home and resting it. We wish her well.

This week I managed to spend some time in our main showroom at Affinity park. Rodrigo and his team have done a fantastic job adding all the new products and revamping the displays. Year ago when AW was born, I started with gift shops in Derbyshire, so retailing is in my blood. There is nothing better than reorganising a shop and seeing instant results. OK, ours is not a shop, and serves a different function but I still get to "play shop". 

And the thing is - I have an emotional connection to so many of the products. I'm personally friends with many of the artisans and folk behind making those products. I have been involved in the design process in many cases, helping to inspire people and helping to create new things. Almost everything I touch as a story I could tell you behind it. 


Getting organised.

 

Those Bali umbrellas are from a family business in a village along the coast, off a side road down a track by a rice terrace. Literally the middle of nowhere. The thing is to export those things you need special treated wood, the fabric is different and thie finish has to be made to last. Compared to the local use ones that get replaced every season, they are a different thing. Same skills to make - see how many details there are.. but next level materials. Not many people make it for export. 

That Banja Incense is designed and made by two guys, Harri Krisna devotees who have a very well organised and professional factory not far from the ISKCON temple in Bangalore.  I have known them for a long time, before they made an incense brand for the temple and we used to sell it, now they have branched out with their own designs initially aimed at the South American market.. but perfect for AW and our customers.
Those Magic Candles were designed by the Spanish team, with text and concepts from myself and manufactured in the Soywax candle factory by Coco in China.
Those Indian Rag Rugs.. are direct from a family factory in Panipat - the recycling city of India. Raj our man there, recently got married, and on our last trip he picked us up from the train station in a new car - a wedding gift.    

Everything - everything has a story behind it.

 

So next week we have an open showroom week.. you are invited to come and see.  

I will be around, so if you are very lucky you might get to hear some of those stories :)

Do come along if you can.. there are lots of surprises and incentives, and we can show you some winning products that might just make a big difference in your business.

 

So wishing you an amazing weekend. 

Hope to see you soon.

 

All the best David

title: Surprise!
content_html:
Greetings from a surprise location..

Last week I was telling you about extreme scary weather in Ubud and wishing you a Happy Halloween. If you missed it you can catch up here
Some staff members at AW dressed up and as usual and as usual Ula won the vote for best costume - no surprise there. She has won every year for as long as we can count..


This week is Bonfire night in the UK.. Enjoy but please be careful - all those rockets and explosions we don't want any nasty surprises..

In the spirit of Halloween trick or treating.. I promised you a surprise.. well I was due to return to Spain for November.. but LastMinute.com (remember them) sent me an email and on impulse I changed my plan..
Sat in bed in the early hours rain lashing against the bedroom window and autumn leaves swirling amongst the trees.. It dawned on me that even though I love working with the team in Spain.. there was important tasks left undone elsewhere..  A place I could be productive, with warm weather and amongst the most gentle kind people. It was surprisingly easy - I clicked the button.. 

Here is the SURPRISE! I'm back in Ubud.


Surprisingly peaceful.
Only for a short while but that offer was too good to miss..  and not only do we have quite a few projects to complete, it's promising to be an historic couple of weeks as the G20 meeting is due to finalise with a meeting of the top 20 heads of state here in Bali. At the time of writing Mr Putin is hinting he might not attend..  Jokowi the rock-star president of Indonesia has said the unique peaceful culture of Bali could form a backdrop for successful peace talks.. Seems unlikely but the power of positive thinking is amazing. 

Actually when things are too cheap there is often a reason.. and my arrival here was anything but smooth. I flew with Korean Airways.. Manchester to Amsterdam, then to Seoul with a connection to Denpasar, Bali. On closer inspection the connection had only a time of 55 minutes.. 

It's a bit strange how you can leave the UK without passing border control - you can't leave the EU without being checked in and out.. every Asian country checks you in and out.. Now, from the UK you arrive in an Amsterdam Schiphol airport terminal that is already outside the EU zone, they don't care, no need to check you at all. And no security checks either. In fact the only security check I had was in Manchester.. all the way to Asia. 
I'm waiting to board the flight to Seoul and an announcement is made that due to technical issues boarding will be delayed one hour, "Thank you for your understanding".. Oh I thought - that's it.. connection missed.. Then after about five minutes... "We'd like to invite business travellers and people traveling with children to board the aircraft".. that's strange I thought.. Then they ask me if they can see my luggage ticket.. this Korean guy is photo'ing with his phone.. what's the problem I ask.. we can't actually track your luggage.. but don't worry he tells me, thank you for your understanding.
On the plane a series of announcements.. The plane will be delayed..
Due to a paperwork issue
Waiting for a few late passengers..
The captain has requested a safety check (slightly alarming)
There is a problem with the air conditioning, we assure you it will be cooler once we are airborne. I realise I'm sweating.
after each announcement.. "Thank you for your understanding".
I'm beginning to worry.. By the time we leave to a K-Pop version of the safety routine - we are almost two hours late. 

The staff all Korean are delightful behind their masks, they do a kind of bowing of the head in supplication on every interaction. 
It's 11 hours and I console myself with the thought that they might catch up the time on the way.. 
I switch on the flight map tracker to see if there is any hope - the route passes over Kiev towards Moscow... this can't be right..  

We arrive in Seoul airport flying alarmingly low from the sea over clumps of rocky islands as the sun is setting.. I have just been reading about North Korean missile tests over the South Korean sea. 


The horrible news of the Halloween crush with awful loss of life in Seoul city centre has cast a dark depressing shadow, this all ends up feeling fatalistic.
I'm thinking I'm going to me stuck in Seoul with no entry visa, no luggage and no escape. for sure all the seats on to Bali are sold out because of the G20.

But as I embark the aircraft a nice Korean ground staff girl is holding a sign with my name and bowing slightly.. 
"I'm sorry you flight has already left.. thank you for understanding.. here is a ticket to Singapore it is boarding now so you have to run, and here is a connection to Bali on Singapore Airways"
The connection time in Singapore was 6 hours.. but the flight to Singapore was in first class - spectacularly nice. The flight to Bali short and nice. Things were looking up.. I had expected huge queues in Denpasar airport, but in fact we was the first flight to land and I was off the plane first.. No queuing at all - delightful helpful passport control.. and a big surprise.. my luggage appeared like magic one of the first bags.
Ringo and Bondan waiting outside - hugs, smiles and a big welcome. 

I left on Tuesday morning from AW Sheffield and arrived in Bali Thursday morning.. looking a little bit bedraggled  and worse for wear. 
I'm sorry if this newsletter is a bit long.. Thank you for your understanding ...

Meanwhile in the UK a container arrived with some new items from China.
I went to the warehouse to check.. the Crystal Infused water bottles have arrived. They landed in our Slovakia warehouse a few weeks ago and created a storm.. almost sold out in days. 
Coco our China agent (and my wife) has done an amazing job.. checking every producer she could find, working with Bryant head of buying in the UK and Sandra our UK designer has done a fantastic job on the packaging. AW team work at it's best. Well done team.. I think we have the best quality and value on the market. See below..

Have a safe and fun Bonfire night weekend.
More news next week.

David

title: Asia Alert: News from KL
content_html:
Greetings from hot and humid Kuala Lumpur.

I just arrived yesterday and have meetings with our IT team (based here and lead by Raul the Mexican) and I'm also meeting with our main Salt Lamp supplier flown in from Pakistan.
Last week I was telling you about my wife (also our China agent) in lockdown in Jiangxi province (further update below) - you can read about it here.

It's only a week to go - to V day as they call in India.. Valentines day is almost upon us, but it is just the start of the Season of Love at AW which takes through Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter and the Wedding Season.
I arrived in KL yesterday afternoon after taking the evening KLM flight from Amsterdam. I never seen Amsterdam airport this quiet, the Coronus virus I guess is having an impact on the number of people flying, or maybe it's just because it is final Chinese New Year celebrations.
Mr Sugar my regular driver was waiting for me at the airport. He is a lovely South Indian guy with a goaty beard, jolly chat and always fills me in with updates on his family and local news. He told me that the virus had arrived, just a few cases but people were in flat our panic mode. He said it was impossible to buy face masks and sanitary hand wash the whole city had sold out. I checked in my usual hotel, before I had to fill in a lengthy declaration of health, a list which countries I had been to recently and tick any symptoms I may have from a long list, then they took my temperature with a laser gun pointed at my forehead. Finally deemed healthy I was actually allowed to check in. Over reaction? Maybe but if any hotel has a case or even a suspected case it could I suppose bankrupt them overnight.   

Since last week it's been mad busy at AW partly because of the approaching Valentines day, but also because lots of new stock arrived from India and Indonesia - and that always creates a bit of excitement. Also a container of Salt Lamps arrived. 
See below for the lines we have managed to get online...  
I'm so happy to see those products finally land in our warehouse and website - it's the result of hard work some four or five months ago. Regular readers will have followed the last Asian trip and how those products came to be.
Now the circle of life continues, because the next trip is just starting. From KL I will go to Bali and work with our man Ringo on the next Indonesian products, we opened a new warehouse there last year and it has spacious offices attached that I'm thinking to put to creative use. From there I will go to Kolkata to meet our man in India Mr Chatterjee - Tomas will arrive in India the same time. We will visit the orphanage in Serampore that we support to check on progress. Later we will go to Delhi then Bangalore to see some incense companies. The plan after that was to go to China.. but right now that seems to be a problem. There is a guy called Amila who works with Raul here in KL, he is from Sri Lanka - his home town is the centre of the gemstone area - so maybe we will go there and see if we can do business while we wait for China to open.

Coco update. 
First of all I have to say a big thank you to everyone who emailed words of support - I have passed on the emails to her and she is very much encouraged by them. Thank you.
I just spoke to her and all is OK, or as OK as it can be when you are in a locked down village. Normally for Chinese New Year I am also in that village, (it was only because of starting our new Spain company that I didn't go) I know the village and it's people very well. The residents are mostly old folks, at CNY the younger relatives come home and I think about 200 people will be there. It's literally a one road town, houses each side of the road, one or two behind and surrounded by rice fields as far as you can see. There are no restaurants, only two shops, one a small supermarket and agricultural supplies store belongs to Coco's brother and his wife.  The road in and out has been blocked with access only for police and health officials. Every few hours a police car drives through with loud speaker telling residents to stay in-doors at all time. Only one designated person is allowed out to shop every two days and they must wear a mask. A government health official stands guard at the shop to police this policy, and even though the shop belongs to Coco family she is not allowed any extra visits, she was even warned about trying to visit after hours. Anyway there are no new deliveries coming along the road so all the meat ran out a week ago, eggs are gone now they only have veg and rice. They have been told to expect the lock down for at least another week, but could be end of February. The good news is that no-one in the village has any symptoms everyone is healthy, but rumours abound that cases have been found in just the next village. The nearest city about 30 minutes away has a lot of cases, it's a big worry. Coco is like, well it is what it is, can only take it a day at a time, they are playing a lot of card games and Chinese chess. 
I'm sure it will be OK in the end, but who knows how it will play out. I'll keep you posted. But yes I'm worried, I'm losing sleep every night. 

Life goes on.. on Monday I made a visit to the NEC in Birmingham - it is years since I have been there and was interested to see what is grabbing attention. The main reason was to check on Agnes & Cat our posh British brand that needs this kind of trade show exposure. It was great to see the team in action, and was delighted to see it buzzing busy. Well done guys, I can see you worked incredibly hard. 

https://www.agnesandcat.org/

Anyway I hope you are also buzzing busy for Valentines Day, next Friday is the 14th and I'll update you then.
Wishing you have a lovely weekend, don't work too hard :)

Take Care

David

title: 7 Reasons why Soy wax will Boost your Sales
content_html:
If you haven’t had the chance to try burning soy wax instead of traditional paraffin, you could be missing out on a host of benefits for your nose and your health. In fact, burning soy wax in melt or candle form is a much better option than traditional paraffin for many reasons:

#1. Soy Wax is Natural

Derived from the soybean, soy wax is a hydrogenated vegetable oil that turns to a solid at room temperature. Soy wax contains nothing artificial, which makes it a better alternative to paraffin wax, which is made from petroleum oil and produces harmful by-products when burned or melted.

Luxury Soy Wax Melts
#2. Soy Wax Delivers a Cleaner Burn

Paraffin candles are associated with the blackness that accumulates on their jars and on surrounding walls and counters. However, soy candles give off very little of this soot which allows for a more pleasing appearance and easier breathing. In addition, soy candles are also non-toxic.

Soy Wax Jar Candles
#3. Soy Wax is Good for Earth

After harvesting, the soy beans are cleaned, cracked, de-hulled, and rolled into flakes. The oil is then extracted from the flakes and hydrogenated. This is the pure soy wax we make our candleswith. Soy is biodegradable and cleans up with water.

Soy Wax Candle Pots
#4. Soy Wax has a Lower Melting Point

From a safety standpoint, soy wax is the better choice because it has a very low melting point, it will melt at around 45C which is like warm bath water. This means less risk of burns should you accidentally spill any melted wax on your skin.

Soy Wax Jar Candles
#5. Soy Wax Scents are Stronger

Because soy wax burns cleaner than paraffin wax, the scent from its essential or fragrance oils is more pleasant and stronger-smelling than the scents added to paraffin. Here at Ancient Wisdom we add 20% Fragrance onto Soy Wax Melts so you can compare the strength to one 10ml bottle of Fragrance Oil.

Soy Pot of Fragrance
#6. Soy Wax Scents can be used on the Skin

Did you know your soy candle infused with essential oils makes a nourishing massage oil? Soy is only slightly warmer than your body temperature, so there is no risk of burning the skin.

Simply light the candle and wait about 20-30 minutes until a melt pool forms. Extinguish the flame, dip your fingers into the oil (or drip onto the body) and apply directly to the skin. The warmed oil can be directly massaged into the skin, leaving the skin smooth, soft, and pleasantly scented. Ancient Wisdom Soy Wax Massage Candles are made with pure blends of Essential Oils and Jojoba Oil.

Aromatherapy Soy Wax Massage Candles with Jojoba Oil
#7. We are Soy Wax Candles and Melts Experts

For many years we are developing range of Aromatherapy Massage Candles, Soy Wax Melts and Candles with carefully blended high-quality Essential Oils and Fragrance Oils. So rest assured AW candles can help you create a premium candle option for your customers at a reasonable price point.

Soy Wax Massage Candles

title: Scary, spooky, sad & happy in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Words cannot describe how thrilled I am to be back here. I have been here for one week, last week I was telling you about my (Squid Games) quarantine in Jakarta, which panned out differently than expected.. You can read about it here.

The flight from Jakarta to Denpasar, Bali was a Lion air flight. It's always a bit disconcerting because the way they pronounce Lion air over the tannoy.. sounds just like Ryanair.. and the flight was crammed and very cramped I had my knees crushed up against the seat. The customers were mostly Java people going on holiday to Bali. These days Bali survives on domestic tourists. However there was a scattering of europeans on the flight, mostly instagram influencers and I think one businessman like me. 


Boarding Lionair to Bali.

On arrival we were soon through the terminal, not really busy - ours was the only flight at that time. I had to queue up with the cool, trendy and tattooed influences to have my vaccine and PCR and proof of quarantine papers checked and stamped and then could grab my luggage and head outside.. 
Ringo is there, waving and jumping up and down waiting for me of course. Hugging like long lost friends..OMG Ringo it's so nice to see you!
It's been 433 days since I had to leave under dramatic circumstances. Our warehouse in Sheffield burned down.. regular readers will know the story. It's 1 year, 3 months, 6 days since I last hugged Ringo.
Sometimes numbers are significant.. Do you find that? Like from the day our warehouse burned down to the day we got the keys to Affinity Park.. was highly significant. 
I felt compelled to use timeanddate.com and check the time and date since last seeing Ringo. And the result makes the hairs on my neck stand on end...

  • 40,000,020 seconds
  • 666,667 minutes
  • 11,111 hours
  • 463 days
  • 66 weeks and 1 day
 In that time (the last 40 million seconds) so much has changed, so much happened, Ancient Wisdom has been through a massive period of change and renewal.. 
When the bubonic plague gripped Europe during the Middle Ages, ships would be isolated in harbours for 40 days before passengers could go ashore. The word quarantine originates from the Venetian dialect form of the Italian quaranta giorni, meaning “40 days”.
In the bible 40 is shorthand for "a long time" - eg 40 days fasting etc.

OK calm down everyone.. this is Bali, land of spirits and everything has meaning.
Ringo takes me to the warehouse and offices.. "Happy" our adopted dog remembers me tail wagging maddly happy as always to see me. As of course are all our team. It seems we also have acquired a new pet.  It's a pretty bird that sings to us as we work.
I ask where it came from? A little concerned that we are keeping caged animals.. Ringo explained that this bird had adopted us, rather like Happy did. She (I think it's a she) started tapping on the office window.. and for a few weeks would always be there.. tap tap.. then if it could get inside the office would come and sit - and sing and poop.. which is not ideal.  Regular readers will remember we had the same issue with a big black Raven at our old warehouse, when we moved into Affinity.. weirdly it happened again.
So Ringo bought a cage, and Putra jumped right in and seemed happy there. In the evenings she likes to fly around for a while. We think maybe she belonged to someone who had to leave Bali and had set her free.. Then in the wild wasn't comfortable so she looked for a new home. She chose Ancient Wisdom.


Putra, our new pet.


Happy, the AW guard dog.


The AW Bali Team.. 

So this week has been mad busy.. the office was stuffed full of sample products that we had initiated from Europe.. so I had a programme to go and see as many regular suppliers as possible and perfect and progress the products.


Meeting with the bead ladies in Sukawati.


The family that makes display stands and furniture. They were delighted to see me, almost crying.
We have seen so many people and kick-started projects everywhere that my head is spinning.. I could bore you for hours but I won't.
But Ringo wanted to take me to the bone carving village.. I told him our customers wouldn't really buy animal products. But we went anyway.. It turns out that near the bone carving village is a coconut oil factory, the discarded shells are available for crafting into new products such as candleholders and hanging plant holders.. the carving skills repurposed to carve coconut shells rather than (unpopular) bones. 
I have tried to buy these things before but always felt that the end price in your shops would be too high to get volume sales.. 


We met with the boss of one showroom on the main street with a large family compound behind with his extended family all employed in cleaning and carving the shells..


It's hot in Bali.. and as is common in the more remote villages he didn't really like to wear clothes too much :) 

I'm so happy to be back in Bali.. and I think we have a world of opportunities but still some obstacles to overcome. Shipping costs are high and shipping times are horrible as ships have to queue at major transit ports.

My first night in Bali - I abruptly awake at 4.20am.. heart beating. 
Bali welcomes me with an earthquake..the room is rocking around..  4.8 I later learned. That's not huge, but the epicentre was nearby. Close to Ringo's home town in Bangli. Sadly three people died.

So I have been staying at the Mansion Hotel in Ubud.. as a regular customer they were delighted to see me and gave me a grand suite room for 700,000 Indonesian rupee including breakfast. That's about £35 a night.. the normal list price for my room is $450 / night. Check out the hotel website for an idea of what Ubud is like. 
It's a little sad.. all the same staff are there, they know my name - the manager personally welcomed me. Breakfast is served in the room (the restaurant is closed)..  by a team of six staff - because they want to say hello. 
I'm the only customer, do they have any bookings? Not yet they tell me sadly.. 

More tales from Bali next week.

Take care and don't forget to be kind to someone today.

David

We met with the boss of one showroom on the main street with a large family compound behind with his extended family all employed in cleaning and carving the shells.. It's hot in Bali.. and as is common in the more remote villages he didn't really like to wear clothes too much :) I'm so happy to be back in Bali.. and I think we have a world of opportunities but still some obstacles to overcome. Shipping costs are high and shipping times are horrible as ships have to queue at major transit ports. My first night in Bali - I abruptly awake at 4.20am.. heart beating. Bali welcomes me with an earthquake..the room is rocking around.. 4.8 I later learned. That's not huge, but the epicentre was nearby. Close to Ringo's home town in Bangli. Sadly three people died. So I have been staying at the Mansion Hotel in Ubud.. as a regular customer they were delighted to see me and gave me a grand suite room for 700,000 Indonesian rupee including breakfast. That's about £35 a night.. the normal list price for my room is $450 / night. Check out the hotel website for an idea of what Ubud is like. It's a little sad.. all the same staff are there, they know my name - the manager personally welcomed me. Breakfast is served in the room (the restaurant is closed).. by a team of six staff - because they want to say hello. I'm the only customer, do they have any bookings? Not yet they tell me sadly.. More tales from Bali next week. Take care and don't forget to be kind to someone today. David

title: Why wet paint in Delhi?
content_html:
Greetings from Delhi airport.

We are escaping Delhi just ahead of the G20 meeting that is about to kick off. Next stop is the Pink city of Jaipur.

Last year I was in Bali, where the same event was taking place.. I have to say considerably calmer and better organised, but India likes it hectic and honking and all last minute.

Mr Chatterjee and I stayed at The Connaught, close to Connaught Place, the iconic circular shopping area built by the British and still a thriving lively place. 

Last week I was in Serampore, in Mr Chatterjee's home town.  If you missed that update you can catch up here. I stayed in the delightful Denmark Tavern.. the only hotel in Serampore without bed bugs.

When I checked out the staff came to say goodbye and wish me well and wave us off. it was quite touching. 



Since then we took an Indigo Air flight from Kolkata to Delhi. Mr Chatterjee organised a car and driver to meet us and then be at our disposal all week. You can do that kind of thing in India. 

One of our suppliers told us that the city will soon be closed for 3 days totally. In Delhi there are 20 five star hotels and for the duration every one of them is block booked. One hotel for the Americans, one for the Chinese, one for the British, one for the French etc.. as we leave for the airport they are still painting the curbs, sprucing up the gardens and erecting huge billboards (with G20 uplifting messages) to cover anything not pretty.. it's all very last minute. G20 is everywhere.. even humble rickshaw drivers have stickers.



You have to love and hate Delhi.. one thing I really hate is the smog and air quality that clogs your nostrils with strange black stuff.. but now I can see blue sky and and fluffy white clouds..the air is clean. I can breath deep .. so refreshing.. I hope it is a permanent improvement.. We went deep into the bowls of Old Delhi to meet our metal artifacts guy, Karman. It was sticking hot, and he met us curbside and lead us through the maze of tiny lanes, deep inside the wholesale area, into a tiny alley up several flights of windy stairs clogged with giant metal lions, or rusting iron pots.. finally to an upper room with just a long table.  Karman is an earnest young guy who has learned to love "Ancient Wisdom", and understand what we are looking for. He is well connected with the artisans of Delhi and an excellent organiser.. On the table he lays out a limited selection of goodies.. actually on the various floors of this building and other lock-ups around here he has an endless selection of erm.. various junk. Far to much, and enough to confuse your brain. But Karman is calm and well informed, he already knows our price points and he needs to be competitive.. 

However, selecting the ranges, taking photos, making design notes.. is hard work.. and in this hot humid room, with the overhead fan just barely chopping up the air and despite chilled Red Bull we ended up three sweating guys in a fug. Mr Chatterjee had a good idea.. lets grab all the samples we need and go back to The Connaught.. sensible idea and we met three other suppliers this week the same way.



Our hotel was not far (on the map) from Paharganj, one of the oldest gift trading areas - and we have a couple of suppliers who have showrooms there.. One day we decided to leave our driver and get some exercise and walk there..

On foot you see things.. things the average G20 delegate is never going to see.. here's a few snaps I took on the way.. from Connaught Place to Paharganj early morning by foot. 




I love and hate India at the same time.. so many rude annoying people and many polite gentle absolute angels. Dilapidated buildings and grand palaces.. On balance - I love it..

 

Anyway back in the UK.. it's all happening.. the hard work from earlier trips - is coming to fruition.. this week we have new incense lines, new Indonesia products, new China products, new xmas bath-bombs and more...So much new.. check everything out below. 

 

They are calling our flight.. so it's time to go to Jaipur.. it's many years since I was there.. we have two suppliers to see.. and I hope new ones to discover.

Full report next week.

 

Wishing you a lovely weekend, take care..

Namaste!

 

David

title: The Phoenix Phenomenon
content_html:
Greetings from Spain..


Hope you are well and enjoying (or escaping) the football :)
My good friend and next door neighbor; Alan is from Denmark.. so on Wednesday I had little choice but to join him in a sports bar to watch the England / Denmark match..
I'm not a football fan.. but I have to admit I enjoyed the buzz and bonamie of a bar half full of Danish and half Brits bonding over the beautiful game. 
Next up is the final on Sunday against Italy, and the  Italians at AW are beyond excited.. Josara here in Spain and Mauro from Customer service in the UK..
Actually I don't mind if Italy wins..  at least we won't have to suffer Borris trying to take credit whilst pretending he is a football fan (he isn't). OK ok calm down.. of course I want England to win.. but it's only a game for goodness sake.

Last week I was telling you about the anniversary of the fire at AW.. and shared some shocking screenshots from the CCTV  - if you missed it you can read about it here.
Lots of people wrote to congratulate us on our bounce back from the abyss.. Thanks everyone for your amazing support.. sure we came back but could not have done it with you.
It's not the first time (and probably not the last) that AW has faced serious setbacks but always and everytime something good has come from the bad.. it's the phoenix phenomenon. 

One example maybe I haven't mentioned in these newsletters.. is nasty set back that gave birth to the Spanish Team and AW Aromatics. 
Last night after work I had the privilege to have dinner with the AW Artisan team. I should give credit to Toni the team leader.. because the young team are as fresh and lively and full of ideas and quick witted and getting on together and loving making things happen and loving the products and delighting in customer relationships..as the Three Lions Team.. Now I know how Gareth Southgate feels.

    Some of the AW Artisan team enjoying an after work dinner.

Quentin, our French guy in Spain, said something very profound.. he said he really appreciated the fact that he had "A Team Leader" and not "A Boss" and that when mistakes happen it's not one persons fault, it is a collective issue and the team leader seeks to improve systems to make it not happen again. To see a team enjoying working together - enjoying spending time together - is like watching the beautiful game. 
A Team Leader is part of the process and involved and takes collective blame and collectively enjoys the success. A Boss distributes blame, lords it, dispenses punishment & favours, claims personal credit for successes. 

And the nasty set back that gave birth to AW Artisan.. well we used to have a partnership agreement and a 50% ownership of a company in Spain to distribute AW products here. Back in 2016, we began to discover "The Boss" of this company was faking the accounts, not paying taxes, and had even tried to fake 100% ownership. I should have known earlier due to the playboy lifestyle of "The Boss".. but you live and learn. When I refused to sign off fake accounts it all blew up and the partnership relationship broke down, the boss stopped paying for stock and services from AW and  refused to communicate at all. So quite a large investment blocked plus a large potential bad debt, so a hefty setback for AW. 
And today they still sadly pretend to customers they are part of AW.. even using pictures and product codes that reflect ours.  It's all very sad and desperate. Yes of course we are taking action but in Spain the court system is painfully slow.. and will grind on for years.. Anyway I don't much get involved just leave that to the lawyers, while enjoying getting on with developing and working with the team at AW Artisan in Spain. 
They really are a joy to work with, I call them "MFT '' it's an in-joke but whenever I mention this name there are gales of laughter.. can you work it out?

Meanwhile in the UK the new workspace for the team there is really taking shape.. The chill-out zone, the collaborative space, a table tennis table, a full kitchen and now we are adding in a "The Little Balianese workshop" where you can move to when you need to reset your thoughts.
It's going to be super cool, I'm just sorry I missed it happening.  

      

And finally I was telling you about a new logo for AW.. we commissioned a professional logo designer, who took note of the life story of AW, made a list of our values, and then listened patiently to Tomas and my impossible range of elements and ideas we wanted to incorporate.. actually an impossible task..
So it's still work in progress but here is a sneak preview.. 
Starting with the idea of fairly trading across the earth.. the circle of harmony that is trading with Artisans, dealing with Family retailers and trying to do it sustainably whilst treating the Earth with respect..
So Harmony & Earth.. at the core of AW.
                                


    This simple idea with a lot of work gave birth to this.


    and on packaging something like this.
 

Please feel free to give your feedback and thoughts..

Hope you have a wonderful weekend, if you are working, be kind to yourself and your team.
Stay safe - and more news next week.

David

title: A strange new normal. We are back
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield

Last week I was telling you about my trip back from Bali to the UK, following the devastating fire in our main warehouse. I was writing to you from the Qatar business lounge in Doha. You can read about it here.
The trip back was strange as you can imagine, on the only international flight out of Bali, empty airports, staff dressed like astronauts, I was given a face visor to wear over my mask.. in Doha strict social distancing and mandatory masks except if eating.

 

All flights but one cancelled.
Tomas met me at Manchester airport. My transit through the airport was pretty quick, not many checks - 30 second chat with an official medic guy.. not all staff wearing masks.. compared to Bali or Doha airports - a pretty poor show I thought. 

It all felt pretty depressing. Tomas drove me back to Sheffield, and straight to AW. Seeing the burned out Block B I knew would be difficult, but the physical sight was.. well there are no words..

I met with the team, who have all been through a gamut of emotions. I was here to take charge and lead them, I had to be strong. It had been only 6 days since the fire, and what they had achieved in that time is beyond belief.



We have a pretty good stock control system, so we know almost to the penny what stock was lost, really fortunately we had a lot of over-spill stock held in outside warehouses plus in our remaining three units on site. It has been a massive disaster but lots of lucky things like delayed shipments meaning that stock was saved. For example, we shipped face masks by air from China, they were due to be delivered on Friday but came Monday. Just in time for Borris Johnson to decide masks are actually a good idea.

The hottest selling thing right now is fashion masks.. and we have them.. but selling fast.

I'm happy to report that many essential oils back are online, some soaps, the olive oil soaps and we are working hard to get other production items online. A China container just came this week, and an Indonesian one that came last week is now online. So there is actually quite a bit of new stock available. The websites need cleaning up and that is work in progress, but you can see it happening fast.
In the meantime we have been looking for a new home for AW, our plan (right now) is to use the remaining units as production only, this would potentially double our old production abilities. And all the finished stock and imports go to a nice new warehouse. 
We have viewed some big beautiful places, as yet not settled on where to go. Our landlord says he can rebuild the old unit as quickly as possible and we could move back there. That is also a good and likely option, but we would still need a big temporary location. I'm working on it.  Lots of options, we identified about 10 possible locations around the area, and have been viewing big sheds all week.



In just a week so much has happened.. most employees back at work, some production underway, from Monday we started dispatching orders and we are starting a night shift from the coming Monday in order to double our current dispatch rate..
We just got the phone line back on, fast internet rather than tethering to mobiles is expected by Monday. It's gradually coming back to a new normal.
Thank you so much for all your massive support, all the messages that just keep coming, and the faith you put in us by continuing to order. Our new normal is a bit extreme.. but the first steps are being taken.

In my weekly newsletters you have followed me around the world, on various journeys..India, Nepal, China or Indonesia..  this journey is a different type on a different road .. the road to rebirth and then resurgence. . 
We have to do this, not just for the charities we support, not just for the 60 plus staff at AW, not just for the thousands of artisans and their families who depend on us.. We must do this for you.. our customers who complete the circle. 

I thank you for your support.

Now let's get back to business..

I hope you are staying safe, wearing a mask and getting used to the new normal.

Take care
More updates next week.
PS: Discover a wide range of high-quality wholesale soaps and indulge in a luxurious bathing experience - Click on the link now to explore our collection!

David

title: Brains, Rocks and Pandals in Kolkata.
categories: Kolkata | ancient wisdom | bad hotel | Durga Puja | Jute
content_html:
This week I'm in Kolkata with our Mexican computer genius; Raul from our UK office.. I'm buying cotton and jute products, Raul is acquiring a different but equally prolific product of this town.. Brains.
Yes you read correctly we are buying brain. Not Hannibal Lecter style but putting those very cleaver Bengally chaps to work for AW.

In a nutshell we use a contact management and marketing software the mad Mexican Raul has been designing and refining for a few years. We thought of making it available for other companies but to recast it as generally useful, customisable and user friendly is a herculean task for one Mexican.. so we are hiring a whole team here.
 Sector Five - Salt Lake Kolkata.

Kolkata is chaotic and crazy at any time, but this week is the big festival called the Durga Puja where the whole city is involved in building Pandals - sort of temporary temples some of which are bigger than real temples and stunningly beautiful. There is no denying though that this is a dirty and disorganised place. But out of all the craziness, power cuts and traffic james comes a kind of energy distilled in the very studious and gentle Bengally character. This is why all the big software companies come here to a place called Sector Five in Salt Lake. It's brain factory central.
 Pandals at night..  Building a Pandal.  Pandal Party.

I have to tell you a little story.. we have been staying in a (so called) boutique hotel.. called the Stadel it is claimed by the website to be 10km from the airport and a charming retreat. Both claims are 10km off mark. This hotel has been built beneath a monstrous crumbling concrete football stadium (hence the name). And like Kolkatta generally it's accident prone place. I kid you not.. while relaxing in my room late one evening. I'm reading a book on my bed when I'm shocked by a huge bang. The next thing I'm showered from above by plaster and small stones. Looking up a boulder shaped rock is protruding from the ceiling above me. I leap out of bed - get dressed and rush to reception waking Raul on the way. With in a few minutes I have the management and half the hotel staff in my room. Seems a chunk of concrete far above in the stadium has come loose and come crashing down. 
   That rock..

They were very apologetic and moved me to a new room with no charge and a bottle of good wine. This is India.. what can you do but smile?
More adventures next week.

title: The rain in Spain..
content_html:
Greetings from Malaga..

Shortly I will be travelling (with our man in Spain; Toni) to the UK.. for lots of things but the immediate one is the AW Christmas party.
Last week I had just arrived in Spain and was telling you about the creative folk of Indonesia, and speculating that Creative types are generally nicer people. 
I arrived exhausted from my trip to Indonesia.. and this week have been busy recovering and catching up with developments at AW-Artisan our Spanish company.
It's been raining in Spain.. a lot - flash floods and massive black thunder clouds.. I even had trouble getting out of my house this morning.. The front garden had flooded and the road outside turned to a small lake.

I arrived in Spain last Friday (36 hours travelli) and that same evening headed out to the AW-Artisan Christmas party in a very nice restaurant in central Malaga. Of course there was excellent food and wine and even better company.. We had a delightful time with plenty of little speeches and everyone was grateful and happy to work for AW.. eventually between the main course and the desert it was my time to give a speech.. By this time I'm a little frazzled and jetlagged and slightly tipsy.. but the speech went down well - I thanked them for their hard work all year and wished them the best for the future and didn't forget to mention that right now they are my Favorite Team..


Our group picture.. can you spot the sleep deprived Englishman?

The other evening here in Spain I visited my local bar to watch the football with my neighbour Allen.. It was Spain against Morocco - and eventually Spain lost.. You can imagine how that went down..
Anyway.. tomorrow evening (strikes and weather permitting) I will be in Sheffield for the AW and AW-Aromatics Christmas party.. and as it happens it coincides with the quarter final between England and France.. So that should be interesting.. I'm not really a football fan but I'm always interested to watch people watching football - all those tribal instincts kicking in.. 

I'm happy to see that more products arrived from Indonesia.. particularly the 2 million year old petrified wood candle holders.. These are really collectors pieces and in limited supply... (see below)
Regular readers might remember our trip to a village in Central Java where we met a delightful couple with a small business producing products from the local gemstones mined nearby..Natural River-stones, real onyx, local marble and rare petrified wood. I'm delighted those products are now here and available.


If you want to re-read that newsletter - here is the link.
 
Now Christmas is upon us.. I hope the season is treating you and your business well.. 
I know you are super busy - so this week's news is short and sweet..

Stay calm and be happy..

More news next week.

David

title: What Things Cost in Indonesia
content_html:
Greetings from Pantai Lembeng 

Pantai Lembeng, or Lembeng Beach is the site of our new office in Bali. We are getting to know the locals.. more details later.
Last week I was telling you about the adventure continuing.. and how we are making things happen at pace including beautiful new products coming your way soon. If you missed it you can catch up here..
Turkey update. Because of your support we were able to send more money to Hatice our agent, who is allocating funds directly to needy people. She messaged me this morning she is planning at trip to one of the worst affected areas to ensure your money is spent wisely. Thank you for your support, if you want to help you can by stocking the Turkish products we stock, link below.
On Tuesday we will catch a flight via Kuala Lumpur to Kathmandu so these are our last few days on Bali, and as always it's a mad dash to finish projects, place orders and get things done.

The mornings are spent visiting suppliers checking samples, refining details - if possible placing an order. In the afternoon we head to beach.. not to chill but to check on the progress of our new office.
I thought you might be interested to know what things cost here.. where our office feels lost and remote but actually we are only 15 minutes from the centre of Denpasar city. 


It's a small community here. There is a Balinese lady who looks after the carpark and charges a little money to the surfers that come to the one beach shack. She was happy to do a deal with us, for about £10 a month all our staff can access any time. Next door a guy called Ketut lives in a beach shack with four dogs, he was acting as security for the shack and the previous owner of our place. A helpful and jolly guy, with lots of local contacts, he is happy to keep an eye on the place at night and be a key holder, he says he will give us an early morning cleaning service and prepare the workspace ready for the team - cost about £80/month.. The warung (or local cafe) is run by a guy who at first glance looks European, a super gentle guy and super cook. He explains shyly that despite his looks he is Indonesian, from Java and is English is not that good. Apparently there are Dutch ancestors somewhere in his family tree and he was cursed to be born totally European looking. His limited menu includes some dishes that Dutch people would recognise, a tasty lunch dish is less than £2, a large freshly squeezed fruit juice less than £1. 
Today we have a dozen workers, plastering, tiling, fixing windows, laying a new road.. it's all happening. This morning I went with Ringo to a place that sells coconut trees. We selected and bought two from a lady called Kiki for £150 - her husband will come tomorrow and plant them. Ringo who loves gardening was horrified, they should be £30 each he thought, but Kiki told us since the Russians came she can sell all she can get and prices are high. But garden plants will still be cheap - you can buy all sorts of fast growing plants for £3 / dozen. So we will make a tropical garden.. for small money.. the high quality windows that we ordered and installed within a week cost about £1000, inside is now already quiet and peaceful. 


So we have everything we need to create a haven of creativity and hopefully attract the best and brightest young talent in Indonesia. Any beach front property in the world (especially near a city) is expensive. But apart from that our total renovation cost and set up of a fully functioning (very cool) office desks and everything we think will be about £15,000. Of course the total investment to bring the project to fruition is many times more than this.. but this is why we believe we can offer services at a serious advantage to you..  it will take time but we already have the bones of a product that can sky rocket your business super cost effectively.. more details later.

Russians & Ukrainians
They are everywhere, looking serious, slightly grumpy, conflicted and lost. Mostly young, often glamorous and good-looking. If you go in any bank it is full of them trying to open bank accounts. Our bank manager told me they have to limit applications to certain days otherwise regular customers cannot get service. They are severely limited as to how much money they can get out of Russia per month, and the Russian banks charge 20% commission on transfers. Only super rich have resources to get round that, probably with crypto currency. There are enclaves for rich Russians already like ParcQ (tagline The City of the Future) hidden away in the hills. But many here are not that well off and are struggling to survive. Foreigners cannot run businesses here without proper papers which are expensive (I know), and the local news is full of stories of Russians running illegal taxi services or such. This morning I had to visit the Immigration department for a brief interview and photo taken, with respect to my working visa.. there was a massive queue almost a thousand people a day I'm told are applying for Kitas papers - long stay visa's. Huge credit to the Balinese government, they have geared up for it, meet and greet people to help, free snacks for those waiting, ultra friendly staff. Now nine interview rooms rather than three, and an interview done with good humour and quickly in two minutes. 

They are mostly anti-war but some are not, I listened to one guy rant on about how all the western media have it wrong, Russia didn't start a war, blar blar blar.. but when I asked him, he said he never ever wanted to go back to Russia. 
Ukrainians here are even more conflicted, they escaped the war, but feel I guess like they are letting down the country by not staying to fight. Long faces.

We live in strange times.. next week we will be in Nepal, catching up with all our suppliers - the first visit since before the pandemic. 
Full report next Friday.

Meanwhile - lots of stuff is back in stock this week, such as Crystal Infused Glass Bottles and  Aromatherapy Candles ... plus some absolutely cracking new lines. We have solid colour dinner candles.. made in the UK.. and selling like crazy. Hot lines abound.. heaps of gemstone stuff, some new gemstone Glass Tea Infuse Bottles. 

Take care..

David

title: Do Calm Down
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I'm just packing up ready to go back to Asia. It's been a hectic few days in Spain, I had to extend my planned time here but at least we seem to be making progress.

I was chatting to a lawyer friend of mine.. he said all of Spain all, everyone he knows is appalled by the language of Boris in Parliament. "We always looked to the English as the example of politeness and fairness" this guy is mad and somehow we let him be in charge. 
Brexit is a serious business, lots of British people in Spain are thinking of leaving because of the uncertainty of their future here, and the economy, lots of businesses exist because of them. What happened to you Brits? he asked, Have you all gone totally mad?
Putting the serious consequences aside for a moment, what I find interesting is that the whole world is following the Brexit story.. I met two guys from Zambia in gemstones wholesale place in China. Got chatting.. and all they wanted to know about was Brexit. From India to Morocco to the middle of no-where in China people follow Brexit like it is a box set on Netflix. I really don't understand why our Brexit machinations just so fascinating to everyone..


All I can say is that those words.. "Surrender Bill" and "Do or die"  are no accident.. they have been carefully chosen to create emotions.. In marketing, words are vitally important.. this is marketing, and marketing is power, in the wrong hands - very dangerous.
Please, everyone.. Calm Down! don't get sucked into the emotional traps laid out by people who know how to hack your emotions/votes.

Katka in the UK has been attending Brexit readiness seminars.. reading everything possible, getting all the advice. Lots of letters from the government, telling us to get ready.. How? What do we need to do? When it all boils down they don't have a fringing clue.

At AW we do have a kinda plan.. our warehouse in Slovakia and now in Spain.. but how we will deploy things? - who knows until it happens.
Hopefully, we have the beginnings of our team in place for the new Spain warehouse, I have been interviewing and chatting to prospective team members. There is lots of talent in Spain. It's all going to come together in November, right now just preparing the ground ready for the big launch.  Talking about calming down.. I really am getting excited about our new Spain project. must try not to bore everyone.

Olive tree update.. a few weeks ago I was telling you about our new olive tree (it's a meta-fore also for our new Spain company), the fox that had been digging up the soil at night has gone, stopped it's vandalism. So now it is doing well, a huge crop of olives are in the branches, and the other night I found an owl sitting in the branches.. what does it mean? In the bible it says judge a tree by it's fruit, not how pretty it looks. I need to learn how to cure olives so we can eat them.. 



Got to leave our olive tree (and house) for a few weeks. Tomorrow back to China will meet up with Tomas who has been working day and night ceaselessly on the next ranges of products that we hope will fly of your shelves and websites.. We hope to finalise some deals next week, and then it's off to India, to do something similar. Then if all goes to plan - but who knows with crazy Brexit.

The good thing is we are mega busy, and coping with it as well.. orders are 30% up on the last year.. we have masses of temporary staff in AW to help out. Many from the EU of course.. Katka tells me there are some really great guys who we should be thinking of taking on permanently.. but with Brexit uncertainty - how can we?

Salt Lamps are back in stock.. lots of other new products this week. It's kinda crazy..

Take care.. news from China next week.. It's the big China party.. 70 years celebration.. apparently it's going to be HUGE! I'll give you a full report.

David
