title: David's AW News: 9 Years in Slovakia... and Wedding Bells Too
content_html:
Greetings from Spain...

Well, I am still here.

The Spanish summer is slowly turning up the thermostat and while parts of the UK seem to have reverted to their traditional "four seasons in one afternoon" weather pattern, here in Andalucía it is definitely feeling more like summer every day. 

Last week I was telling you about the Jacaranda trees of southern Spain, whose spectacular purple blooms transform whole streets into rivers of colour for just a few short weeks. If you missed it, you can catch up here: Why Málaga Has Turned Purple

Unfortunately there is still no news on my TIE residency card. No card. No appointment. No useful information. The Spanish bureaucracy machine continues to operate at its own mysterious pace. As regular readers know, this saga has already provided enough material for a small novel, and I suspect there may yet be another chapter or two to come. Stay tuned.

Meanwhile, life across the AW family rolls on.  

This week is a very special one in Slovakia as Peter and Tamara are getting married. Peter works closely with our Bali team and, judging by the messages flying around, the excitement levels in Indonesia are every bit as high as they are in Europe. Weddings have a wonderful way of bringing people together, even when they are separated by thousands of miles and several time zones.


Congratulations, Peter and Tamara from all of us. We wish you both every happiness for the future.

Talking of celebrations, this week also marks nine years since the first day of trading for our Slovakian operation.

Nine years!


The first day was a little basic :)

What started as a small adventure has grown into one of the most important parts of our group. The team there have built something truly impressive through hard work, determination and a lot of belief along the way.

Happy Birthday AWGifts Slovakia. You have come a very long way and we are all incredibly proud of what you have achieved.






The good news is he is leaving for what sounds like a dream job at a paddle club. Opportunities like that don't come along every day, and we wish him every success in his new adventure.

One thing I've noticed over the years is that people often stay with Ancient Wisdom for a long time. And when they eventually move on, they never really disappear. They remain part of the wider AW family. We still bump into them at trade shows, hear about their adventures, exchange messages, and occasionally even persuade them to come back and visit.

Once you're part of AW, you're always a little bit part of AW.

Good luck Kane — and enjoy every minute of the new role.

Hot weather - Summer Vibes - It's a great time for t-shirts - Check our the Nomad Sari range - selling well right now.. It's a great time for Tote Bags.. Check out the new Iconic Bags - also selling well right now.. 

See Summer Gifts At AW -  Hot sales for hot weather..




With Father's Day getting closer and summer events beginning to fill calendars across Europe, we're also seeing plenty of activity across the business. New stock arrivals from India are now landing online, fresh product lines are appearing daily, and there are some excellent deals available across the ranges.  

So if you haven't visited the website recently, it might be worth taking another look. And check out the latest from Holly.. Can you Sell This?


Until next week, thank you as always for your support. 

All the best!

David

Befit from keen shipping rates and we do the hard work bit. Con's: You will still need to buy samples to work with. There are some very successful and creative sellers using the AW and doing just this.. you know who you are!

We are learning as we go along.. We have just set up a backend store for the aforementioned Agnes & Cat products. Ask for Rodrigo on our Whatsapp link in the AW website for more details if you'd like to get involved. 

Meanwhile 
There are new products coming online from our AW Aromatics factory.. and we are still socking it to you.. with Free Hop Hare sock samples with every order.

title: Meet the music Guru
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali, Indonesia

Happy Haloweeen weekend - scary how it has come round so fast. 
Of course we are holding the traditional AW Halloween costume competition.. watch out for a separate email where you can vote for your favorite scary AW spook.  Free shipping vouchers for contributing.
Here's a sneak preview picture..


This is my second Friday in Bali, and I still can't get over how strange it feels. Am I the only Engishman in Ubud? 
No sign of Halloween here.. in years past when I have been here - all the bars and restaurants would embrace our odd festival and entertain the visitors.. today almost no visitors so Halloween is redundant.
It's scary, peaceful and quiet. Ubud used to be a creative hub of energy and activity has now regressed into a sleepy backwater village where everybody knows your name.
It's hotter than normal even for Bali and that makes everything a bit slow, if I take a morning walk along the lane outside my hotel, old ladies wave and say "Salamat pagi pak" - Good morning Mr.. The young girl in the laundry shack smiles brighter than the sun when I give her a tip of 15k Rp - less than £1.. My laundry all neatly ironed and carefully packed and scented with frangipane only costs the same. Fresh healthy local food from the warung costs about £2 or less a dish - and they will deliver it to my room. 
I was locked down in Bali in the early part of the pandemic, and it was peaceful and quiet then.. but now it seems that Bali has slipped further back to another earlier simpler kinder age..Ringo told me people have forgotten about money these days and now value friends and family and good community relations as what is most important.

Last week I was telling you about my arrival in Bali, and how immediately the spiritual side of Bali makes itself known. If you missed it you can read about it here.

Meanwhile of course I have been busy, all our old suppliers want to show me the product developments they have been working on. And plenty of new ones too.  So I've been really busy.. not at all sleepy.
A while back at a trade show in India I was chatting to an American buyer, who had a very big business (not very different in scope to AW) based in California. He asked me where else we were sourcing from and I mentioned Indonesia, "Oh really" he said, "musical instruments right?" - I said no, not at all.. after chatting I learned that they had done really well with everything musical from Bali including Hapi Drums, Healing Drums, Kambela, bamboo flutes and allsorts of tribal instruments. I took a look at their website and was inspired.
On my next trip to Bali I went to the music wholesaler area.. and immediately came unstuck, because I'm about as musical as a sausage sandwich. And since I clearly didn't know foggest about music.. the vendors lost interest in me.

While I was locked down in Bali early last year.. trapped indoors.. for something to occupy my free time I thought I might try guitar lessons.. So I hired a teacher.. or as they call them here a Guru.  So I met Bondan, a very cool guy who worked at a local music store and in his off time taught guitar. This time.. thinking about those musical instruments.. I had a bright idea.. let's hire a Music Guru to help us, I whatapped him and arranged a meeting  with Ringo and myself. Bondan and Ringo immediately bonded and Bondan readily agreed to spend a couple of days helping us tell fake gongs and rattles from the real stuff.

Here is Bondan doing his stuff.


Any ideas and feedback is of course welcome!
 
Meanwhile in the UK it's almost November (clocks go back, don't forget on Sunday.. you can sleep an extra hour).
We were expecting lots of stock.. something like a container a day for the next couple of weeks.. but gradually it seems every container is getting set back.. no drivers, congestion in the port, ships stuck at sea.
In the past at a push this time of year ships could divert to an EU port and the goods could tranship via the channel tunnel.. since Brexit this option is not available.
It's very bad! We are arguing like mad and doing our best.. but stand by for major shortages. More scary than Halloween.. It's no joke I'm afraid.
 
Take care, have a great weekend.
Lots of love, cool vibes, mystical whispers and a few dings and dongs from Bali.
More news next week

David

title: Explaining what it means..
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield!

Yes it's true I'm here at the beating heart of AW.. in  Affinity Park the HQ of AW.
I flew here with Toni (our man in Spain), Malaga to Manchester on Ryanair. I was expecting a lot of stress but it seems no-one wants to go to the UK and therefore there were no queques anywhere.
Even the covid tests in both Spain and Manchester were stress-free, quick and easy. 
Last week I was telling you about the epic journey I had from Bali, Indonesia to Malaga, Spain. And Tomas' even more epic journey from Sheffield to Malaga. If you missed it you can read about it here.

o sadly not much time in Spain, but we did have our AW-Artisan Christmas Party.. sorry I mean gathering. Which was actually pretty epic, it was one of the reasons that Tomas was also in Spain. It's actually only our third Christmas of AW-Artisan - the first in the innocent days of December 2019, just before the pandemic. The Spanish company had just been re-born as our previous distributor relationship had broken down.  So we started fresh, and despite AW-Artisan immediately having to face the pandemic, and then deal with fire at AW in July later that year, by the Christmas of 2020 it had grown considerably.. by the Christmas of 2021.. we had leapt forward and really made things happen. 
I'm really proud of the team and what they have achieved in just three Christmases. A good team with a good heart, hard work and a good leader can make magic happen. And they have achieved much more in a little over two years than the old team did in ten years. I'm really proud of them and jokingly like to call them "My favourite team" - it's a bit of an in-joke at AW.. 

At the Christmas party, there were lots of heartfelt speeches and toasts.. And so after my speech I asked them to raise a glass and to huge cheers I said.. "To my favourite team!" Everyone was very happy.
But.. yes.. erm of course I can't say that. It's going to upset the other favourite teams.. So just to clarify what I mean.. compared to the old Spanish team.. Toni and his team are definitely my favourites.

MFT!!!

Of course last year, Christmas parties anywhere at AW were off the menu as we dutifully followed the rules (unlike our friends in no.10). This Christmas we are determined to make up for that where possible.
Hence a lovely party in Spain and tomorrow at AW UK is our Christmas gathering.. a 1920's themed happening in a nice hotel. 
Sadly in Slovakia our team is suffering from the worst wave of covid yet so things are not happening.. Hopefully we can make it happen in January. Despite the restrictions they are making it happen - our thoughts are with them.

So I had been looking forward to seeing the AW HQ.. the offices have been completed after my last visit.. and I was dying to see the work space we have created for the team (MFT) at Affinity. And I'm not disappointed it's lovely.. a creative zone for marketing and nurturing and a very green zone for customer service.. a chill out room and a collaborative space for meetings. Even more impressive is the now pretty full and buzzing warehouse, the projects at our production unit all coming to fruition soon.. the dropshipping products and team in action.. And despite a difficult year, with a pandemic, supply chain issues and not least the crazy madness of the destructive effects of that thing called Brexit.. Through it all we came through and found a way and made it happen. 

And as promised I have to explain the thinking behind our logo revamp and the new look AW that is slowly emerging.. I hope you like it and come to love it..  

First of all notice how the Triangle, Circle and Bar are intertwined, linked and dependent on each other.
Then understand that the combined symbol is made up of two ancient alchemy symbols, first the earth symbol ..

Not just the planet earth but the actual earth beneath our feet. The earth that gives forth life as plants grow. It symbolises prosperity, fertility, groundedness & creativity.

Earth that supports and sustains us but must be nurtured and cared for hence.






The circle is symbolic of care and harmony ..
From the earliest of times, the circle has been a symbol of care, harmony and completeness. An unbroken and never ending circle symbolises a commitment of love that is also never ending.

So at Ancient Wisdom we always instinctively felt that our mission is to complete the circle whilst caring for the earth. Hence combining these most ancient elemental symbols.The triangle in the symbol also means the three way link between Artisans - Retailers - Customers - with that circle making it happen. The family businesses in India or Indonesia that make beautiful things, the family businesses that do the important task of retailing and connecting with the actual family that is giving a gift as an act of love (symbolised by the circle). The bar across represents the supply line from the hands of artisan to the homes and hearts of your customers.  We are intertwined, linked and dependent on each other.

So you my friends are part of, actually at the heart of, the mission of Ancient Wisdom. Welcome to our world.

Well it's all happening at AW and we want you to be part of this..
Today as I arrived it was Xmas Jumper Day ..


So Seasons Greetings
More news next week from the worlds of AW..

Take care.

David

title: About Albesia and a dodgy deal...
content_html:
I just want to thank everyone who is supporting the Kiva microbank initiative I mentioned in last weeks newsletter. Absolutely brilliant. You know only half the world has access to finance, the very poor in the developing world are just too small fry for regular bankers to bother with. Via Kiva you can be a small scale bank, you won't make any money but you will help real people.
People like the tipsy family I mentioned last week (also thanks for ordering their mosaic bowls).
More Indonesia stock is arriving on-line by the day, (and there is another container due).

We just uploaded these really cool gold painted Albesia wood Buddahs, which reminded me of the trip to the candlestick village, where these are made.
Ringo (our man in Indonesia) had heard that a village head man had secured an order for one design of candlestick to a very big French company. He then shared the work thought the village, bringing a mini wave of prosperity with it. We went to see him.
In a low long workshop, below the water-level of the village damn we found him turning albesia wood on a lathe. Next to him a pile of freshly turned candlesticks. Sunlight streamed in though a back window, and looking out I could see dragonflies skimming the palm fringed water at eye level mist shrouded mountains behind. Damn! they so often have spectacular views to work with.
He turned out to be a jolly chap, somewhat of a local hero.
Ringo knows everything, a regular insiders guide to handicrafts in Indonesia.
In the hills all the farmers and craft workers grow a few albesia trees where they can, but they cannot be cut by law until the trunk reaches 50cm, this ensures a sustainable supply. So a lot of wood is brought from Java where they have large commercial farms. They grow quickly, to maturity in about four years. If a handicraft producer can use his home grown wood, obviously it's a big bonus. It's a relatively new handicraft wood, only really useful with modern curing and drying technique. Thus I'm happy to say it is a very eco-friendly wood.
Taking us outside in the sunlight he proudly showed us a crumpled piece of blue paper, stamped and signed in various places and bearing the name of a big French supermarket. I could see the price agreed, and he showed us a nice classic whitewashed candle stick they had made. Eighty thousand pieces. Wow.
I asked him what it was like dealing with such a big company. He told us that an agent from Jakarta had turned up and dealt with everything, he'd never met anyone from the company.
It had been like a blessing from above and changed everything, why anyone would want so many lumps of trees was beyond him.
I said we might - not as many but a few. Ringo gave him his usual speech about how AW is an importer from Europe, how we try to be straightforward, how AW pay his (Ringo's) wages and that we won't be asking for hidden commissions or last minute discounts. I gave him my business card in the usual Asian fashion - held between finger and thumb of both hands details facing him. He studied it carefully - although I'm sure he wouldn't understand anything - and tucked it safely away.
In that case, he told Ringo, he could give us a good discount off the supermarkets price. But we don't want that many, and not just one design, a lot of designs. No problem.
Turns out that the dodgy agent from Jakarta had demanded a hefty backhander, which had to built in to the price. That was the day we got a better price than the big boys.
View from the workshop. Notice the albesia logs.
Ringo explaining about albesia
Take care and happy trading.
David

Damn! they so often have spectacular views to work with. He turned out to be a jolly chap, somewhat of a local hero. Ringo knows everything, a regular insiders guide to handicrafts in Indonesia. In the hills all the farmers and craft workers grow a few albesia trees where they can, but they cannot be cut by law until the trunk reaches 50cm, this ensures a sustainable supply. So a lot of wood is brought from Java where they have large commercial farms. They grow quickly, to maturity in about four years. If a handicraft producer can use his home grown wood, obviously it's a big bonus. It's a relatively new handicraft wood, only really useful with modern curing and drying technique. Thus I'm happy to say it is a very eco-friendly wood. Taking us outside in the sunlight he proudly showed us a crumpled piece of blue paper, stamped and signed in various places and bearing the name of a big French supermarket. I could see the price agreed, and he showed us a nice classic whitewashed candle stick they had made. Eighty thousand pieces. Wow. I asked him what it was like dealing with such a big company. He told us that an agent from Jakarta had turned up and dealt with everything, he'd never met anyone from the company. It had been like a blessing from above and changed everything, why anyone would want so many lumps of trees was beyond him. I said we might - not as many but a few. Ringo gave him his usual speech about how AW is an importer from Europe, how we try to be straightforward, how AW pay his (Ringo's) wages and that we won't be asking for hidden commissions or last minute discounts. I gave him my business card in the usual Asian fashion - held between finger and thumb of both hands details facing him. He studied it carefully - although I'm sure he wouldn't understand anything - and tucked it safely away. In that case, he told Ringo, he could give us a good discount off the supermarkets price. But we don't want that many, and not just one design, a lot of designs. No problem. Turns out that the dodgy agent from Jakarta had demanded a hefty backhander, which had to built in to the price. That was the day we got a better price than the big boys. View from the workshop. Notice the albesia logs. Ringo explaining about albesia Take care and happy trading. David PS: If you have never ordered before... Check out our First Order Bonus : £100 worth of stock (@RRP's)!

title: Moving Times
content_html:
Greetings From the New AW-Aromatics factory in Sheffield. 

Last week I was writing from Malaga airport on the way here. We had been having the usual parties in Spain.. and I was explaining about "My Favourite Team".. if you missed it you can catch up here.

The main reason to be in Sheffield, apart from catching up with family and friends (and downing the world's best pale ale) is to be here for the huge move into our new production facilities.. It's a massive opportunity, gamble and big adventure all rolled into one. 

Sheffield is my home town.. and it's always nice to be home. 

My other home town (regular readers will know) is the magical town of Ubud in Bali.. it's giftware heaven - full of artisans and small family businesses making beautiful things..

This week they have been having a terrible weather condition turning Ubud into a mud bath. My friends there keep sending me updates on how big the mess is there.



Only one mess is bigger and a welcome distraction for them (and causing great amusement) is the disaster that is British politics.. sometimes it feels as if the whole world is bemused by Britain.

The idea that Boris is coming back, and there are plenty of people who like that idea is just beyond me.

 

Anyway we have our own distractions the grand move is underway.. our old warehouse (it burned down if you remember in 2020) has now been rebuilt bigger and better and we are moving our production in right now.

The move is literally a few meters.. so from early this morning a stream of AW folk have been hand carrying .. Pot plants, desks, bath bomb machines, mixes, pallets of oils, stacks of boxes all manner of things.. it's like an anthill of activity taking down one world and recreating it on a larger scale just across the way.

Over the next few weeks, we will fill in the details.. new production lines coming on stream, a beautiful new showroom, and nice reception area. The staff will get a lovely staffroom and we will keep you updated..

Our brand Agnes & Cat which is made here will officially move here.. meaning you are buying directly from the factory..  which we hope will improve service levels and less out-of-stocks.

So you can see it's all go at AW..

 

 

Meanwhile, lots of stock is being delivered to our main AW warehouse.. some exciting new products are coming online from India, Indonesia and Morocco.. 

I have to mention the Wild Hare Gift sets.. our outstanding best-selling products.. see below.

 

Take care and have a wonderful weekend.

More news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: My first time as a Youtuber (it's not good)
content_html:
Greetings from the AW warehouse, Ketewel, Bali


It's been one of those weeks, lots of challenges and super busy.

I have been spending time in the beach office, because we have a new Dropshipping website with lots of enhanced features in the pipeline. This needs lots of brain power and attention to details, the programming team are totally on it. But yesterday I escaped with Bondhan and his friend who is a professional photographer to Ubud and the villages beyond. It finally stopped raining and the rice terraces and hidden away country lanes looked pristine and beautiful.. or mission, to catch up with suppliers but also to make some content. Bodhan had a plan to interview one of our oldest suppliers in his home.
Lush rice terrace in real Bali.

On the way we dropped in to see a few suppliers.. and made "content" because you see the plan is I'm to be a youtuber.. I'm not sure about this..
We will put this particular content out later.. this Pacman (we call him) he is like the village head.. and at any time maybe 50 local artisans are making products for AW. Pacman is pretty creative himself but spends a lot of time sourcing materials and organising the artisans of his village. The guy sitting with him is a Buddha carver.
He tells us the impact doing business with AW has had on his village. You will soon in the AW youtube channel.

Well it is the last day of February.. the Season of Love is underway.. In Spain they tell me it is Andalusia Day!   which means lots of flowers and lots of Love. Mother's Day is coming - Spring is round the corner and hints of sunshine over the British Isles. Soap Flowers are trending.. lots of orders I can see.. So 

Meanwhile an update.
The petition I started to fairly Tax Temu..

THIS HAS TO STOP! TEMU IS KILLING UK RETAIL AND THE ENVIRONMENT!

Well amazingly it went/still going viral.. gaining 36,000 signatures (and counting)... as I type this.

Quite exciting really - and the amount of comments and feedback is immense! This topic has really hit a nerve.  

Even Change.org contacted me directly to say how good the response was and maybe they could introduce us to their contacts in the media.
I'm really hoping we can get some action.  If you didn't sign yet, check it out here. Tax Temu.

If you have already done that thank you so much! 
Next (this is a one minute job). go here:. parliament.uk then use the search at the bottom of the page.
Find your MP and send them a link to the petition. I know many of you are already doing this..But the more we do it the better. And one better would be to send it to Rachel Reeves herself.. 
Thank you so much.

Now this is embarrassing.. 
You can also watch my very first youtube video.. Subscribe, like and share!  OMG haha.. this is not me..   

So here it is my very first actual attempt at being a Youtuber :/  Actually I enjoy writing this newsletter. I have been writing every Friday for Donkey's years.. but the idea of being on camera is not my style. But what the hell. 
Since now apparently I have to be a Youtuber.. Well at least this particular cause motivated me enough to try.. 
Please be kind.. constructive criticism accepted.. the next will be better I promise. I only relented and did this because.. well I am VERY ANGRY.
Meanwhile..
There is new stock.. We have some beautiful Bali made Silver just landed. See below.
Also a container from India with beautiful boxes and more.. you have to see it to appreciate it.
Consider a trip to our showroom.. we are getting rave reviews recently. And Rodrigo and team love to see you.

OK guys thanks for your support.
Have a lovely weekend.

David
(AW founder and Youtuber )

title: It's a Kinda Magic
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

I'm leaving on a jet plane.. very soon! Next week if all goes well I will be just starting quarantine in a hotel in Jakarta. Yes, it's time to return to Indonesia.
Less than two weeks to Valentine's Day - which I always think is like the starting gun for the Season of Love.. Mother's Day, Easter, Father's Day etc up to and into the Wedding season. It's a great time for gift traders like you.
But the cost of living crisis is upon us, people are going to be squeezed like never before - this can't be good for business. Calm down everyone I will explain why below..

Last week I was telling you about the "Year of the Tiger" and reminiscing about visiting my wife's hometown at Chinese New Year in 2019. It's actually a tiny village in Jiangxi province - in the middle of nowhere.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Don't panic. It was back in 2008 everyone was stressed in the aftermath of the financial crash, banks were in trouble, mortgages were hard to get, companies crashing on every side. I remember it well, we were running around like crazy trying to fulfill orders. We couldn't work it out, everyone else was complaining but as if by magic we seemed to be doing ok. Then I figured out the reason why.. and we doubled down and refocused to even greater success.

So what was happening then? Maybe history won't repeat itself exactly.. but I feel there is a lesson to learn.

When those times of financial uncertainty hit, people naturally put off buying the big things like new cars, homes or home extensions.. Instead what we humans do is comfort each other with the little things. Buy each other small affordable gifts, make our homes feel more homely and secure, and turn to the more spiritual / comforting / homely / magical things in life. If we don't buy cars - we do buy candles. And at AW we have exactly that kind of comforting and magical giftware.. think not only candles, but aromatics, gemstones, crystal balls, windchimes, dreamcatchers, herbal tea.. you name it, at AW we have everything and anything that will give your customers that warm spiritual glow. 

So don't fear AW is here :)

Talking about candles. I was delighted to see the new Magic Spell Candle range selling.. well like magic. Why? Because this was a real team effort that made this happen and if you will indulge me I'd like to tell you the story whilst giving credit to the team that made it happen. Over the last few weeks, containers of stock arrived from China in Spain, Slovakia and UK.. with a brand new range of candles from our AW candle factory in Yiwu. Please note I'm not trying to sell you these candles, because within a week or so they will be sold out. 6 months estimated supply will sell (it seems) in 6 weeks, so I'm sorry but it will be about May before they can be back in stock.

Here is the team.. (that made it happen)
Tomas.. called me in April.. a customer had seen some repurposed grave candles (those plastic tube candles) with esoteric designs called Spell candles.. Let's make something like this he excitedly told me and opened a shared google spreadsheet with a list of possible candles.
David (that's me).. "But not in plastic please.. and if we are going to make it.. it needs to be soy wax..- Let me ask Coco in China".
Coco.. "Yes we can do that.. and I checked with our glass jar supplier and they have exactly a jar like that and at a good price".
Graciela.. (that's our Spanish designer girl) "Give me the ideas I can design packaging and labels.. but someone needs to write the text.."
David: "I can do that" - thinks.. Spell candles are the perfect gift - and a perfect Ancient Wisdom thing.. candles have always been a focus point of devotion or prayers. A gift for every eventuality whatever your friends problems are there's a candle for that. A candle for love, one for friendship another for protection. 
Tomas: "What if they had gemstones in them? what if the fragrances & gemstones matched the spell's purpose?"
David.. "I'm on it!"
Toni (our man in Spain).."is it possible to put a cork on top, it is going to look more magical.."
Coco.. "Let me try and find a cork supplier.."
Graciela, Toni, Coco, Tomas and myself spend May, June and July - tweaking the designs, and concepts. Coco ordered the jars, corks, chipstones and organised production. A few weeks of product testing.. the right wick, how many chipstones is good, what's the burn time.. this is hard work.. meanwhile label designs went through various shapes and sizes, test candles made. Our trusty box maker man made several different boxes and we tested several designs.. 
Coco.. "Yes we are finally in production.. and should have stock ready to ship by October".


So it was teamwork.. and many more AW people tossed in thoughts and ideas along the way.. it was a team effort.. and together we made something magic.. I'm not claiming these candles are really magic.. but they make a lovely gift with a new slant, that sells well in your shops and websites... and that dear reader really is magic.

The creation of new products is always hard work, but thoroughly enjoyable.. it's what we like to do at AW.. the most satisfying part of course is when our customers (and their customers) are happy.
Many of the best ideas of course come from our amazing customers.. 

That's just one new product story.. but we have lots more in the pipeline.
And this week quite a few new products have emerged from the UK aromatics factory...
See below.. all exciting stuff.. and we might be sold out of Magic Candles (for now) but there is always something magic on the way at AW.

Next week: news from Indonesia.
If you have any ideas for products do let me know.

Take care.. have a totally magical weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: Hotel room meetings in India..
content_html:
Greetings from Greater Noida, India

It's more noisy than ever in India. I'm visiting our suppliers in the trade show in Greater Noida which is an extension of Delhi. Last week I was telling you about being a Festival VIP and not really liking that. If you missed it, you can catch up here.
Since then Mr Chatterjee and I caught an Indigo flight from Kolkata to Delhi, and the same day Tomas flew from Denpaser to Kuala Lumpur and on Batik Air (highly recommended) to Delhi. Mr Chatterjee's son, Drishanta met Tomas at the airport and brought him to our hotel. Arriving late at night, so on Wednesday morning we met, had breakfast and hit the trade show here. Our hotel (you need to book it six months in advance) is inside the grounds of the exhibitions and we can walk directly into the sprawling halls of creativity.
Tomas and Drishanta

Lost money saga.
As soon as Mr Chatterjee and I landed in Delhi and exited the airport (quick and efficient these days) we were of course checking messages. A long time ago we sent €29,000 to Mr Chatterjee's trading company, I was telling you before that because our accounts department used the word "Zest" in the reference text the money was blocked because there is a Russian company under sanctions with that name. The bank in Paris, an intermediary branch had blocked it.. but obviously fashion shows and long lunches meant the compliance team took their time and many emails and calls and the help from our awesome local manager and eventually they accept that Mr Chatteree makes harmless Tote bags (not WMD) and ticks the box that releases the fund.. Only to have the next bank in the antiquated Swift system block the fund. This bank in New York, too busy and probably preoccupied with some local election, is not getting on with it either.. A few hundred emails later from our bank, the Indian receiving bank, Mr Chatterjee and me.. they finally released the fund. In the taxi at the airport Mr Chatterjee shows me the email detailing the transfer release.
But.. the value date on the release form shows 26th Feb 2026 - In 2 Years time!.. Some dyslexic kid in NY has mistyped the date and we are back to square one. All the way from the airport to our hotel Mr Chatterjee is on the phone, persuading, arguing, shouting.. in the honking jarring traffic for over an hour. We roll up at the hotel and he says.. they have accepted it's a mistake and just released the funds.
Thanks to all one million Indian gods.. finally. Only six weeks to send a so-called "Swift" payment.  

Still noisy in India - My theory.
Every few minutes in the trade show, an announcement is made by some lady with a loud screeching voice. Music pounds, people shout. Out on the street cars honk constantly and the traffic is crazy.. I have been coming to India for more than 20 years.. is it getting better?. actually no it's not. The rest of Asia has rapidly got cleaner, quieter and more organised. India despite much more efficient airports and new roads.. is getting more noisy than ever. I have a theory. It's in the DNA - they love the chaos, noise and the hecticness. 1.4 billion people of lots of different cultures, classes and religions rub up against each other. In the main everyone gets on with each other, but they need to fight their corner or get crushed..  and they embrace the process, heck it's fun! Cars and trucks have signs saying "Please Honk" traffic rules are not enforced all of life is a vibrant noisy game.
The Durga Puja I was telling you about last week is basically a non-stop 24/7 riot.. Interestingly it used to last four days, a regional holiday in Kolkata. Now it's a full 10 days. Why, because extending the holiday is a vote catcher so every election one party or another promises another day extra.. and local businesses have to pay. In October there are two more festivals to go.. India is a wall to wall party.
A brass band to welcome guests to the show, taking a rest.. thankfully.

Trade show deals, new tactics.
This year we have been invited to people's hotel rooms a lot. Quite a few of our regular suppliers have opted to do the tradeshow from a nearby hotel. The bed becomes a display, the wardrobe a hanging display every surface showing the company wares.. It saves the cost of a fair, the buyers are here and if you get them to the room.. there's no distractions to take away focus. So now we work the tradeshow and then in the evening get a taxi to another hotel room. 
Selections on the bedroom floor.
AW India
For some reason, I don't fully understand... Chatterjee has renamed his trading company..  AW India, some kind of ruse to get an extra stand.
So if you are in the trade show and see this.. it's not really AW.. 
It's just that Mr Chatterjee feels so part of the AW team (and he certainly is) that he named his trading company after us.
Lot's of creativity here in India.. as usually we are doing deals.. but soon we will be in Delhi and meeting with more regular suppliers to find more products you need.
Full update next week.

Meanwhile back in the UK..
As it happens lots of new Indian products are coming online..
And it's getting busy, busy, busy..  not long until Halloween and then Christmas.. 

Namaste from India.. we have to go.. we are meeting a gemstone guy in a hotel room..

Take care.
David

The bank in Paris, an intermediary branch had blocked it.. but obviously fashion shows and long lunches meant the compliance team took their time and many emails and calls and the help from our awesome local manager and eventually they accept that Mr Chatteree makes harmless Tote bags (not WMD) and ticks the box that releases the fund.. Only to have the next bank in the antiquated Swift system block the fund. This bank in New York, too busy and probably preoccupied with some local election, is not getting on with it either.. A few hundred emails later from our bank, the Indian receiving bank, Mr Chatterjee and me.. they finally released the fund. In the taxi at the airport Mr Chatterjee shows me the email detailing the transfer release. But.. the value date on the release form shows 26th Feb 2026 - In 2 Years time! .. Some dyslexic kid in NY has mistyped the date and we are back to square one. All the way from the airport to our hotel Mr Chatterjee is on the phone, persuading, arguing, shouting.. in the honking jarring traffic for over an hour. We roll up at the hotel and he says.. they have accepted it's a mistake and just released the funds. Thanks to all one million Indian gods.. finally. Only six weeks to send a so-called "Swift" payment. Still noisy in India - My theory. Every few minutes in the trade show, an announcement is made by some lady with a loud screeching voice. Music pounds, people shout. Out on the street cars honk constantly and the traffic is crazy.. I have been coming to India for more than 20 years.. is it getting better?. actually no it's not. The rest of Asia has rapidly got cleaner, quieter and more organised. India despite much more efficient airports and new roads.. is getting more noisy than ever. I have a theory. It's in the DNA - they love the chaos, noise and the hecticness. 1.4 billion people of lots of different cultures, classes and religions rub up against each other. In the main everyone gets on with each other, but they need to fight their corner or get crushed.. and they embrace the process , heck it's fun! Cars and trucks have signs saying "Please Honk" traffic rules are not enforced all of life is a vibrant noisy game. The Durga Puja I was telling you about last week is basically a non-stop 24/7 riot.. Interestingly it used to last four days, a regional holiday in Kolkata. Now it's a full 10 days. Why, because extending the holiday is a vote catcher so every election one party or another promises another day extra.. and local businesses have to pay. In October there are two more festivals to go.. India is a wall to wall party. A brass band to welcome guests to the show, taking a rest.. thankfully. Trade show deals, new tactics. This year we have been invited to people's hotel rooms a lot. Quite a few of our regular suppliers have opted to do the tradeshow from a nearby hotel. The bed becomes a display, the wardrobe a hanging display every surface showing the company wares.. It saves the cost of a fair, the buyers are here and if you get them to the room.. there's no distractions to take away focus. So now we work the tradeshow and then in the evening get a taxi to another hotel room. Selections on the bedroom floor. AW India For some reason, I don't fully understand... Chatterjee has renamed his trading company.. AW India, some kind of ruse to get an extra stand. So if you are in the trade show and see this.. it's not really AW.. It's just that Mr Chatterjee feels so part of the AW team (and he certainly is) that he named his trading company after us. Lot's of creativity here in India.. as usually we are doing deals.. but soon we will be in Delhi and meeting with more regular suppliers to find more products you need. Full update next week. Meanwhile back in the UK.. As it happens lots of new Indian products are coming online.. And it's getting busy, busy, busy.. not long until Halloween and then Christmas.. Namaste from India.. we have to go.. we are meeting a gemstone guy in a hotel room.. Take care. David

title: Should I go or stay?
content_html:
Greetings from Slovakia

Yes it's great to be travelling again, this time last week I was just leaving Spain and telling you about how the team there knows how to have a party.. you can read about it here.

This week I have been visiting the team in Slovakia at our AWGifts distribution centre in the town of Trnava.


It has been a little more than two years since I was last here, and things have changed a lot.. not least the size of the team. There were 6 people, now there are 26.
I arrived last Friday at 9.30am Tomas collected me from the airport and we drove to Trnava past vast fields of brilliant yellow sunflowers, open roads and blue sky. Arriving at the office slightly bedraggled from the early morning flight I plunged into meeting all the new people, all looking keen and nervous and smartly dressed. It was slightly emotional to see Erika & Matej, the original team members.. What have you been up to? I asked them as I met the people who now work at AWGifts.

I really like Slovakia, the serious, gentle people, the neat tidy towns, the good food and the culture. I had forgotten how much I like it. 
We went to see several potential new warehouses and met possible new landlords. All super polite, super keen and very open and easy to do business with. 
It seems because of Brexit quite a few developers built distribution warehouses in the area, a little more than needed so there are amazing deals to be done.
You remember whilst in Spain I took the team for dinner on the beach. In Slovakia there is no beach and the managers have families so dinner was tricky. So instead we took the management team out for breakfast at my hotel. Which was great, and we did some serious brainstorming over cappuccinos. Then we outlined our plan to move to a new warehouse in a few months enabling us to keep growing at pace. I gave them a little speech and asked if they were up for the challenge? In Spain there would be whoops and cheers.. here some serious nodding and scratching of heads.. so serious.. 

    Tomas on the left with our management team.. Juraj,  Matej and Erika. 

It has to be said - they might be just a touch serious, but when you get to know them they are all delightful. But not just delightful but under Tomas's leadership - mostly from a distance - this team has worked miracles, growth rates of 200% plus.. opening up new websites and markets like crazy and not least organising a warehouse so well it is a dream. And doing all this in a pandemic. I'm so proud of them. They are a top team at AW!!

Global warming is affecting us.
We expected a container from Indonesia this week, but it seems to be lost in transit delayed by the flooding in Germany. I spoke to Coco in China yesterday and she told me there was a severe weather warning.. tornadoes no less and had been told to stay indoors.
In Slovakia this week it's been damned hot,viewing one of the warehouses with a mask on I almost passed out with the heat. On Wednesday we had to go to Bratislava, the normally languid Danube was rushing and almost bursting its banks. Boats moving upstream could barely fight the current. In Spain forest fires. Now I hear the UK is in a heatwave.

     The Danube From pandemic to weather crisis.

By the time you read this I will be back in Spain, in a few days I'm due to travel to Jakarta, Indonesia where I will quarantine for 7 days before transiting to Bali.
But Indonesia is in covid meltdown, on an epic Indian type scale, it seems almost madness to go. I had a long chat with Ringo (our man in Indonesia) yesterday he assured me that Bali is not so bad, although there is a strict lockdown right now. By the time I get there after quarantine things could change. But which way?
Tomas tried to persuade me to delay, Coco (my wife) thinks I should stay in Spain.
But I so want to see the suppliers in Bali, we have lots of projects in the pipeline.. Also there is a chance that Thailand might open for vaccinated people including from China, so then I could see Coco again.
Should I go or should I stay?

Next week I will update you..

Take care, stay safe.

David

title: The World's Biggest Turtle
content_html:
Greetings from Bali, Indonesia
A million miles away fro Brexit Britain, but very much on all minds right now.
Of course this is one of my favorite places, and I'm here with Tomas our marketing wizard. 
Last week I was telling you about visiting the children's home in India we support for a cup of tea, and how that went.. you can read about it here. 
Since then I have caught the night flight to Kuala Lumpa, met up with Tomas flown to Semerang, Indonesia on the island of Java.
Semerang is a fast developing port city, it is from here that containers of products from the central Java area are loaded on to container ships and sent via Singapore to the rest of the world. 
It is also the entry point of raw materials such as teak and other timber from Kalimantan the vast island to the north, you may better know as Borneo.

Two and a half hours drive from Semerang is a trade secret. There is place that I first heard about five years ago, Ringo our man in Indonesia told me about it, at trade shows in India I have heard the name muttered, and I have long wanted to visit. 
Importers that know about it (much like Yiwu in China a few years ago) like to keep it secret, they don't reveal their sources... but you know at Ancient Wisdom we are open and I'm going of course going to tell you about the city of Jepara.

The City of Jepara 
You probably touch products that came from Jepara everyday, you may sleep on one, sit on one, work on one. If you have any garden furniture than it almost certainly came from here. Jepara is the worlds biggest manufacturer of garden furniture.

The hard woods - all strictly controlled - from Borneo and Java make long lasting quality furniture and the industrious people of Java have developed a remarkable business out of it. 
Japara town centre is all showrooms of every kind of furniture, there is one street that is pretty much like Ubud with handicraft gift products all for export, but head to the outskirts of the town and vast hanger like factories sprawl for miles. We went to visit a few to get a feel for the furniture market. I'm not sure what I expected to see, but we have seen super organised well run factories with hundreds of workers well equipped and in great working conditions beavering away producing every kind of furniture.

Everything from super ornate French style to pared down minimalist Japanese. We visited one factory that can and does produce 30 40ft container loads a week for shipping to B&Q and Walmart.

And the workers are multi ethnic, mostly Javanese Muslim - ladies in hijabs deftly making tables, alongside ethnically chinese and also Christian Javanese. There are Mosques and Churches and Buddhist temples here. And the bosses - well you might find it surprising - but many are ladies, the ladies are organized and big thinking here.


There is one business hotel grandly names the Jepara International Hotel. We went and it looked like it seen better days to say the least. Our driver a big jolly Christian guy from Semerang called Roberto, told us that most buyers prefered to stay by the sea in the newly established tourist zone very nearby. So we went and found what was basically a wedding and conference hotel it was nice and I can tell you that at Muslim weddings here they love Ed Sheeran songs.



Roberto was hilarious, he was delighted and excited to have foreign customers and we invited him to join us meals at which he spent most of the time taking pictures for his facebook page.



Google Jepara and most of the pictures feature a giant house sized turtle. Where is the turtle? we kept asking, but during our few days there whizzing around we never found it. Last day after we finished work we asked Roberto about it.. no problem, turns out it is inside an amusement park built to attract tourists, so before we left of course we had to go to take selfies with the worlds biggest turtle!

Now we are in Bali. 


I'll update you next week.
Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: Just Astonishing / Vitamin C
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

It's exciting and just astonishing things happening this week... details below.

 

Last week I was telling you about the Summer Solstice and how in every corner of the AW world.. UK, Spain, Slovakia, India & Bali.. a celebration or party of one sort or another was happening. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Now it's one week on from the longest day so we are firmly in the summer season.  The Euro football season (England v Slovakia) this weekend.. Haha I'm not a football fan but I might even watch that.

And so many containers arriving in the UK and EU warehouses it dare I say it... almost feels like (yikes) Christmas.. 

I'm planning a 90th Birthday party (not mine).. see below.


I need your opinion.. 

I have been thinking about this for a long time about how to differentiate us from our competitors and (those apparently) copycat businesses. Our long time customers know us well and have been along for the ride with me and the AW team for years.. you know we import direct and manufacture and supply direct (so authentic real wholesalers - not middlemen). You know we go out of our way to deal directly with Artisans and have our own artistic designers in house (so genuinely artisan focused). Our long-time customers also know how hard we work to come up with and keep coming up with Astonishingly Good Products that your customers love make a real difference to your business.

So I was thinking maybe we need a new tagline...

Ancient Wisdom - Authentic, Artisan & Astonishingly Good Products 

Oh well it's work in progress.. lots of reasons we can claim to be authentic even more to be artisan.. but Astonishing.. sounds a bit (Trumpish) arrogant.. even if we do have great products.. speaking of which..

 

Big news is the long awaited launch of our Vitamin C  range of products.

I can't tell you how much work has been put into this, it's been a year in the making.. Testing, refining, trying to make sure we have an Astonishingly Good Product.  Packaging design by our talented Designer Sandra, product creation involving all the AW-Aromatics team. Big input from Tomas and Bryant. And the Aw-Aromatics Artisans working all hours to get stock produced for the launch.. 

You know if you are thinking big and would like to Create your own brand and Astonishing Product.. we are here to help you.. at AW-Aromatics.. our showroom and Creative Zone awaits you.

Why not kick off your dream product by coming to see us. Make an appointment by using the online chat on the  AW-Aromatics website. We are looking forward to working with you..

More big news - containers are arriving fast now.. this week we have some long awaited stock.  Including a much requested range of new Tabletop Water Features.

Also for all you crafty folk who like to make your own jewellery designs we have a range of Pendant Cords. make yourself and ready made. And wholesale Red Cord for those that understand how special that is.

And so much we will be adding shortly.

 

It's the last day of the month! Last trading day for us.. so everyone is crazy busy running around like mad people wrapping up the Month of June..

So July - Holiday season.. and My Big News.. is that Coco and Tomas are both on the way to Spain. Both of them have been working incredibly hard recently. Coco despatching containers from our warehouse in Yiwu almost every other day for the past month or so.. Tomas dealing with a million things in the UK and Slovakia.. They both deserve a well earned rest.

On the way..

Coco (my wife and your agent) from China: she will get a SwissAir flight from Shanghai, change in Zurich and arrive in Malaga on Tuesday night around midnight. Coco just turned 50 so a big party is planned.

Tomas (marketing wizard and main man in Slovakia and all AW) will catch a (much less glamorous) Ryanair flight from Bratislava to Malaga on Tuesday morning. Tomas will shortly celebrate his 40th Birthday.. 

Neither of them look anything like their age.. Just Astonishing no? - maybe it's the Vitamin C products.. 

So that's why I'm planning a big 90th (50+40) party shortly..  haha


Coco & Tomas.

So have a just an astonishing weekend, enjoy the football, enjoy the rays if you can catch a few. Hope your businesses are bright & buzzing.

 

Take care - more news next week.

David

title: We are Sub-Normal in Spain
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

Last week I was in Sheffield getting ready for Brexit day - and yes of course it didn't happen. But Halloween went ahead as normal, or should I say sub-normal.. and last week I was telling you about our costume competition at AW HQ.. you can read about it here.

Whether you are a believer in Brexit or not you have to agree the disruption caused by the dither and delay is bad.. very bad. Every business that imports or exports to Europe (and we do both) is unable to plan effectively for the future in the UK.. the only sensible thing to do is move where possible operations to the safe and stable euro zone. You can't invest in staff you might not need, you can't make major infrastructure investments.. you maybe stock up more, but at the end of the day it's simply not good. Dear brexiter reading this - lets face it when brexit day finally dawns, hard, soft or scrambled.. it's still only the beginning of a transition faze that will consume years and years of further uncertainty.  I have no idea where we are going.. or why we are in a hand-cart :)
So... that's why me Raul (the IT wizard), Rodrigo (the Brazilian) and Tomas (the marketing wizard) are in Spain..

We escaped the biblical downpour in Sheffield - massive rains and flooding all very close to AW - I read this morning that some shoppers found themselves trapped and had to spend last night in a shopping centre.. extreme sub-normal weather conditions seem to be becoming the norm. 
I'm hoping by the time you read this things are getting back to normal in Sheffield.


Here in Spain, it's mostly sunny with the odd shower.. and we got the keys to our new wonderful warehouse. On the same day.. 27 pallets of stock arrived from Sheffield. several containers are on there way from China, Indonesia and India. It's all go and very exciting as we make big plans. 
Lots do.. today we sign a deal with the racking company, in the end we should have a 1000 pallet spaces. The offices are being decorated, the internet should be connected. The alarm company, CCTV, folk-lift trucks, electric, water, insurance.. etc etc.. all need sorting but the most important thing is selecting our new team..  despite stringent criteria we have had over 900 applicants who want to work for AW Spain.. some are very keen. We start interviews on Monday.. 

One person we are not recruiting is a sales person. There are NO sales people (pushy or otherwise) at AW.. that's sub-normal no?

Let me explain: For sure our staff our people are vitally important assets, and our people must first and foremost love gifts.. love lovely things. Because at the end of the day it's about the products. If the products are good (and the prices are correct) you don't need sales people to persuade you to buy.. you do need effective marketing, and great customer service.. for this reason you won't find AW at trade shows - no sales guy is knocking on your door - our customers are smart enough to find us, realise the products/prices are good order directly themselves and they do so in ever greater numbers. 
Our other sub-normal thing is that we don't secretly compete with you (our customers).. no shops, no Amazon / Ebay selling - no online retail stores. Our job is to focus on great products - yours is to do the great retailing. 

There is no other gift wholesale company that can make these claims.. we are sub-normal!

So as we start the process of building a team in Spain.. we are looking for passionate people who can get passionate about gifts.. we need odd and unusual people.. normal we don't need.
I'm so excited.. 
It's only a couple of years ago (regular readers will know) that we started the distribution centre in Slovakia. At the other end of Europe.. the team there are amazing, and it's rewarding to see them grow in their job as the company rapidly expands. We are successfully selling to the Slovakian, Czech, Austrian markets and just launched into the Hungarian market.. (Check our English site AWGifts.eu supplying world-wide). 
Time to do something like this here.

The Spain website: AWGifts.es  has been running from the UK warehouse.. and growing super fast under the careful attention of Antonio Jesus and Rodrigo - and (brexit permitting will continue). But now we need a new website based in Spain.. "won't that be confusing?" you (rather astutely) ask.. and you would be correct.. so what is the solution?

We have a Sub-Normal - extraordinary idea.. haha I'll tell you all about it next week.
Meanwhile meet the winner of the Halloween costume competition..

content_text: Greetings from Spain. Last week I was in Sheffield getting ready for Brexit day - and yes of course it didn't happen. But Halloween went ahead as normal, or should I say sub-normal.. and last week I was telling you about our costume competition at AW HQ.. you can read about it here. Whether you are a believer in Brexit or not you have to agree the disruption caused by the dither and delay is bad.. very bad. Every business that imports or exports to Europe (and we do both) is unable to plan effectively for the future in the UK.. the only sensible thing to do is move where possible operations to the safe and stable euro zone. You can't invest in staff you might not need, you can't make major infrastructure investments.. you maybe stock up more, but at the end of the day it's simply not good. Dear brexiter reading this - lets face it when brexit day finally dawns, hard, soft or scrambled.. it's still only the beginning of a transition faze that will consume years and years of further uncertainty. I have no idea where we are going.. or why we are in a hand-cart :) So... that's why me Raul (the IT wizard), Rodrigo (the Brazilian) and Tomas (the marketing wizard) are in Spain.. We escaped the biblical downpour in Sheffield - massive rains and flooding all very close to AW - I read this morning that some shoppers found themselves trapped and had to spend last night in a shopping centre.. extreme sub-normal weather conditions seem to be becoming the norm. I'm hoping by the time you read this things are getting back to normal in Sheffield. Here in Spain, it's mostly sunny with the odd shower.. and we got the keys to our new wonderful warehouse. On the same day.. 27 pallets of stock arrived from Sheffield. several containers are on there way from China, Indonesia and India. It's all go and very exciting as we make big plans. Lots do.. today we sign a deal with the racking company, in the end we should have a 1000 pallet spaces. The offices are being decorated, the internet should be connected. The alarm company, CCTV, folk-lift trucks, electric, water, insurance.. etc etc.. all need sorting but the most important thing is selecting our new team.. despite stringent criteria we have had over 900 applicants who want to work for AW Spain.. some are very keen. We start interviews on Monday.. One person we are not recruiting is a sales person. There are NO sales people (pushy or otherwise) at AW.. that's sub-normal no? Let me explain: For sure our staff our people are vitally important assets, and our people must first and foremost love gifts.. love lovely things. Because at the end of the day it's about the products . If the products are good (and the prices are correct) you don't need sales people to persuade you to buy.. you do need effective marketing, and great customer service.. for this reason you won't find AW at trade shows - no sales guy is knocking on your door - our customers are smart enough to find us, realise the products/prices are good order directly themselves and they do so in ever greater numbers. Our other sub-normal thing is that we don't secretly compete with you (our customers).. no shops, no Amazon / Ebay selling - no online retail stores. Our job is to focus on great products - yours is to do the great retailing. There is no other gift wholesale company that can make these claims.. we are sub-normal! So as we start the process of building a team in Spain.. we are looking for passionate people who can get passionate about gifts.. we need odd and unusual people.. normal we don't need. I'm so excited.. It's only a couple of years ago (regular readers will know) that we started the distribution centre in Slovakia. At the other end of Europe.. the team there are amazing, and it's rewarding to see them grow in their job as the company rapidly expands. We are successfully selling to the Slovakian, Czech, Austrian markets and just launched into the Hungarian market.. (Check our English site AWGifts.eu supplying world-wide). Time to do something like this here. Urszula - and I'm sure she doesn't mind being described as sub-normal :) wins the competition by a landslide vote (yet again). Urszula is head of customer services in the UK.. and you would have to go a long way to find a person more passionate about gifts.. (and erm dressing up!) She thanks you for voting for her! More news next week. Take special care. David

title: To the Pink City
content_html:
Greetings from Goa, India

So yes in Goa.. arrived here with Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) after a few days in the Pink City, known as Jaipur. Last week I was in Delhi and telling you why there was so much wet paint.. If you missed it you can catch up here.
From Delhi we took an evening flight from Delhi to Jaipur.. the flight time was short and the plane was small and cramp with propellers..all very old school.. we arrived at Jaipur airport which was surprisingly nice and very organised. Then a short taxi to the Marriott hotel. A huge and it turned out extremely busy hotel. There was a conference of brain surgeons going on.. so some of smartest people in India were there. 


Boarding the evening plane to the pink city.

I have been to Jaipur before, many years ago. In those days its was mostly a tourist hub, famous for the ancient buildings and pink city. Now it has developed into a 3.5 million people busy city with lots of industry of all types. Tonk Road dissects the city and is where many textile factories have showrooms.. there are so many handicraft producers here but sadly we actually have only two suppliers so and it was about time to make a visit.
If you have seen the movie: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel, then you will have an idea about the place, if you have been as a tourist then probably didn't see the new developed part of Jaipur and that's where our suppliers are. A totally different vibe to Delhi, more laid back and the streets are relatively clean and organised. It just feels a bit more cared for to me and the locals seem genuinely helpful and friendly.  

The leather books have become a very popular item.. and we expanded the range quite a bit over the last couple of years.. I wanted to get our range to the next level and that is one aim of our trip.
The factory in sleepy backstreet was surprisingly peaceful place with about thirty staff beavering away doing the various processes that go into making those journals. It's a family business and the boss and his brother gave us a guided tour explaining how it all works.. very nice thoughtful people. Good to work with.  I made video..


I feel that there is so much more to discover in Jaipur and it's probably as good a creative hub as Delhi so we are definitely coming back.
But we have a tight schedule, so after only four days (some new contacts made) it was time to catch the early morning flight down to Goa.. actually we landed at the brand new airport in North Goa. Impressive and very jolly. Our regular taxi guy Rosario picked us up and took us down south to where we have a bit of a base. AW has an apartment there that is currently under restoration.. so need to check on it.. plus have some personal stuff to attend to.
It's off season, actually the monsoon season in Goa, so nothing is open and its very quiet. But surprisingly (or maybe not) the weather is quite nice with plenty of sunshine. 

Back in the UK - it's all happening all at once...
There is so much new stuff arriving, including Enchantment Lights.. strings of raw crystals that light up.. I'm so excited to see. Going to be a brilliant xmas and beyond gift.
Lots of incense products rolling in.. so much.

Anyway I hope you have a wonderful weekend.
Take care and Namaste.

David

title: 463 Reasons
content_html:
Greetings Bangalore, India


This is our final day of the grand Nepal / India tour.. it's been hard work, an emotional roller coaster, epic and I hope successful.  
How to measure success on a sourcing trip? Well, we have sourced and ordered 463 new products, added six new approved suppliers, ordered about 20 containers of goods, and probably (with your support) created work for several thousand Indian artisans. The true measure of success will be how happy we can make you and your customers, if your customers love any of those 463 products then you can grow your business, reorder again and again and everyone benefits.. the circle of life continues. Last week I was telling you about the good guys we do business with in India. If you missed it you can catch up here.

It's been an emotional month, not least because it's my first trip since before covid, and meeting with the families that run the businesses many of which were impacted by covid, some lost members. India was ravaged by covid more than anywhere and a few old friends are lost to us.. but life goes on and hope remains. We spent a few days in South Goa staying with good friends Alex and Maria and their kids: Anthea and Mac. It's like a second home and a second family, and they hosted me and Tomas and Bryant. Mr Chatterjee (our India agent) was there - and as we took the short flight to Bangalore he flew back to Kolkata.. we said an emotional farewell in the departure hall at the airport.

Bangalore is many things, to us it is the incense capital of India. But it is famous as an IT hub, home to many international businesses and a fast growing city. It's a beautiful tropical city - I love the ancient leafy trees that line the streets, the grand old buildings, the friendly chatty people. Even though the traffic is horrendous it feels calm and homely. Bangalore leafy streets.



We checked into the Raj West End, a heritage hotel with a long history. In Panipat on our first days in India we stayed in the world's worst hotel.. (if you missed that newsletter it's here), now we are at the other extreme. 

I always think India is a land of extremes - rich and poor, dodgy and delightful people, beautiful and squalid places, humble and arrogant, you find it all here. One thing that India has always done well since the days of the British Empire is run five star hotels. We arrived to great excitement - the RCB cricket team are staying here and the hotel is hoisting all sorts of events around the team. I know next to nothing about Indian cricket, but some of the faces are familiar to me from the adverts they appear in. Some guys are English, David Willy and Reece Topley are on nodding terms with us and on the team. Tomas and Bryant are googling the guys we rubbing shoulders with at the breakfast buffet.. They have Instagram followers in the millions and all are multi millionaires, but to a man are polite and gentle.

I'm not sure why or how.. but we got upgraded all three of us from the standard room to luxury suite rooms and even though the hotel is stuffed full of celebrities and movers and shakers, the staff are taking exceptional care of us. It seems to me that the management style is to totally trust the staff and empower them to do whatever they can to make the guests stay as good as possible. All the people I talked to had worked at the hotel for ten years or more. Two guys in the breakfast area had worked for 32 and 36 years.. and served Prince (King) Charles amongst other VIPs in the past.. Today they showed no more special attention or favour to the cricket team than they did to us.. 

As well as enjoying the old-world delights of our hotel we have spent two days with to new incense suppliers, visiting the factories and working on new exciting and pretty unique ranges. 
Tomas even tried his hand at rolling hand made incense sticks. The incense ladies can hand roll ten thousand sticks a day, Tomas managed one stick in ten minutes.. 


Meanwhile in the UK as Easter approaches we just completed our showroom open days, they tell me some customers made epic journeys to visit us - thank you to everyone who came and thanks for the feedback and ideas you brought with you.  The new Bath bombs with gemstone chip bracelets are proving a huge success selling faster than we can make.. and compliment the gemstone bath bombs perfectly.
Other good news the fast selling Spell Candles back in stock.. grab them while you can . 

Now our work in India is almost done - 463 new exciting products on the way -  at least for a few months. Bryant will return to the UK on a midnight flight shortly, and Tomas and I will fly back to Bali tomorrow.

Something exciting is happening in Bali.. full report next week.

Take care. And of course, thank you for your support.
Wishing you a wonderful weekend.

David

title: Midsummer Madness
content_html:
Greetings from Old Town Rhodes, Greece.

Last week I was telling you about the importance of Knowing Your Wholesaler (KYW) and was in the UK at AW HQ..
You can read about it here.
Since then a lot has happened! I'm supposed to be on holiday.. 

It's a long time since I last went to a Slovakian wedding..  my wife (that's Coco - also our China agent) flew from the UK to Slovakia.
In the town of Trnava (where AW has it's main EU distribution warehouse) a wedding was taking place between Lenka & Paul. 
Paul from Sheffield and Lenka from Trnava. At the wedding were a goodly number of AW people, the links between AW and Trnava go back a long way. Tomas (now our marketing director)  original ventured to Sheffield and over the years family and friends followed him, many working with AW.. The wedding was an eclectic mix of Yorkshire folk and Slovakian folk with some extra more international guests tossed in for seasoning. There was traditional folk dancing with an axe ceremony involving the bride and groom, when the words of the song were translated I was quite shocked..politically incorrect doesn't come close.. but this is real culture.. Then the plate smashing, the bride is given a dustpan and the groom a brush to sweep up the pieces. The friends of the couple make the job as hard as possible to much merriment. What is the symbolism? I asked. It's like your going to have problems, you are going to have to work together to fix them, and sometimes your friends are not going to help...  don't you just love wedding traditions. 
Anyway, I'm sure you will wish Lenka (from customer service at AW UK) and Paul all the best - I was a lovely lovely day.



Tomas is also supposed to be on holiday, so we drove together with a group of friends that had been at the wedding to the City of Budapest in Hungary. Three days in Budapest, I won't bore you with holiday stuff, but what a grand city - buildings to rival Rome, beautiful parks and gardens and the majestic Danube. If you have never been go, it's a great city break. From here, (Coco and I) took a Wizz air flight down to the Greek island of Rhodes.. I'm writing this before heading out to explore the gift shops of Rhodes.. haha.. actually we might check out the sites and culture also.  Seriously though, I also always like to check how many AW customers there are in a place.. (12 in Budapest) - here there are 10, maybe we'll just call by and say hello.  

It's the Longest Day! 21st of June.. The Midsummer solstice is on the 24th - A very Ancient Wisdom kind of a day, so watch out for our Mid-summer madness deals below.
I'm a bit confused, it's the start of summer, and also mid-summer, depending which website you look at.. anyway greetings and blessings to hippies and druids everywhere. 
All around the world, the midsummer solstice is celebrated much like the Slovakian plate smashing and axe ceremony - in mysterious ways.  We will also celebrate with some AW Solstice Special Deals :)

Have a wonderful time, but now I'm supposed to be on holiday :)
In the last 7 days since the last newsletter - we have been in 4 countries. UK, Slovakia, Hungary and Greece. Time to chill.. 

More news next week..

Take care

David
