title: Fire at AW
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Last week I was telling you about Holy Smoke in Spain.. otherwise known as Pallo Santo, you can read about it here.
This week is a memorial of sorts at AW as we remember a different kind of smoke.
Even now what happened exactly a year ago seems unreal, seems like a supernatural event. A million to one chance happening, and yet it happened.

A warm July day almost a year ago someone at AW cleaned up a minor oil splash, the oil soaked rag as per health and safety was carefully binned. The bin must be (as per H&S) stored outside of the building. The bin must be lockable to avoid some smoker tossing in a fag end.. As per H&S guidance.

Six hours later a little before midnight, in that hot sealed pressure cooker bin a self combustion occurred. It probably should have smoldered and gone out for lack of oxygen, but a small hole in the plastic melted open, and a hot westerly wind that night was just enough to rouse the flame.

Due to H&S regulations IBC's of oils must be kept outside. Now a burning bin might have just burned out, but the IBC nearby began to melt from the heat. The oil escaped and ran across the carpark and under a door that contained the essential oil room, and of course it caught fire as it went.

Something (probably the gas for the underfloor heating) caught fire and exploded blowing off the roller shutter doors. The wind blew the flames west through the building. First though the factory, then the main warehouse then the office block.

I was in a different time zone. Early in the morning in Indonesia, my mobile is buzzing. I will never forget Tomas's tear stained face framed by a massive blaze. It's over, it's over.. Was all he could say.
Within two and a half hours despite a rapid response and valiant effort from the fire brigade the place was burned to the ground. It was the biggest fire that Sheffield had seen for years.

The whole drama from the bin combusting to the fire engines arriving to the total destruction was captured on CCTV by a high level camera in the carpark.

 
from this to this...


in 2 hours..


That day was a monumental shock not only to me but everyone at AW, and many of our customers and suppliers who had been with us for years.

People ask me how I felt at that moment? 
The answer is part of me could have just given up, I told myself I'm too old to deal with this. The thought went through my brain, that the company could be liquidated, insurance claimed, everyone paid off.. retire, game over the easy way out.
My brain did the cold hard calculations, but my heart held the casting vote.. and when I thought about the people that depend on AW, the 25 years of hard work building it up. When I started to receive thousands of messages of support from customers, from you maybe.. then there was no alternative..

The Plan.
There was no way we could give up.. I got myself on the only plane out of Bali in a month.. and made it back to the UK within the week.
So Tomas, Katka and I made a plan. We put it to the team. This job was not going to be easy, but with enough support, energy and teamwork I believed we could recover.  
But more than that, to borrow a phrase.. I told the team.. we had to build back better.. and to think 3X up. 

Forged in the Fire..
As we set to work, there were some who couldn't hack it and left us, but most stayed, and rolled up their sleeves and got on with building back better (to borrow a phrase). I have to say there are some people at AW  who stepped up to the plate and exceeded all expectations. And remember not only the fire, but the pandemic and bloody Brexit we have had to deal with.. 
My personal thanks to those AW Hero's without whom AW wouldn't be here today. Many people at AW grew in character and abilities. 
Of course this has been a trial for you also, the pandemic has tested the whole world, so there is a sense that we all came through this. 

Thank you!
We had tremendous support from our suppliers, both with practical help and moral support. Even competitors offered help. But without question, without doubt, without the generous support of you; our amazing customers we would not have made it.
And so..  I have to say on behalf of everyone at AW, on behalf of all artisans in Bali, India and China, on behalf of our agents, Ringo, Coco & Chatterjee, I have to say a big heartfelt THANK YOU!!
And rest assured - everyone from our Jacob in the warehouse to the ladies who carve Hati-Hati Angels in Bali to the machinists stitching Indian cotton bags.. all of us (myself included) are humbled, thankful and grateful for your support.

One year on...
Our mission - To Bring You The Best in Giftware - is now forged in the fire.. to serve you better and stronger.
Keith, our landlord has got on with rebuilding the warehouse.. and we may move our aromatics factory back into that space.
As regular readers will know.. last October we moved the warehouse to Affinity Park.. a self contained 100k sq ft distribution centre. 
Our central hub office is now coming together, soon we will move from a temporary office to the new work space..


    Affinity

   Office coming together...

A New Look.
And to complete the reinvention of AW.. Tomas has been working on a new AW logo, a new image.
We actually brought in a famous logo designer, and told her our life story, our mission, our heritage, our dreams.. give me a month to work on it..
A steady flow of ideas and designs and iterations is being gradually formed into a new look AW..

Next week all will be revealed.

Until then, once again THANK YOU for supporting and helping make AW what it is..

Hope you have an amazing weekend.

David
content_text: Greetings from Spain Last week I was telling you about Holy Smoke in Spain.. otherwise known as Pallo Santo, you can read about it here . This week is a memorial of sorts at AW as we remember a different kind of smoke. Even now what happened exactly a year ago seems unreal, seems like a supernatural event. A million to one chance happening, and yet it happened. A warm July day almost a year ago someone at AW cleaned up a minor oil splash, the oil soaked rag as per health and safety was carefully binned. The bin must be (as per H&S) stored outside of the building. The bin must be lockable to avoid some smoker tossing in a fag end.. As per H&S guidance. Six hours later a little before midnight, in that hot sealed pressure cooker bin a self combustion occurred. It probably should have smoldered and gone out for lack of oxygen, but a small hole in the plastic melted open, and a hot westerly wind that night was just enough to rouse the flame. Due to H&S regulations IBC's of oils must be kept outside. Now a burning bin might have just burned out, but the IBC nearby began to melt from the heat. The oil escaped and ran across the carpark and under a door that contained the essential oil room, and of course it caught fire as it went. Something (probably the gas for the underfloor heating) caught fire and exploded blowing off the roller shutter doors. The wind blew the flames west through the building. First though the factory, then the main warehouse then the office block. I was in a different time zone. Early in the morning in Indonesia, my mobile is buzzing. I will never forget Tomas's tear stained face framed by a massive blaze. It's over, it's over.. Was all he could say. Within two and a half hours despite a rapid response and valiant effort from the fire brigade the place was burned to the ground. It was the biggest fire that Sheffield had seen for years. The whole drama from the bin combusting to the fire engines arriving to the total destruction was captured on CCTV by a high level camera in the carpark. from this to this... in 2 hours.. That day was a monumental shock not only to me but everyone at AW, and many of our customers and suppliers who had been with us for years. People ask me how I felt at that moment? The answer is part of me could have just given up, I told myself I'm too old to deal with this. The thought went through my brain, that the company could be liquidated, insurance claimed, everyone paid off.. retire, game over the easy way out. My brain did the cold hard calculations, but my heart held the casting vote.. and when I thought about the people that depend on AW, the 25 years of hard work building it up. When I started to receive thousands of messages of support from customers, from you maybe.. then there was no alternative.. The Plan. There was no way we could give up.. I got myself on the only plane out of Bali in a month.. and made it back to the UK within the week. So Tomas, Katka and I made a plan. We put it to the team. This job was not going to be easy, but with enough support, energy and teamwork I believed we could recover. But more than that, to borrow a phrase.. I told the team.. we had to build back better.. and to think 3X up. Forged in the Fire.. As we set to work, there were some who couldn't hack it and left us, but most stayed, and rolled up their sleeves and got on with building back better (to borrow a phrase). I have to say there are some people at AW who stepped up to the plate and exceeded all expectations. And remember not only the fire, but the pandemic and bloody Brexit we have had to deal with.. My personal thanks to those AW Hero's without whom AW wouldn't be here today. Many people at AW grew in character and abilities. Of course this has been a trial for you also, the pandemic has tested the whole world, so there is a sense that we all came through this. Thank you! We had tremendous support from our suppliers, both with practical help and moral support. Even competitors offered help. But without question, without doubt, without the generous support of you; our amazing customers we would not have made it. And so.. I have to say on behalf of everyone at AW, on behalf of all artisans in Bali, India and China, on behalf of our agents, Ringo, Coco & Chatterjee, I have to say a big heartfelt THANK YOU!! And rest assured - everyone from our Jacob in the warehouse to the ladies who carve Hati-Hati Angels in Bali to the machinists stitching Indian cotton bags.. all of us (myself included) are humbled, thankful and grateful for your support. One year on... Our mission - To Bring You The Best in Giftware - is now forged in the fire.. to serve you better and stronger. Keith, our landlord has got on with rebuilding the warehouse.. and we may move our aromatics factory back into that space. As regular readers will know.. last October we moved the warehouse to Affinity Park.. a self contained 100k sq ft distribution centre. Our central hub office is now coming together, soon we will move from a temporary office to the new work space.. Affinity Office coming together... A New Look. And to complete the reinvention of AW.. Tomas has been working on a new AW logo, a new image. We actually brought in a famous logo designer, and told her our life story, our mission, our heritage, our dreams.. give me a month to work on it.. A steady flow of ideas and designs and iterations is being gradually formed into a new look AW.. Next week all will be revealed. Until then, once again THANK YOU for supporting and helping make AW what it is.. Hope you have an amazing weekend. David

title: In This Together... 🙏
content_html:
Greetings from Affinity Park - The UK HQ of AW

 

Last week I was telling you about Reincarnation and other Special offers.  I updated you about Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) and the terrible situation there and they are coping. You can read it here.

Many of you kindly sent messages of encouragement, which I passed on to Mr Chatterjee, he called me to say how moved he and his family were by your messages.. He asked me to pass on this message to you.

 

Hi David

I am really very honoured  for all of your concern about us. As a my family friend you always care for us. I have conveyed  to my family & the children home about your newsletter, and all your customers' messages. All of them are really very happy to know this because all of you worried for us. In India maximum states are either semi or full lockdown. Our State local train closed and the market only open 7 to 10 am & 5 to 7 pm only for essential commodities.  But I think complete lockdown will start soon for breaking the chain of covid. ..

 

My family and children request me to convey their thanks & regards to you and all others.

Best Regards

Chatterjee

 

Since then he has messaged me that things are getting worse, many deaths in his village, there are no beds available in the town's hospitals and severe oxygen crisis. However he will do his best to prepare product samples. I told him not to worry about this, just to stay safe.

 

One thing about Sheffield I really like is the street art. There are a few prolific artists, some authorised and some not, but always edgy or fantastic. I noticed driving to work a new poetry mural on the side of the road..

As I sat in the traffic it caught my eye and reading it - I thought about Mr Chatterjee in India.


     

We are all waves in the same sea, leaves of the same tree, flowers of the same garden.


Which seemed to me to expose the vaccine nationalism argument as very sad and short sighted. No-one is safe until we are all safe. The whole world needs to be vaccinated before we can put this behind us and move on. Sure countries should look after their vulnerable folks first, but then asap help the poor of the world. Vaccine patents need to be scrapped (at least in the short term) and knowhow made open source. It's crazy that big pharma guard secrets to boost profits at the cost of lives.

We are all waves in the same sea..

 

The mural was inspired by a poem written on the side of a package sent to the Sant’Anna School, a university in Pisa, Italy, during the coronavirus pandemic. The package contained protective equipment that was donated by former Chinese students of the University as an expression of gratitude and friendship to the community who had welcomed them so warmly. Sent on the package in Italian, the poem was written by the ancient Roman philosopher Seneca and translates to: ‘We are waves of the same sea, leaves of the same tree, flowers of the same garden.’  And I should absolutely give credit to local artist Will Rea - his work appears all over Sheffield and certainly brightens our lives.

 

Creative people are the lifeblood of any community, company or country.. 

At AW we are fortunate to have lots of creative talent, channelling your ideas and suggestions into real products and projects.

Last week I was also telling you about our beefed up Customer Service team.. 

This week we branched out and added an (hopefully very creative) member to our marketing team.

We are all leaves on the same tree..  

 

Meet Ash.. here with Rodrigo.



As you know at AW we don't have sales people or do the tradeshows (even before covid) - we believe the products should be fairly priced and pretty much sell themselves. So no pushy (or otherwise) sales people.

This business model (we were the first to try this I believe) has worked well, in that AW has grown organically every year for over 20 years. But we still need to communicate with our lovely customers, and we do that via marketing and the websites. 

At AW the plan is rather than have a nationwide team of sales reps, cars, expenses, commissions and egos - a small enthusiastic marketing team tasked with imparting ideas, sales tips and information - is a better use of resources and your time. 

Thus Ash will work with Rodrigo to communicate more.. The idea is to give you more useful information that will help you to sell more and more easily identify products that will delight your customers. Plus hopefully more chance to give us the feedback to further shape the future products.. he is going to revamp and invigorate our social media presence. 

 

Don't worry..  this doesn't mean we are going to sell to the general public (ie your customers) - as you know we are strictly B2B at AW. We will never sell on amazon, run our own retail shops online or in the high street. Your job is the retailing, ours is the sourcing and wholesale. But Ash is going to make AW Instagram, YouTube and Facebook come alive with useful game changing info and ideas to help you expand your business and delight your customers.

 

Supply lines are still rather rusty, but stock still manages to arrive - this week Soap Flowers and some Indian shipments. Check out the back in stock lines and special deals we have for you below. 

 

So as lockdown eases and soon restaurants and pubs open up, it's time to take heart. Things are getting better, holidays can happen, the sun will shine again. 

Just remember others are not so lucky, and as we once again enjoy nature and live after lockdown.. that we are all flowers in the same garden..

 

Take care

 

David

title: Coco is so busy in China!
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China

So busy in Yiwu, lots to do and this being China things happen at pace it's quite invigorating..
Coco my wife (and your China agent) makes it all happen. I'll describe a typical day below.
Last week I was telling you about catching up with some of our old suppliers and always greeting each other with the Chinese greeting.. "Long Time No See!" .. if you missed it you can catch up here..
I also mentioned our trip down the G60 (China's Route 66) to Coco's home town where we caught up with the rest of her family and made a visit to the ancestral village.

Coco's family are the nicest people, she has a brother (James Dean good looking) who runs the village supermarket and farmers supply store. His wife (beautiful and fashionably dressed) is a close friend of Coco and came with Coco's sister (also beautiful and super jolly) to take me out for a welcome meal.. over the next few days we had to meet and eat with all the extended family at various restaurants always serving the local food.. which I really like.. it's nothing like what you would find in Chinese restaurants in Europe. We eat lamb and pork chops dusted with spices you have never tasted before, all sorts of vegetable dishes and local river fish.. always served for sharing on a revolving table top with cartons of local beer stacked on the floor for easy access. Peanuts are a local crop and a delicacy is peanut veg dish.. de-shelled peanuts but still attached to the root stems, steamed and served as a vegetable.. the stems taste of peanuts.. Who knew!





There are a lot of relatives.. this area has a Christian culture, and maybe because of this in the bad old days the local villagers colluded to evade the one child policies. Coco tells me fascinating tales of how the rules were got around, pregnant women hidden away, and children "allocated" to different families in "official" documents.. Hence these days we are lucky to have big family meals.

At family meals of this kind everyone has to give special attention and respect to everyone else.. they way you do this is by standing up with a full glass of beer and toasting your respected person and both parties have to down the full glass. Fortunately the beer is not too strong, but if the rice wine appears.. then believe me it's time to run away..

After dinner they like to play a drinking game - a bit like Paper, Rock, Scissors.. but with numbers chanted loudly in the local language with corresponding hand-signs that have to add up to something.. it's complicated and involves considerable mental arithmetic - the loser has to down the drink. Late afternoon on May day in the local restaurant every table was playing the game - total raucous fun.
Coco posted a video from one meal on her social media.. I'm the only foreigner in town (at least I didn't see anyone else), and this propelled the post to an amazing 70,000 views (at the last check) - with thousands of comments. Coco has switched it off after a small amount of what you might call "racist comments" came.

After three days of feasting it's time to head back to Yiwu, we decide to go early (mid-holiday) to avoid the traffic.. It works and we get back to Yiwu in four and a half hours.

Coco's life in China.
Coco, like the rest of her family is immensely hard working and naturally entrepreneurial. She learned how be an export agent from a good friend and took over from a dodgy agent some six years ago, and we haven't looked back since.
Now we do straight honest business, no kickbacks or commissions, whenever we start with a new supplier Coco will explain that she is not expecting and doesn't want commission and they should just give us the best prices and quality.. this is the way to build trade over the long term. The smiles from suppliers reflects better relationships and much more scope for producing bespoke products.



Coco spends all her day organising things, deliveries, the next container date, chasing orders etc. A lot of time is spent on compliance papers these days, customs officers in UK and EU like to make importing anything as difficult as possible so Coco spends a lot of time getting things tested and checking that products are to proven standards and are what they claim to be. Her phone is literally red hot, messages from and to suppliers at all hours of the day.
We have a warehouse for loading our own containers (same system as in Indonesia) and Coco checks every delivery, and container loading personally.. it's hard and detailed work.. and (don't tell her) but I'm immensely proud of her.
On top of this job, part of the warehouse is turned over to a small candle factory.. we pioneered Soywax candle making in China.. no-one was making candles with Soywax and they laughed at us, because in those days the mentality was to make candles as cheap as possible, why would you use wax at double the price? Now of course as we walk around Yiwu market every candle showroom has a Soywax section.
We are working on a new range of rather exciting candles.. totally different and quite special.. watch this space.

Coco is just busy by nature.. never stops. When she is not organising exports or the candle factory she has her grandchildren to entertain and an apartment to look after. And any free time is taken up with Yoga (which she is super advanced at) and her DouYin (TikTok) channel.

Anyway that's my update for this week.
More news next Friday.. have a great long weekend (if you are in the UK) The King apparently is going to be crowned the king.. he is already but any excuse for an extra bank holiday.. Enjoy!!
And a good excuse for some King Sized Flash Deals to give you a Right Royal Bonus.
.. and wishing you much peace, love and laughter. Take care.


David

title: Lots of news
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Hope you are well and business is not running out of gas or sparkle.. like parts of the UK..
The shortages are a worry but these things will pass.
Last week I was telling you about the fearsome fires in south Spain and how the fire planes were regularly buzzing my house. You can read about it here.
But it started raining and things changed - panic over. But not before one brave firefighter sadly lost his life.

When a container arrives in the country they have a system.. it's put into a green, amber or red channel. Green means the customs guys are relaxed and the container can sail through the port and wing it's way to our warehouse. Amber channel means they have some questions or checks to make, so there may be some delays until they are sure you're not doing anything dodgy. And Red.. well if you get in the red channel expect big trouble, inspections, multiple checks, exrays.. you name if the container is red listed big delays and huge expense.. all of which pushes prices up in the end for consumers.. but there are elements of bureaucracy that just love to cause trouble for importers.
This week on Tuesday our container from China to Spain was red listed..  we waited for the list of queries and demands.. our shipping agent every hour asking what the problem was.. nothing. Then yesterday afternoon for no apparent rhyme or reason.. the container was moved from Red to Green and could we take delivery at 7am.. 
Importing these days in Europe is stressful.. but the team all agreed to get up early..
As I write they just finished unloading.. and sent me a picture..


This is the AW-Artisan warehouse team (MFT)

Over the years in the UK we must have imported hundreds of containers, and maybe one in twenty spends a day or hours in the Amber lane.. never stressful but these days everything is.. hopefully this will pass.

In Slovakia it's not as bad as Spain, but every container they will make checks.. recently we received a €4000 fine for under invoicing.. This is a dodgy trick where an importer undervalues a product in the invoice so the duty payable is less. 
Of course we don't do this. At AW we have always played it straight, and proud of our ethics and standards.. but even when we gave them copies of invoices and the money trail they just said we don't accept you bought the product so cheap - pay the fine.
In a way it's a backhanded compliment.. we managed to source products at a price they don't believe.
What is it?


The Power Bracelets. Made from gemstone beads. In the UK all are out of stock right now.. but some are coming soon.
The thing is - of course Rose Quartz etc are quite high value, but the beads are made from waste and off-cuts or larger stones.. in the China domestic market they like big fat beads 10mm.. in Europe we like 6mm or even smaller..
In the back streets of Yiwu is a whole area of gemstone traders. Stones come from all over the world and are carved and made into all sorts of exotic items..
I love this area, the stores trade with each other and you see Africans and East Asians and Tibetans, it's an amazing place. We got to know many of the traders very well, some are good friends.


This is a typical store - that machine outside the door is tumbling beads. The rocks are too small to do anything else with.


Here is Coco checking stock in a Turquoise specialist.
They are all small family businesses - who love what they do.. the type of people we like to trade with.

Anyway we are fighting the fine.. not for the money but for the principle, we don't and never will do dodgy things. The lawyer will cost more than the fine, but  this is getting annoying. Our lawyer is sure we will win the case as we are innocent, but it's not clear we will be able to recover costs.. But I really feel strongly about this.. just because we found a way to bring you great gifts at great prices we are being attacked..I'm not even sure what they want us to do? Next time we import, do we increase the invoiced value to make them happy? Where would that money go...(to an off-shore bank account) that would be seriously dodgy. Are we expected to pay a fine on every import? I'll update you on what happens. 

In other news from Slovakia - this week we signed the "Head of Terms" agreement to move to a new larger warehouse early next year - if all goes according to plan.
Our current warehouse is bursting at the seams, and growth is still running high.. so we have no choice but to expand.. 


Not the whole building, just the first five sections (I think).

Last week I was telling you about an amazing new product from the Aromatics team,,
And I am delighted to announce the Official Launch is TODAY!!
Do-Nut Bath Bombs.. 
See below..

Also there is a load of new products all (finally) reaching the finishing line..
Amongst them.. Wild Hare solid shampoo and conditioner.. a very special product years in development.. watch this space..

Take care.. be kind to someone..
Have a great weekend and more updates from the world of AW next week.

David

And Red.. well if you get in the red channel expect big trouble, inspections, multiple checks, exrays.. you name if the container is red listed big delays and huge expense.. all of which pushes prices up in the end for consumers.. but there are elements of bureaucracy that just love to cause trouble for importers. This week on Tuesday our container from China to Spain was red listed.. we waited for the list of queries and demands.. our shipping agent every hour asking what the problem was.. nothing. Then yesterday afternoon for no apparent rhyme or reason.. the container was moved from Red to Green and could we take delivery at 7am.. Importing these days in Europe is stressful.. but the team all agreed to get up early.. As I write they just finished unloading.. and sent me a picture.. This is the AW-Artisan warehouse team (MFT) Over the years in the UK we must have imported hundreds of containers, and maybe one in twenty spends a day or hours in the Amber lane.. never stressful but these days everything is.. hopefully this will pass. In Slovakia it's not as bad as Spain, but every container they will make checks.. recently we received a €4000 fine for under invoicing.. This is a dodgy trick where an importer undervalues a product in the invoice so the duty payable is less. Of course we don't do this. At AW we have always played it straight, and proud of our ethics and standards.. but even when we gave them copies of invoices and the money trail they just said we don't accept you bought the product so cheap - pay the fine. In a way it's a backhanded compliment.. we managed to source products at a price they don't believe. What is it? The Power Bracelet s. Made from gemstone beads. In the UK all are out of stock right now.. but some are coming soon. The thing is - of course Rose Quartz etc are quite high value, but the beads are made from waste and off-cuts or larger stones.. in the China domestic market they like big fat beads 10mm.. in Europe we like 6mm or even smaller.. In the back streets of Yiwu is a whole area of gemstone traders. Stones come from all over the world and are carved and made into all sorts of exotic items.. I love this area, the stores trade with each other and you see Africans and East Asians and Tibetans, it's an amazing place. We got to know many of the traders very well, some are good friends. This is a typical store - that machine outside the door is tumbling beads. The rocks are too small to do anything else with. Here is Coco checking stock in a Turquoise specialist. They are all small family businesses - who love what they do.. the type of people we like to trade with. Anyway we are fighting the fine.. not for the money but for the principle, we don't and never will do dodgy things. The lawyer will cost more than the fine, but this is getting annoying. Our lawyer is sure we will win the case as we are innocent, but it's not clear we will be able to recover costs.. But I really feel strongly about this.. just because we found a way to bring you great gifts at great prices we are being attacked..I'm not even sure what they want us to do? Next time we import, do we increase the invoiced value to make them happy? Where would that money go...(to an off-shore bank account) that would be seriously dodgy. Are we expected to pay a fine on every import? I'll update you on what happens. In other news from Slovakia - this week we signed the "Head of Terms" agreement to move to a new larger warehouse early next year - if all goes according to plan. Our current warehouse is bursting at the seams, and growth is still running high.. so we have no choice but to expand.. Not the whole building, just the first five sections (I think). Last week I was telling you about an amazing new product from the Aromatics team,, And I am delighted to announce the Official Launch is TODAY!! Do-Nut Bath Bombs.. See below.. Also there is a load of new products all (finally) reaching the finishing line.. Amongst them.. Wild Hare solid shampoo and conditioner.. a very special product years in development.. watch this space.. Take care.. be kind to someone.. Have a great weekend and more updates from the world of AW next week. David

title: Name our warehouse competion
content_html:
Greetings from Bali. 

Last week I was telling you about going Mad in Marrakesh. You can read about it here. 

From there Tomas and I flew to Malaga, Spain - finalised a deal on an amazing new warehouse just 9 minutes from the airport, Tomas went to our Slovakia warehouse (which is his baby) I flew to Kuala Lumpur to see Raul who is our IT wizard.. Spent a couple of days with the team who are working on some game changing projects.. Jet lagged and seriously knackered I almost missed the flight to Bali, arriving late last night. So in a week.. Morroco, Spain, Malaysia & Indonesia. PHEW! 

In Bali airport, I got profiled.. passport control asked me lots of questions, why was I travelling alone? Why did I come from Malaysia business class, what was I doing in Bali.. He looked suspiciously at all the Indonesia entry stamps in my passport. So it was no surprise that they pulled me in at customs, a uniformed guy in black gloves, emptied all my luggage every item one by one and inspected even my toothpaste. Are you looking for drugs? I asked him, Yes sir.. He said, sorry its my job.. No problem at all, I said and gave him my business card.. I have samples of gemstone things from Morocco which rather confused him.. he sniffed at a selenite heart stone. But after a while he smiled helped me repack everything.. And thanked me warmly for doing business with his country. 

Arrived at the hotel late.. Worked until 1am, up at 7am.. Ringo here at 8am.. Breakfast with Ringo and big catch-up then we go to see the new warehouse. Last time I was here was to sign the lease. And the place was seriously run down and in need of TLC.. I made a plan with Ringo and had given him a budget. 

I'm so excited to see it..   Wow.. It's lovely I absolutely love the place now. Amazing what a paint job, new gates, new floor and some attention can do.


Ringo, always a man to get things done has exceeded himself and done it under budget. The warehouse has been transformed from an abandoned dump to place of beauty.

Let's go buy some big pots and nice plants and make the yard beautiful.. Frangipani trees I suggested. By 3pm we had a truck load of pots come, a truck load of flowers and a truck load of potting soil.  We diverted some staff from packing molten glass bowls and walking sticks to potting plants. But we couldn't find any frangipani tree's in roadside garden centres.. next week we will find. My first day in Bali has been blooming marvellous. 

We went for a walk down to the sea, it's about 10 minutes and along the way past frangipani trees and jack fruit trees.. Ringo explained that the Village is called Jack Fruit Village, it's actually a fishing village, it's very peaceful an absolute backwater in Bali. . Near the sea are a few fishing boats being cleaned and repainted. We made friends a fisherman called Ketut who carves fish from driftwood in his spare time, from him we learned that a Japanese millionaire built a villa here but never comes, he took us to see, did we want to buy it?  There a small warung (snack bar), a guy making rattan furniture and running a street bar in his show room, a shipping company and one villa style hotel. Everything else is local business. By the sea (which wild and natural) is a temple with a coral display by the door, a sign says "Pura Segara" it means Sea Temple. So many temples in Bali - this is a fishing village so a sea temple is apt. Even our warehouse has a small sacred place.. of course we will keep it pretty and well maintained.


I loved the village, and I'm looking forward to getting to know the locals. 

Regular readers will know our last warehouse was in Yellow Coconut Village, so we named our warehouse "AW Yellow Coconut Depot"  and we had an artist paint a yellow coconut tree on the entrance with our logo - and Yellow Coconut Depot in English and Indonesian.
It's part of our lease that we have to make the place beautiful, we will need to paint something on that blue door and office walls..


"AW Jack Fruit Depot" just doesn't feel right to me..  
Anybody got any idea.. lots of clues in the pictures and descriptions above..  let me know your ideas.. 
The winner gets - A bottle of fine wine, a £50 worth of Bali stock, a big thank you from Ringo and me, lots of karma points and the bragging rights to your idea being painted on our warehouse.

More news next week.

Have a great weekend whatever the weather!!

David

title: David's AW News: And so it begins
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


Hope you had a great week.. a good month.. because now it is December. Yes it's here: Full on Christmas.. 
Do you feel it? Here in Spain,
it doesn't feel like Christmas yet.. I know the traditional Christmas runs later here - with Three Kings Day in January the traditional day for gifts, but still I'm not feeling it.
Well we have the 12 days of Christmas kicking off today.. see below for details. This is another chance for Rodrigo the Uk marketing wizard and part-time Christmas Elf to give away AW stock at ridiculously low prices..


Picking your lucky 12 days of Christmas Deals.
Maybe it is a good opportunity to dip into some new product families.. and get stock ready for NY sales.. but I guess you already thought of that.
It's busy here in Spain, so lots to do.. this weekend we have the AW-Artisan.eu Christmas Party.. in downtown Malaga. Katka and James are coming from the UK, and Matej from Slovakia. 
And so begins.. the Party Season.. 
Last week I was telling you about our Big Plans for next year.. and an update on our pool terrace revamp at our home here in Spain. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Our terrace revamp is coming along Spanish style (slowly).. another week gone and even though the Father and son team seem to be (and actually are) working hard.. only little by little progress. They estimated it was a two week job, but already four and I pointed out to them it must be done before I leave for the UK. They have promised to find extra workers and started working later.. so lets see. But they still have a Siesta every afternoon.. 2 - 3pm I found them sleeping on sacks of concrete.. even though I told them they could use the spare bedroom, or sun loungers.. oh no we like it here they told me. Actually they are from Brazil and very nice guys, so just roll with it.. 


Coco is back in China and gearing up for another busy period. Because the Chinese New Year falls very early this year. Logistically if we don't get all our orders in place right now.. and despatch the next containers in January we won't have stock for Mother's Day in March. So the purchasing teams at AW are focused on that right now. We call it "The Season of Love" at AW. It's pretty big for AW because of the kind of stock we have.. From Valentine's Day through to Mother's Day and the Wedding Season May & June.. Yes I know it's Christmas.. but now is the time to think and plan for the next big sales season... 

In Bali.. our team almost all came down with a mysterious flu bug. It seems to be sweeping Asia, not helped by unusually heavy rains. This and this rain is also disrupting production and slowing things up. Ringo (our man in Indonesia) called me most upset that they had not met November's target for the number of containers dispatched. I know they are doing their best but it's a worry, lots of things are working against us. Lots of artisans are being lured away from their villages for jobs in hotels or construction... creating a shortage of artisans. Small business owners complain about not having enough staff all the time. Is there a solution? I think so.. in January I will go with James (our UK logistics guy) and try to implement my radical plan.. but only have a short time before the Epic India / Nepal trip starts..

Eipic 2024 Plan
So meanwhile the India / Nepal planning is getting more and more complicated.. I'm not sure we can meet all the objectives.. in the time we have.. but almost daily I'm working on it with our man in India: Mr Chatterjee. Last year we bagged 436 new (all good) product lines.. some of which are still arriving in the warehouses now and some already sold and re-ordered. Altogether a massive boost to our esoteric products.  Tomas told me that this year we have to top this.. I'm travelling with Toni (our man from Spain). Last year me and Toni went to Morocco. We went down mines, got lost in dusty mountain villages, made friends with the locals and came back with a brilliant range of geodes and selenite from the foothills of the Atlas mountains.. It was pretty wild.. but that was just the beginning.. basically just the induction course.. now it's time for Toni (and me) to venture to the unknown hard-core parts of India and Nepal.. 



Middle of nowhere in deep Morocco.
 
So it begins.. the search for new products to boost your sales, to bring you the latest esoteric, aromatic, artisan and exotic products. 
Hope you will join us on the journey..

Meanwhile it's Christmas .. and lots to do..
And So Begins December.. the Christmas Season is full on for you.. and for us the planning begins for next year.
I know you are jolly busy.. have a wonderful weekend.

More updates next week from the UK.

Take care.
David

title: David's AW News: THINK BIG (no AI)
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


It's a little chilly here but pretty damn cold in the UK and the poor guys in the Sheffield warehouse, (which is too big to heat), are AW Heros working under extreme conditions. Even so they are managing the current busy patch very well and getting your orders out in a timely fashion. Well done guys and gals.
Last week I was delivering a personal New Year message, basically a little rant and reality check: If you missed it you can catch up here.
I mentioned TEMU and SHEIN undermining the gift trade in general, and it seemed to have struck a chord, quite a few people messaged me about that. More ideas on how to fight that below.
And it is time to think BIG, think POSITIVE and think OUTSIDE the BOX.. 

But first I have to mention that we have been short-listed for Gift of the Year in three categories..Very exciting for our talented designers. We are crossing our fingers I definitely think all three should win.. but then I might be a tad biased!  In 2024 - our HOP HARE brand has been making leaps and bounds.. and Sandra has been very busy bringing you more.. watch this space coming soon.

Also very important.. the GOLD REWARD AMNESTY - Must end soon..  (Sunday Midnight) - act now!
Hope you understand how it works.. 

GOLD REWARD AMNESTY.  It means order now and whether you are a member or not, you are getting MAXIMISED discounts upto 28% off. So now is the perfect time to stock up and grab those discounts.. PLUS we are adding some crazy DOUBLE DISCOUNT DEALS..  including off Essential Oils.. and fast selling Soap Flowers. Perfect for Valentine's Day and Mother's Day.

The thing is - Think Positive - kick of 2025 with your refreshed Gold Reward membership.. you can top up with small orders and get those discounts.. and keep your membership. But early Feb when you stock up for Valentines Day you can take advantage again.. 

==================================================================================

So Let's Think Positive without asking AI - because everyone else is doing that and we are all going to end up doing the same things!

My thoughts (without consulting Mr AI) are like this..

1.  Be Special. Become an expert in a particular specialist area, because humans trust experts (Doctors, Lawyers, Trump etc) - at least if you have a passion or interest and can communicate enthusiasm, whatever the qualification (eg. I have been doing X for X years) then you can establish credibility. Blogs, YouTube, Social Media.. linked to your website. Specialist display in your Store, a corner dedicated to Nepal and Singing bowls and decorated with prayer flags)  Areas of expertise that people love and you can find heaps of products for in 2025 @ AW are: A. Aromatics (Eg. Essential oils, Scented Candles, Home Fragrance)   B. Esoterics (Incense, Singing Bowls, Gemstones, Zodiac things) C. Artisan & Home (Eg Coconut Wind-chimes, Teak Bowls, Home Decor) all made by real artisans not in faceless factories. 

2. Don't Compete on Price. Don't sell things that people can buy on TEMU, don't even try to compete. You can leave the bottom of the market to bottom feeders, slugs, snakes and rats.. You need to rise above that to find ethical, aromatic and interesting products with authenticity and style. At the end of the day, you have to find the RIGHT product for your store and your type of customer. Remember NEW IN STOCK  and ON SALE are two motivating signs in a store.. but only one has a much healthier profit margin for your store. One more related thing.. at AW we DON'T sell retail, we are pure B2B we support our trading partners like you not undermine them. When you see AW products on Amazon, it's not from us. It's someone like you buying and selling, or using our Dropshipping service. 

which brings me on to..

3. The 80/20 Rule. It's a well known fact (ask AI) that 80% of your profit will come from 20% of your products.. and holds true for almost any business. And that 20% of best sellers you need it to be a healthy margin product.. especially these days with hefty overheads to carry.   It's your mission (you know this but I'm just reminding you) to seek out and discover the 20% products that sell 80% of sales. They can be vastly different for different giftware traders.. What works like magic for one might fail for another.. but you're the one with a vision (and enthusiasm) for your store or online presence. Don't give up, keep searching.. actually at AW we have many hidden gems.. I can see product families that not many people stock, but those that do repeat buy big regularly. But don't fanny around trying a bit of this or that to try and find your golden ticket.. Go BIG or go home. It's why at AW we have bulk discounts and starters to encourage traders to make a bit of a flash. 

4. Think Big. Rinse and Repeat. GROW LIKE CRAZY.. once you find your winning formula.. don't be scared to open more outlets.  Popup shops, markets, tourist hot zones.. the same 80/20 Rule applies.. but unless you open 5 stores you may not find your goldmine - plus more than 5 stores you can begin to think outside the box and have middle management to do the day to day work - giving you time to create - and go even bigger faster.  Need help expanding - Drop us a line in the chat box, ask for a Key Account manager.. We can help with deals on starters and shopfitting, even finance with BNPL options. 

5. USE AI..  Haha I know I just told you not to because if you follow AI advice like everyone else - you are basically a Sheep. (BTW.. see our cute sheep). But a little advanced, carefully deployed  AI to aid your marketing, customer service or design (like that Gold Reward banner above).. can save you time.. Just don't use it instead of your brain. Unless you like being a sheep of course. Baa. 

So our resolution at AW in 2025 - is to bring you all of the above.  I'm especially keen to bring our regular customers brilliant deals - NO BRAINER DEALS. This year starting now, we are working hard to bring you bigger Gold Reward discounts.. like the 28% off Satya Incense. Fast selling, an excellent product and very good retailer margin. 

So wishing you a fantastic 2025 trading year! 

I'm off shortly travelling to the next place. Working hard to make AW your preferred Giftware partner.

Take care.

David

And that 20% of best sellers you need it to be a healthy margin product. . especially these days with hefty overheads to carry. It's your mission (you know this but I'm just reminding you) to seek out and discover the 20% products that sell 80% of sales. They can be vastly different for different giftware traders.. title: Big Wheels Turning
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

This week has been brainstorming week. Tomas, Raul and myself figuring out the AW master plan.
Raul is our IT wizard and flew in from Kuala Lumpur last Saturday..  I was waiting for him at Malaga arrivals and to fill the time checked the last time I had seen Raul - It has been 802 days since we met in  KL on route to Bali early 2020.  and as he emerged blinking into the Spanish sun we hugged and I told him.. Raul, the world has changed, AW has changed it's a different place, a different planet.  We have to rethink everything.
Tomas came from Slovakia where he dragged himself away from the excellent team there that are in the middle of moving warehouse. AWGifts.eu is moving to a much bigger place, AW UK moved to Affinity Park, and even in Spain we doubled our racking and expanded the staff and offices since Raul was last in Europe. You won't believe the changes I told him.
Big wheels turning, as the world around us changes but actually we know half the truth and probably twice the fake truth.

China update..
Coco is quarantined for seven days in a hotel on the outskirts of her hometown. It was a five star hotel, but now it is run down and nothing works. She told me this morning that for food they gave her a pot noodle and cheap electric kettle to boil water, but the tap water runs a muddy yellow. She was given a small mineral water and told to make it last two days. It's OK, she told me, only seven days.. I told her to (expletive) scream at someone. This is China she told me, nothing to do but follow the rules. The madness of zero covid in China is leading where? Even if they win the battle against covid... What then? They can never ever open the borders. What is really going on?

Boris went to India to talk about free trade deals, and relaxed imigration rules to fill gaps in the labour market (caused by Brexit).. meanwhile he forgot to sort the small detail about Brits travelling to India. The rest of the world (including Russians) can get an e-visa quickly and easily online. But UK nationals are banned. I mean what hell is going on? 
Mr Chatterjee keeps asking me when I am coming..  all I can say is ASAP.. meanwhile he is doing a good job finding new products and keeping stock flowing.

But at least it has been possible to travel to Indonesia, and the fruit of previous trips is arriving in our warehouses in Europe. Ringo and his team have been working really hard to ship goods from our warehouse in Bali. One consequence of the lockdown in Shanghai is that shipping containers are at last available and plentiful. But despite the glut, shipping costs have only fallen a smidgen.. I mean what the flipping-heck is going on?
The president of Indonesia just announced that export of palm oil is banned in order to protect food supplies to the nation. My intel sources in Indonesia tell me that the farmers and exporters are angry because the price of vegetable oil is rocketing up on world markets so they had stood to make a fortune. Now blocked..A massive 50% of the world supply comes from Indonesia. So this is huge. All oil prices will be affected.  
Soy wax in China for example is only available at ridiculous prices, we have closed the AW candle factory for now. Where will this madness end?

Good news is that stock is still flowing and new beautiful products arrived from Indonesia this week. It makes me happy to think that all over Indonesia artisans are working hard producing beautiful things that land in our Frangipani warehouse and then wend their way to your shop and to your customers' homes. Everyone is happy and a virtuous - magical, life improving circle is maintained.
Like big wheels turning.. but in a good way.


Check out our Indonesian Products Page..
Spring is in the air.. and those Indonesian products are perfect for your spring refresh..
Here in Spain it is Mother's Day - and flowers are blooming everywhere..
In the UK we have a long weekend.. It's May day and Spring has sprung..

Lots of things back in stock.. including amazingly those Salt Lamps you are waiting for.
Lots of new products perfect for spring.
Plus check out our amazing Bank Holiday Weekend Offer.

Wishing you a lovely weekend.

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: A Christmas Thank You (30 Years of Ancient Wisdom)
content_html:
Greetings from the AW office in Slovakia

 

Well here it is (almost) it's Christmas Time.

And well this is the last AW Newsletter Before Christmas  (Can You Believe It?)

Last week I was telling you about our Serious Christmas party in Spain. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Well after that I was back to the UK.. then on Saturday we had the UK AW Christmas party..  It was crazy, fun and wonderful to celebrate with our teams in the UK.

I did a speech (as did others) then we danced the night away..




Yesterday afternoon I took a Ryanair flight with James to Bratislava, and then drove to the pretty town of Trnava. 

Checked in the hotel and met up with Tomas and friends - where we managed a quick walk around the Christmas market.



Slovakia Christmas market - that Christmas feeling.

As I write this, I’m in Slovakia getting ready for the AW Slovakia Christmas party tonight — one of many AW gatherings happening around the AW world. As we all tidy up, open the Secret santa, switch off spreadsheets, and remember why we started this whole thing in the first place.

 And this feels like a good moment to say thank you.

This year marks 30 years of Ancient Wisdom.
Yes.. Thirty. Years.

Which means:

 30 years of sourcing, packing, unpacking, re-packing

 30 years of ideas that worked… and a few that really didn’t

 30 years of candles, oils, incense, notebooks, bags, gifts, mistakes, lessons, friendships and stories

 From a freezing market stall in Sheffield to warehouses and teams across the UK, Europe and beyond — none of this would exist without you, our customers.

You’ve stuck with us through thick and thin: economic chaos, Brexit, various shipping crises, our warehouse burning down (in covid), and the occasional “why on earth did they make that?” product - sorry about that.

Yet you’re still here. Still ordering. Still believing in what we do. That means more than you probably realise.

I have always said AW isn’t just about products — it’s about stories, people, ideas, and a bit of soul in a world that sometimes feels like it’s losing the plot.

And so after 30 years, that feels truer than ever. So wherever you are reading this — in your shop, warehouse, office, kitchen, or hiding from customers with a cup of tea...

Thank you for being part of the AW journey.

From all of us at Ancient Wisdom, Including the AW teams in India, China and Indonesia we all send you Greetings and thanks.

 we wish you a peaceful Christmas

a profitable New Year

and enough calm moments to enjoy why you do what you do!

 And finally… Since tonight is the Slovak Christmas Party.. (and I'm hoping they can loosen up a little and have some fun) raise a glass with us.

To 30 years of Ancient Wisdom — and to whatever slightly mad, beautiful ideas come next.

See you in 2026.
(Yes… 2026. That sounds crazy even to me.)

Warmest Christmas Wishes,
David

PS in the UK.. you can still place orders this weekend. We will ship every order on Monday or Tuesday.

title: We Have a Problem...
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Wow it's getting busy now.. it's a good job we made the leap to our new warehouse. I can't believe we received the keys just one month ago, a ridiculous amount of things have happened in that short time.
Last week I was telling you about the Beast from France.. a nice bit of kit that is going to produce amazingly beautiful soaps for you.. if you missed it you can read about it here. 
Talking about soaps and bathroom products, we are excited to be able to add a huge swathe of new items.. see below..
A few weeks back I was askinging for a name suggestions for the new warehouse. First time round almost every suggestion involved a phoenix, which while apt (since we are just recovering from a fire) to me seemed a bit corny. Also puts me in mind of those dodgy companies that go bust and start again, and use the word in their new name. The second batch of suggestions is much more imaginative. Some really clever, thought provoking, cultured and inspired suggestions. I'm going to compile a shortlist of the best.. and then we will vote at AW. But it's too early to adopt a name for our building yet.. simple because it is not quite ours yet. And there is a potential problem.
If you have been following the story you will know that, the people who own the building now didn't want to rent, they wanted to sell. And the price (several million) was really outside our power. So the solution was to an investment fund to buy it and rent it back to us. Someone who was happy with the building and happy with AW being in it. This was the first task..and miraculously we managed it.  Now as you know buying a big building takes some time maybe months. And that was time we simply didn't have, because of the massive flow of incoming stock with no-where to put it, Christmas and a big backlog of orders. So the next hurdle was to persuade the current owner to let us use the place under license, paying a monthly rent. 
On the 18th of September we finally managed this and got a set of keys. What a relieve it has been, but also a massive task..  stock coming from storage, a backlog of containers and all the stock from the other warehouse.. There is 96,000 square feet, but as yet no racking, but no problem we can just put pallets on the floor.


Now as you can see the floor is almost full. We have quotes and plans drawn up for the racking, it will cost something like £240,000 and give us about 7000 pallet spaces. Of course, we are not going to spend that kind of money until we have a secure long term lease. 
Everything was going swimmingly, the very nice people at the American owned fund came to see us and the building and all was good. 
But then my lawyer called me.. a snag.. it seems there are eight mine shafts running under the building. No-one can find papers to say they have been filled in and made safe. My lawyer is frantically calling the coal board, checking townhall documents and doing searches every which way. Of course, the US fund won't commit to buying a building that could disappear down a sink-hole without a trace. So it's not like we haven't had enough stress lately.. here's an extra dollop. 

I'm sure it will be OK.. but we have to manage without racking a bit longer.
Meanwhile, it's all going great guns.. lots of orders been picked, every day better than the last. James and Tomas have plans to make it all super efficient. 

As Christmas approaches, and a second wave is pushing more people into soft lockdowns, then I think online sales will get another massive boost like in June/ July.. I know many of our customers have online retail sorted. Many already doing really well. Just a nudge.. did you know you can sell most AW products via our Dropshipping Dept. AW-dropship.com . I'm pleased to say Lucy and Adriana who run DS are catching up and turning round orders better each day. Register today.

I'm sure you are super busy. Wish you happy trading.

Take stay safe. Wear (an AW) mask, and keep positive.

More news next week.

David

title: The Hump
content_html:
Hi ,
Last week I was telling you about the Albesia wood village in Indonesia.
This week I'm in India. I needed to get to Kolkatta from Yiwu in China, that's tricky there are no direct flights, so I ended flying to the northern city of Kunming and changing planes to fly to Kolkata. Kunming is in the middle of nowhere, but has a beautiful modern airport and did a pretty good sales pitch on me as a place to visit properly one day. Misty lakes high in rocky mountains, something called ice wine, and a culture of intricate dress and dance almost Thai like. A Shangri-La of a city.
On the plane, half Chinese business people and half boisterous excited (to go home) Bengali guys. In mid air, bouncing over some clouds - it hit me. Of course... I was flying the HUMP. I'd read about it lots. The most dangerous scheduled air route in the world. Calcutta to Kunming and back. In 1942 as the Japanese had an almost complete China blockade in place it was the only way to bring essential supplies to China. The British and Americans built an air bridge over the Himalayas and across Burma, which was a hairy jump made worse violent winds, blinding snow and Japanese fighter planes coming at you. Hundreds of people died, why we did it, and what good it did, is all but forgotten, but it was a mammoth operation for it's day. The Hump.
Today we land at Kolkata international terminal in the middle of the night. It's hot and sticky and a battered hump-era bus, smelling of curry is waiting in the gloom to take us to the terminal. The culture shock for the Chinese is complete, they are taking pictures of the broken windows and threadbare plush red seats. The terminal is a delight, practically colonial, faded and smelling of corruption complete with a magnificent painting of Bengali tigers prowling for the kill. Beneath it old school Bengali immigration staff, khaki uniforms, fat bellies and eyes prowling for the backhander. Almost all the Indian airports have smartened up, even the Kolkatta domestic airport is first class but this is the business. Real India!
We line up for passport control, there are no signs in Chinese and even the English signs are confusing. NRI here, SAAC here. Of course the Chinese all get in the wrong lines, which hugely amusing for the young Indian guys. There are immigration forms to fill. In China it's a tiny slip of paper, here it is long form. It must be filled in English, and to satisfy these rheumy eyed old timers on the desks - it must be tip-top and correctly filled in. The Chinese who are pretty slap-dash at form filling have filled things in on a random basis. They keep getting sent back to the end of the queue with new forms. It becomes clear to me that non of the officials speak Chinese, not a word. And most of the Chinese left in the hall have very little English.
So there I am my awful Chinese being stretched to the limit as I try to help all these Chinese fill the forms to a satisfactory level. Even I get ticked off for not filling the full address of my hotel, what chance have they got. The weary official stamping my forms, sighs and rolls his eyes, "they come here with no English" and then, "help this guy here, would you". After half an hour - I too am filling the guys forms for them... randomly. Chatting in Chinese the best I can and putting any old date in. Translating for the official.. "He says he's here for two weeks" - (when he told me he didn't know how long). I'm damned if the old boys are getting any bribes tonight.
Finally I'm though and at 3am spill out into the warm night air. The good thing about India is little luxuries come cheap. As everyone else is scrambling for dilapidated ambassador taxies, I'm met by a smart guy in a grey suit and peaked cap, a sign with my name and a waiting limo to whisk me to the hotel. "Pleasant flight sir?" asks the chauffeur. Interesting I tell him.
More news next week.
Take care
David

title: Bali Updates New Office
content_html:
Greetings from Bali  now lock-down day 48

Last week I was telling you how something strange is going on In Bali, with covid-19 situation.. you can read about it here.

Since then the figures for Bali stay low and improving, and yet the lock-down measures are ramping up day by day. It is now illegal to be out without a mask.. even in a car. You will be fined on the spot. Yesterday right outside my villa on the street was an army guy brandishing a machine gun. I mean what the hell is going on? From today they stopped travel without a permit from any village area to another.. this means I can't go to the warehouse - because it's over the border from this section of Denpasar that I'm living in. Ringo is trying to find away to get permission to cross the blockades.

Meanwhile, so far anyway our warehouse is business as normal. Ringo shipped a container load this week. People often ask if shipping is still working, and the answer is yes, pretty much. Logistics have to continue or everything stops. The only hick-up was that our container booking was bumped. We had a confirmed booking with a shipping line and therefore a timetable for the container stuffing and transporting to the port. At the last minute, we got a call to say - sorry the ship is full you will have to wait for the next one. Pretty much the same thing happened in China last week. I think it's a bit like getting bumped off a flight because they over booked it. Annoying but could be worse.  The warehouse is still full, but at the end of last week, it was totally brimming meet Happy our adopted mut.. Ringo feeds him half his breakfast every morning and a quick tour of our warehouse.


We have a nice big office, we turned part of it into a photo studio (I was telling you the other week) but it's not really what I would call a nice office space. So I said to Ringo lets make it cool. We need a sofa, some art, nice tables. If you want me to come and work here I want it nice, anyway it should be nice for you and your assistant. So we went up the road towards Ubud, on the way is an area famous for cool furniture. If you are ever in Bali check it out.. (I know travelling seems a distant dream) tell your taxi guy to take you to Mas village. See I tell you all the trade secrets :)   - mostly to annoy the competition haha. There are actually some quite big businesses producing rattan furniture, recycled teak wood furniture (which I absolutely love) and a place that makes Japanese style sea-grass furniture. They have showrooms bordering the road, and at the back barn-like workshops where the furniture is made. Of course this been corona-time no showrooms are open, but by shouting hello, we soon roused an owner or two. 
To say they are delighted and amazed to see an actual buyer is an understatement. We met one lady, called Ebu Siri has a business making beautiful furniture for local hotels and for export, mainly to USA and Sweden.


I liked her because she was so happy and had a wicked laugh and a twinkle in her eye. She told us she was 53 got 3 grand children, and I noticed a .. beautiful house at the back. It's lovely I said as she leads us past to the factory behind. She roared with laughter and said - I'm so lucky because I married into a rich family! Self depreciating I think because the products produced there are really nice and I could see her staff (wearing masks and social distancing) clearly loved her. She was the boss for sure. We bought some furniture for the office nice leather backed chairs and a beautiful river table that would cost thousands of pounds in Europe. 
When her truck came to deliver, she came along with her daughter to nosy our warehouse.. and we promised in the future to try and do some proper business. 
I think we could sell the river tables, they are basically made from imperfect teak-wood with the gaps filled with an opaque resin and polished smooth, giving the effect of a river running through the natural wood. 

   Ringo in our new office space. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. we took most of our staff off furlong this week as the business seems to be bouncing back. It helps that we have soap, essential oils and home items that people really want. Also the fact that we can offer a drop-shipping solution has made a big difference to many of our customers. (Check out AW-Dropshipping.com) register if your interested now, because we are already at breaking point and may need to stop registrations soon, although I think we will keep it open of course to existing AW customers. Yes I know we could add more staff and we are doing this, but because of social distancing, there is a limit on how many people can work in the department. We are a few days behind with orders, please bear with us.  

Stock update.
The frustrating thing is that we are running out of stock of many items.. our own production because of limited capacity because of social distancing rules (it must be safety first). But we are working hard to increase production this week. China stock is a problem because it was all frozen for February and March because of the lockdown there, but since early April is flowing again.. first containers arriving last week and this so stock is coming back online. Indonesian stock is OK and flowing still.. it helps that I am here to help keep an eye on things. More containers are in transit. 
Indian and Nepal stock - was and still is frozen. Still no flights from Nepal, so no stock and I think we have a substance sum locked up there. Same with India, we continue to advance funds to suppliers (even though they cannot ship), to help with their cash flow and hopefully still pay workers. Bryant our shipping manager is keeping an eye on the situation and hopefully, soon we will be able to unblock stock and get it flowing again. Difficult times. 

I hope you are keeping safe and keeping fruitfully occupied. I know many of you are finding ways to carry on trading, and we thank you for your support.
I'm writing this in the new office space at our warehouse near Sukawati outside of the Denpasar city boundary.. I came here this morning as normal, but getting home this afternoon might be a problem. They announced a major lock-down in Denpasar and no-one is supposed to go to the city without good cause and supporting documents. There are road blocks.  Next week I will tell you if I made it home.

Take care.

David

title: David's AW News: Police Station
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Well it's all happening all at once.. again.. as usual. This Sunday - obviously is going to be crazy.. Spain v England.. I'm sure the local bars around here are going to be crammed.
Last week I was telling you about our new Search Bar (have you tried it yet?) - and told you my slightly sad story about the Slouchy Tote bags from Kolkata. If you missed it you can catch up here.
My thanks to the several people who wrote to me about this, and yes you're all correct. Now the pictures are fixed to look more like it. Slouchy Bags.
Earlier this week Coco and I had to go to Torremolinos police station...
We arrived very early for the appointment.. It's been a long time coming and we couldn't be late.. Just past the main entrance just round the back is a small scruffy outdoor waiting area with a few rows of sun battered chairs, a small crowd of people are milling around maybe on the same mission as us. For some this is a life changing moment. I can see it in the faces. A battered peeling sign on a window says "DOCUMENTACION" . 
After a while an impossibly smart policeman appears in the doorway armed with a gun and a clipboard. Montana, who is also our accountant, met us there just in case there were any issues - she has done this kind of thing before.. she elbowed her way to the guy and practically stabbed the clipboard, "aqui, aqui" here is my client name.. Then shouts to Coco "vamos!".. I said go go Coco looks like your first in line. I sit down to wait patiently on a battered chair but only five minutes later Coco and Montana emerge.
Coco has an official Spanish ID card and right to remain. No need to get troublesome visa's any more and freedom to travel in Europe. 
It's all good news!  Later we celebrated this and Tomas 40th Birthday on the beach with a slap up meal. 

Whatever happens on Sunday there will be a lot of people celebrating here in Spain.. I'm looking forward to the fun.
Meanwhile - in the UK - everything is happening.. if you are quick you can Bag a Bag Bargain - in our 50% off sales.. Now is the peak summer season for summer bags sales (ahead of the summer hols)- so with that in mind we have slashed a swathe of bag items to help you stock up.

More good news - a Container that Coco shipped over 2 months ago arrived.. that's pretty quick these days.  It has lots of new exciting stock on it. and many fast selling lines back in stock. I know the warehouse team is working extra hard to get everything booked in, and Rodrigo and his team are frantically getting new products online.  Amongst them is a range of Gemstone Pendants to go with the Pendant cord range we received last month..  

Also have you seen them? 
I first came across them in India. It's called a Floating Frame. They are awesome for making small jewelry items stand out and look so much more pretty.
They make an effective gift box and cheap enough you can "give" them away.. or sell as an extra. If someone is buying a bracelet as a gift then they for sure will want a nice box to put it in. Use also to take your jewelry display to the next level.  In China we went to our long-time jewelry display supplier. They told us these are the hottest thing in years, that if we wanted to order we had to go on a waiting list as production was maxed out, and even if we paid cash up front we'd still have to wait.   
But Coco worked miracles and found a small factory with capacity and charmed them enough to get us enough stock to get going.  Yes I realise before you ask.. these are plastic. But not single use - this is to keep your precious jewelry dust free and looking good for years to come. 

Anyway, enjoy your weekend. Apparently Football is coming home. 

Take care
David

title: David's AW News:Temu, Surfing & Success
content_html:
Greetings from the AW digital marketing office.


Yes, I'm working this morning from what we call the beach office.
Raul came over from Kuala Lumpur and this week we have been working closely with the development team here to bring some really useful functionality to our Fulfilment and Dropshipping websites.
Looking out of the window I can see some serious surf rolling in. And inside the team of developers and digital marketing guys heads down "surfing" the online world to connect AW to the world.
Temu and Shen are in the news these days.. and finally for the right reasons. The tax loopholes they have exploited are being closed step by step..And this could be great news for the gift traders of UK and Europe.. I have Raul and the team here focused on how we can help our valuable customers (that's you!) grab your share of the multi-billion gap in the market that will appear if what I think will happen - happens.  
Last week I was telling you about our hard working warehouse team here in Bali.. behind the scenes.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

I was just chatting with Coco in China - she is celebrating Chinese New Year with her family in the hometown area. Yiwu, where we have our warehouse and office, she told me, is in a state of shock. The Trump tariffs and EU crackdown on Temu, Shen and the thousands of remote dropshippers that operate from Yiwu has cast a long shadow over Chinese New Year Celebrations.
I found this youtube video that explains it well. Although some of the comments are off the mark, you can get the big picture by watching this. The Loophole.
The thing is, one reason why Temu could be so crazy cheap, was the brutal system they applied to the China vendors. If vendors products were not moving from staging warehouses then storage and fees would be applied forcing small businesses to sell at a loss. Often businesses going bankrupt would get their stock shipped below cost to pay off fees,(I am told anidocally) hence those crazy prices. So the end of Temu is not all bad. Even for China. 

Are you ready to take back control..of the gift trade?
AW-Dropshipping.com has already seen a mini surge in registrations and users.. If you can master online sales with Shopify, Tiktok or even Amazon, we can ship your orders, no need to hold stock, pack orders or do your own shipping we can handle it all.. and coming soon much more automation. Those guys above are making API's that could make you millions. (seriously).

Meanwhile..
A container just arrived from China (all duty and taxes paid) with lots back in stock but also some brilliant new and useful stock.

Including.. We are so excited a range of Tarot Cards including unique designs. 

Introducing Irina!
And welcome to a new member of our team in the UK..Irina.. She is here to help you connect in the Showroom and give you inspiration for marketing AW products.
https://www.instagram.com/p/DFr6w8oMhXR/
Welcome to the AW team Irina! 


Valentine's Day is almost upon us.. Now is a great time to stock up for the season of love.. 

Travel plan.. Next week I'm off to Java for a road trip around some remote and interesting Artisan towns and villages. 
I'm hoping we can find something like time.. Full report next week. 

Wishing you a lovely lively weekend. 
Take care. 

David
