title: What Can Possibly Go Wrong?
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Happy Friday the 13th.. what can possibly go wrong? 

It's my last day here in our Malaga warehouse before going to the UK for Christmas.
Last week I was telling you about our new Spanish warehouse.. and the very different business culture to the UK and even other parts of Europe. You can read about it here.

So last night like many of you I was awake half the night watching the election dramas unfold. Some major upsets and spills, but at least now we know.. Brexit is on..it's going to happen. And on the 31st of January 2020.
I'll be honest I don't like it, I feel we have been sold a lemon, it seems crazy to cause trading friction with all our European neighbours.. especially when half our sales at AW are into Europe.. BUT... now is clarity, now we can put plans into action.


Raul went back to Malaysia, Tomas and Rodrigo are back in the UK.. from Monday the new team in Spain will be on their own at least for a week or so. Thrown in the deep end. 
It's still early days, there are workmen all over the place, stock deliveries still to come, the showroom is not set up yet.. but the website is buzzing, customers keep popping in to say hello and make friends (as is the Spanish way) - even with limited stock available orders are flowing.. and the team is mega motivated and soaking up lots of knowledge and developing skills breathtakingly quickly. I think they are going to be awesome.. 

And now Brexit is getting done.. they will need to be, because depending how it works a flood of orders could move from UK to Spain (and to our Slovakia base).. maybe then some staff will move from the UK.

2020 is going to be a big shake-up year, but I feel at last we are ready for whatever happens. As Katka in the UK likes to say.. when life gives you a lemon.. Make a gin and tonic.
It's Friday the 13th and unlucky for some we got Boris. At least the jokes will be thick and fast, and life should be interesting.

It's a bit noisy in the office here in Malaga, mostly because of all the workers, plastering, fitting floors. putting in doors and installing air-conditioning.. they should be finished in a few days, and it certainly looks like it. I have to say I am blown away by the Spanish workers, not only are they superbly professional, incredibly polite but between breaks and long lunches they work like the wind - so fast.. and so clean. Every-time there is dust and dirt, they stop and clean, at the end of the day everything is swept clean all tools are put away. The construction site is left spic and span. No "Grand Designs" style drama what's so ever.

The only drama we had was from a jolly English guy who came to quote for some work, did all that sucking in of breathe and scratching his head - told us he was sooo busy but at a push could fit in the job. We asked that he was legal, and his workers insured and paying taxes - yes of course he said Boris-like with heaps of confidence. On the day, just before starting Mario our accountant guy said, do you mind if we just check that.. "saying yes is not good enough" he told me we need to see papers. Here you can be fined huge sums if your not careful. Mario had a quiet word.. five minutes later the guy came to see me.. Sorry David.. he shook my hand, "no hard feelings mate.. but we are off the job", and with no further ado he and his team vanished like bats in the night.   

Meanwhile in the UK the team is still working like crazy to get orders out. I understand we are keeping up and even catching up bit by bit.
Lots of new products came in including a beautiful elegant range of candle holders and ready for the new year some super cool note books - perfect for making a list of things to do in 2020.
Speaking of which as mentioned - next week I will be in the UK, and making plans for next year. 

Hope you have a great weekend and get through Friday the 13th unscathed and smiling.
In any event.. Don't worry be happy.. make a G&T :)

Take care.

David

No "Grand Designs" style drama what's so ever. The only drama we had was from a jolly English guy who came to quote for some work, did all that sucking in of breathe and scratching his head - told us he was sooo busy but at a push could fit in the job. We asked that he was legal, and his workers insured and paying taxes - yes of course he said Boris-like with heaps of confidence. On the day, just before starting Mario our accountant guy said, do you mind if we just check that.. "saying yes is not good enough" he told me we need to see papers. Here you can be fined huge sums if your not careful. Mario had a quiet word.. five minutes later the guy came to see me.. Sorry David.. he shook my hand, "no hard feelings mate.. but we are off the job", and with no further ado he and his team vanished like bats in the night. Meanwhile in the UK the team is still working like crazy to get orders out. I understand we are keeping up and even catching up bit by bit. Lots of new products came in including a beautiful elegant range of candle holders and ready for the new year some super cool note books - perfect for making a list of things to do in 2020. Speaking of which as mentioned - next week I will be in the UK, and making plans for next year. Hope you have a great weekend and get through Friday the 13th unscathed and smiling. In any event.. Don't worry be happy.. make a G&T :) Take care. David

title: David's AW News: 🌸 Why Málaga Has Turned Purple
content_html:
Greetings from Spain...

And strangely enough... it has actually been hotter in parts of the UK than it has been here this week. Hope you fully enjoyed last weeks Bank Holiday.

I've been spending a few days with Toni and the Spanish team in our Málaga warehouse. Nothing especially dramatic to report this time, although my Spanish residency card saga continues. The card itself is ready, but actually obtaining an appointment to collect it appears to be another challenge entirely. My agent checks every morning for available slots... and every morning the answer is the same. None available. I am beginning to suspect it may be easier to source gemstones from a mine in the remote backwaters of India than secure an appointment with Spanish bureaucracy.

Last week I was telling you about my adventures in Spain and the ongoing residency card saga. If you missed it, you can catch up here: 

One thing that certainly caught my eye this week was the spectacular Jacaranda trees that are now in full bloom all around Málaga. 



Although they feel completely Spanish, Jacaranda trees actually originate from South America. They were introduced to Spain over a century ago and have become one of Málaga's most recognisable sights. For just a few weeks each year they burst into flower, turning streets, parks and even industrial estates into a sea of lavender-purple blossoms. In some cultures, the Jacaranda is associated with wisdom, good fortune and new beginnings. So this is an Ancient Wisdom tree! Whatever the meaning, they certainly make the morning drive to the warehouse rather more cheerful.

Of course, while the trees may look relaxed, the team certainly isn't.

Today is the final trading day of the month and across Ancient Wisdom, from Sheffield to Slovakia, Spain to Bali, everyone is working flat out to dispatch every possible order before month end. Warehouses are buzzing, customer service teams are chasing last-minute requests and buyers are already planning the next arrivals.

And naturally, because this is Spain...


Warehouse team member Brahyan appears to have been inspired by the wedding season and decided to model his future wedding outfit using a generous quantity of bubble wrap. There is never a dull moment in a wholesale warehouse. Especially in Spain where every day is a party.

Talking of arrivals, some exciting new gemstone products have landed from India this week. We have been working closely with trusted suppliers and gemstone specialists to bring in ranges with genuine provenance and quality. See new products below..

The recent spell of warm weather has also got us thinking about outdoor living, festivals, glamping and camping. Most people don't immediately think of Ancient Wisdom as a camping supplier, but you might be surprised how many products fit perfectly into that market.

Which brings me neatly to Holly's latest "Can You Sell This?" video.

This week Holly explores camping and outdoor-living gift ideas, sharing practical tips on how retailers can turn seasonal trends into real sales opportunities.


As we head into the summer season, - 1st of June is offically Summer (can you believe it) let's hope the sunshine continues, the campsites stay busy and the Jacaranda flowers hold on for a little while longer.

Until next week, thank you for your business and support.

Best wishes,

David

title: Bali Lockdown Developments
content_html:
Greetings from the Bali lock-down day (sigh) 34..

Happy worker's day.. May Day.. is it springtime?.. It's a good time to recognise the workers of the world that are still going to work in the this time of corona.. the front line nurses of course, but also all the unseen people that feed us and keep essential services running. 
Here in Bali, as I was telling you last week.. I'm well and truly stranded. All travel in or out of Bali suspended until further notice. You can read about it here. But somehow life goes on. 
And even though the advice is #StayHome many people are able to work. Some days Ringo will pick me up and we go to the warehouse - it's only about 15 minutes from here on the edge of Sukawati, an area famous for it's art market and a major centre for artisans. I can see as we drive around plenty of activity, but everyone, everyone is wearing a mask and generally keeping social distance. And there are police everywhere enforcing the rule. 

We have been setting up a photo studio so that product shots of new items can be taken, well before they reach us in Europe. Yesterday a guy came from the photo equipment shop (we are good customers now) to give us training.. wearing a mask and keeping 2 meters apart he still managed to impart a huge amount of stuff.. I learned so much, and I thought I knew how to picture things.

Afterwards I suggested to Ringo that what we really need is some natural props to give texture to the pictures.. like some driftwood, or pebbles. Ok lets go to the nearby beach, which I know to be barely used - must be some driftwood knocking around.  But the beach was blocked by a large barricade and a security guy wasn't going to let us pass.. no problem says Ringo, there's lots of beaches we can get to.. and we tried, at the next road entrance which was way to a small port area, there was police and army and flashing lights. Some guy - with a machine gun came over to ask us what our business was going to the beach..    "Erm.. to look for driftwood" didn't impress. Mission abandoned. 

Turns out the problem is Mudik.. it's the beginning of Ramadan and lots of people from Java and other islands want to be in the home-town for Ramadan.. this is a huge travelling time - called Mudik.. and quite rightly the government is terrified that a mass movement of of millions of people is a bad idea right now. Most people are complying with the rule, but some miss-guided folk are determined to get home even using small boats to travel in.. hence the beach lock-down.  


Ringo had a visit from the police at home.. his daughter called and Ringo dashed home to find out what the problem was. Turns out Ringo has been identified as the neighbourhood trusted person and given the task of handing out free food parcels to anyone in need.
It's a major problem in Bali, the population of 4 million, half work in tourism related jobs.. all the tourists have gone, almost all hotels are closed, all restaurants and bars closed. Many of these workers are not rich, living from week to week.. now out of work the local government is actually worried about starvation, hence the food parcels. Also on the main junctions I have seen food banks opening up, with free food for anyone who needs it. Ringo says surprisingly few people are using them.. maybe it's a pride thing. Even on the street near my villa, a lady sits with a pile of  packets of rice wrapped in banana leaves.. a big sign says "Makanan Gratis"  - Free Food. I didn't see anyone avail themselves - yet..

Another guy handing out food is our man in India Mr Chatterjee.. I speak to him most days. The issues in Bali are nothing compared to India, and there the local government don't seem to be able to do much. I sent some money and Mr Chatterjee and friends turns it into food for his laid-off workers and the poor people of his town. 

 Feeding the poor in India. Mr Chatterjee - a Hero.



Chatterjee delivered food to the Children's home we support and they sang him a song.. and sent me a personal message - saying they are fine, how are you Mr David?


We live in difficult times.   

Meanwhile back in the UK.. things keep happening. A Boris baby boy.. and if they don't name him Tom (after Captain Tom - who turned 100 the same time) then there is no justice in the world. 
Talking about the workers on May Day.. I have to give a big hand to the AW Hero's that are keeping the ship afloat.. we have been surprisingly busy - drop-shipping is crazy.. and to keep the orders going whilst staying safe, social distancing and all is no mean feat. So I applaud the AW team.

Take care - stay safe.

David

title: Wear with Confidence
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ - I'm in a very rainy Sheffield.

Last week I was telling you about KYS.. the importance of knowing your supplier, in the gift trade and how important it is especially in the gift business. Also updates on my Morrocan trip, you can read it here.

Last week I was in very sunny Spain, On Saturday took the Easyjet flight to Manchester and it's been raining ever since. The wettest June on records and we are only halfway through.
I don't know how wet weather affects your business, maybe online traders will do better. Years ago, way back in ancient history - before the internet (as we call it in the north) I had a couple of AW gift shops in Derbyshire and I remember the best weather was a sunny morning (to bring everyone out) and a rainy afternoon, to drive everyone into the shops. I don't know if that still holds true.. 

It's Father's Day on Sunday - so a big day in the gift trade - so Happy Father's Day.. to all the Dad's and to all you gift traders that are Dad's or otherwise..

So this week has been at HQ - where as usual it is a hive of hectic activity. New products under development in production, new deliveries from Indonesia, a Salt lamp container came - so lots back in stock. Oh and also we had a Silver delivery from an artisan supplier in Bali.
Beautiful Gold & Silver mix jewellery with an exotic mystic feel. Everyone in the office is in love with it - we had packaging made to compliment the product and feel this is a special gift anyone would be pleased to own. Bracelets are suitable for men or women, and Tomas who was there in Bali at the birth of this product and worked with the artisans and designer to tweak the designs for the European market has been wearing a bracelet ever since. See below.

Sooo.. last week I was telling you how banks have to KYC.. Know your customer,, to make sure they don't inadvertently enable bad people to do bad things.. Likewise, we try to KYS.. Know your supplier.. and this Silver & Gold jewellery - you can be sure is ethically sourced. We have all read about blood diamonds, about Jade being produced in drug fuelled open cast mines and even worse things that can happen when greed distorts morals. The jade mines in Kachin state in Burma I was aware of a long time ago, and it is this type of supply that is simply bad Karma to the gift trade. Read about the horrors in this Guardian article here.  
Open the packaging on our new silver jewellery and you can see it says "..wear with confidence.." it's meaning is on two levels..





A word about Salt Lamps..
They come from Pakistan, famously mined from under the Himalayan mountains - the purest salt on earth. Rana (our main supplier) is a gentle guy wears traditional clothes. He meets me regularly in Malaysia with new samples, and we will eat together in a Pashtun restaurant where he updates me all about his business. It's a family business and we have dealt with them for a few years, I'll admit I haven't (yet) been to Pakistan to see the mining and production personally, but I have regular live Whatsapp updates from Rana. He told me a while back about unauthorised mines, open cast mines that use dynamite to blast apart hillsides and then let subcontractors scramble for it.. Many people die in this area each year, the salt from there is half the price of government regulated mines. The area the salt is mined called Khwera and there are good and bad mines. Bad mines have lower quality, poor safety records but very low prices. This really is a case of KYS.. 
Rana assures me his raw salt comes from government regulated mines, while not perfect are trying to improve standards. Salt Lamps Back in Stock.

KYW... likewise know your wholesaler.. do they care? do they check these things? I'm sure you will ask. 
Anyway, more news next week.

By the time you read this, I will be at our Slovakian distribution warehouse. Regular readers will know about our own Brexit backstop, insurance against a Boris no-deal outcome.
More news next week.

Take care - have a great Father's Day.

title: David's AW Newsletter: Trying not to complain.
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

 

How are you doing today?

Here in Spain, it's still almost too hot.. I'm trying not to complain. Last week I was telling you about heatwaves, Holly and India. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

I hear good weather is also blessing the UK this weekend.. so hopefully you can enjoy it...  Rodrigo, our marketing man in the UK.. will certainly be enjoying it. Here he is enjoying the weather with the recently expanded team.  This week, we are excited to welcome Alex (the cool guy in the baseball cap). 

A traditional AW picture.. always includes a Buddha statue.


Toni is stressed.

Toni, our man in Spain, has had a busy (and stressful) week - a container from India finally arrived after clearing customs with what seems to me ridiculously unfair treatment. (I'm trying not to complain). Despite having all our paperwork carefully prepared and in place, answering every customs query and despite never ever doing anything dodgy.  The delays in customs create storage charges, which we have to pay even though it's not us causing the delay.. and then, when everything is found to be in order - someone decides they want to off load the container to check if the number of cartons declared is correct. Guess what we have to pay for that check also.. and more delay because the person sent to check was off work ill.. more storage charges.  And after unloading, of course, they cannot get it all back in the container.. the balance has to be sent on pallets to us.. who pays for that.. yes you guessed it. Actually, the cost of the products goes up by 5-10% because of this kind of bureaucracy.. so in the end everyone pays. I'm trying not to complain!

Party in Spain

I have mentioned before - how the team in Spain love to party - almost any excuse. Usually when I'm in Spain in the summer, we will have a team building event.. on the beach in a chiquito with plenty of food and drink. For some reason, this time the team wants to use my villa for a pool party.. haha, it should be fun. Last time we did that, I was pushed fully clothed in the pool.. and the culprit has never been found. They are coming over later.. wish me luck.

Tomas and his family are also here in Spain (he is supposed to be on holiday) - and yesterday, having launched the NEW Dropshipping site in Slovakia.. Raul came down to join us in Spain. 

So the old team all together.. and due at my house shortly.

Meanwhile in the UK..

We have a massive summer sale underway.. see details below.

And Holly has been getting touchy feely with the felt coasters and other Nepal felt products. She is asking if you can sell this?

More details below..

Please subscribe to our YouTube channel and leave a comment (some feedback about the Nepal mats would be great), then DM us on Instagram, and we will send you a free shipping voucher* for your next order. More Info here.

So let's not complain.. Hope you have a wonderful weekend.

More updates next week. 


David

title: Sound of bells on the holy mountain.
categories: Silver | Bali | ancient wisdom | Eat Love Pray | Ubud
content_html:
Just wanted to add some old posts from my newsletters, that were popular..


Anyway Bali, was pretty disappointing at first glance, my appointed agent, called Ringo met me at the airport and took me to a business hotel close by.  I have seen the film "Eat, pray, love" and this place looked nothing like the idyllic place that Julia Roberts seemed to float around. Some dodgy bars, a few very drunken Australian youngsters and scruffy shops selling magic mushrooms. Worse, when I stepped outside to explore, big well fed rats seemed to run free in the drains by the road.

It was still early evening so Ringo took me to the local wholesale market area, a cramped street lined with open fronted stores claiming to be exporters. I checked a few out and was not particularly impressed, although some beach jewellery  looked pretty cool. Ringo explained to me that the real production area for handicrafts was about an hour and half away. I went to bed not feeling particularly enthusiastic.

Next morning, as we headed out of the city, Ringo explained to me that Bali has a huge craft industry, which has been shaped in part by collaborations with Australian importers. Australia is only a short flight from here, and from the tourist industry has sprung a cool and designer lead gift industry. We started to climb to higher ground, past beautiful rice terraces, and Ringo told me about Ubud. 
Ubud is the craft zone, beyond the town of Ubud is Ubud mountain. The mountain is the market. 

As you climb up the mountain, on each side of the road are craft showrooms, each are specializing in different items, we passed a village of stone carvings, then wood carvings, then a row of outlets selling colorful kites, next a glass blowing area, then wooden recycled furniture, then bamboo items.. my eyes are like saucers.
Beyond the showrooms are workshops, with products being made to order, beyond the workshops is some of the most beautiful countryside you have ever seen.
We stopped to take in a vista.. two ladies approached selling tourist nic-nacs, Julia Roberts stopped here to take pictures they told me, in good English.
    
That was quite interesting, but what was more interesting was the quality of the goods they were selling, and the prices.

There is so much I could tell you, it would take all day. But to cut a long story short, the main event on Bali is Silver. One of the mountain villages is home to the silver market, buyers come here from all over the world, and it was the main reason I was here. The silver village is quite different, opulent mansions, stunning compounds, one even has Gothic creatures carved in stone rising like a giant angelic host from the roof of a palace like showroom. The silver-smiths of Bali are renown for their craftsmanship, and beautiful intricate designs.  There are big companies here, employing hundreds of artisans producing silver jewellery for the worlds biggest jewellery retailers.

But I'm looking for something quite special. Ubud mountain, the holy mountain, is the home of Angel Calling Bells.. Artisans have been making and blessing small silver clasps containing a sweet sounding brass bell for generations. Wear one and, with a good heart, the chances are you will attract the attentions of good spirits, angels even. On this sacred, stunningly beautiful mountain.. I want to believe.
Outside a modest but elegant house an old lady is placing small bamboo baskets containing incense and small piles of rice as offerings to the Balinese gods. Two or three baskets on the footpath, one in the branches of a tree, several at the foot of an empty stone chair. Each basket is prayed over, an incense stick lit and bell gently chimes to call the spirits and maybe bring good business.
The stone chairs are everywhere in Bali, often dressed in silk, and protected from the hot sun with ornate umbrellas or palm leafs. The hope is spirits will come and sit on the chair.  Sound of silver bells are in the air..
 

These bells have been huge sellers in Spain for the past year or so, and a contact tipped me off to the possible source. In an upper room in the modest house, I meet a family of silversmiths who tell me they produce many designs and yes they sell to a number of Spanish companies. A young couple also customers, Spanish speaking, tell me they sold over nine thousand in one year. interestingly they also told me that the market in UK, France and Germany was just starting. 

They have names, names of angels, and each is craft-made in 925 sterling silver and lovingly detailed. You can wear them like pendents, or just carry them in your purse. Very special, made and blessed on Ubud mountain. A delightful family, only the young son spoke English, but his father and grand-father came to shake my hand. 
A few days later I came back to do the QC checks and found the whole family sat on the floor in a shady courtyard carefully packing and preparing the order. The old lady I had seen making offerings smiles at me warmly like an old friend and offers me a glass of sweet tea.

title: David's AW News: 30 Years!
content_html:
Greetings from the 60th Edition of the IHGF Delhi Fair.


Mr Chatterjee, Toni and I are at the huge Indian bi-anual trade show. It's a big deal because this is the 60th edition.. Actually 30 years of trade shows. It's changed a lot over the years, and many familiar faces, old friends, competitors and the odd fraudsters are here. More than a few read this newsletter.

I have been attending more years than I'm happy to admit. It was here that I met Mr Chatterjee, who became a good friend and our agent.. our Man in India. He is a well known figure in the show.. mostly because he is tall, towering above most other Indians and sports that trademark white flash hair style and always wears the brightest of clothes. I feel a bit like AW and this trade show have grown up together.. see below why.


Last week I was telling you about the noisy city of Varanasi and our search for silk, if you missed it you can catch up here.
But I also found time to make a YouTube video about it.


Thanks for watching and supporting my YouTubes.. (I'd be very happy if you could like, comment and share).  This is still just a hobby for me, I'm not super slick at it, but I quite enjoy making them. I was quite happy (erm excited even) to see the second video I made in Nepal the other week actually kind of go viral.. 190k views.. It was about our visit to Bhaktapur near Kathmandu. We had heard that the Gen Z were planning more protests there.. which I mentioned in the video.. and then the protests happened.. and the algorithm liked that I guess.

After Varanasi.. we took a train to a small city in the middle of nowhere. Between Varanasi and Kolkata. Where we met up with an actual mine owner. A rather exuberant fellow, with a lively young team all absolutely passionate about gemstones.  We wanted to see an actual gemstone mine.. we arrived in the evening and checked in the only hotel in town, which was cheap, dodgy with a damp and dark nightclub on the roof that pumped out thumping Punjabi music - our new mining friend and his team insisted on buying us drinks and food there. We kept asking for the music to be turned down (we were the only guests) so we could talk.. but the DJ kept winding it back up to head banging levels after one soft song. 

The next morning after breakfast with the whole team.. we took two cars and drove out of town.. 20 minutes we understood. But an hour and half drive through actually beautiful countryside, lakes, forests, passing other-wordly rock formations, we began to ask how much further? The road was small but well maintained.. It felt more like central Java in Indonesia than India. 


A strange place and finally we arrived, went off road for a while bumping over a dirt track. Then told us we would need to walk a while.. through a narrow ravine a little flooded in parts but we clambered past. 


We eventually came out into a fairytale scene.. a landscape, a small open cast mine with a small lake in the bottom and the whole area shmiring in the sunlight. Mica shards used in glitter covered ground. Our mining friend picked some up and showed us how the mica slid between fingers and was actually like ice thin sheets of crystal. The mica is cleansed, crushed and sold to cosmetics companies. But amongst the mica deposits are found actual gemstones..  Here just lying amongst the shining rocks we could pick up chunks of brilliant blue Aquamarine, black Tourmaline and chunks of ruby Garnet. Guys armed with nothing more than a trowel and a bucket were collecting gemstones ready for sorting. 

A magical place.. you could feel the gemstone aura.

We were only there a short time.. and the guys chatting on the phone told us we had to leave, the area was being cleared ready for a blasting. Oh I said I want to see.. they said no of course not, they have strict safety procedures. The whole area must be cleared.. so we clambered back out to the cars.  

The mining guy has a government license to mine - he told us he has five such mines. The mica is mined commercially, but the gemstones, almost a by-product, are collected, sorted and taken by truck to Gujeratt on the opposite side of India to the artisan town of Khambat where his brother (he explained) distributes to artisans and they buy back the finished products.. The other day our man and his team checked into a hotel near the tradeshow.. and set up one room like a private trade stand to show off the raw and finished products.. We were impressed!


We have a deal to exclusively sell their production in Europe.. 

Anyway standby for 30 YEARS..
This tradeshow is celebrating.. but across the world of AW we will be soon celebrating another 30 years celebration. Stand by for something special.

Meanwhile in the UK an Indian container just arrived.. Back in stock.. And lots of new items from my previous trip. 

Halloween is so close! Scary close. 
And we have scary deals for you.

I have to go now.. We have finished at the trade show and now. 
Time to go to Goa for a few days. 

Take care. 
Nameste from India 

David

title: 5 Key Retail Trends for 2022
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I hope you had a good Christmas and New Year without too much Omicron disruption.

It's already the 7th day of 2022, here in Spain that is only one day after 3 Kings Day, which is a bit like Christmas day.. so it still feels like the beginning of a new year.
So a good time to plan, to think ahead and figure out where this year will take us.
Last newsletter I was updating you on the international parts of AW.. an update from each location.. if you missed it you can read it here.
A year ago Boris was telling us in his new year message that he had actually "Got Brexit Done!" and that we were going to prosper mightily..  do you remember?
Well a year on and Brexit is still not done, this week further import checks come into place to further disrupt your ability to trade, and did we prosper mightily?
Lets not start the year on a grumble, but try to see the way to make it happen..

Here are some of my retailing trend predictions I have a feeling will emerge this year. 


1. Travel is back on the books..

Hopefully Omicron is as much a solution to the pandemic as it is a problem, and it will give us all antibodies with much less risk and pain. Then the world can move on.. for sure we will want to travel again, so I see travel related gifts making a come back.. think travel diaries, solid travel shampoo or experience vouchers. But pop-up stores and travel location shops may well become super viable as we all start to move again.. 


2. Merging of online and retail stores.. 

Think about QR codes on products displayed, linking to more information, and the option to have it delivered to your home direct, or as a gift to a friend. No need to hump it around town. Think about furniture, all the hassle of getting it in your car etc.. You could tastefully display furniture items in your shop.. and have them all shipped to your customer via a 3rd party drop-shipper.. NB coming to AW soon.


3. Social Marketing.. 

Online marketing was originally eBay, then came Amazon with smarter people realising they need to make their own stores, typically Shopify stores. The savvy used social media to support their online retail efforts. The super savvy paid influences to endorse their products..

That's how it kind of developed, but what if this all gets flipped on it's head.. (And it's happening already in China)  What is it?  Well, think shoppable Instagram posts.. influencers (and this could be you) not just endorsing a product controlling the whole sales process. The backend of the shoppable post is a single page Shopify store (or similar) which feeds the orders to a drop-shipping service that does the fulfilment part of the process. Your market is as big as your followers, and some influencers in China are doing million dollar sales on a weekend.


4. Changing Customer Preferences

I'm not sure I agree with every change in customer preffernce, but wether you do or not it is important to adapt or die. One of the biggest preffence changes I have seen in years is the developing anti-Chinese product trend. Most of the companies we deal with in China are small family concerns with hard working people who don't deserve to suffer. However maybe it is time to rebalance.. as you know at AW we have been making our own UK products and importing from India for 20 years. These days we also import from Nepal, Morroco and more and more Indonesia. 


By the way, two containers just arrived from Indonesia.. see below for back in stock news.


5. Independent Specialists are the new retail champs.

Department stores are dead and almost gone. More and more chain stores are struggling. Town centres across the UK are changing, It's bad, but the flipside is it is creating opportunities for specialist independent retailers. People just love to buy from enthusiastic specialist retailers, and now empty shops at great deals are available to fill the retail gap left by the department store demise. Stores with a sense of experience, engaging their customers and entertaining them are doing great. Couple that with social marketing as above.. and as we start to get out more the independent retailer, I believe  will prosper mightily :)



Hope that's a little food for thought, I hope 2022 is an awesome year for you.

At AW we will be working hard to continue to bring you the best in giftware.. and we have big plans.

Thank you so much for your trade over the last year, and we look forward to working together with you to make the very best of 2022


Take care..


David

title: Jakarta Squid Games & Whisky
content_html:
Greetings from Jakarta

Yes I finally left on a jet plane.. and I'm not really sure when I'll be back again.
I'm in quarantine in the Novotel Hotel not far from Jakarta airport, when I get out the next stop is Bali.
Last week I was telling you about feeling quite emotional about leaving Spain and a party we had in the office.. you can read about it here..

Seven nights, eight days they told me.. quarantine in solitary confinement. They took my passport away from me andI had to sign a letter to say I understood and agreed to the rules. No leaving the room, no outside food or drink deliveries, no visitors and ..break any of these rules and you will be eliminated.. The last one a joke.. 
So I had to make a survival plan. A daily routine to get me through. I packed a bottle of Black Label whiskey and figured it would last me 8 days.  Squid Games on Netflix, I had read so much about the hit series that I thought now was a good time to watch it - one episode, one glass of whiskey a day. I also exercised every morning using an app, sit ups, skipping without a rope, plank etc. and the other thing is to keep a diary..
Here it is..as you will see things didn't quite pan out as I thought...

Quarantine blog Jakarta

Day Zero - Saturday 9th October

I arrived at Jakarta International Airport in the early evening after travelling forever in a mask. Malaga to Amsterdam to Singapore to Jakarta. Now I need to spend 8 days in quarantine before going to Bali. But first I have to go through the Airport. We are taken to a holding room and told to social distance by security guards. It's a long wait but finally in groups of four people we are waved to a row of registration desks and issued with an official QR code. All the staff are in hazmat suits and goggles but still manage to be friendly and polite. Then to another area where vaccine certificates and PCR tests are inspected. Then a health scan, then to a PCR test area with nurses in tented off rooms. Ouch that swab right back of the nose into the brain..

Then more scanning of the QR code..finally allowed to go to passport control. They need to see my visa, quarantine hotel booking,return flight.. then collect my luggage next to the hotel pickup zone, QR code scanned again. There is someone waiting for me. Welcome to Jakarta Mr David.. I have to have a picture taken with the guy holding my passport. He pockets my passport and hands me a receipt for it apologising and assures me it will be returned on departure from the hotel. I have just given my passport to some guy just because he is wearing an armband with the name of my hotel on it. As I follow him to the taxi stand I notice large signs saying: "Beware of quarantine scams" - OMG what does it mean. 

This guy has my passport.
  
Then he puts me in a taxi to the Novotel which is about a 30 minutes drive. I'm happy to be in Indonesia!

Passing Indomart local stores, street food vendors, this is Asia. Yes, I'm truly back in asia! At the hotel, no grand lobby entrance for me, we are directed to a dank underground car park where a makeshift lobby for quarantine arrivals has been set up on bench tables.  After checking in and a small friendly lecturer I'm taken to my prison cell erm room.

It's actually quite a nice suite with lots of space and a view to the swimming pool.

On the bathroom window is a hand painted message..Welcome Mr David to Novotel, we hope you enjoy your quarantine. Stay safe!

There is also an elephant in the room. 

Minutes later my evening meal arrives.. it's looks like very good food and lots of it. Beef rendang, pasta and some purple sauce.. 

Day One - Sunday 10th

Jet lagged. I actually couldn't sleep until 3am, woken up by a breakfast delivery. Huge omelette sausages and hash browns,  a heaped bread, coqusants and a toast basket to feed me for the week plus a platter of exotic fruits. Fresh coffee was all I needed but what else is there to do but eat?

I called Ringo on WhatsApp. He was beyond delighted to see me, laughing and crying. They are just loading a container and I have to say Hi to all the staff one by one.

Evening meal is Indonesian food and really good,  

My PCR test results from the airport haven't come as promised. The checking in guy said it would be slipped under my door.

Glass of whiskey and.. “Netflix and chill”.. Time for.. Squid Games E1


Day Two - Monday 11th

4am still wide awake. Jet lag is worse when you are locked up because I have no sense of time. At least today from the afternoon here -  the UK and Europe offices are open so that will keep busy rather than dropping off to sleep.

9.15am I'm vaguely aware of a knocking noise.. I stumble out of bed, grab my mask and open the door..fresh coffee being delivered. Selamat Pagi Mr David. Good morning.. I mumble in just a mask and pants

 Breakfast, everything that comes is wrapped in clingfilm.

Lots of emailed suggestions for Indonesian products from customers, I work through them adding the best to my hit list. Thank you everyone!!

And it's very busy, everything happening on several fronts. So by the time I'm done it's after 11pm local time and I feel ready to sleep, jet-lag be gone!

The PCR test has still not come so I call reception asking to check where it is. No problem they will find and send it up.

Time to sleep.Still no sign.

Problem is can’t sleep damn Jet-lag body and brains confused. A glass of whiskey helps, but Squid Games is giving me nightmares - maybe it’s a bad idea to fill my lonely head with that dystopian stuff in a dystopian quarantine.


Day Three -Tuesday 12th

Only flipping Tuesday!

Wake up early and try to exercise. I'm eating too much and not burning anything. Plus only breathing air conditioning air. I switch it off for some peace and quiet but the room temperature soon drifts up to 30c .. last night I woke up in a pool of sweat.

I'm beginning to understand what solitary confinement feels like.  Face to face contact is almost zero just a few seconds of social distanced drop off of meals. I'm more hungry for the human contact than the food.

There is a connecting door to the next suite, the sort that has a lock on each side. I can hear the sound of Chinese television, and consider unlocking my door and pushing and saying hello to my fellow quarantine victim next door. This afternoon the guy (I heard him talking) unlocked his side and rattled the door..

By 8pm my eyes are closing, but folks in the UK office keep whatsapping me. Please leave me alone and let me sleep.. If I sleep at least Wednesday will come quickly.


Day Four - Wednesday


Another day in solitary.  I wake up 5am, wide awake. The jetlag is still messing with my body.

Not hungry but waiting for breakfast mostly for a bit of interaction with a human.

What they do is bring a stand with the breakfast tray on it, knock on the door and stand back against the opposite wall while I help myself and bring the previous tray of used plates and cups out.. We chat both masked up.. I try a little of my limited Indonesian, and my breakfast delivery man is so happy to chat. We manage to communicate.

I'll be so glad to get out of here.

Still don't have my airport covid test results, I think it must have been lost. I hope this doesn't hinder my exit process. Spend the evening checking out luxury villas with pools and all the amenities. Ridiculously cheap prices,it seems any money is welcome. At least when I get to Bali I can live in luxury for half the price of a travel lodge.

E4 - things are getting wild.

As I fall asleep I think to myself...I'm halfway there. Four gone, four more to go.


Day Five - Thursday

Dring dring.. I'm woken early by the phone ringing. Still almost asleep I answer.

Good morning Mr David, I'm calling to tell you the new government regulation.

Different thoughts run through my brain.. have they closed the border again? Is the period extended?

Mr David, I want to know if you'd like to take the PCR test today? because the quarantine period has been reduced to five days. When you have the result you can check out, which means you can leave tomorrow.

Wow that's good news! Yes please, yes of course.

I put the phone down and thought.. Ah..well I just need to change the flight from Jakarta to Bali.. this proved to be impossible, so I decided to just book another flight, also impossible because the airlines don't accept credit cards less than 48 hours before the flight. So I called Ringo (our agent in Indonesia)..

Yes he could book for me..

There are very few flights and from what I could see online most were sold out. So slightly stressful.

While I'm waiting for Ringo to book, there is a knock on the door. I open the door to two PPE clad ladies giggling uncontrollably. I'm not sure why they find a disheveled Englishman so funny. "Your test sir" waving the kit under my nose. Between them they had very little English and my Indonesian is rudimentary.. I wanted to know how long the test was good for? For the purpose of flying in case Ringo didn't secure a ticket for the next day. I had to fly tomorrow, they told me. I asked if they could come back in an hour.. no not possible,  now or never. Just then Ringo called - To tell me the ticket is booked.

Breathing a sigh of relief I said "OK ladies I said let's do it". They asked me to bring a chair out of the room into the corridor, I sat down while they did that thing, digging around deep up the nostrils tickling my brain again.  Ouch.. enough is enough.

When will I get the result? I ask.

Later this evening sir,  we'll put it under your door.


As I write this it's 11pm and it has not come yet. What is it with missing test results?

Nothing to do but binge watch the rest of Squid Games and drink the rest of the Black Label - I know from experience they don’t let you carry opened bottles in your luggage. Can’t waste it :)


Day Six - Friday

Wake up this morning early.. Check for my result under the door.. It’s not there. Oh bugger.

I call reception asking if I can check out, and where is my PCR result?.. Don’t worry sir we have it here - just come to reception and check out as normal.

You mean I can just walk out of the room.. A free man?

Wow.. that is strange. I’m free to leave! And yet strangely I feel compelled to stay.. a bit like those contestants in the squid games.
I pack my luggage and head down to the lobby. There is almost no-one around. 
A young lady at the desk seems to be expecting me.. she has my Passport, PCR test, and a letter from the hotel to say I have done quarantine.
One more thing, she asks for my credit card. I think I have paid, I tell her. No sir we owe you a refund of two days, I need to process it.
Wow things are looking up.

I'm writing this now in the Blue Sky lounge at the airport - I couldn't find the check in desk for my flight so I thought I would ask in the lounge. 
No problem sir, the young lady on the desk said, please give me your passport and covid papers. I will go and check you in, you can relax.
Half an hour later she found me in the lounge, and handed me my papers and passport and a boarding card.
Well that never happened in Manchester airport.

Next stop is Bali. News has reached our suppliers, my whatsapp is filling up with messages - Welcome to Bali sir.. when are you coming to visit us?
Full update next week.

Take care

David

title: Stormy Weather Ahead
content_html:
Greetings from Spain where I am being lashed by Storm Philomena.

As I type I can see huge Atlantic style rollers in the sea below and a howling wind is literally rocking my house, which I feel is not accustomed to such weather and seems to be creaking.. moaning under the strain.

I have never seen extreme weather like this here before. 

Last week I was telling you how we could "prosper mightily" in 2021 you can read it here. 

 

In the UK, storm Brexit is just beginning to bite.  Things are unravelling fast, all our EU shipments are in various stages of limbo as every shipping company is in crisis. 

Dear customer, we have plan A, B and C to deal with this.. we were fully prepared for Brexit. But this Free Trade Deal, it turns out is anything but.. nothing is free as far as I can see.

If you are an EU customer with an order with us (and there are still many orders).. we have all hands on deck sorting out the issues.


I strongly recommend using our EU warehouses for future orders, at least until this storm settles down. AWGifts.eu  (Slovakia) or  AWArtisan.eu (Spain)  

Current shipping update: DPD (the biggest) has halted all shipments until next Wednesday - when it will give us an update. See BBC for details.  Where they describe it as the perfect storm.

Courier Logistics - UK all OK, but Northern Ireland technical problems.

UPS - the online system for uploading customs documents is not correctly working.

DHL & TNT - still seems to be working, and goods sent by them have cleared UK customs, but after that - at this point we don't know what's happened.

 

There may be trouble ahead
But while there's music and moonlight
And love and romance
Let's face the music and dance  

 

That Nat King Cole song comes to mind.. it's the right attitude, do our best and dance.

This Brexit thing is truly awful, it's all coming home to roost..  making the Project fear projections hopeless understatements. I'm sorry I feel strongly with the covid crisis this thing should have been delayed.

When Borris said, lets get Bexit out of the way so we can concentrate on covid it sounded perfectly reasonable. But the Brexit genie just came out of the bottle and there hell to pay, it's far from out of the way. Heck. It's just beginning.

 

OK let's calm down and focus.

Soon, we'll be without the moon
Humming a different tune ..

 

India. oh.. India.. I miss travelling in India so much. This week some long awaited Indian shipments arrived. Including one from a new supplier that Tomas and I discovered deep in the heart of Old Delhi back in early March last year. It brought the memory back to mind.

It seems a world away, a lifetime away. I had been in Indonesia and flown down to Kolkata to meet Tomas, with Mr Chatterjee we had gone upto Delhi to see some existing suppliers and check out some new ones. Coronavirus was already serious, but in Delhi just breaking news at that time. That day we arranged to meet Kamran outside a shop near the Red Fort, then we followed him deep into the depths of Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar. Teaming with people all going about their business, street food vendors, cows , rickshaws, people on bikes.. then through an ancient arch down a rabbit hole of tiny lanes. I remember feeling uneasy, it was a hot sunny day with a surprising blue sky. But the worry that covid could be easy lurking here occupied our minds. 

This was an area of Delhi that I had not explored before, a giftware zone as well. Surprisingly tidy and lots of wholesale showrooms full of esotic and esoteric items. Later we came back to explore and discovered some interesting people and things.




As we followed, the lanes got narrower, twisted and turned. We followed for quite a way, so I started taking pictures in case we had to find our own way out of the maze. Eventually we arrived at the company go-down, a back street warehouse crammed with brass artifacts. A narrow entrance was dominated by huge brass tigers, and then we followed him up at least five flights of stairs, each level containing a different type of stock. One floor all decorative padlocks, another brass singing bowls, another Indian gods of every deity. Finally on the top floor a room full of brass Buddahs of every size, pose and decor. Kamran explained that he commissioned and bought work from a range of artisans, some of them Tibetan exiles who produced designs handed down generations. In his workshop area workers cleaned polished, finished and packed for export all over the world.  



It was most of a day's work but we selected a range, asked for some redesigns and placed an order. Refreshingly Kamran was very honest, he told us it would take at least four months to make this order as the artisans could only make so many pieces a day. And true to his word the order was produced on schedule, but by then India was in solid lockdown, and nothing could be shipped. Lots of things happened between then and now, but finally the shipment came. 

 

I miss India, traveling with Tomas and Mr Chatterjee. I miss dealing with gentle guys like Kamran, I would love to go back to Chawri Bazar, and explore those back lanes some more. Ah.. one day.

But for now.. we have to face the music and dance..



That should lift your mood!!

 

Meanwhile, lot's of Indian stock is back online.. 

And if you feel the need to support the artisans of old Delhi,

Stay safe and dream of better days.

More updates next week.

 

David

title: David's AW News: Run like the wind.
content_html:
Greetings (again) from Bali..

Yes, back in Bali. Last week I was telling you about our Mooncake overload in China and our trip to a lonely mountain village. If you missed it you can catch up here.
Coco and I took a China Southern flight from Yiwu to Guangzhou, with a short transit time onward to Bali. Always a risk, but no choice because these days there are not so many flights out of China.

Of course, after we boarded the plane the captain announced a one hour delay which turned into two hours. Yiwu is a military airport and if they decide to use it for exercises..  then you're buggered. Window blinds down, your strictly not allowed to look outside, but they served us snacks (and even a cold beer) while we waited. We resigned ourselves to missing the connection in Guangzhou to Bali and assumed we would be on the next day's flight. 
The plane landed and the air hostess told us that they are going to help us make the connection but we would need to run like the wind. There were other passengers making the same connection, and as we got off the plane someone was waiting with a list of names. They slapped blue dots on us, to give us superpowers to pass quickly..  Instead of entering the terminal we had a mini bus on the tarmac that took us to the right terminal directly and even by-passed security. We still needed to clear immigration which fortunately had no queues. At the otherside staff were waiting and urging us to run.. like spectators in a marathon. Run, run, run...


We were running and laughing, not really expecting to make it. Last time this happened in Athens airport, we arrived too late. 
But we made it with seconds to spare, they closed the door right after we boarded. "Well done guys" the air steward said cheerfully, "you made it - you're on the way to Bali".  Then told us that our luggage would not be there. We had to just go and give the baggage handling office our hotel address.  After we landed in Bali and cleared immigration, which these days is easy because we have businesses there and what they call; kittas papers, there is a VIP channel on the right hand side of the hall. We went to the lost luggage office, and filled in the forms. Where we got a personal apology for the delayed luggage and.. "could you just sign this receipt" I asked what it was for? "This.. " she said and counted out one million Indonesian rupiah each! Cash compensation on the spot. That's about £100 in total. Wow.. you don't get that with Ryanair. Coco was so happy!
I don't know why but this year, but that's the forth or fifth time me or Coco has lost luggage.in transit. I learned that you don't need to worry - the lost luggage always always turns up.  Sure enough it arrived at our hotel on the second day.

Tomas and Raul arrived in Bali the next day.. it's the reason we are here.. Peter the PPC marketing wizard from Slovakia is already here. We have a summit meeting with the Digital Marketing team. And together we can power forward to the next stage. AW-Advantage.com is taking shape and we already have a few customers, other than the AW group.  Regular readers will know we (almost) by accident bought an abandoned beach bar, not far from our warehouse and turned it into a super cool work space, yards from the crashing surf. 

We came bearing gifts.. mostly Mooncakes (see last week's news) but also Coco brought personally made Manifestation Bracelets for all the marketing team. 
Which they really seemed to appreciate.. 


It seems the beach office is working great, we have had zero staff turnover these last three months, and a super dedicated team of young bright people. They start early and often have to be turfed out of the office at night. At the moment we have a foundation team of 15 people.. when we are ready we can expand step by step. If you are interested in using the team to supercharge your online businesses.. drop us a line, we are only taking on a very small customer base right now, because we are still a small team and our USP is that here in Indonesia we can give your business lots more of the careful analytical attention than you could possibly get from a UK or EU agency. Contact Form here.. we will be happy to take a look at your web-site and see if we can actually add value, and if we can then we can quote you. My bottomline is that any investment in digital marketing should (if your product is good) earn a 10X return in the medium term. But there are a lot of factors in the mix, every business is different. But if you have an online business you have nothing to lose by clicking here.

AND SO IT CONTINUES... stuff just keeps relentlessly arriving.. I'm so excited to see the Raw Crystals have arrived. These are the next big thing... elemental simple rock crystals.. you can do endless things with them.. the Crystal Enchantment Lights are made with them and selling (out) fast.. The (just arrived) beautiful Chakra Crystal Candles use them and will sell out fast also..  You can sell them at big profit just in pick and mix mode.. or you can get creative.. or your customers can get creative.   There are endless things you can do with them.. I asked ChatGBT and the list was too long to fit here ...  (you can check yourself). Anyway we have them!! 
More things below...

Here in Bali it is hot.. and dry.. last time I was here in October it was rainy season.. but hot is good, because many things need to be dry before we can export them. 
I'm here at the warehouse, working with Ringo and today they are taking advantage of the heat to sun dry the Wooden Buddhas a bit more before packing them. That's another product that always sells out faster than we can get made. 
A beautiful gift at Christmas.. we have some stock.. but you need to run.


Christmas is coming.. it's time to get organised..

Yiwu is a military airport and if they decide to use it for exercises.. then you're buggered. Window blinds down, your strictly not allowed to look outside, but they served us snacks (and even a cold beer) while we waited. title: Bringing more to the Table..
content_html:
Greetings from Spain,
Last week I was asking where the very British saying "Dog's Breakfast" comes from.. you can read about here.
I arrived last week and have been working hard on a few projects that hopefully will sky rocket your business with AW.
Always we are looking for the next great product.. those products don't just magic themselves up, they are always the result of hard work by a team of people.
Designers, producers, agents, creative types and a bit of speculative entrepreneurship.. to make amazing things happen you need collaboration.. you need team work.
So aneighbourpened my old friend and neighbor in Spain was in residence, so we went for dinner to catch up. Allen is a Danish millionaire mad inventor, an engineer by profession and a Harrison Ford lookalike.
Also a lovely humble guy with very thoughtful views on the world. We got talking about Brexit - of course - he told me Danish people are not big fans of Brussels but the benefits of collaboration clearly outstrip any downside.
The whole world instinctively takes the view that closer collaboration brings better results and general improvements. The whole world (in my experience) is looking at the UK in a kind of fascinated shock, the same way you might view a guy on the 20th floor threatening to jump. Why would you do that..? it's self harm.
Allen told me they have a saying in Denmark, people who bring more to the table, benefit everyone and in the end themselves even more. I like the visual picture of.. Bringing more to the Table.. Humans collaborating generously and unselfishly thus creating a better world.
But, I asked Allen.. What happens when you are the one collaborating, bringing more to the table.. and someone else (a business partner for example) is taking more and taking advantage of that situation. Some people are good at this, we have all come across them, able to present an image of trustability whilst simultaneously taking advantage.. but it can only work for so long before it breaks down and ends in tears.
Different industries attract different people, the Gift Trade - I believe - mostly attracts nice people, kind people, we are in the business of giving.. the act of giving, is nothing short of love.. it's a privilege to be in a business that enables other humans to give a gift, a gift is after all an act of love. Maybe the engineering business attracts more hard-nosed types - I don't really know. But Allen's advice is it's better to get those who take from the table out of your life sooner rather than later, hack them out like a cancer, chop them off, no mercy.. he says. Give back to those who are bringing more to the table.
Mmmm, I say to Allen, I just don't find it easy to do that.. what about forgiveness, second chances..?

I wish I could describe the look on his face.. I'll let you imagine...
Meanwhile.. It's almost Easter. Spring is in the air.. it is the Season of Love. And we have lots of fresh deals for you.. lots of new products.
Check out the deals below.
It's been a week of "B" words.. the Buzz words this week all start with "B".. and they are all kinda related..
Brexit
Brussels
Black Hole
Bringing more to the Table..
I bet you can think of a few more..
Have a great weekend, lots of love and laughter!
David

title: Candle Factory Closed By Heat
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China. Last week I was telling you about how confusing the names are in Bali. You can read it here: By George that's Confusing. In China today, temperatures are just subsiding after some violent storms. Earlier it was the hottest and most humid in this region's history. Yiwu was stonking hot. In the 40's.. and even with air conditioning you seem to end up a sweaty mess by the end of the day, clothes like sodden rags. It's been so hot we have had to suspend candle production in our little factory, because the wax is behaving so strangely.
Yes, the massage candles from our factory just landed. I can tell you they were a huge job. To get the product perfect we had to ship essential oils from the UK, source the very best brand soywax in China and spent weeks perfecting the blends and designing the packaging. But the response is worth it.. I'm really pleased to see so many people enthusiastic.
Plus I think Tomas in marketing at HQ Sheffield has done a great job with the web pages. Any feedback, tips or ideas on how to retail or use in spa's or therapy sessions - that we can share - would be appreciated.
Talking about Bali (where the weather is always barmy and equitable), I'm pleased to report that our new little warehouse (you may have read previously) in Yellow Coconut Village near Ubud is in full swing.
Ringo (our agent) sent me pictures yesterday..
It's great because now our suppliers - who are all small family businesses can bring finished stock as they make it, and we can pay them faster. Another advantage is that since no artisans pack the goods in cartons for export, we can now do this job ourselves (rather than the local shipping agents, who charge way too much) and ensure that quality is good at the same time.
Before you ask.. there is a container enroute, arrives possibly next week.. and yes there are Hati Hati Angels on board.
Hati Hati - means take care in Indonesian.
So until next week - I'll be in India..
Hati Hati!

title: Escaping China, Coco Lands in Bali
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

The big news is that Coco, my wife (and your AW China agent), escaped from China and arrived in Bali.. It has been almost two and half years (900 days) since I said goodbye to Coco in Malaga airport thinking I would see her in China after a trip to India. But whilst I was in India in February 2020 the covid cloud descended on the world and the world changed. Coco's escape from China was a little dramatic.. details below.
Last week I was updating you about what's happening with AW suppliers here in Indonesia. If you missed it you can catch up here.

Coco has been working hard in China.. non stop really. Organising continued supplies, working with the family businesses that supply AW in very difficult times.. she needed a holiday. The zero-covid system in China makes it very hard to travel even between cities and to go outside China is made almost impossible. For one thing there are almost no flights out of China, and the ones that operate are eye wateringly expensive. They really don't want the locals to leave..  Getting a Schengen visa to visit Europe Coco was told was impossible as all the visa offices had been closed in China, so it was not possible to come to Europe. The only possible plan was to meet in Asia. In Bali it would be ideal to mix business with a reunion. I scanned google flights everyday to try and find a route, checking from every city in China, very strange results would come up.. Like if you search from Shanghai to Kuala Lumpur, it would only route you through Guangzhou with a long stop over, so I would try to book direct from Guangzhou but would only show routes via another China city. Very strange. 
I had seen videos on YouTube showing people being turned away from airports, passports even being cut so they couldn't be used - holiday travel strictly discouraged, visiting family was not considered a valid reason to travel. Only business travel could possibly be allowed.
When I mentioned all this to Coco, she didn't believe, fake-news - she said, of course we can travel.. why not? 

I had an idea.. I could apply for an Indonesia Business Visa for Coco.. this would validate her trip as for business.. which it partially is. Then on the Malaysia Airlines website by searching consecutive dates I worked out that there were one way flights you could book about every ten days or so to KL.. one of these days coincided with a flight from KL to Bali.. This meant that Coco could get a connecting flight, luggage straight through without having to enter Malaysia and avoid any complications.. I also knew (from YouTube) that China passport control would ask to see return tickets.. this is an impossible task - whatever I tried return flights were routing around the world, $20,000 or both.. The system was stacked.   But then I found Airasia had just started selling tickets from KL to Hong Kong in September (at a reasonable price), so I booked one of those hoping that would be good enough to show as a return ticket to China.
Coco didn't believe there would be a problem.. In China news or on social media the subject of international travel was a big fat blank space. 

There are four flights a day from Yiwu to Guangzhou international airport.. Coco booked the first, even if that meant waiting 8 hours for the Malaysia Air flight.. But it was a good job she did because the flight was cancelled, and auto rebooked on a later flight, which was then delayed three times.. from having an 8 hour window to less than 3 hours, Coco was starting to get a little stressed, many other passengers had already missed their international flights.. 
On arriving in Guangzhou, Coco messaged me she had to take a covid test on the tarmac, before being allowed in the terminal..  more delay.
From domestic arrivals to International departures is a short walk, and she was able to grab her luggage and get to Malaysia Air check-in in time.. she messaged me all was ok.

Now she had only to pass through passport control, security check and then to the gate.. 
But then there was a new check.. Police control.. a policeman checked her tickets and asked her which province of China she came from. Ok he said you will have to be interviewed by the police force of that province. Apparently there were police from every province in China stationed in the airport.. Jiangxi province policemen came to ask questions.. "What is your reason to travel?'' they asked, a little flustered and stressed Coco said without thinking... "Holiday". - "In that case" they said "you will have to turn around right now and go home"..  
Coco remembering what I had told her quickly changed track.. sorry sorry, I mean business.. I have an Indonesian business visa, business ticket.. and showed them. Still not happy, they demanded proof that she was a business person, so Coco fortunately had company documents in her name for AW China on her phone.  Very reluctantly they let her pass.
Four hour flight to Kuala Lumpur, eight hours connection, no trouble at all, three hours to Bali..

And so that's how Coco escaped China and arrived in Bali.. 


900 days is a long time.. and I was expecting things to be a bit strange.. but it was like no time had passed. 
So happy to see my wife again.. this week seems a little unreal.. 
For Coco very strange.. no need to wear a mask, no need to get tested every 72 hours, no stress over your phone covid-passport turning red.. a taste of freedom.


Back together in Bali..
Coco posted a simple video of us having breakfast in Ubud on the China version of Instagram and was amazed to see it go viral within minutes.. I hope she doesn't get in trouble in China for having a holiday..
Yesterday we visited some factories and discussed exporting Indonesian products to China.. I said you need to post online also..  she did.. so far it didn't go viral..

In other news..
There is a G20 foreign ministers meeting in Bali this week. The airport is all prepared for VIP arrivals.. one of which was Liz Truss.


Indonesian foreign minister greets Liz Truss, who stayed only a few hours before deciding to return to London.. 
Locals are not impressed, apparently world peace and food security are less important than London politics. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. Indonesia and China containers arriving.. so actually whole swathes of things are back in stock..
It's all going a bit crazy .. some big selling gemstone items, Power bracelets etc back in stock, I recommend grabbing stock while you can.

Next week the plan is we go to Java, to a stone carving village that our man Bondhan has discovered.. should be interesting..

Take care.

David

title: Tea & the Queen in Slovakia
content_html:
Greetings from Slovakia

Yes, I'm in the pretty town of Trnava, not far from Bratislava. Home of AWGifts.eu our newest and smartest warehouse and offices.


It's an absolute and total delight to be here!! I'll tell you why below.
Last week I was in Spain, doing what I do best, and that's taking the team out to a nice meal and having a party. Well they deserve it, this year Toni and his team have done amazing things and since I was there.. I was telling you; things in Spain were getting hot.. much too hot.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
From Spain I met up with Erika (our manager in Slovakia) and her family - who had been on holiday in Spain and we travelled back together. A flight from Malaga to Vienna on Lauda airways. It was very turbulent and we landed with an almighty crunch, those planes are quite old I think. From Vienna a taxi took us to Bratislava airport, and Tomas met us there..  

It was Saturday and lunchtime so since we were near Bratislava we went into town for lunch. As we walked across town in the central park a big event was taking place with a concert by lots of young people dressed in pink, singing theme songs from the new Barbie movie. We stopped to watch, and a TV reporter and camera crew approached us and basically interviewed Tomas for a vox-pop opinion piece. He was quite thrilled, now he thinks he is going to be famous..


We went for lunch by the Danube river, to discuss his new media career :)

It's been a while since I was in Slovakia and I was eagerly awaiting Monday morning when we would go to AWGifts and meet the full team. 
Regular readers will know that in Spain our team is full of fun, hardworking but always up for a party.. whilst here in Slovakia they are hardworking, industrious and always up for a.. a long serious discussion.. Haha it's just the way it is.
As much as I try I can't get the party started.. 
Anyway today I'm taking the managers for a thank you lunch..


Actually I couldn't be more proud of the team here and what they have achieved. In just a few years we outgrew our first warehouse and moved in one massive leap and a bound from a 1000 sq meter warehouse to a 8000 sq meter super modern distribution warehouse. A lot of diligent hard work by the team here, and lots of websites developed - in every european language - it's a major achievement..



Tomas and I have this tradition of exploring the charming town centre after work and finding a nice restaurant to dine in. Despite its small size, the town has good dining options. Yesterday, we ended up an old favorite called Pizza Kitty. It has been serving the locals since Tomas was a kid and has become a beloved establishment in town. The restaurant itself is quite impressive, spread across various rooms in a historic building. However, with the summer heat, all the action has moved outside where the outdoor seating area is pretty busy. And since Tomas is a well-known figure in town, he's often greeted by old friends. Trnava has a thing about art, so it's not unusual to stumble upon an art installation or exhibition. Yesterday, near Pizza Kitty, we discovered an exhibition dedicated to the Queen's visit to Slovakia in 2008 - it was interesting! 


I'm not a royalist or otherwise, but the idea that someone thought it good to celebrate this event 15 years ago - today on a street in Slovakia. Connecting Slovakia to the UK. Somehow seems both incongruous and heart warming.  

And back in UK.. lots of stock arriving in the warehouse. Lots back in stock. (see below)
And I'm sooooooooo excited to see Gemstone Tea Strainers!  Believe me heaps of work went in to bringing you this gem of a gift. A gift for both gemstone and tea loving folk.. so the best of two worlds. You can display and sell in your Gemstone Dept and your Tea Department.. The product is absolutely beautiful. But check out the packaging.. (by Sandra our talented designer). A five sided pyramid box, with silver foil print, embossed and with details about what the gemstone is for. (Coco made that packaging happen).  And the product matches and compliments the  Crystal Glass Tea Infuser Bottles. Well done guys! See below.. truely (as it says on the box) a mystical tea experience. 

Anyway onwards.. I arrived here on Lauda airways, and I'm leaving on Eva Airways shortly. I never really heard of either of those airlines. 
Eva Airways should be an interesting experience. And you might ask where am I off to? 
I'll report on both of those things next week.

Have a wonderful weekend!
Thank you once again for your support.

Take care
David
