title: David's AW News: Flirting with Danger in Mijas
content_html:
Hello again from a very, very hot Friday...

Hope you are enjoying the weather wherever you are!

It is hotter than ever across the UK and Europe, and here at AW, our Midsummer Madness Season is going out with a bang—quite literally, like the San Juan fireworks lighting up Andalucía this week. Meanwhile, Coco and I have been flirting with danger in peaceful, quaint Mijas. 


We still have a swathe of 30% off deals, but they are disappearing quickly now, so please do have a look before the madness finally melts away.

Last week, I was telling you about the good news on my Spanish TIE card and how I was finally close to being properly documented again. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

Well, this week the card arrived — and nearly disappeared again on the very same day. More on that little drama below...

Meanwhile, a container from Bali arrived at our Malaga warehouse, and I was there to see it being unloaded. Always a satisfying moment, but also a slightly worrying one. As any Indonesian importer will tell you, extreme heat and artisan products are not always best friends.

Heat and humidity can be a real problem. Damp can creep in. Mould can appear. Wood can swell, crack, warp or smell musty. Natural products are beautiful because they are natural, but that also means they need care, skill and a lot of boring behind-the-scenes work before they arrive looking lovely on your shelves.

Of course, we use superdry pads on the inside walls of the container, and little sachets inside many products. But even then, problems can still happen. Our man in Indonesia, Bondhan, together with James in the UK, has literally been sweating over this problem for the past year.

We have tried everything. Honestly, there is nothing on the internet, or even from AI, that gives a perfect answer to this one. But I am hopeful we may finally have stumbled on a solution — a combination of measures rather than one magic trick.

A new brand of superdry that claims to be 400% better. A little device we found in the China store — trade secret, sorry. And now a machine that checks the humidity of every product at the point of loading. It has to sit between two carefully tested points before it goes in.

It has been hard work. Lots of trials, lots of head scratching, lots of “why is this still happening?” moments. But finally, on one of the hottest days we have seen, a container arrived dry, clean and sweet.

Well done, Bondhan, James and everyone involved. This is the sort of invisible work that customers never see, but it makes all the difference.

And then came San Juan.

All across Andalucía, people were on the beaches until the early hours, jumping over bonfires, watching fireworks, making wishes, and generally proving once again that Spain knows how to party properly.

The next morning, at 9.30am, I had my appointment to collect my ID card from the notoriously grumpy Marbella Police Station. After San Juan night, I did wonder if anyone would actually turn up. But this is Spain — they can party all night and still go to work looking sharp.

After hanging around outside with the waiting crowd until my name was called, badly pronounced, of course, I was ushered through by possibly the coolest and best-dressed police officer I have ever seen. Very Marbella. Then a very smart policewoman in shades processed the papers, handed over my card, and that was that.

Outside, I checked the expiry date and nearly did a little dance. Ten years. I had expected three, hoped for five, and somehow got ten. Result.

So later, Coco and I went up to Mijas Pueblo, the beautiful whitewashed village on the mountainside above where we live. We were wandering around, just enjoying the views, when we found an alleyway we had not seen before. It snaked around the outside of some old buildings, with dramatic views on one side, leading towards a park and the bullring.

Then suddenly — splat.

Both Coco and I felt something horrible land on us. Massive bird poo, or so it seemed.

Immediately, a kindly old man rushed over with water and tissues, very concerned, offering to help. He started tugging at my shirt, trying to get me to take it off so he could clean it over the railings. Then a younger guy also appeared, ready to help.


And that is when every alarm bell in my head started ringing.

I said to Coco, “Hold your bag tight,” and put my hand in my pocket and held on to my wallet — the wallet containing my brand new Spanish ID card.

I muttered to Coco - This is a scam.  And just like that, they vanished.

AI recreated the scene for me. Amazing, the helpful guy was EXACTLY like that!

Later, I asked AI, and yes, we had apparently been treated to the classic “Mustard Scam”. Something messy is sprayed or splattered on you. A helpful stranger appears with tissues and water. You are distracted, uncomfortable, embarrassed, and suddenly there are hands near your pockets, bag, belt or phone.

I can imagine this happening in the back streets of Old Delhi or Paharganj. But in fragrant, peaceful, whitewashed Mijas Pueblo? Wow.

Thankfully, nothing was taken. My wallet stayed exactly where it was. The new TIE card survived its first day in the wild.

Later, sitting in a tapas bar in the square opposite the old bullring, I did reflect on how close it had been. All that effort, all those appointments, all the paperwork, all the waiting — and then nearly losing the card to a pickpocket before the ink was even dry.

But maybe that is the lesson of the week.

You can do everything right. You can work hard for a year to keep a Bali container dry. You can navigate Spanish paperwork. You can finally get your precious ID card. And still, life throws something messy at you from above.

The trick is not to panic. Hold on to what matters. Keep your sense of humour. Have lunch afterwards if possible.

So this week I am grateful — for dry containers, sharp police officers, loyal staff, lucky instincts, and tapas in the shade.

And as Midsummer Madness draws to a close, thank you as always for being part of our slightly chaotic, always interesting, never boring AW journey.

Remember to have Hydration Breaks (like in the World Cup).. https://www.instagram.com/p/DZ-Lm6rI9YG/  Rodrigo and crew (in the UK office) are setting a massive trend..

Now, please do grab the last of the 30% off deals before they vanish like two suspiciously helpful strangers in a Mijas alleyway.

Stay Cool - Enjoy the weekend!

David

title: David's AW News: Finally Nepal / Coco arrives
content_html:
Greetings from Kathmandu, Nepal

Yes, Toni and I have just arrived in Nepal. Last week was telling you about our hectic trip across India, ending for a break in Goa. If you missed it you can catch up here.


Before Goa, we spent four hectic days in Jaipur, known as the pink city. It's famous for being on the Golden Triangle (Delhi, Agra, Jaipur) tour and has many iconic sites to see. Unfortunately, Toni sacrificed the sites of Jaipur for factory and showroom visits because Jaipur is also a major handicraft and textile hub in India. We have three existing suppliers in this huge busy city and after visiting them set out to uncover some new suppliers...

Block print textiles are famous in Jaipur.

Last year on holiday in Crete I bought a nice block print shirt in a trendy boutique in Chania. I happened to be wearing it in Jaipur and one supplier told me that the shirt is made in the town, I checked the label and yes it said it was made in India. I'd paid €50 but here wholesale was about 450 Indian rupees. Also in Jaipur are leather products and recycled paper, the latter made from textile cut offs. Combine the two and you get leather notebooks which have been a solid good seller at AW for a number of years. We went to visit our old suppliers and managed to add one new one.

Small workshop making notebooks very much by hand.
Jaipur is also famous for Jewellery: gemstones and diamonds. Although whenever we try to buy in that market we get quoted crazy prices and can't seem to get past the wily middlemen to the genuine artisans.  Nice products but crazy prices. It will take time to uncover the artisans build relationships and do business. I'm trying to explain to Toni that sometimes it takes years to find the best suppliers and many trips to an area. 


One guy admitted that there are plenty of Japanese and Americans on Golden Triangle tours who pay top dollar so there is no incentive to be competitive in an export market.

After Jaipur we took a very early Indigo flight (getting up at 4am) from Goa to Mumbai, then changed for another Indigo flight to Kathmandu. 
I think Kathmandu airport might have had a lick of paint since last time I was here, but it's still an old school airport. The staff are welcoming and friendly but the processes needlessly complicated. It can take over an hour to transit the airport, there is even strangely a hand baggage security check before baggage reclaim. Luggage appeared randomly on any belt and not it seemed the belt on the screen. 
When we finally made it out Mr Padam, our shipping agent and old school gentleman, was waiting for us and drove us to our hotel, he told us an opposite story to India, business is very good - lots of folk come to buy handicrafts in Nepal and he was jolly busy. A story confirmed by the suppliers we met yesterday (our first day here). 

Last night Coco arrived.. on a five and an half hour flight from Jaipur. I went with the hotel car and a driver called Sanjeev to meet her at the airport. A lovely guy, he bought VIP tickets so we could meet inside the airport on comfortable seats, he had a big sign printed with Coco's Chinese name and while we waited asked me lots of questions about Coco and our life - I showed him pictures.  Around midnight she emerged looking fresh and excited and not at all tired. Sanjeev leaps to his feet.. look she's here, she's here!


Today in Kathmandu
Meanwhile back in the UK..

We have an amazing new Hop Hare product launch. Great excitement because this has been under development for a year.. it compliments the Hope Hare Candles (awesome for Easter by the way) and could be your next best seller.. 

More news from the Kingdom of Nepal next week.

Namaste and take care.

David

title: Animals.. They know don't they?
content_html:
Greetings from lock-down in Bali day 14

Happy Easter Weekend.. but it's not is it? It's more of the same. Easter normally a time of Chocolate, family gatherings and trips to Church (for the faithful) is now just a time for quiet reflection. Easter is a time of renewal, and maybe after this terrible virus has done it's worst the world will have a kind of renewal with different values installed. Seems to me that humans as the dominant most powerful creature on earth, abused the position.. killing whales, and animals big and small.. now a thing so small we can't even see it, has this terrible power over us. Ironic no?

Hope you are safe and well, and not going stir crazy. Obviously I'm still here stuck in Bali, learning to adapt, finding ways to keep fit, feed myself, keep occupied. Actually keeping occupied is not a big problem, the day fills up with tasks, and I'm spending more time talking to family and friends than I ever did. Must be the same (but different) for you also. Last week I was telling you how I was almost homeless.. you can read about it here.
I was also asking you what you going to do now? With my suggestion that you invest in your future by building websites and establishing new revenue streams.

Lots of you responded to this with suggestions of ways to build websites.. I'll add the ideas below.
The big news in the UK is that we finally managed to get our own AW Aromatherapy Sanitiser on sale. But not an easy task as everyone and their uncle are looking for the ingredients needed and prices are rocketing. See BBC news on this.

So the past few weeks Alan our able production manager in the UK has been fighting to find the ingredients, fortunately we had stock of bottles and spray tops, essential oils we have ample supplies from long relationships with suppliers who will support us. Alcohol more tricky but he fought the good fight to secure some stock. Tomas was in the factory booting up equipment to get production flowing. There is compliance issues, form filling, red tape galore.. and Alan is keen a perfectionist and ensures that we have a great product.
Tomas (marketing wizard) wanted it to look good. Last night we quietly launched.  I think we broke the internet.. :/  
Well to say demand is high is an understatement. So today I have spent working with Coco in China to secure more bottles and caps, she is fighting to get supplies for us. Pleasantly surprised that even though demand is high the prices are the same as before for the packaging.  For sure we will sell out soon.. but we are all working to bring more asap.

It's peaceful and quiet, its so quiet.. the air feels cleaner. The animals, the birds something about them.. they know. 
In the hotel where I was week before last sitting outside this bird would come and sit near by. We kind of became friends, he was always there - sometimes singing.

 

But maybe I'm going mad.. but in the villa garden I have now, the same bird is coming (well OK could be a different one) but I can hear him singing as I type. He knows..  I'm sure.

Drop-shipping is buzzing - and lots of enthusiastic users are finding ways to sell on-line. 
Here's my recommendations for creating a webshop again..

1. Shopify - probably the most popular these days and we are working on a plugin for this first to streamline AW dropshipping and Shopify. At $29/ month you pretty much get what you pay for but what many people don't realise with Shopify lite, (just $9/month) you can add order buttons to any site even Facebook, and sell stuff everywhere.
2. Squarespace - I have had a little experience with this, and was delighted how easy it is to make a cool website quickly. An eCommerce site starts at £20 / month.
3. Bluepark - this I like because you can add your own payment method in the cart.. meaning you're giving a cut of your sales to the platform. Gets good reviews. From £25 / month
4. Wix - this is cool but budget.. you can pretty much make it do what you want. I have played with it in it's early days and it was good then. From about £10 / month (or even free - but don't do that it's not a cool look)  

and we can add to that..
5.  WordPress  .. One of the oldest website solutions, but still manages to be cool. Lots of plugins.. costs from £20 / month. I understand you might get cheap access via a deal with GoDaddy when you register your domain there.  WooCommerce is a plugin to access the e-commerce - getting complicated no? But many people like it.
6. Jimdo - this one is made in Germany, they have a Coronavirus offer to help small business right now. Use the code: JIMDOHELP when paying to get a huge discount just $1 per month (usually £15 / month). I had a quick look round, it's pretty nice.

Anyway, I wish you a peaceful Easter. Stay Home. Stay Safe. 

David

With my suggestion that you invest in your future by building websites and establishing new revenue streams. Lots of you responded to this with suggestions of ways to build websites.. I'll add the ideas below. The big news in the UK is that we finally managed to get our own AW Aromatherapy Sanitiser on sale. But not an easy task as everyone and their uncle are looking for the ingredients needed and prices are rocketing. See BBC news on this. So the past few weeks Alan our able production manager in the UK has been fighting to find the ingredients, fortunately we had stock of bottles and spray tops, essential oils we have ample supplies from long relationships with suppliers who will support us. Alcohol more tricky but he fought the good fight to secure some stock. Tomas was in the factory booting up equipment to get production flowing. There is compliance issues, form filling, red tape galore.. and Alan is keen a perfectionist and ensures that we have a great product. Tomas (marketing wizard) wanted it to look good. Last night we quietly launched. I think we broke the internet.. :/ Well to say demand is high is an understatement. So today I have spent working with Coco in China to secure more bottles and caps, she is fighting to get supplies for us. Pleasantly surprised that even though demand is high the prices are the same as before for the packaging. For sure we will sell out soon.. but we are all working to bring more asap. It's peaceful and quiet, its so quiet.. the air feels cleaner. The animals, the birds something about them.. they know. In the hotel where I was week before last sitting outside this bird would come and sit near by. We kind of became friends, he was always there - sometimes singing. But maybe I'm going mad.. but in the villa garden I have now, the same bird is coming (well OK could be a different one) but I can hear him singing as I type. He knows.. I'm sure. Drop-shipping is buzzing - and lots of enthusiastic users are finding ways to sell on-line. Here's my recommendations for creating a webshop again.. 1. Shopify - probably the most popular these days and we are working on a plugin for this first to streamline AW dropshipping and Shopify. At $29/ month you pretty much get what you pay for but what many people don't realise with Shopify lite , (just $9/month) you can add order buttons to any site even Facebook, and sell stuff everywhere. 2. Squarespace - I have had a little experience with this, and was delighted how easy it is to make a cool website quickly. An eCommerce site starts at £20 / month. 3. Bluepark - this I like because you can add your own payment method in the cart.. meaning you're giving a cut of your sales to the platform. Gets good reviews. From £25 / month 4. Wix - this is cool but budget.. you can pretty much make it do what you want. I have played with it in it's early days and it was good then. From about £10 / month (or even free - but don't do that it's not a cool look) and we can add to that.. 5. WordPress .. One of the oldest website solutions, but still manages to be cool. Lots of plugins.. costs from £20 / month. I understand you might get cheap access via a deal with GoDaddy when you register your domain there. WooCommerce is a plugin to access the e-commerce - getting complicated no? But many people like it. 6. Jimdo - this one is made in Germany, they have a Coronavirus offer to help small business right now. Use the code: JIMDOHELP when paying to get a huge discount just $1 per month (usually £15 / month). I had a quick look round, it's pretty nice. Anyway, I wish you a peaceful Easter. Stay Home. Stay Safe. David

title: Earth Day @ AW
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

Hope you are well and enjoying Springtime.
Tomas is here in Spain, yesterday we had our first proper AGM of the Spanish  co.. AW-Artisan.eu .. Mario the Administrator and Toni the manager produced the accounts to show Tomas and I, we told them well done, pretty amazing.. then as is the way in Spain.. we went for lunch on the beach. A business lunch I might add, since I'm sure Adam the chief accountant and financial controller is reading this.. 


Actually we had a major brainstorming session, where I brought up my main point (again): OK guys we can revamp marketing, we can improve customer service, we can implement better warehouse systems.. BUT.. only one thing really matters.. and that is our PRODUCTS.. we have to give our customers what they need to keep their customers happy. Last week I was telling you about the search for dream stones, you can read this here.
Recently we asked all our customers to give us feedback, we asked a bunch of questions...

Thank you so much to everyone that responded, because you gave us plenty to chew on over lunch.. 
Lots of suggestions and feedback.. Basically we have to get even better at the things we do best. Gemstones, Incense, Aromatherapy, Esoteric things.. We are always looking for new interesting lines, but somehow we have to find the best and make sure we are competitive. Lots and lots of people asked for even more gemstones and more crystals.. it was the number one request. 
Also of course many people are interested in Vegan products and Eco products.. to protect the earth.. Since today is Earth Day 2022 this seems appropriate.. 

We have put some of our best selling Earth products below.. 

I'm quite excited because tomorrow - Raul arrives in Spain. Raul is our IT wizard. He is the brains behind all the software that runs AW, from the websites to the stock control to the marketing. Last time that I have seen him in the flesh was before the pandemic. Raul lives in Kuala Lumpur and in the old days I would often stop over in KL on the way to China or Indonesia and spend a few days there working on some aspect of our IT. Raul is originally from Mexico, he is married to a Malaysian Chinese girl who works in investment banking and they have two cute kids. While I know he will miss his family he is excited to see the changes at AW since he last came to Europe.
 
Coco update.. Regular readers will know that Coco is my wife and our China agent. I haven't seen her since before the pandemic either. 
Yiwu, where our warehouse, candle factory and offices are.. is two hours from Shanghai and so far escaped most of the madness that we have all seen on TV and social media. But this morning she told me that one covid case had been found in the neighbouring area. We know it well because until last year that's where we had an apartment. Within an hour of finding the case the whole place was locked down and testing started working through the night. No-one allowed to sleep, loud speakers blaring, an army of  hazmat suits descended. Kind of obsessive. 
This is Yiwu yesterday.. from social media.


The soy wax candle factory will close today, we have run out of wax and it seems that there is none available in China right now. Maybe a consequence of the war in Ukraine. 
We are still managing to load containers, and one slight positive is that because many factories are closed in Shanghai there are plenty of spare containers available.. so we are loading while we can.  
The ports are being kept open to try and support economic activity, but drivers arriving from the port are not allowed to leave their cab. 


This medical robe guy's job is to simply watch the cab driver to make sure he never leaves the cab. He came in the yellow taxi all the way from the port, Coco gave him a cup of tea. When he went to the loo, Coco managed to pass some food to the poor driver who was complaining he needed a toilet. All a bit obsessive.
Today she was warned that if anyone leaves or enters the warehouse not actually wearing a mask she will get an order to close immediately. It's only a matter of time before Coco and family are locked down and the warehouse closed.
Here in Spain as in many places the need to wear a mask in shops and transport was scrapped. It is almost back to normal, we are living with covid these days.
In China it's another world, I really don't know how China will get out of the zero covid mindset and open the borders again. I will see Raul tomorrow, but I have no idea when I will see Coco.

On a more positive note we have new stock a container from Indonesia just arrived today.. some new products and I know the guys are working hard to get them online.
Plus check our special deals for Earth Day.

Take care, have a lovely weekend.

David

title: Can We Keep The Good Bits?
content_html:
Greetings from Bali.. now day 76.

Just when things were relaxing, it's all gone fraught again. 

There is a market in the centre of Denpasar city next to the river. At street level it is a wet market (fresh fish, animals etc) but above in a warren of stalls on four levels is a wholesale craft market. Lots of small businesses and one or two large ones show off their products there. It attracts international buyers from all over the world. We have four suppliers that are based there. Last time I was there was in April, when Tomas was here. We went with masks and latex gloves because the place is cramped and stiflingly hot always. I always thought it was a place the virus would like.. and my fears unfortunately not unfounded. Yesterday a cluster of cases, 18 in total centred on this market. Now it's been closed down until further notice, the total number of cases in Denpasar has almost doubled in a week. So now I understand why so many temperature checks everywhere.

The worrying thing is Ringo was in there picking up a shipment of brass items about ten days ago. He had a slight fever last weekend - I tell him to get checked but he says ..no problem.

The mask debate never happened here. In Asia, as far as I know, nobody questioned if masks were effective or not. Very quickly a law was passed requiring everyone outside their home to wear a mask at all times. I'm sure it helped contain the virus, as in Vietnam, Thailand, Korea - masks wearing countries with low R numbers.. Now I see a report on the BBC about Germany where mask wearing was rolled out city by city, and so the effect could be quantified.  And the conclusively is effective. 

The news from India is very distressing, stories of poor people unable to find hospitals or doctors willing to treat anyone with suspect symptoms and many hospitals overwhelmed anyway. In some kind of crazy madness, the lockdown is being relaxed. These are terrible times. Mr Chatterjee (our man in India) continues to help people with food every day, small gifts of money were helpful. I talk to him most days, and the news is not good. To support Mr Chatterjee here. GoFundMe

But life goes on and we continue to do business in Bali. Yesterday I went with Ringo to visit our bamboo wind chime supplier high up in the mountain and then meet with a potential new supplier in Ubud. 
It really is like Bali is reborn, the sky is more blue, the hedgerows more green and lush. No cars, no planes in the sky.. even the ducks seem happy in the rice terrace.


As we drive around, I'm struck by how green everything is.. we had to go to visit one of our bamboo wind chime guys in a village high on the mountain above Ubud.. it's remote, it's stunningly quiet, it's ferdent it's just beautiful. On the way, we drive through a disinfectant gate, and also see several disinfectant trucks spraying anything that moves.. only in Bali would they make the gate pretty with local cultural design.


Just a few random snaps as we drive around.. but you get the idea. Blue sky and greenness.. the world over is more like this.. and I wonder.. when this craziness will all end? And if, when it does.. can we please keep the good bits?

Meanwhile in UK..
It's very busy.. very busy.. and I don't know why really. But we are trying our best to deal with an unprecedented amount of orders under very difficult working conditions. The first priority of course is safety, and Tomas, Katka and the team are working hard to achieve this and get your orders out, I believe they are doing a great job.. 
Please understand we are doing our best.

Lots of new stock now arriving.. so the out of stock position will improve a bit this week.

Please stay safe.. wear a mask.. it works!

More news next week.

David

title: Today is Life - Tomorrow never comes. Maybe.
content_html:
Greetings from Matala, Crete

Hi Guys, yes officially on holiday, but unofficially still 100% AW focused. Last week I was telling you about Bali (the other one here in Crete) and the story of the lost luggage.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Since then we travelled down the island to the wonderful town of Chania, parked up near the old town and (without a Hotels.com booking) wandered the ancient Venetian back streets looking for a room to stay. I highly recommend it - go old school and as my wife would say "see what happens come". Chania was way busier than I have seen before, and finding a room was not so easy, we began to worry when five places in a row said sorry fully booked...


Don't worry I said, let's try the area at the very bottom of the harbour opposite the iconic ancient stone lighthouse. The maze of narrow lanes, hung with flowers and steeped in history have a mirid of old traders houses turned to guest houses, above small shops and cafes. In the evening locals still pull out wonky wooden chairs and sit in small groups drinking Greek coffee or raki and gossip, nod and smile at the tourists. We asked at one guest house and an old gentleman apologised that they were full, but offered to help us find accommodation..  he took us to a small mini-mart where a young boy got on his mobile and asked around.. the then guy led us around a couple of corners to a beautiful alleyway and called out the name of a lady.. who after a minute appeared..  yes she had a room.. only two nights, but after two we could move to a nicer room for another two. 
So friendly, breakfast wasn't available, but that didn't stop Mrs Tomas (I think that was her name) from waking us up with tray loads of Greek yogurt, honey, cheese cakes and mountain tea. Greeting us in the afternoon with homemade apple sponge cake. Boutique hotel it wasn't but the genuine experience it certainly was.


Chania port and harbour and the rambling old town in June is sublime.. but the gift shops are next level.. and I'm a little ashamed to say we spent a lot of time appreciating the creativity, the ideas the local crafts and the blend of gifts on offer. I was particularly impressed with one giftshop that made hand-painted local tee-shirts in the back and complimented it with Nepal bags, Bali sarongs, some gemstone jewellery and Indian cotton bags. The blend of natural products with a local input just worked, although the obvious good taste of the owner made the place awesome. A nice touch was that every product had been branded (or re-branded) with stores logo.. labels stitched in or hang tags. Nice.

Crete has always been face cream kind of place.. the local, herbs, aloe vera and olive oil and the ancient wisdom in making herbal remedies. Maybe the sea sponges, maybe the mountain herbs, maybe Venetian traders bringing exotic ingredients..   Anyway the range of stuff and competition between several well established local companies is amazing.. We ended up spending a lot of money on all sorts of things.. and collecting ideas for future development at AW-Aromatics..  We have spent 20 years developing our range of aromatics at AW, but I'm slightly in awe of the products available here.... maybe a few thousand years of advanced civilisation.. since the ancient Minoans and Mycenaeans with influence from traders from across the Mediterranean.. maybe they acquired ancient wisdom we don't understand. Maybe.


Maybe they knew things we don't know..

Anyway.. did the ancient Minoans know how to make whipped cream soaps? Maybe they did... but at AW we have that one covered.. launching today.. see below..  our very own whipped cream soaps.. beautiful and eye catching.. going to look good in any shop display..

After a few days in Chania we decided to drive to the south side of the island.. and escaped to Matala.. one of the most beautiful in Europe (I think) places. We have been here before and I have written about this hippy place before. The Beatles came here, hippies lived in the caves by the beach.. they still live here.
"Today is Life - Tomorrow never comes" is the towns slogan.. originally graffiti painted on the port side wall.. now lovingly replicated on mugs, tee-shirts, tea-towels and art all over town. They even have there own patron saint of Matala an old hippy that everyone remembers meeting.. immortalised in a song by Joni Mitchell. Matala Moon. 



We found a small apartment above the village with a spectacular view over the beach to the caves.  Coco is up before the sunrise, talking to suppliers in China and organising shipments.. we generally work until about midday and then go exploring..  And did I tell you the gift shops here are also pretty awesome.. maybe we will stay here a few more days.. maybe.

Have a wonderful weekend, take care, enjoy.
Today is Life, tomorrow never comes.

David & Coco

title: Holy Smokes in Spain
content_html:
Greetings from Málaga, Spain.

 

Yes it's true.. the time has come to start the journey.. Last week I was telling you about my travel plans and all about saying goodbye to everyone in the UK. You can read about it here.

I had hoped that our new offices would have been completed before leaving but in these covid/brexit days everything takes a 100 years to get done.. anyway since I left it's all happening. Our new super cool office space, complete with collaborative zone, chill-out space, kitchen and media room has begun to finally spring to life.. It's great but also frustrating that I'm missing all the action..


On Friday last week, I went to see as many people as possible in the flesh - wished them well and said my goodbyes. Late afternoon I had a (business) lunch with Tomas & Katka, my fellow directors at AW. A little emotional, with much laughter, love and warmth - I feel lucky to be able to work with my best friends. Katka I might not see for a long time, but hopefully I will catch up with Tomas in Slovakia in a few weeks.

 

I arranged an Uber for 2am - to T1 Manchester airport.. went to bed early but simply could not sleep.. the excitement of finally travelling again. 

I had my Spanish covid forms filled, tickets printed and because I'm going back to the EU outside of the new Brexit 180/90 ruling - a special visa obtained at great effort. Plus due to all the news that travelling to an Amber List Country was tantamount to treason, and you cannot travel for anything but absolutely essential reason. So I have papers (stamped & signed) showing I need to sign off the accounts of our AW Artisan at a board meeting (which I do).  So with all my papers, triple checked, with lots of stamps and neatly arranged in order.. I was ready to do battle with any bureaucracy that came my way.

 

In Manchester airport at 4am, a sleepy Ryanair lady barely glanced at my passport, no-one she wasn't interested in any papers. There is still no passport control OUT of the UK.. (is that right?).. and when I arrived in Spain - the passport control guy was not the slightest bit interested in my papers either.  A quick covid scan of my QR code to show I'm double jabbed and I was back in the EU!!  All that stress over nothing.. 

Here people still wear masks in the streets, the shops, public transport and even cars if there is more than one passenger.  Those rules are due to be relaxed this weekend.. so it is a grand coming out party.

 

On Monday I drove to Málaga to visit the AW Artisan team. The plants outside in our garden have grown quite a bit, and the stock in the warehouse has also grown, the confidence and chattiness of the team.. wow so much louder. Last time I was here three months ago we installed another section of racking.. It's great to see it fully used and the warehouse and offices buzzing with activity. While I'm here we will plan the next leg of expansion.. 

 

Toni has been hard at work on a range of projects, one of which is becoming an expert importer of Palo Santo items from South America, we have suppliers from Peru and Mexico. 



To be honest I never really understood this form of incense. But sitting in the office here as I type today's newsletter I'm engulfed by the Palo Santo aroma. title: In the wood carver's market
content_html:
This week finds me in Ubud, Indonesia. My third trip this year, and like a good book Ubud gradually unfolds its secrets. Before I tell you this weeks trade secret, I must tell you about the celebration days in Bali. Basically almost every day has some kind of celebration attached, upon arriving the skies were full of kites, some as large small cars, diving and swooping, small children running up and down the mud paths between the paddy fields engaged in serious competition. Kite flying day in Bali.
The day after was "bless my small appliance day", which included cars and motorbikes. From early in the morning bikes and cars are been cleaned, mirrors fixed, scratches polished. Everything must be perfect for the local holy guy to do blessing and attach palm leaf decorations to your vehicle. Time to be grateful for these possessions and then ask for safety for the coming year. Or at least the next 220 days.. because they have four separate calendars here each with a list of holy and high days. Each calendar has different systems and numbers of days in a year, so you can see that some days come round more than one time (in our year).
Then on top of all this they have been taking the Euro football very serious here, even in the most remote mountain villages great silk flags float in the hot breeze denoting the country a particular household is supporting. Staying up all night to watch the footy, it's a wonder anything gets done.
But they do, this is a very industrious place. Ringo, our man in Bali had discovered an early morning market where wood carvers go to sell unfinished work to traders. Traders finish it off to the clients specifications and then pass it off as their own work. Interesting.. I wanted to see this market, and since it started at 6am (when the best deals are struck) I had to get up jolly early.
Maybe, Ringo thought, we could trade direct with artisan families.
We found the market on the edge of a small village, little more than a cattle shed, on arrival almost dark but for the morning light cutting through the holes in the roof and slanting through the rising incense. It soon brightened up and became quite busy, a regular hive of activity. I love markets of all kinds. Like a deeply furrowed field great mounds of carved wooden items were plied high, each stack with an old lady making offerings for harmony and good trade, and ready and more than able to make a hard Bali bargain.
Turns out that it is the wife's (or Grannies) job to sell the stock, while the husband sits and carves his particular speciality at home. Just about anything you can imagine is carved in about six varieties of available wood. I had to learn very quickly, the pluses and minuses of all the woods, (now I'm checking on the back story to the various types). These ladies are no push over, they know the value of the stock can make a sales pitch (with limited English) and take great pride in the workmanship of their stock. What's more they will (for a fee) finish off pieces in any finish you want; dark stain, high polish, gold filigree.
It crossed my mind at how old the traders were and if this is in away a dying profession. The younger generation, better educated want a life other than farming and carving. Supplies are sorely limited, try negotiating by offering a large quantity, and you get a sigh and open hands, "sorry we can only make 300 pieces a month, I can spare you half that". Thus prices are rising and therefore giving a little more money to these hard working artisans and that's not a bad thing.
More news next week.
Regards
David

title: Epic Journeys
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Spain..

Last week I was telling you about Heaven and Hell in Bali.. and introduced you to the wood carving family, if you missed it you can catch up here.

Yes, I'm in Spain this week. I just travelled back from Bali. It was an epic 36 hour journey. Denpasar to Jakarta on wonderful Airasia, change of terminals, a six hour wait and the KLM to Singapore, 2 hours, then a 14 hour flight to Amsterdam, 6 hours again and then a short flight down to Malaga. Epic journey, I arrived rather frazzled with dry lips and red eyes from constant mask wearing.
But if my journey from Asia was traumatic it was nothing compared to Tomas's from Sheffield..

The plan was Tomas would arrive in Spain the day before me.. he actually set off to drive from Sheffield to Manchester airport just as I left my hotel in Ubud, Bali.  

But storm Arwen hit just as he reached the top of the Snake Pass . He sent me pictures of a snow blizzard just as I'm boarding the flight to Jakarta, in Jakarta he messaged me that he was in danger of missing the flight and was going to turn back and try to get to the A6 via Hope Valley.. he never made it. In Singapore I learned that he was totally stuck. Tomas spent the night in his car in the Snake Pass Inn car park (which was closed). It was 3am before he finally gave in and tried to get some sleep.. not until 11.30am the next day did the snow plough arrive. As I landed in Amsterdam I learned he was still stranded. I thought he was joking.. which brought forth some colourful language..  So finally he made it back to Sheffield, and rebooked the flight, this time taking the train.




So I actually arrived first. I thought I'd had an epic journey, but I think Tomas beat me on that.

My last days in Bali were a bit of a mad rush around to finalise deals and designs. To put in place a decent plan, and make sure everything was as organised as it could be. 
I'm quite happy with what our AW Bali team achieved in the seven weeks I was there.. We have just under 200 new products in production, and we estimated the initial orders will be at least ten container loads, on top of our usual re-orders.. so I think my trip put more than a thousand artisans back to work and along the way I'm sure we saved a few small businesses from bankruptcy. 
But none of this would be possible without the amazing support of you guys.. the hardworking and creative retailers who complete this magic circle. 

And talking about a magic circle.. the new AW logo is finally settled after six months of development.. of debate, of staff feedback, of me asking for more. Our professional logo designer, a lovely saintly lady.. almost lost it with us being unreasonable.. but finally it was born. And I, because I could.. immediately had it deployed on the wall of our Bali warehouse..
 

The circle, the triangle and the bar.. are highly symbolic. See if you can figure out the inner meanings.. I'll reveal all next week. The symbol will be the same for all parts of AW, but the colours will change to reflect each part's identity. Here in the Indonesian outpost of AW - it's a black circle, brown triangle and green bar. 
Watch out for it being gradually rolled out, first in marketing and later will appear in product packaging and labelling.

My last night in Bali turned into an impromptu leaving party in the local restaurant near my hotel. I had become quite friendly with the owner and his staff. Plus Bondhan, our new staff member who likes to play his guitar, had also bonded. He came along with his wife Debbie, Ringo brought his two daughters and we had a lovely evening saying goodbye to all my new friends. The boss and his team with Bondhan got on stage and sang.. "David's leaving on a jet plane, we don't know when he will be back again"..  But the highlight of the evening was when I jokingly asked Ringo's daughter if she wanted to sing with the band, and she shyly said maybe yes.. and to Ringo's absolute amazement got up and sang like a professional doing a spirited version of "Price Tag".. that "It's not about the money".. song. the whole restaurant and the boss just flipped, and Ringo just sat there with tears in his eyes shaking his head.  



So, the last night in Bali was very special for me, an evening I will never forget. And yes, it's not about the money at AW, we do it for the love of giftware, and that magic circle. And I left on a jet plane, but I DO KNOW when I will be back again..  as soon as possible! There is so much to do yet.

Tonight is AW Artisan's Christmas party in Spain and regular readers will know they know how to party.

In the UK it's beyond mad busy.. we are working all hours to get your orders out.. this week two containers arrived from Indonesia.. so lots of stuff is back in stock.  Check out the new items and deals below.
Once again thank you for your support.. And since it is now the 3rd of December.. I think I can wish you all a jolly.. SEASONS GREETINGS.. 

Take care.

David

title: Coming Together X3
content_html:
Greetings from AW HQ - Sheffield.

It's now just over 2 months since the fire.. and things are, well they actually are.. coming together. 
Last week I was telling you about The Dilemma.. you can read about it here. 
The old destroyed warehouse has gone, pulled down and loaded into skips and taken away.. Rodrigo made a time-lapse video of the process.. You can watch here. 


With that scene of destruction finally gone, it feels better. Also, I can report that the insurance is finally sorted, in the end they were understanding and kind, settlement made and today actually paid so now it's really time to move forward.
We have been working hard to find a warehouse because working out of 30% of the space we had is simply unsustainable. Waiting until our landlord rebuilds the warehouse that was burned down would mean moving to a temporary site and then moving again. Finding a temporary location is almost impossible and every large warehouse in the area is seeking long term commitment. We are stuck between a rock and a hard place.  

There is one option that was a huge long shot.. that is starting to look like it might just work. It's a complicated arrangement which involves a London investment company buying the property and then leasing it to us. the property in question is much bigger than we need, but then it's just about the only thing actually available now. I don't want to jinx the deal.. so I can't tell you more.. only that hopefully we can get access next week. 
If we can pull it off AW UK will have 3x the capacity.. our production will expand over the three units we are in now. The distribution will move to the new unit - not far away.. and we will have in a little over two months gone from 45 thousand square feet.. to 15 thousand.. to combined 111 thousand. It's been a hell of a journey.. and now for the next phaze.. I feel a bit like Moses leading his people to the promised land.   

The process has been emotional, stressful, tearful, heart-wrenching and cathartic. As a team we have been to hell and back together. As a team I feel we are closer than ever. In that team I include everyone at AW, many suppliers, our agents: Coco, Ringo and Chatterjee and even our customers. Now the emotions looking forward as a closer battle scarred team.. are - excitement, humility, thankfulness and a little fearful. I stood in the potential new warehouse yesterday, thinking OMG this is big, how is this going to go..? 

But I can remember 18 years ago standing in Lancelot Works, a rambling old silver works at Heley, Sheffield, and having the same feeling.. then later here at Parkwood Business Park.. now it's our 3rd big move.  
That time 18 years ago, I looked at this vast empty space and wondered aloud how on earth we would fill it profitably.. the landlord looked at me and said something that has stuck with me ever since. "It's simple" he said, "just find out what your customers want and make it available".  
I thought wow yes! He's absolutely right.. and something clicked into place. Focus on the product, spend more time getting the product right, and less time trying to flog it. So we opted to never have salespeople, never do trade shows, never be pushy. Listen instead, take our customers suggestions and ideas seriously. Over the years the readers of this blog.. people like you have shaped the product ranges we stock. You guys were pushing for plastic free, vegan friendly, fairly traded, artisan products etc years ago. 

Well it's kind of obvious isn't it?  And most business people would agree, but how many actually put it into action..  lots of companies still focus on sales teams and huge efforts to persuade you to stock products, rather than just get the product right and offer it open-handed and wait patiently for the orders to come. 

So what does the future hold? 
Despite the fire, despite the pandemic, in the teeth of Brexit.. the future is exciting I can't wait. Hope you are along for the ride.
It's coming soon, it's my goodness practically upon us.. Halloween, Christmas and the busy season.. we need to be able to cope with your orders efficiently. 

More news next week, hopefully good news about the warehouse.

Take care  

David

title: Mooncakes & Mulberry Trees
categories: moon cake | Mid-Autumn Festival | ancient wisdom
content_html:
Last week I told you about my frustrations at getting a visa for Indian in a UK passport whilst in China. You can read about it here.
Update on this situation.. I went to the regular Indian visa place with all the Chinese folk wanting visa's to discover that the consulate had scribbled in GP style scrawl on my application that I could have only a 3 month 1 entry visa even though I was (again) paying top whack for a full year business visa. Why? I have no idea.. have I done something to upset them? Feeling dispirited about India and in particular petty puffed up arrogant power mad bureaucratic suits that clearly have no love for their own country.

Sorry to rant.. after all I'm writing this on calm and forgiving Moon Day in China. I have to admit I had never heard of the Mid-Autumn / Zhongqiu Festival.. or as I prefer to call it.. the Mooncake Day.
For the past week all over Shanghai I have witnessed huge queues of folk waiting in line to order or pre-order Mooncakes from particularly auspicious bakeries. I think if you put all the Mooncake queues in China end to end they would probably stretch to the moon. That's just conjecture but a jolly poetic one don't you think?
Alternatively you can go to a department store and pay any amount of money for a richly packaged rich tasting cake. I have seen cakes on sale for a $1000. 

Actually Moon Day is celebrated all over Asia each country in it's own way. I'm typing this to the sound of fireworks and crackers.. I'd like to tell you about the associated legends that surround Moon Day.. but they are just too complicated.. something to do with immortal/mortal Princesses, Jade rabbits and fairies. The story starts.. "At that time, there were ten suns, in the form of three-legged birds, residing in a mulberry tree.." enough already.
  Mooncake.. Eggs inside and sticky gooey lotus seeds.. comfort food for Asians.

It reminds me a little of our Harvest celebrations.. which reminds me soon it will be Halloween and then Bonfire night then pretty much Christmas.
Gosh it's that time of year. Sadly it's raining in Shanghai.. so the years biggest and brightest moon will most likely be hidden, ho well.. I'll just console my self with some cake.

For the past week all over Shanghai I have witnessed huge queues of folk waiting in line to order or pre-order Mooncakes from particularly auspicious bakeries. I think if you put all the Mooncake queues in China end to end they would probably stretch to the moon. That's just conjecture but a jolly poetic one don't you think? Alternatively you can go to a department store and pay any amount of money for a richly packaged rich tasting cake. I have seen cakes on sale for a $1000. Actually Moon Day is celebrated all over Asia each country in it's own way. I'm typing this to the sound of fireworks and crackers.. I'd like to tell you about the associated legends that surround Moon Day.. but they are just too complicated.. something to do with immortal/mortal Princesses, Jade rabbits and fairies. The story starts.. "At that time, there were ten suns, in the form of three-legged birds, residing in a mulberry tree.." enough already. Mooncake.. Eggs inside and sticky gooey lotus seeds.. comfort food for Asians. It reminds me a little of our Harvest celebrations.. which reminds me soon it will be Halloween and then Bonfire night then pretty much Christmas. Gosh it's that time of year. Sadly it's raining in Shanghai.. so the years biggest and brightest moon will most likely be hidden, ho well.. I'll just console my self with some cake. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- www.AncientWisdom.biz

title: Prosper Mightily with AW in 2021 ❤
content_html:
Greetings and welcome to Ancient Wisdom 2021


The less said about the last year the better.. let's hope 2021 is going to be prosperous and happy... and a lot less trouble. 

If you missed the review of 2020 newsletter you can read it here.

We are not out of the woods yet, there are still a lot of hurdles to overcome. But you can be sure AW will be there to support and help you develop your gift trading business.. whatever they throw at us.

Over the years life at AW has always been an adventure, none as extreme as 2020 but nevertheless it's always been an exciting ride.

I'm hoping the vaccine is good and quick and we will all be allowed to travel, not least so I can see Coco in China. She is our China agent and my wife.. now almost a year since she was here in Spain for New Year.  

I'm also missing Ringo our man in Indonesia and lots of contacts including Mr Chatterjee in India. Make sure you add this email address to your contacts, so you don't miss out on this years adventures. 

 

IMPORTANT INFO.. if you have customers in the EU, or are an AW customer in the EU. See below.

 

 

Anyway we have lots of plans to develop and bring you the exciting new products to delight your customers and give your business a welcome boost. 

Even over Christmas, stock has been arriving, so watch out for lots of things back in stock and few new lines.. 

Over the next few days the team at AW and I will be devising a plan for the product areas we want to develop in 2021.. if you have any suggestions, needs, ideas or strokes of genius - do click reply and let us know!



So at 11pm last night the UK (most of it) left the EU, and Boris like Moses will lead us into this new exciting promised land where he assures us we will Prosper Mighterly.. 

At 7am this morning Tomas Whatsapped me.. it's all going wrong already!!  Last time he did that it was because our main warehouse burned down.. so I was a little stressed. Turns out that all our websites with the .EU domains had stopped working. Including the very busy AWGifts.eu site.. Sorry your not in the EU now.. you can't use that.  Major stress, Raul our IT wizard who lives in KL, Malaysia was already on it.. those domains should be registered to an EU AW company not the UK company.. 

 

Haha.. so off to a flying start.. 

But this is what we expect, it's going to be a wild west for a bit as things realign, whatever happens, stay calm we will find away.

 

So, many of our customers - and maybe you - have thriving on-line businesses, and maybe you have customers in the EU..  

You can still supply them without all the new forms and red tape. AW products can be shipped direct to your customers, and as far as I know it's completely legal. We have two warehouses in Europe one in Spain and one in Slovakia, each warehouse has a Dropshipping website. Slovakia: AW-dropship.eu  (in English) and Spain: AW-dropship.es  (in Spanish, but google will translate for you and it's pretty easy to use). You will just need to register, then when you sell an AW product to a customer in Europe, you just need to add that customer address to your list and order the product and we do the rest - sending to your customer. Obviously you will need to make sure we have the product in stock in that warehouse before you sell it, but there is no stopping you drop-shipping to your EU customers and thus Prospering Mightily :-)

 

If you are an EU customer and normally order from the UK website. You can still do this of course, but as you will know there will be customs forms and delays. We also have a plan to get around this, and I'll update you in the near future once we can be sure our systems are functioning. Alternatively you can order directly from our EU warehouses.. Spain: AWArtisan.eu  and Slovakia: AWGifts.eu  -  again you will need to register but these sites are in English. The Spain site is fairly new, so products are still being added but you can always use the online chat if something you need is missing and we can add for you.

 

SO here we are it's 2021.. let the adventure begin. On behalf of everyone at AW I wish you all the best for the coming year, both in your business and family life. 

Take care, stay safe, hold on to your hat.. lets goooooooo...

  

David

title: David's AW News: Home for Christmas.
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield..

Yes I'm back in the UK.. at AW HQ.. 
I flew back from Malaga to Manchester on Tuesday with Katkta and James who had been in Spain. We arrived from sunny Spain to a rather chilly but still sunny UK.. The journey over the Pennines to Sheffield was stunning, cold clear air and winter sun and the Derbyshire countryside is spectacular. 


Coming Home for Christmas.
I have spent the first days at AW-Aromatics.com where it's all happening. We revamped the team about six months ago and now there is no stopping them.. new products (especially the Whipped Soaps) have really really changed the game.. Dusan the production manager, has been showing me how they solved the production process.. meaning we can make them cost effectively. Rather clever use of sausage making machines to make the whipped soap. I'm impressed. And I sat in on the Thursday product development meeting, and I can tell you there are lots of beautiful, on trend, innovative products just, itching, bursting to be released to the world. 
Last week I was telling you about the travel plans for next year and how Christmas properly is kicking off.. If you missed it you can catch up here.

So James and Katka came from the UK to bond with the Spanish team and to attend the AWArtisan.eu Christmas party.. sadly I had a nasty bout of flu and had to opt out and missed it. I was just thinking that since I had my first covid jab, I have not had a cold, not even sniffles in four years.. I never (to my knowledge) had covid either so a bit of bad luck. But now I'm ok and looking forward to the UK Christmas party which is themed 1970's just my era, so should be fun. 
I was looking around the showroom in our Affinity Park HQ.. it had a big re-merchandise with all the new products from India, Nepal and from AW-Aromatics beautifully displayed.   I got quite emotional seeing all our hard work, every product comes with a story behind it, each one has taken creativity and effort from different AW team members.. Every product has some small family business, artisans.. who have worked hard - sometimes all night - to meet deadlines to get the goods to us. I'm so proud of our product ranges now.. I really believe we have the best selections right now in the history of AW. 



My absolute favorite product has just arrived in the UK.. it's the next in our Hop Hare range of products.. Designed by our talented designer Sandra in Sheffield, with input from Tomas, and editing from me.. It's a concept candle range.. with a story behind each candle and beautiful artwork and packaging. Coco produced it in our own candle factory in China using only top-end elements.. soy-wax, wooden wicks, natural botanicals, green glass jars, fine fragrances  (selected by my nose). The love, devotion, emails, wechats, sample packs, revisions and Sandra's uncompromising determinatuin to make it awesome.. has.. (I believe) paid off.. And a total AW team effort.
Last time I was in China, I was with Coco hunting for botanicals in the dried flower market and seeking out the raw crystals in the gemstone area of Yiwu. No expense has been spared to make this happen..

They arrived in our EU warehouse a few weeks ago and are already our best selling candle line.. by far.. an epic response from customers and almost immediate reorders.. we have sold out of some references already and people are actually fighting for stock, getting quite upset. 
Here's Sandra.. 


Introducing.. The Lovers, The Magician, The Moon, The Devil, The Sun, The Lion, The Knight of Swords..  Check out the Hope Hare Crystal Floral Candles. 
See below for more details..

Anyway.. there is lots more to come.. 
It's all happening at AW.. 
I hope you are trading well in the run up to the big day.. not long now.
Have you been following our 12 Days of Christmas?  Just a few more days to go...

Tomorrow is our AW Christmas party.. full update next week.

It's the penultimate weekend before Christmas.. 
Have a wonderful jolly weekend.

David

title: David's AW News: Varanasi to Kolkata
content_html:
Greetings from the banks of the Ganges.

Toni and I are in Mr Chatterjee's home town, Serampore just along the river from Kolkata. 
Last week I was telling you about our last day in Nepal, getting a Tika blessing and then travelling to Varanasi on Buddha Air. If you missed it you can catch up here.


Varanasi is very wet, crazy, busy, noisy as hell, holy cows everywhere but despite all that it's surprisingly clean and tidy! I was pleasantly surprised. Plus we found the people open and friendly and didn't at all get hassled or swamped by beggars.

We went looking for Varanasi silk, real silk.. Because it's something special if you can get it. These days polyester has been improved so much it's hard to tell the difference (at least when it is new) and the traders in most touristy areas of India will sell you the fake silk because of the huge profit they can make. However there is something special about the real Varanasi silk. 


It has that Billionaire vibe. Which Toni can absolutely rock. 

Mr Chatterjee took us to see one trader deep in the market alleyways not far from the Ganges. After our meeting he suggested we go to his godown (warehouse),only 5 minutes walk away..
Down tiny alleyways, it's was in a monsoon rainstorm and we had to squeeze past this massive mean looking cow or or was it a bull.


The things we have to do for AW! 

Well we survived to tell the tale.
Later after meetings with several silk traders we found a nice family business with close links to the production process. Like almost all artisan products different parts of the process are done by different people. From the silk farm to the silk looms, to the dyeing house to the stitching and finishing workshop. We wanted to see as much of the process as possible. 

That was much harder than we thought and the traders gave us the run around (trying to palm us off on tourist trap museum style set up) but eventually we made it into the heart of the silk loom quarter and found ancient looms in little family workshops in back alleyway crammed in impossible spaces. The artisans were wide eyed and happy that some foreigners had taken an interest and were really friendly and proud to show off their skills.
I think I have enough content for a YouTube video, I'll upload something when I get chance.






Silk is as Ancient Wisdom as it gets, ever since the silk route traders Marco Polo and all that. 

From Varanasi we took a train to a small town called Kaderma in the middle of nowhere. Midway between Varanasi and Kolkata.
We went to visit a gemstone mine owner who had promised to show us an actual gemstone mine. It was nothing like what I had expected. 
I'll tell you about it next week. 

Meanwhile in the UK it's all happening. 
We have some new (but ancient) Chinese wormwood massagers.

Something big is happening soon at Ancient Wisdom.. Very Big. Stay tuned. 

Check out the new Can You Sell This? .. YouTube from Holly here.


Anyway Namaste from India. 
We are about to board a flight from Kolkata to Delhi. More update next week. 

Peace and happiness


David

title: It's Elemental
content_html:
Hello everyone, is it summer yet? Last week I was telling you about Rugrat bags and Indian Red tape, you can read it here.
Well it's June and sun or not, folk have holidays on their minds. If you're not on holiday now, then you will soon.
The good news for retailers (especially those in holiday spots) is that nothing loosens the cash in your pocket more than being relaxed and having a good time.
I have been reading books about Behavioural Economics recently. It's absolutely fascinating. Basically a new science, studying why we do things and the relationship humans have to money. Every retailer should study it, because the human mind is less under our control than we imagine. I was a retailer years ago, and I learned all the usual tricks like; Don't block the doorway, make it open and inviting. Put stuff to the left of the entrance you really want to sell (people scan/read from left to right). Keep the shelves well stocked (but not absolutely full), sublimely people don't often buy the first one.. they think it's not popular. Or if there is hardly any on show, then they can't be popular either. And so on.. you know the tricks already I'm sure.
But this guy, Dan Ariely who pretty much invented Behavioral Economics takes this to a whole new level. Check out his Ted Talk. Remember you heard it here first.
Since that talk, lots of smart people have jumped into this area and there are new books coming out all the time. The top companies like Facebook, even employ Behavioral Economists as directors.
Check out the book: Hooked, how to build habit-forming products. by Nir Eyal It's worth reading on the beach this year, if only to find out how Candy Crush is messing with your mind.
About six months ago I asked for advice on buying scarves.. our plan is to be market leader in the wholesale scarves market within a year or so.
You were incredibly generous, and flooded me with ideas. One thing we learned was that there are (broadly) two types of scarve markets..
1) The cheap and cheerful, wear a few times and ditch. Bought by younger people or bargain hunters. - Polyester or Rayon - retail range £1.75 - £6
2) The added value, gift to someone special, or for yourself if you like good things. Cotton, Linen or Silk - retail range £7 - £18 and upwards.
To sell well, cheap or premium they need to be a good price/value combination.
I went to China, India and Indonesia in search of such things.... and the fruits of those trips are just beginning to come now.
Some of those scarves are beginning to arrive.. Some ready for the winter market, see our Men in Tartan (Ok Father's Day as well), and some are cool accessories for the summer season.
Check out our Elemental Scarves - which really are a product of all the feedback and ideas we received. They are in our Cheap & Cheerful range.
You can buy packs of 12 scarves in a range of elemental colours, the scarves themselves are graduated colours, meaning they will blend well with more outfits.
Synthetic material, but feels like cotton and in a nice textured rebel look. Light and floaty. The perfect Summer accessory.
So even if you only buy one pack you will have a range to sell, but better a pack of each of the four ranges to have a scarf to match any outfit.
I think they will sell well at £2 each, or you can offer 3 for £5 - still a good margin and if displayed well.. a flier.
Have a great summer!!
Take care.
David

title: Opportunity in EU
content_html:
Greetings from sunny Spain

I hope everyone in the UK enjoyed the festive long weekend.

Last week I was in Slovakia at our new warehouse not only to celebrate a successful relocation, but it turned out to celebrate the 5th Birthday of AWGifts. More below.
I was telling you about the crazy turbulent economics of Turkey and some opportunities that might come out of that.. if you missed it you can catch up here.
Lots of opportunities in Turkey and so we made lots of connections and negotiations starting on several fronts.. we absolutely need to go back soon to finalise deals. So we made a plan, meanwhile I needed to head home to Spain and Raul (our IT wizard) needed to go home to Kuala Lumpur.  Tomas drove us to Vienna airport, where I took a Wizz air flight down to Malaga and Raul Turkish airways to Asia. It was smooth as it could be, the flight was full but no queuing at all. I checked in online, printed my own baggage tag by scanning a barcode on the phone, dropped it on a belt and went to the gate. This Hungarian budget airline is really going places. According to the onboard magazine they now fly to Abu Dhabi, and from there to Sri Lanka. Wow, so now you can actually fly a budget airline to Asia. 

So Jubilee Celebrations in the UK kick off with HRM and Paddington Bear.. so delightfully British. Seventy years is a long time to do that job, in Slovakia AW celebrates 5 years, with a move to a new warehouse and a birthday cake.Tomas and I made speeches and we thanked everyone for their hard work.  It was immediately after that Brexit vote in 2016, when we figured that it was time to get started inside the EU. I used to joke that Slovakia is in the middle of nowhere but in fact it's perfect for distribution in Europe.. Slovakia has easy access to 13 countries. And it seems in five years that lots of companies made the same choice of location. When we came it was difficult to find a suitable warehouse. Now the whole area is a distribution hub with massive warehouses on big new hi-tech business parks. And they are building like crazy.. it's all changed so much in 5 years. It seems like this is where the action is.


The new warehouse in Slovakia is much bigger than we need right now.. they gave us such a good deal (long rent free and cash back) it was hard to turn down. So we find ourselves in a huge shed with plenty of space and the ability to distribute across Europe. If you need services inside Europe maybe we can help, big and small customers welcome. Check out AW-fulfilment.eu maybe we can be your distribution partner.

Hope the week ahead is good for you. I'm in Spain right now - full report later.

Take care

David

title: Secret Soup of Life
content_html:
Greetings from Slovakia

I'm here at the EU distribution centre for AW in Trnava near Bratislava. AWGifts.eu.
Last week I was telling you about why some guys are looking forward to Brexit when it finally happens, you can read about it here.

So I have been working with Tomas and Raul on some exciting new projects and new EU websites. It all seems to be going well.

In Slovakia it's really getting quite hectic, yesterday was our busiest so far, but we are still discovering what our customers want.. so exciting time.
#TRNAVA
In the center of the town are some big letters.. with art painted onto them.. each year they change allowing local artists to show off their styles.. A great way to promote the town and its art. Everywhere should do it. 



Head in hands drinking coffee guy (letter A).. Typical.. Slovakians are so serious.. 
I have been getting up extra early in the mornings. The culture here is that they start work early but also finish early.

It's actually really good, the working day seems to pass quickly and by 4.30pm all work is done. The other cultural thing I like is that employees get subsidised lunch food included in their package. It's great - lots of companies compete to provide the working lunch package, and deliver it to your desk, naturally, I'm joining in - and the food especially the Cabbage soup.. is delicious. The food is cheap and healthy here anyway, but after the subsidy - workers get a good quality hot lunch for less than €2..  
The cabbage soup.. it's really sauerkraut with veg or meat in a tomato soup sometimes with sour cream dolapped on top. Every restaurant has their own special recipe and there is a lot of competition to be the best. I love that soup.. honestly I could live on it, and I'm sure it does my body good.  sauerkraut a superfood after all.  It is fermented food.. and if any food is the ancient wisdom of foods it's this.  

Sauerkraut is thought to have originated in the north of China among the Mongols and was introduced in Europe by migrating tribes. Eastern Europeans, in particular, consume a large amount of sauerkraut.  But more than this some evolutionary biologists have speculated that hunter gatherers may have fermented cabbage and other foods to preserve them for when other food was scarce.  So our bodies could have evolved over thousands of years eating fermented foods.. so this is why it's good for us. I was reading this: Health benefits of Sauerkraut. Certainly, there are plenty of healthy looking people on the streets of Trnava - not so many overweight people as in the UK for sure, and now I know why.. it's in the Soup. 

Meanwhile back in Sheffield, a China container is been delivered today.. so lots of great things back in stock.
We also have some cracking deals - a real May madness..

title: David's AW News: So Surprising
content_html:
Greetings from Kuala Lumpur


Hope you guys are doing well and the Christmas uplift coming your way.. 
Last week I was telling you about our trip to the gemstone mine.. in Jharkhand - a small Indian state - surprisingly peaceful and beautiful place.. I'm working on a YouTube video about our trip.. coming soon, but if you missed the newsletter you can catch up here.

As is traditional we spend a few days in South Goa, with our good friends. The last days in India sorting out the loose ends and relaxing. Me, Toni and Mr Chatterjee. Then yesterday Toni heading back to Spain, Chatterjee and I parted in the airport, him going home to Kolkata. Me onwards.

I just arrived from India to KL on an overnight red-eye flight. The journey started with a taxi from our apartment in Goa to the airport, in which a young crazy guy on a motorbike tried to squeeze through an impossible gap and managed to scrape two taxis in one go. Fortunately no-one was hurt, but two angry Goan taxi drivers you don't need shouting at you. 

I was impressed, the police arrived in five minutes, took pictures, worked out the motorbike guy had no insurance, so issued an on the spot fine to cover the damage. There was more discussion as to how much the damage would cost to repair, at this point all the locals came to join the debate. Whilst this is happening no traffic can move in either direction, a backlog building up. As soon as agreement was made we were on our way.. and Rosario, our driver, said the guy will have to pay and will come to his account in a few days. That seemed so damn efficient. Surprising.


Conflict resolution Goan style!

Then a very short flight from South Goa airport to Bangalore, change to the International terminal, T2 - which is garden themed and beautiful. The most beautiful airport in India, maybe all of Asia. Surprisingly beautiful airport. The whole airport is business lounge standard, and theme park Indian. 


 Then around midnight a four hour Batik Air flight to Kuala Lumpur. Surprisingly the passport control in KL is as friction free as it possibly can be. If you fill in an online arrival form within 36 hours of arrival, you can just use an e-gate. Enough booths so no queue at all, it's a one second job to enter Malaysia. I can remember when there was a hall with thousands of people waiting, snaking for up to two hours. People getting angry and frustrated, even one time a large guy keeled over and appeared to die (but maybe just passed out) in the middle of the hall. His poor wife screamed the place down. When some medics came and put the body on a stretcher.. the officials came and wouldn't let them take him until they searched his pockets for the passport, did fingerprints and photo and actually stamped him in.
I digress.. Anyway afterwards, I used the Grab Taxi App to get a smart EV and friendly driver into the city.. Just in time for breakfast in my hotel. 

The taxi driver told me there is a major ASEAN summit about to start. Donald Trump has invited himself, and the city security are in a flat panic setting up roadblocks escorting world leaders creating massive traffic chaos. Looks like I arrived at a bad time.. let's see how it goes.

Holly has been getting excited about a new range of Jewellery -Nymph Aurora - again with design input from Sandra.


It's almost Halloween. and soon as the nights draw in - folk begin to think about Christmas.
So much new and surprising stock came this last week.. we are still working to get it online. 
The Indian Floral Glass candle holders are so beautiful.. SURPRISINGLY beautiful.



These massive singing bowls arrived (finally) big enough to stand in.
Can you guess who these SURPRISINGLY fine feet belong to?

Take care, have a lovely weekend - I hope with lots of nice surprises!

David
