title: Lucid Dreams, The Jab & Penjors
content_html:
Greetings from Affinity Park, Sheffield.

 

Oh boy, it's all go. Your (non-essential) shops are opening again, and everything changes. 

Last week I was telling you about our plans for super cool offices in Affinity and also our plans for expanding the aromatics production.

If you missed it you can read about it here.

I had my vaccine the first day out of quarantine.. and no ill effects at all. Actually quite the opposite, something rather strange is happening to me..

Usually I spend most of my time travelling, India, Indonesia, Nepal, China..and I love it. Working with artisans and producers all over the world..I love it and I miss it so much.  This pandemic has kind of put the blocks on that.

I was lucky enough to be locked down in Bali from February to July last year, regular readers will know how that went and how it came to an abrupt end.  

So I had the AstraZeneca jab, the nice nurse who jabbed me ask if I wanted to go over the possible side effects. "Heavens no!" I said.. "please don't do that, once you tell me I'm bound to get everything on the list including the blood clots".

In China they have a saying; "80% of all illness is in the mind" - I think there is some truth in this, we are all 80% hypochondriacs. Fortunately the nice lady smiled and nodded and didn't force feed me side effects. 

Everytime I switched on the radio, it was news about vaccine problems, so for three days I hardly heard the news and avoided reading anything related. And, yes I can report absolutely no ill effects.. 

 

But the vaccine has given me a kind of superpower, maybe it is just a coincidence but since the jab I have been having the most vivid lucid dreams.. 

Every night a different adventure, I even go to China and Bali in my dreams.. I googled it and vaccine dreams are actually a thing.

 

In Bali they know stuff about dreams.. driving around the island visiting or seeking out artisans chatting to Ringo - is one of my favourite things in life. He explains to me the unique Balanise Hindu belief system. For sure they know things that we just don't understand. 

There are special days in the Bali calendar (a 210 day cycle) when the spirit world comes close to the human world. The ten days of Galungan are the most potent. During these ten days of festivals and ceremonies ancient spirits come to earth to play. The whole island sprouts tall bamboo poles, or penjors, which are decorated with fruit, coconut leaves, and flowers. They appear outside homes and business entrances everywhere. I have been in Bali at this special time quite on quite a few visits.  

 

So naturally I wished Ringo a happy Galungan via Whatsapp.. I asked if we were erecting a penjor pole at AW warehouse.  The penjor is very symbolic, every element of it contains spiritual symbolism. But the basic idea is that the pole sends our prayers and offerings to the heavens, the bowing end of the pole points to earth and it is the route the spirits take to visit us during the ten day romp on earth, to invite them to our business will create good karma and Ringo was delighted make it happen.

Ringo acquired a suitably large bamboo pole and a young pejor design guy came to decorate it on site and then erect it with a suitable ceremony asking the spirits to visit Ancient Wisdom. Ringo of course took pictures and made a short video.


Here is the penjor pole outside our warehouse. The cost of the pole, the decorating guy and the erection ceremony was about 400,000  IDR - sounds expensive but that's about £20. 

Pretty good value to get on the good side of the spirits if you ask me.


As humans sometimes I think we confuse self sacrifice and unselfishness above everything. Obviously good things, but you need to care for yourself first in order to do the other.. in business it's the same (if and when you can afford it). So this is the dream office.. I don't know if it will work like this but we are sure going to try..

Since the day of the jab and the days since roughly coincide with the days of Galungan, maybe the dreams are a gift from the spirits rather than the vaccine..  

Well all I need now is the second jab as soon as possible and for Indonesia to open it's airports.. I'm on my way as soon as possible, if only in my dreams.

 

Do let me know if you too are having lucid dreams after the jab.. 

 

Meanwhile here in Affinity park we are getting really organised, goods can be generally shipped super quickly.. and we have some spectacular deals for you this week.

If you'd like to make some good karma and you are happy with AW then do consider giving us a positive review.. right here. Thank you!

 

Take care, stay safe, dream lucidly.

 

David

title: Pool Boys, Digital Wizards, and a Blood Moon
content_html:
Greetings from Ketewel, Bali.

Yes, folks I'm back to the island of the Gods... I have lots of jobs to do here very quickly, including acquiring a China visa, meeting the Digital Marketing team, catching up with Ringo (our man in Indonesia) and also they need a pool boy... More below.


I got the pool boy job..
Last week I was telling you about my time in Slovakia with Tomas and the team.. Tomas was on TV and discovered that our Queen once visited.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

So from Slovakia I took a taxi to Vienna airport and booked myself onto an EVA  Airlines flight. The first thing I learn is that it's not pronounced Eva like my Mothers middle name, but like you would pronounce TNT.. EE V AAA.. and apparently it is short for Evergreen Airways. I was a little apprehensive because the website and booking process was all a bit cranky with bad taste in typefaces and a very odd logo. So I was pleasantly surprised to find myself on a brand new Dreamliner with big windows, super polite staff and excellent food. A 12 hour flight to Taipa in Taiwan. The plane skirted the coast of the island and I got a pretty good view. It looks mystical and mountainous with large glassy wetlands making land and sea hard to discern. The Portuguese who first discovered it called it Ilha Formosa, meaning "Beautiful Island".  I can also see why it might be hard to invade those wetlands are not boat or tank friendly and the mountains give a commanding view of your attackers.  I spent 3 hours in the business lounge observing Taiwan folk and then onward on a 4 hour flight onwards to Denpasar. 

I was met as always by Ringo and his assistant Bondan.. and as we drove to the hotel they filled me in with all the happenings at AW Indonesia. I had arrived the day before Galungan a Bali holiday.. like Christmas day for Bali. 
So a day full of pretty ceremonies and a chance to get some rest and relaxation. I met Bondan and his wife Debbie for a late dinner on the beach and after walking along the shore we was lucky enough to see the Blood Moon Rise, almost like a sunrise but a big red moon rising dramatically and rapidly into the night sky.. 


Regular readers will recall we bought a beach bar, and turned it into dream offices to help attract the best programmers and digital marketing folk possible. Since I was last here Raul and Peter with Debbie's help have recruited and trained 10 people. Totally AW style multi cultural.. we have guys and girls, Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Javanese, Sumatra and local Balinese people. There is a Buddha statue in the garden, a Balinese Shelf Temple on a wall and a room with prayer mats in the back.  The next day I went along to meet the team. One by one they introduced themselves, (in perfect English) told me where they hail from and what they are currently working on.  My initial reaction - so young and earnest! Like a start-up which I guess what it is.. watch this space because one day soon when we are ready these guys are skilled and primed to skyrocket your business. They are already achieving remarkable results with AW websites. Here is a peak at the website.. it's not live yet and the prices won't apply to AW customers.. AW-Advantage.com



Then Bondan took me to the AW warehouse just up the road. A storm had blown off the roof of the office, but it had been fixed already. New racking in the warehouse because we are fighting for space.. and some new staff to meet.
Also I was thrilled to see some really innovative product samples.. A next level incense burner (idea of Toni in Spain) the prototype has been made and I tried it and it works a treat. That's going boost incense sales and hopefully we can get it to you first ahead of the market.

So it's all happening in Bali!!
Back in the UK - it's all rocking as well.. this month all of August is FREE Shipping.. and we have loads in stock. 
And new things like the Volcano effect humidifiers. Coco found these and I ordered them when in China not long back.. they arrived already! 
They are awesome like a mini volcano and with dramatic effects. Should be an easy sell in a physical shop were you can demo.

Also great for keeping kids occupied in the holidays.. Bath Bomb Kits.. have landed.

I have so much to do. 

Take care have a lovely weekend and once again thank you for your support.

David

title: Swamp Work
content_html:
Last week I was telling you about the Bol Bam, the bare foot pilgrimage from the banks of the Ganges in India... And other madness. You can read it here.
Right now I'm back in the UK, briefly. They are swamped with work. So much new stock and cracking offers (see below) things are really buzzing.. talking about swamps. Continuing my tale of my trip to Kolkata.
Afterwards a couple of days at the jute bag factory doing product development and some creative brainstorming, I asked my host if it would be possible to go and see an actual jute farm. Maybe meet a farmer, especially since this time of year is a harvest period. Our jute craft supplier (check out our ultraeco-friendly jute bags, baskets and stuff) was more enthusiastic than I expected. Turns out that his factory managers, had never met a jute farmer either. So we end up with hunting party, off to the jute farming area.
Skip to the deals below if I’m boring you, but the history of jute (to me at least is fascinating). Originally woven jute was used for sacks and the backing for carpets. It was made in (dark satanic) mills in and around Dundee in Scotland, the raw jute shipped from colonial India. Scottish industrialists developed the trade, then one day some guy had the bright idea of shipping British weaving machines to India.. And in the usual pattern the industrial production was shipped to a cheaper cost base. The Indian mills were (and still are) magnificent and huge, perhaps the first mega factories. I have been round one and seen equipment made in Birmingham in 1820 still in daily use.
At independence (65 years ago) the mills were taken over by Indian interests and formed the basis of the biggest dynastic Indian companies of today. They were serious big business, and the money flowed in the Ganges basin. Then in the seventies synthetic backing for carpets was found, and non-woven sacks replaced jute. The industry and the whole area went into serious decline.
The jute farmers are also rice farmers, alternating crops. It’s a hard life, but there is no doubt that jute is a more lucrative crop. Recent years have seen the condemning of the plastic bag, and the green movement. Jute bags not only replace plastic and can be used over again, but jute crops assimilate vast amounts of carbon, more per acre than rain forest. So jute is a green win-win. Add to this craft and gift uses and you have a real possibility of growth in this impoverished area.
An hours drive into the farming area and we started to spot the 100kg jute bicycles. The raw jute trader only buy 100kg lots, and the farmer generally loads his bike and takes it to the local trader, who, when he has a truck load takes it to the mill.
We found this guy pulling out on to the road and asked him if we could interview him. He told us he would get 2500 rupees, about £28 for his bike load. Which in here in India is good money, where menial work pays £2 a day. Would he show us his farm - he was on the way to the market, but another guy came over and said he would be happy to show us.
I knew that the jute stalks have to soak in ponds for twenty days or so to make the fibres swell, but I hadn't realised that the golden jute fibre is stripped from the sticks actually in the water. We asked our man if he could show us how it was done, he was delighted to show us, and without more ado stripped naked, changed to some other swamp-ware, slipped into the pond and started work. Here is my film.
This little guy was the farmers friend. Lovely chap he shook my hand and told me that he had seen one western guy like me, just once before. My goodness I thought a what connected / disconnected world we live in. Pick up that jute bag in your shop, feel the fibre and think what a different world it came from. When you sell that bag to your customer you are an essential part of the chain that brings much needed prosperity to very poor part of the world.
So when you stock and sell jute products.. Now you have a tale to tell your customers.
That’s why I love this business. Your comments please.
Take Care
David

title: David's AW News: Trending Item Hunt / China
content_html:
Greetings from Yiwu, China


Hope you are well and your gift trading is prospering!
I'm so happy to see we have a good number of trending gift lines right now, join us to get jump on those trends..
Last week I was telling you about our time in Nepal hunting for the next trending products from there. We said goodbye (for now) to Toni and took a few days R&R in Pokhara, where we got high.. you if you missed it you can catch up here. From Pokhara we took Yeti airlines flight back to Kathmandu, 30 minutes only. One of the worlds most dangerous airlines... but we made it.


So we just arrived in China - Coco and I caught the midnight flight out of Kathmandu to Guangzhou. China Southern, a very old plane - seats tighter than Ryanair and fully booked with excited Nepalese workers heading to jobs in China. Outside the airport in Kathmandu we was surprised to see large crowds of people with waving off relatives, it seemed like whole villages had come to see off the lucky family member heading off with ceremonial scarves and heads dotted red for good luck. They gave us the very back seats, next to the toilets.. squeezed in like sardines with no space at all for our hand luggage as everyone had brought far too many carry on bags. I tried to blag us an upgrade to one of the four business class seats at the front, but they wanted big money so we suffered the 5 hour flight sandwiched. Ironically Coco's hand luggage ended up being stashed on the business class seats at the front, I pointed out that the luggage got an upgrade for free, but the airhostess didn't seem amused by my observation.

From Guangzhou we had one of those super short connection times for the flight to Yiwu - they gave us an escort to speed us through the airport, jumping the immigration queue and security and running to the gate. We made it. And surprisingly our luggage also. Which was good because we have lots of presents for the grandchildren from Nepal.. 

Right now as I write this, Tomas is on his way to China. Coco organised a car to pick him up from Hangzhou airport and drive him to Yiwu.. we should see him, later today.
I spent most of the morning trying to hack my way past the firewalls here so I can work and do business here. It's a ridicules and paranoid that they control connectivity and yet want us to trade. 
It's hard work, but at least we can trade with the small family businesses that we prefer. Here in and around Yiwu we have many suppliers. Last time I was here we managed to create the Gemstone Enchantment Lights. My idea (he says modestly) and one of our old suppliers said they could do it.. Boxes designed by our designer in Bali; Bondhan, Coco negotiating, mountains of compliance paperwork later we managed to import them and they have become one of our top trending products. We just received another shipment just recently.. We will be visiting them soon to see what else we can make happen... I have seen a cute irresistible light up gemstone tortoise , which could be your next big seller.. 

Anyway lots to do.. we need to go to the warehouse and sort out some issues. Our landlord has gone bankrupt, and they want to to move warehouse  - and forfeit 6 months rent, It's a bit of a wild west here at the moment. Coco is trying to fix the problem  I'll update you what happens next week.

Meanwhile back in the UK.. lots of new stock, heaps of trending products.. I'm particularly happy with the Chakra Products collection page.. Chakra Inspirations here.
We also have an amazing collection of trending items for Easter this year.. Best ever I think.. 

Take care and happy trading.

David

title: In Transit
content_html:
Greetings

A week ago I was holed up in Bali, writing my weekly news update. I was telling you about my indecision as to when or even if I should make my way back to Europe. You can read about it here.
Events decided for me.. I'm writing this in the vast Qatar airways business lounge, almost the only customer as I wait for my connection to Manchester.
The event if you didn't know was a devastating fire at our main warehouse in Sheffield. If you didn't know, you can read about it here.

In all my life I have never mentally had to deal with something of this magnitude and scale. It's like (for everyone at AW) our own personal 9/11 - those that can remember that event will recall the two jets crashing into the World Trade Centre in NY, played over and over on TV until the images seared into your brain. Tomas was the last person to leave AW at around 6pm on Friday night. There is CCTV in the carpark, and if you have ever been there you will know it is a very secure compound, once the gates are locked you cannot access with both a passcode and a call to the security company with a knowledge of the password. At 23.23 a euro bin in the carpark weirdly started smoking, it burst into flames a couple of times and then died back, I keep watching the video, over and over. Then that furious little fire seems to develop a demonic life of it's own as if it is fighting itself, almost like a supernatural event flames erupt suddenly spraying directly back - it seems at a particular window, behind that window is what we call the oils room where all the fragrance and essential oils are stored in bulk.  The fire flares and burns inside, at exactly midnight - to the second - I guess it was the alcohol IBC we bought for making hand sanitisers explodes, a vast fireball engulfs the carpark and I assume also blew through the internal parts of the warehouse.. within the hour our lovely warehouse is completely ablaze. 
The fire brigade were there super quick, but unable to stop the spread, within an hour everything was gone. Gone. And with it.. it seemed my life's work. 

In Bali, we had an earthquake, not a big one but the tremors continued all week. Quite literally the ground beneath my feet was shaking. Alone and scared, I had to get back somehow. As it happened this week one international flight is available. 
My friends all called me, encouraging me to be strong. My staff in Bali made prayer offerings for me and cried. Keith, our landlord whose property it is, has been super kind and supportive.  
Then the emails started coming.. thousands.. and many many used the word Phoenix.. AW will rise from the ashes.  Take heart, they said, be strong, some wrote poems and some found ancient wisdom quotes. Our customers are amazing.
Many of our competitors wrote directly to me offering moral support. I realise the gift industry is special, special people, we help people give love to each other.. but the simple gift of empathy is a powerful gift indeed. 
I'm 60 years old.. can I face this? Can I really do this?  Friends, those emails made the difference. Thank you.

Tomas & Katka and the team at AW were and are still going through trauma, the emails (I believe) helped them also. Let me tell you the people of AW are amazing - many have been with AW a long time - grown as people with the company over many years.. this event is a character forming. Maybe it is too much for some, we will see, but those that remain will be bound even more by shared experience to the AW family. 
Taking stock.. well all that stock gone, but we still have stock in Spain and Slovakia warehouses, we have 400 pallets of stock held in outside storage and we have some stock in three smaller warehouses on site. Quite litrally all is not lost.
The AW people this week have already set up a dispatch area - and despatched orders, we already ordered a lot of the equipment we need to rebuild production. Our materials suppliers have pulled all the stops out to get product to us.. we will have some production in place next week. 
Bryant our order guy is re-ordering from suppliers in India, Indonesia and China.. Coco, my wife is on it in China.. already shipping one container yesterday with two more in the pipeline. Everyone is on it.
The AW hero's are already fighting back. I will join the fight.. in a few hours I will be there - it's 1.30am here, my flight to Manchester boards at 6.25am, I expect to be in Sheffield about 3pm.
Yes we can do this.. yes we do this - yes - we can rise like the phoenix.  Your support is greatly appreciated. Check out our Phoenix page.  

Only two things survived in Block B,  one was the sign that says welcome to Ancient Wisdom, and one was our big Buddha. The one we pose in front of for group pictures at Christmas and halloween. He still stands looking calm and steadfast. 
I'm not a Buddist but the idea that possessions are not yours but only yours to be cared for, for the greater good. Thousands of people depend on AW. From artisans in Bali to market traders in Burnley to good people who used to work in Block B, AW.
Losing something, Ringo, our man in Bali, told me, focuses you on not being the owner of possessions, just the guardian - the caretaker.  


Once again thank you for your moral support.
People ask me if they can support us with money.. no need, I hope the insurance will do this.. if you want to help, please support my friend in India Mr Chatterjee.. everyday he calls me to encourage me - supports me. Then he goes and feeds people affected by the coronavirus crisis that is rampant in India now.  Up to 200 people a day. These people need real help. Thank you.  Go fundme.   

I'm in transit in Doha, AW is in transit - join us for the journey.. the phoenix rises.

Next Friday I will update you from Sheffield.
Stay safe - wear a mask (we can supply those..)

David

title: Keep Calm it's Buddha Day
content_html:
Greetings, serenity and inner calm. I'm at Ancient Wisdom HQ this week, and calmness abounds. Yes really. 
This week has been busy at AW (a short week because of the Bank Holiday) but we found time to install our new giant Buddha on the entrance to our complex.
Here are some pictures. Looks nice and calming and serene.. don't you think? One guy said "Wow looks great I want one, but I guess they cost a couple of thousand pounds".
We installed it on the 6th of May which just happened to be International Buddha Day, and Buddha's birthday.
Yes, we had one before, our last Buddha, was a little smaller but in a gale force wind the poor chap was whisked away to nirvana. Or maybe he just levitated and landed a few feet away as a kind of sign that we need to be calmer and more unselfish at AW. We don't as far as I know have any real live Buddhists at AW, and hope we don't cause offence to any, but it is strange how the Buddha statue does bring a sense of calm to all who see it.
These statues are made in Yogyakarta on the island of Java. Not far from one of the oldest, and the largest Buddhist shrine in the world.
This is Borobudur home to 504 Buddha statues and not far from our supplier.
They are cast using a mix of resin, cement and gypsum. Hollow inside, so not impossible to move, but solid enough to look and feel like a real statues. Can you sell them?
The perceived value is high, and we can ship direct to your customers, via our drop-shipping site. So in other words, you can have one as a display, and have them delivered to your customers each time you sell one. They truly look the business in any garden, hotel lobby, restaurant or luxury chillout lounge :)
So hoping you find inner peace and calm.. (it says let go of your ego and reflect on your navel here).. have a great weekend!
David
Made in Indonesia and shipped direct to us they represent excellent value.
Available to pre-order.

title: So Excited...
content_html:
Greeting from Yiwu, China.
Last week I was telling you about our new warehouse in Jackfuit Village in Bali, and the strange fascinating social requests attached to the lease.
You can read about it here.
Since then we have spent a mad week rushing round Bali finalising deals and designs, from there we flew to Kuala Lumpa to bond with our newly expanded IT team.
They are now busy working on a new generation drop-shipping system that (we hope) will revolutionise your business and allow you to sell across Europe - whether Mrs May wants you to or not.
I keep remembering that time at the Conservative conference when Mrs May was speaking the letters were falling off the sign behind her. It's all falling apart behind our backs folks.
Do your worst you Brexiteers! We will find away to trade :)
We had a working lunch with the team and bounced around ideas. So excited.. perhaps amazing things can happen, we will have to see how the team gels.
Our IT wizard Raul from Mexico (who lives in KL) is joined by Amila from Sri Lanka a can-do ex-navy guy bursting with big ideas and Sasi a quiet thoughtful South Indian guy.

We welcome them to the AW family and look forward to an interesting journey.
From there Tomas and I flew down to Hangzhou and met our driver who brought us to Yiwu.
Regular readers will know that Yiwu is giftware central in China. 88,000 showrooms are open year round in Futian market - the worlds biggest small items market.
We have offices and a warehouse here. Lots and lots of projects on the go.
It's been busy, like Christmas on steroids at AW we have been working like crazy to get your orders out, while taking in unprecedented amounts of stock as we stock up to cope with whatever happens.
It's all a bit surreal. Our europe customers are understandably worried about supplies and doing a spot of panic buying, but sales are up across all channels. What is happening? Everyone stop panicking.
Meanwhile here in China we are calmly looking for the next big thing, because as I always say it's about the product. Give your customers the right product at the right price and everything else will be ok.
The Packaging Guy.
We have a packaging guy, we used him for years in Yiwu and he can do anything. Anything and super quick. Our day starts in his office in downtown Yiwu, we bring him designs for the next range of packaging for a candle or diffuser or whatever. His office is stuffed from floor to ceiling with every product pack he ever had a hand in designing or producing - and perfect for prompting ideas. He is cool guy, wears funky tracksuits and a bright smile. Give him the ideas, print designs and put the product in his hand and he just gets what it is we want. Computer cad designs produced in minutes. By the afternoon after visiting suppliers and doing the deals we swing past his office to see actual pre-production samples. Tomas says what takes me five weeks in England and costs a fortune, is done here in five hours and is included in the price.
That's the thing about Yiwu, it's not just the products, it's the huge infrastructure you can draw on instantly. Here you really can get things done PDQ.
We should put the packaging man in charge of Brexit.
More news next week.
Keep smiling,
Take care
David

title: Getting Serious
content_html:
Greetings from Malaga airport - 5am.


It's been a hectic week.. lots happening at the Spain warehouse.. and lots to sort out.
But now I'm on the way to Slovakia - our other warehouse in Europe.. from AW-Artisan to AW-Gifts.
The flight is at 6.10am  which means getting up at 2.30am - which means it's hardly worth going to bed.. I didn't sleep at all, just an hour or so full of restless thoughts, and fears of oversleeping.
But here I am waiting for the Ryanair flight..
Last week I was telling you about the "Phoenix Effect" at AW.. and how lots of apparent setbacks have actually turned out good. I explained the set back that gave birth to the team that is AW-Artisan. You can read about it here.

But you know no matter how busy it gets in Spain.. there is always time for a party... or two.
On Friday a container came from Bali, during the week a container from Morocco, a shipment from India, two trucks from the UK aromatics factory and today a container from China. Non of those shipments was straightforward; each one needs special licenses approving, clearance documents, stamps and verification letters.  It's complicated.. but Toni, our man in Spain is getting adapted to getting all his stuff in order..
Despite all this we still had time to organise and celebrate the birthday of Attila.  Attila is originally from Hungary.. so we can call him Attila the Hun. He doesn't seem to mind :)
He's a great guy - works very hard in the warehouse. Last week I was telling you about taking the team out to dinner (another party) and whilst there Attila, unfamiliar with the area, had parked his car in the wrong spot.. His car got towed away, it was a bit of a shock and must have spoiled the dinner for him, but he put on a brave face. Later the team had a collection, (I chipped in) and we raised the €150 that he needed to fork out to get his car back. 
Toni privately gave him the envelope - but Attila whilst pleased that we tried to help.. was having none of it - he made a speech to everyone about how this was wrong - he must take responsibility and he didn't want the money. Because if he did - how would he ever learn from his mistakes.. Like I said.. a great guy..

    Birthday party in Spain, Attila is the guy in the football shirt.


We put on a good spread for him and sang him happy birthday in Spanish and then again in English.. 
Those eastern Europeans are so serious about honour and integrity.. but I think Attila actually smiled.

And now I'm on a plane to Slovakia.. land of the serious.. where the Spanish team work hard and know how to have fun.. In Slovakia they work hard.. and know how to... erm.. have a serious discussion over some seriously strong drinks.. 
No seriously.. they are a great team, work very hard and seriously.. it's been two years - and the team has gotten much bigger than last time I was there. So I'm looking forward to meeting all the new faces, and making a plan for the future.
Tomas will meet me at the airport (hopefully) and we will go straight to the office.

Last night Tomas forward several emails with details of large warehouses.. we are thinking of moving.. upwards and onwards..
It's time to get serious in Slovakia.

I'll give you a full report next week.

Take care and stay safe.

David

title: Freaking Bonkers
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I arrived here earlier this week. Flight from Yiwu to Beijing, then onward overnight to Amsterdam by China Southern airline. Then I was stuck in Amsterdam for 6 hours - finally the hop down to Malaga.
Lovely Malaga, sunny Malaga, nice clean air and smiling people. Including Rodrigo - you remember Rodrigo? The Brazilian guy, married to Jess - Sheffield lass.. Teresa May's Home Office had wanted to deport Rodrigo, heartlessly separate him from his wife and family and send him back to Brazil. We got a minor concession and he was allowed to go to Spain, whilst his deportation was contested. And so for 6 months he lived and worked from my house in Spain. Rodrigo is helping with the Spanish project so he is down here already. Like old times back in the Villa in La Cala de Mijas.

Last week I was telling you about Moon-Cake Day in China. I can't believe it was only a week since Friday the 13th and a full moon was shining over a minor riot in the gardens by our our China apartment. You can read about it here.

It's been a very busy week. We need a folk-lift company, a racking company, to advertise for staff.. we have been back again to our wonderful new warehouse to measure up.
Can you keep a secret? It's currently occupied by a major film studios, who are building sets for a major production there.. we went hoping to bump into a famous person or two.. whilst there was lots going on, it was a bee-hive of activity.. we didn't meet anyone famous.. and if we did we had been sworn to secrecy anyway. Not even a photo allowed, a closed set. Anyway they were all very friendly and helpful and help us measure everything up that we needed. They are out by the end of October and our lease starts on the 2nd of November.. immediately after Brexit. I'm so excited I can barely sleep - or it could just be the jet lag - anyway it's going to be amazing, I have all good vibes about it. Rodrigo is also buzzing, everyone is buzzing. 
Our Spanish website is flying.. although we are currently shipping from the UK, Antonio is doing a good job. AWGifts.es if you interested. 

Meanwhile back in the UK.. everything is beyond buzzing. It's that time of year when it's just gone Freaking Bonkers.. but the team are on it like never before. Warehouse organised.. customer service and a team in over-drive.. buzzing.. I don't really understand why.. maybe it's just that we have the right products.. but we are way up on last years sales.. and (I'm so proud of the team) pretty much keeping up with the orders. Well this is AW we are always a bit behind.. it's always a stretch.. but it's going good. Let me just find a lump of wood to touch.
Lots of new products are flooding in.. we are getting them on-line PDQ.. It seems the theme now is: eco-friendly.. if you & your customers want eco-friendly - and we do, we absolutely do.. then we have it.. Check out the new stuff below.

We are working on the next batch of products.. I was just reading in the Times that the Italian government are encouraging retailers to sell products loose, allow customers to bring their own containers and refill them - cutting out the need for any plastic and packaging. In another life way back in the 1980's I started a business called "Weigh & Save" - anybody remember that? We opened shops all over the UK selling loose food. It's coming full circle.
One project just coming together is to help you retail shampoo and liquid soaps in bulk, high quality products  - customers can buy and keep refillable beautiful containers. If you have any suggestions do let me know.

Next week I will go back to China.. Tomas will be there. Then Malaysia, then Nepal, then India then UK.. it's all getting a bit of a whirl.

Take care.

David

title: Do or Die!
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield

Yes, I'm back in the UK at AW HQ.. ready to deal with Brexit Day..
"Do or Die!"  and "I'd rather be Dead in a Ditch" and "Come Hell or High-water we will be out of Europe on the 31st of October".
So (like the gullible fool that I am) taking Boris at his word, I arranged my scheduled to be here. And... well... of course, erhum.. now it's kinda obvious it ain't happening. I learned one thing.. don't be fooled by all that over confidence bluster. The more ASSERTIVE and BOMBASTIC the statement - the more you should question it's validity..   
Last week I was in India with Tomas - learning the same. I was telling you about the fake glamour of an Indian trade show (complete with lots of BS), and the Real India of Old Delhi, complete with rickshaws, back street go-downs and holy cows where the people are more genuine and deals can be done with-out the BS.. you can read about it here.

Since then we flew to a monsoon lashed Goa for a few days then to Mumbai - then to Paris, changed for Manchester and then the beautiful drive over the Woodhead pass to sunny Sheffield.  

As we left India the festival of Diwali was just kicking off - the festival of lights - comes with tremendous good-will and waves of love. Doesn't matter if you are Muslim or Christian or Hindu.. everyone participates in the festivities. It's definitely the feel good festival of India with lashing of smiles and love all round. As we came in to land over Mumbai, the city twinkled with Diwali lights and fireworks like a magic kingdom. in the airport everyone is celebrating dressed in their finest clothes as if for a wedding. We need to get from the domestic terminal to the international and the best way is to take a local taxi.. A dodgy looking guy in an ancient cab lashes our cases to the roof and we head out into a total party zone, honky traffic and happy people.. our taxi guy once underway, suddenly for no apparent reason begins to sing loudly - grinning when we clap, and doing a pretty good rendition of - I guess Diwali related songs complete with sweeping arm movements. He didn't stop until we reached T2 international. Of course he got a big tip and we took pictures and wished him "Happy Diwali".


India is like that, full of extraordinary people.India is great, but it's totally amazing to be back at the Heart of AW  with the amazing team that devote themselves earnestly to bringing you the best in giftware.. Everyone is working extraordinarily hard. No BS here just genuine enthusiasm for the products and giving the service. But that doesn't mean we cannot have fun at the same time..  Thursday was not only No-Brexit Day but also Halloween, and we have a highly competitive dressing up situation. This year quite a few people up their game and went all out to win the Halloween Costume Competition.. You the customers get to vote.. 
You should have another email with the chance to vote.. Vote and you get a voucher for free stock (worth £27 at RRP).. watch out for the email.

 

Anyway .. it's now November, the clocks have gone back, Bonfire Night is upon us, Black Friday is approaching.. it's serious shopping time.. The CHRISTMAS season is officially launched.
So it's "A Do or Die - Dead in a Ditch Deal".. Rather unbelievably FREE SHIPPING (in November.. unbelievable no?)

Check out the DDD Deals below.. no BS just great deals and fantastic giftware..

Next week I will be in Spain.. 
Please take special care over Bonfire night.. 

Love and Diwali Lights to everyone :)

David

title: David's AW News: Seven Years ago / Travel Hack
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.. 

It's just turned crazy hot (over 30c) and the yellow fire planes are buzzing my house. Lot of news this week.. I have never seen it this early in the summer. 
It's hot and getting hotter in Spain. Last week I was telling you about possible criminals in Malaga.. if you missed it you can catch up herecatch up here. (update below).
I hope you are organised and ready for Father's Day.. now is the time to make hay.. good luck guys!
This week Raul, our IT wizard who was staying with me and working night and day to bring you some tech upgrades (coming soon) had to return home to his family in Kuala Lumpur. I drove him to the airport yesterday.. We said emotional goodbyes. Raul has an interesting travel hack.. that almost always works.. tell you below. 

I really cannot believe it was SEVEN YEARS ago.. 
Another big event (at AW anyway) is the Seventh Birthday of AWGifts.eu in Slovakia.. regular long time readers of this newsletter will remember our founding of that company in response to the Brexit vote. We figured out early (I think before most of our competitors) that it would be increasingly hard to sell from the UK to gift shops in Europe.. we were (sadly) so right in that judgement call was a success at least.
So Tomas, Katka and I went looking for a warehouse and a team in Slovakia.. in the town of Trnava near Bratislava simply because this is Tomas's hometown and it gave us connections. Our original team (Erika, Matej & co) was carefully put together and what can I say except they have far exceeded our expectations. Slovakia AW is now our biggest and trades in every EU country, we moved from our modest warehouse after few years and now work from a big beautiful shed distribution warehouse. We keep expanding and the team keeps growing. Of course we wish them continued success!
They are not big on partying (like our Spain team hahah) but there was coke and cakes.. and speeches..
Well done guys!

Rauls secret travel hack.
Raul is not a business class fan, and likes to travel cheap but in comfort. His flight to KL was via Abu Dhabi. About 7 hours each leg. 
Here's the hack and it takes a strong will not to follow the crowd. You need to overcome the herding instinct. First job.. buy late about 7 to 10 days before you fly.. the cheapest seat is probably an under-booked flight. Second,  travel light, you don't need the overhead locker. Finally, arrive at the gate very late, and wait until everyone else has boarded.. wait a bit longer and then when you are reasonably confident you are last.. stroll on.  Look for the empty row.. and sit in the middle seat..(someone else trying the same trick is not going to take a seat next to you) after take off you claim the whole space to lie down. Worst case you have to use your assigned seat. But he says he has 80% success. A good hack for lone travellers.. 

Meanwhile in Spain..
The (possible) crooks who took our money for three second-hand containers failed to deliver as promised yesterday. Now they are saying the 16th June.. which is too late anyway - we need that extra storage space NOW.. I worry they are just fobbing us until they disappear.. updates later.

Meanwhile in India..
You remember a few months ago Toni and I were on the Epic Asian Tour - in India.. the stock we ordered then is pretty much ready to ship.. there are a lot of products. I'm a little concerned there could be major cock-ups..  So Drishtanta (who is the son of Chatterjee) bravely set out from Kolkata with an assistant to retrace that Epic Tour..  they are visiting every supplier and doing Quality Control checks.. checking a long list of things that could go wrong and confirming specs, labelling, paperwork ect..  He was in Delhi yesterday, today in Agra, later back to Delhi then Panipat and Jaipur.. 
We have a shared whatsapp group at AW and Drishanta is uploading (it seems) thousands of pictures and videos as he checks and tests every product. I think he is doing an awesome job. 
He has already found some underweight issues, some labeling errors.. I think the fact he was coming probably helped sharpen the mind. 
Good job Drishtanta!

Meanwhile in the UK..
We have an India container and China container just unloaded. Lots of fast selling Incense back in stock.
And key products from China also.. stock up while you can.
Also some amazing deals.. including (don't miss it) on Fragrance Oils.

Hope you have a lovely weekend.
More news next week.

David

I hope you are organised and ready for Father's Day .. now is the time to make hay.. good luck guys! This week Raul, our IT wizard who was staying with me and working night and day to bring you some tech upgrades (coming soon) had to return home to his family in Kuala Lumpur. I drove him to the airport yesterday.. We said emotional goodbyes. Raul has an interesting travel hack.. that almost always works.. tell you below. I really cannot believe it was SEVEN YEARS ago.. Another big event (at AW anyway) is the Seventh Birthday of AWGifts.eu in Slovakia.. regular long time readers of this newsletter will remember our founding of that company in response to the Brexit vote. We figured out early (I think before most of our competitors) that it would be increasingly hard to sell from the UK to gift shops in Europe.. we were (sadly) so right in that judgement call was a success at least. So Tomas, Katka and I went looking for a warehouse and a team in Slovakia.. in the town of Trnava near Bratislava simply because this is Tomas's hometown and it gave us connections. Our original team (Erika, Matej & co) was carefully put together and what can I say except they have far exceeded our expectations. Slovakia AW is now our biggest and trades in every EU country, we moved from our modest warehouse after few years and now work from a big beautiful shed distribution warehouse. We keep expanding and the team keeps growing. Of course we wish them continued success! They are not big on partying (like our Spain team hahah) but there was coke and cakes.. and speeches.. Well done guys! Rauls secret travel hack. Raul is not a business class fan, and likes to travel cheap but in comfort. His flight to KL was via Abu Dhabi. About 7 hours each leg. Here's the hack and it takes a strong will not to follow the crowd . You need to overcome the herding instinct. First job.. buy late about 7 to 10 days before you fly.. the cheapest seat is probably an under-booked flight. Second, travel light, you don't need the overhead locker. Finally, arrive at the gate very late, and wait until everyone else has boarded.. wait a bit longer and then when you are reasonably confident you are last.. stroll on. Look for the empty row.. and sit in the middle seat..(someone else trying the same trick is not going to take a seat next to you) after take off you claim the whole space to lie down. Worst case you have to use your assigned seat. But he says he has 80% success. A good hack for lone travellers.. Meanwhile in Spain.. The (possible) crooks who took our money for three second-hand containers failed to deliver as promised yesterday. Now they are saying the 16th June.. which is too late anyway - we need that extra storage space NOW.. I worry they are just fobbing us until they disappear.. updates later. Meanwhile in India.. You remember a few months ago Toni and I were on the Epic Asian Tour - in India.. the stock we ordered then is pretty much ready to ship.. there are a lot of products. I'm a little concerned there could be major cock-ups.. So Drishtanta (who is the son of Chatterjee) bravely set out from Kolkata with an assistant to retrace that Epic Tour.. they are visiting every supplier and doing Quality Control checks.. checking a long list of things that could go wrong and confirming specs, labelling, paperwork ect.. He was in Delhi yesterday, today in Agra, later back to Delhi then Panipat and Jaipur.. We have a shared whatsapp group at AW and Drishanta is uploading (it seems) thousands of pictures and videos as he checks and tests every product. I think he is doing an awesome job. He has already found some underweight issues, some labeling errors.. I think the fact he was coming probably helped sharpen the mind. Good job Drishtanta! Meanwhile in the UK.. We have an India container and China container just unloaded. Lots of fast selling Incense back in stock. And key products from China also.. stock up while you can. Also some amazing deals.. including (don't miss it) on Fragrance Oils. Hope you have a lovely weekend. More news next week. David

title: Strange noises and haunted house
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

Sunset in Ubud

It strange weather everywhere these days.. my house in Spain had a snowfall.. never seen that before - I was there only two weeks ago and it was 22c. While here at AW warehouse Bali the temperature hit 40c the other day and today dropped to a chilly 23c.. 

It's been a busy week rushing around the island catching up with old projects and launching new ones. Last I was hinting at a major new project we have in the offing here on the "Island of Gods" - if you missed it you can catch up here. 
That project involves renting (or buying) a sizable office space, in or not too far from Denpasar city. I really thought that this would be the easy part, but it seems there are not so many options available. As Ringo keeps reminding me we should have done this in the middle of the lockdown, then there were many closed and broken businesses. Not so now.. business is booming.

As we scoot around Bali or walk the streets of Ubud, I keep hearing a noise.. At first I thought it was in my head. Clackerty clack.. clackerty clack.. strangely sound that seemed to induced flashbacks to my childhood in a Sheffield suburb.
I know that sound but couldn't quite place - everywhere I go I hear it.. maybe I'm going mad.

I could hear the sound but couldn't see where it came from.. then I spotted some kids.. doing that clackerty clack thing.. Do you remember them?  If you are old enough (1970's).. you will. I remember them being a little dangerous, and bruised hands and wrists a consequence of mastering the art.  It's brand new craze that has swept all Indonesia in a matter of weeks.. here they call it "Lato-lato" 


This is Ringo's daughter showing off her skills.. It's a classic viral thing.. the noise they make is an excellent free advertising message, and of course every child has to master the skill and do tricks to be cool.


Even Jokowi, the Indonesian president, gave them ago.. 

The thing is should I get Coco on this? They come from China I'm sure.. and do we want to indulge in this even.. 
I remember seeing those Solar pal things in India a year before they appeared in Europe, and the fidget spinners in China also..
I'm not sure they are an AW thing.. but let me know your thoughts.. I'm sure they are coming to Europe pretty soon.

Anyway the search goes on for a nice office, the other day we went to visit a property not far from our warehouse on the main road to Denpasar.. the previous tenant met us with the key so we could go and look it over.
The guy was waiting outside and from his accent I thought he was Polish.. I asked him where he was from and he reluctantly told me Ukraine, and from what was left inside was maybe a holiday tour company - now deserted.
It must have been a big company because the space was huge three big floors lots of rooms off them, a big damp basement and a large roof terrace with views to the sea. 
A big grand old villa, it seemed a bit sad and haunted.. apart from being too big for our needs - the feng shui just wasn't there..


So we keep looking..

Next week Tomas and Raul will be here (Marketing and IT wizards).. I was hoping to have shook hands on a cool office before they come..

I have to go now.. got another place to view.
And lots of new products already underway.. very excited - the creativity in Ubud already running hot.


Take care.. have a wonderful weekend.
More news next week.

David

title: 2 Huge Announcements
content_html:
Greeting from lockdown Europe


It's a lockdown across swathes of Europe again. Friday the 13th to stress us more.. and  only the glimmer of a vaccine hope to keep us cheerful. 
That and watching Netflix, the number one show right now is "Queen's Gambit" - I loved it - it made me cry at the end. It's about a young girl, an orphan, who is thought to play chess by the janitor in the basement, and goes on to become world champion.  A feel good production, with some ups and downs and in the end it's a story about friendship and collaboration.. and now everyone will spend lockdown playing chess. It's a major trend.. So we have some lockdown / chess set deals below.


It's also Diwali this weekend - so greetings to all those that celibrate this. I'm often in India durring the festival of lights.. All our Indian suppliers are readers of this newsletter.. I miss you guys!!.. and so send this greeting:
May the festival of lights be the harbinger of joy and prosperity!
It seems fitting that this celibration about the power of good over evil..  Diwali is celibrated across faiths and people in different ways (and not only Hindu)  for example I know that in Kolkata home of our Mr Chatterjee there they associate the festival with the goddess Kali, who symbolises the victory of good over evil. In Mr Chatterjee factory he has Muslims, Christians and  Buddist and all cellibrate Diwali togeather. Lets hope the vaccine is the light to fight the covid evil. 

Last week I was telling you about a problem with whales.. and about a happy supplier from Indonesia, you can read about it here. But first let me tell you about 2 huge announcements.. one an anniversary, another a christening.. 


On Tuesday next week.. It will be incredibly 25 years ago that Ancient Wisdom was born. As they say on Strictly "it's been a hell of a journey". Just like any good Netflix production, a story with quite a few ups and downs, but thankfully every cloud has had a silver lining..  Born on a street market in Sheffield, all that time ago.. I can remember it well. Here (if you have time) is the story of that first day.. 


It was a wet cold Thursday morning a long time before Google and Facebook, and as I laid out my market stall on a Sheffield street I was more than apprehensive about what people would think. But I was ready by eight, my humble offering laid out on that simple stall.. and stomping from foot to foot I awaited my first customer.


A few months earlier, I'd been reading a book called "Ancient Wisdom" - now out of print. The book highlighted many things that seem out of place in history - the pyramids, Stonehenge etc. At the same time I'd been researching aromatherapy. It struck me that essential oils had been used for thousands of years and ancient people must have known more about them - (healing and enchanting) than perhaps we did. So I put the two together and devised the brand of "Ancient Wisdom" slowly (very slowly, no Internet remember) I found supplies of oils. I found a potter down in Stoke who made me my own design of oil burner, and invested in a pallet load of candles. 

The truth was I was stone broke, every penny and more I put into my unusual retail business. In those days no-one had any idea what aromatherapy was, oil burners were a new fangled thing and this was Yorkshire!


The first person to approach was a well built lady of colour with a broad Yorkshire accent. Picking up a bottle of Lavender oil she asked me bruskly "what's it good for lad?" Oh I said recalling my Julia Lawless quotes.. "it's good for relaxing, will help you sleep and if you burn yourself it's an amazing healing oil". Well I can remember it clear as day.. she looked at me, took me in with big brown eyes, and in a low voice said; "You are completely bloody bonkers". And wandered off to the fruit and veg. You can imagine how I felt. The first day I sold one lavender oil and gave some tea tree away to a spotty teenage girl. I went home and almost packed it in.

The next day, I decided I need to get my act together, and made an offer, Lavender Oil, Oil Burner and a nightlight...I piled the oil burners up in bread baskets with a sprinkling of potpourri for good measure. for £4.50. I sold my first oil burner set in five minutes... and Ancient Wisdom was born. Soon I would sell fifty sets a day and gradually found customers for my range of essential oils. 

I devised a range of Fragrance Oils - I put my heart into that range working nights to get it right, I listened to customer feedback and I'm pretty sure that nice lady who rejected my lavender became a regular customer for fragrance oils.


That was, amazingly.. almost 25 years ago. On 16-11-20 it is Ancient Wisdom's 25th Birthday.

Since then.. the company has grown, with a few ups and downs, to be an international Giftware company, we still sell Lavender Oil, Fragrance oils and Oil Burners. And also 10,000 other products to more than 80,000 customers all over the world. With warehouses in Indonesia, China, Slovakia, Spain and the UK.. we really couldn't have got here without you.Recently following an horrendous fire in July (another down).. we moved to our new warehouse in Sheffield (a huge up!) - from here it is onwards. 

The warehouse has no name.. so we asked for suggestions.. and had hundreds, and after much debate we have decided that the best suggestion came from someone called "Ben" who posted his idea to the AW Blog page.



Calling Ben.. we don't have your contact, please message us so we can send you a bottle of Champagne :)

 

Our amazing customers have always supported this company with feedback, ideas and criticism (when we need it), our customers - YOU - have shaped AW and helped us to our Birthday.
We want to say thank you.. to Ben.. for his name.. and thank you to YOU - for making AW what it is today..

Stand by for some celebration surprises and news next week.


David

title: It's Sant Jordi's Day
content_html:
Greetings from Spain,

Where we are still working on getting AW Artisan our new Spain distributor up and running.
My job here is almost complete, staff trained, products online, orders flowing.. I must move on soon.
Tomas is already moving to Slovakia warehouse. 
Last week I was telling you about the customer service team trip to UK for training.. you can read about it here.

Here in Spain it was glorious and sunny until a few days ago.. 24c last week.. then massive storms, wind and waves and today this..


Can you believe this is Malaga?
Global warming or what, it's certainly feels like things are going to pot.
Meanwhile Coco, my wife (and AW China agent) is back in China for Chinese New Year. Which is this weekend. 
So Happy New Year.. or if you want to surprise your Asian friends say.. Xīnnián kuàilè - yes I know - that doesn't help.. Xinnian.. pronounced "shin knee hen" (say it quickly).. then  kuàilè.. pronounced "Cur why le" now sing it out in a joyful way.
Coco is about thee hours away from Wuhan and there has been one case near by, everyone in the city close to her hometown is wearing surgical masks. The other city now on lock-down is Huanggang near Hangzhou and not far from our China base. Scary times.

Meanwhile here in Spain I think we are upsetting the local competition, someone it seems doesn't want us bringing AW products to our Spain customers. It started with a stiff DDOS attack on the website, fortunately we have defences in place. Raul our IT wizard, who is a genius was on it within the hour and fended off the attack like a Mexican ninja. Then came the gg.gg attack.. this is where the registration page is swamped with dodgy registrations. Raul was a little surprised, he said those attacks cost money.. in an hour 2000 registrations, effectively blocking other people. Some nifty code swatted that away, then bam... 8000 came in the night, even by passing the hidden defences.. Raul was on it.. writing the code and sidestepping the problem. Whoever the fox is that forked out to trash us wasted their money.

Sant Jordi
Meanwhile our customers keep going on about books and roses.. Its Sant Jordi's Day - it's another romantic day here in Spain, especially in Catalonia..



Give someone you love a book and a rose. 
Yes.. it's yet another day of love.. 23rd April. The tradition is you give a Red Rose and a nice book.. The basic idea for Sant Jordi is that men give women roses and women give men books. And it can be anybody, not necessarily your partner or somebody who you have taken a liking to. For this feast, boys buy roses for their mums; girls buy books for their friends. Also, in today's forward thinking society the rules are no longer set regarding who gets what. A girl is just as likely to receive a book and vice versa. So books and roses all round..
And of course at AW we have both a range of Soap Flower Roses and lots of books.. see the deals below.

In Sheffield it's all go.. only days to the start of the "Season of Love"  - Valentine's is almost upon us. It is mad crazy mad mad and more mad busy.. everyone running around like CRAZY. We are getting the orders out.. 
Shortly it will be the Spring Fair in Birmingham.. and people ask which is the Ancient Wisdom stand.. listen folks AW is not there - never has been. So you won't find us. To do that we'd need salespeople and we don't have them (or need them) so we don't do it.
However... our brand Agnes & Cat.. is making an appearance.  Tomas and Tiphanie  - also Rodrigo will be there - so stop by and say hello. 2-6 February 2020 NEC Autumn Fair Hall 3, Stand T24

Come and say Hi..

Next week I will be in the UK.. 

Take care

David

title: A Big Thank You
content_html:
Dear customers and readers.

Here is a quick update from my friend Mr Chatterjee - you will know he is our India agent. 
Right now he is putting his energy into helping jobless people in Serampore his home town near Kolkata.


Almost everyday he organises catering and with help from his group of friends who are also local business people, they feed from 150 to 200 people at a time.
The area is suffering still from lock-down, bankrupt businesses and was recently hit by a cyclone. The conjunction of the two disasters - Covid-19 and Cyclone Amphan is an under reported disaster, in normal times more help would flow.
So Mr Chatterjee is doing his best.. we have had offers of help from several quarters and direct donations..I personally help and AW also.
Quite a few people asked me how they could.. and so I made a quick Gofundme page.. So if you would like to help you can also donate here: 


I just spoke to Mr Chatterjee, and he actually took my call whilst handing out meals.. so I said quick make me a video and take some pictures I can share. He really appreciates this support as it greatly expands what his group can afford to do.  


Thank you for your help
David

title: Mad Marrakesh
content_html:
Greetings from Spain

I'm only here on a flying visit to sign up for a new warehouse, having been in Marrakesh for the last week.
Mad Marrakesh, totally bonkers Marrakesh. Details below.
Last week I was in the UK drinking Yorkshire tea and learning about Smudge Sticks, you can read all about it here.

If you have been keeping up, you will know that Coco (my wife) and I was in Marrakesh in May. where we found and appointed a young guy as our agent and started to put feelers out as to what Morocco can offer the customers of AW.
This time I took Tomas, we flew from Manchester and checked into the same hotel we stayed at before. All the staff were overjoyed to see me again. It was hot in May, but since then it's gone from stinking hot to OMG! it's Sooooo HOT!  - In the day 40c plus and at night it's hot in a different way.

So Aymen our budding new agent took us to meet the Argon family, they owned a farm and Argon press outside of Marrakesh, would we like to see? Yes of course.. so jumped in Aymen's car and soon found ourselves in the desert, driving along a straight road toward the horizon the heat rising, man-sized cactus here and there, scrub-land and the occasional palm tree.  If Hotel California had been on the radio it would have been so apt. The factory - when we found it was in a walled compound, like an oasis in the desert, almost the middle of nowhere. But inside was a small perfectly clean and modern factory, Japanese equipment, staff with hairnets, and in mixed French and English a lady who was the manager explained the whole process of turning argon nuts into oil. 
It was really quite surprising how smart and organised a place could be, and this kind of sums up our experience of Morocco so far. 


The souk and Medina are totally mad, head in there and it's so easy to get lost.. there are no cars because all the passageways are narrow, but motor bikes, barrows and a mass of people flood them. Especially in the evening as people flow through the streets and alleyways heading to the main square - our hotel was tucked away behind a big silver door in the corner of Jema al Fna Square.  After dark, the square explodes into a kind of madness. Snake charmers, guys with monkeys, stalls loudly selling fruit juice, everyone making a racket, but the Berber music troupes are the loudest by far.. sat around in groups, drums and chants with dancers grabbing people to join.. almost trance like. Rumour has it that in the 70's the Rolling Stones came to get inspiration, Keith Richards sitting jamming with the tribal music. Instagram has been a god-send for the locals.. every pose is Instagram ready.. and that's 10  Dirham or about £1 a time.  



We were there five nights and every evening was a different adventure.. plenty of people will to rip you off in grand style, and plenty of other kind people to willing to help you. Deep in the Medina you can get very lost especially since Google maps totally fail, make a left where there is just a wall, send you the wrong way.. some parts are completely local - no tourists, dark alleyways with little shops here and there, a butcher, a sewing shop, a Mosque - everyone praying.. and then an unmarked door, behind which is fabulous Riad with a spectacular rooftop restaurant. 


Doing business in India for twenty years is a pretty good grounding for doing business here.. and like India there are seriously dodgy people and amazingly genuine people, it's not that hard to avoid the former - if you just use your gut instincts and say no.
In the souks it's almost in possible to do meaningful business, it's great fun to make deals - if you have time  - but trader mentality isn't conducive to serious business. There is a professional artisan area on the outskirts of the city.  Proper factories, shipping companies all the infrastructure to do business. And plenty of French people there bringing stunning designs to the traders, many businesses are partnerships between locals and French people.. so we went and walked the streets making friends.. the contrast between the Souk and the artisan industrial estate quite opposite extremes. 

We managed to do a couple of big deals.. soon; if all goes according to plan - lots of lovely Moroccan items coming to delight your customers. 
Tomas asked me what's the big thing from Morocco?  Well I said.. obviously the lanterns, we all know those, then there are lots of gemstones and fossils for rock shops, then of course Argon oil and oh of course.. perfume oils, massage oils.. (all perfect AW items)... but the one thing they have in abundance is... Style.. Style in spades.. the merging of French and local cultures brought forth beauty..  so much drop-dead gorgeous it's untrue.  We went to see the fabulous Yves St Laurent Museum, and your eyes are opened to how (particularly the Berber culture) and local art inspired his designs.  


Very very early tomorrow I'm flying east.. to Kuala Lumpa to see Raul the IT wizard, and on to Bali, to see Ringo (our Indonesian agent) and our other new warehouse..

Full report next week. 

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: Asia begins
content_html:
Greetings from Kuala Lumpur

I just arrived here from Spain. Not without some drama. I was having a last late lunch on the beach with Toni, Tomas and Raul, partly to celebrate the rollout of the new Dropshipping website in Spain and partly to say goodbye (for now). As we were eating the beach grilled sardines ,I received an auto-call that my flight from Malaga was delayed 90 minutes, now since I had a 2 hour connection in Istanbul, that seemed like fun.. but at least had time for another glass of wine... almost missed the connection..
Last week I was telling you about trying not to complain about the hot weather and other complaints.. If you missed it, you can catch up here.

The brightly lit landmass on the left is the European side, and across the water to the right is the Asian side. The Bosphorus is the dividing line where Europe meets Asia.

First Drama of the Trip 
As we came into land at Istanbul, I was able to grab this dramatic view of where Europe ends and Asia starts. A fitting view for my next Asia adventure. And the adventure started with a little drama..I landed with my connecting flight already being boarded and at a gate on the other side of the airport, Gate A1D, about as far as you can get.  Some people on my flight were also on that flight and started to run like crazy.. (my trip.com app said 25 minutes walk that would be too late) But here's a tip: in Istanbul they have freelance guys with electric buggies.. really for old or disabled people.. but give them a small tip and they will crank the speed and wizz you through the airport. I quickly found a guy..  the crook wanted $20, but no time to argue.. as we sped along, he was calling his mates to go help the other runners. We arrived in 12 minutes and I just caught the gate before it closed. The check-in guy said well done and yes, we have your luggage, it will be on board, he showed me on his screen. Wow, that's pretty impressive.  

I arrived in KL early in the evening yesterday, and yes, my luggage made it.. and took a taxi to the town centre to my usual hotel. Terrible traffic.
Today feeling a bit jet lagged but ready for the adventure to come. I had a little walk to catch the vibe of one of my favourite cities. 
Street food shacks, Chinese temples and the world's second largest building. A flavour of KL.

Meanwhile, in the UK.
Holly has been investigating the classic Salt Lamp range
I know many of you sell Salt Lamps.. if you don't then maybe you should.. check out the YouTube video. if you don't yet sell this classic range. If you didn't know... Best quality and prices at AW.

Also in the UK.. big news (kind of)
The British Independent Retailers Association (Bira) has condemned the Government’s inaction over the de minimis import loophole following a Sky News investigation.
Link Here.
They just worked out that the government has lost a Billion pounds in lost taxes it could have raised.. I don't want to sound like I told you so.. why are people so slow to wake up.. we have been banging on about this for six months.. We started a Change.org petition.. 40,000 of our customers signed. Long time ago.

We made a hiphop music video with AI music.. 
The USA stopped it, the EU (are slowly) stopping it.. Indonesia banned it within two weeks.. India never let them in. UK.. well we are a bit slow in the UK.

And at AW not so slow.. we still have a MASSIVE upto 60% off summer Sale.
And this weekend, serious money-saving vouchers.. 

Wishing an amazing, lovely weekend!

All the best.
David

title: David's AW News:Mothers Day in Bali - You will cry.
content_html:
Greetings from the AW warehouse in Bali


Extreme weather everywhere, Spain has massive rain, China unseasonably hot, here we have hurricanes and downpours causing flash flooding - but at least in the UK the sun is shining and Spring is in the air..At least one place in the AW world has some good weather. Last week I was telling you about the lady boss who makes some of the shop fittings we stock. And news from India.. if you missed it you can catch up here. 

Today we went in the rain to the Bali Baby Home, the charity we support here. It's not far from the warehouse, but roads were closed or flooded and we struggled to even get there.
So Spring is in the air.. Mother's Day very soon.. Then Easter, it's Spring!
And if you are looking for quality artisan Dream Catchers, always good at this time of year.. then now is the time to stock up.. (see below).

Trip to the (Dream Catcher) component village.. 
So we heard about this Kampung, a village area not far from the airport.  So we went to explore and see what we could find.  There is one street, where small wholesalers sell supplies to artisans. It was a little hard to find, but behind a row of local restaurants and past a temple and school we found a sleepy street. Small shops stuffed to the rafters with everything you can imagine for making. So we went to explore and see what we could find.
It helps that Bondhan is from Java and can speak the language, all the shops were owned and staffed by Java people. In this way we elicited lots of information. 

One lovely lady in one shop explained that every week a truck load makes its way from Java and deposits stock to her store - the Java artisan produced in home industry fashion, collected up and shipped here to be sold to Bali guys. And the guys that make our Dream Catchers get many of their materials and components this way. In fact the Pastel Macramé Dream Catchers, which are a Spring Best Seller.. we found all the components here. 
I noticed a carton with Chinese markings on it, and asked if actually the components were Chinese, no she said the only place they can get quality feathers was China, and of course the Glue guns that everyone needs but everything else came from Java. 

By the way, if you prefer vegan dream catchers.. yes of course we have.. and recently arrived Glue Guns for you or your crafty customers.

Well we often describe the creations with these components as Macrame, but you could also describe them as Crochet. And famously a genuine crochet machine has yet to be invented, so I asked if the round doilies (above) were machine made, our lady said not, all home industry. And went on to describe how many a lady could make in a day and even gave us a little demonstration.. impressively fast.
For best prices (she suggested) we could buy a truck load direct from her hometown and have it delivered to our warehouse.. what do you think? Is there a market for ready made macrame craft components? The soap flowers components we sell are a big seller and an always growing market... maybe this could be interesting.

However, before we get too excited I have some due diligence and questions.. 
1. Need to check this isn't actually a sweatshop product, 2. that no exploitation is happening and 3. that the cotton used is Indonesian (not Chinese).
Now we have our contact, such a nice happy lady, we can plan a trip to that part of Java and see first hand, like we did the other week with the sarongs supplier in Java. 

Today we went to the Bali Baby home.. 
We have supported it for a couple of years.. but it's still a pretty new Charity. The founder is a lovely guy, who was moved to do something about a terrible problem in Indonesia, unwanted pregnancies resulting in abandoned babies, sometimes dead babies. Often very young girls in conservative areas find themselves pregnant, some runaway in shame, and often to more liberal Bali - Pak Burhan the founder came up with the concept of taking in the girls, helping them with the pregnancy, and then working to reunite the girl and baby with the family. 
We came to pass on a substantial donation, that they will use to make a seperated kindergarten room and employ teachers, because as the years pass the children are getting to that age.
From the Bali Baby Home website:
Will abortion be the solution? Or the baby is born and then thrown away? Have you ever thought when society condemns you, your family ostracizes you, no one will accept you? 
Legal Facts will not side with pregnant women. Abortion is a criminal offence (in Indonesia), while giving birth is not ready? Throwing away is also a crime that is no less than murder?

Social media powered.
He has many success stories that if you hear them will make you cry. But the number of babies not nested back into the community continues to grow, last time we visited he had 21 babies from 1 week to 2 years old, now he has 32 in Bali and we learned 15 and 18 in two new homes in Java. 
Thanks to social media (they have a dedicated guy for this), volunteers regularly come from Europe to help, this time there were two sisters from Southampton and three French girls. The same social media brings visitors everyday bearing bags of baby food and toys. They even found volunteer medics to help with health issues. The babies themselves even have instagram accounts and this aids the renesting process grandparents can get to see and gradually reaccept ostracized girls and babies back into the society. 
The founder Pak Burhan wasn't there today, he is in Java currently, but his manager spent time with us.

It's Mother's Day next Sunday.. (After celebrating the Mothers in your life)  What could be better than supporting these Mothers and their babies and saving lifes? 
Three ways to help.
You can make donations directly on Bali Baby Home website
Or to our donations page, we will pass it on and make sure it is spent on a specific project. Freedom Fund.
Or spend more than £500 between now and Mothers Day at midnight, and we will donate £50 - just write Bali Baby Home (or something) in the shopping cart comments. So we can appreciate your support (but we will do it anyway).

So Bondhan made a YouTube video.. please like and share.. and maybe we can raise more funds because this is so important. 
Take care everyone
Have a lovely weekend.

David

title: David's AW News:  From Kathmandu to Kolkata to the Kenwood Hotel… and a 12-hour sleep
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield. I'm staying at the Kenwood Hotel as usual.

I just woke up this morning after sleeping like a log… a full 12 hours out cold (I’ll explain why in a minute). It’s Friday 1st May — May Day… Labour Day across much of Europe… a full moon… and the eve of a bank holiday weekend. One of those moments where the calendar quietly lines up and says: pause, reflect, enjoy it.

Last week I left you with my strange night in Guangzhou — if you missed that cautionary tale, you can catch up here…

Since then… quite a journey.

I made it safely to Kathmandu, caught up with our suppliers, checked on orders in progress… and yes, even squeezed in a wedding (as you do) see last weeks new..

But the real highlight — a short trip just outside the valley to visit a felt factory.

Now this is interesting… the felt business in Nepal is booming. It’s not just a factory story — it’s a village story. Thousands of people involved. Most artisans actually choose to work from home, and the system is brilliant in its simplicity: small trucks heading up into the mountain villages, dropping off raw materials, collecting finished pieces… even taking waste back for recycling.
There’s a small kitchen on site too. We all sit together for lunch — simple local food, shared stories, a bit of gossip… one of those moments that reminds you why we do what we do.
From there — a quick hop on Buddha Air (a story in itself…) down to Kolkata.
A slightly surreal flight. The air hostess came with cotton wool - everyone (except me) stuffed cotton wool in their ears!  
Mr Chatterjee met me at the airport—and what a moment for him and his family. They’ve just moved into a brand new apartment in a huge, Chinese-style development right on the banks of the Ganges. A real lifestyle step up — and they are proud as punch to have me as their first guest in the “spare room”.
Timing-wise… I arrive right in the middle of the Bengal regional elections. A strange atmosphere—the election commission effectively takes over governance, alcohol is banned, and only one person is allowed on a motorbike (yes, really). It’s all about controlling political tensions. Flags everywhere. Army guys everywhere. Strong opinions. Quite a scene.

Still — we got to work.

Managed to develop some new product ideas with Mr Chatterjee and his son — keeping the factory busy, pushing things forward.

And then… the journey home.

Possibly the cheapest “business class” flight I’ve ever booked — £500 from Kolkata to Manchester via Mumbai. Indigo Air. What could possibly go wrong?

Well… not a flatbed, but what they call “Stretch”. And actually… very decent. Comfortable enough to sleep, excellent food (served anytime), a glass of wine when needed, and genuinely friendly service.

Would I do it again? Yes — absolutely.

Fast forward… I landed back in Manchester Thursday afternoon, got home… and disappeared into that 12-hour sleep.

And here I am. 5am. Writing this. Quiet room, sunlight just breaking. Clear head.

Time now to head in and see the team.
