It’s Friday 1st May — May Day… Labour Day across much of Europe… a full moon… and the eve of a bank holiday weekend. One of those moments where the calendar quietly lines up and says: pause, reflect, enjoy it. title: David's AW News: Secrets & Surprises!
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield, UK.. 


Happy Friday the 13th - don't worry what can possibly go wrong:) it's almost Christmas!

Yes it's true I am actually back at the mothership.. at AW Aromatics and AW HQ.. Home for Christmas... and found some big surprises.
Last week I was making a flying visit to Spain just in time for the AW-Artisan Christmas party, which was lovely and very emotional, if you missed it you can catch up here.
On Wednesday evening I returned my hire car to Malagacar.com (best car hire by far) and checked in for my EasyJet flight to Manchester. The flight was almost empty.. and left early arriving 30 minutes ahead of schedule in Manchester. Whilst the staff were friendly and kind, the seats are basic and the experience is third world.. actually any Indian or Asian budget airline is much better. Then I arrive at Manchester airport, it's such a bad impression for first time visitors.. (apart from Kathmandu) any Asian airport is class. Manchester on arrival feels distinctly 3rd world. It makes me feel something is wrong with Great Britain. But not everything.. 

It was 2am before I made it to my bed at the super friendly and cosy (city centre almost) Kenwood Hall Hotel. If you are in Sheffield I can recommend it. At 4am I'm dealing with some production issues with Mr Suman our Nepal supplier, talking to Debbie our office manager in Bali and resolving some design details with Mr Chatterjee in India. By 9.30am, a little late for work, I get an Uber to AW-Aromatics, a friendly guy tells me he is one of only three Sri Lankan Uber drivers in Sheffield. By the time we make it to work, he has called his friend in Galle, Sri Lanka who has interests in tea exporting and we have swapped WhatsApp numbers. Most surprising morning!

At AW-Aromatics I found the place buzzing with creativity, and visited the beautiful showroom (if you are into creating your own products we can definitely help you). James and Bryant and team have done a great job this year with some truly award winning products some of which we are struggling to keep up with.. 
I was given a really surprising sneak preview of next year's big launch.. top secret - but imagine fortune telling bath fizzies linked to your star sign.. whoops I'm hopeless at secrets.. 
Great excitement as the company was doing it's secret Santa.. 
The Zodiac Crystal Candles are a massive hit.. so we are keen to develop more like this..
Shhhh.. it's a secret.

Then I went to AncientWisdom.biz HQ at Affinity park just across town.. the place was as usual a hive of activity.. delighted to see the return of the Big Buddhas - regular readers may remember my trip with Bondhan to Java a few months ago. Well that container just arrived (the first I hope of many).. Years ago we used to sell these statues made in a vast artisan workshop in a village on the outskirts of Yogyakarta, Java. Bondhan and I called to visit our old supplier. It's a family business and the driving force is the youngest son, who now a few years older has developed the business tremendously . 
They cast in a unique fibre concrete mix all sorts of things, from life size dinosaurs and horses to fantastical fountains. Not many of these huge beasts fit in a container, so minimum order is a 40ft container and they load containers every day. Now the shipping cost of these big things would be astronomical but they kindly allow us to deliver other Java produced stock (textiles, teak items etc) and they stuff them carefully in the void spaces around the big statues. Reducing the shipping costs by half. 

We are interested in the oversize Buddhas - Big Buddhas we used to sell well years ago, but we had issues with them easily getting damaged. Saying that we had one outside our old warehouse to welcome visitors. When we had the fire in 2020 and everything was destroyed, only our lucky Buddha survived (Surprisingly!) and now he sits at the entrance to Affinity Park. 

Teams of skilled artisans cast them in a mix of concrete and resin - and they sold very well but we had issues with them easily getting damaged. Now the technology has changed and the finished statue is harder and stronger. Still surprisingly light, and finished with more detail and polish for a realistic metallic / stone look.  Securely packed individually on wooden pallets wrapped in plastic with foam protection padding.
We opened one and installed it in the lobby to greet visitors. 
Then we held our annual Christmas jumper competition..
Happy Christmas Jumper Everyone!

Well it's almost Christmas.. We have our Christmas Party tomorrow night, so all AW is ready to party.
Finally, more great excitement.. the Ukuleles I told you about from the Guitar Village in central Java.. arrived. We are loving them.. the whole office is learning to play them..
Hope you are having as much fun as us..
Enjoy the weekend. Wishing you lots of Big Surprises!

Take care
David

content_html:
I would like to see something with Lotus in the title as not only a national flower with huge symbolism, but it has the meaning of re-birth, self generation, self enlightenment and purity. Plucked from the web......The lotus flower's daily resurrection is certainly interesting, and surely symbolic of revival. (This makes it the perfect gift for anyone recovering from injury or a traumatic experience.) But the flower also has a fascinating will to live. A lotus seed can withstand thousands of years without water, able to germinate over two centuries later.
The flower also blooms in the most unlikely of places such as the mud of murky river water in Australia or Southern Asia. Not only does it find sanctuary in the muck, but due to the waxy protection layer on its petals, its beauty is blithely unaffected when it re-blooms each morning. It continues to resurrect itself, coming back just as beautiful as it was last seen. With such refusal to accept defeat, it's almost impossible not to associate this flower with unwavering faith. Although cultures have largely dubbed the lotus as a spiritual figurehead, it is most emblematic of the faith within ourselves. 
.

title: Because Magic Happens
content_html:
Greetings from Ubud, Bali

It's getting hot here.. Tomas and Raul both just arrived. Raul (our IT wizard) and Tomas (our marketing wizard) - yes the old team is together and hopefully the magic productivity will spark. Tomas met our Bali team - Ringo and for the first time Bondan.  So let's see if magic happens.
Last week I was telling you about the strange noises - that turned out to be a flashback to my childhood. If you missed it you can read about it here.

Quite a few people wrote to me, advising us against getting in on the Lato-lato craze (in last weeks newsletter). Mostly on the basis that these things can break little fingers, and after the craze dies out there will be tons and tons of extra non-biodegradable plastic on this earth. Yes guys you are absolutely right, so we will leave this craze to the other wholesalers. But when you see it on every street corner.. remember where you heard about it first :)

Ubud is a hot-bed of creativity, you can walk around the streets here and see tomorrows trends unfurling their magical wings day by day. I already have a little list of awesome potential next level products and ideas to boost the businesses of you our wonderful customers.. Now Tomas and Raul and Bondan our creative magical team are on it.. lets see what happens..


Tomas and Raul get to work..

Last week I was telling you about setting up a new business here - it's going to be your superpower - and now the team is here we can really make it happen.
We need a business bank account - obviously.. and I expected to spend a few hours in the bank filling forms and jumping through hoops. But Ringo called me and said come to the office in the morning, the bank manager and assistant are coming to us... our lawyer a nice lady called Corry also came to advise and we had the meeting in our office / showroom at AW Frangipani Warehouse. 
Such lovely people from PermataBank, and banking services and apps that make UK banking look so last century. I remember opening a personal account with them ten years ago and being surprised about how informal and security free the whole experience was. But this was next level service. When was the last time you bank teller bowed with namaste style greeting? 


Even though there was like fifty forms to fill in and signatures on every page, they came prepared with almost everything prefilled in, the lawyer checked everything and Ringo and I just signed and signed..
The business bank account has all the usability I would expect.. multi currency, interest on balances, ability to create payments (the accountant) and approve them by another person. So absolute control.

Our dream offices are actual quite close to the warehouse.. there is a restaurant and creative hub called Masa-Masa. It's in a totally undeveloped area, pretty much standing alone in a rice terrace area not too far from the sea.
The owner is a lovely gentleman from Sumatra. He bought the land and invested in it only recently. There is an open plan area restaurant decorated impeccably in Sumatran styles and two showrooms that display a huge collection of premium quality Indonesian giftware.. yes this guy has been in the giftware business almost as long as me. He has a team of designers and marketing people working from Joglo style offices in the grounds.. 
Some of the space - just enough for our start-up - is available.. and I already pitched him with the idea we could rent the space for a couple of years. After a few days he sent me a long WhatsApp apologising and saying that he was sorry but they didn't feel they could host us.. 
So we went for lunch, Tomas, Raul, Bondan, Ringo and myself. The guy was there in the restaurant area and greeted me warmly.. I introduced him to Tomas and Raul and he granted us a second guided tour.. Tomas turned on the easy-going charm and maybe it worked.. he said he would re-think our offer, speak to his team and get back to us next week.


OK there are a few options on the table, but for me this feels good. Close to the AW warehouse, not far from the city, beautiful place, tasty food, perfect coffee, already with giftware connections and lovely people. So this is my dream location to plant and grow our new business. Well as they say.. if you don't have a dream how can you have a dream come true. Fingers crossed. 

Well it's the "Season of Love" in full swing.. are you ready? Valentine's day is very soon, and then Mother's Day.. and the Wedding season.. At AW we have what you need to be ready and able to satisfy your customers.. check out our Soap Flower products, perfect and top selling.. Bath Bombs are trending again.. and we have a bigger and better range.. Candles are trending.. and again you won't find better..
Get ready for the Season of Love. You can make the Magic Happen in your business today.

More news next week - take care.
Hopefully will have good news about the new office.

David

title: Un-mistakable smell
content_html:
Hello, right now I'm in Java, Indonesia discovering some new suppliers and checking one one or two existing ones. 
I also had to take a trip to the relatively undiscovered north of the island, To get there you have to cross over the volcanic ridge that rises over 2000 meters in the centre of the island. I have to say it is not only a fantastic trip with grey monkeys, glassy lakes, dramatic drops and awesome volcanic feature's but really botanically interesting. The road takes you past every kind of plantation, orange groves at lower levels, then past vanilla and coffee plantations. Everything seems to grow here in this lush land; Chilly, Cinnamon, Coffee, Coriander, Cumin, Garlic, Ginger, Lemon-grass - I lost track.. Along the way you are invited to stop and enjoy the views whilst sampling some of the worlds finest coffee. Cevet coffee (Kopi Luwak) is the best and most expensive, I learned not to ask for the best coffee.. not because of the price. Because, well it is produced in a pretty unorthodox way. The cevet is a small cat/weasel like creature that loves to eat fresh coffee beans. It has a nose for sniffing out the very best beans, however it doesn't digest them totally and they pass through the little creature somewhat enhanced and partly fermented. These specially processed beans make the best coffee. You have been warned.
Over the top of the volcano past the temple in the lake, built after the last eruption you descend through lush rain forest complete with dense green trees stretching out for miles like super tall and rather regal privet bushes. With the window down I could smell something distinctive and faintly nostalgic. But could I place that smell wafting on the warm breeze? In small villages long plastic sheets filled every available sunny spot sun drying something dark brown. On the side of the roads were long bamboo poles made with cross sticks.
On the edge of the road some guys were bashing one of the tall trees with the bamboo pole and like amber rain pods were tumbling. Turns out on investigation that this is a clove forest and we were there in the midst of the harvest. A lucrative business Ringo (our agent) told me, cloves fetch around £4 a kilo from traders, vastly more than rice and with far less work.
Somewhere here, I thought, must be someone distilling beautiful clove essential oil.
I'm working on it..
Then the smell came back to me.. yes I know that aroma.. it's "Old Spice" circa 1985.
More news next week.
Regards
David

title: It's Been a Hell of a Journey
content_html:
Christmas Greetings from Spain

 

This dear friends is the last proper newsletter of 2020.

And what an Epic, Traumatic, Overwhelming,  Sad, Joyful, Stressful, Triumphant... if there is one word that describes 2020.. it's probably one my mother would not approve of..

Everyone has had one hell of a year, I know many of you have lost loved ones, have struggled with covid hit business, have had to face unmanaged challenges. But together it is possible to pull through and even dare I say it be stronger and thrive.

 

If you have been following this newsletter you will know something of this extraordinary, unbelievable year at AW.

Last week I was telling you not to worry.. we have a Brexit plan.. You can read about it here.

This week if you will indulge me I'd like to share the 2020 AW journey with you.. below.

 

But first - some good news - a massive backlog of containers and stock deliveries have arrived at our warehouse in Sheffield. We have been seriously struggling to keep many products in stock for all the reasons you well know about, but this week we are happy to have lots of best selling lines back in stock.. containers and shipments from EU suppliers ahead of Brexit  came, two more containers from China, one from India, one from Indonesia. 

I can confidently say we are Lock Stocked and Loaded ready for the 2021 season of love - the sales, the run upto Valentines day, Mothers day, Easter (which could be a mini Christmas) and fathers day.. The season of love, we call it.. and AW is dare I say your best supplier at this time.  Check out the deals below. We can take orders upto 3pm on Tuesday 22nd December for dispatch this year. After that we will dispatch in the new year, your order placed early will mean early dispatch.


January

My 60th birthday was perfect, surrounded by my friends, family including Coco, Tomas and Katka from AW and our new friends from AW Artisan Spain. A nice meal in Sinbad's restaurant on the beachside, a lovely day all sat together at a long table (do you remember doing that) enjoying good food and wine chatting and enjoying each other's company. My idea of a perfect time. One small shadow.. Mario, who is our company administrator in Spain, complained of feeling strange, the perfect gentleman he is, he joined us for the meal but insisted in not hugging and kissing all and sundry as usual - and placed himself at the end of the table and slightly away. He spent ten days in bed after with a mysterious illness, it was quite some time before he was back to full health - he is convinced he was an early victim. Two days later, I dropped my wife Coco at Malaga airport, she was heading home to China for Chinese new year. The plan was that I would go to Indonesia, India and then to meet back up in China in six weeks. Little did I know this was the last time I would see Coco this year..



February

Late Jan and early Feb is spent in the UK at AW HQ.. planning the future, working out what products to focus on to delight our customers - I'm especially excited about our new dropshipping website.

AW doesn't do tradeshows, but we did showcase our Agnes and Cat brand at the Spring Fair in Birmingham. I drove down to visit the team and see how it was going. Coronavirus was just beginning to raise its ugly head, notices on the entrance if I remember asking recent visitors to China to get a temperature check. Nobody had any idea what was about to unfold. 

7th of Feb I fly to Kuala Lumpur. Meetings with our Pakistani salt lamp suppliers, a father and son business.  Also working all hours to get the dropshipping website finished with Raul the IT wizard who works out of KL. 

I notice people in the streets wearing masks, The hotel I stay at checks everyone's temperature, supplies hand gel, and strictly only allows registered and guests into the lobby. There is an air of panic.

10th Feb the Dropshipping site is launched.. 

11th Feb - I take the flight to Bali.. Ringo meets me at the airport. 

The next two weeks are spent in a whirlwind of activity - recently moved to a new warehouse, I also want to make it the most beautiful warehouse in Bali.. 

While we are working, the covid crisis is slowly becoming apparent, but no panic, people selling homemade masks on street corners, government posters already advising keeping distance and washing hands (this is way ahead of the UK).

26th Feb I fly to Kolkata, India. Flights are normal - no special measures. Check into the Swisshotel close to the airport in the early hours of the 27th.

In the morning meet up for breakfast with Tomas - who arrived earlier and Mr Chatterjee, our man in India. It's great to be back in India. 



March

We stay at the newly opened Denmark Tavern, a restored heritage hotel on the banks of the Ganges. We visit the children's home  that AW supports, news of the pandemic is coming but we still high five all the kids. 

Later fly to Delhi to meet a whole range of suppliers, it's hard work. Deep in the crammed and busy back streets of old Delhi building new relationships. I do remember thinking if a virus gets loose in here it could be hell.  

Rumours that India will close the airports and lockdown, seem fanciful at this stage.

We fly down to Goa for a few days' rest and to meet our gemstones guy, who comes from nearby Mumbai. 

Flights are being cancelled. There is panic buying of masks, all the Japanese and Chinese tourists are wearing masks. Allsorts of rumours. Tomas and I decide maybe it is time to cut short the India trip - we manage to get a flight back to KL via Bengaluru.

Our flight to China has been cancelled, so we decide to go back to Bali, and see what happens. Anyway Tomas wants to see the new warehouse and has lots of product ideas.

We escaped India it turns out just in time.. days later all flights are cancelled.

By late March - it's all kicking off.. Tomas decides it's time to go back to the UK, and he actually gets out of Bali on the last flight before lockdown. I stay hoping to find a way to go to China, or at the very least for Coco to come to Bali.



April

Lockdown in UK.. Sales drop dramatically.  I'm trapped in Bali (which honestly could be worse). But tough decisions have to be made. We furlough most of the staff. Katka throws herself into making AW as covid safe as possible for the remaining staff.

It's bleak.. we are making survival plans. All the shops are closed, how long can we survive? Will our customers' businesses survive? I call and ask all our landlords for discounted rent, they all help - the new landlords in Spain (who are Chinese) give us 100% discount until whenever this is over. 

Sad news, my Father passed away, coronavirus - he was always there to help at AW, for a while a non executive director and always a wise advisor - a strange zoom memorial service.

 

May

My hotel in Bali closes down. There are no tourists left, I'm the only customer. So I need to find somewhere to stay, and new government regulations stop hotels from accepting new guests, I'm almost homeless in Bali.

Meanwhile in UK we are making soap like crazy, devising our own AW hand sanitisers. Tomas is working on designs for a range of face masks, Coco in China looking for suppliers. The new dropshipping site is booming.

Amazingly, sales are picking up.. so we start taking staff back off furlough.

I'm happy developing lots of new products with Ringo in Bali. We also make beautiful new offices and staff rooms at the warehouse.


June

What happened? Tomas and the team are working twelve hour days, the aromatics factory is at full stretch. Extra shifts, so we can keep covid distance. It's all go, we have gone from bust to boom in the space of a month.

June which is normally the quietest month of the year at AW turns out to be the best on record. 85% up. Lots of our switched on customers are moving to online sales, dropshipping goes crazy. We pay back all the rent to our landlords. Everyone except the vulnerable are taken off furlough. Where possible staff are working from home, covid restrictions and work pressure means everyone is exhausted.

Meanwhile Bali is like the Garden of Eden, no planes, no tourists, a gentle, green quiet place. Locals delighted to do business with us. I'm ashamed to say I was having a lovely lockdown.

At the end of June all the management at AW are sending each other well done emails.. in my last newsletter of June.. I write about how busy it's been.. and I quote..

"Of course we are thankful for the business, a few weeks ago it seemed like the world would fall in. Who knows what the future holds.. Stay safe please, wear a mask.
Enjoy the weekend".

 

July

3rd of July, I will never forget being woken by Whatapp at 7am and seeing Tomas's tear stained face framed by a massive fire. "David it's over, it's over"

Our main warehouse, factory and head office were engulfed in a huge fireball. Parkwood business park is on top of a hill, the whole of Sheffield could see the fire, one of the largest ever in Sheffield.

A eurobin in the carpark had self combusted at 11.23pm by midnight the fire had spread to the room where we kept the essential oils, which had spread to the area we were making hand sanitisers, alcohol in 1000kg containers.  There was a massive fireball explosion which a hot summer wind that night blowing exactly the right direction blew the fire like the bellows in a furnace through the warehouse block. All captured on the car park CCTV system. In two hours despite the fire brigade arriving in minutes it was a burned out shell. 

A rest in peace AW facebook page emerged the next day. Everyone assumed it was over.

9th July I managed to get on the international single flight out of Bali. On the 10th Tomas picked me up at Manchester airport, and drove me to see the devastation.

We had already made a recovery plan. Are we going to let this thing beat us? Or are we going to turn it around?

Within the week we had a dispatch department in operation,website revamped and was back in business.. the rebuild had started. 

By a stroke of luck the Facemasks had been delayed by two days and arrived after the fire - turned out to be a huge best seller.


August

The big search for a new warehouse.. the stress that the insurance company may not pay out.. re-ordering, rebuilding managing with almost no space in our surviving warehouse. 

All credit to the AW Heros, almost everyone pulled together, working amazingly well. Rebuilding the factory from scratch,  all our suppliers pulling out all the stops to help. The thousands of emails and messages of support our customers.

Finding a warehouse proved to be harder than imagined, a short list of ten dwindled to two or three.. there are not that many large warehouses empty and ready for occupation at short notice. 

The one place we liked was actually big.. three times bigger than our old place. The problem was the owners didn't want to rent it, they needed to sell it. And the price was more money than AW could raise in the circumstances. The answer was a longshot.. find an investment fund to buy it, and then rent it back to us.. 

 

September

Stressful in the extreme, so much uncertainty.. insurance company not communicating.. deals grinding slowly along. 

But it all comes together and we persuade enough people to trust us, the owners of what will be Affinity Park allow us to use the 100,000 sq ft warehouse on license pending the sale and lease back. The insurance company finally paid up, and we can afford to move forward. 77 days after the fire we got the keys to Affinity Park.



October

A huge backlog of shipments arrive at the new warehouse, the offices are quickly set up. Everyone again is working round the clock.

We really are back in business. Meanwhile the factory rebuild continues, we buy a big machine - nicknamed the beast to produce natural soaps from a French company. If you have been reading these newsletters you will know the details.

The stress takes a toll on my body..I need a change of pace and a rest.. once the train is back on track I return to my home in Spain to focus on the rest of AW. The Spain warehouse is now really busy and Slovakia also.

Coronavirus has had an unnatural boost to business as online trade booms and people across Europe want things to make their homes more cozy, safe and aromatic.

 

November

Now the focus moves to Brexit, and how we are going to manage when half our trade is to EU customers.

Sales across AW are good, 92% up on last year. Seems incredible that we could go from despair to boom to bust and back to boom in such a short time.

The property fund finalises the deal and the lease we have been simultaneously negotiating comes into being.  

We also celebrate our 25th Anniversary of AW - it's 25 years to the day I sold the first bottle of Lavender oil on an outdoor market in Sheffield (story here).. And Ben in Ireland comes up with the name "Affinity Park" - for the new warehouse which we all instantly love. 

 

December

I'm still missing my wife Coco, we speak everyday but almost a year is a long time.

The vaccine gives some hope that international travel may start up and it is possible to go to China.

Borris says have a Merry Little Christmas.. 

Will be very little in my case.. but there is hope. All the people around me at that birthday table in January are still with us, and all the rest of the AW team in the UK and around the world .. but for sure they changed, forged in that fire that quite literally changed them into AW Hero's that will take AW into 2021. Come with us on the journey!

 

Take care - I will write the year's final message next week.

Stay safe, 

 

David

title: David's AW News: Fire Jumping and other strange things.
content_html:
Greetings from Spain on the day after the longest day.

Hope you are doing well and the summer is treating you well so far.
It's the Euro season and usually not a good time for the gift trade, but let's see how it pans out this time. 
Last week I was telling you about a new age in retailing.. the live streaming influencer.. there is big money to be made in this.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

It's a real Ancient Wisdom time of year.. around this time almost every culture has developed Ancient Wisdom practices and rituals.
To celebrate... We have some ritual type products on offer for you - (plus a free gift on all orders over £200).. 

In UK - It's all about Stonehenge.. it is the focal point of summer solstice celebrations. Thousands gather at this ancient stone circle to witness the sunrise aligning with the Heel Stone, a spectacle dating back over 4,500 years. Druids, pagans, and orange paint protestors.. participate in rituals, music, and paint throwing. Check out our Pagan products..
To purify and protect in Spain.. Toni tells me.
Here in Spain this weekend it's all happening..  Noche de San Juan, or St. John's Night, is a lively celebration marking the summer solstice. On the evening of June 23, beaches across Spain will light up with bonfires and fireworks. In old days (before health & safety) people would jump over fires and into the sea, traditions believed to purify and protect. Except that jumping over fires and swimming in the sea whilst drinking sangria turns out is not particularly purifying or protecting.  It's still a night of music, dancing, and joyful gatherings, celebrating light and renewal. In Malaga a huge midnight beach party.. (of course)

Ringo (our man in Bali)  tells me the summer solstice coincides with Purnama Sasih Sade (Full Moon Celebration) - it happens tonight also on the beaches like Spain but very different...  he tells me it's all about purification and renewal.. Catch the Bali vibe with our Bali Parasols.. 

Meanwhile in India - Chatterjee tells me.. .They are hoping that the Solstice (as it often is) will bring the cooling Monsoon and some relief from the heat.   Meanwhile Mr Modi, the world's biggest  yoga enthusiast is making everyone  participate in International Yoga Day today, engaging in mass yoga sessions that highlight wellness and spiritual harmony. So that's also an Ancient Wisdom thing.. Check our Chakra Yoga mats (they sell great any time).

And in China. Coco (you China agent) tells me the summer solstice is called.. Xiàzhì, and is a time for honoring ancient customs and nature. Traditional foods like dumplings and noodles are enjoyed, symbolizing prosperity and longevity. The Dragon Boat Festival, though not always aligned with the solstice, is celebrated around this time, featuring boat races, zongzi (sticky rice wrapped in leaves), and commemorations of the poet Qu Yuan. By the way Money Cats are back in stock..


I didn't know this but in Slovakia, like in Spain they like to jump over fires on the Solstice, a tradition.

These diverse celebrations all over the parts of the world where AW is working.. all show how we are different yet somehow all the same..AW is your natural Summer Solstice Supplier.. so stock up now to harness the magical powers and boost your business! 

Anyway whatever you are planning, jumping over fires or watching the football.. I hope you have a wonderful weekend.


Take care

David

title: It's an Adventure!
content_html:
Greetings from Jakarta

We didn't plan to be here more than a few days, Coco was on her way back to China. In last week's newsletter was telling you how it all went horribly wrong.. if you missed you can catch up here.
Last week was also a major milestone in our EU distribution centre in Slovakia, you can also catch up with that news.
So Coco tested positive and her flight ticket was cancelled. At first we had no idea what to do.. but when the clinic told me it was a borderline case - we went immediately for a retest.. that came back negative, confirming my feeling that it was probably a false positive test. I googled the type of test the Chinese authorities insist on and sure enough they expect a 2% rate of false positives. But it was too late anyway.
Since there are only flights to China on a Monday.. we have to wait a week.. maybe more.. according to social media advice once you have a positive test you need to wait a month. Problem is Coco's visa will expire on the 3rd of September and if you overstay you can be blacklisted..

You can get stressed in these kinds of circumstances or you can just accept it as a grand adventure and do whatever you can. Coco is happy.. me too, at least we can spend more time together.. even if it is in a self imposed semi-quarantine in an apartment-hotel. Coco is calling the Chinese travel agent.. but they have no solution. I called the visa agent back in Denpasar, Bali.. they were super helpful and have found a way to get an emergency visa extension. It will take a few days and cost money. That arrived yesterday.. in the form of a letter we can print off and Coco can give to passport control. So at least she is legal.

Then two days ago we got good news: the system has been changed and now she must get 4 different PCR tests from different clinics over two days.. all a bit vague, no proper addresses. 
Coco asks for street addresses, because in Jakarta there are a lot of Medistra Hospitals.. the agent doesn't know.
Here's what they sent us.. to get from one place to another could take hours.. 


Now as you know Jakarta is one of the biggest cities in the world, it is well known for having the worst traffic in the world. Even with an odd and even registration plate system the traffic is horrendous at all hours. You can walk faster.


Check on Google maps and on foot comes up often quicker. But as we found out it's not a good idea.. we tried.. the other day we decided to walk to our previous hotel just for exercise and to see what we might see.
But it was not a good idea.. nobody walks here, first it's too damn hot and humid, second the pavements are often blocked, third Google maps wasn't working good on foot. We ended up lost, dripping with sweat and feeling rather foolish. I gave in and called a Grab (like Uber) and we learned our lesson.

So yesterday we went to the Medistra Hospital nearest to us to check if this was the right place. We found the PCR testing station and asked.. the people in hospitals (or anywhere) are unfailingly nice and helpful. They didn't know, but they checked the computer, no the couldn't find a test listed in Coco's name. But we should go and find Mr Little.. he would know, because he was the China guy. A security guard help us find the right place and we knocked on a door, it was immediately opened.. come come..  Mr Little sat behind a tiny desk in a camped office with a nurse at his elbow.. "how can we help" in good English. We showed him the paper, and asked if this was the right place.. after a bit of checking he told us yes, Medistra Hospital had been contracted to do the tests, but they were to be done in a hotel across town. He gave us the address and recommended we get to the first test at 7.30am - should start at 8am you will need to be early to make the second appointment.. he gave us the mobile phone number of his China contact and wished us luck. 

So it's 6am - The Chinese powers that be, have set us a test with just few random clues to help.. we have to from one end of the worlds biggest city and back, two days running. If we miss the test we are dead, no second chances.. it's like a challenge game.. and those tests have a 2.5% chance of a false positive.. so that's a 10% chance (4 x 2.5%) plus whatever the chance of actual an covid infection (I calculate about 0.03%) .. do you think Coco will make it back to China? 
Coco's social media fan club on Chinese TikTok have lots of suggestions and advise.. everything for taking anti-viral drugs a few minutes before the test - to paying bribes to shadow agents to smooth the way.. not a good idea.. we will take our chances and play the game..

Will she make it?. Certainly her family, her mother and the grandchildren want her back.. everyday they call, I think they are beginning to worry that she might never come home.   I'll let you know next week what happens.

Meanwhile back in UK.. 
It's September - welcome to the official start of the Christmas season. And already it is getting busy. A few weeks and it will be Halloween and Bonfire night.. then the clocks go back and the nights draw in. This year we are going to need a cosy comporting Christmas.. My feeling is candles, fragrances and pamper gifts to ease the troubled times we live in.. 

We have plenty of deals and offers coming your way.. including specials on 33 Indonesian products.

Take care, more news next week.

David

title: From Xiamen to Sheffield
content_html:
Greetings from Sheffield UK..

Yes we are not in China anymore.. last week I was telling you about the Gemstone back streets of Yiwu in China, and spilling some trade secrets. If you missed it you can catch up here.
From Yiwu we took the train to Xiamen four and a half hours south and noticeably more tropical on the coast the city facing Taiwan. It's a lovely island city with a holiday vibe, and so we enjoyed a couple of days being regular tourists visiting the small historic island of Gulangyu just off the coast and walking around the beautiful Siming District. We realised that we had actually been here 10 years ago. Just outside our hotel was the spot where I took a picture of Coco. The world changed so much in 10 years.. but Coco still likes to scare me by posing on top of walls.
 


Gulangyu is a fascinating place. No cars, so you have to walk everywhere. And everywhere ancient (in many cases) crumbling but still impressive villa's once owned by wealthy traders. The island was divided up in the same way that Shanghai was by colonial Europeans. You can see that many fortunes were made and lost on these rocks.  We climbed to the highest point: Sunlight Rock where you can admire the modern Xiamen city on one side and glimpse in the distance the Island of Taiwan. Which in itself is of course a massive shadow hanging over the good trading people of China.

I had expected to see jets flying overhead, warships in the bay, guys in army fatigues in the streets. But nothing - actually everything was normal, subdued but normal. 
From Xiamen we took a friendly local taxi to the airport and Xiamen Airline to Amsterdam (11 hours), changed for Manchester Airport (one hour) and was met by our James (aw-fullfilment.com) manager who loves to drive to Manchester and pick me up, because we will usually stop off for a pint of pale ale and catch up with everything going on.  That was all day Monday travelling.. we left at 10.30am and arrived at 7pm the same day but strangely jetlagged.
Now it's Friday and I still feel a little jetlagged.. 

Coco was interested to see how things have changed at AW since she was last here (just before the pandemic) and also meet in person the people she messages everyday, plus catch up with old friends. So this week has been a massive catch up time. 

Today an Indonesian container arrived, they are unloading it now. I'm of course quite excited to see lots of new products arriving.. especially the Healing Powder Incense - made by three holy men which regular readers will know the back-story about.. and the new ritualistic way to burn incense - I'm sure your customers are going to love it!  Here's the news letter link.   See details below.. 

It's great to be home. Only four weeks to Father's Day and all is a bit of a buzz.. We have brilliant gifts like this, and more arriving by the day.

Plus it's all happening - big changes - at  AW-Aromatics. The factory is in full swing making new fun bath bombs, but also did you know if you want unlabeled essential oils, bulk essential oils (or any ingredients) you can now buy direct from the aromatics factory.. We realised that packing and shipping, storing and shipping these low margin things from one side of Sheffield to the other and shipping them again.. was well just a bit mad. So we open up lower prices direct from AW-Aromatics.com - sorry you will need to register there also but get the keenest possible prices. 

Lots of work to do, lots of catching up, lots of plans to make.. it's all go as usual.
Take care - have a lovely weekend. 

More news next week.

David

title: David's AW News: Muggy Weather & Mooncakes
content_html:
Greetings from a humid Yiwu, China

Yes I made it to China, and I can tell you it is unnaturally hot here.. The streets are oven hot with a humid hair-dryer-breeze. Evenings are sticky and tropical.
From Bali I took the daily China Southern flight, which leaves every day at 30 minutes past midnight and arrives in Guangzhou five hours later. A big storm further up the coast was blasting Shanghai and I think we were feeling the effects, we had bouncy turbulence for almost all the flight. In Guangzhou I cleared passport control and made my way to the domestic terminal with a flight at 11am to Yiwu. We landed in Yiwu on time and my luggage arrived quickly, within minutes I find Coco waiting for me at arrivals. All seemed pretty smooth and it is amazing to be back in China.
Last week I was telling you about foreigners behaving badly in Bali.. if you missed it you can catch up here.  
Coco.. and Tomas is also here..

I arrived just in time for the Mid autumn festival.. or as I call it Mooncake day.. all our suppliers send boxes of mooncakes, some nicer than others but far too many to eat.
It's auspicious this year because not only is the festival on a full moon, but a super large harvest moon,  a lunar eclipse sending the moon red, and a visible comet in the night sky. All these astrological events the Chinese believe predicts major events in world affairs. Feels strange.. The hot humid sticky weather adding to the strangeness.
At this time in China.. Moons and Rabbits everywhere..
Anyway so Tomas arrived, and we hit the ground running.. visiting existing suppliers first and checking out the projects already in development. Our designers have been super busy ahead of our trip here and now we need to make things happen.. which here is fast and fun. 
Only had a couple of days to check out new stock ideas and we have lots! Almost beside ourselves with excitement!  I think a lot of creativity has been going on this summer.. that means we will have stock on the way for Spring, Easter next year that going to be awesome.. 

Here is Mid-autumn festival but in Europe it's the Equinox.. and that means it is officially autumn - making the start of the "back-end" in the gift trade.. Time to think about Christmas.. and Halloween
We had a lot of stock delivered this week.. I know the warehouse team have containers most days. Lots back in stock.. a quite a lot of new stock.. Including some India stock which has taken forever to arrive here, mostly because if the shipping container delays, but also for some reason Indian suppliers have many domestic issues causing delays.. 

Talking about Christmas.. well a big wow.. we have Christmas Chill Pills.. and they tell me they are awesome. I'm also delighted to see The Oudh Experience Room Sprays.. because I was there when those heady fragrances were being sampled.. I feel a nice Christmas gift or sexy addition to any hamper or gift box..
 
Just a reminder we have a Showroom Open Week coming up in Sheffield.. do come along if you get the chance - you can see and hold and smell that new stock.. Plus Rodrigo and his team will as always be delighted to see you.

Take care .. have a lovely Equinox weekend..
More news from China next week.

David

title: Fire in Spain
content_html:
Greetings from Spain


I hope you are well, and trade is good.
Last week I was telling you about the trade show in Delhi, and a report from  Mr Chatterjee - you can read about it here.

Here in Spain it rained the other day and it was the best thing ever.
You might have seen the pictures of the fire raging in the hills behind the coast.. at one point 42 fire planes and helicopters were fighting the biggest fire ever seen in Spain.
Every few minutes a yellow plane buzzed over my house and out to sea to scoop up water and then fly very low and return to dump it on the approaching blaze. 
On Sunday I was having lunch with friends at the beach, slightly strange watching the smoke rising behind the mountains while those yellow planes flew past. 




The smoke rising from the hills reminded me of Bali and the ash rising from the volcano. 
Anyway the rain was very welcome and I believe a big help to the firefighters, I understand there are still fighting but things are under control.

Talking about Bali.. There has been some good news. Business visa applications are open again and a government announcement on Thursday said borders were open for business trips with immediate effect.  I have already submitted my application, assuming there is no problem. I could be on my way to Indonesia within weeks. So watch this space for developments.


Talking of developments.. 

Regular readers will know about the terrible fire that destroyed our main warehouse in July 2020, well it is being rebuilt bigger and better.. the plan now is to move our aromatics factory into that space and massively increase production capacity. 



It's really taking shape, and we are getting excited about the move.


Meanwhile in Slovakia, our company there AWGifts.eu really needs to move to a bigger warehouse. When I was there with Tomas a few weeks ago we went to visit the available sites.
Our short list is down to two locations, one close to the Amazon warehouse, and another very close to our current warehouse. And to say the competition between the two landlords was fierce is an understatement. 
This week has been a series of conference calls with Tomas, the agent and the developers. We still haven't decided which way to jump but the deal on the table is surprisingly good. 
So we could be moving as soon as January next year.. It's all very exciting.

Talking about exciting - a new range of bath bombs is about to hit, radical and fresh.. Donut shaped bath bombs..


Calm down, not officially launched yet.. but very soon.

The only cloud on the horizon is the approaching inflation storm..  a lot of price rises lately, we have done our best to absorb as much as possible but from Monday there will be some unavoidable price rises on most aromatics products.
You should have received an email already with details.
So just a heads up order now to avoid the price rises. You also might want to think about reviewing your retail selling prices.
I believe we remain competitive, if you can buy like-for-like products cheaper - please do let us know.

Hope you have a great weekend.
Don't forget to be kind to someone :)

David

title: Made in Old Kolkata
content_html:
I'm delighted to see the new leather products arriving online, these are also from Kolkata. Although if you see them in the you will assume they are Spanish or perhaps Moroccan. This is how it happened, I was shopping in that Carrefour supermarket behind Torrelomenous. The sea views from the checkouts are delightful. There are independant shops behind the checkouts, where I spotted a rather nice handcrafted wallet, price 29 euros. I bit expensive but I liked it because it had a nice motif of a lizard on it. I assumed it was local, made in Morocco.. perhaps.
A few weeks later I'm at a trade show in Delhi, and see the self same wallet displayed on a stand. "Where is this made?" I asked slightly surprised to see it, pulling out my wallet to compare. It's actually goat skin, the guy told me and made in Kolkata. After some conversation, I discovered the trader was an agent, therefore we wouldn't be buying direct from the source and would be unlikely to check the production was ethical or not.
Some time later I'm in Kolkata, and have made enquires though our man there; Mr Chatterjee. (see last weeks newsletter). We found a couple of promising companies to see.
The centre of this industry is Old Kolkata. A maze of lanes running between ancient houses, some which would have housed East India Company traders a hundred years ago. Rickshaw men still rush up and down these narrow streets, and behind closed doors a host of handicraft work is going on.
Our chosen man is a dapper chap. He has displayed his work in Milan a few years ago, and has been making designer brand leather bags for a major label. He is also the home of the "Cat Bag" very famous and his biggest selling product. The system here is that the trader will develop designs, often working closely with customers, then finance the orders. The craftwork is mostly done in family co-operatives, with final stitching and packing done in house.
The Italian bags you will find, in high end shops, with "Made in Italy" labels on them. Strikes me that Kolkatta doesn't get much recognition.
We went to see the family cooperative where his goods are mostly made.
This lady was pretty much in charge. She worked with the trader to get the designs right, and then allocated the jobs, showing the artisans exactly how to do it.
This chap does stitching work, on special extra tough sowing machines.
​
So you can see we are very proud of our collection of leather goods from Kolkata. The craft industry provides for work for thousands of artisans in this area.
Generations of artisans have been producing leather goods here for hundreds of years, support them by checking out the products below.
Of course if you have any ideas for products do let me know.
Also check out our rather posh Stripy (Milan inspired handbags) - notice the label inside proudly says "Made in Old Kolkata"
Take care.
David

title: We bought a beach bar
content_html:
Greetings from Bali.

Last week I was telling you about how magic happens in Bali.. if you missed it you can catch up here.

I was telling you Tomas and Raul arrived.. and we embarked on a new adventure.. one part of plan is we need beautiful offices for a team working from here..


Things can happen quickly here, you can get things done PDQ - I'm not sure why but a combination of high-trust, minimal bureaucracy and a young enthusiastic population means things just happen.

Last Saturday we went to look at a dream office location, by Thursday afternoon we found ourselves sitting in a Notary office in Denpasar exchanging contracts and after a trip to the bank to make a transfer we are the proud owner of a dream office on the beach complete with swimming pool. 



Two sisters owned the property, as the deal was finished, they handed me a big bunch of keys.


Actually we had an idea we would find an old house in Denpasar or some commercial offices in the business quarter.  But we spotted this advert for a beach bar, in Ketewel, the same village area as our warehouse. It's not really a tourist area, whoever built this place miss-judged the market because not far away are much better beaches with hundreds of bars and restaurants, here is just a windswept area with no facilities. There is (next door) a beach shack cafe popular with Japanese surfers, but that's it. The place is wild and remote even though it is only 20 minutes from Denpasar city.




Tomas has made a design plan already.. And today they are cleaning everything and taking out all the stuff we don't need. 


The Internet was ordered this morning and will be installed by Monday or Tuesday. It's amazing how quickly you can get things done here.


Now I'm sure you are asking yourself: What on earth are they playing at? Why do they need cool offices overlooking the sea in Bali? 


Stay tuned and soon I will tell you everything.. but what I can tell you now is this is something in the pipeline (maybe in 6 months) that you will use to take your online business to a whole new level without spending a fortune.

Cool offices we hope will attract the brightest and best of young Indonesian tech talent, that can be used to your advantage..

 

Meanwhile in between doing property deals we are of course doing giftware deals. One trending item right now are musical gifts for children, and Indonesia is a rich source.. We have been working hard on this and this morning ordered a good range I think you will love. As it happens this week two containers arrived, one with gemstone jewellery.. yes the power Bracelets are back in stock! And another container from Indonesia with lots of new beautiful items.. including some stunning tamarin wood and resin coffee tables. These come from a small artisan workshop, the right shaped blocks of wood are rare and production is very limited so it's not possible to stock quantity, but I was so taken with the beauty of them we bought whatever they can make.. which is just a dozen or so per month. I'm also excited to see the Lombok vases arrive, beautiful ceramics from the island next door to Bali.. great value and team perfectly with other products.. see below.

 

It's all happening at once!!

More news next week.

 

Take care, hope you have a great Valentine's weekend trade and a romantic day on Tuesday.

David

title: A sad day
content_html:
Greetings from sunny but cold España

Hope you had a good week, and things are picking up for the upcoming season of love, kicking off with Valentine's day.. in only 3 weeks.
It's been super busy, partly because of the aforementioned V-day.. but also because so much.. much delayed stock is finally rolling in. The supply line crisis is kind of ridiculous, not only are shipping costs astronomically high but the delays are crazy. One container of incense (normally 4 to 5 weeks shipping) is now four a half months in transit. What the hell is going on?
Gosh.. sorry to rant. These days it is hard work being an importer or comes to that.. an exporter. Which (big sigh) brings me to the fact that we have finally reluctantly reached a point where we had to make a sad and difficult decision. And so I have a statement to make.. see below.
Last week I was telling you about the ONE important thing never to forget in any business and especially the gift trade if you want to grow and succeed.. if you missed it you can recap here.. 

Ok deep breathe. We fought against this for a long time, but inch by bloody inch we have been slowly losing the damn battle. There was a time when our sales to the EU were more than half of our sales. Our French, German, Polish and Italian websites were booming.. growing 30% a year.  Every week truck loads of British made aromatics products, plus our Indian and Indonesian imports flowed across the channel and found their way to thousands of European gift shops. Creating and sustaining lots of jobs in our marketing office, the warehouse and the aromatics factory. Sadly as you know Brexit happened, and even though we put our best brains on the problem and devised cunning plans to overcome the obstacles.. bit by bit the inevitable happened. The EU customers that used to love us gradually became disillusioned with the long transit times, the unexpected taxes, the complicated paperwork, the VAT to pay and reclaim.  They started giving us bad reviews.. sales growth reversed.. and nothing we could do could save the day. 

So this week we reluctantly decided to close our dedicated EU websites. They after so many years are being wound down. It's a sad day.

It's really sad, we sadly had to let our French webmaster go Mauro, our Italian mystro has been redeployed and so has Radek our Polish guy. All those EU websites are being redirected to our EU distribution warehouses. Of course, we can still handle exports via our UK website just like we always did to the rest of the world.. it's just that now the EU is the same system as "the rest of the world".
It's not all bad.. UK sales are up as customers struggle to buy stuff from Europe, our EU based businesses are doing really well, but they were growing even before Brexit and as department stores close, independents are opening fast.. so new customers are coming our way. The world is changing. We have to change with it.

If you are an EU customer, the good news is you can order from our Spain or Slovak distribution centres. Until the end of the month, you can still place an order on the EU dedicated sites. After that you can still order as an importer from our UK main site (in English).

But as I pointed out two weeks ago.. the ONE THING that saves us is blinking obvious but easy to lose track of.. and whatever they throw at us we must not lose sight of the fact that.. Excellent Products - New Products - Repeat Selling Products.. that delight our/your end customers. It is what not only keeps us all in business but sustains that virtuous circle that supports family businesses in India, Indonesia and beyond.  

Early yesterday morning I took a call from Bondan (Ringo's new assistant in Indonesia) on a trip to Java.. He was quite excited to find a town with lots of small family businesses making seagrass and bamboo products.. OMG!..  so creative and beautiful. Yesterday I spent time with our new agent in Nepal who had found a factory out in the Kathmandu valley.. another family business making eco-felt products that look amazing. Both online meetings resulted in potential winning new products put into development.  The other day Mr Chatterjee went to a remote village in Bengal to visit a singing bowl factory. Without giving away too many secrets here are some pictures and videos.


From Upendra in Nepal


From Bondan in Java


From Mr. Chattergee in India


We also have lots of things happening in India.. Mr Chatterjee found a village making Singing Bowls deep in the Bengal hinterland.
But you know it is seriously hard to make it happen from a distance.. so I booked my flights to Asia.. I will be on my way again in a few weeks.
These are difficult times to travel.. but I'm hoping that by the time I go things will ease and I can get around without long quarantines and complex visa requirements. 

Challenging but exciting times..  
Hope you are along for the ride by following these newsletters.

More good news.. Indian and Chinese containers this week - lots of things back in stock. New: Spell Candles  they have already been on sale in Slovakia and selling very well there.

Take care

Have a great weekend.

David

title: Beyond Excited
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.

Back to a Friday update after last week's jubilee hiccup.

The last update I was telling you about our 5th Birthday in Slovakia and my trip down from Vienna to Malaga, and boy is it hot here. (You can catch up here)
But not as hot as in Kolkata where Mr Chatterjee our man in India and his team just loaded a container in 43c heat. I sent my heartfelt thanks to the team. Mr Chaterjee and his son are very very excited.. 

I only decided to come to Spain on the spur of the moment, the original plan was to fly back to Kuala Lumpur with Raul (The IT wizard) from Vienna. But I just felt I wanted to see my home before taking off to Asia.
As it happened it was probably a good thing, because my house plants needed care and I wanted (of course) to catch up with my favourite AW team in Spain.  And anyway Graciela (our designer) has been working hard on some product designs for India - which I wanted to see and tweek. Which we are sending to Mr Chatterjee in India..


  Thank you Graciela!

From here I will go back to Istambul - a stop over to finalise deals - then on to Kuala Lumpur..
Mr Chatterjee and his son are flying from Kolkata to Kuala Lumpur, with suitcases stuffed with samples from our best Indian suppliers. For some unknown reason (despite Borris's trip to Delhi in search of closer ties with India) they are not issuing e-visa to UK nationals, so at this point I can't easily go to India.. So India in the shape of Mr Chatterjee and son is coming to me.

It is an understatement to say they are excited, myself also. Mr Chatterjee is a very old friend as well as business partner, we have been working together for almost 20 years. Of course I haven't seen him since before the pandemic. Tomas and I were in India just as the virus cases started to emerge, we escaped on one of the last international flights out on the 12th March 2020. If all goes well I will meet Mr Chatterjee on the 18th in Kuala Lumpur (after 820 days) it will be quite a reunion - he is, he assures me,  bringing Black Dog Indian whiskey. Just like old times..


After KL the plan is I will go to Indonesia in search of more great products, I'm hoping to find something as successful as the Molten Glass on Wood range, or at least as good as the iconic Coconut Lamps.. Both are back in stock and with special deals this week (see below). Also the Pampas Grass or Rayung Grass with vivid exotic colours is a great look for your shop this summer. 

And talking of people we have worked with for many years... Many of you will know Kerry from AW UK customer service.. She will always be part of AW, having been with us since 2007.. almost 15 years. 
Kerry has been a valuable team member, and a massive source of information, there is nothing about AW that Kerry doesn't know.. I think she will miss us and we will certainly miss her.
She has decided to make a new chapter in her career, and of course we wish her all the best. If you want to pass on wishes you can email her or reply to this email.


It's not long until Father's Day.. are you prepared?

Next week I will be back in Istanbul. The week after the grand reunion with Mr Chatterjee.. if all goes to plan.
Full reports here..

Take care

David

title: David's AW News: Angels & Babies
content_html:
Greetings from Pantai Lembeng, Bali


I'm sat in the Beach office of AW-Advantage, where Raul (the IT wizard) is deep in consultation and concentration with his small team of programmers.. 
You might have noticed things happening on our websites recently.. New search bar, new discounts, a revamped Gold Reward System and a new way to display product prices.


It's a lot more complicated than you can imagine.. but big changes are coming soon.
Actually I'm feeling a little traumatised.. I have just come back from a trip to the nearby Bali Babies Home.. and made an important decision.. (see below)
Last week I was telling you about 7 surprising surprises... if you missed it you can catch up here.

This week has been manic.. lots of problems that need fixing, suppliers to see and deals to be renegotiated.
We went to see one of the families that are making Hati Hati Angels and managed to catch them in full production mode. 
Off the beaten track, in a traditional wood carving village in family compound down a little back alley we found them..

Family team..

The father told me he had been carving wood since he was 6 years old.. so for 50 years and his father before him. The whole family are involved, the son cuts the raw suar wood into the rough shape, father and daughter skilfully carve the angles, and the wife and grandmother are doing the sanding and polishing. The grandchild is in charge of feeding ice cream to the pet dog. We took pictures and chatted to them as they continued working. They told me that they make about 25 angles in one day, so that's just 5 per person per day.  So slowly no? Fortunately Ringo has a collection of other artisans making the same shape.. but we can never keep up with demand.
I asked them if they was happy doing this? Yes they said smiling, it is their life they love it, and the job gives them freedom to attend the many Balinese ceremonies, do some farming and be involved in the complex Bali community. Yes they could get work in boutique hotel at the end of the village, but the demands of that kind of job means the cultural life suffers. 

We take the carved angels, and then another artisan does the finishing, that's painting and polishing. Later we laser carve the angel name on the base in our warehouse.  
Hati Hati Angels was one of the first products we developed in Bali.. Hati Hati means "Take care" - and over the tears we have never been able to buy enough to keep them in stock.. Regular customer will know we are out of stock more than in.. and sadly as the artisan in Bali gradually dwindle and take jobs outside the villages I fear that this kind of product will be more and more difficult to source. 
Bondhan made a little video of our visit.. 


This morning we took a trip to see the Bali Baby Home. It's our second visit.. last time was in February, 6 months ago. Actually I wanted to meet the founder of this amazing project. A guy called Burhan.
What I didn't appreciate on the first visit is that this is a relatively new venture.. only two and years old and in the last 6 months has done amazing things. What they do is create a safe space for young mothers who have been ostracized or run away from their families because of a pregnancy.   Burhan told me that on average one baby is abandoned somewhere in Indonesia everyday. Left on the side of the road, in rubbish bin or sometimes left outside his home. Indonesian society especially in the rural areas and remote islands is so unaccepting of pregnancy out of wedlock, and abortions are illegal in Indonesia, so young girls often run away and sometimes to the comparatively liberal island of Bali.  


Burhan told me they have saved over a hundred babies in the last two years that otherwise might be dead. And he and his team work hard at reuniting babies and family.. he will go to remote village find the family of girl - negotiate the safe and loving return of girl and baby. 43 babies have been successfully returned to families. Part of the process is that every baby has an Instagram account, so that grand parents can see how cute their kids are and hopefully melt hardened hearts.
We arrived just as Barham also returned from a four day trip to Java where they are setting up another home, the house where we met is the toddler place and all the little ones were excited to see him crowding round and calling him papa.  They have volunteers come from Europe right now two girls from France, the mothers who are here all pitch in and local ladies help, you can see how they are all devoted to the energetic and charismatic Burhan. I sat with him and he told me the whole story.. 



On behalf of Ancient Wisdom we offered our help, there is a large house next to the existing home which last time we came was clearly over crowded. It belongs to a Japanese businessman who has agreed to rent it to the charity, so we agreed to cover the rent and some extra for services. Also a lump sum big enough to do meaningful work, and pay off debts. 
He told me that they are not short of nappies and baby food, tourist arrive everyday with boxes of supplies, in return for a tour of the building. They have so many donations that he sends a truck every month to Java for use in the other two homes he has set up. 
You can find out more here: .Bali Baby Home.
Our plan is to develop a product line from Bali, where a chunk of the profit can on that line goes directly back to the home. In this way you can help support what I believe is a super worthy cause.

So Angels and Babies.. 
Regular readers will know we have a children's home in India we have supported for many years.. You can read about it here.
Our plan is develop relationships with on-the-ground people in all the areas we do business in. I hope you are coming along for the ride. And help us to support more people.

Moving on.. 
Next week after a major revamp.. We have a SHOWROOM OPEN WEEK..  9am until 3am feel free to come along without an appointment.
Katka, Rodrigo and Martina and team are ready with cups of tea, sample packs, 10% discount, free shipping if you need it.. and a Spectacular FREE gift on all orders over £1000.
Rodrigo invite..

There are also new products coming online..
New discounts on almost every product! 

Take care and more news next week.
Hati Hati!

David

Regular customer will know we are out of stock more than in.. and sadly as the artisan in Bali gradually dwindle and take jobs outside the villages I fear that this kind of product will be more and more difficult to source. Bondhan made a little video of our visit.. This morning we took a trip to see the Bali Baby Home. It's our second visit.. last time was in February, 6 months ago. Actually I wanted to meet the founder of this amazing project. A guy called Burhan. What I didn't appreciate on the first visit is that this is a relatively new venture.. only two and years old and in the last 6 months has done amazing things. What they do is create a safe space for young mothers who have been ostracized or run away from their families because of a pregnancy. Burhan told me that on average one baby is abandoned somewhere in Indonesia everyday. Left on the side of the road, in rubbish bin or sometimes left outside his home. Indonesian society especially in the rural areas and remote islands is so unaccepting of pregnancy out of wedlock, and abortions are illegal in Indonesia, so young girls often run away and sometimes to the comparatively liberal island of Bali. Burhan told me they have saved over a hundred babies in the last two years that otherwise might be dead. And he and his team work hard at reuniting babies and family.. he will go to remote village find the family of girl - negotiate the safe and loving return of girl and baby. 43 babies have been successfully returned to families. Part of the process is that every baby has an Instagram account, so that grand parents can see how cute their kids are and hopefully melt hardened hearts. We arrived just as Barham also returned from a four day trip to Java where they are setting up another home, the house where we met is the toddler place and all the little ones were excited to see him crowding round and calling him papa. They have volunteers come from Europe right now two girls from France, the mothers who are here all pitch in and local ladies help, you can see how they are all devoted to the energetic and charismatic Burhan. I sat with him and he told me the whole story.. On behalf of Ancient Wisdom we offered our help, there is a large house next to the existing home which last time we came was clearly over crowded. It belongs to a Japanese businessman who has agreed to rent it to the charity, so we agreed to cover the rent and some extra for services. Also a lump sum big enough to do meaningful work, and pay off debts. He told me that they are not short of nappies and baby food, tourist arrive everyday with boxes of supplies, in return for a tour of the building. They have so many donations that he sends a truck every month to Java for use in the other two homes he has set up. You can find out more here: . Bali Baby Home . Our plan is to develop a product line from Bali, where a chunk of the profit can on that line goes directly back to the home. In this way you can help support what I believe is a super worthy cause. So Angels and Babies.. Regular readers will know we have a children's home in India we have supported for many years.. You can read about it here. Our plan is develop relationships with on-the-ground people in all the areas we do business in. I hope you are coming along for the ride. And help us to support more people. Moving on.. Next week after a major revamp.. We have a SHOWROOM OPEN WEEK. . 9am until 3am feel free to come along without an appointment. Katka, Rodrigo and Martina and team are ready with cups of tea, sample packs, 10% discount, free shipping if you need it.. and a Spectacular FREE gift on all orders over £1000. Rodrigo invite.. There are also new products coming online.. New discounts on almost every product! Take care and more news next week. Hati Hati! David

title: Love in the Time of Corona
content_html:
Greetings from Spain.


Happy Halloween Weekend. Even if it is a lockdown Halloween I hope you can have some fun. 
Here in Spain they have just imposed an evening curfew - from 11pm to 6am..  Some people are upset about it.. but for me 11pm is well past my bedtime and I wake up with the sunrise at about 7.40am. So I don't think I will get into trouble :)
Last week I was telling you about how things were slipping into "Warp Speed" at AW.. You can read about it here.


Tomas, James and Kane have been hands on in the warehouse in Sheffield.. really making it happen introducing an improved system. Still away to go, but almost all products are located, so easy to find, more label printers on the packing benches, more packing benches, an improved software system that automates more. Result an extra few hundred orders a day. We are catching up with orders and improving efficiency. It's amazing what some extra space and a bit of hard work and talent can do. Well done guys.



As well as catching up dramatically - it's all happening - two containers from Indonesia, one from China and one from India. So lots of new stock this week. The first Indonesia container had stock of the Natural Coco Lamps.. we practically sold out in hours of putting them back in stock. But more stock will shortly be available. It's great that the Indonesian stuff sells so well, this makes me personally very happy.  Those artisans in Bali and Java we work with more than need the re-orders. It feels good to be able to support them with trade.

Regular readers will know I was in Bali locked down for a few months - able to work quietly with Ringo developing the products that are arriving. Bali is of course very reliant on tourism and a lot of the artisans supplied local gift shops. As the tourists all went home, the streets fell silent and this part of their trade dried up all together. The central wholesale market in Denpasar closed, partly because of covid, but also because no international buyers could come. So most export trade also shrank.
Inland Bali is a peaceful place even in normal times. But after lockdown it regressed to an Eden like idle, rural, green, lush, tranquil, no planes above, almost no traffic. When we called on a supplier to do business - we felt like we were tiptoeing through paradise.  
It was a special bitter/sweet time - brought abruptly to an end by the fire at our warehouse in Sheffield.. 
I have this picture on my laptop desktop.. it's  beautiful right?...  but look very closely and you can tell it is in the time of corona.



So with no tourists many of the workers have gone home to the farms and rural life, living simply from the land. But there are still car leases, mortgages, electric bills to pay. So you would not believe how grateful our suppliers are to be supported by orders from AW (actually from you.. or even we could say - your customers). This story is repeated but with urgency in India, Nepal and Morocco.  


More news from our Aromatics factory.. the "Beast" started to produce its first soaps this week.. we started making Chill Pills again.. and we keep expanding bath bomb production.. Hopefully soon we can fully meet demand.
The problems with mine shafts discovered under our new warehouse has - I understand - been resolved, the lease is in the final stages of negotiations.. so hopefully we can take official occupation on a brand new ten year lease very shortly.
Maybe by next week.. at which stage, I will announce the new name for our building. It's been decided, and I think it is apt, classy and suggested by only one of our customers. To be revealed soon.. maybe next week..


So here we are heading for more lock-downs across Europe.. it's a strange and sometimes terrifying world we live in. Christmas is coming and (even in the time of corona) - one thing remains true. Giving a gift an act of love, in which we (as gift traders) are privileged to be part of. Whatever they say, however they classify it..  an act of love is an essential item in these difficult days. Online trade in June boomed, and I guess there will be a second online wave.. are you ready?  Check out AW-dropship.com  - if you are forced to work from home this is your future..


We normally have a Halloween costume competition at AW - this year we cancelled it (of course) although a few staff turned up dressed rather strangely all the same.



Take special care - enjoy the weekend.. 
More news next week.


David
